entries.label: Short action lines at a contact point
entries.description: A tight starburst of short strokes stamped at the point of contact to mark the hit.
entries.frame_evidence: A compact cluster (typically under 15 percent of frame width) of 6-20 short radiating strokes appearing for 1-4 frames.
entries.detector_note: Hough segments constrained to a sliding window; require >=6 segments of length 8-40 px within a window whose radial consensus point is inside the window, and a lifetime of <=4 raw frames.
entries.notes: Grass tufts, hair spikes, sparkles and star fields give similar local segment clusters.

entries.label: Discrete afterimage clones (speed illusion)
entries.description: Fully opaque duplicate figures shown simultaneously to imply a character moving faster than the eye follows.
entries.frame_evidence: Two or more complete, fully saturated copies of the same character in one frame, usually evenly spaced.
entries.detector_note: Crop the union bounding box of the candidate repeated components (from self-matchTemplate peaks) at >=384 px and ask qwen2.5vl per THE CROP RULE; deterministic self-match only proposes the crop, the VLM confirms it is the same character rather than twins or a mirror.
entries.vlm_question: Does this image show the same single character drawn two or more times in different positions? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Genuine twins, reflections and a character standing in front of a poster of themselves all defeat the deterministic proposal stage.

entries.label: Animation on 1s
entries.description: A new drawing every frame, used for the fastest and most expensive action.
entries.frame_evidence: Within a shot, the duplicate-run length is 1 for a sustained stretch.
entries.detector_note: Modal duplicate-run length == 1 over >= 8 consecutive raw frames, with per-cel flow magnitude above the shot noise floor to exclude noisy holds.
entries.notes: Camera-only motion (a pan over a still) also produces run length 1; separate with the pan_across_still test.

entries.label: Animation on 3s
entries.description: Each drawing held for three frames, common in dialogue and low-budget cuts.
entries.frame_evidence: Duplicate-run lengths cluster at 3 through the shot.
entries.detector_note: Same histogram test with mass at run length 3 > 0.5 and a period-3 autocorrelation peak.
entries.notes: Mixed 2s/3s cuts split the histogram and neither entry fires; report the full histogram, not just the winner.

entries.label: Animation on 2s
entries.description: Each drawing held for two frames, the standard TV anime cadence.
entries.frame_evidence: Duplicate-run lengths cluster at exactly 2 through the shot.
entries.detector_note: Histogram of duplicate-run lengths within the shot; on 2s when the mass at run length 2 exceeds 0.6 and the run-start phase is regular (period-2 autocorrelation peak of the MAD signal > 0.5).
entries.notes: On a 23.976 fps stream carrying telecine, pull-down duplicates masquerade as 2s; check the 3:2 pattern first.

entries.label: Looping / repeating background (harmonica)
entries.description: A scrolling background made from a tiling plate, so scenery visibly recurs during the pan.
entries.frame_evidence: During a horizontal scroll, a strip of the image reappears at a fixed spatial period.
entries.detector_note: Accumulate the scrolled panorama by integrating the per-frame dx, then autocorrelate the panorama along x; a tiling plate produces a strong peak at the tile width.
entries.notes: Genuinely repetitive scenery (identical buildings, a fence, a forest) is indistinguishable from a tiled plate.

entries.label: Book pan / layered scroll
entries.description: Several background layers scroll horizontally at once, usually with a foreground plate moving fastest.
entries.frame_evidence: Different horizontal image bands translate at clearly different rates in the same frame pair.
entries.detector_note: Per-band (rows split into 8 strips) phaseCorrelate; report the set of distinct dx values; book pan when >=2 bands differ by more than 1.5 px/frame with each band internally consistent.
entries.notes: A real camera pan over a scene with depth produces the same band statistics; this is the point - see multiplane_parallax.

entries.label: Brush / painted smear texture
entries.description: The smear is rendered with visible brush or airbrush texture rather than flat cel fill.
entries.frame_evidence: The elongated smear region carries a directional streaky texture with a strong single-orientation frequency signature.
entries.detector_note: skimage.feature.structure_tensor inside the smear mask; coherence = (l1-l2)/(l1+l2) > 0.7 plus a non-zero high-frequency residual (frame minus cv2.medianBlur k=5) inside a region that is otherwise flat-filled.
entries.notes: Compression ringing along a hard edge also produces oriented high-frequency residual.

entries.label: Camera shake as whole-frame offset
entries.description: An impact shake applied by translating the entire composited frame, leaving edge slivers or a slight zoom-in.
entries.frame_evidence: Frame-to-frame global translation with high-frequency alternating sign and no internal parallax.
entries.detector_note: phaseCorrelate global shift series; shake when the shift series has power concentrated above 4 Hz with alternating sign and the per-tile shifts all agree (std of tile shifts < 0.3 px), which distinguishes a flat 2D shake from a real handheld 3D camera.
entries.notes: Rolling-shutter wobble and stabilisation artefacts in live action give non-uniform tile shifts, which is the useful separator.

entries.label: Shake revealing frame edges (uncovered border)
entries.description: The shake exposes the edge of the artwork, leaving a black or repeated sliver at the frame boundary.
entries.frame_evidence: A 1-10 px band at one frame edge goes black or clones the adjacent column for a few frames.
entries.detector_note: Sample the outer 12 px border columns/rows; flag frames where a border strip is near-black (mean < 12) or exactly equal to the neighbouring interior column while the shift series is non-zero.
entries.notes: Letterboxing, mastering pillarboxes and dirty broadcast edges look the same on a static shot; require concurrent shake.

entries.label: Graphic cast shadow shape
entries.description: A shadow drawn as a hard flat shape (character-shaped blob, window bars across a face) rather than a rendered occlusion.
entries.frame_evidence: A uniformly darkened region with a crisp boundary whose shape is unrelated to the local geometry it lies on.
entries.detector_note: Find regions where luminance is multiplied by a near-constant factor (ratio image against a local median-filtered version has a flat plateau at 0.5-0.8) with boundary transition < 2 px; report the shape's solidity and boundary straightness.
entries.notes: A real hard-lit shadow in live action satisfies the same multiplicative flat-plateau test; the entry is descriptive, not medium-diagnostic.

entries.label: Cel shading with a hard terminator
entries.description: Light and shadow separated by a crisp step edge with no gradient in between, the defining look of cel shading.
entries.frame_evidence: Inside a single skin or fabric region, luminance is bimodal with a transition that completes in 1-2 px.
entries.detector_note: Within a colour-quantised region, take the luminance histogram; require two modes separated by >20 LSB with midtone mass < 0.08, and measure the 10-90 percent transition width along profiles crossing the shadow boundary (median < 2.5 px).
entries.notes: Upscaling and soft compression widen the step; measure on native resolution, and be aware that a 3D toon shader produces an identical statistic (which is the point - use applies_to both).

entries.label: Chromatic (colour-separated) flash
entries.description: An impact flash accompanied by deliberate RGB channel offset, so the burst leaves coloured fringes.
entries.frame_evidence: During the flash frames the R, G and B channel edge maps are spatially offset from each other by several pixels.
entries.detector_note: cv2.phaseCorrelate between the R and B channel Sobel magnitudes; flag |shift| > 1.5 px during the flash window while the same measurement on surrounding frames is < 0.5 px.
entries.notes: A chromatic-aberration grade applied to the whole show gives a constant non-zero baseline; only the DELTA above the shot baseline is evidence.

entries.label: Colour hold (line art filled with the fill colour)
entries.description: The outline of a region is coloured to match or tint toward its fill so the drawing reads as glowing or as being in shadow.
entries.frame_evidence: A region's contour loses its dark ink and takes a hue/luminance close to the fill, while other regions in the same frame keep black ink.
entries.detector_note: Per-region boundary dip depth (as in line_absent_paint_only) compared against the frame median: colour hold when one region's dip depth < 8 LSB while the frame median is > 25 LSB, and the boundary hue is within 25 degrees of the fill hue.
entries.notes: Cannot distinguish an intentional colour hold from a paint error that filled the line layer; both look identical in a frame.

entries.label: Looped / cycled animation (any length)
entries.description: A repeating cel cycle of any length reused to fill duration (running, flapping, machinery, fire).
entries.frame_evidence: The unique-cel sequence contains an exactly repeating subsequence.
entries.detector_note: Self-similarity matrix of unique cels; find the lag maximising the mean diagonal similarity, and require at least two full repeats with per-cel MAD below the intra-cel noise floor.
entries.notes: Distinguishing a deliberate reused cycle from a genuinely periodic performance (real running in live action) is not possible from similarity alone - only the EXACTNESS of the repeat separates them, and that exactness is destroyed by compression.

entries.label: Radial debris / rubble burst
entries.description: Small drawn shards, dust chunks or rocks thrown outward from the impact centre in the frames after the hit.
entries.frame_evidence: Many small blobs appear within a few frames and their motion vectors all point away from a common centre.
entries.detector_note: Farneback flow (cv2.calcOpticalFlowFarneback) on unique cels; least-squares fit for a focus-of-expansion, then report the fraction of flow vectors whose direction is within 30 degrees of radially outward from that point; require >0.6 with a fresh blob count spike from skimage.feature.blob_log.
entries.notes: A forward camera dolly produces a genuine focus-of-expansion too; check that the camera is otherwise static.

entries.label: Flat-plate fake dolly zoom
entries.description: A vertigo effect faked by scaling separate flat layers at different rates.
entries.frame_evidence: Two or more layers scale at different rates about the same centre with no perspective change inside any layer.
entries.detector_note: Per-layer (flow-segmented) similarity transform; flag differing scale terms with each layer's internal warp residual near zero.
entries.notes: Requires reliable flow segmentation, which fails whenever layers share texture statistics.

entries.label: Stamped elliptical drop shadow
entries.description: A simple dark ellipse placed under a character as a cheap contact cue.
entries.frame_evidence: A soft or hard dark ellipse under the feet whose major axis is horizontal and which translates with the character.
entries.detector_note: cv2.fitEllipse on dark connected components below the subject bbox; require aspect < 0.45, angle within 15 degrees of horizontal, and centroid tracking that follows the subject bbox centroid across cels with correlation > 0.9.
entries.notes: Any dark ellipse in the lower frame (a puddle, a manhole, a rug) will fit; the tracking correlation is what makes the claim.

entries.label: Energy beam with hot core and glow falloff
entries.description: A drawn or rendered beam with a white core, a coloured halo, and a soft outer falloff.
entries.frame_evidence: A long straight or gently curved band whose cross-section profile is white in the middle, saturated colour at the edges, fading outward.
entries.detector_note: Fit the dominant long bright axis (PCA on saturated-bright pixels), sample perpendicular intensity/saturation profiles, and require a centre with V>250 and S<0.15 flanked by S>0.5 shoulders with monotone falloff.
entries.notes: A blown-out practical light source with lens bloom in live action gives the same cross-section.

entries.label: Flash breaks the 2s/3s cadence
entries.description: The impact burst is drawn on 1s while the surrounding action holds on 2s or 3s, which is what makes it read as a jolt.
entries.frame_evidence: A run of consecutive UNIQUE frames inside a shot whose duplicate-run length is otherwise 2 or 3.
entries.detector_note: Compute per-frame duplicate-run lengths (mean abs diff < 1.0 after 2x downscale); inside a shot whose modal run length is 2 or 3, flag a window of >=2 frames with run length 1 that coincides with a luma spike.
entries.notes: Encoder noise can break exact duplicate equality; use a tolerance and confirm on downscaled frames.

entries.label: Clear centre inside a radial line field
entries.description: The radial field has an empty circular hole at its focus so the subject stays readable.
entries.frame_evidence: Line density drops to near zero inside a disc around the vanishing point and rises sharply outside it.
entries.detector_note: cv2.warpPolar around the vanishing point; radial profile of line-mask density; find the radius where density crosses 0.2 of its outer plateau and report it as inner_clear_radius.
entries.notes: Needs a reliable vanishing point; a wrong centre produces a meaningless profile.

entries.label: Concentration / focus lines on a character
entries.description: Radial lines converging on a face or object to draw attention or signal shock, with the convergence point on the subject.
entries.frame_evidence: Radial line field whose vanishing point falls inside the head or torso region rather than at the horizon.
entries.detector_note: Radial detection as in speedlines_radial, then test whether the vanishing point lies inside a face/head ROI (mediapipe face detection if it latches, otherwise the largest skin-toned or highest-saturation blob); emits the normalised distance from vanishing point to ROI centre.
entries.notes: Cannot be separated from a radial speedline field aimed at the camera when no face is found; face detection on anime is itself unreliable.

entries.label: Airbrush / gradient shading
entries.description: Soft continuous-tone shading inside a region, breaking the flat-cel convention (blush on cheeks, glow on hair).
entries.frame_evidence: Inside a single region the luminance varies smoothly with a low gradient magnitude and no step edges.
entries.detector_note: Within a region: luminance range > 20 LSB while the 95th percentile of the Sobel magnitude stays < 6 LSB/px; the wide-range-plus-low-gradient combination is the airbrush signature.
entries.notes: Blur from compression or defocus produces the identical statistic on any region.

entries.label: Halftone gradient (variable dot size)
entries.description: A tone whose dot size grows across the region to produce a gradient, rather than a constant tone.
entries.frame_evidence: Dot lattice frequency stays fixed while individual dot area increases smoothly across the region.
entries.detector_note: blob_log over the tone region; regress blob area against position along the region's principal axis; halftone gradient when the lattice frequency is constant (FFT peak radius stable within 5 percent) but the area slope is significantly non-zero.
entries.notes: blob_log misses dots once they merge at the dark end of the ramp, biasing the slope.

entries.label: Held pose with blink-only movement
entries.description: Only the eyes change over a hold, usually a 2-3 cel blink cycle.
entries.frame_evidence: A small horizontal pair of regions in the upper face changes for 2-3 cels then returns to the prior state.
entries.detector_note: Changed-area analysis as for mouth-only, additionally requiring the change to be A-B-A (the post-change cel matches the pre-change cel with MAD < tau) and the changed region to split into two horizontally separated components.
entries.notes: Any 2-cel flicker that returns to its original state (a light, a sparkle) satisfies the A-B-A test.

entries.label: Held pose with only hair or cloth moving
entries.description: A static character with a secondary-action loop on hair, scarf or coat.
entries.frame_evidence: Change is confined to elongated regions at the periphery of the character silhouette and repeats cyclically.
entries.detector_note: Changed-region mask intersected with a 15 px shell around the subject silhouette; require >70 percent of change inside the shell and a periodic autocorrelation of the change signal with period 4-24 cels.
entries.notes: Needs a subject mask; on a moving background the shell test is meaningless.

entries.label: Held pose with mouth-only movement
entries.description: The body is a frozen drawing and only the mouth region is swapped, the standard dialogue cheat.
entries.frame_evidence: Between unique cels, a small region around the mouth changes while >95 percent of the frame is pixel-identical.
entries.detector_note: Per-tile change mask between consecutive unique cels; flag when the changed area is < 3 percent of the frame and its bounding box lies in the lower half of the detected face/head ROI, with a change period of 2-6 cels. Face ROI from mediapipe face detection when it latches, else the largest skin-hued blob.
entries.notes: Without a face ROI this cannot be separated from any other small looping element (a blinking light, a flag). mediapipe face detection is unreliable on stylised anime faces and fails silently.

entries.label: Localised hit flash
entries.description: A small bright bloom at the exact point of contact, lasting 1-4 frames, without whiting out the whole frame.
entries.frame_evidence: A compact blob of near-saturated pixels appears and disappears within a few frames while the global exposure is unchanged.
entries.detector_note: Threshold V > 245 in HSV, connected components (cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats); flag a component whose area grows from 0 to >200 px and back within <=4 frames while frame mean_luma changes < 8 percent; record centroid.
entries.notes: Specular highlights on a moving 3D object and practical light glints in live action fire this constantly; requires a size/duration floor.

entries.label: Hit-stop (impact freeze)
entries.description: Animation holds for several frames at the moment of contact to sell the weight of the hit.
entries.frame_evidence: A run of identical or near-identical frames of 4+ frames occurring immediately after a high-motion frame pair.
entries.detector_note: Detect a duplicate run of >=4 raw frames whose immediately preceding unique-cel pair has mean flow magnitude in the top decile of the shot; report the ratio of pre-freeze motion to freeze-length.
entries.notes: Indistinguishable from an ordinary 4s hold or a stall for dialogue unless the preceding motion spike is required.

entries.label: Horizontal shock bands
entries.description: Wide horizontal bands or stripes flashed across the frame as a shock or interference beat.
entries.frame_evidence: Strong horizontal banding with a single dominant vertical spatial frequency, lasting 1-4 frames.
entries.detector_note: Column-averaged row profile, then 1D FFT; flag a single peak carrying > 0.4 of the AC power with a lifetime <= 4 frames.
entries.notes: Interlacing artefacts, rolling shutter and CRT scanline overlays are indistinguishable by this statistic alone.

entries.label: Drawn crack / shatter graphic overlay
entries.description: A branching crack or glass-shatter graphic is stamped over the frame at the moment of impact.
entries.frame_evidence: A thin high-contrast branching line network appears within 1-2 frames and is spatially locked to the frame rather than to the scene.
entries.detector_note: Difference against the previous unique cel, skeletonize the difference mask (skimage.morphology.skeletonize), then measure branch-point density (>= 0.004 per skeleton pixel) and total skeleton length; require the network to appear in a single cel step.
entries.notes: Bare tree branches, power lines and lightning give the same skeleton statistics; the single-step appearance is the discriminator.

entries.label: Black impact frame
entries.description: A 1-3 frame burst to near-black, the inverse punctuation of the white impact frame.
entries.frame_evidence: One to three consecutive frames with mean luminance below ~25/255 and low variance, surrounded by normally exposed frames.
entries.detector_note: Same run-detector as impact_frame_white with mean_L < 0.10*255 and std_L < 20; require both neighbours mean_L > 0.35*255 so it does not fire on a fade-to-black.
entries.notes: Fade-outs, shot-boundary black, and encoder-inserted black frames all mimic this; the neighbour condition is what separates them.

entries.label: Graphic-silhouette impact frame
entries.description: The 1-3 frame burst carries a high-contrast two-tone graphic (silhouette of the fighter, a cracked shape, a stylised sunburst) instead of a flat flood.
entries.frame_evidence: A frame with an extremely bimodal luminance histogram (two spikes, near-empty midtones) and large flat regions with hard boundaries.
entries.detector_note: Bimodality: fit two-mode histogram, require mass in the middle third of the luma range < 0.08 and Otsu (skimage.filters.threshold_otsu) inter-class variance in the top decile; require the frame differ from both neighbours by mean abs diff > 40.
entries.notes: Silhouette-lit dramatic shots (sunset backlight) are also bimodal; the 1-3 frame duration is the discriminator.

entries.label: Inverted (negative) impact frame
entries.description: A 1-3 frame burst where the artwork is shown as a photographic negative or with inverted line/fill polarity.
entries.frame_evidence: A frame whose per-pixel values are strongly ANTI-correlated with the frame before and after it, while the structure (edge map) stays almost identical.
entries.detector_note: Pearson correlation of the grayscale frame against the previous frame < -0.5 AND IoU of Canny edge maps (cv2.Canny 80/160) with the previous frame > 0.6; the structure-preserved + value-flipped pair is the signature.
entries.notes: Partial inversions (only the character inverted, background kept) fail the global correlation test; a masked variant is a separate entry.

entries.label: Partial / masked inversion burst
entries.description: Only a region (usually the character or the struck object) is inverted or solarised for 1-3 frames.
entries.frame_evidence: A spatially connected region shows anti-correlation with the previous frame while the rest of the frame is unchanged.
entries.detector_note: Block-wise (32x32) Pearson correlation map against the previous frame; flag when a connected component of blocks with corr < -0.4 covers 5-60 percent of the frame and the complement has corr > 0.9.
entries.notes: Large colour-cycling effects and rapid palette shifts can produce the same block statistics.

entries.label: Solid-colour impact frame (red/blue/yellow)
entries.description: A 1-3 frame flood of a single saturated hue rather than white or black, keyed to the effect (red for damage, blue for energy).
entries.frame_evidence: A frame with a single dominant hue occupying >85 percent of pixels and near-zero spatial detail.
entries.detector_note: HSV histogram: max hue-bin mass > 0.85 with S > 0.5 and Laplacian variance (cv2.Laplacian ddepth=CV_64F) < 20; report the dominant hue in degrees.
entries.notes: A shot that legitimately cuts to a flat colour card (title, eyecatch) matches; check the surrounding shot length.

entries.label: White impact frame
entries.description: A 1-3 frame burst where the frame goes to near-full white, used as a percussive punctuation on a hit.
entries.frame_evidence: One to three consecutive frames whose mean luminance jumps above ~230/255 with collapsed variance, bracketed by normal-luminance frames.
entries.detector_note: Per-frame mean/std of L channel (cv2.cvtColor BGR2LAB); flag runs of 1-3 frames where mean_L > 0.88*255 and std_L < 25 while the frames immediately before and after have mean_L < 0.6*255; run length measured on RAW frame indices, not unique-cel indices, because the burst is deliberately sub-cel.
entries.notes: False positives from real white-out transitions, lightning in live action, and camera flashes; distinguish by burst length (a transition ramps over >6 frames).

entries.label: Drawn lightning / electric arc
entries.description: Jagged high-contrast electricity drawn around a character or weapon, re-drawn differently every cel.
entries.frame_evidence: Thin, sharply angular bright polylines whose shape changes completely between consecutive cels while the host object stays still.
entries.detector_note: Bright-thin mask (top-hat, cv2.morphologyEx MORPH_TOPHAT k=3, then threshold); measure per-cel skeleton length and the IoU of consecutive cel skeletons; lightning gives long skeletons with IoU < 0.2 while the underlying object mask IoU is > 0.85.
entries.notes: Boiling line art on a detailed character also gives low skeleton IoU; require the arcs to be brighter than their surround.

entries.label: Limb elongation smear
entries.description: An arm or leg is drawn several times its anatomical length for one cel to cover a fast arc.
entries.frame_evidence: In one cel the wrist-to-elbow or ankle-to-knee span is 1.8x or more the value measured on the neighbouring cels.
entries.detector_note: mediapipe pose landmarks 13/15 (elbow/wrist) and 25/27 (knee/ankle); compute segment length normalised by shoulder width per cel and flag a single-cel spike > 1.8x the shot median.
entries.notes: mediapipe pose is trained on photographs and latches unreliably on stylised 2D characters; it silently returns a plausible-but-wrong skeleton rather than failing, so every landmark metric must be gated on visibility scores and treated as low-confidence on drawn art.

entries.label: Limited animation - long static hold
entries.description: A drawing held for many frames with no or almost no change, the core economy of TV anime.
entries.frame_evidence: A duplicate run of 6 or more raw frames with no camera motion.
entries.detector_note: Duplicate run length >= 6 combined with phaseCorrelate global shift < 0.2 px across the run; emit hold length in frames and seconds.
entries.notes: A freeze inserted by a stalled encoder or a dropped-frame stream looks identical.

entries.label: Lineless / paint-only rendering
entries.description: Forms are defined by colour boundaries with no drawn outline at all, common in effects animation and modern digital styles.
entries.frame_evidence: Shape boundaries exist as colour steps with no darker contour band between them.
entries.detector_note: At each colour-segment boundary, sample a 5 px perpendicular profile; lineless when fewer than 20 percent of boundaries have a local luminance minimum at least 25 LSB below both adjacent plateaus.
entries.notes: Soft-focus and blur destroy the dip statistic; measure only on sharp regions.

entries.label: Line boil (shimmering outlines)
entries.description: Outlines wobble frame to frame because each cel is redrawn by hand, even on a static pose.
entries.frame_evidence: On a held pose, the edge map jitters by 1-3 px between unique cels while the fill colours stay fixed.
entries.detector_note: Between consecutive UNIQUE cels of a static shot, compute the symmetric mean distance between Canny edge sets (scipy.ndimage.distance_transform_edt of one edge map sampled at the other's edge pixels); boil is 0.5-3 px with fill-region colour delta < 2 LSB; report also the temporal std of that distance.
entries.notes: Meaningless if computed on duplicate frames (identically zero) - it MUST run on unique-cel indices; encoder noise and film gate weave also displace edges, so a global-translation compensation (cv2.phaseCorrelate) must be applied first.

entries.label: Boil-free static line (digital hold)
entries.description: Outlines are pixel-locked across a hold, the signature of a digitally repeated cel or a 3D render.
entries.frame_evidence: Consecutive unique cels of a held pose show sub-0.1 px edge displacement.
entries.detector_note: Same measurement as line_boil with the flag inverted: edge_jitter_px < 0.15 across >=4 unique cels of a static shot.
entries.notes: If the unique-cel detector mistakenly treats duplicates as unique, this entry fires trivially; verify the cel-uniqueness threshold.

entries.label: Coloured line art (line colouring)
entries.description: Outlines are drawn in a hue tied to the adjacent fill (brown for skin, dark red for hair) instead of black.
entries.frame_evidence: Contour pixels carry significant saturation and a hue related to the region they bound, not neutral grey.
entries.detector_note: Sample HSV on the skeletonised ink mask; report the fraction of ink pixels with S > 0.25, and the median hue difference between ink pixels and the fill region immediately inside the contour.
entries.notes: Chroma bleeding from 4:2:0 subsampling colours black outlines next to saturated fills; requires a chroma-upsampling-aware sampling step or a high-bitrate source.

entries.label: Line-tone / hatching tone fill
entries.description: Shading applied as a field of fine parallel hatch lines instead of dots.
entries.frame_evidence: A shaded region filled with evenly spaced parallel strokes at a consistent angle, usually 45 degrees.
entries.detector_note: Tile FFT with a single dominant orientation peak (not a symmetric dot pair) plus structure_tensor coherence > 0.75 inside a region bounded by character line art; report stroke spacing from the peak frequency.
entries.notes: Cannot be separated from parallel speedlines by texture statistics alone; the containment inside a closed character region is the only cue.

entries.label: Line-weight modulation within a drawing
entries.description: Outline thickness varies deliberately along a contour (thick on the shadow side, tapering at the ends).
entries.frame_evidence: Measured stroke width along one continuous outline varies by more than a factor of two.
entries.detector_note: Binarise the ink layer (adaptive threshold on the darkest colour cluster), skimage.morphology.skeletonize plus scipy.ndimage.distance_transform_edt; sample 2x distance along each skeleton branch and report the coefficient of variation of width per branch.
entries.notes: Upscaled or heavily compressed sources smear thin lines and inflate width variance; measure only on native-resolution frames.

entries.label: Uniform hairline weight (digital vector look)
entries.description: Every outline is the same width, the signature of vector or 3D-toon outlines rather than a brush.
entries.frame_evidence: Stroke-width distribution across the whole frame is a narrow spike, typically 1-2 px at native resolution.
entries.detector_note: Same width measurement as line_weight_modulation, but reported globally: flag when the interquartile range of widths is < 0.6 px and the median is < 2.5 px.
entries.notes: Resolution-dependent; a downscaled 4K master flattens genuine width variation into a uniform-looking spike.

entries.label: Mixed cadence within one shot
entries.description: The same shot switches between 1s, 2s and 3s (the character on 2s, an effect on 1s, a hold on 8s).
entries.frame_evidence: Duplicate-run lengths vary across the shot and different image regions change on different schedules.
entries.detector_note: Compute per-tile (64x64) duplicate-run lengths instead of whole-frame; mixed cadence when the entropy of the per-tile modal run length distribution exceeds 0.8 bits and at least two tiles differ by >=2 in modal run length.
entries.notes: This per-tile version is the honest one: whole-frame cadence is destroyed by a single fast element, so whole-frame 'on 2s' claims are usually the cadence of the fastest layer.

entries.label: Attached motion streak
entries.description: Short drawn streak lines fixed to and trailing directly off a moving object, distinct from full-screen speedlines.
entries.frame_evidence: A small fan of parallel strokes anchored to the trailing edge of the moving object, extending 10-80 px.
entries.detector_note: cv2.HoughLinesP restricted to a dilated mask of the high-flow region; require >=4 segments with angular std < 12 degrees and length 10-80 px, with one endpoint within 8 px of the object contour.
entries.notes: Hair strands, whiskers, grass and rain all produce short parallel Hough segments; the endpoint-anchoring and flow-alignment tests are essential.

entries.label: Detached motion streak (free-floating dashes)
entries.description: Free-floating dashes or slashes placed in empty space around a moving subject.
entries.frame_evidence: Isolated short high-contrast strokes in otherwise flat background areas, oriented along the motion axis.
entries.detector_note: Hough segments whose both endpoints lie in regions of low local variance (flat painted background) and whose orientation is within 20 degrees of the dominant flow direction of the shot.
entries.notes: Snow, rain, sparks and film scratches are the standing false positives.

entries.label: Multiplane parallax (discrete depth layers)
entries.description: Motion parallax produced by a small number of flat layers rather than a continuous depth field.
entries.frame_evidence: The horizontal-flow histogram is multimodal with sharp separated peaks instead of a continuous spread.
entries.detector_note: Farneback flow on unique cels; histogram of horizontal velocity; count modes with prominence > 0.1 of the peak and measure the mass in the valleys between them. Discrete layers give <=4 sharp modes with valley mass < 0.1; a real 3D scene gives a continuous distribution.
entries.notes: Sparse texture in painted skies yields no flow at all and fakes a clean mode; mask out low-texture regions before histogramming.

entries.label: Absence of contact shadow / ambient occlusion
entries.description: Characters sit on a background with no darkening at the contact point, a hallmark of flat cel compositing.
entries.frame_evidence: At the foot-to-ground boundary the background luminance is unchanged within a few pixels of the character silhouette.
entries.detector_note: Sample background luminance in shells at 2-6 px and 20-40 px outside the lower subject mask boundary; flag when the ratio is > 0.97 (no darkening). Requires a subject mask and a ground contact estimate.
entries.notes: Depends entirely on a correct subject mask and on the character actually touching the ground in frame.

entries.label: Painted background vs animated foreground separation
entries.description: The background is a painting with continuous-tone texture while the foreground character is flat cel art, a visible style seam.
entries.frame_evidence: Two spatial regions with sharply different texture statistics: the background carries brush texture and gradients, the character carries flat fills and hard outlines.
entries.detector_note: Per-tile feature vector of [local colour-cluster count, Sobel-magnitude entropy, flat-area fraction, hf residual std]; the background tiles show high texture entropy with many clusters, cel tiles show <=3 clusters and >0.6 flat-area fraction. Report the bimodality of that per-tile statistic and the spatial coherence of the two classes.
entries.notes: Modern digital productions paint backgrounds flat enough to close this gap, and a heavily compressed source flattens the painting; on those the metric collapses toward zero and must not be read as 'no separation'.

entries.label: Camera pan across a still artwork
entries.description: A single painted or drawn image scrolled or tracked across, giving motion with zero animation.
entries.frame_evidence: Every frame is a translated crop of the same image: after compensating a pure translation, consecutive frames are identical in the overlap.
entries.detector_note: cv2.phaseCorrelate per frame pair gives (dx,dy); warp the second frame by -(dx,dy) and compute MAD in the valid overlap; pan-across-still when MAD < 2 LSB while |(dx,dy)| > 0.5 px, sustained over >=8 frames.
entries.notes: A locked-off shot of a real static scene under a moving camera also passes; and a pan over a still with an animated element (blinking eyes) fails the MAD test on a small area only, so report residual area rather than a binary.

entries.label: Eased pan (slow-in / slow-out on a still)
entries.description: The pan across a still accelerates and decelerates rather than moving at a constant rate.
entries.frame_evidence: The per-frame translation magnitude follows a smooth ramp up and down across the shot.
entries.detector_note: Sequence of phaseCorrelate magnitudes; fit and report the first and second derivative; eased when |accel| exceeds 0.02 px/frame^2 with a single sign change and R^2 of a smooth fit > 0.9.
entries.notes: Cadence on 2s quantises the pan into steps and corrupts the derivative; compute on unique cels or fit through the steps.

entries.label: Stepped pan (camera move quantised to 2s)
entries.description: The pan advances in discrete jumps because the camera move was rendered on the same 2s/3s cadence as the drawings.
entries.frame_evidence: Translation between frames alternates between zero and a double-size step.
entries.detector_note: phaseCorrelate magnitude series showing a period-2 or period-3 pattern of (0, 0, s) with s equal to the cadence multiple of the mean rate; report the step period and jerk.
entries.notes: Also produced by frame-rate conversion of a smooth pan; check whether the drawings themselves share the same cadence phase.

entries.label: Straight-line parallax layer boundary
entries.description: The seam between two parallax layers is a hard straight cut-out edge rather than an object silhouette.
entries.frame_evidence: The boundary between two different-velocity flow regions follows a long straight line.
entries.detector_note: Threshold the flow field into layers, extract the boundary, and fit lines (cv2.HoughLinesP on the boundary mask); flag when >50 percent of boundary pixels lie within 2 px of a fitted line longer than 20 percent of the frame width.
entries.notes: Flow segmentation is noisy at layer edges, which is exactly where this measures.

entries.label: Rim / edge light band
entries.description: A bright band hugging the silhouette edge of a character, painted or rendered.
entries.frame_evidence: A thin bright strip whose centreline is roughly parallel to and within a few pixels of the subject contour, present only on one side.
entries.detector_note: Distance transform from the subject mask boundary; report the mean luminance of the 2-8 px inner shell versus the interior; rim when the shell is >20 LSB brighter and the effect is directionally asymmetric (angular histogram of shell brightness has one lobe).
entries.notes: Requires a subject mask; on a busy background the mask is unreliable and the shell samples background pixels.

entries.label: Rotating still plate (tilt / roll on artwork)
entries.description: A drawing is rotated as a whole for a dutch-angle or spin effect.
entries.frame_evidence: Consecutive frames related by a pure rotation with near-perfect residual, plus resampling softness on diagonal edges.
entries.detector_note: Similarity transform estimate with |rotation| > 0.2 degrees per frame and warp residual MAD < 3; corner regions may go black, which is corroborating evidence.
entries.notes: Rotation estimation from ORB matches fails on low-texture painted plates.

entries.label: Rough / unclean-up key drawings left in
entries.description: Frames that keep sketchy construction lines or unclosed contours as a deliberate stylistic choice in a sakuga cut.
entries.frame_evidence: Multiple overlapping unclosed strokes per contour and un-filled or partially filled regions inside the character.
entries.detector_note: Deterministic pre-filter: high skeleton endpoint density (unclosed strokes) plus an unusually high ratio of ink pixels to filled-region area; then crop the subject at >=448 px and put the closed question to qwen2.5vl per THE CROP RULE.
entries.vlm_question: Is this drawing a rough pencil-style sketch with loose, overlapping, unfinished lines rather than a clean finished outline? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Heavy grain, dense hatching and compression noise all inflate the endpoint density pre-filter.

entries.label: Sakuga fluidity burst
entries.description: A stretch of unusually dense, fully animated motion standing out from the limited-animation baseline around it.
entries.frame_evidence: A sustained window with drawings on 1s, large per-cel change, and high deformation, surrounded by holds and 2s/3s.
entries.detector_note: Composite score per shot: unique_cel_ratio, mean per-cel changed-area fraction, mean flow magnitude on unique cels, and per-cel contour-shape change (Hu-moment distance of the subject mask); flag shots in the top decile of the episode on the combined z-score. The episode itself is the null model - without it the score means nothing.
entries.notes: This measures DENSITY OF CHANGE, not quality. A shot of noisy fire or a fast pan scores like a sakuga cut. The z-score is only meaningful against a per-episode baseline; reported without it, it is a confident number that means nothing.

entries.label: Screentone dot pattern
entries.description: A regular grid of small dots used as a shading tone, borrowed from manga.
entries.frame_evidence: A region whose local texture is a periodic dot lattice with a single spatial frequency and a fixed lattice angle.
entries.detector_note: Per-tile 2D FFT (np.fft.fft2 on 64x64 tiles, windowed); flag tiles with a pair of symmetric off-DC peaks whose magnitude exceeds 6x the local spectral median; report the peak radius (dots/px) and its angle. Confirm with skimage.feature.blob_log spacing regularity (std/mean of nearest-neighbour distance < 0.15).
entries.notes: JPEG/H.264 8x8 block artefacts, dither patterns and printed-fabric textures produce the same FFT peaks; the lattice-angle consistency across tiles is the discriminator.

entries.label: Drawn shockwave ring
entries.description: An expanding circular or elliptical ring of light/white emanating from an impact point over several frames.
entries.frame_evidence: A bright annulus whose radius grows monotonically across 3-10 frames while its centre stays fixed.
entries.detector_note: cv2.HoughCircles on the Canny map of each unique cel, or radial profiling: warpPolar around candidate centres and look for a peak whose radial index increases monotonically frame to frame; fit radius_growth_px_per_cel by least squares.
entries.notes: HoughCircles is fragile on stylised broken rings; the polar-profile method is the reliable one but needs a centre hypothesis (use the hit-flash centroid).

entries.label: Ground shockwave ring in perspective
entries.description: The expanding ring is drawn as a flattened ellipse lying on the ground plane, typical of a power-up or a landing.
entries.frame_evidence: An expanding ellipse with an aspect ratio well below 1 whose major axis is roughly horizontal and whose centre sits at the character's feet.
entries.detector_note: cv2.fitEllipse on the largest bright contour; require minor/major < 0.5, major-axis angle within 20 degrees of horizontal, and monotonic major-axis growth over >=3 unique cels.
entries.notes: Any elliptical bright object (a lamp, a pool of light) with camera motion can be mistaken for growth.

entries.label: Smear frame (single distorted drawing)
entries.description: One drawing in which a limb or object is stretched into an elongated blur-shape to bridge two poses.
entries.frame_evidence: A single unique cel containing a strongly elongated, low-detail shape aligned with the direction of motion, absent in the cels either side.
entries.detector_note: skimage.measure.regionprops on colour-quantised connected components; flag a component with eccentricity > 0.95, major/minor axis ratio > 6, solidity > 0.8 and internal edge density (Canny pixels / area) at least 40 percent below the shot median, present in exactly one unique cel.
entries.notes: Drawn objects that are genuinely long and thin (swords, poles, hair strands) score identically; the one-cel-only lifetime and the LOW internal detail are what carry the claim.

entries.label: Ghosted afterimage trail
entries.description: Semi-transparent copies of the character trail behind the current pose.
entries.frame_evidence: Faded, lower-contrast duplicates of the subject offset behind it along the motion path within a single frame.
entries.detector_note: Self-matchTemplate as in multiple-image smear but requiring the secondary peaks to have reduced local contrast (patch std < 0.7 of the primary) and lower saturation; the contrast ladder is the ghost signature.
entries.notes: Motion blur from a long shutter in live action and echo/trails compositing produce continuous rather than discrete ghosts.

entries.label: Multiple-image smear (repeated limb copies)
entries.description: A single drawing shows the same limb or object drawn several times along its arc of travel.
entries.frame_evidence: Three or more near-identical shapes repeated along a line or arc within one cel.
entries.detector_note: Template self-matching: take the highest-gradient patch in the moving region and run cv2.matchTemplate (TM_CCOEFF_NORMED) against the same frame; flag >=3 peaks above 0.75 whose centres are collinear or fit a circular arc within 5 px RMS.
entries.notes: Repeated background elements (fence posts, windows, a crowd of identical extras) trigger the same self-match; restrict to the region with high inter-cel flow.

entries.label: Speed ramp around an impact
entries.description: The effective frame rate slows into a hit and snaps back out, drawn as cadence changing across the beat.
entries.frame_evidence: Unique-cel interval lengthens monotonically for several cels then abruptly shortens within one shot.
entries.detector_note: Sequence of duplicate-run lengths within a shot; fit a monotone increase over >=3 cels followed by a drop of >=2; also check that per-cel flow magnitude falls then jumps.
entries.notes: Streaming re-encodes and frame-rate conversion synthesise fake cadence changes; verify the source fps and look for blended frames first.

entries.label: Background-replacing speedlines
entries.description: The painted background is entirely swapped for a speedline field so only the character remains rendered.
entries.frame_evidence: The character occupies a normal-detail island while the rest of the frame is a two-tone line field with no scene geometry.
entries.detector_note: Segment the frame into the largest closed high-saturation region (the character) and the remainder; require the remainder to have <=3 significant colour clusters after quantisation, a line-field detection (radial or parallel above), and near-zero low-frequency luminance structure (std of a 32x downsampled remainder < 12).
entries.notes: A character against a flat sky with rain, or against a striped wall, reproduces this; and a shot with no character at all breaks the segmentation assumption.

entries.label: Parallel speedlines
entries.description: A field of straight parallel lines indicating lateral motion or emotional intensity.
entries.frame_evidence: Many strokes sharing a single orientation with very low angular spread, spanning a large fraction of the frame.
entries.detector_note: Hough segments; require count >= 25, circular std of orientation < 6 degrees, and the covered area (dilated line mask) > 25 percent of the frame; cross-check with a single dominant peak in the FFT power spectrum orientation histogram.
entries.notes: Rain, venetian blinds, hatched shading, fence railings and screentone line-tone all match; the entry is only trustworthy combined with a background-replacement check.

entries.label: Speedlines overlaid on an intact background
entries.description: Speedlines are drawn on top of a still-readable painted background rather than replacing it.
entries.frame_evidence: A line field coexists with resolvable scene geometry and background colour variation underneath.
entries.detector_note: Detect the line field as above but require the residual after removing the line mask (cv2.inpaint over the dilated Hough mask) to retain >=6 colour clusters and low-frequency std > 20.
entries.notes: Inpainting large line masks corrupts the residual statistics on dense fields.

entries.label: Radial speedlines
entries.description: Straight lines radiating from a single vanishing point, implying rush toward or away from that point.
entries.frame_evidence: Dozens of straight strokes whose extended axes intersect within a tight cluster; density increases toward the frame edge.
entries.detector_note: cv2.HoughLinesP (rho=1, theta=pi/360, threshold~60, minLineLength=30, maxLineGap=4); least-squares intersection of all line pairs, then report the fraction of lines passing within 15 px of the best point (RANSAC over intersections). Radial when that fraction > 0.7 and line count >= 25.
entries.notes: Architectural perspective (corridors, tiled floors, ceiling beams) is the dominant false positive; require the lines to be thin, unbranched and to sit over a low-detail field.

entries.label: Only the character layer changes (background pixel-locked)
entries.description: The background is a single held plate while only the character cel changes, the canonical cel-compositing signature.
entries.frame_evidence: Between unique cels, changed pixels form one connected island; the rest of the frame is bit-identical.
entries.detector_note: Change mask between consecutive unique cels; require the unchanged region to have MAD < 1 LSB (not merely small) and the changed region to be a single connected component covering 3-40 percent of the frame.
entries.notes: Only survives on a clean source; any re-encode puts noise everywhere and the 'bit-identical' criterion has to be relaxed to a noise-floor criterion, which weakens the claim.

entries.label: Bank / stills montage (recycled still frames)
entries.description: A sequence built from held illustrations with camera moves instead of animation, or reused stock footage.
entries.frame_evidence: Several consecutive shots each containing exactly one unique drawing with only a camera transform applied.
entries.detector_note: Per shot: unique_cel_count after warping every frame back by the estimated global affine (cv2.estimateAffinePartial2D on ORB matches); if the warped-back frames collapse to one drawing, the shot is a still. Flag runs of >=3 such shots.
entries.notes: Affine estimation fails on low-texture painted skies, producing spurious 'multiple drawings'.

entries.label: Squash and stretch deformation
entries.description: The subject is non-rigidly elongated or compressed along the motion axis across adjacent cels.
entries.frame_evidence: The subject's bounding box aspect ratio changes sharply between consecutive unique cels while its area stays roughly constant.
entries.detector_note: Track the subject mask (background-subtraction on a static-camera shot, or largest moving component); report d(aspect_ratio)/d(cel) with area held within +/-25 percent; require |delta| > 0.25 over one cel step.
entries.notes: Camera zoom, rotation of an elongated object, and simple occlusion all change bbox aspect without any deformation.

entries.label: Bishie glint (tooth or eye ping)
entries.description: A single sharp cross-shaped highlight flashed on a tooth or eye, often with an audible ping.
entries.frame_evidence: A single tiny 4-point star at very high luminance on a tooth or eye, present for 1-3 frames only.
entries.detector_note: Proposal: a sparkle-template peak with area < 0.05 percent of frame, V > 250, lifetime <= 3 raw frames, located inside the mouth or eye ROI; crop that region at >=336 px and ask qwen2.5vl.
entries.vlm_question: Is there a bright star-shaped sparkle flash on this character's tooth or eye? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Needs an accurate face ROI on a stylised face, which is the weak link; small VLMs also confabulate sparkles on any bright highlight.

entries.label: Flat blush patch (no lines)
entries.description: A soft or flat pink oval on each cheek without hatch lines.
entries.frame_evidence: Two symmetric warm-hued patches on the cheeks whose hue is shifted toward red relative to surrounding skin.
entries.detector_note: Inside the face ROI, compute the hue/saturation delta of cheek-region pixels versus the forehead skin sample; blush when saturation rises > 0.12 and hue shifts toward red by > 6 degrees in two roughly symmetric regions.
entries.notes: Depends on a face ROI; warm side-lighting on the cheek reproduces the whole statistic, and it fires on any character with rosy cheek design permanently.

entries.label: Blush lines (hatched cheek marks)
entries.description: Two or three short parallel strokes on each cheek denoting embarrassment.
entries.frame_evidence: Small groups of 2-4 short parallel dark or red strokes symmetrically placed on both cheeks.
entries.detector_note: Proposal: two symmetric clusters of >=2 short parallel Hough segments (length 4-20 px) inside the face ROI at cheek height; crop face at >=336 px, ask qwen2.5vl.
entries.vlm_question: Does this character have short parallel blush lines drawn on their cheeks? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Whiskers, scars, freckle rows and glasses frames land in the same ROI.

entries.label: Chibi / super-deformed switch
entries.description: The character is redrawn with a huge head and tiny body for a comedic beat, then reverts.
entries.frame_evidence: Within one shot, the head-to-body height ratio jumps from roughly 1:6 to 1:2 or 1:3 in a single cel step.
entries.detector_note: Proposal: subject-mask bbox aspect changes sharply while the detected face bbox area as a fraction of the subject bbox area more than doubles in one cel step; crop the whole figure at >=448 px and ask qwen2.5vl. mediapipe pose can supply head/torso proportion when it latches but must not be trusted alone on stylised art.
entries.vlm_question: Is this character drawn in a simplified super-deformed style with a very large head and a tiny body? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: A cut to a close-up produces the same face-to-subject area jump; require the change to happen WITHIN a shot with no shot boundary.

entries.label: Gloom aura cloud (depression cloud)
entries.description: A dark scribbled or smoky mass hanging over a character to signal misery.
entries.frame_evidence: A dark low-saturation textured region directly above or around the head, boiling in shape across cels.
entries.detector_note: Proposal: dark region (luma < 0.4 of frame median) above the head ROI with high per-cel Hu-moment shape change; crop the head-plus-above region at >=384 px and ask qwen2.5vl.
entries.vlm_question: Is there a dark gloomy cloud or shadow hovering over this character's head? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Night skies, dark interiors and actual smoke all satisfy the proposal.

entries.label: Drool
entries.description: A line of saliva from the mouth corner, for hunger, lust or sleep.
entries.frame_evidence: A thin light streak descending from a mouth corner.
entries.detector_note: Proposal: a thin low-saturation elongated component with its top endpoint at the mouth ROI corner; crop the lower face at >=336 px and ask qwen2.5vl.
entries.vlm_question: Is saliva or drool coming from the corner of this character's mouth? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Chin highlights and blood streaks look the same to the proposal stage.

entries.label: Floating ellipsis (awkward silence dots)
entries.description: Three dots drawn near a character to mark speechlessness.
entries.frame_evidence: Three equally spaced small dark dots in a horizontal row in empty space near the head.
entries.detector_note: Proposal: exactly 3 similar-sized blobs, collinear within 2 px, evenly spaced within 15 percent, in a flat background region near the head; crop at >=336 px and ask qwen2.5vl (never moondream - this is text-shaped).
entries.vlm_question: Are there three dots drawn in the air near this character? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Background patterns (tiles, buttons, rivets) satisfy the geometric proposal constantly; and moondream must not be used.

entries.label: Floating exclamation mark
entries.description: A large exclamation mark drawn beside or above the head to mark surprise or realisation.
entries.frame_evidence: A bold vertical bar with a separate dot beneath it, appearing suddenly near the head.
entries.detector_note: Proposal: a new component with a tall thin main body plus a small detached blob directly below, near the head ROI; crop with context at >=336 px and ask qwen2.5vl - and do NOT route this to moondream, which confabulates on anything text-shaped.
entries.vlm_question: Is there a large exclamation mark symbol drawn in the air near this character? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: moondream CANNOT be asked this - it confabulates text. Even qwen2.5vl confuses exclamation and question marks at small crop sizes.

entries.label: Eyes replaced by a glyph (X, hearts, stars, blank)
entries.description: Both eyes are swapped for a symbol - crosses for unconscious, hearts for love, stars for excitement, blank white for shock.
entries.frame_evidence: Both eye regions contain the same non-eye shape, changed within one cel from normal eyes.
entries.detector_note: Proposal: both eye ROIs change simultaneously in one cel step and become near-identical to each other (patch cross-correlation > 0.8 after mirroring); crop both eyes together at >=336 px and ask qwen2.5vl.
entries.vlm_question: Are this character's eyes drawn as symbols such as X shapes, hearts, or stars instead of normal eyes? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: A small VLM will often name whichever symbol was mentioned in the question; ask the yes/no form only and never let it enumerate.

entries.label: Protruding fang
entries.description: A single pointed tooth drawn over the lip as a character or mood marker.
entries.frame_evidence: A small white triangle overlapping the lower or upper lip line.
entries.detector_note: Crop the mouth ROI at >=288 px and ask qwen2.5vl; the deterministic stage can only supply the ROI.
entries.vlm_question: Does this character have a single pointed fang tooth visible over the lip? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Character-design constant rather than an event; log it per-frame but expect it to be constant across a character's shots.

entries.label: Stamped facial marker (bandage, plaster, forehead mark)
entries.description: A flat graphic stuck on the face - a crossed plaster, a bandage, a sect mark - drawn as a stamp rather than modelled.
entries.frame_evidence: A small flat high-contrast graphic on the face whose shape does not deform with the face across cels.
entries.detector_note: Proposal: a small component inside the face ROI with a stable shape (Hu-moment distance across cels near zero) despite head turning; crop the face at >=336 px and ask qwen2.5vl.
entries.vlm_question: Is there a bandage, plaster, or drawn mark stuck on this character's face? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Shape stability under head rotation is itself the interesting finding (the marker does not follow perspective), but head-turn detection on drawn faces is unreliable.

entries.label: Floating hearts
entries.description: Heart glyphs floating around a character to signal love or attraction.
entries.frame_evidence: Small pink or red heart shapes, often multiple and drifting upward across cels.
entries.detector_note: Proposal: small warm-hued components with a concave top notch (two convexity defects at the top of the contour, cv2.convexityDefects) drifting upward; crop the cluster at >=336 px and ask qwen2.5vl.
entries.vlm_question: Are there heart shapes drawn floating in this image? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Heart-patterned clothing and props fire the proposal; the drift requirement removes most static cases.

entries.label: Cartoon star-burst impact glyph
entries.description: A stylised jagged starburst stamped at the point of a comedic hit.
entries.frame_evidence: A jagged closed polygon with many alternating convex/concave vertices, stamped for 1-4 frames at the contact point.
entries.detector_note: Contour analysis of a newly appearing component: count convexity defects (cv2.convexityDefects) >= 6 with alternating radial extrema in the polar profile, lifetime <= 4 frames.
entries.notes: Explosions and drawn fire have similar jagged contours; the short stamped lifetime is the discriminator.

entries.label: Drawn swoosh arc
entries.description: A crescent or ribbon arc drawn along the path of a swung weapon or limb.
entries.frame_evidence: A tapering crescent band following a circular arc, present for 1-3 cels around the swing.
entries.detector_note: Fit a circle to the skeleton of a newly appearing elongated component (least-squares circle fit, residual < 3 px) and require the width to taper from one end to the other by > 50 percent; lifetime 1-3 unique cels.
entries.notes: Curved props (blades, ribbons, hoops) fit a circle equally well; the taper and the short lifetime carry the claim.

entries.label: Triangle / cat mouth stylisation
entries.description: The mouth is drawn as a simple triangle, a 3-shape (cat mouth) or a wavy line as an emotional shorthand.
entries.frame_evidence: The mouth region is a small geometric glyph rather than a rendered mouth.
entries.detector_note: Crop the mouth ROI at >=288 px and ask qwen2.5vl; no reliable deterministic proposal exists because the mouth ROI is always occupied by something mouth-shaped.
entries.vlm_question: Is this character's mouth drawn as a simple geometric shape such as a triangle or a rounded W, rather than a normal mouth? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Highly design-dependent; a series whose default mouth is already a simple shape makes this fire on every frame.

entries.label: Nosebleed
entries.description: A stream of red from one or both nostrils, a comedic arousal/shock gag.
entries.frame_evidence: A narrow saturated red streak running downward from the nose region, absent in earlier cels.
entries.detector_note: Proposal: an elongated vertical component with hue in 340-10 degrees and S > 0.6 whose top endpoint is inside the face ROI at nose height; crop the face at >=384 px and ask qwen2.5vl.
entries.vlm_question: Is blood running from this character's nose? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Genuine injury blood, red hair strands falling across the face, and red mouth interiors are the false positives; the VLM cannot separate a comedic nosebleed from a real one.

entries.label: Drawn onomatopoeia / sound-effect lettering
entries.description: Large stylised Japanese (or Latin) sound-effect lettering composited into the frame.
entries.frame_evidence: Large high-contrast glyph shapes with stroke structure, placed over the artwork and often skewed or motion-styled.
entries.detector_note: Needs a text/glyph detector we do not have installed (no rapidocr, no trained scene-text model). A deterministic pre-filter can propose regions - dense stroke clusters with high branch-point density and a consistent stroke width - but confirming that a region IS lettering rather than a drawn effect requires the missing model.
entries.notes: Logged as a known blind spot: rapidocr is NOT installed, and moondream cannot be asked about text. qwen2.5vl can sometimes answer, but its reading of stylised vertical kana is unreliable enough that we do not claim it.

entries.label: Floating question mark
entries.description: A question mark drawn near the head to mark confusion.
entries.frame_evidence: A hooked curved glyph with a detached dot below, appearing suddenly near the head.
entries.detector_note: Same proposal as the exclamation mark but with a curved (non-straight) skeleton in the upper part; crop at >=336 px and ask qwen2.5vl only.
entries.vlm_question: Is there a question mark symbol drawn in the air near this character? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: moondream must not be used here. Confusion with exclamation marks is the dominant error; both entries can fire on the same glyph and the analyzer should report the pair, not pick one.

entries.label: Shadowed eyes (despair / menace)
entries.description: The upper face is blacked out with only the eyes visible or blanked, signalling despair, rage or menace.
entries.frame_evidence: A dark band covering the eye region with a hard horizontal or hair-shaped lower boundary, while the rest of the face keeps normal skin tone.
entries.detector_note: Proposal: mean luminance of the eye-band ROI drops > 45 percent versus the cheek/chin ROI within one cel step, with a hard boundary (transition < 3 px); crop the face at >=384 px and ask qwen2.5vl.
entries.vlm_question: Are this character's eyes hidden in a dark shadow across the upper part of the face? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: A hat brim, hair falling forward, and ordinary top-lit shadow are indistinguishable without the sudden onset.

entries.label: Snot bubble (asleep)
entries.description: A bubble at the nose that inflates and deflates to indicate sleep.
entries.frame_evidence: A translucent circle at the nostril whose radius oscillates over a cycle of several cels.
entries.detector_note: Proposal: a near-circular light component at the nose ROI whose radius oscillates with period 4-20 cels; crop the face at >=336 px and ask qwen2.5vl.
entries.vlm_question: Is there a round bubble coming from this character's nose? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Rare enough that a positive is more likely a false one; treat a lone hit as low confidence.

entries.label: Sparkle / star twinkle
entries.description: Four-pointed or star-shaped sparkle glyphs scattered around a subject to signal beauty, delight or preciousness.
entries.frame_evidence: Small bright four-pointed star shapes with thin tapering arms, often at several scales, twinkling on and off across cels.
entries.detector_note: Match a bank of rotated 4-point star templates via cv2.matchTemplate at 3 scales on the bright-thin top-hat mask; require peaks > 0.7 and a twinkling lifetime of 1-4 cels; report count and mean scale.
entries.notes: Real lens star-filters, specular glints on metal and starfields match the template; template matching is scale/rotation limited so hand-drawn irregular sparkles are missed.

entries.label: Drawn speech or thought bubble
entries.description: A manga-style balloon composited into the animation for a gag or aside.
entries.frame_evidence: A closed white rounded shape with a black outline and a tail pointing at a character.
entries.detector_note: Proposal: a large near-white closed contour with high solidity, a dark outline, and a protruding narrow tail; crop with context at >=384 px and ask qwen2.5vl.
entries.vlm_question: Is there a comic-style speech or thought bubble drawn in this image? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: White props (paper, clouds, signs) match the proposal; do not ask about the bubble's TEXT.

entries.label: Spiral eyes (dazed)
entries.description: Eyes drawn as spirals to indicate dizziness or being knocked out.
entries.frame_evidence: Concentric spiral line patterns in place of both irises.
entries.detector_note: Proposal: warpPolar around each eye ROI centre, look for a monotonic diagonal ridge in the polar image (the signature of a spiral) via Hough on the polar map; then crop both eyes at >=336 px and ask qwen2.5vl.
entries.vlm_question: Are this character's eyes drawn as spirals or swirls instead of normal eyes? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Concentric-ring iris designs and patterned contact lenses give the same polar ridge; the eye ROI is unreliable on stylised faces.

entries.label: Steam / smoke from the head or ears
entries.description: Puffs of steam venting from the head to indicate rage, embarrassment or overheating.
entries.frame_evidence: Soft white curling puffs rising from the ears or top of the head, changing shape every cel.
entries.detector_note: Proposal: low-saturation light components above the head ROI with high contour-shape change between cels (Hu-moment distance) and upward centroid drift; crop the head-plus-above region at >=384 px and ask qwen2.5vl.
entries.vlm_question: Is steam or smoke rising from this character's head or ears? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Breath vapour in a cold scene, cigarette smoke and background clouds are the false positives.

entries.label: Sweat drop (anxiety bead)
entries.description: A single oversized teardrop shape on the head or temple signalling embarrassment or nervousness.
entries.frame_evidence: One large light-blue or white teardrop with a hard outline, usually on the side of the head, appearing within one cel.
entries.detector_note: Propose a crop: new connected component appearing in one cel step, area 0.2-4 percent of frame, located within 1.5 head-widths of the face ROI, with high circularity at one end and a taper at the other; crop it with 40 percent context at >=336 px and ask qwen2.5vl (THE CROP RULE - do NOT ask on the full frame).
entries.vlm_question: Is there a large cartoon sweat drop or teardrop shape drawn on or next to this character's head? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Real drawn tears, water droplets, and hair highlights produce the same proposal; the VLM confuses a sweat drop with a tear when the drop is under the eye.

entries.label: Multiple sweat beads (panic)
entries.description: Several small beads on the forehead indicating stress, distinct from the single giant anxiety drop.
entries.frame_evidence: 3+ small light ovals clustered on the upper face, appearing together.
entries.detector_note: Proposal: >=3 blobs of area < 0.3 percent each inside the upper-face ROI appearing in one cel step; single crop of the forehead region at >=336 px to qwen2.5vl.
entries.vlm_question: Are there several small sweat droplets drawn on this character's forehead or face? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Skin highlights and freckles are the standing false positives.

entries.label: Single realistic tear
entries.description: One small drawn tear rolling down the cheek in a dramatic (non-comedic) register.
entries.frame_evidence: A single small bright bead below one eye that translates downward across cels.
entries.detector_note: Proposal: a small bright blob below an eye ROI whose centroid moves downward monotonically over >=2 unique cels; crop the cheek at >=336 px and ask qwen2.5vl.
entries.vlm_question: Is there a single tear on this character's cheek below the eye? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Sweat, rain, blood and a cheek highlight all present the same blob; on a rainy shot this entry is meaningless.

entries.label: Comedic tear fountain / waterfall tears
entries.description: Exaggerated jets of tears streaming from the eyes as a comedy gag.
entries.frame_evidence: Two wide light-blue streams issuing from the eyes, far larger than realistic tears.
entries.detector_note: Proposal: two elongated light-blue (hue 180-220) components originating at the eye ROIs, each wider than 3 px and longer than 20 percent of face height; crop the face at >=384 px and ask qwen2.5vl.
entries.vlm_question: Are exaggerated cartoon tears streaming from this character's eyes? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Cannot be separated from realistic crying by the VLM question as phrased; the size metrics carry that distinction, not the answer.

entries.label: Cross-popping vein (anger mark)
entries.description: The stylised cross-shaped bulging-vein mark used for anger.
entries.frame_evidence: A small red or dark cross/hash glyph with four radiating arms stamped on the forehead, fist or frame.
entries.detector_note: Proposal: newly appearing small component with 4-fold rotational symmetry (correlate the patch with itself rotated 90 degrees, score > 0.8) and hue in the red band; crop at >=336 px with context and ask qwen2.5vl.
entries.vlm_question: Is there a small cross-shaped or X-shaped anger vein symbol drawn on this character or beside their head? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Plus signs, crosses on clothing, window frames and first-aid symbols all pass the symmetry proposal.

entries.label: 3-frame walk cycle
entries.description: A walk built from a tiny number of repeating drawings, so the same poses recur exactly.
entries.frame_evidence: Unique cels within the shot cluster into 3-4 exact repeats: cel N is pixel-near-identical to cel N+3.
entries.detector_note: Build the pairwise MAD matrix between all unique cels of the shot (after phaseCorrelate translation compensation to remove the character's forward travel); a short cycle shows a strong off-diagonal band at lag k; report k as cycle_len_cels and the mean MAD on that band.
entries.notes: Only works when the character is composited over a scrolling or static background that can be compensated; if the character moves within the frame with a changing background, the MAD matrix is dominated by the background.

entries.label: Third tone / specular highlight added
entries.description: A brighter third tone is painted on top of base and shadow, typical of feature-grade or modern TV shading.
entries.frame_evidence: A region carries three flat luminance plateaus, the brightest occupying a small area near the light direction.
entries.detector_note: Same region quantisation as two_tone_flat_fill but requiring exactly three qualifying clusters with the brightest holding 2-15 percent of region area.
entries.notes: Rim light and bloom create bright bands that quantise as a third tone without being painted as one.

entries.label: Two-tone flat fill per material region
entries.description: Each material is painted in exactly two colours: base and shadow, with no third tone.
entries.frame_evidence: Colour-quantising the character yields close to two clusters per contiguous material region, each perfectly flat.
entries.detector_note: K-means-free quantisation via np.unique on 5-bit-per-channel values inside each region; count clusters holding >5 percent of region area and measure within-cluster std (< 3 LSB when flat).
entries.notes: Grain, banding and chroma noise fragment flat fills into many quantisation bins; denoise (cv2.bilateralFilter) before counting.

entries.label: Unique-cel index map (base measurement)
entries.description: The mapping from raw frame indices to distinct drawings, the prerequisite for every temporal metric in this domain.
entries.frame_evidence: Consecutive raw frames that are pixel-identical (or within noise) belong to one drawing; the boundaries are where the drawing changes.
entries.detector_note: Downscale to 1/4, convert to grey, compute mean abs diff between consecutive frames; a frame is a duplicate when MAD < tau where tau is set from the per-shot noise floor (median MAD of the lowest decile) times 3. Emit the unique-cel index array and duplicate-run lengths. EVERY other temporal detector consumes this, never raw indices.
entries.notes: Re-encoded sources add per-frame noise that can make true duplicates look unique; frame-blended frame-rate conversion destroys duplicates entirely and this detector must report low confidence when blended frames are found.

entries.label: Vertical dread / gloom lines
entries.description: Vertical hatch lines or a dark vertical wash dropped over a character to signal dread, shame or despair.
entries.frame_evidence: A field of near-vertical strokes or a vertically graded dark overlay confined to the upper body region, with the frame otherwise unchanged.
entries.detector_note: Orientation histogram from structure_tensor restricted to the subject ROI; require dominant orientation within 10 degrees of vertical, coherence > 0.6, and mean luminance inside the ROI dropping >15 percent versus the previous unique cel while the background luminance is unchanged.
entries.notes: Rain, bars, curtains and vertical architecture inside the ROI all fire it.

entries.label: Drawn whip-pan blur plate
entries.description: A deliberately smeared horizontal blur plate used to cover a fast pan or a cut.
entries.frame_evidence: 1-6 frames of extreme unidirectional blur with almost no vertical detail loss.
entries.detector_note: Anisotropy of the gradient: mean |Sobel_x| divided by mean |Sobel_y| far from 1 (>3 or <0.33) plus an FFT power spectrum collapsed onto one axis; lasting <=6 frames between two sharp shots.
entries.notes: Real motion-blurred whip pans in live action are identical by this measure; the drawn version is only distinguishable by whether the blur is CONSTANT across depth, which needs a layer estimate.

entries.label: Digital zoom / push-in on a still
entries.description: A scale ramp applied to a single drawing, softening as it enlarges.
entries.frame_evidence: Consecutive frames related by a pure scale about a fixed centre, with rising blur as scale increases.
entries.detector_note: cv2.estimateAffinePartial2D between consecutive frames restricted to similarity; flag when the scale term departs from 1 by >0.002 per frame with rotation ~0 and the warped residual MAD < 3; also track the falling Laplacian variance as evidence of resampling softness.
entries.notes: A real dolly-in changes parallax; a zoom does not - the warp residual is what separates them.

entries.label: Force / weight of an action
entries.description: How hard a strike lands or how heavy a lifted object is, in physical units.
entries.frame_evidence: There is no frame evidence that yields Newtons or kilograms; apparent effort is a rendering choice.
entries.detector_note: No installed method estimates force, mass or ground reaction. Any number would be invented. Logged as a permanent blind spot.
entries.notes: Proxies exist (deceleration, recoil distance, absorption depth) and are emitted by their own entries, but they must never be relabelled as force.

entries.label: Intent behind an action
entries.description: Whether an action is a feint, an accident, a threat or play - the meaning rather than the movement.
entries.frame_evidence: No frame-level evidence separates a feint from a committed strike that missed.
entries.detector_note: Requires narrative context beyond the frame window; a VLM asked this confabulates a confident story, so no vlm question is offered.
entries.notes: Deliberately unsupported. Asking a small VLM for intent is the classic overclaim this taxonomy exists to prevent.

entries.label: Action onset / offset boundary
entries.description: The frame indices where a discrete gross-motor act starts and ends, needed so every other entry can report a time span.
entries.frame_evidence: Motion energy rises out of the idle floor and later returns to it.
entries.detector_note: Change-point detection on the smoothed camera-compensated motion-energy series: threshold at idle_median + 3*MAD, require a minimum run of 2 unique cels, emit onset/offset pairs.
entries.notes: Shot boundaries must be removed first or every cut becomes a false onset.

entries.label: Braced aiming stance
entries.description: A held two-handed aiming posture: both hands together forward, shoulders squared or bladed, low motion.
entries.frame_evidence: Several cels with the wrists close together at chest/eye height, arms extended along a common axis, the whole body still.
entries.detector_note: Wrist-to-wrist distance below 0.4 shoulder widths, both elbow angles above 130 degrees, wrists forward of the shoulder line, and low motion energy for >=3 unique cels.
