entries.notes: mediapipe pose is trained on photographic humans; on stylised 2D art, chibi proportions, masks, heavy occlusion or non-human anatomy it silently returns a low-visibility or hallucinated skeleton - gate every landmark metric on body_action.pose_landmark_confidence_null.

entries.label: Sprint
entries.description: Maximal-effort running: high knee lift, large flight fraction, extreme arm drive, strong forward lean.
entries.frame_evidence: The knee rises above hip height, the trailing heel kicks toward the buttock, and flight frames outnumber contact frames.
entries.detector_note: run_cycle conditions plus knee y above hip y at peak (landmark 25/26 vs 23/24), flight_fraction > 0.35 and normalised stride above the shot's run baseline.
entries.notes: mediapipe pose is trained on photographic humans; on stylised 2D art, chibi proportions, masks, heavy occlusion or non-human anatomy it silently returns a low-visibility or hallucinated skeleton - gate every landmark metric on body_action.pose_landmark_confidence_null. Cannot distinguish sprint from a fast stylised run cycle played at a low frame rate; thresholds are relative to the shot, not absolute.

entries.label: Stagger
entries.description: Loss of postural control producing uneven, corrective steps while the com is outside the support base.
entries.frame_evidence: Irregular quick steps with a large torso lean and no gait periodicity.
entries.detector_note: com projected outside the support foot x-range for several consecutive unique cels with irregular step intervals (high cadence coefficient of variation) and a high torso_lean_deg.
entries.notes: mediapipe pose is trained on photographic humans; on stylised 2D art, chibi proportions, masks, heavy occlusion or non-human anatomy it silently returns a low-visibility or hallucinated skeleton - gate every landmark metric on body_action.pose_landmark_confidence_null. Needs several steps; a two-step stagger is statistically indistinguishable from a change of direction.

entries.label: Standing up
entries.description: The transition from seated, kneeling or prone to standing, driven by leg extension and a forward-then-up com path.
entries.frame_evidence: The com moves forward over the feet and then rises while knee angles open.
entries.detector_note: com_y rise of more than 20 percent of leg length with knee_angle opening past 150 degrees, ending with both contact flags true and a vertical torso.
entries.notes: mediapipe pose is trained on photographic humans; on stylised 2D art, chibi proportions, masks, heavy occlusion or non-human anatomy it silently returns a low-visibility or hallucinated skeleton - gate every landmark metric on body_action.pose_landmark_confidence_null.

entries.label: Held pose (no gross motion)
entries.description: A deliberate held frame or pose where the body does not move, which anime uses constantly and which every temporal metric must treat as a valid state rather than a failure.
entries.frame_evidence: A run of consecutive unique cels with a near-identical figure and no landmark displacement beyond the jitter floor.
entries.detector_note: Consecutive unique cels whose figure-ROI mean |absdiff| stays below the per-shot duplicate threshold; report run length in source frames and in unique cels.
entries.notes: Must be computed on the figure ROI, not the full frame: a held character over a panning background is not a duplicate frame but IS a held pose.

entries.label: Stomp / axe kick down
entries.description: A downward-driving foot strike onto a low target or the ground.
entries.frame_evidence: The foot travels rapidly downward and stops abruptly, often with a ground-impact accent on the same cel.
entries.detector_note: Ankle velocity dominated by the downward component, terminating in a velocity collapse coincident with an impact_frame_index.
entries.notes: mediapipe pose is trained on photographic humans; on stylised 2D art, chibi proportions, masks, heavy occlusion or non-human anatomy it silently returns a low-visibility or hallucinated skeleton - gate every landmark metric on body_action.pose_landmark_confidence_null.

entries.label: Stretch
entries.description: Slow extension of the limbs and spine to their range limits, held briefly.
entries.frame_evidence: The arms extend fully overhead or outward and the torso arches, with a slow rate and a short hold.
entries.detector_note: Both elbow angles above 160 degrees with wrists above the head and a low peak angular velocity (below the gesture threshold), plus a hold of >=2 unique cels at the extreme.
entries.notes: mediapipe pose is trained on photographic humans; on stylised 2D art, chibi proportions, masks, heavy occlusion or non-human anatomy it silently returns a low-visibility or hallucinated skeleton - gate every landmark metric on body_action.pose_landmark_confidence_null.

entries.label: Stride length
entries.description: Distance covered per step normalised by body size, separating a shuffle from a stride.
entries.frame_evidence: The gap between the two ankles at maximum extension, measured against the character's own leg length.
entries.detector_note: max |p27 - p28| over a cycle divided by hip-to-ankle length; also com displacement per cycle in torso-lengths.
entries.notes: mediapipe pose is trained on photographic humans; on stylised 2D art, chibi proportions, masks, heavy occlusion or non-human anatomy it silently returns a low-visibility or hallucinated skeleton - gate every landmark metric on body_action.pose_landmark_confidence_null. Image-plane only: a walk toward camera has a near-zero apparent stride.

entries.label: Strike flurry / combo rate
entries.description: Number of distinct strikes per second within a burst, the marker of a combo sequence.
entries.frame_evidence: Repeated extension-retraction cycles of the arms with alternating sides in rapid succession.
entries.detector_note: scipy.signal.find_peaks on the combined wrist_tip_speed series with a minimum separation of 2 unique cels; strikes per second on unique-cel timestamps, plus a left/right alternation flag.
entries.notes: mediapipe pose is trained on photographic humans; on stylised 2D art, chibi proportions, masks, heavy occlusion or non-human anatomy it silently returns a low-visibility or hallucinated skeleton - gate every landmark metric on body_action.pose_landmark_confidence_null. All temporal derivatives are computed on UNIQUE-CEL indices (dedupe by mean |absdiff| < 0.5/255 against the previous frame); dt is the real gap between unique cels, never 1/fps. On 2s/3s animation a very fast flurry may have fewer unique drawings than strikes, so the count undercounts by construction - report unique_cels_per_s alongside.

entries.label: Strike contact (upper body)
entries.description: The frame at which a hand, fist or elbow actually meets a target.
entries.frame_evidence: The striking hand coincides with a second figure or object on the impact cel and its motion is arrested there.
entries.detector_note: Crop 1.5 torso-widths around the striking wrist at the impact_frame_index and ask the VLM; corroborate with wrist deceleration and a motion-energy spike at that location.
entries.vlm_question: Is the fist or hand touching another person in this image? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: THE CROP RULE. Impact flashes, speed lines and smear frequently occlude the actual contact point; a near-miss framed to look like a hit is intentionally ambiguous.

entries.label: Swimming stroke
entries.description: Locomotion in water with cyclic arm recovery and leg kick, body roughly horizontal and partly occluded by the surface.
entries.frame_evidence: Arms cycle over or under a waterline that repeatedly cuts the body, with splash accents at entry.
entries.detector_note: VLM on the figure crop for the act; body_action.locomotion_cycle_period for the stroke rate; the waterline hides landmarks so pose is not trusted.
entries.vlm_question: Is the person swimming in water in this image? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Water occlusion, splash and refraction defeat mediapipe; treat any landmark output here as unreliable.

entries.label: Tackle / body charge
entries.description: One figure driving its whole mass into another, ending in combined motion or a takedown.
entries.frame_evidence: A running figure lowers its shoulder and the two silhouettes merge into one blob that then travels together.
entries.detector_note: Track two silhouette components converging (centroid distance collapsing to zero) and merging into a single connected component whose combined centroid keeps the aggressor's velocity direction.
entries.notes: Silhouette merging also happens on simple occlusion crossing; require the pre-merge approach velocity and the post-merge shared motion.

entries.label: Tail swing / lash
entries.description: Motion of a trailing appendage, often the largest single moving element on a creature.
entries.frame_evidence: A long thin protrusion sweeps across frame with a different phase from the body.
entries.detector_note: Ask the VLM on a crop of the moving protrusion; corroborate with a high-aspect connected component in the motion mask whose motion phase lags the body centroid.
entries.vlm_question: Is there an animal or creature tail visible in this image? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: No part-segmentation model is installed, so tail-versus-rope-versus-hair cannot be resolved deterministically.

entries.label: Throw an object
entries.description: Accelerating an object and releasing it, with a full-body kinetic chain and a follow-through.
entries.frame_evidence: The arm whips forward over the shoulder, an object separates from the hand on one cel and continues on its own arc.
entries.detector_note: Peak wrist_tip_speed with torso_axial_rotation and a step, followed by a small foreground component that continues along the wrist's velocity vector after the wrist decelerates.
entries.notes: mediapipe pose is trained on photographic humans; on stylised 2D art, chibi proportions, masks, heavy occlusion or non-human anatomy it silently returns a low-visibility or hallucinated skeleton - gate every landmark metric on body_action.pose_landmark_confidence_null. The projectile is often only a few pixels or is drawn as a speed-line; the separation test then fails and only the arm motion is reported.

entries.label: Throw / takedown of a person
entries.description: One figure lifting, rotating and driving another to the ground.
entries.frame_evidence: The two overlap, one silhouette rotates through a large angle relative to the other, and it ends at ground level.
entries.detector_note: Confirm with the VLM on a crop of the pair; corroborate with the thrown silhouette's regionprops orientation unwrapping and its centroid dropping to the shot's ground baseline.
entries.vlm_question: Is one person throwing or slamming another person down to the ground? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Requires both figures to be separable in the mask at the start and end; mid-throw they are one blob.

entries.label: Tiptoe / sneak walk
entries.description: Slow crouched locomotion on the balls of the feet with exaggerated foot placement.
entries.frame_evidence: Heels stay above toes throughout stance, knees stay bent, com is lowered and cadence is low.
entries.detector_note: Contact detected on foot_index (31/32) while heel (29/30) stays higher for the whole stance, com_y depressed versus the shot standing baseline, cadence below 1 step/s.
entries.notes: mediapipe pose is trained on photographic humans; on stylised 2D art, chibi proportions, masks, heavy occlusion or non-human anatomy it silently returns a low-visibility or hallucinated skeleton - gate every landmark metric on body_action.pose_landmark_confidence_null. Footwear and low resolution destroy the heel/toe distinction; on 2D, feet are often drawn without heel definition.

entries.label: Torso axial rotation (twist)
entries.description: Rotation of the shoulder girdle relative to the pelvis about the spine, the engine of a punch, a throw and a roundhouse kick.
entries.frame_evidence: Shoulder width foreshortens or the shoulder line and hip line diverge in angle within a few frames.
entries.detector_note: shoulder_line_angle(11,12) minus hip_line_angle(23,24); plus foreshortening ratio (|x11-x12| / torso_length) tracked against its per-shot maximum as a yaw proxy.
entries.notes: mediapipe pose is trained on photographic humans; on stylised 2D art, chibi proportions, masks, heavy occlusion or non-human anatomy it silently returns a low-visibility or hallucinated skeleton - gate every landmark metric on body_action.pose_landmark_confidence_null. The foreshortening proxy conflates yaw with distance-to-camera changes; mediapipe world landmarks (z) are too noisy on stylised art to use instead.

entries.label: Torso forward/back lean
entries.description: Angle of the trunk away from vertical in the image plane, present in every acceleration, brace, bow and stagger.
entries.frame_evidence: The shoulder-midpoint to hip-midpoint line tilts off the frame vertical.
entries.detector_note: angle between vector (mid_shoulder(11,12) - mid_hip(23,24)) and the image vertical, via numpy.arctan2; report signed degrees.
entries.notes: mediapipe pose is trained on photographic humans; on stylised 2D art, chibi proportions, masks, heavy occlusion or non-human anatomy it silently returns a low-visibility or hallucinated skeleton - gate every landmark metric on body_action.pose_landmark_confidence_null. Cannot separate lean from a camera roll unless camera roll is estimated first.

entries.label: Trip / stumble
entries.description: A gait interruption where a foot is arrested and the upper body continues, followed by a recovery or a fall.
entries.frame_evidence: One foot stops abruptly mid-swing while the torso pitches forward past its support.
entries.detector_note: Detect a swing-phase foot whose velocity collapses to zero off-schedule, followed within 3 unique cels by torso_lean_deg exceeding the gait maximum and the com passing outside the support foot's x.
entries.notes: mediapipe pose is trained on photographic humans; on stylised 2D art, chibi proportions, masks, heavy occlusion or non-human anatomy it silently returns a low-visibility or hallucinated skeleton - gate every landmark metric on body_action.pose_landmark_confidence_null. The obstacle itself is not detected (no object detector), so a trip and a deliberate lunge look similar.

entries.label: Vault / hurdle over an obstacle
entries.description: Passing over an obstacle with a hand plant or a leg swing rather than a plain jump.
entries.frame_evidence: A hand or foot briefly plants on an object at mid-height while the com arcs over it.
entries.detector_note: VLM on a crop spanning the figure and the obstacle; corroborate with a com_y arc plus a short wrist-velocity-zero interval (the plant).
entries.vlm_question: Is the person jumping or climbing over an object such as a wall, railing or table? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Requires the obstacle to be in the crop; no object detector is installed to find it automatically.

entries.label: Walk
entries.description: Bipedal locomotion with at least one foot always in contact, alternating support, moderate cadence.
entries.frame_evidence: Legs scissor through contact / down / passing / up poses with no frame where both feet are airborne.
entries.detector_note: Require alternating body_action.foot_ground_contact with a double-support overlap > 0 and com_x_velocity below the run threshold; cycle period from scipy.signal.correlate autocorrelation of the ankle-separation series.
entries.notes: mediapipe pose is trained on photographic humans; on stylised 2D art, chibi proportions, masks, heavy occlusion or non-human anatomy it silently returns a low-visibility or hallucinated skeleton - gate every landmark metric on body_action.pose_landmark_confidence_null. On anime the deterministic sibling body_action.locomotion_cycle_period is the fallback.

entries.label: Weapon clash / block
entries.description: Two implements meeting, arresting both motions at a point, usually with a spark or flash accent.
entries.frame_evidence: Two long shapes intersect on one cel and both stop, with a bright flash at the crossing point.
entries.detector_note: Detect two tracked lines whose intersection coincides with a motion arrest and a luminance spike, then confirm with a VLM crop centred on the intersection.
entries.vlm_question: Are two weapons touching or crossing each other in this image? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: THE CROP RULE. Impact flashes routinely blow out the contact region so the weapons themselves are unreadable on the very frame that matters - sample the cel before and after too.

entries.label: Draw or sheathe a weapon
entries.description: Removing an implement from or returning it to a carried position.
entries.frame_evidence: A long shape emerges from or disappears into a region at the hip or back while the hand travels there and away.
entries.detector_note: Detect a hand excursion to the hip/back region followed by the appearance or disappearance of a long line attached to the hand, then confirm with a VLM crop.
entries.vlm_question: Is the person pulling a weapon out of, or putting it into, a sheath or holster? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Draw and sheathe are time-reverses of each other and the direction must come from the frame ordering, not the appearance.

entries.label: Overhead chop / downward strike
entries.description: A weapon raised above the head and driven downward with the whole body.
entries.frame_evidence: The weapon line passes through vertical from above, the arms extend and the body drops.
entries.detector_note: Hough-line angle passing through the vertical from above with a downward tip velocity, corroborated by a com_y drop and terminating at an impact_frame_index.
entries.notes: Requires the weapon to be visible above the figure; heavy VFX trails swamp the edge map.

entries.label: Weapon swing
entries.description: A held implement swept through an arc by the arms and torso.
entries.frame_evidence: A long rigid bright shape rotates about the hand across consecutive cels, often with a trail or smear.
entries.detector_note: In the hand ROI (from wrist landmarks or the fastest motion blob), fit the dominant line with cv2.HoughLinesP on a Canny edge map and track its angle per unique cel; swing = monotonic angle sweep beyond 45 degrees with the pivot near the hand.
entries.notes: Hough lines also latch onto railings, door frames and background edges; require the line's endpoint to stay attached to a wrist landmark or to the fastest-moving blob.

entries.label: Weapon thrust / stab
entries.description: A linear extension of a held implement along its own axis toward a target.
entries.frame_evidence: The blade's tip travels along the blade direction with little change in blade angle, while the arm extends.
entries.detector_note: Same Hough-line tracking as the swing, but requiring low angular change and high tip displacement along the line's own direction, concurrent with elbow extension.
entries.notes: Thrusts aimed at the camera are foreshortened to nothing and are undetectable by this method.

entries.label: Lateral weight shift
entries.description: Transfer of body weight from one supporting leg to the other, the primitive underneath walk, stance change, windup and dodge.
entries.frame_evidence: The pelvis centre moves horizontally toward one ankle while the other foot unloads or lifts.
entries.detector_note: Signed offset (mean(x23,x24) - x_of_contacting_ankle) / shoulder_width; contacting ankle chosen by body_action.foot_ground_contact; sign changes mark a weight transfer event.
entries.notes: mediapipe pose is trained on photographic humans; on stylised 2D art, chibi proportions, masks, heavy occlusion or non-human anatomy it silently returns a low-visibility or hallucinated skeleton - gate every landmark metric on body_action.pose_landmark_confidence_null. Image-plane only: a shift along the camera axis is invisible.

entries.label: Wing flap
entries.description: Cyclic up/down beating of wings driving flight or hover.
entries.frame_evidence: Two large appendages sweep symmetrically up and down about the body axis at a fixed period.
entries.detector_note: Silhouette bounding-box height/width oscillation plus symmetric left/right contour-extent series; autocorrelate for the beat period; verify bilateral symmetry by correlating the two side series.
entries.notes: Cape, cloak, hair and fabric produce the same oscillation; a VLM crop question is needed to confirm the appendages are wings.

entries.label: Wrist end-effector speed
entries.description: Linear speed of the hand through the frame, the quantity that a punch, slap, throw and swing all maximise.
entries.frame_evidence: The wrist landmark jumps a large normalised distance in one unique-cel step, often with a smeared hand.
entries.detector_note: |p15(t)-p15(t-1)| and |p16(t)-p16(t-1)| normalised by shoulder_width per second on unique cels; scipy.signal.find_peaks(prominence=...) for burst events.
entries.notes: mediapipe pose is trained on photographic humans; on stylised 2D art, chibi proportions, masks, heavy occlusion or non-human anatomy it silently returns a low-visibility or hallucinated skeleton - gate every landmark metric on body_action.pose_landmark_confidence_null. All temporal derivatives are computed on UNIQUE-CEL indices (dedupe by mean |absdiff| < 0.5/255 against the previous frame); dt is the real gap between unique cels, never 1/fps.

entries.label: Crossing the line (180-degree rule break)
entries.description: Consecutive shots place the camera on opposite sides of the action axis, flipping screen direction.
entries.frame_evidence: A character who exited or looked screen-left in one shot looks or moves screen-right in the next, with no re-establishing move between.
entries.detector_note: Needs cross-shot subject identity plus a reliable gaze/motion-direction vector per shot; identity is unavailable and gaze on 2D is unreliable, so this cannot be measured honestly today.
entries.notes: Logged so the blind spot is visible. Any implementation without re-id would produce confident nonsense.

entries.label: Subject facing away from camera
entries.description: The subject's back or back of head is toward the lens.
entries.frame_evidence: Pose landmarks resolve with shoulders present but no face detection, and the shoulder landmark ordering is mirrored relative to the hips.
entries.detector_note: pose landmarks present AND face_detection empty within the head ROI; confirm via the sign of the cross product of the shoulder vector (11->12) against the hip vector (23->24) in image space.
entries.notes: Heavy hair, hoods, masks and helmets all suppress face detection from the front and produce the same signature.

entries.label: Bird's-eye view (steeply overhead, oblique)
entries.description: The camera is high above the scene looking down at a steep but not fully vertical angle.
entries.frame_evidence: Ground plane fills most of the frame, figures are foreshortened to their tops, and the horizon is at or above the top edge.
entries.detector_note: Horizon detection via LSD-derived horizontal vanishing point plus the dominant-plane homography from cv2.findHomography on ground features; flag when no horizon is found inside the frame and the dominant plane's normal is near-vertical.
entries.notes: TIER CORRECTED by completeness critic: deterministic, while camera.angle_high and camera.angle_low - the milder versions of the same measurement - are landmark. Extreme angles need the SAME subject or ground reference; being extreme does not remove the requir

entries.label: Dutch / canted angle
entries.description: The camera is rolled about its optical axis so the horizon and verticals sit at an angle.
entries.frame_evidence: The dominant horizontal structure in the frame is tilted several degrees off the image horizontal, consistently across the frame.
entries.detector_note: lsd=cv2.createLineSegmentDetector(); take segments longer than 0.08*frame_diagonal, build a length-weighted angle histogram modulo 90 degrees, take the circular mode; roll = signed offset of that mode from 0. Flag dutch when |roll| > 3 degrees with mode concentration (circular variance) below 0.25.
entries.notes: A genuinely tilted subject (a leaning building, a hillside, a listing ship) reads as a dutch angle. Modulo-90 folding also makes a 46-degree roll indistinguishable from a -44-degree roll; report the folded value and say so. A null model is mandatory: measure the same statistic on a known level-camera shot from the same title to get the noise floor and report any |roll| below it as zero, or this detector emits confident sub-degree tilts on every shot in the file.

entries.label: Eye-level angle
entries.description: The camera sits at roughly the subject's eye height, giving a neutral read.
entries.frame_evidence: The subject's eye line falls near the vertical centre of frame and facial foreshortening is symmetric top-to-bottom.
entries.detector_note: From face_mesh, compare the vertical span forehead-to-eye against eye-to-chin (points 10, 168, 152); at eye level the ratio sits in the shot-normalised neutral band. Corroborate with the horizon line from cv2.createLineSegmentDetector near the eye-line height.
entries.notes: The face-geometry pitch proxy needs a per-title neutral band; head pitch (subject nodding) and camera pitch are confounded in a single frame. Only a shot-level median with a static-head null separates them, and often not even then.

entries.label: Profile (side-on) framing
entries.description: The face is seen from the side, roughly 90 degrees off axis.
entries.frame_evidence: Only one eye contour resolves and the nose breaks the face silhouette.
entries.detector_note: face_mesh yaw proxy > 0.35 or mesh failure combined with a face_detection hit; corroborate with silhouette convexity defects along the face contour from cv2.convexityDefects.
entries.notes: face_mesh degrades badly near true profile - the mesh either fails or hallucinates the occluded half. Treat a mesh failure plus a face box as weak profile evidence, not proof.

entries.label: Subject framed frontally (face to camera)
entries.description: The subject's face is turned toward the lens.
entries.frame_evidence: Both eyes, both ears' regions and a centred nose in the face mesh, left-right symmetric.
entries.detector_note: face_mesh; yaw from the horizontal offset of the nose tip (1) relative to the midpoint of the outer eye corners (33, 263), normalised by inter-ocular distance; frontal when |yaw_proxy| < 0.12.
entries.notes: This is a subject-orientation measure that framing analysis borrows; it is not camera angle. Keep the distinction in the log or the two get conflated.

entries.label: High angle (camera above subject)
entries.description: The camera looks down on the subject from above eye height.
entries.frame_evidence: The top of the head is foreshortened toward the viewer, the chin is compressed, and ground plane occupies more of the frame than sky.
entries.detector_note: face_mesh solvePnP: cv2.solvePnP against a canonical 3D face model using landmark subset (1,152,33,263,61,291) then decompose rvec for pitch; high angle when pitch indicates the camera is above. Corroborate with ground-plane fraction from the lower-third texture/colour statistics.
entries.notes: solvePnP on a canonical face model is only meaningful for roughly photoreal proportions; on 2D anime the canonical model is wrong and the pitch number is fiction. Gate this on a 2D/3D style flag and drop to VLM for 2D.

entries.label: High angle, 2D drawn
entries.description: In drawn animation the high angle is a compositional convention: converging verticals downward and a visible ground plane with figures small at the bottom.
entries.frame_evidence: Vertical architectural lines converge toward a vanishing point below the frame and the figure's head is drawn larger than its feet.
entries.detector_note: Ask qwen2.5vl on the full frame downscaled to 768px (this is a global-geometry question; the crop rule does not help here and the answer is correspondingly less reliable).
entries.vlm_question: Is the camera looking down at the scene from above? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Violates the crop rule by necessity - camera angle is a whole-frame property. Expect noticeably lower reliability than crop-based questions and never treat a single-frame yes as a shot verdict; take a majority over sampled unique cels.

entries.label: Low angle (camera below subject)
entries.description: The camera looks up at the subject from below eye height.
entries.frame_evidence: The underside of the chin and jaw is visible, nostrils read, and the subject towers against sky or ceiling.
entries.detector_note: solvePnP pitch as in camera.angle_high with the opposite sign; corroborate by testing whether the upper half of the frame is sky/ceiling-like (low texture, high luminance or uniform ceiling geometry) via per-tile Laplacian variance and hue uniformity.

entries.label: Over-the-shoulder framing
entries.description: The camera sits behind and beside one subject, whose shoulder and head edge occupy a foreground corner while the other subject faces camera.
entries.frame_evidence: A large, often defocused, dark head-and-shoulder mass anchored to one vertical frame edge, with a sharp face in the opposite two-thirds.
entries.detector_note: Gate deterministically first: one image side has a large connected region of low Laplacian variance touching the frame edge and spanning >25% of frame height, while a face_detection box sits in the opposite half. Then confirm with qwen2.5vl on a crop covering that edge region plus the face.
entries.vlm_question: Is there a person's head or shoulder seen from behind in the front corner of this image, with another person facing us? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Any large defocused foreground occluder (a pillar, a chair back) trips the deterministic gate; the VLM confirmation is doing the real work here.

entries.label: Camera pitch estimated from scene geometry
entries.description: The camera's up/down tilt inferred from where the horizontal vanishing line falls, independent of any subject.
entries.frame_evidence: The horizon line's vertical position relative to the frame centre.
entries.detector_note: LSD segments -> two dominant angle clusters -> vanishing points by least squares -> the line joining them is the horizon; pitch_proxy = (frame_center_y - horizon_y)/frame_h. Positive means the camera is tilted down.
entries.notes: Only valid with a real focal-length estimate to convert the proxy into degrees; without one, report the normalised proxy and do not call it degrees.

entries.label: Point-of-view / subjective camera
entries.description: The camera stands in for a character's eyes, so the audience sees what that character sees.
entries.frame_evidence: Another character looks directly into the lens, and/or the character's own hands or weapon enter frame from the bottom edge, with handheld-consistent motion.
entries.detector_note: Combine three cheap signals as a gate - face_mesh iris/gaze pointing at the optical axis, mediapipe hands detected anchored to the bottom frame edge, and handheld shake from camera.motion_handheld_shake - then ask qwen2.5vl on the full frame.
entries.vlm_question: Are we seeing this scene through a character's own eyes, with their hands or body entering from the bottom of the frame? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Direct-to-camera address (a presenter, a narrator, a talking head) is the dominant false positive and is not POV.

entries.label: Reverse angle of a preceding shot
entries.description: The camera has crossed to roughly the opposite side of the axis between two subjects.
entries.frame_evidence: The subject who faced left in the previous shot now faces right, at similar scale and against a complementary background.
entries.detector_note: Requires matching subject identity and scene geometry across a cut - needs re-identification and scene-matching models we do not have installed (no insightface, no sklearn for embedding clustering).
entries.notes: Blind spot by design. A histogram-flip heuristic was considered and rejected: it fires on any symmetric set and cannot tell a reverse from a different location.

entries.label: Top-down / nadir (true 90 degrees)
entries.description: The camera points straight down; the ground plane is parallel to the image plane.
entries.frame_evidence: No perspective convergence at all in the ground pattern, and figures read as flat silhouettes with no visible vertical extent.
entries.detector_note: Two tests must both pass: parallel-line test (LSD segment angle histogram shows two tight modes with near-zero convergence, i.e. vanishing points at infinity) and, on a moving shot, a pure-translation global model with scale_ratio ~ 1 and uniform flow magnitude across the frame (no depth parallax gradient).
entries.notes: A flat wall shot head-on produces the identical parallel-line signature. The uniform-flow test on a moving camera is what separates a nadir plate from a frontal wall; on a static shot the two are genuinely indistinguishable from geometry alone. | TIER CORRECTED by completeness critic: deterministic, while camera.angle_high and camera.angle_low - the milder versions of the same measurement - are landmark. Extreme angles need the SAME subject or ground reference; being extreme does not remove the requir

entries.label: Worm's-eye view (extreme low)
entries.description: The camera is at or near ground level looking steeply up.
entries.frame_evidence: Verticals converge strongly upward toward a vanishing point above the frame; the ground plane is at or below the bottom edge.
entries.detector_note: cv2.createLineSegmentDetector segments, cluster by angle, intersect line pairs to find the vertical vanishing point via least-squares in homogeneous coordinates; flag when the vertical VP lies above the frame within roughly 2 frame heights and vertical convergence exceeds a per-shot threshold.
entries.notes: Requires man-made straight edges. In forest, water or a plain sky there are no usable segments and the entry is simply undetermined - report 'insufficient line evidence', never 'not a worm's-eye'. | TIER CORRECTED by completeness critic: deterministic, while camera.angle_high and camera.angle_low - the milder versions of the same measurement - are landmark. Extreme angles need the SAME subject or ground reference; being extreme does not remove the requir

entries.label: Active image aspect ratio
entries.description: The aspect ratio of the actual picture area after any bars are excluded.
entries.frame_evidence: The width and height of the non-bar region of the frame.
entries.detector_note: Container dimensions from ffprobe (-show_streams: width, height, sample_aspect_ratio, display_aspect_ratio) combined with the measured bar thicknesses from camera.letterbox_bars and camera.pillarbox_bars; active ratio = (w - left - right)/(h - top - bottom) * SAR.
entries.notes: Non-square pixels are common in older material; ignoring SAR silently reports a wrong ratio, so always read it from ffprobe rather than assuming 1:1. Also derive is_portrait_flag (active ratio < 1.0) and is_windowboxed_flag (letterbox and pillarbox both positive, which is almost always a pipeline defect rather than an authoring choice) from this same measurement.

entries.label: Aspect ratio changes during the piece
entries.description: The active image ratio changes between shots or sequences, as with IMAX expansions or format-shifting flashbacks.
entries.frame_evidence: Bar thicknesses that are stable within a shot but differ between shots.
entries.detector_note: Compare per-shot bar thicknesses across the whole file; flag when the active aspect ratio differs by more than 2% between shots.

entries.label: Canting that changes during the shot
entries.description: The frame rolls into or out of a canted angle while the shot runs.
entries.frame_evidence: The measured dutch angle drifts monotonically or oscillates across unique cels within one shot.
entries.detector_note: Track roll from camera.global_motion_model (atan2 of the affine) accumulated across unique cels, and cross-check against the per-frame LSD dutch angle; flag when the accumulated roll exceeds 2 degrees with consistent sign.

entries.label: 2D layer blur (uniform per-layer defocus)
entries.description: Drawn animation fakes depth of field by applying one gaussian blur to a whole plate, so the blur radius is constant within a layer and steps discontinuously at layer boundaries.
entries.frame_evidence: Blur amount is identical across an entire background region and changes abruptly, not smoothly, at the character silhouette.
entries.detector_note: Estimate a local blur radius per tile by fitting the slope of the log power spectrum (or by the ratio of gradient magnitude at two Gaussian scales), then test for piecewise-constant structure: low variance within regions, a step at the boundary. Compare against the smooth radius gradient expected from real optics.
entries.notes: Modern compositing sometimes uses a depth map to vary the blur smoothly, in which case this test correctly reports 'optics-like' on a drawn frame. That is not a false positive - it is the observable.

entries.label: Blur bleeding halo at a matte edge
entries.description: A defocus applied after compositing pulls sharp foreground colour into the blurred background, leaving a bright or dark halo tracing the subject.
entries.frame_evidence: A thin band around the subject silhouette whose colour is a smeared version of the subject, distinct from both subject and background.
entries.detector_note: Dilate the subject mask by 3-9 px, subtract the mask to get a ring, and test whether the ring's mean colour lies between subject and background means with an anomalous gradient profile; flag when the ring's colour distance from the local background exceeds a per-shot threshold.
entries.notes: Genuine rim light produces a similar ring. The separator is that a matte halo's hue is the subject's own hue smeared outward, whereas rim light is the light source's colour.

entries.label: Bokeh highlight discs present
entries.description: Point light sources rendered as discrete defocus discs.
entries.frame_evidence: Distinct bright circular or polygonal blobs in the blurred regions, well separated from each other.
entries.detector_note: Threshold above the 99th luminance percentile within low-sharpness tiles, connected components with area between 40 and 4000 px and circularity above 0.7; count and size them.
entries.notes: The gateway measurement for the whole anamorphic/cat's-eye/blade-count family; if bokeh_count is low, all of those entries must report insufficient evidence rather than a value.

entries.label: Deep focus
entries.description: Foreground, midground and background are all acceptably sharp.
entries.frame_evidence: High-frequency detail is present at every depth in the frame simultaneously.
entries.detector_note: Per-tile Laplacian variance normalised by local contrast; deep focus when the sharp-tile fraction exceeds ~0.8 and the sharpness map has no strong spatial structure (low variance of the tile sharpness distribution).
entries.notes: A frame that is uniformly flat and textureless (fog, sky, a plain wall) also has no sharpness structure; require a minimum overall edge density before calling deep focus.

entries.label: Whole frame out of focus
entries.description: Nothing in the frame is sharp - a transitional beat, a subjective blur, or an error.
entries.frame_evidence: The sharpness map is uniformly low across every tile.
entries.detector_note: sharp_tile_fraction below 0.05 with the frame still carrying real luminance structure (nonzero large-scale gradient energy), which excludes black frames and flat cards.
entries.notes: Heavy compression on a dark frame reads the same; check the bitrate/quantiser context before reporting.

entries.label: Focus hunting / pumping
entries.description: Autofocus oscillates, so the subject's sharpness rises and falls repeatedly within one shot.
entries.frame_evidence: The subject's sharpness series oscillates several times without a corresponding change in subject distance.
entries.detector_note: FFT or peak-count of the subject-region sharpness series over unique cels; hunting when three or more full oscillations occur within the shot with amplitude above the sharpness noise floor and no matching scale change.
entries.notes: Compression breathing (bitrate-driven quality oscillation on GOP boundaries) produces sharpness oscillation at the GOP rate; check whether the oscillation period matches the keyframe interval from ffprobe before calling it focus hunting.

entries.label: Missed focus (subject soft)
entries.description: The intended subject is not the sharpest thing in frame.
entries.frame_evidence: The subject's face or body is measurably softer than some background element.
entries.detector_note: Compare the mean normalised sharpness inside the face_mesh/pose bounding box against the 90th percentile of background tile sharpness; flag when the subject is below it by a clear margin sustained over the shot.
entries.notes: A deliberately soft-focus portrait, a diffusion filter, and a genuine focus miss are indistinguishable by this measure; report the observation, not the intent.

entries.label: Defocused background
entries.description: The background is thrown out of focus to isolate the subject.
entries.frame_evidence: Sharp subject silhouette against a smoothly blurred field with no high-frequency detail behind it.
entries.detector_note: Sharpness map plus mediapipe selfie_segmentation or pose-derived subject mask: background mean sharpness below 25% of subject mean sharpness.

entries.label: Out-of-focus foreground occluder
entries.description: A blurred element sits between camera and subject - foliage, a shoulder, a railing - framing the shot.
entries.frame_evidence: A large blurred mass touching a frame edge and partially occluding a sharp subject behind it.
entries.detector_note: Connected low-sharpness region that touches a frame border, has area between 5% and 45% of frame, and whose boundary occludes (rather than being occluded by) the sharp region - test occlusion by which side the boundary's blur gradient falls on.
entries.notes: Distinguishing an out-of-focus foreground from an out-of-focus background at the same frame edge requires the occlusion test; without it the two are routinely swapped.

entries.label: Rack focus / focus pull
entries.description: Focus is shifted during the shot from one subject to another.
entries.frame_evidence: One region sharpens while another softens across a few unique cels, with the transition monotonic in both.
entries.detector_note: Track per-region sharpness for at least two regions across unique cels; rack when one series rises and the other falls with a significant negative correlation (scipy.stats.pearsonr r < -0.6) over a window of 4-20 unique cels, and the global affine shows no scale change beyond the breathing allowance.
entries.notes: Anime rack focus is a crossfade between a sharp and a pre-blurred layer, which reads identically here - correctly so, since the observable is the same.

entries.label: Shallow depth of field
entries.description: Only a narrow depth band is sharp; everything nearer and further is blurred.
entries.frame_evidence: A compact sharp region surrounded by clearly blurred content with a smooth transition.
entries.detector_note: Bimodality of the tile-sharpness histogram (dip test proxy: fit a two-component split by Otsu on the sharpness map and require good separation), plus the sharp region being spatially compact (its connected component's fill ratio).
entries.notes: In 2D animation this is achieved by gaussian-blurring whole layers, which produces the same measurement with a characteristically uniform blur radius per layer - see camera.focus_2d_layer_blur.

entries.label: Split diopter (two sharp planes, visible seam)
entries.description: A half-lens element puts two very different depths in focus at once, leaving a soft vertical or diagonal seam between them.
entries.frame_evidence: Two separated sharp regions at obviously different depths, divided by a narrow blurred band running across the frame.
entries.detector_note: Sharpness map showing two high-sharpness regions separated by a narrow low-sharpness band; fit a line to that band (cv2.HoughLinesP on the thresholded low-sharpness mask) and require it to span the frame.
entries.notes: Rare; a vertical architectural element that happens to be defocused will trip it. Require both sharp regions to contain substantial detail.

entries.label: Dirty frame edges / blanking
entries.description: The outermost rows or columns carry non-picture content - repeated edge pixels, half-lines, or noise from a telecine or capture.
entries.frame_evidence: A one-to-three pixel border that differs statistically from the adjacent picture and does not track scene motion.
entries.detector_note: Compare the outer 1-3 px border's statistics against the adjacent interior band across the shot; flag when the border is constant, clamped (identical to the neighbouring row), or has anomalous variance while the picture moves.
entries.notes: Edge-clamp replication from a stabiliser or a resize produces the same signature as capture blanking; both are worth reporting but they are not the same defect.

entries.label: Frame rate and pulldown cadence
entries.description: The container frame rate and any repeating field/frame cadence, which sets what a 'frame' even means for every temporal metric here.
entries.frame_evidence: A regular repeating pattern of duplicated frames or interlaced field combing.
entries.detector_note: ffprobe -show_streams for r_frame_rate / avg_frame_rate; then autocorrelate the hold-run-length series from camera.unique_cel_index to expose a 3:2 or 2:3:3:2 cadence; detect combing by comparing even-row and odd-row differences on motion frames.
entries.notes: This is a prerequisite for the whole movement group: velocities in px/frame are meaningless without knowing what a frame is, and a telecined 24-in-30 file will otherwise report jittery motion that is pure cadence.

entries.label: Bilateral (mirror) symmetry
entries.description: The composition is mirrored about the vertical centre line.
entries.frame_evidence: The left half of the frame is a near mirror image of the right half.
entries.detector_note: Flip the frame with cv2.flip(img,1) and compare against the original using skimage.metrics.structural_similarity on a downsampled grayscale; also compare edge maps to reduce the influence of lighting. Symmetric when SSIM exceeds a per-title threshold calibrated on a random-frame null distribution.
entries.notes: Uniform frames (sky, fog, a plain wall) score very high mirror SSIM and are not compositions; require a minimum edge density before reporting symmetry.

entries.label: Centre-framed subject
entries.description: The subject is placed on the frame's vertical centre line.
entries.frame_evidence: The subject centroid sits within a few percent of x=0.5.
entries.detector_note: |subject_x_normalised - 0.5| < 0.05, held for the majority of unique cels in the shot.

entries.label: Explicit foreground / midground / background layering
entries.description: The composition is built from distinct depth planes rather than a single flat field.
entries.frame_evidence: Three or more regions with clearly different sharpness, scale or motion, stacked in depth.
entries.detector_note: Combine the sharpness map clusters with the flow-mode count from camera.motion_multiplane_parallax on moving shots; layer count = number of consistent clusters across both cues.
entries.notes: On a static shot only the sharpness cue is available, and a deep-focus composition with real depth layers will report one layer. That is a limitation of the cue, not of the composition.

entries.label: Eyeline height in frame
entries.description: Where the subject's eyes fall vertically, the classic anchor for headroom decisions.
entries.frame_evidence: The mean y of the two eye centres in normalised coordinates.
entries.detector_note: face_mesh landmarks 33/133 and 362/263 midpoints averaged; report normalised y and its distance from the upper third line.

entries.label: Foreground dressing / dirtying the lens
entries.description: Objects placed close to the camera at the frame edges to add depth, usually heavily defocused.
entries.frame_evidence: Blurred shapes intruding from one or more frame edges that do not participate in the action.
entries.detector_note: Low-sharpness connected components touching the frame border, area between 3% and 30%, present for the whole shot and moving with the camera rather than independently (frame-locked test from the global motion model).

entries.label: Frame within a frame
entries.description: The subject is enclosed by an in-scene aperture - a doorway, window, arch or mirror.
entries.frame_evidence: A closed quadrilateral or arch of strong contrast surrounds the subject, with markedly different content inside and outside it.
entries.detector_note: Deterministic gate: find large quadrilaterals via cv2.findContours + cv2.approxPolyDP with 4 vertices and area between 10% and 70% of frame, then check that the subject's face box lies inside. Confirm with qwen2.5vl on a crop of the quadrilateral plus a margin.
entries.vlm_question: Is the person in this image framed inside a doorway, window, arch, or mirror? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: The contour gate misses arches and soft-edged apertures entirely; it is a recall-limited pre-filter, so a negative means 'no rectangular aperture found', not 'no frame within a frame'.

entries.label: Head cropped by the top frame edge
entries.description: The top of the head is cut off by the frame.
entries.frame_evidence: Face landmarks extend past y=0, or the face box's top edge is clamped to the frame boundary with the face continuing.
entries.detector_note: face_mesh points with y < 0 after unnormalising, or a face_detection box whose top is at y==0 while the box height suggests more head above; count the fraction of head points outside.

entries.label: Headroom (space above the head)
entries.description: The distance between the top of the subject's head and the top frame edge.
entries.frame_evidence: The gap in normalised frame heights between the highest head landmark and y=0.
entries.detector_note: From face_mesh take the topmost forehead point (landmark 10) or, better, extend to the hair line by taking the top of the face_detection box; headroom = that y in normalised coords. Report as a fraction of face height too, which is scale-invariant.
entries.notes: face_mesh stops at the forehead, not the hair, so raw headroom is systematically overestimated on subjects with volume hair - and dramatically so on stylised 2D hair.

entries.label: Excessive headroom
entries.description: Too much empty space above the subject's head, dropping the subject low in frame.
entries.frame_evidence: Headroom exceeding roughly one face height with the subject's eyes below the lower third line.
entries.detector_note: headroom_per_face_height > 1.0 AND eyeline_normalised_y > 0.55, sustained across the shot.
entries.notes: Deliberate low placement (a figure dwarfed by a ceiling) is the same measurement; this is an observable, not a criticism.

entries.label: Horizon tilt in degrees
entries.description: The measured angle of the true horizon or dominant horizontal, independent of any interpretation as a dutch angle.
entries.frame_evidence: The slope of the longest near-horizontal structure spanning the frame.
entries.detector_note: LSD segments within 20 degrees of horizontal, length-weighted circular mean of their angles; report the value with its concentration and the supporting length.
entries.notes: Deliberately kept separate from camera.angle_dutch_canted: this is the measurement, that is the interpretation. Conflating them is how a listing ship becomes a canted camera in the log.

entries.label: Lead room / looking room
entries.description: Space left in front of a subject in the direction they face or move.
entries.frame_evidence: The subject sits off centre with the larger empty area on the side their face is turned toward.
entries.detector_note: Determine gaze/facing direction from the face_mesh yaw proxy sign (or from subject velocity when no face), then compare the empty width on the facing side against the trailing side; lead room present when the facing-side width exceeds the trailing side by >20%.
entries.notes: Yaw sign from the mesh is unreliable near frontal and on 2D; when |yaw_proxy| is below 0.1 report the ratio without asserting lead room.

entries.label: Short-sided framing (no lead room)
entries.description: The subject looks or moves toward the near frame edge, feeling cramped or deliberately trapped.
entries.frame_evidence: The empty space is behind the subject rather than in front of them.
entries.detector_note: lead_room_ratio < 0.8 sustained across the shot with a confident facing direction.

entries.label: Subject cropped by a frame edge at a joint
entries.description: A limb or the body is cut by the frame boundary, and specifically whether the cut lands on a joint (conventionally avoided).
entries.frame_evidence: Pose landmarks fall outside the frame rectangle, with the cut line passing through or near a joint landmark.
entries.detector_note: For pose landmarks with visibility>0.5, find the ones nearest the frame boundary; flag joint-cut when a joint landmark lies within 3% of frame height of an edge, and limb-cut when a bone segment crosses an edge between joints.

entries.label: Negative space ratio
entries.description: How much of the frame is empty or low-detail relative to the subject and structure.
entries.frame_evidence: The fraction of the frame with low edge density and low local variance.
entries.detector_note: Edge density per 16x16 tile from cv2.Canny; negative space = fraction of tiles below the 25th percentile of the title-wide edge-density distribution (a per-title null, not a fixed constant).

entries.label: Subject on a thirds line or intersection
entries.description: The main subject sits on one of the two vertical or two horizontal third lines, or on their intersection.
entries.frame_evidence: The subject's centroid or the eye line falls within a narrow band around x=1/3 or 2/3, or y=1/3 or 2/3.
entries.detector_note: Take the face centroid (or pose centroid when no face) in normalised coords; flag when it falls within 0.05 of a third line. Report distance to the nearest intersection as a continuous value.
entries.notes: The thirds grid is a convention, not a fact about the image; a 0.05 tolerance means roughly 20% of arbitrary placements will 'satisfy' it by chance. Always report the continuous distance so a consumer can see how weak the claim is.

entries.label: Content outside title/action safe
entries.description: Important content sits in the outer margin that broadcast cropping would lose.
entries.frame_evidence: A face or key graphic overlaps the outer 5% (title safe) or 10% (action safe) border.
entries.detector_note: Test whether the face_detection box or a detected high-contrast graphic region intersects the outer 5%/10% frame margins.
entries.notes: Text and graphics detection is not available (no rapidocr installed), so this covers faces and high-contrast blocks only.

entries.label: Subject drifts within a static frame
entries.description: The camera does not move but the subject wanders relative to the composition.
entries.frame_evidence: The subject centroid migrates across the frame while background features stay pinned.
entries.detector_note: Static global model AND subject centroid travelling more than 10% of frame width across the shot; report the trajectory and its net displacement.

entries.label: Tangency (element just touching an edge or another element)
entries.description: A compositional element grazes a frame edge or another contour without clear overlap or separation, creating visual tension.
entries.frame_evidence: A strong contour runs parallel to and within a couple of pixels of a frame boundary or another contour.
entries.detector_note: Extract contours with cv2.findContours on a Canny map; measure the minimum distance from each long contour to the frame rectangle and to other long contours; tangency when the minimum distance is between 0 and ~0.5% of frame width over a run of at least 5% of frame width.
entries.notes: Noisy on textured frames; restrict to contours above a length threshold and to smooth (low-curvature) runs.

entries.label: Vanishing point location in frame
entries.description: Where the dominant perspective vanishing point falls, which encodes camera orientation and composition together.
entries.frame_evidence: The intersection of the dominant parallel-line family.
entries.detector_note: cv2.createLineSegmentDetector segments longer than 0.1*frame_diagonal; cluster by angle and take the largest cluster; RANSAC for the common intersection in homogeneous coordinates. Report normalised coordinates, the supporting segment count, the fit residual, whether the point is inside the frame, and its distance from the frame centre (a centred VP with support in three or more quadrants is the corridor / one-point-perspective look).
entries.notes: Any two lines intersect somewhere; require at least four independent supporting segments with a tight residual before reporting a vanishing point at all. Useless in nature, water or fog where there are no straight edges - the honest output there is 'insufficient line evidence', never 'no perspective'.

entries.label: Global camera motion model (tx, ty, scale, roll)
entries.description: The per-pair 4-DOF similarity transform describing how the whole image moved, from which pan/tilt/zoom/roll are all read off.
entries.frame_evidence: The dominant, background-supported displacement field between two consecutive unique cels.
entries.detector_note: p0=cv2.goodFeaturesToTrack(gray, maxCorners=800, qualityLevel=0.01, minDistance=8); p1,st,_=cv2.calcOpticalFlowPyrLK(g0,g1,p0,None,winSize=(21,21),maxLevel=4); M,inl=cv2.estimateAffinePartial2D(p0[st==1],p1[st==1],method=cv2.RANSAC,ransacReprojThreshold=2.0). Decompose: scale=hypot(M[0,0],M[0,1]), roll=atan2(M[0,1],M[0,0]), tx=M[0,2], ty=M[1,2]. Fall back to cv2.findTransformECC(MOTION_EUCLIDEAN) on textureless frames, and to cv2.DISOpticalFlow_create(PRESET_MEDIUM) dense flow when corner count < 40.
entries.notes: Everything downstream inherits this fit's failure modes: a large moving foreground subject can win RANSAC and be reported as camera motion. Guard by masking mediapipe person boxes out of the corner set and re-fitting; if the two fits disagree by more than the noise floor, log motion_model_ambiguous instead of a move.

entries.label: Horizon placement in frame
entries.description: Where the horizon sits vertically, which sets how much ground versus sky the composition carries.
entries.frame_evidence: A long, near-horizontal luminance or colour boundary spanning most of the frame width.
entries.detector_note: Row-wise gradient energy from cv2.Sobel(dy) summed across columns; take the strongest row with support over >60% of the width, cross-validated against the LSD horizontal cluster.

entries.label: Horizontal anamorphic flare streak
entries.description: The signature horizontal blue streak thrown across the frame by an anamorphic element when a bright source is in shot.
entries.frame_evidence: A long, thin, strongly horizontal bright band with a distinct blue-cyan cast, emanating from a blown highlight.
entries.detector_note: Threshold at the top 0.5% of luminance, dilate with a horizontal structuring element (cv2.getStructuringElement(cv2.MORPH_RECT,(51,1))), keep components with aspect ratio > 8 and near-zero orientation from cv2.fitEllipse, and test the mean hue of the component against the blue-cyan band in HSV.
entries.notes: Drawn anime lens flares are extremely common and deliberately imitate this; a positive here on 2D is a stylistic finding, not evidence of an optical path.

entries.label: Anamorphic squeeze / de-squeeze
entries.description: An anamorphic optical path compresses the horizontal axis at capture, producing a distinctive geometry when de-squeezed and oval defocus.
entries.frame_evidence: Out-of-focus highlights are vertical ovals rather than circles, and horizontal detail is softer than vertical at equal radius.
entries.detector_note: Isolate bright defocused blobs (threshold above the 99th luminance percentile, connected components in low-sharpness tiles), fit cv2.fitEllipse to each and report the median major/minor ratio and orientation; anamorphic when the median ratio exceeds ~1.3 with the major axis vertical. Cross-check with a directional sharpness ratio: Sobel-x energy versus Sobel-y energy on matched frequency bands.
entries.notes: Needs enough bright bokeh blobs to fit; a shot without point highlights simply yields no evidence. Motion blur also produces elongated highlights - require the elongation to be vertical and static across frames.

entries.label: Barrel distortion
entries.description: Straight lines bow outward from the frame centre, typical of wide and action-camera lenses.
entries.frame_evidence: Long lines that should be straight are visibly curved, with curvature increasing toward the frame edges.
entries.detector_note: Detect long edge chains with cv2.findContours on a Canny map, fit a straight line to each and measure the maximum perpendicular deviation (sagitta) normalised by chain length; regress sagitta sign and magnitude against the chain's mean radius from the principal point. Barrel gives outward-bowing sagitta growing as r^2.
entries.notes: Genuinely curved architecture (arches, domes, car bodies) is the standing false positive; requiring the r^2 radial trend across many independent chains is what makes this defensible.

entries.label: Circular bokeh
entries.description: Round out-of-focus highlights, from a wide-open or many-bladed iris.
entries.frame_evidence: Smooth circular discs of light in the defocused regions.
entries.detector_note: Blob circularity 4*pi*area/perimeter^2 above 0.88 with an ellipse ratio below 1.15, aggregated as a median over blobs.

entries.label: Polygonal bokeh (aperture blade count)
entries.description: Stopped-down irises render out-of-focus highlights as polygons whose side count reveals the blade count.
entries.frame_evidence: Defocused highlights have straight edges and visible corners rather than a smooth circular boundary.
entries.detector_note: For each bokeh blob, cv2.approxPolyDP on its contour with epsilon = 0.02 * perimeter and count vertices; also compute the angular FFT of the radial boundary profile and read the dominant harmonic order (5, 6, 7, 8 blades give the corresponding harmonic).
entries.notes: Small or dim blobs are dominated by noise; restrict to blobs above roughly 20 px diameter or the vertex count is invented.

entries.label: Cat's-eye bokeh (mechanical vignetting)
entries.description: Defocused highlights near the frame edges are clipped into lens shapes by the barrel, pointing at the frame centre.
entries.frame_evidence: Bokeh blobs are round at the centre and progressively lemon-shaped toward the corners, their long axis radial.
entries.detector_note: Fit ellipses to bokeh blobs as in camera.lens_anamorphic_squeeze, then regress each blob's eccentricity and major-axis orientation against its radius and azimuth from the centre; cat's eye gives eccentricity growing with radius and major axis tangential/radial-aligned.
entries.notes: Needs many bokeh blobs spread across the frame; usually only measurable on night exteriors and practical-lit interiors.

entries.label: Lateral chromatic aberration
entries.description: Colour channels are magnified slightly differently, fringing edges red/cyan more strongly toward the corners.
entries.frame_evidence: High-contrast edges near the frame edges show a coloured fringe on one side, with fringe width growing with radius.
entries.detector_note: Split into R, G, B; for tiles at increasing radius, use cv2.phaseCorrelate(R_tile.astype(np.float32), B_tile.astype(np.float32)) to get the sub-pixel R-B shift; lateral CA when the shift is radially oriented and its magnitude grows monotonically with radius.
entries.notes: Anime and CG frequently add fake CA as a post effect - identical measurement, different cause. Also, coloured scene content (a red object against cyan) can fool a per-tile phase correlation, so require the radial trend.

entries.label: Longitudinal CA / purple fringing
entries.description: Focus differs by wavelength, so out-of-focus high-contrast edges bloom purple or green regardless of position in frame.
entries.frame_evidence: Purple-magenta halos on blown highlight edges anywhere in the frame, including at the centre.
entries.detector_note: Mask pixels adjacent to blown highlights (luminance > 250) via dilation minus the mask itself, then measure the mean hue of that ring in HSV; flag when hue concentrates in the magenta-violet band and the effect is not radius-dependent.

entries.label: Diffraction starburst on point lights
entries.description: A stopped-down iris turns point lights into stars with a spoke count equal to (or twice) the blade count.
entries.frame_evidence: Sharp radiating spikes from small bright sources, all sharing the same angular orientation across the frame.
entries.detector_note: For each small saturated blob, sample luminance on a polar grid and take the FFT of the angular profile; a strong harmonic at order 6, 8, 10 or 14 with consistent phase across multiple blobs indicates diffraction spikes.
entries.notes: Drawn 'sparkle' effects in anime imitate this exactly and will read as diffraction; a shared angular phase across widely separated blobs is the only real optical tell.

entries.label: Digital zoom (resolution loss on push)
entries.description: The image is scaled up in post rather than optically, so detail does not increase as the frame tightens.
entries.frame_evidence: As the frame pushes in, edges get softer and the high-frequency energy per unit subject size falls.
entries.detector_note: Track the high-frequency energy of a tracked subject patch across the push (normalised by patch area); optical zoom holds it roughly constant, digital zoom drops it in proportion to the scale factor. Also check for a stationary resampling grid signature in the FFT.
entries.notes: Source compression and grain can dominate the high-frequency measurement; use a matched frequency band rather than total energy.

entries.label: Dirty lens / smudge / rain on glass
entries.description: Contamination on the front element producing localised soft blooms or droplet lenses that stay fixed while the scene moves.
entries.frame_evidence: Soft blurred patches or droplet discs that hold identical image positions while the whole scene pans behind them.
entries.detector_note: Compute a per-pixel temporal median of the sharpness map across the shot's unique cels after warping every frame into a common reference using the global motion model; contamination shows as regions that are persistently soft in FRAME coordinates but not in SCENE coordinates.
entries.notes: This frame-locked-versus-scene-locked test is the same machinery used for camera.lens_dust_specks and camera.lens_vignetting; it needs a shot with real camera movement to work at all.

entries.label: Dust or sensor spots
entries.description: Small dark spots fixed in frame coordinates, from dust on the sensor or the rear element.
entries.frame_evidence: Tiny soft dark discs that never move with the scene.
entries.detector_note: Same frame-locked test as camera.lens_dirty_glass_smudge, restricted to small (<0.3% frame width) low-luminance blobs with high temporal persistence in frame coordinates.
entries.notes: Physically impossible in animation unless simulated; frequently added as a 'film look' texture, in which case it is a grade artefact rather than a lens one.

entries.label: Wide-angle edge stretching of subjects
entries.description: Rectilinear wide lenses stretch objects near the frame edges, most visibly widening faces and heads.
entries.frame_evidence: A face at the frame edge is measurably wider relative to its height than a face of the same person at the centre.
entries.detector_note: face_mesh; compute the face width/height aspect from landmarks (234,454 for width; 10,152 for height) and regress that aspect against the face centroid's radius from the principal point across all faces in a shot or title.
entries.notes: Needs several faces at different radii to be meaningful; a single edge face proves nothing because people's heads genuinely differ in width.

entries.label: Fisheye
entries.description: An extreme wide lens with heavy barrel distortion and, at the extreme, a circular image inside a black frame.
entries.frame_evidence: Massive edge curvature, a near-180-degree field, and often a visible circular image boundary with dark corners.
entries.detector_note: Two paths: circular-image fisheye detected by fitting a circle to the boundary between image content and black surround (cv2.HoughCircles on the thresholded luminance mask, or contour + cv2.fitEllipse); full-frame fisheye by an extreme |k1| estimate from camera.lens_barrel_distortion.
entries.notes: A vignetted or matted circular frame (a spyglass or keyhole mask) has the same circular boundary; the line-curvature test must also pass.

entries.label: Lens flare (non-anamorphic)
entries.description: Scattered light inside the lens producing bright veils, streaks or starbursts around a strong source.
entries.frame_evidence: A blown light source with radiating spokes or a soft halo, plus reduced local contrast around it.
entries.detector_note: Find saturated blobs, then measure radial spoke structure: sample luminance along rays from the blob centre and look for periodic angular peaks via FFT of the angular profile; combine with a local contrast drop measured as the ratio of local standard deviation inside versus outside the halo radius.

entries.label: Focus breathing during a pull
entries.description: Changing focus slightly changes the field of view, so the frame appears to zoom a little during a rack.
entries.frame_evidence: A small scale change of a few percent synchronised exactly with a focus change, with no camera movement.
entries.detector_note: Correlate the per-pair |log scale_ratio| series against the per-pair change in the global sharpness map (mean Laplacian variance over the subject region) across a rack; breathing when the two are significantly correlated (scipy.stats.pearsonr) while translation stays at the static noise floor.
entries.notes: Requires a rack focus to exist; the effect is a few percent at most, so this sits close to the noise floor and needs the static-shot null distribution to be meaningful.

entries.label: Lens ghosts (internal reflections)
entries.description: Faint polygonal or circular replicas of a bright source arrayed along the line from the source through the frame centre.
entries.frame_evidence: A chain of soft, low-contrast coloured blobs on the opposite side of the centre from the light source.
entries.detector_note: Locate the primary source, then search along the line through the principal point for low-contrast blobs at the mirrored radii; test collinearity of detected blob centroids with the source and the centre (perpendicular distance below 3% of frame diagonal).
entries.notes: Sparse practical lights in a night scene can accidentally fall on that line; require three or more collinear low-contrast blobs.

entries.label: Off-centre optical axis / shifted principal point
entries.description: The lens axis is not at the image centre, from a shift lens, an off-centre crop, or a reframed extraction.
entries.frame_evidence: Radial effects such as vignetting and CA are centred somewhere other than the geometric frame centre.
entries.detector_note: Fit the vignetting radial profile and the CA radial trend with the centre as a free parameter (scipy.optimize.least_squares); a consistent centre offset above ~3% of frame width across both fits indicates a shifted axis or a reframe.
entries.notes: Needs both radial cues to agree; either alone is too weak. Very useful as a reframe/crop detector on repurposed footage.

entries.label: Pincushion distortion
entries.description: Straight lines bow inward toward the frame centre, typical of the long end of zoom lenses.
entries.frame_evidence: Edge lines curve toward the centre with curvature growing with radius.
entries.detector_note: As camera.lens_barrel_distortion with the opposite sagitta sign (k1 estimate positive).

entries.label: Corner softness versus centre
entries.description: The lens resolves less at the edges than at the centre, independent of focus.
entries.frame_evidence: Fine detail is crisp centrally and mushy in the corners on a subject that spans both.
entries.detector_note: Per-tile high-frequency energy: for each tile compute the ratio of the high-band to the total energy from a Laplacian pyramid (skimage.transform.pyramid_laplacian) or from cv2.Laplacian variance normalised by local contrast, then regress against radius across the whole shot.
entries.notes: Confounded with depth of field: corners are often further away. Only trust this on flat, frame-filling subjects, and log the confound whenever the scene is not flat.

entries.label: Telephoto compression
entries.description: A long focal length flattening depth so foreground and background appear stacked at similar scale.
entries.frame_evidence: Near-parallel lines with vanishing points far outside the frame, and background objects rendered unexpectedly large relative to the subject.
entries.detector_note: The same VP-based FOV estimate with horizontal FOV below ~25 degrees; corroborate on moving shots with a very low parallax gradient despite substantial camera translation.

entries.label: Tilt-shift / non-parallel focus plane
entries.description: The focal plane is tilted relative to the sensor, producing a band of sharpness across the frame with blur above and below it, often used for a miniature look.
entries.frame_evidence: A horizontal band of the image is sharp while both the top and bottom are progressively blurred, regardless of actual scene depth.
entries.detector_note: Build the per-tile sharpness map, then fit sharpness as a function of a single linear coordinate (a rotated axis found by PCA of the sharpness gradient); tilt-shift when the fit is strongly 1D with sharpness peaking in a band and falling on both sides, and when that band does not correspond to a depth-consistent region.
entries.notes: A genuinely shallow depth of field on a receding ground plane produces the same top-to-bottom sharpness ramp; the discriminator is blur returning above AND below a mid-frame band, which a normal lens on a ground plane does not do.

entries.label: Veiling glare / haze from a bright source
entries.description: Non-image-forming light lifts the black level across a region, washing out contrast.
entries.frame_evidence: The shadows near a strong light source are noticeably lifted and desaturated compared to shadows elsewhere.
entries.detector_note: Compare the minimum-luminance percentile (1st) inside a radius of a blown source against the same statistic in the far quadrant; glare when the near black level is lifted by more than ~8 of 255 with no corresponding scene explanation.
entries.notes: Atmospheric haze and fog produce the same lift globally; requiring the lift to be spatially tied to a bright source is the discriminator.

entries.label: Vignetting (corner falloff)
entries.description: Luminance falling off smoothly toward the frame corners.
entries.frame_evidence: Corners measurably darker than the centre in a smooth, radially symmetric way independent of scene content.
entries.detector_note: Build a radial luminance profile: bin pixels by normalised radius from the principal point and take the median luminance per bin, then fit a cos^4 or low-order even polynomial; vignetting when the fitted corner/centre ratio is below ~0.85 and the fit residual is low. Aggregate across the whole shot so scene content averages out.
entries.notes: A single frame with a dark corner from scene content is not vignetting; the shot-level aggregation with a good radial fit is what makes this trustworthy. Deliberate post vignettes are indistinguishable from optical ones.

entries.label: Wide-angle look
entries.description: A short focal length exaggerating depth: near objects loom, lines converge steeply, the frame feels spacious.
entries.frame_evidence: Strong perspective convergence with vanishing points close to or inside the frame, and noticeable size falloff from foreground to background.
entries.detector_note: Estimate field of view from vanishing points: with two orthogonal VPs v1, v2 from LSD clustering, the focal length in pixels satisfies f^2 = -(v1-p).(v2-p) with p the principal point; FOV = 2*atan(frame_w/(2f)). Wide when the horizontal FOV estimate exceeds ~65 degrees.
entries.notes: Needs at least two orthogonal line families - reliable in architecture and interiors, useless in nature. In 2D, the drawn perspective is whatever the artist chose and the recovered focal length describes the drawing, not a lens.

entries.label: Letterbox bars (top and bottom)
entries.description: Black bars above and below the picture, from a wider image in a narrower container.
entries.frame_evidence: Rows at the top and bottom whose luminance is near zero and whose variance is essentially zero across the whole shot.
entries.detector_note: For each row compute mean and standard deviation over the shot's unique cels; a bar row has mean < 6/255 and std < 2/255 sustained for >95% of frames. Scan inward from the top and bottom until the condition breaks.
entries.notes: A shot that is genuinely dark at the top (a night sky, a black ceiling) can be misread on a per-frame basis; the shot-level persistence requirement is what prevents that. Bars are also frequently not exactly black after compression - use a threshold, not equality.

entries.label: Bars that animate open or closed
entries.description: The matte moves during a shot, opening up or closing down the frame as an effect.
entries.frame_evidence: Bar thickness changes smoothly across unique cels within a single shot.
entries.detector_note: Per-frame bar thickness (not per-shot); flag when the thickness series changes monotonically by more than 4 px over 3 or more unique cels with no cut.

entries.label: Background pan under a held character cel
entries.description: The background slides while the character drawing stays identical, the standard drawn-animation pan.
entries.frame_evidence: Within one unique-cel pair the background region translates while the character region has exactly zero difference.
entries.detector_note: Segment with mediapipe pose/selfie_segmentation or by flow-mode membership; measure per-region mean absolute difference. Flag when character-region mad is at the codec noise floor while background-region flow is well above it.
entries.notes: A very still live-action actor in front of a panning camera can produce the same numbers; the discriminator is that the character-region difference is exactly zero (identical pixels) rather than merely small.

entries.label: Repeating / cycled background pan
entries.description: A looping background plate is scrolled so a walk or run can continue indefinitely over a short painting.
