entries.frame_evidence: The same background content reappears at a fixed spatial period as the pan continues.
entries.detector_note: Build a rough panorama by accumulating tx, then autocorrelate the background strip along the pan axis (np.correlate or FFT-based) and look for a strong secondary peak at a lag well below the total pan distance.
entries.notes: Genuinely repetitive real environments (fence palings, colonnades, tiled corridors) autocorrelate the same way; require the peak ratio to be very high and the period to be exactly consistent.

entries.label: True 3D camera parallax
entries.description: A rendered or live camera moving through a real 3D volume, producing continuous depth-dependent flow and genuine occlusion change.
entries.frame_evidence: Flow magnitude varies smoothly with depth and background objects are progressively revealed and hidden at object silhouettes.
entries.detector_note: Dense flow with a unimodal-but-broad magnitude histogram (no discrete modes), plus occlusion detection via forward-backward flow consistency: run DIS flow both ways and mark pixels where the round trip error exceeds 1.5 px, which concentrates along silhouettes when true parallax is present.
entries.notes: High-quality 2D compositing with many layers converges on this signature; the distinction is a spectrum, not a binary.

entries.label: Arc / orbit around subject
entries.description: The camera travels along a curve around the subject, keeping it framed while the background sweeps behind it.
entries.frame_evidence: The subject's size and screen position stay roughly constant while background features translate rapidly and the subject's visible side changes.
entries.detector_note: Person-masked subject box stationary (centroid drift < 5% frame width) and near-constant scale, while the background affine shows sustained tx well above the subject's; additionally the face yaw proxy from face_mesh drifts monotonically.
entries.notes: A subject turning in place in front of a truck-moving camera gives a similar signature. The face-yaw drift direction relative to background flow direction is what distinguishes them, and on 2D the yaw proxy is unreliable.

entries.label: Synthetic whole-frame shake (post-applied)
entries.description: A shake added in compositing by translating the finished frame, rather than by moving a camera.
entries.frame_evidence: The entire frame including any letterbox or graphic overlay shifts as one rigid block, sometimes exposing blank edges.
entries.detector_note: Global affine is a pure integer or near-integer translation with residual essentially zero everywhere (inlier ratio > 0.98), and/or blank/duplicated edge columns appear at the frame boundary (check the outermost 4 px rows/columns for constant value or edge-clamp replication).
entries.notes: Distinguishing 'post shake' from 'in-camera shake' is genuinely possible only when the edges reveal it or when overlaid graphics move with the plate.

entries.label: Crane / jib move
entries.description: The camera rises or descends through a large vertical arc, usually combining pedestal with tilt and often a lateral component.
entries.frame_evidence: Large sustained vertical displacement with a simultaneously swinging horizon and changing ground-plane geometry.
entries.detector_note: Compound test: |ty| total > 40% of frame height across the shot AND horizon_y_normalised changing AND the ground-plane homography from cv2.findHomography evolving (measure the change in the recovered plane normal via cv2.decomposeHomographyMat).
entries.notes: decomposeHomographyMat needs a camera intrinsics matrix; with an assumed focal length the recovered normal is only qualitatively meaningful. Report the change, not the absolute geometry.

entries.label: Dolly in / push-in
entries.description: The camera physically moves toward the subject, so perspective changes as the frame tightens.
entries.frame_evidence: The image scales up AND near objects grow faster than far objects, with background occlusions changing.
entries.detector_note: scale_ratio > 1 sustained AND parallax present: after removing the global affine, the residual flow magnitude correlates with a depth proxy (per-tile defocus from Laplacian variance, or vertical image position on a ground plane). Correlation tested with scipy.stats.spearmanr; dolly when rho magnitude > 0.3 with p < 0.05.
entries.notes: The depth proxy is the weak link. Prefer the differential-scale test: fit separate affines to the top and bottom image halves (or to person-masked versus background regions) and compare their scale factors - a true dolly gives different scales, a zoom gives the same.

entries.label: Dolly out / pull-back reveal
entries.description: The camera physically retreats, widening the frame and revealing context.
entries.frame_evidence: The image scales down with parallax, and new scene elements enter from the frame edges rather than being merely uncovered by resampling.
entries.detector_note: scale_ratio < 1 sustained with the same parallax and differential-scale tests as camera.motion_dolly_in_push.

entries.label: Dolly-versus-zoom discrimination
entries.description: The explicit test that separates a physical move toward the subject from a focal-length change, since both produce a scale ramp.
entries.frame_evidence: Whether near and far image regions scale by the same factor.
entries.detector_note: Segment the frame into a near set (mediapipe person mask, or the sharpest tiles) and a far set (background), fit cv2.estimateAffinePartial2D independently to each, and compare scale factors: delta = log(s_near) - log(s_far). Zoom gives delta ~ 0; dolly-in gives delta > 0. Null model: run the same test on a synthetically zoomed still to fix the zero band.
entries.notes: Fails on flat subjects (a wall, a sky, a 2D cel) where near and far do not exist - the honest output there is 'indeterminate', which is a legitimate and frequent verdict.

entries.label: Dolly zoom / vertigo effect
entries.description: The camera dollies while zooming in the opposite direction, holding the subject's size constant while the background perspective violently changes.
entries.frame_evidence: The subject stays the same size in frame while the background expands or contracts around it.
entries.detector_note: Simultaneously: near_region_scale ~ 1 (subject size constant, |log| < 0.02) AND |log(far_region_scale)| growing monotonically, i.e. |differential_scale_delta| large and increasing, sustained over at least 8 unique cels.
entries.notes: This is the one camera move whose signature is genuinely unambiguous in the differential-scale space, which makes it a good sanity check on the discriminator itself.

entries.label: Drone / aerial move
entries.description: An airborne camera producing smooth multi-axis motion over a landscape from height.
entries.frame_evidence: Sustained translation over a ground plane at a high angle with very low jitter and slow, continuous heading change.
entries.detector_note: Compound gate: high angle (camera.angle_birds_eye or a horizon at/above the top edge) AND steadicam-class smoothness AND sustained multi-axis translation AND near-uniform flow magnitude across the frame indicating a large camera-to-subject distance.
entries.notes: Cannot distinguish a drone from a helicopter, a crane at height, or a virtual camera in a 3D render - and in animation the distinction has no physical referent at all. Report the observable, not the rig.

entries.label: Follow lag / operator drift
entries.description: The camera trails or overshoots the subject, so the subject drifts within the frame during a follow.
entries.frame_evidence: The subject's screen position oscillates slowly toward and away from its nominal framing position.
entries.detector_note: Low-pass the subject centroid series (scipy.signal.savgol_filter) and measure the excursion amplitude and the lag correlation between subject velocity and camera velocity (np.correlate on the two series; the argmax offset is the lag in unique cels).

entries.label: Handheld camera shake
entries.description: The camera is body-supported, producing continuous small irregular displacement across several Hz.
entries.frame_evidence: Translation traces that jitter every unique cel with no sustained direction, plus intermittent micro-roll.
entries.detector_note: Take the tx/ty series over unique cels, resample to a uniform time base using the unique-cel timestamps, detrend, then scipy.signal.welch to get the power spectrum. Handheld when significant power sits in 1-8 Hz and the high-frequency (>2 Hz) energy fraction exceeds a shot-independent threshold calibrated on a tripod reference clip.
entries.notes: Resampling matters: on animation held for 2s or 3s the effective sample rate is 8-12 Hz, so anything above about 5 Hz is at or past Nyquist and the frequency estimate is aliased. Report shake frequency for anime only with an explicit alias warning.

entries.label: Impact shake / camera hit
entries.description: A single sharp jolt of the camera synchronised with an on-screen impact, then a decay back to rest.
entries.frame_evidence: One or two unique-cel pairs with a large displacement spike, followed by a damped oscillation returning to the original framing.
entries.detector_note: Find isolated peaks in the translation magnitude series exceeding 6x the shot median (scipy.signal.find_peaks with prominence), then check that the post-peak series decays back toward the pre-peak mean within 4-10 unique cels.
entries.notes: Field order note: this is a short-window entry. In anime, impact shake is frequently a 2-3 frame offset of the whole cel and reads as a rectangular pulse rather than a damped oscillation - both should be accepted.

entries.label: Slow micro push (creeping scale)
entries.description: A very slow, near-subliminal push in or out that reads as tension rather than as a move.
entries.frame_evidence: Total scale change of only a few percent spread evenly across the whole shot.
entries.detector_note: Cumulative |log scale| between 0.01 and 0.06 across the shot, with per-pair scale changes below the single-pair noise floor but the cumulative trend significant under a linear fit (scipy.stats.linregress p < 0.01).
entries.notes: This is exactly where a detector without a null model invents moves. The linear-fit p-value against the static-reference noise distribution is mandatory, not optional.

entries.label: Multiplane parallax (discrete depth layers)
entries.description: Drawn animation fakes depth by sliding separate background, midground and foreground plates at different speeds.
entries.frame_evidence: The optical flow field is not smooth in depth but piecewise constant: several sharply bounded regions each moving at their own uniform speed.
entries.detector_note: Dense flow via cv2.DISOpticalFlow_create(cv2.DISOPTICAL_FLOW_PRESET_MEDIUM) on unique-cel pairs; histogram the horizontal flow component and count well-separated modes (peaks in a 256-bin histogram with prominence > 5% of total mass, separated by more than the intra-mode spread). Layer count = mode count.
entries.notes: Live-action true parallax gives a continuous flow gradient, not modes, so mode count is a reasonable 2D/3D discriminator - but a live-action shot with a single strong foreground object also yields two modes. Require three or more modes with hard boundaries before calling multiplane.

entries.label: Locked frame with subject motion
entries.description: The camera is still while action moves inside the frame - the baseline against which all camera motion must be measured.
entries.frame_evidence: Background features are pinned while a localised region of the frame changes.
entries.detector_note: Static global model (camera.motion_static_locked passes) AND the residual difference image has significant energy confined to a compact connected region (cv2.absdiff + cv2.threshold + connected components, largest component area < 40% of frame).
entries.notes: This is the null model for the whole movement group: if the analyser reports camera motion here, the global fit is being captured by the subject.

entries.label: Pan (horizontal rotation)
entries.description: The camera rotates left or right about its vertical axis.
entries.frame_evidence: The whole image slides horizontally with no change of scale and only weak depth-dependent flow differences.
entries.detector_note: Sustained same-sign tx across consecutive unique cels with |ty| small, scale_ratio ~ 1 and low residual parallax; direction from sign(tx) (negative tx means the frame content moves left, i.e. the camera pans right).
entries.notes: Record the direction convention explicitly - camera-right versus content-left is the classic reporting inversion in this kind of tool.

entries.label: Pan left
entries.description: The camera swings to the left, so frame content travels right.
entries.frame_evidence: Sustained positive tx of the image content across unique cels.
entries.detector_note: camera.motion_pan_horizontal with tx > 0 sustained over at least 5 unique cels and a total displacement above 3% of frame width.

entries.label: Pan right
entries.description: The camera swings to the right, so frame content travels left.
entries.frame_evidence: Sustained negative tx of the image content across unique cels.
entries.detector_note: camera.motion_pan_horizontal with tx < 0 under the same sustain criteria.

entries.label: Pedestal (vertical body rise or fall)
entries.description: The camera rises or lowers on its column without tilting.
entries.frame_evidence: Vertical image slide with the horizon staying at a constant angle but the vertical perspective of nearby objects changing.
entries.detector_note: Sustained ty with vertical parallax present and near-constant vertical convergence of scene verticals (LSD vertical VP roughly stable) - a tilt instead swings the vertical VP.

entries.label: Move ramp (acceleration and deceleration)
entries.description: The camera move eases in and out rather than running at constant speed.
entries.frame_evidence: The translation-per-frame series rises from zero, plateaus, then falls back.
entries.detector_note: First difference of the displacement series over unique cels; classify the velocity profile by fitting to constant / linear-ramp / trapezoid / ease-in-out (smoothstep) templates and reporting the best fit R-squared.
entries.notes: Unique-cel resampling distorts the velocity profile in animation because holds are irregular; interpolate onto a uniform time base using real timestamps first.

entries.label: Camera roll about the optical axis
entries.description: The camera rotates about the lens axis, spinning the frame.
entries.frame_evidence: All image content rotates about a common centre with no translation or scale change.
entries.detector_note: roll from camera.global_motion_model sustained and accumulating; verify the rotation centre is stable and near the principal point by fitting the flow field to a pure rotation.

entries.label: Rolling shutter skew / jello
entries.description: A CMOS sensor reading out line by line, so fast horizontal motion shears vertical lines.
entries.frame_evidence: Vertical edges lean consistently during fast pans and snap back when the pan stops.
entries.detector_note: During high-|tx| pairs, measure the angle of long near-vertical LSD segments as a function of image row; a linear row-dependent lean whose slope tracks pan velocity is the skew signature. Correlate lean slope against tx across the shot (scipy.stats.pearsonr).
entries.notes: Physically impossible in drawn or rendered animation unless deliberately simulated - so a positive here on an animated title is itself an interesting finding, not a bug. | TIER CORRECTED by completeness critic: All three deterministic while frame_metrics.rolling_shutter_skew - the primitive they all rest on - is marked unsupported. A direct, load-bearing contradiction: whoever writes the code will implement it three times or ze

entries.label: Move settle / overshoot at the end
entries.description: The camera overshoots its final framing and springs back, or drifts to a stop.
entries.frame_evidence: The last few unique cels of a move show a small reversal of direction before the frame comes to rest.
entries.detector_note: Detect a sign flip in the velocity series within the final 25% of the move, with reversal magnitude between 5% and 40% of peak velocity, followed by at least 3 near-static pairs.

entries.label: Snap zoom / crash zoom
entries.description: An abrupt, very fast zoom covering a large focal range in a few frames.
entries.frame_evidence: A scale ramp of tens of percent inside 2-6 unique cels, usually with radial motion blur.
entries.detector_note: Per-pair |log scale_ratio| exceeding 0.06 for at least two consecutive unique-cel pairs, with radial blur confirmed by an FFT anisotropy that is rotationally symmetric rather than directional (distinguishing it from a whip pan).
entries.notes: Order of fields matters: this entry is short-window. Frequent in anime as a 'zoom punch' on a held cel, where the underlying drawing does not change at all.

entries.label: Digital stabilisation artefacts
entries.description: Software stabilisation leaves a low-frequency non-rigid wobble and a breathing crop at the frame edges.
entries.frame_evidence: Straight lines near the frame edge bend slightly and undulate over time while the frame centre is rock-steady.
entries.detector_note: Fit a global homography and then measure the residual flow field's low-order non-rigid component: project residuals onto a 2D polynomial basis (quadratic) and track the coefficient magnitudes over time; wobble when those coefficients oscillate at 0.5-3 Hz while the rigid part is near-static.
entries.notes: Rolling-shutter jello produces a similar non-rigid residual; the separator is that stabilisation wobble persists when the camera is nominally still, whereas jello only appears during fast motion.

entries.label: Static / locked-off camera
entries.description: The camera does not move for the duration of the shot.
entries.frame_evidence: Background features hold identical image coordinates across every unique cel of the shot.
entries.detector_note: From camera.global_motion_model on unique-cel pairs: |tx|,|ty| below the sub-pixel noise floor, |log scale| < 0.002 and |roll| < 0.1 degrees for >95% of pairs. Noise floor established from a genuinely locked reference clip, not assumed.
entries.notes: On anime this must run on unique cels only; measured between duplicate held frames every shot is 'static' by construction.

entries.label: Steadicam / gimbal float
entries.description: A body-borne but stabilised move: smooth low-frequency drift with the high-frequency jitter removed.
entries.frame_evidence: The camera clearly travels through space, yet frame-to-frame displacement is smooth with no per-frame jitter.
entries.detector_note: Substantial total translation (>20% frame width) with low high-frequency energy fraction (<0.15) and low jerk: third difference of the translation series RMS below the handheld reference. Essentially handheld's complement in the same spectral space.
entries.notes: Digitally stabilised handheld (warp stabiliser) looks identical here; check camera.stabilisation_warp_wobble to separate them.

entries.label: Tilt down
entries.description: The camera pivots downward.
entries.frame_evidence: Frame content travels upward while the horizon rises toward and past the top of frame.
entries.detector_note: ty < 0 sustained with the corroborating horizon trend.

entries.label: Tilt up
entries.description: The camera pivots upward, revealing what is above.
entries.frame_evidence: Frame content travels downward across unique cels while the horizon exits the bottom of frame.
entries.detector_note: ty > 0 sustained; corroborate with the horizon_y_normalised trend from camera.horizon_line_height moving downward.

entries.label: Tilt (vertical rotation)
entries.description: The camera rotates up or down about its horizontal axis.
entries.frame_evidence: The whole image slides vertically at constant scale.
entries.detector_note: Sustained same-sign ty with |tx| small and scale_ratio ~ 1; separate from pedestal by the presence or absence of vertical parallax (see camera.motion_pedestal).

entries.label: Tracking / following shot
entries.description: The camera moves to keep a moving subject in a stable place in frame.
entries.frame_evidence: The subject's bounding box holds position and size while the background streams past.
entries.detector_note: mediapipe pose/face box centroid variance across unique cels below 4% of frame width, while |background tx| accumulates beyond 25% of frame width; the two must be measured on the same unique-cel pairs.
entries.notes: Requires the subject to be detectable throughout; a subject the pose model loses mid-shot silently breaks the lock metric. Log the detection coverage fraction alongside.

entries.label: Truck / crab (lateral translation)
entries.description: The camera body slides sideways rather than rotating.
entries.frame_evidence: Horizontal image slide accompanied by strong depth-dependent parallax - foreground sweeps faster than background.
entries.detector_note: Sustained tx as in a pan, but the post-affine residual flow shows a monotonic horizontal-speed gradient with depth; test via per-tile flow magnitude from cv2.DISOpticalFlow versus tile sharpness rank (scipy.stats.spearmanr).
entries.notes: A pan and a truck are the same tx signature; only parallax separates them, and a flat backdrop makes them identical. In 2D, a multiplane truck and a multiplane pan are also the same construction.

entries.label: Whip pan / swish pan
entries.description: A very fast pan that smears the image into directional blur, often used to hide a cut.
entries.frame_evidence: A short burst of very large horizontal displacement with heavy anisotropic motion blur along the pan axis.
entries.detector_note: Detect the displacement burst (|tx| > 8% of frame width per unique-cel pair) AND confirm directional blur: the FFT magnitude spectrum of the frame collapses to a ridge perpendicular to the motion, measurable as the anisotropy ratio of the second-moment matrix of np.abs(np.fft.fftshift(np.fft.fft2(gray))).
entries.notes: Optical flow itself fails during a whip - features are destroyed by blur - so the blur-spectrum test is the primary evidence and the flow magnitude is a lower bound. Whip pans are also frequently the cut point, so the shot segmenter must not split mid-whip.

entries.label: Zoom in (optical, no camera translation)
entries.description: The focal length lengthens, magnifying the image without any change of viewpoint.
entries.frame_evidence: Everything scales about a single centre with no parallax whatsoever and no change in occlusion relationships.
entries.detector_note: scale_ratio > 1 with the post-affine residual flow indistinguishable from noise and the top/bottom-half differential scale within the noise floor; the flow field must be purely radial about a fixed centre (fit the centre by least squares and check its stability across the shot).
entries.notes: In 2D animation nearly all 'push-ins' are literal digital scale-ups of a flat cel and will correctly measure as zooms even where the intent reads as a dolly. Report the measurement and the ambiguity, not an intent.

entries.label: Zoom out
entries.description: The focal length shortens, shrinking the image about a fixed centre with no viewpoint change.
entries.frame_evidence: Uniform de-magnification about a stable centre with zero parallax.
entries.detector_note: As camera.motion_zoom_in with scale_ratio < 1.

entries.label: Pillarbox bars (left and right)
entries.description: Black bars at the sides, from a narrower image in a wider container.
entries.frame_evidence: Columns at the left and right with near-zero luminance and variance across the shot.
entries.detector_note: Column-wise version of camera.letterbox_bars_horizontal.

entries.label: Upscaled source (no real detail at nominal resolution)
entries.description: The file's nominal resolution exceeds the real detail present, from an upscale somewhere in the chain.
entries.frame_evidence: The frequency spectrum has no energy above a cutoff well below Nyquist, with a hard shelf rather than a natural rolloff.
entries.detector_note: Radially averaged power spectrum of the luminance channel (np.fft.fft2 then radial binning); look for a sharp knee followed by a floor. Report the effective resolution as the knee frequency scaled to pixels.
entries.notes: Heavy denoise, low-bitrate compression and genuine defocus all remove high frequencies. The tell for upscaling specifically is the shelf's sharpness plus its constancy across every shot in the file; a per-shot positive alone is weak.

entries.label: Shake amplitude in pixels
entries.description: The magnitude of the camera's involuntary displacement, reported as an RMS in pixels and as a fraction of frame width.
entries.frame_evidence: The spread of the detrended translation series across the shot.
entries.detector_note: np.sqrt(np.mean(detrended_tx**2 + detrended_ty**2)) over unique cels, normalised by frame width; report both raw pixels and percent so resolutions are comparable.

entries.label: Shake dominant frequency
entries.description: The characteristic rate of the camera's jitter, which separates a nervous handheld from a slow float.
entries.frame_evidence: The peak of the power spectrum of the translation series.
entries.detector_note: scipy.signal.welch(detrended_series, fs=effective_unique_cel_rate, nperseg=min(64,N)); take the argmax frequency and the spectral centroid.
entries.notes: Meaningless below roughly 20 unique cels in the shot; emit null rather than a number for short shots.

entries.label: Hard cut (shot segmentation primitive)
entries.description: The instantaneous frame boundary between two shots, needed because every 'shot'-window camera metric is undefined across a cut.
entries.frame_evidence: A single frame pair where the HSV histogram correlation collapses and the global affine fit fails to find inliers.
entries.detector_note: Per unique-cel pair: cv2.calcHist 3D HSV (8,8,8) + cv2.compareHist(..., cv2.HISTCMP_CORREL); combine with the RANSAC inlier ratio from cv2.estimateAffinePartial2D. Cut when correl drops below mu-4*sigma of the shot-local distribution AND inlier_ratio < 0.25. Null model: run the same statistic on a known single-take clip to fix the false-alarm rate.
entries.notes: Fast whip pans, strobe lighting, and full-frame anime impact flashes all mimic a cut. Anime cross-dissolves and white flashes are NOT hard cuts and must not split a shot, or every dissolve invents two bogus camera moves.

entries.label: Close-up (head and shoulders)
entries.description: The head dominates the frame.
entries.frame_evidence: Face bounding box occupying roughly 30-60% of frame height with the full face-mesh contour inside frame.
entries.detector_note: mediapipe.solutions.face_mesh(max_num_faces=4, refine_landmarks=True); face_h/frame_h in [0.30,0.60) and >=95% of the 468 points inside the image rectangle.
entries.notes: face_mesh on 2D anime is unreliable - large eyes and absent nose bridge shift or drop the mesh. For 2D, prefer the face-detection box plus a VLM confirmation rather than the mesh geometry.

entries.label: Shot size changes during the shot
entries.description: The framing tightens or loosens across a single uncut shot, without regard to whether it was a zoom or a dolly.
entries.frame_evidence: The global scale factor accumulates monotonically across the shot while no cut is detected.
entries.detector_note: Cumulative product of scale_ratio from camera.global_motion_model across unique cels; flag when |log(cumulative_scale)| > 0.15 and the sign is consistent for >70% of pairs.
entries.notes: Does not distinguish zoom from dolly; that separation is camera.motion_dolly_vs_zoom_discriminator.

entries.label: Extreme close-up (feature fills frame)
entries.description: A single facial feature or small detail fills the frame, with the head cropped on multiple sides.
entries.frame_evidence: Face-mesh points spill past two or more frame edges, or an eye/mouth region alone spans more than half the frame width.
entries.detector_note: face_mesh with facemesh_inside_fraction < 0.6 and face_h/frame_h >= 0.6; if the mesh fails entirely, fall back to a VLM confirmation on the full frame (see camera.shot_size_insert_detail).

entries.label: Extreme wide shot
entries.description: Environment dominates the frame and any human figure is a small element within it.
entries.frame_evidence: A full-body figure whose bounding box is under about 15% of frame height, with large landscape or architecture filling the remainder.
entries.detector_note: mediapipe.solutions.pose(static_image_mode=True, model_complexity=1); bbox over landmarks 0-32 with visibility>0.5; classify when bbox_h/frame_h < 0.15 AND head (0) plus both ankles (27,28) are inside frame. If pose returns nothing, do NOT assert EWS - route to camera.shot_size_no_subject.
entries.notes: mediapipe pose is trained on photoreal humans; recall collapses on stylised 2D linework and on figures below ~60px, so a missed detection is exactly the case an EWS produces. Treat pose-negative frames as unknown scale, not as evidence.

entries.label: Full shot (head to toe, frame-filling)
entries.description: The figure fills the frame vertically from just above the head to just below the feet.
entries.frame_evidence: Ankle landmarks within the bottom 15% of frame and head landmark within the top 15%, body box above 55% of frame height.
entries.detector_note: mediapipe pose; bbox_h/frame_h >= 0.55, landmark 0 y < 0.15 and max(y of 27,28) > 0.85 in normalised coords.

entries.label: Group shot (three or more)
entries.description: Three or more subjects share the frame.
entries.frame_evidence: Three or more distinct face or person detections at similar depth.
entries.detector_note: mediapipe face_detection (model_selection=1) count >= 3, deduplicated by IoU>0.4.
entries.notes: Undercounts crowds severely; treat >=3 as 'group' and never report an exact crowd size from this.

entries.label: Insert / detail shot (no person)
entries.description: A tight shot of an object, hand-held prop, screen or texture, carrying no full human subject.
entries.frame_evidence: No face or pose detection, shallow depth of field, and a single large in-focus object occupying the frame centre.
entries.detector_note: Gate on pose==None and face==None and a bimodal tile sharpness map (cv2.Laplacian var per 8x8 tile), then ask qwen2.5vl on the centre 60% crop.
entries.vlm_question: Is this a close view of a single object or a small detail, with no whole person visible? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Do not send this to moondream if the object is a screen, sign or page - it will confabulate the text and drag the answer with it.

entries.label: Medium shot (waist)
entries.description: The figure is framed from roughly the waist up.
entries.frame_evidence: Shoulder and elbow landmarks present, hip landmarks at or below the bottom frame edge.
entries.detector_note: Lowest-visible-joint rule: shoulders (11,12) and elbows (13,14) visible; hips (23,24) absent or y>=0.98.

entries.label: Medium close-up (chest)
entries.description: Head and upper chest fill the frame; shoulders are visible but arms are largely out.
entries.frame_evidence: Face box between roughly 15% and 30% of frame height with both shoulder landmarks still inside frame.
entries.detector_note: mediapipe face_detection or face_mesh for the face box + pose landmarks 11/12 for shoulder presence; band 0.15 <= face_h/frame_h < 0.30.

entries.label: Medium-full / cowboy shot (mid-thigh)
entries.description: The figure is cut by the frame edge somewhere between knee and mid-thigh.
entries.frame_evidence: Hip landmarks are inside frame while knee or ankle landmarks fall outside the bottom edge.
entries.detector_note: Lowest-visible-joint rule: hips (23,24) visible with y<0.95, knees (25,26) either absent or y>=1.0. This joint-cut rule is far more stable than any area threshold.
entries.notes: Occlusion by scenery (a desk, a wall) produces the same landmark pattern as a frame cut. Cross-check that the missing joint is beyond the frame boundary rather than merely low-visibility inside it.

entries.label: Shot-size jump across a cut
entries.description: Consecutive shots of the same subject differ in scale by too little (a jump cut feel) or by a large deliberate step.
entries.frame_evidence: Face-height ratio changes sharply at a cut boundary while the subject appears to be the same person.
entries.detector_note: Needs a re-identification embedding to assert 'same subject' across the cut; we have no face-recognition model installed (insightface absent), so identity cannot be asserted today.
entries.notes: Logged as a known blind spot. Without re-id, a cut to a different character at a different size is indistinguishable from a size jump on the same character.

entries.label: Empty frame / no subject present
entries.description: The frame contains no human figure at all - landscape, architecture, texture or object only.
entries.frame_evidence: Neither face nor pose detection fires anywhere in the frame across the whole shot.
entries.detector_note: pose==None AND face_detection empty on every unique cel of the shot; require persistence across the shot to avoid a single-frame miss being reported as an empty frame.
entries.notes: Conflates 'no person in the scene' with 'detector cannot see this person' - which is the dominant failure on 2D and on very wide or very dark shots. Log it as detector-negative, not as a claim about the content.

entries.label: Two shot
entries.description: Two subjects framed together at comparable scale.
entries.frame_evidence: Exactly two person detections whose bounding-box heights are within roughly 40% of each other.
entries.detector_note: Iterate mediapipe face_detection boxes (or pose instances via repeated ROI passes); require count==2 and 0.6 <= h_a/h_b <= 1.67.
entries.notes: mediapipe pose is single-person by default; multi-person requires either face_detection boxes or a tiling pass, and both under-count in crowds and on stylised 2D.

entries.label: Wide shot (full figure with air)
entries.description: The whole body is visible with clear space above and below it, establishing the subject in its space.
entries.frame_evidence: Head-to-ankle landmarks all inside frame and the body box spanning roughly 15-55% of frame height.
entries.detector_note: As above; band 0.15 <= bbox_h/frame_h < 0.55 with landmarks 0, 27 and 28 all visible and at least 5% margin from the frame edges.
entries.notes: Band edges are conventions, not physics; report the continuous ratio alongside the label so a downstream consumer can re-band.

entries.label: Continuous subject scale ratio
entries.description: The raw, unbanded measure of how much of the frame the subject occupies, from which any shot-size taxonomy can be derived.
entries.frame_evidence: Face height and body height as fractions of frame height on every unique cel.
entries.detector_note: Emit face_h/frame_h and body_bbox_h/frame_h per unique cel; report median and interquartile range across the shot.
entries.notes: This is the honest primitive; the banded shot-size entries above are interpretations layered on it.

entries.label: Unique-cel index (temporal substrate)
entries.description: The per-frame flag marking whether a frame is a NEW drawing/render or a duplicate hold, which every temporal camera metric must be computed on.
entries.frame_evidence: Two consecutive decoded frames are bit-near-identical: mean absolute difference of the 64x64 grayscale downsample is below the codec-noise floor.
entries.detector_note: Decode with cv2.VideoCapture; per frame g=cv2.resize(cv2.cvtColor(f,COLOR_BGR2GRAY),(64,64)); mad=np.mean(np.abs(g.astype(np.int16)-prev)); hold if mad < thr where thr is the 5th percentile of the shot's own mad distribution (never a fixed constant). Emit unique_indices[] and hold_run_lengths[]; ALL pan/tilt/shake/zoom metrics index into unique_indices only.
entries.notes: This is the single most important entry in the domain. Anime on 2s/3s gives exactly-zero optical flow between duplicate frames; that zero is an artefact. Live action with a locked camera also yields near-zero mad, so cel_hold_ratio alone cannot distinguish 'animated on 2s' from 'static live-action shot' - use estimated_drawings_per_second together with residual flow energy on the unique pairs.

entries.label: Physically impossible camera move
entries.description: A move that no physical rig could execute - passing through solid geometry, an infinite crane, a continuous impossible orbit - marking a virtual camera.
entries.frame_evidence: The camera passes through an object, or executes a sustained move with no plausible rig support.
entries.detector_note: No geometric test exists in our stack; ask qwen2.5vl on sampled frames of a long uncut move, gated on the shot having a long continuous move with no cut.
entries.vlm_question: Does the camera in this sequence pass through a solid object or move in a way a real camera on a crane or dolly could not? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: A weak, whole-frame VLM question against the crop rule; treat any positive as a flag for human review, never as a finding. In fully animated material every camera is virtual anyway, so the entry is only interesting for live-action-styled or hybrid work.

entries.label: Jagged / aliased edges
entries.description: Insufficient edge anti-aliasing leaves visible stair-steps on near-horizontal or near-vertical edges.
entries.frame_evidence: A straight edge is built from discrete pixel steps of equal length rather than a smooth sub-pixel ramp.
entries.detector_note: Along Hough-detected straight edges at angles 5-40 degrees from an axis, sample the edge transition profile; count steps where the transition happens within a single pixel and report their fraction of the edge length.
entries.notes: Upscaling and sharpening re-create hard transitions on already-antialiased source; record the delivery resolution alongside.

entries.label: Moire on fine texture
entries.description: A periodic texture beats against the pixel grid, producing large false interference bands.
entries.frame_evidence: Broad curved rainbow or light/dark bands appear across a finely striped surface that has no such bands in reality.
entries.detector_note: Detect regions whose 2D FFT holds a high-frequency peak near Nyquist together with a strong low-frequency envelope peak; report the ratio and the envelope wavelength.
entries.notes: Chroma subsampling in the codec creates similar coloured banding on fine detail.

entries.label: Specular sparkle / firefly highlights
entries.description: Under-sampled sharp speculars flash on and off on individual pixels across frames.
entries.frame_evidence: Isolated single-pixel or few-pixel bright dots appear and vanish on a glossy surface with no consistent motion.
entries.detector_note: Detect pixels above the 99.9th percentile that are local maxima with an area under 6px, then track their persistence; report the fraction whose lifetime is exactly one unique frame.
entries.notes: Sensor hot pixels, dust and codec ringing produce the same isolated maxima.

entries.label: Temporal shimmer / crawling edges
entries.description: High-frequency detail samples differently each frame, so edges and fine texture sparkle during motion.
entries.frame_evidence: Fine detail such as railings or foliage sparkles and crawls between frames rather than translating cleanly.
entries.detector_note: Motion-compensate consecutive unique frames with Farneback flow, then report the residual high-pass energy as a fraction of the source high-pass energy; shimmer shows a residual ratio above 0.35 concentrated on high-frequency regions.
entries.notes: MUST run on unique-cel indices: between duplicate frames the residual is exactly zero and shimmer reads as absent. Flow failure on fine texture also inflates the residual.

entries.label: Ambient occlusion contact darkening
entries.description: Creases and contact points darken because ambient light is occluded there.
entries.frame_evidence: A thin dark gradient hugs the junction between two surfaces, strongest at the seam and fading outward over a few pixels.
entries.detector_note: At detected object-contact boundaries, sample luma along the boundary normal with cv2.distanceTransform and fit the falloff; report the darkening depth and the 1/e width.
entries.notes: Genuine cast shadow at a contact is the same shape; AO is distinguished only by being light-direction-independent, which needs multiple views.

entries.label: AO halo / white outline artefact
entries.description: SSAO with a too-large radius leaves a bright halo just outside a foreground silhouette.
entries.frame_evidence: A bright band of a few pixels traces the outside of a foreground object against a darker background.
entries.detector_note: Sample the background luma profile outward from the object mask boundary; flag a local maximum 2-8px out that exceeds the background plateau by >4 DN, present around >40% of the silhouette.
entries.notes: Sharpening halos and matte-line artefacts produce an identical profile; correlate with the sharpening detector before attributing.

entries.label: Missing AO / floating object look
entries.description: An object sits on a surface with no contact darkening, so it appears to hover.
entries.frame_evidence: The join between object and ground shows no gradient at all, luminance is continuous straight across the contact line.
entries.detector_note: Same boundary-normal profile as cg_3d.ambient_occlusion_contact_darkening, flagged when the darkening depth is below 2 DN while other object-ground contacts in the same frame exceed 8 DN.
entries.notes: Requires at least one in-frame reference contact; on a single-object frame there is no null and the metric is unusable.

entries.label: AO too strong / dirty crevices
entries.description: AO is dialled up until every crease reads as grime, flattening the render.
entries.frame_evidence: Every geometric crease in the frame carries the same dark band regardless of the light direction or material.
entries.detector_note: Correlate the darkening-depth map at all detected creases against the local light direction estimate; a near-zero correlation with uniformly high depth across many creases indicates over-applied AO.
entries.notes: The light-direction estimate from a single frame is crude; this is a soft indicator.

entries.label: Backface / inverted normal visible
entries.description: A surface with flipped normals or no backface culling renders black or inside-out.
entries.frame_evidence: A patch of an object is uniformly black or lit opposite to its neighbours, bounded by a hard polygonal edge.
entries.detector_note: Find polygonal-bounded regions inside an object whose mean luma is below 15% of the object mean while their boundary matches the object's straight-segment structure rather than a shadow's soft edge.
entries.notes: Deep self-shadow gives the same darkness; only the hard polygonal boundary separates them.

entries.label: Cloth passes through the floor/prop
entries.description: A skirt, cape or tablecloth sinks through collision geometry.
entries.frame_evidence: The lower edge of a garment disappears below the visible ground contact line rather than resting or bunching on it.
entries.detector_note: Detect the ground contact line (strong horizontal edge under the character's mediapipe ankle landmarks 27/28), then crop the garment hem region and ask the Qwen3-VL judge.
entries.vlm_question: Does the bottom edge of the clothing sink into or pass through the floor instead of resting on top of it? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Deep shadow at the hem looks the same as sinking; the geometric part is only a prior.

entries.label: Cloth self-intersection / poke-through
entries.description: Cloth passes through itself or the body pokes through the garment.
entries.frame_evidence: A patch of skin or an inner surface appears inside the garment silhouette for a few frames and then disappears.
entries.detector_note: Flag transient regions where the skin-tone mask (YCrCb ellipse) appears strictly inside the clothing mask and persists <8 unique frames, then confirm on a tight crop with the Qwen3-VL judge.
entries.vlm_question: Is part of the body poking through the clothing, so skin appears where fabric should be? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: THE CROP RULE: full-frame this is invisible to the judge. Skin-tone masks fail on non-human skin tones and on stylised palettes.

entries.label: Cloth simulation
entries.description: Garment or flag geometry driven by a cloth solver rather than skinned to bones.
entries.frame_evidence: Fold lines within the garment appear, travel and dissolve independently of the body's bone motion.
entries.detector_note: Inside a mediapipe-derived torso ROI, track ridge lines from a Frangi/Hessian filter (skimage.filters.frangi) and measure their motion relative to the torso's rigid transform; cloth folds move in the residual.
entries.notes: Drawn 2D cloth folds also live in the residual; and a skinned garment with baked fold normal maps looks static in the residual and reads as 'no sim'.

entries.label: Cloth reads as wrong material
entries.description: Fabric moves like cardboard, plastic or rubber instead of the material it is textured as.
entries.frame_evidence: A garment that looks like silk swings as a single rigid plate with no secondary folds.
entries.detector_note: Crop the garment across a short motion window into a 2x2 contact sheet and ask the Qwen3-VL judge; deterministic support is only the fold-count-per-area statistic.
entries.vlm_question: Does the fabric in this image move like stiff cardboard or plastic rather than like soft cloth? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Material judgement from stills is unreliable; the contact-sheet framing helps but the VLM still guesses.

entries.label: Cloth over-stretch / texture smear
entries.description: Cloth constraints fail and the fabric stretches, smearing its texture.
entries.frame_evidence: The garment's weave or print texture becomes locally anisotropically stretched in one direction for a few frames.
entries.detector_note: Local structure tensor anisotropy (skimage.feature.structure_tensor eigenvalue ratio) inside the garment mask, tracked over unique frames; flag transient spikes above 3x the shot baseline.
entries.notes: Motion blur creates identical directional anisotropy; must be gated on low local flow magnitude.

entries.label: Contact shadow present
entries.description: A hard dark shadow directly beneath an object anchoring it to the ground.
entries.frame_evidence: A dark region adjoining the object's lowest silhouette point, sharp near the contact and softening with distance.
entries.detector_note: Threshold-below-local-median region adjoining the bottom of the object mask; report its area relative to the object footprint and its edge-gradient sharpness at the contact point.
entries.notes: On a dark floor the shadow is invisible; on a busy floor the threshold picks up texture.

entries.label: Denoiser eats fine strands
entries.description: Fine structures such as hair, fur and fine cloth are removed by the denoiser and read as a soft mass.
entries.frame_evidence: Hair at the silhouette is a smooth grey wedge with no individual strands even though the frame is otherwise sharp.
entries.detector_note: Gabor-bank filament energy in the hair annulus compared against the sharpest region of the same frame; flag when hair filament energy falls below 15% of the frame's 95th-percentile band-pass energy.
entries.notes: Shallow depth of field on the hair produces the same reading; require the face to be in focus in the same crop.

entries.label: Denoiser smearing / waxy patches
entries.description: An AI or bilateral denoiser removes real detail along with noise, leaving smooth plasticky patches.
entries.frame_evidence: Patches of the image have near-zero high-frequency content while neighbouring patches of the same material retain texture.
entries.detector_note: Patchwise high-frequency energy map (8x8 blocks, band-pass via cv2.Laplacian variance); report the bimodality of the energy distribution within a single material region and the area fraction below the material's own 10th percentile.
entries.notes: Defocus, motion blur and low-bitrate encoding all remove high-frequency energy in patches; the within-material comparison is the only control.

entries.label: Denoiser temporal blotching
entries.description: A temporal denoiser's patch decisions change between frames, so smooth blotches crawl over the image.
entries.frame_evidence: Soft blotches of differing sharpness migrate slowly across a static surface between frames.
entries.detector_note: Track the patchwise high-frequency energy map across motion-compensated unique frames and report the temporal standard deviation of per-patch energy on regions with near-zero flow.
entries.notes: Variable-bitrate encoding does exactly this too; the two are practically indistinguishable in a delivered file.

entries.label: True displacement on the silhouette
entries.description: Real geometric displacement changes the object's outline, unlike a normal map.
entries.frame_evidence: The silhouette itself is bumpy and irregular at the same scale as the surface's visible relief.
entries.detector_note: Compare the boundary roughness (RMS of the mask boundary's deviation from a smoothed spline) against the interior relief scale from band-pass energy; displacement gives comparable magnitudes, a normal map gives a smooth boundary with rough interior.
entries.notes: Anti-aliasing and low resolution smooth the silhouette and bias this toward 'normal map'.

entries.label: Foot sinks into the floor
entries.description: A character's foot passes below the ground plane instead of resting on it.
entries.frame_evidence: The ankle is lower than the established ground contact line and no part of the shoe sole is visible.
entries.detector_note: Estimate the ground line from the shot's median mediapipe ankle-landmark (27/28) y over frames where the character is standing, then flag frames whose ankle y exceeds that line by more than 1.5x the ankle-landmark noise sigma while the character is not descending stairs.
entries.notes: mediapipe ankle landmarks are noisy under occlusion and long garments; without the sigma null this fires constantly.

entries.label: Frame-interpolation warping
entries.description: Optical-flow frame interpolation produces liquid warping around fast edges and thin structures.
entries.frame_evidence: On a single frame, limbs or thin objects appear rubbery and locally bent, with the distortion vanishing on the neighbouring frames.
entries.detector_note: Detect frames whose forward and backward flow fields disagree strongly (forward-backward consistency error above 3px) in localised patches, and whose edge structure is locally curved relative to both neighbours.
entries.notes: Also fires on genuine fast non-rigid motion; a duplicate-frame map from the unique-cel index helps, because interpolated content breaks the 2s/3s duplicate pattern.

entries.label: Fur shell-layer banding
entries.description: Shell-based fur shows concentric translucent layers instead of continuous strands, visible at grazing angles.
entries.frame_evidence: At the silhouette, fur reads as several discrete parallel translucent bands offset from the surface.
entries.detector_note: Sample the intensity profile along the outward surface normal at the silhouette (normals from the mask gradient) and FFT the 1D profile for a peak at a period of 2-12px repeating across many boundary samples.
entries.notes: Only visible at grazing silhouettes; the interior gives nothing.

entries.label: Geometry clipping / interpenetration
entries.description: Two meshes pass through each other, most often hands into props or feet into floors.
entries.frame_evidence: An object's silhouette is truncated by another surface with no occlusion contact, so it appears buried.
entries.detector_note: Locate hand/foot landmarks with mediapipe (15/16, 27/28) and crop that neighbourhood; put the crop to the Qwen3-VL judge via vlm_inspector.py.
entries.vlm_question: Is one solid object sunk into or passing through another solid object in this crop? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: THE CROP RULE is essential; the judge scores full frames as clean. Depth cannot be resolved deterministically.

entries.label: Hair clumping / spiky groom
entries.description: Strands bunch into hard pointed clumps, the classic under-tuned groom look.
entries.frame_evidence: The hair silhouette shows repeated sharp triangular spikes rather than a soft feathered edge.
entries.detector_note: Boundary curvature histogram of the hair mask: count high-positive-curvature extrema per 100px of boundary and report their mean apex angle from cv2.approxPolyDP vertices.
entries.notes: Anime hair is spiky by design; this must be gated by applies_to/medium before being read as a defect.

entries.label: Hair frizz / strand aliasing flicker
entries.description: Sub-pixel strands alias, so the hair edge sparkles frame to frame.
entries.frame_evidence: High-frequency binary speckle at the hair silhouette that changes pattern every frame while the head barely moves.
entries.detector_note: After motion-compensating with the head's affine transform, compute per-pixel temporal variance in a 5px band around the hair mask boundary; report the ratio to the interior variance.
entries.notes: Must run on UNIQUE-CEL indices; duplicated frames give exactly zero variance and mask real flicker.

entries.label: Hair / fur strand simulation
entries.description: Individual hair strands or curves driven by a dynamics solver with lag behind the head.
entries.frame_evidence: Fine directional filaments at the head silhouette whose tips lag the head's motion by several frames.
entries.detector_note: Gabor/steerable-filter energy (cv2.getGaborKernel bank, 8 orientations) in an annulus outside the mediapipe face oval; cross-correlate the annulus flow against the face-landmark velocity to measure the lag in unique frames.
entries.notes: Requires resolution: below roughly 30px of hair width the strands are sub-pixel and only a soft mass is visible.

entries.label: Hair passes through shoulders/body
entries.description: Hair curves lack body collision and sink into the shoulders, neck or face.
entries.frame_evidence: Strands terminate abruptly at the shoulder silhouette with no occlusion contact, or reappear on the far side.
entries.detector_note: Crop the neck/shoulder junction using mediapipe pose landmarks 11/12 and the face oval, and ask the Qwen3-VL judge.
entries.vlm_question: Does the hair sink into or pass through the shoulder or face instead of lying on top of it? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Very hard for a small VLM; expect low recall.

entries.label: LOD pop
entries.description: An object switches level of detail on a single frame, changing silhouette or texture detail instantly.
entries.frame_evidence: Between two consecutive unique frames the object's fine detail and outline change abruptly while its position barely moves.
entries.detector_note: On unique-cel indices, motion-compensate the object crop and measure the step change in band-pass energy and in silhouette_roughness_rms; flag a single-frame step exceeding 4 sigma of the shot's own frame-to-frame distribution.
entries.notes: A focus pull produces the same detail step; correlate with the global sharpness trace before reporting.

entries.label: Missing or metronomic blinks
entries.description: A CG face never blinks, or blinks on a perfectly regular timer.
entries.frame_evidence: No eyelid closure occurs across a long shot, or closures occur at exactly equal intervals.
entries.detector_note: Eye aspect ratio from mediapipe face-mesh eyelid landmarks over unique frames; detect closures as EAR minima below 0.6x the open baseline and report the count plus the coefficient of variation of the inter-blink intervals.
entries.notes: Blinks last 3-6 frames at 24fps, so on 2s/3s anime a blink can fall entirely between unique cels and be missed.

entries.label: Candy-wrapper twist
entries.description: A twisted forearm or wrist collapses to a pinched waist because the twist is carried by a single bone.
entries.frame_evidence: Mid-forearm narrows to a waist while both ends stay full, and the surface texture spirals into that waist.
entries.detector_note: Sample limb width along the bone axis between mediapipe elbow(13/14) and wrist(15/16); prefilter on a local minimum of width more than 30% below both endpoints, then confirm on the crop with the Qwen3-VL judge.
entries.vlm_question: Does the forearm narrow to a pinched twisted waist in the middle, like a twisted sweet wrapper? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Sleeves and bracelets create legitimate width minima; the prefilter alone false-positives constantly.

entries.label: Dead-eyed / non-tracking gaze
entries.description: Eyes stay locked forward with no saccades or convergence, a strong uncanny-valley cue.
entries.frame_evidence: The iris centres hold a constant offset within the eye openings across many frames while the head turns.
entries.detector_note: mediapipe face-mesh iris landmarks (468-477) expressed relative to the eye-corner landmarks; report the temporal variance of that normalised offset and the count of step changes exceeding a saccade threshold.
entries.notes: Iris landmarks need the refine_landmarks flag and a face larger than roughly 120px; they are unreliable on stylised eyes.

entries.label: Lip-sync timing offset
entries.description: Mouth shapes lead or lag the audio, or fail to correspond to it at all.
entries.frame_evidence: The mouth opens on frames where the audio is silent, or stays closed through a loud plosive.
entries.detector_note: Mouth-opening signal from mediapipe face-mesh upper/lower lip landmarks cross-correlated against the audio envelope extracted with ffmpeg (astats/loudnorm print, or a raw PCM RMS envelope); report the lag at peak correlation and the peak value.
entries.notes: Off-screen dialogue and music destroy the envelope correlation; requires a clean single-speaker on-screen segment.

entries.label: Frozen / default hand pose
entries.description: Fingers hold one rigid default pose for the whole shot because no hand capture existed.
entries.frame_evidence: The hand's finger configuration is identical frame after frame while the arm moves through a large range.
entries.detector_note: mediapipe hands 21-landmark set normalised into the wrist frame (translation and scale removed); report the temporal standard deviation of the normalised landmark vector over unique frames, flagging values near the detector's own noise floor while the wrist moves substantially.
entries.notes: mediapipe hands frequently fails on stylised or small hands; require detection confidence above 0.6 on >70% of frames.

entries.label: Foot slide / skating
entries.description: A planted foot drifts across the ground during its stance phase, the classic retarget failure.
entries.frame_evidence: During the frames when the foot is visibly flat on the floor, its contact point translates horizontally relative to the ground texture.
entries.detector_note: Identify stance frames as those where the mediapipe ankle landmark (27/28) vertical velocity is near zero and the ankle is at its lowest; measure the ankle's horizontal displacement over the stance minus the global camera translation from cv2.estimateAffinePartial2D on background ORB matches.
entries.notes: Requires the camera-motion subtraction or every dolly shot reports slide; mediapipe ankle jitter sets the noise floor, so report the sigma null alongside.

entries.label: Hip hitch / retarget proportion error
entries.description: Motion retargeted to a differently proportioned skeleton makes the hips rise, sink or sway wrongly.
entries.frame_evidence: Hip height oscillates out of phase with the footfalls, or the pelvis floats above where the leg length allows.
entries.detector_note: Ratio of the mediapipe hip midpoint (23/24) height above the estimated ground line to the measured leg length; flag frames where the ratio exceeds 1.0 (hips higher than a fully extended leg) or where its phase against the ankle-contact signal is inverted.
entries.notes: Camera perspective changes the apparent leg length; needs an approximately constant framing across the measured window.

entries.label: IK pop / snap
entries.description: An IK solver switches solution branch, snapping a limb to a new pose in a single frame.
entries.frame_evidence: An elbow or knee flips its bend direction or jumps several degrees between two consecutive unique frames while everything else moves smoothly.
entries.detector_note: Per-frame joint angle from mediapipe triples (shoulder-elbow-wrist 11-13-15, hip-knee-ankle 23-25-27); flag a single-unique-frame angle step exceeding 6 sigma of that joint's own frame-to-frame step distribution for the shot.
entries.notes: mediapipe left/right limb swaps and momentary occlusion produce identical single-frame steps; require landmark visibility above 0.7 on both frames.

entries.label: Mocap jitter / unsmoothed marker noise
entries.description: Raw capture noise survives into the animation, so joints buzz at a high frequency.
entries.frame_evidence: Joint positions vibrate by a pixel or two every frame on top of the intended smooth motion.
entries.detector_note: High-pass the mediapipe joint trajectories (subtract a Savitzky-Golay smoothed version via scipy.signal.savgol_filter, window 7, order 2) and report the residual RMS per joint, normalised by torso length and compared against the static-subject landmark noise floor.
entries.notes: mediapipe's own estimation noise is of the same magnitude as the artefact; without measuring the noise floor on a genuinely still subject this metric is meaningless.

entries.label: Joint collapse / skinning pinch
entries.description: Bad weights make an elbow, shoulder or knee lose volume and crease into a pinch when bent.
entries.frame_evidence: At a bent joint the limb's silhouette width drops sharply and a hard crease appears where the mesh folds in on itself.
entries.detector_note: Use the mediapipe joint position to crop a 1.5x-limb-width box around the bend, measure limb width perpendicular to the bone as a prefilter (drop >35% versus the straight-limb reference), and put the crop to the Qwen3-VL judge.
entries.vlm_question: Does the arm or leg at this joint look pinched, collapsed or crushed rather than keeping its normal thickness? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: THE CROP RULE: a full frame hides the pinch. Loose clothing masks the effect entirely.

entries.label: No weight shift / floating gait
entries.description: A walk lacks the vertical bob and lateral hip sway that carrying body weight produces.
entries.frame_evidence: The pelvis translates horizontally at constant height through a full walk cycle with no vertical oscillation.
entries.detector_note: FFT of the mediapipe hip-midpoint vertical trajectory over unique frames; flag when the power at twice the step frequency (derived from the ankle-contact signal) is below 5% of the horizontal-translation power.
entries.notes: Needs several full step cycles; a short shot or a locked-off close-up gives nothing.

entries.label: Uncanny / robotic interpolation
entries.description: Motion moves at constant velocity between keys with no ease, giving a mechanical feel.
entries.frame_evidence: Joint trajectories are piecewise linear with sharp corners at the key frames instead of smoothly accelerating curves.
entries.detector_note: Second derivative of each mediapipe joint trajectory; report the fraction of the shot with |acceleration| below noise (linear segments) and the count of acceleration impulses (corners) relative to segment count.
entries.notes: Must be computed on unique-cel indices; on 2s/3s animation every trajectory is a staircase and reads as linear-with-corners by construction.

entries.label: Motion blur direction mismatched to motion
entries.description: An element's blur streak points in a different direction than the object is actually travelling.
entries.frame_evidence: A vertically falling object carries a horizontal smear.
entries.detector_note: Angular difference between the region's structure-tensor orientation and its Farneback flow direction, reported only where both anisotropy and flow magnitude exceed threshold.
entries.notes: Structure-tensor orientation is 180-degree ambiguous, so the comparison must be folded to 0-90 degrees or half the results are spurious.

entries.label: Missing motion blur / strobing
entries.description: A fast-moving CG element is rendered with a zero shutter, so it strobes and stutters instead of smearing.
entries.frame_evidence: An object jumps a large distance between frames while remaining perfectly sharp with crisp edges.
entries.detector_note: Flag regions whose per-frame flow magnitude exceeds 12px while their edge transition width stays under 1.5px and their anisotropy stays isotropic.
entries.notes: Must be computed on unique-cel indices; on 2s animation every drawing jumps by design and the whole frame reports strobing.

entries.label: Rendered motion blur
entries.description: CG motion blur applied per-object along its own motion vector.
entries.frame_evidence: A moving object is directionally smeared along its travel direction while static objects in the same frame stay sharp.
entries.detector_note: Per-region structure-tensor anisotropy and orientation compared against the region's Farneback flow direction; blur is present when anisotropy is high and its orientation matches the flow within 15 degrees, while low-flow regions stay isotropic.
entries.notes: Photographed motion blur is identical; this measures presence, not origin.

entries.label: Motion-vector-driven vector blur artefact
entries.description: Post vector blur driven by a motion-vector pass tears at object boundaries where the vectors are discontinuous.
entries.frame_evidence: A moving object's blur bleeds outward past its silhouette onto a static background, or stops abruptly mid-object.
entries.detector_note: Measure the blur anisotropy just outside the object mask (2-8px band) where the flow magnitude is near zero; a high anisotropy there aligned with the object's motion indicates vector bleed.
entries.notes: Real optical motion blur also spreads past the silhouette; the tell is the hard truncation, which this metric only partly captures.

entries.label: Near-clip plane cutting geometry
entries.description: The camera's near plane slices through an object, revealing its hollow interior.
entries.frame_evidence: A foreground object is cut by a perfectly straight edge that stays fixed relative to the camera, showing backface interior beyond it.
entries.detector_note: Detect long straight cuts through an object mask (Hough) that remain at a fixed screen position across frames, then confirm the hollow interior with the Qwen3-VL judge on a crop.
entries.vlm_question: Is this object sliced open by a flat cut, showing a hollow inside instead of solid material? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Rare and hard; a legitimate cross-section prop looks identical.

entries.label: Normal-map-only relief (flat silhouette)
entries.description: Surface detail comes from a normal map, so the outline stays perfectly smooth while the interior looks carved.
entries.frame_evidence: Deep-looking grooves and rivets in the interior stop dead at a mathematically smooth outline.
entries.detector_note: Same ratio as cg_3d.displacement_silhouette_detail, flagged in the opposite direction: interior relief high while silhouette_roughness_rms is below the anti-aliasing floor.
entries.notes: Only meaningful when the object occupies enough pixels; below ~150px across, everything reads smooth.

entries.label: Normal-map relief lit from the wrong direction
entries.description: Bump detail is shaded as if lit from a different direction than the object's main key.
entries.frame_evidence: Small bumps have their bright side facing left while the object's overall form shading is lit from the right.
entries.detector_note: Estimate the low-frequency shading gradient direction (Sobel on a heavily blurred luma) and the high-frequency detail's mean light direction (mean of Sobel angle weighted by band-pass energy); report the angular difference.
entries.notes: Curved surfaces rotate the local light direction; the metric must be computed per-patch relative to the local form normal, not globally.

entries.label: Hand-drawn spark/debris element (2D)
entries.description: An anime element of drawn sparks, dust or debris that is animated as a shape, not simulated.
entries.frame_evidence: Small shapes with hard ink outlines and flat fill that change shape wholesale between drawings rather than translating.
entries.detector_note: Blob field where each blob has a closed dark contour (cv2.Canny high-threshold ratio inside the blob >0.4) and where frame-to-frame IoU between matched blobs is low (<0.3) despite small centroid movement.
entries.notes: Must run on unique-cel indices; on a held cel the IoU is exactly 1.0 and the entry reads as 3D.

entries.label: Particle collision with geometry
entries.description: Particles bounce off or slide along a surface rather than passing through it.
entries.frame_evidence: Track trajectories reverse or shear their normal component at a common line or surface in the image.
entries.detector_note: Detect per-track direction discontinuities (angle change >60 deg in one unique frame) and test whether their positions are collinear via cv2.fitLine with a low inlier residual across >=8 tracks.
entries.notes: Cannot distinguish a real collision plane from a coincidental alignment; requires many events.

entries.label: Density falloff from emitter
entries.description: Particle density decreases with distance from the emission point, as physical dispersal requires.
entries.frame_evidence: Blob counts binned by radius from the emitter fall off monotonically instead of being flat or ring-shaped.
entries.detector_note: Radial histogram of blob centroids about the emitter ROI centre normalised by annulus area; fit log(density) vs log(radius) with numpy.polyfit and report the exponent.
entries.notes: A shaped emitter (line, disc, mesh) has no single centre and this metric is meaningless there.

entries.label: Emission burst / one-shot spawn
entries.description: A single-frame spike in emission, as from an impact or explosion trigger, rather than a continuous stream.
entries.frame_evidence: Particle count jumps by an order of magnitude on one unique frame and then decays monotonically with no further spawns.
entries.detector_note: First difference of particle_blob_count over unique-cel indices; flag when d(count)/dt exceeds 5x the shot median and the following 5 unique frames show no positive spikes.
entries.notes: A hard cut into a different shot produces the same spike; must be gated by the shot boundary list.

entries.label: Particle emission rate
entries.description: Number of new particles born per unit time at the emitter.
entries.frame_evidence: Count of blobs appearing inside a small radius of the emitter point that were not present in the previous unique frame.
entries.detector_note: Track blobs frame-to-frame with a greedy nearest-neighbour match under a max displacement gate, then count unmatched-new blobs whose centroid lies within the emitter ROI (the mode of birth positions over the shot); divide by unique-frame delta-t.
entries.notes: Birth and re-appearance-after-occlusion are indistinguishable to a greedy tracker; must be computed on UNIQUE-CEL indices or duplicated frames report zero births.

entries.label: Ballistic / gravity arc on particles
entries.description: Particles follow parabolic trajectories consistent with a constant downward acceleration.
entries.frame_evidence: Tracked blob paths curve downward with near-constant second difference in y across their visible life.
entries.detector_note: Fit y = a*t^2 + b*t + c per track by numpy.polyfit; report median 2a (px/frame^2) and the fraction of tracks whose fit R^2 exceeds 0.9.
entries.notes: Perspective foreshortening bends straight 3D paths into curves in image space, producing false gravity.

entries.label: Particle lifetime / fade-out
entries.description: Particles dying by fading opacity or shrinking after a roughly fixed age.
entries.frame_evidence: Individual tracked blobs lose brightness and area monotonically over a consistent number of frames before disappearing.
entries.detector_note: Per-track regression of blob mean intensity and sqrt(area) against track age; report median track length in unique frames and the slope; lifetime is the age at which 50% of tracks have terminated.
entries.notes: Tracks broken by occlusion or crossing produce a short-lifetime bias; the null model is a track-length histogram from shuffled-frame data.

entries.label: Particle pops out (no fade)
entries.description: Particles vanish on a single frame at full opacity instead of fading, a classic un-tuned lifetime curve.
entries.frame_evidence: A blob at near-peak brightness is present in frame N and completely absent in frame N+1 with no intervening dimming.
entries.detector_note: Fraction of terminated tracks whose last-frame intensity is >0.8 of that track's peak intensity; flag when that fraction exceeds 0.3 across >20 tracks.
entries.notes: Particles leaving frame at the border, or occluded by a foreground object, pop by construction; exclude tracks terminating within 20px of the frame edge or on a moving-object mask.

entries.label: Particles pass through solid surface
entries.description: A collision-off particle sim lets sparks or debris travel through what reads as solid geometry.
entries.frame_evidence: Blob tracks cross the silhouette of an opaque object without occlusion or deflection.
entries.detector_note: Crop the region where a track crosses a strong long edge (cv2.Canny + Hough) and put it to the Qwen3-VL judge; no purely geometric method can decide which side of an edge is solid.
entries.vlm_question: Do the sparks or debris pass straight through the solid object instead of bouncing off it or being hidden behind it? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Depth is not observable from a single view; the VLM is guessing from semantics too.

entries.label: Suspiciously uniform particle size
entries.description: All particles are the same size, a giveaway that no size randomisation was applied.
entries.frame_evidence: The histogram of blob areas is a single narrow spike rather than a broad natural distribution.
entries.detector_note: Coefficient of variation of blob areas within one frame; flag when CV<0.15 with n>50 blobs, comparing against a per-shot null built by depth-agnostic resampling.
entries.notes: A distant particle cloud at uniform depth is legitimately uniform in size; perspective is the confound.

entries.label: Particle sorting / draw-order flicker
entries.description: Transparent particles swap depth order between frames, causing brightness to flicker where they overlap.
entries.frame_evidence: In the overlap region of two puffs, luminance flips between two values on alternating frames while both puffs move smoothly.
entries.detector_note: On unique-cel indices, compute per-pixel temporal variance inside the particle mask after motion-compensating with cv2.calcOpticalFlowFarneback; flag pixels whose residual variance exceeds 4x the shot median and that lie in a region where >=2 tracked blobs overlap.
entries.notes: Optical flow on semi-transparent overlapping smoke is unreliable, so the motion compensation itself leaves residual; the null is the same statistic on non-overlap particle pixels.

entries.label: Emission spread / cone angle
entries.description: The angular width over which particles leave the emitter.
entries.frame_evidence: Velocity vectors of newly born particles fan out from the emitter within a measurable angular wedge.
entries.detector_note: Per-track initial velocity angle atan2(dy,dx) over the first 3 unique frames of each track; report the circular standard deviation and the 5-95 percentile angular width around the circular mean.
entries.notes: Camera motion adds a common-mode velocity that widens or narrows the apparent cone; subtract the global flow first.

entries.label: Sprite billboard rotation
entries.description: Each particle is a textured card that spins about the view axis.
entries.frame_evidence: A single particle's internal texture pattern rotates while its silhouette stays the same size.
entries.detector_note: For tracks with area>150px, cv2.phaseCorrelate on log-polar transforms of the crop pair (cv2.warpPolar with WARP_POLAR_LOG) to recover per-frame rotation angle; report median |d_theta| per frame.
entries.notes: Only works on large, textured, non-radially-symmetric sprites; a symmetric soft puff has no measurable rotation.

entries.label: Visible sprite card edge
entries.description: The rectangular boundary of a particle's billboard texture is visible as a hard straight cut.
entries.frame_evidence: A soft smoke puff terminates along a perfectly straight vertical or horizontal line at its bounding box.
entries.detector_note: Crop each large particle blob's bounding box with 20% padding, upscale to 448px, and ask the Qwen3-VL judge via vlm_inspector.py; deterministic pre-filter: cv2.HoughLinesP on the alpha-gradient finds axis-aligned segments longer than 0.7x the blob width.
entries.vlm_question: Does this smoke or effect element end along a perfectly straight hard edge, as if it were cut off by a rectangle? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: THE CROP RULE applies: a full frame hides these; ask only on the tight crop.

entries.label: Particle system present
entries.description: A field of many small similar sprites/points spawned from a source and moving coherently.
entries.frame_evidence: Dozens-to-thousands of small bright blobs of similar size distributed in a plume or cloud that translate together between frames.
entries.detector_note: cv2.SimpleBlobDetector (minArea 2, maxArea 400, filterByCircularity off) on a top-hat of the luma (cv2.morphologyEx MORPH_TOPHAT, 9x9 ellipse); declare present when blob_count>40 and the interquartile range of blob areas is <2x the median area.
entries.notes: Falls over on rain/snow plates, bokeh, star fields and heavy film grain, which are all blob fields too; use the plate-vs-element distinction downstream, not here.

entries.label: Particle motion trail / streak
entries.description: Particles render as elongated streaks rather than points, from motion blur or a trail shader.
entries.frame_evidence: Blobs are strongly elliptical with their major axis aligned to their per-frame displacement vector.
entries.detector_note: cv2.fitEllipse on each blob contour; report median major/minor axis ratio and the mean absolute angle between the ellipse major axis and the track's velocity direction.
entries.notes: Interlacing and rolling shutter also elongate blobs along the motion axis.

entries.label: Turbulence / curl-noise on particles
entries.description: A noise field perturbs particle paths, giving wiggly non-ballistic trajectories.
entries.frame_evidence: Tracked paths show high-frequency lateral wobble superimposed on the mean drift direction.
