entries.detector_note: Per-track residual after removing the quadratic fit; report the RMS of the residual perpendicular to the mean direction and its dominant frequency via numpy.fft.rfft on the residual series.
entries.notes: Tracker centroid jitter on small dim blobs is itself a high-frequency residual; report the noise floor from static blobs.

entries.label: Particle velocity coherence
entries.description: Whether particles move as a coherent driven field or as independent random walkers.
entries.frame_evidence: Neighbouring particles' displacement vectors point the same way over several frames rather than scattering.
entries.detector_note: Spatial autocorrelation of per-track velocity vectors: mean cosine similarity between each track's velocity and that of its k=5 nearest tracks, compared against a null from angle-shuffled velocities.
entries.notes: Requires the null; raw cosine similarity is high even for random fields when the sample is small.

entries.label: Implausible albedo (too dark / too bright)
entries.description: A material's base colour sits outside physically plausible reflectance, e.g. pure 0 black or pure 255 white diffuse.
entries.frame_evidence: A large lit surface region clamps at 0 or 255 across a broad area with no texture detail surviving.
entries.detector_note: Fraction of pixels at exactly 0 or 255 in each channel inside a region mask, plus the local variance in those regions; flag clamped patches larger than 0.5% of frame area.
entries.notes: A legitimate practical blowout (window, sun) and a deliberate crush give the same numbers; this is a description of clipping, not of albedo.

entries.label: Anisotropic specular streak
entries.description: Brushed metal or hair reflects in an elongated streak perpendicular to the grain.
entries.frame_evidence: The highlight is a long thin band whose orientation stays perpendicular to the visible surface grain as the object turns.
entries.detector_note: cv2.fitEllipse on the highlight region for aspect ratio, and structure-tensor orientation of the surrounding texture; report the angle between the highlight major axis and the texture orientation.
entries.notes: Motion blur elongates highlights identically; gate on low local flow.

entries.label: Non-energy-conserving shading
entries.description: A surface reflects more light than it receives, from stacked emissive or additive terms.
entries.frame_evidence: A diffuse surface in shadow is brighter than the same material in direct light elsewhere in the frame.
entries.detector_note: Would require per-pixel material identity and incident-illumination estimation to compare like with like; neither is recoverable from a single rendered frame with the installed stack.
entries.notes: Logged as a known blind spot rather than faked with a brightness heuristic.

entries.label: Fresnel grazing-angle brightening
entries.description: Reflectance rises toward the silhouette, brightening the rim of any dielectric.
entries.frame_evidence: Luminance increases monotonically toward the object's silhouette independently of the key light direction.
entries.detector_note: Sample luma as a function of distance-to-boundary (cv2.distanceTransform on the object mask) and fit; a positive edge-ward slope present on BOTH the lit and shadowed sides indicates fresnel rather than a rim light.
entries.notes: A practical rim light gives the same edge lift on one side only; the symmetry term is what separates them and it needs a clean mask.

entries.label: Metallic material response
entries.description: A metal surface with no diffuse term: its colour comes entirely from tinted reflections.
entries.frame_evidence: The surface shows a high-dynamic-range mirror-like image of the environment with coloured specular and near-black unlit regions.
entries.detector_note: Within a segmented material region, measure the luminance histogram's bimodality (Otsu separability) plus the correlation between local hue and local luma; metals show high specular contrast with hue riding on the highlight rather than the base.
entries.notes: A polished dielectric (wet plastic, glass) is easily confused with metal without spectral information.

entries.label: Roughness read from highlight width
entries.description: Surface roughness controls how broad and soft the specular lobe is.
entries.frame_evidence: The specular highlight on a curved surface has a measurable angular half-width and edge softness.
entries.detector_note: Isolate the brightest connected component on the material, fit a 2D Gaussian by second moments, and report sigma normalised by the object's mask radius plus the 10-90 edge rise distance.
entries.notes: Highlight clipping at 255 destroys the shape; report a clipping fraction alongside and invalidate the sigma when it is high.

entries.label: Uniform roughness / no breakup
entries.description: A single roughness value across a whole surface, with no smudges, wear or variation, reading as CG-clean.
entries.frame_evidence: The specular response is perfectly even across a large surface with zero mottling in the highlight region.
entries.detector_note: Standard deviation of band-pass energy sampled inside the highlight region across the surface; flag when it falls below a per-shot null built from other surfaces in the same frame.
entries.notes: Genuinely new/clean real surfaces read the same; this is a stylistic observation, not proof of CG.

entries.label: Constraint pop / solver explosion
entries.description: A solver blows up for one or two frames, throwing geometry to an absurd position before recovering.
entries.frame_evidence: A single unique frame in which part of the sim geometry is displaced enormously, with the neighbouring frames clean.
entries.detector_note: Frame-differencing on unique-cel indices: flag a frame whose mean absolute difference from BOTH neighbours exceeds 6x the shot median while |diff(N-1,N+1)| stays near the median.
entries.notes: The same three-frame signature is produced by a single dropped/duplicated frame, a flash frame, and a one-frame cut; check the shot list.

entries.label: Sim scale reads as miniature
entries.description: Debris, water or smoke falls too fast or too slow for the object scale it depicts, the classic miniature tell.
entries.frame_evidence: Building-sized rubble falls at the pixel acceleration of a pebble in a close-up.
entries.detector_note: Converting px/frame^2 to m/s^2 requires known focal length, sensor size and scene depth; none of these are recoverable from the pixels alone and no metadata path supplies them reliably.
entries.notes: Logged deliberately as a known blind spot; a VLM asked directly about scale confabulates.

entries.label: Missing secondary motion
entries.description: Hair, cloth or accessories are rigidly locked to the parent, with no follow-through or overlap.
entries.frame_evidence: During a head turn the hair rotates in perfect lockstep with the face, arriving and stopping on the same frame.
entries.detector_note: Cross-correlate the hair-annulus flow signal against the face-landmark velocity signal on unique-cel indices; flag when the peak lag is 0 frames and the correlation exceeds 0.95.
entries.notes: Short shots give too few unique frames to resolve a 1-2 frame lag; require >=8 unique frames of head motion.

entries.label: Raytraced multi-bounce reflection
entries.description: Reflections that include objects outside the frame and reflections-within-reflections.
entries.frame_evidence: A mirror shows geometry that never appears in the frame, and a second mirror inside it shows a further nested image.
entries.detector_note: Detect a reflector region, then ask the Qwen3-VL judge on a crop; no deterministic method can establish that reflected content is off-screen without a 3D scene model.
entries.vlm_question: Does this mirror or reflective surface show objects that are not visible anywhere else in the picture? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: The VLM has no way to check the rest of the frame from a crop, so this question is asked on the full frame plus an inset crop and remains weak.

entries.label: Dispersion / prismatic fringing in glass
entries.description: Wavelength-dependent refraction splits colour at the edges of a glass object.
entries.frame_evidence: Coloured red/blue fringes appear on high-contrast edges seen through glass but not on the same edges outside it.
entries.detector_note: Per-channel edge position from cv2.Sobel zero-crossings; report the R-vs-B sub-pixel offset inside the glass mask minus the same statistic outside it.
entries.notes: Lens chromatic aberration produces global R-B offsets increasing with image radius; the outside-glass subtraction is the control.

entries.label: Reflection does not match the scene
entries.description: A CG object reflects a generic HDRI environment that has nothing to do with the plate around it.
entries.frame_evidence: A chrome object reflects a bright sky and window shapes while the surrounding plate is a dark interior.
entries.detector_note: Compare the reflective region's colour histogram (cv2.calcHist in HS) against the surrounding frame's using cv2.compareHist HISTCMP_BHATTACHARYYA, and flag distances above a per-shot null built from non-reflective regions.
entries.notes: A legitimate reflection of off-screen space (a window behind camera) is also a mismatch by this test.

entries.label: Refraction through glass / water
entries.description: Background geometry seen through a transparent object is displaced, magnified or inverted.
entries.frame_evidence: Straight background lines bend or invert as they cross a transparent object's boundary.
entries.detector_note: Detect long straight lines with cv2.HoughLinesP, then test for a discontinuity in fitted line angle exactly at a closed contour boundary; report the angular break and the lateral offset.
entries.notes: Needs strong straight background structure; on an organic background there is nothing to bend.

entries.label: Render fireflies (bright outlier samples)
entries.description: Single extremely bright sample values survive into the image as isolated white dots.
entries.frame_evidence: Isolated pixels many stops brighter than every neighbour, scattered without regard to geometry.
entries.detector_note: Pixels exceeding 6x the local 11x11 median with an 8-connected area of 1-3px; report count per megapixel and the median excess ratio.
entries.notes: Nearly identical detector to cg_3d.aliasing_specular_sparkle; the distinction is only in temporal persistence and spatial correlation with geometry.

entries.label: Monte Carlo render noise
entries.description: Undersampled path tracing leaves grain that is uncorrelated between frames and concentrated in indirect-lit regions.
entries.frame_evidence: Fine speckle that is heaviest in shadows and glossy reflections and that changes pattern completely every frame.
entries.detector_note: Estimate per-region noise sigma with skimage.restoration.estimate_sigma, then correlate the sigma map against the luma map; render noise is anti-correlated with luma (worst in dark indirect regions), unlike sensor noise which grows with signal in the highlights.
entries.notes: Heavy compression destroys the grain entirely; on a compressed deliverable this reads as clean regardless of the source render.

entries.label: Neck stretch / head detach
entries.description: The neck elongates unnaturally or the head separates from the body during extreme rotation.
entries.frame_evidence: The visible distance from chin to collarbone grows well beyond its baseline while the head turns.
entries.detector_note: Distance between the mediapipe face-mesh chin landmark and the shoulder-midpoint (11/12), normalised by inter-shoulder width; flag frames exceeding 1.4x the shot median of that ratio.
entries.notes: Head pitch legitimately changes the projected chin-to-shoulder distance; the metric needs a head-pose gate that mediapipe supplies only crudely.

entries.label: Shoulder deformation break
entries.description: Raising the arm above shoulder height tears or flattens the deltoid region.
entries.frame_evidence: With the arm overhead, the shoulder silhouette shows a concave notch or a hard shading crease instead of a smooth mass.
entries.detector_note: Crop the shoulder from mediapipe landmarks 11/12 and 13/14 in frames where the elbow is above the shoulder, then ask the Qwen3-VL judge.
entries.vlm_question: Does the shoulder look broken, flattened or dented where the arm meets the body? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Clothing hides the defect on most shots; low recall expected.

entries.label: Rigid-body debris simulation
entries.description: Many hard-edged chunks tumbling under gravity with collisions, from a destruction sim.
entries.frame_evidence: Polygonal fragments with flat shaded faces rotate about their own centroids while their centroids follow parabolic arcs.
entries.detector_note: Track medium blobs (area 200-20000) and per track fit both a parabolic centroid path (numpy.polyfit) and a per-frame rotation via cv2.phaseCorrelate on log-polar crops; require both to be consistent across >=6 tracks.
entries.notes: Fast-moving fragments motion-blur into unsegmentable smears; the detector under-counts exactly when the sim is most active.

entries.label: Rigid bodies interpenetrating
entries.description: Two solid objects overlap in space instead of colliding.
entries.frame_evidence: One object's silhouette passes inside another's with no occlusion boundary and no contact shadow at the intersection.
entries.detector_note: Crop the region where two segmented object masks share a boundary and put it to the Qwen3-VL judge; deterministically only an absent occlusion edge (low gradient along the shared mask boundary) can be pre-flagged.
entries.vlm_question: Are two solid objects in this crop passing through each other instead of resting against each other? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Depth ordering is not recoverable from one view; the VLM answer is a semantic guess and false-positives on legitimate soft contact.

entries.label: Rigid body jitter at rest
entries.description: Settled debris vibrates instead of sleeping, a solver instability or missing sleep threshold.
entries.frame_evidence: A fragment lying on the ground shifts by a pixel or two every frame in a random direction with no net drift.
entries.detector_note: For tracks whose net displacement over 10 unique frames is <2px, report the per-frame RMS displacement; flag when RMS>0.5px against the static-background tracker noise floor measured on a genuinely static feature.
entries.notes: Needs the noise floor null or codec-induced centroid wobble reads as jitter.

entries.label: Dissolve / disintegration shader
entries.description: An object is erased by a noise-threshold mask that eats away its surface, often with a glowing burn edge.
entries.frame_evidence: Holes of irregular noise-shaped outline grow inside the object's silhouette, bordered by a bright thin rim.
entries.detector_note: Track the object's mask area over unique frames while measuring the Euler number (skimage.measure.regionprops) of the mask; dissolve shows a rapidly rising hole count with a bright ring along each new hole boundary.
entries.notes: Occlusion by foreground elements also punches holes in a mask; require the burn-edge luma excess.

entries.label: Emissive / self-illuminated surface
entries.description: A surface that emits light rather than reflecting it, so it stays bright regardless of scene lighting.
entries.frame_evidence: A region holds high luminance with flat shading and no gradient from the key light, often with a bloom halo.
entries.detector_note: Region with luma above the 98th percentile, internal luma gradient magnitude below 3 DN, and a surrounding radial glow (see cg_3d.volumetric_light_scatter_halo) present.
entries.notes: Practical light sources in a plate are also emissive by this test; this measures the phenomenon, not its origin.

entries.label: Force field / energy shield
entries.description: A curved translucent surface with fresnel edge, hex-cell texture and impact ripples.
entries.frame_evidence: A dome-shaped translucent region whose edge glows and through which the background is visible and slightly distorted.
entries.detector_note: Deterministic pre-filter: an elliptical region with elevated edge luma and non-zero background transmission (background structure still correlates through it); confirm the semantic reading with the Qwen3-VL judge on the crop.
entries.vlm_question: Is there a glowing translucent energy shield or force field in this image? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: The deterministic half fires on any translucent dome (glass, bubble, dome light).

entries.label: Fresnel rim glow shader
entries.description: An artificial rim brightening driven by view angle, used for shields, ghosts and stylised characters.
entries.frame_evidence: A uniform-width bright band traces the entire silhouette including the side facing away from any light.
entries.detector_note: Luma excess in a distance-transform band 1-6px inside the mask boundary, measured as the ratio of the minimum-side excess to the maximum-side excess; a fresnel term keeps that ratio near 1 whereas a rim light drives it toward 0.
entries.notes: Anime rim-lighting is drawn on all sides too, so on 2D content this cannot distinguish shader from style.

entries.label: Hex / grid cell pattern on effect
entries.description: A tessellated hexagonal or square cell texture overlaid on a shield or hologram effect.
entries.frame_evidence: A repeating polygonal lattice with 60- or 90-degree line intersections visible inside a translucent element.
entries.detector_note: Orientation histogram of Canny edges inside the element mask showing three peaks 60 degrees apart (hex) or two peaks 90 degrees apart (grid), plus a lattice peak in the 2D autocorrelation.
entries.notes: Chain-link fences, tiles and honeycomb props satisfy this exactly.

entries.label: Hologram / scanline shader
entries.description: A semi-transparent element with horizontal scan lines, chromatic offset and periodic glitch bands.
entries.frame_evidence: Regularly spaced horizontal stripes ride over a translucent figure and drift vertically frame to frame.
entries.detector_note: 1D FFT of the column-mean luma inside the element mask giving a strong peak at 2-16px period, plus a measurable per-frame phase shift of that peak indicating scroll.
entries.notes: Interlacing artefacts and CRT-photographed screens give the same periodicity; the scroll phase and the translucency separate them.

entries.label: Impact ripple on a surface shader
entries.description: Concentric rings expand outward from a hit point across a shield, water or ground shader.
entries.frame_evidence: Circular bright rings whose radius increases by a consistent amount per unique frame from a fixed centre.
entries.detector_note: cv2.HoughCircles per unique frame, then match circles across frames by centre proximity and fit radius vs frame index; require monotonic growth over >=4 frames from a stable centre.
entries.notes: HoughCircles is notoriously parameter-sensitive and produces spurious circles on textured backgrounds.

entries.label: 3D geometry with generated ink outline
entries.description: An inverted-hull or post-process outline draws a dark line around 3D geometry to fake 2D linework.
entries.frame_evidence: A dark line of near-constant width traces the silhouette and interior creases, with the width failing to vary with the drawing's implied weight.
entries.detector_note: Extract dark thin structures (skimage.filters.frangi on the inverted luma), skeletonise, and measure the coefficient of variation of line width along the skeleton; generated outlines have CV below about 0.15.
entries.notes: Digitally inked 2D linework can also be uniform-width; the discriminator is weak and the entry mainly measures uniformity.

entries.label: Toon / cel shading ramp
entries.description: 3D geometry shaded with a quantised light ramp so it reads as flat 2D cel art.
entries.frame_evidence: Shading on a curved surface is two or three flat values separated by hard terminator lines rather than a continuous gradient.
entries.detector_note: Luminance histogram inside the object mask showing few sharp modes (count peaks with scipy.signal.find_peaks on a 64-bin smoothed histogram) combined with high gradient magnitude concentrated at thin boundaries between those modes.
entries.notes: Colour banding from a low-bitrate encode also quantises gradients; check for the accompanying hard terminator geometry.

entries.label: Scrolling UV / flow-map animation
entries.description: A texture slides across static geometry to fake motion, as on lava, waterfalls or energy beams.
entries.frame_evidence: Texture detail translates in a constant direction at a constant rate while the object's silhouette does not move at all.
entries.detector_note: Farneback flow inside a mask whose boundary is static (boundary IoU across unique frames >0.98) showing a coherent non-zero interior flow with low variance in direction and magnitude.
entries.notes: A genuinely flowing river inside static banks looks the same; the entry describes the phenomenon, not the technique.

entries.label: Vertex-animation wobble
entries.description: A sine-driven vertex shader makes foliage, flags or water bob at a fixed frequency.
entries.frame_evidence: Silhouette points oscillate sinusoidally at one dominant frequency across many independent elements simultaneously.
entries.detector_note: Boundary-displacement time series per element, numpy.fft.rfft on unique-cel indices; flag when >=5 elements share a dominant frequency within 10% and their phases are uniformly distributed.
entries.notes: Real wind also drives foliage at a wind-gust frequency; the tell is the unrealistically tight frequency lock.

entries.label: Shadow direction inconsistent between elements
entries.description: CG and plate elements throw shadows in different directions, betraying a lighting mismatch.
entries.frame_evidence: Two objects in the same frame have ground shadows pointing at visibly different angles.
entries.detector_note: For each object-shadow pair compute the vector from the object footprint centroid to the shadow-region centroid; report the circular spread of these angles across >=3 objects and flag spread above 25 degrees.
entries.notes: Multiple real light sources legitimately produce divergent shadows; a nearby point light also does.

entries.label: Shadow softness mismatch
entries.description: A CG element's shadow penumbra is much harder or softer than the plate's shadows.
entries.frame_evidence: One shadow edge transitions over 2px while another in the same frame takes 30px.
entries.detector_note: Measure each shadow's 10-90 edge rise distance perpendicular to the boundary and report the ratio between the CG-candidate shadow and the plate reference shadows.
entries.notes: Penumbra width scales with occluder-to-receiver distance, so different heights legitimately give different softness.

entries.label: Soft-body deformation
entries.description: An object squashes and recovers on impact under a deformable solver.
entries.frame_evidence: The silhouette's aspect ratio compresses sharply along the impact axis for a few frames and then oscillates back.
entries.detector_note: Per-object mask second moments (cv2.moments) giving major/minor axis lengths; detect a step change in axis ratio followed by a damped oscillation fitted as A*exp(-kt)*cos(wt).
entries.notes: Requires a clean per-object mask; without an instance segmenter this only works on high-contrast isolated objects.

entries.label: Jelly / over-soft wobble
entries.description: A soft-body or jiggle-deform setup is under-damped, so flesh or props wobble far past plausible.
entries.frame_evidence: Silhouette oscillation continues for many cycles after the driving motion stops, with slowly decaying amplitude.
entries.detector_note: Count zero-crossings of the boundary-displacement signal after the driving object's velocity falls below threshold; flag when >3 full cycles persist with damping ratio below 0.2.
entries.notes: Stylised animation deliberately over-wobbles; this is a description, not automatically a defect.

entries.label: SSR reflection cut off at frame edge
entries.description: Screen-space reflections vanish where the reflected geometry leaves the screen, the definitive SSR tell.
entries.frame_evidence: The reflection fades or terminates along a straight line parallel to the frame border while the reflector continues.
entries.detector_note: Within the reflection-matched region, measure the reflection's local correlation score as a function of distance from the frame border; flag a monotone fade to zero within the outer 15% of frame width or height.
entries.notes: Vignetting also darkens the frame border and reduces correlation; measure correlation, not brightness.

entries.label: Object missing from reflection
entries.description: An object visible in the frame has no reflection, or a reflected object has no source, because SSR only sees the depth buffer.
entries.frame_evidence: A prominent object stands on a mirror-like floor and casts a contact shadow but no mirrored image.
entries.detector_note: Detect the reflector plane and compare object mask columns above and below the reflection line; put the discrepancy crop to the Qwen3-VL judge.
entries.vlm_question: Is the object standing on this reflective floor missing its reflection? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Rough or dark floors legitimately swallow reflections; require a high reflection_match_score elsewhere on the same plane first.

entries.label: Screen-space reflection present
entries.description: Reflections computed by marching the depth buffer in screen space on a glossy floor or surface.
entries.frame_evidence: A vertically mirrored, blurred copy of on-screen objects appears below them on a floor plane.
entries.detector_note: For a detected horizontal plane region, correlate the region with a vertically flipped copy of the area above the plane line using cv2.matchTemplate TM_CCOEFF_NORMED after a Gaussian blur; peak score above 0.5 indicates reflection.
entries.notes: Works only for near-planar, near-horizontal reflectors; a real wet-floor plate scores identically.

entries.label: SSR ray-march smear / streaking
entries.description: Failed screen-space rays reuse the last valid sample, producing vertical or radial smears in the reflection.
entries.frame_evidence: The reflection contains long unidirectional colour streaks that do not correspond to any real geometry.
entries.detector_note: Structure-tensor coherence inside the reflection region: flag when >20% of pixels have eigenvalue ratio >8 with orientations clustered within 15 degrees, while the source region above shows no such coherence.
entries.notes: Genuine long thin reflected geometry (railings, strip lights) produces the same coherence; the source-region comparison is essential.

entries.label: Backlit ear / nostril translucency
entries.description: Thin body parts glow red when backlit because light passes through them.
entries.frame_evidence: The ear rim or nostril wing is markedly more saturated red and brighter than the adjacent cheek in a backlit setup.
entries.detector_note: Use mediapipe face-mesh landmarks for the ear/nose region against a cheek reference patch; report the ratio of Lab a* and L between them, flagging when a* ratio >1.4 with L also elevated.
entries.notes: mediapipe face-mesh ear coverage is poor at profile angles; the reference patch must be validated as skin, not hair.

entries.label: Missing SSS / waxy plastic skin
entries.description: Skin renders with no subsurface term, so it reads as smooth plastic or wax.
entries.frame_evidence: Skin has a hard neutral terminator, uniform low-texture surface and a broad specular sheen with no pore detail.
entries.detector_note: Combine three facts inside the face-mesh mask: terminator a* excess below threshold, high-frequency band-pass energy (pore detail) below the shot's fabric-region baseline, and specular-blob area fraction above threshold.
entries.notes: Heavy denoising, beauty retouching and low bitrate all destroy pore detail and produce the same signature on real footage.

entries.label: Subsurface scattering (SSS)
entries.description: Light diffuses inside skin, wax or marble, reddening the terminator and softening shadow edges.
entries.frame_evidence: The light-to-shadow terminator on skin carries a warm red-shifted band several pixels wide instead of a neutral falloff.
entries.detector_note: Inside the mediapipe face-mesh region, sample the Lab a* channel along the luminance gradient direction across the terminator; report the peak a* excess over the lit and shadowed plateaus.
entries.notes: Warm practical lighting and a warm grade produce a global a* lift; the metric must be the LOCAL excess at the terminator, not the mean.

entries.label: Disocclusion smear behind moving object
entries.description: Newly revealed background has no valid history, so the reconstruction smears or blurs it.
entries.frame_evidence: The strip of background revealed on the trailing side of a moving object is noticeably softer than the rest of the background.
entries.detector_note: Build the disocclusion mask as the set difference of the object masks between consecutive unique frames, and compare its Laplacian variance against a matched-area control strip of the same background elsewhere.
entries.notes: A rolling-shutter or motion-blur plate softens the same strip; requires an isolated CG-over-plate case to attribute.

entries.label: Temporal AA ghosting
entries.description: TAA history reprojection fails on disocclusion, leaving a translucent trail behind a moving object.
entries.frame_evidence: A faint copy of the object's previous position trails behind it, strongest along the trailing silhouette edge.
entries.detector_note: Warp frame N-1 to N with the object's own flow, then measure the residual immediately behind the trailing edge; ghosting shows a positive correlation between the residual pattern and the previous frame's edge structure with a lag of 1 unique frame.
entries.notes: Motion blur produces a similar trailing gradient but without the structured copy of the previous edge; the correlation test is the discriminator and it needs unique-cel indices.

entries.label: Polygon faceting / low tessellation
entries.description: Insufficient geometry makes a curved surface read as flat facets with visible straight silhouette segments.
entries.frame_evidence: A supposedly round silhouette is a polygon of straight segments, and the interior shading changes in discrete flat bands.
entries.detector_note: cv2.approxPolyDP on the object contour with epsilon = 0.002 * perimeter; report vertex count and the fraction of the perimeter covered by segments longer than 15px with near-constant angle.
entries.notes: Genuinely angular objects (crystals, buildings) are polygonal by design; needs a semantic gate.

entries.label: Tessellation swimming
entries.description: Adaptive tessellation retessellates as the camera moves, so displaced detail crawls over the surface.
entries.frame_evidence: Surface bumps slide relative to the surface texture during a slow camera move.
entries.detector_note: Two Farneback flows, one on the band-pass detail layer and one on the low-pass body, differenced inside the object mask; a persistent non-zero residual over >=6 unique frames with the object rigid indicates swim.
entries.notes: Shares the whole detector with cg_3d.volumetric_noise_texture_advection; specular highlight travel on a moving light is the main false positive.

entries.label: Texture mip-level pop
entries.description: A texture jumps between mip levels, so surface detail sharpens or blurs in one frame.
entries.frame_evidence: A surface's texture detail level changes in one frame across the whole surface uniformly, with no geometry change.
entries.detector_note: Per-surface high-frequency energy trace over unique frames with the object motion-compensated; a single-frame step with no accompanying silhouette change separates this from LOD popping.
entries.notes: Variable-bitrate encoding changes high-frequency energy per frame; correlate with the frame's total bit cost when available from ffprobe.

entries.label: Texture stretching on geometry
entries.description: Bad UVs stretch a texture anisotropically over part of a model.
entries.frame_evidence: The texture's grain is markedly elongated in one region compared to the same texture elsewhere on the object.
entries.detector_note: Patchwise structure-tensor anisotropy across the object mask; flag patches whose anisotropy exceeds 3x the object's median while their local flow is near zero.
entries.notes: Foreshortening on a steeply angled surface stretches texture in the image legitimately.

entries.label: Visible texture tiling
entries.description: A tiled texture repeats visibly across a large surface.
entries.frame_evidence: An identical distinctive patch of texture recurs at a regular spatial interval across a wall or ground plane.
entries.detector_note: 2D autocorrelation (numpy.fft based) of the perspective-rectified surface patch; flag off-origin peaks exceeding 0.5 of the central peak at a consistent lattice spacing.
entries.notes: Real tiled floors, brickwork and fabric weaves are legitimately periodic; the perspective rectification also needs a plane estimate that we often do not have.

entries.label: Duplicate frame / animation on 2s-3s
entries.description: Consecutive delivered frames are bit-similar because the animation holds each drawing for 2 or 3 frames.
entries.frame_evidence: The absolute difference between two consecutive frames is essentially zero everywhere including the noise.
entries.detector_note: Mean absolute difference between consecutive frames; classify as duplicate below a per-shot threshold set from the bimodal MAD histogram, then emit the UNIQUE-CEL index list that every temporal metric in this taxonomy consumes.
entries.notes: This is the prerequisite entry: any temporal metric computed on raw frame indices instead of unique-cel indices is measuring the hold pattern, not the content.

entries.label: Visible UV seam
entries.description: A texture discontinuity along a UV island border shows as a hard line across a smooth surface.
entries.frame_evidence: A thin line of mismatched colour or texture orientation runs across an otherwise continuous surface.
entries.detector_note: Detect thin elongated ridges in the colour-difference map (skimage.filters.frangi on the Lab dE map) that are not accompanied by a luminance gradient consistent with geometry, and that persist across unique frames on the same surface point.
entries.notes: Real garment seams, panel lines and edges are exactly this; the entry cannot distinguish an intentional seam from a UV break.

entries.label: Drawn light beam (2D)
entries.description: An anime light shaft drawn as a flat translucent polygon rather than raymarched.
entries.frame_evidence: A beam bounded by two perfectly straight hard edges with a flat or single-stop-gradient interior and no particulate texture.
entries.detector_note: Wedge region whose boundary is fit by two straight lines with sub-pixel residual (cv2.fitLine on the boundary halves) and whose interior gradient magnitude is below 2 DN across 80% of pixels.
entries.notes: Some CG beams are also hard-edged by design; this distinguishes construction, not medium.

entries.label: Fire / pyro volume
entries.description: Emissive combusting volume with a blackbody colour ramp from white core through yellow to red tips.
entries.frame_evidence: A connected bright region whose hue shifts monotonically from ~50 deg toward ~0-15 deg as luminance drops, flickering at high temporal frequency.
entries.detector_note: HSV mask (H in 0-45 deg, S>0.4, V>0.6), then check the Spearman correlation between per-pixel V and hue distance from red inside the mask, plus temporal luma variance of the mask above 4x the frame median.
entries.notes: Sunset skies, sodium street lamps and orange-graded footage all satisfy the colour test; the flicker term carries most of the discrimination.

entries.label: FLIP / liquid simulation
entries.description: Simulated liquid with a coherent surface, sheeting and splash droplets.
entries.frame_evidence: A specular, high-curvature surface that deforms continuously while shedding small round droplets that follow ballistic arcs.
entries.detector_note: Combination detector: high specular-highlight density (top 1% luma blobs) on a region whose flow field is divergence-carrying, plus a set of small blobs with ballistic fits per cg_3d.particle_gravity_arc.
entries.notes: This is a weak composite; real water photographs identically and the entry cannot say CG vs practical.

entries.label: Foam / whitewater layer
entries.description: A secondary desaturated bright particle layer generated on top of a liquid sim at high-curvature regions.
entries.frame_evidence: Near-white low-saturation speckle concentrated on wave crests and impact points, distinct from the liquid body.
entries.detector_note: Mask of S<0.15 and V>0.8 pixels, tested for spatial coincidence (Dice overlap) with the top decile of the liquid-mask curvature map.
entries.notes: Blown-out highlights and white clouds satisfy the same colour mask.

entries.label: Liquid surface tension reads wrong
entries.description: Sim droplets are too large, too round or too slow, so the liquid reads as the wrong scale.
entries.frame_evidence: Droplets are perfectly spherical and drift slowly, at a size that would break up in reality.
entries.detector_note: Crop the splash region and ask the Qwen3-VL judge; no available deterministic scale reference exists to convert droplet px size to real-world size.
entries.vlm_question: Do the water droplets in this image look unnaturally large, round and slow, like a miniature or computer simulation rather than real water? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Scale judgements from a small VLM are unreliable; treat as advisory only.

entries.label: Atmospheric depth fog
entries.description: Contrast and saturation reduce with distance because of a fog/atmosphere term.
entries.frame_evidence: Local contrast and saturation both decrease monotonically from foreground to background regions of the frame.
entries.detector_note: Dark-channel prior (min over BGR in a 15x15 window) as a haze proxy; correlate its value against a coarse depth proxy (vertical image position, or the blur-gradient map) with scipy.stats.spearmanr.
entries.notes: Vertical position is a poor depth proxy for anything but a ground-plane exterior; on an interior or aerial shot this reads noise.

entries.label: CG element missing atmospheric fog
entries.description: A CG object sits at plate depth but carries none of the plate's haze, so it reads pasted on.
entries.frame_evidence: An object at the same apparent distance as hazy background elements has full local contrast and saturation.
entries.detector_note: Segment candidate CG regions, compare their dark-channel and RMS-contrast against a distance-matched background annulus, then confirm the semantic distance match with the Qwen3-VL judge on a crop containing both.
entries.vlm_question: Is the object in the centre of this crop noticeably clearer and higher-contrast than the surroundings at the same distance behind it? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Requires a correct depth match; the deterministic half alone flags any legitimately-near foreground object.

entries.label: God-ray step banding
entries.description: Too few raymarch steps make the volumetric beam show discrete slabs instead of a smooth gradient.
entries.frame_evidence: Regular stripe pattern of constant spacing running perpendicular to the beam direction inside the shaft.
entries.detector_note: Sample luma along the shaft axis inside the shaft mask, numpy.fft.rfft the 1D profile, and flag a dominant non-DC peak with power >6x the local median at a period between 4 and 40 px.
entries.notes: JPEG/codec blocking at 8 or 16 px periods is a strong false positive; exclude those periods or check phase alignment to the macroblock grid.

entries.label: In-scatter halo around light source
entries.description: A soft radially symmetric glow around a light caused by media in-scattering rather than lens bloom.
entries.frame_evidence: A monotonically falling radial luminance profile centred on a small saturated source, with no lens-specific star or ring structure.
entries.detector_note: Locate saturated maxima, build a radial luma profile with numpy.bincount on the radius map, and fit an exponential or 1/r^2 falloff; report the fit residual and the halo radius at half-max.
entries.notes: Indistinguishable from lens bloom and from a defocused source without extra cues; this entry deliberately only measures the shape.

entries.label: Volumetric light shaft / god ray
entries.description: Visible beams of light scattering through participating media from a source or through an occluder.
entries.frame_evidence: Elongated bright wedges radiating from a common vanishing point with soft edges and a linear luminance falloff along their length.
entries.detector_note: Radon-style test: cv2.HoughLines on the Canny of a high-pass luma, then check whether >=4 detected lines intersect within a 40px radius (the light origin) and whether luma along each line decreases monotonically away from it.
entries.notes: Radial architectural geometry (staircases, spokes, perspective corridors) converges too; the falloff test is what separates them.

entries.label: Volume noise advection
entries.description: The internal noise texture of a volume moves with the flow instead of sitting still in screen space.
entries.frame_evidence: Fine internal structure inside a smoke mass translates along with the mass rather than shimmering in place.
entries.detector_note: Compare Farneback flow computed on the band-pass detail layer against flow computed on the low-pass body; report the mean angular disagreement inside the volume mask.
entries.notes: Low-texture smoke gives the flow solver nothing to lock onto and produces a meaningless angle; gate on band-pass energy.

entries.label: Screen-space-locked volume noise (defect)
entries.description: Volume or fog noise stays pinned to the screen while the camera moves, a classic shader-space bug.
entries.frame_evidence: During a camera pan, the fog's internal mottling does not translate with the scene at all.
entries.detector_note: Global camera flow estimated by cv2.estimateAffinePartial2D on ORB matches; then measure detail-layer flow inside the fog mask and flag when its magnitude is <0.2x the global camera flow magnitude over >=5 unique frames.
entries.notes: Only meaningful when there IS camera motion; on a locked-off shot the metric is undefined.

entries.label: Shadow cast into a volumetric beam
entries.description: An occluder carves a dark wedge out of a light shaft, proving the volumetric is shadow-aware.
entries.frame_evidence: A dark wedge inside the shaft whose apex is at the light origin and whose angular extent matches an occluding silhouette.
entries.detector_note: Detect the shaft, find angular gaps in its luma profile about the origin, then confirm the gap corresponds to a foreground object with the Qwen3-VL judge on a crop containing both.
entries.vlm_question: Is there a dark shadow gap cut into the light beam by an object blocking the light? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Requires the shaft detector to have fired first; on weak shafts the angular profile is dominated by noise.

entries.label: Smoke dissipation / decay rate
entries.description: How fast smoke density falls off, a tuned sim parameter that reads wrong when too fast or too slow.
entries.frame_evidence: Total smoke-mask area and mean opacity decrease over the shot at a measurable rate.
entries.detector_note: Per-unique-frame smoke-mask area and mean alpha proxy (deviation from the background plate estimate); fit an exponential with numpy.polyfit on log values and report the time constant.
entries.notes: Camera moves that reframe the smoke change the visible area without any dissipation.

entries.label: Sim grid / voxel stepping in smoke
entries.description: An under-resolved voxel grid shows as axis-aligned blockiness or stair-stepping inside the smoke.
entries.frame_evidence: Smoke boundaries show repeated right-angle steps of consistent size aligned to a single world axis.
entries.detector_note: Autocorrelation of the smoke-mask boundary curvature and a directional histogram of boundary tangents (cv2.Sobel angle) showing spikes at two orthogonal orientations well above the circular-uniform null.
entries.notes: Compression blocking mimics this; strongly correlated with bitrate, so record the source bitrate alongside.

entries.label: Volumetric smoke / pyro simulation
entries.description: Fluid-solver smoke with billowing rotational structure and self-shadowing.
entries.frame_evidence: Soft-edged grey masses whose internal texture rolls and curls, with darker cores and lit rims that persist across frames.
entries.detector_note: Region of low gradient magnitude but high mid-scale structure (band-pass energy in the 8-32px octave via cv2.pyrDown differences) whose optical flow field has high mean |curl| computed as the discrete cross-derivative of the Farneback flow.
entries.notes: Real photographed smoke produces exactly the same signature; this entry says 'smoke is present', not 'smoke is CG'.

entries.label: Z-fighting
entries.description: Two coplanar surfaces compete for the depth test, so pixels flicker between them.
entries.frame_evidence: A patch shows a shimmering interleaved pattern of two different surface colours that reshuffles every frame and moves with the camera.
entries.detector_note: After motion-compensating, find pixels whose value alternates between exactly two clusters across >=4 unique frames (bimodal temporal histogram, gap > 12 DN, both modes populated >30%), spatially clustered into a coherent patch.
entries.notes: Dither patterns, halftone and interlacing also produce two-mode temporal histograms; the coplanar-patch spatial coherence is the discriminator. Must run on unique-cel indices.

entries.label: Accelerating cutting (montage build)
entries.description: A run of shots whose lengths shorten monotonically toward a climax.
entries.frame_evidence: A sequence of >=5 consecutive shots with monotonically decreasing durations.
entries.detector_note: Scan the shot-length series for maximal runs with scipy.stats.spearmanr < -0.85 over >=5 shots and a total ratio (first/last) > 2.5.
entries.notes: Needs a null model: report how many such runs appear in a shuffled permutation of the same shot lengths (1000 permutations), otherwise a random edit will look like a montage.

entries.label: Action beat density
entries.description: How many discrete motion peaks occur per unit time, a measure of how busy the action is.
entries.frame_evidence: Count of prominent peaks in the motion-energy envelope over the shot or scene.
entries.detector_note: scipy.signal.find_peaks on the unique-cel energy envelope with prominence set to 0.5 * envelope stddev and a minimum distance of 3 cels; normalise the count by seconds.
entries.notes: The prominence threshold dominates the result; report it with the metric and keep it fixed across a comparison set.

entries.label: Additive dissolve
entries.description: A dissolve whose midpoint is brighter than either shot because the two images are summed rather than cross-faded.
entries.frame_evidence: Mid-transition mean luma exceeds the max of both endpoint means and highlights clip toward white.
entries.detector_note: During a detected dissolve support, compare mean(Y) trajectory to the linear interpolation of endpoint means; flag additive when peak positive deviation > 0.08 of full range and the clipped-pixel fraction (Y>250) rises.
entries.notes: An additive dissolve through a bright sky is easily confused with a plain dissolve; low confidence when either anchor is already near clipping.

entries.label: Anticipation hold
entries.description: A pause or small counter-movement immediately before a fast action, winding up the audience.
entries.frame_evidence: A dip in motion energy, often with a small displacement opposite to the coming action, in the 2-10 cels before an energy peak.
entries.detector_note: For each envelope peak found by scipy.signal.find_peaks, examine the preceding 12 cels for a local minimum below 0.3x the shot median energy; test for counter-motion by the dot product of the mean flow vector in that window against the flow vector at the peak (negative = anticipation).
entries.notes: A held cel before a cut produces the same energy dip without any anticipation; require the peak to follow within 12 cels in the SAME shot.

entries.label: Full anticipation-hold-snap-settle envelope
entries.description: The complete four-part timing signature of a well-animated action.
entries.frame_evidence: An energy curve showing, in order: a small counter-move, a low plateau, a single tall spike and a decaying ripple.
entries.detector_note: Compose the four sub-detectors and require them in temporal order within one shot with no cut between; emit the phase boundaries in unique-cel indices and the ratios between phase durations.
entries.notes: Report which of the four phases were actually found rather than a single boolean; most real actions are missing one.

entries.label: Audio onset track
entries.description: The list of audio transient onsets used as the reference grid for all beat and sync measurements.
entries.frame_evidence: Not visual; the audio energy envelope extracted from the same container.
entries.detector_note: ffmpeg -i file -ac 1 -ar 22050 -f f32le - | numpy; compute a spectral-flux novelty curve via scipy.signal.stft, half-wave rectify, smooth, then scipy.signal.find_peaks with adaptive prominence; convert onset times to frame indices using the container fps or PTS.
entries.notes: Files with no audio stream, or with only music-bed loudness, yield weak or meaningless onsets; audio_present_flag must gate every downstream sync metric.

entries.label: Impact audio-visual sync offset
entries.description: How many frames early or late the sound of a hit sits relative to the visual contact.
entries.frame_evidence: Signed difference between the impact cel index and the audio onset index for the same event.
entries.detector_note: Pair each detected visual impact with the strongest audio onset within +/-8 frames; report the signed offset distribution and its median as a global A/V sync estimate.
entries.notes: A consistent non-zero median across many events indicates a global sync error in the file; a scattered distribution indicates the pairing is unreliable, not that the mix is loose.

entries.label: Average shot length (ASL)
entries.description: Mean shot duration across the file, the classical cutting-rate statistic.
entries.frame_evidence: Aggregate of the shot list.
entries.detector_note: total_runtime_seconds / number_of_shots, with a second robust estimate excluding the first and last shot; report a bootstrap 95 percent CI over the shot list (numpy random resampling).
entries.notes: ASL is only as good as boundary recall; publish it next to the flash-guard and dissolve counts so a reader can see how much it can drift.

entries.label: Crossing the line (180-degree rule break)
entries.description: A cut after which the on-screen left/right relationship of two subjects reverses, breaking spatial continuity.
entries.frame_evidence: Two identified subjects swap horizontal order across a cut without an on-screen move.
entries.detector_note: Requires cross-shot subject identity plus 3D scene reasoning; neither is available. A horizontal-order swap of two blobs is far too weak a proxy and would fire on every reverse angle that is legitimately staged.
entries.notes: Explicitly not detectable today.

entries.label: Looping scrolling background
entries.description: A background that scrolls and repeats its tile, the classic chase-scene cheat.
entries.frame_evidence: After compensating the scroll, the background content recurs at a fixed spatial period.
entries.detector_note: Integrate the per-frame global shift, resample the background band into a long panorama strip (cv2.warpAffine accumulation), then autocorrelate the strip along its scroll axis to find the tile period.
entries.notes: Real environments with regular architecture (fences, columns) autocorrelate too; require a very high correlation peak (>0.95) to call it a literal tile.

entries.label: Black frame gap between shots
entries.description: One or more fully black frames deliberately placed between two shots as a beat.
entries.frame_evidence: A run of frames with p99 luma below 6 that is bounded on both sides by non-black content, without a preceding luma ramp.
entries.detector_note: Run-length encode the boolean p99(Y)<6 mask; classify as a gap (not a fade) when the two frames adjacent to the run are both above 40 mean luma, i.e. the black arrives abruptly.
entries.notes: Encoder-dropped frames and streaming stalls also present as black runs.

entries.label: Bullet time / frozen-moment orbit
entries.description: Time nearly stopped while the camera orbits the subject.
entries.frame_evidence: Large consistent viewpoint change (parallax) while the subject's internal pose barely changes.
entries.detector_note: Requires separating camera-induced parallax from subject articulation, i.e. structure-from-motion plus articulated pose; not available. A homography-inlier proxy fails because the scene is not planar.
entries.notes: Known blind spot.

entries.label: Cadence drop to 1s at an impact
entries.description: A brief switch to on-1s exactly at a hit, landing or explosion so the peak action reads at full frame rate.
entries.frame_evidence: A short window of no duplicates coinciding with the peak of the motion-energy envelope.
entries.detector_note: Intersect the mixed-cadence regime boundaries with the motion-energy envelope peak (from unique-cel Farneback flow); flag when a length-1 hold regime of 3-10 frames sits within 4 frames of the envelope maximum.

entries.label: Animation on 4s or slower
entries.description: Drawings held four or more frames, used for very slow motion, distant background action or extreme economy.
entries.frame_evidence: Duplicate runs of length >= 4 dominating the shot while the frame still changes periodically.
entries.detector_note: Hold-length mode >= 4 with the shot still containing at least 3 distinct cels; report the modal hold length.
entries.notes: Distinguish from a static held cel (only 1-2 cels in the shot) - that is a separate entry.

entries.label: Animation on 1s
entries.description: A new drawing on every frame, the fastest and most expensive cadence.
entries.frame_evidence: No duplicate pairs for a sustained run of frames within a shot that nonetheless contains real motion.
entries.detector_note: Within a shot, hold-length run-length histogram dominated (>80 percent of frames) by runs of length 1, AND mean inter-frame MAE well above the noise floor; require shot motion energy above zero so a noisy static shot is not classed on-1s.
entries.notes: Film grain, sensor noise, heavy compression and any global pan all destroy duplicates and make everything look on-1s. Gate on the null model.

entries.label: Animation on 3s
entries.description: Each drawing held for three frames, common on limited-budget TV animation and on slow moves.
entries.frame_evidence: Duplicate mask pattern new, dup, dup repeating.
entries.detector_note: Hold-length mode 3 with >60 percent of runs at length 3 and MAE autocorrelation peak at lag 3.

entries.label: Animation on 2s
entries.description: Each drawing held for two frames, the standard cadence of most hand-drawn animation.
entries.frame_evidence: A strictly alternating duplicate mask: new, dup, new, dup across the shot.
entries.detector_note: Hold-length runs where the mode is 2 and >70 percent of runs are length 2; verify with the autocorrelation of the inter-frame MAE series showing a peak at lag 2 (numpy.correlate, prominence-tested).
entries.notes: A 3:2 telecined 24p-to-30p source also produces a 2-frame periodicity; check the container frame rate and the pulldown detector before concluding artistic on-2s.

entries.label: Subject motion energy with camera removed
entries.description: Motion energy attributable to the subject after global camera movement is subtracted.
entries.frame_evidence: Residual flow field after the dominant global translation is removed.
entries.detector_note: Estimate global shift by cv2.phaseCorrelate (or the median flow vector), subtract it from the dense flow field, then recompute mean magnitude; report both raw and compensated energies and their ratio.
entries.notes: On a multiplane pan there is no single global motion to remove; report camera_energy_fraction as unreliable when the flow histogram is multimodal.

entries.label: Cel registration jitter
entries.description: Small random frame-to-frame displacement of an otherwise static drawing, from peg registration or scan wobble.
entries.frame_evidence: Sub-pixel to few-pixel random translation between otherwise identical frames, with no consistent direction.
entries.detector_note: Sub-pixel cv2.phaseCorrelate on a held run; measure the stddev of the shift vector and the lag-1 autocorrelation of the shift series - jitter is high-variance and near-zero autocorrelation, a pan is low-variance and high autocorrelation.
entries.notes: Also produced by film gate weave in a scanned print, and by a handheld camera in live action.

entries.label: CG element on 1s inside a drawn shot
entries.description: A 3D-rendered vehicle, crowd or effect updating every frame inside a shot whose drawn elements are on 2s or 3s.
entries.frame_evidence: A spatially coherent region with hold length 1 and smooth sub-pixel motion embedded in a frame whose remainder holds for 2-3 frames.
entries.detector_note: From layer_differential_cadence take the region with modal hold length 1; additionally require its flow field to be smooth (low flow divergence variance) and its edges to be anti-aliased differently (measure edge-transition width via the gradient profile) compared to the drawn region.
entries.notes: A pan on a held background also produces per-frame change; run the warp-compensated hold test first.

entries.label: Container frame rate vs native drawing rate
entries.description: The declared container fps compared with the rate at which the picture actually changes.
entries.frame_evidence: Container metadata versus the measured unique-cel rate.
entries.detector_note: ffprobe -show_streams for r_frame_rate and avg_frame_rate; compare against unique_cels_per_second and report the ratio.
entries.notes: r_frame_rate and avg_frame_rate disagree on VFR files; report both.

entries.label: Repeated cycle across crowd instances
entries.description: The same animation cycle reused on several characters at different phase offsets.
entries.frame_evidence: Multiple spatially separate regions whose motion signals share a period and differ only by phase.
entries.detector_note: Requires per-instance segmentation to isolate each character before comparing cycles; no instance segmentation model is installed (ultralytics absent). Per-tile phase comparison is not enough to attribute a tile to a character.
entries.notes: Known blind spot.

entries.label: Exact cut boundary frame index
entries.description: The integer frame index of the last frame of the outgoing shot, i.e. the precise placement of the edit.
entries.frame_evidence: The single frame pair carrying the maximum of the boundary score inside a detected transition region.
entries.detector_note: argmax of the fused boundary score within the detected transition support; report the index of the LAST frame of the outgoing shot and the container PTS from ffprobe -show_frames -of json.
entries.notes: On telecined or duplicated-frame material the true edit point can be up to 2 frames earlier than the pixel change; report uncertainty rather than a false precision.

entries.label: Cut placed inside a camera move
entries.description: A cut whose adjacent shots are both moving, so the boundary is masked by ongoing motion.
entries.frame_evidence: A confirmed cut where the global phase-correlation shift is non-zero on both sides.
entries.detector_note: cv2.phaseCorrelate over unique-cel pairs on both sides; report the pre and post shift vectors and whether they are continuous.
entries.notes: Boundary recall drops in this condition; report it so the ASL confidence can be discounted.

entries.label: Cut on action
entries.description: A cut placed mid-gesture so a limb or body movement continues seamlessly across the boundary.
entries.frame_evidence: A pose landmark trajectory whose joint angles and angular velocities extrapolate across the cut with small residual, despite framing change.
entries.detector_note: mediapipe Pose on the 4 unique cels either side; normalise landmarks by torso length and hip centre, fit a linear extrapolation of the elbow/knee joint angles (landmarks 11-16, 23-28) from before the cut and measure residual against the observed post-cut angles; flag when residual is below the 20th percentile of the file's own cut population.
entries.notes: mediapipe pose is unreliable on stylised 2D characters, non-human creatures and extreme foreshortening; log landmark_visibility_mean and refuse a verdict below 0.5. | TIER CORRECTED by completeness critic: cut_on_action is landmark and the other two deterministic, but all three compare CONTENT across a cut, which needs subject correspondence across the boundary. Nothing establishes that correspondence at a tier below model

entries.label: Periodic cutting rhythm
entries.description: Cuts falling at a near-constant interval, giving a metronomic edit.
entries.frame_evidence: Aggregate: autocorrelation of the cut-time impulse train shows a strong peak at a non-zero lag.
entries.detector_note: Build a binary cut train at frame resolution, autocorrelate with numpy.correlate, find the dominant non-zero lag with scipy.signal.find_peaks; report peak prominence relative to a Poisson-process null with the same cut count.
entries.notes: The Poisson null is mandatory - any cut list has autocorrelation structure by chance.

entries.label: Cut-to-beat alignment
entries.description: How closely the edit points land on musical beats.
entries.frame_evidence: The signed frame offset between each cut and the nearest beat grid position.
entries.detector_note: For every confirmed cut compute the offset to the nearest beat; report the distribution and the fraction within +/-2 frames; compare against a null built by shifting the whole cut list by 1000 random offsets and recomputing (a random edit is on-beat surprisingly often at fast tempi).
entries.notes: The random-offset null model is mandatory; without it every cut list looks rhythmic at 140 BPM.

entries.label: Cutaway / insert shot
entries.description: A brief shot of a detail or a second subject inserted inside an ongoing scene, returning afterwards to the original framing.
entries.frame_evidence: An ABA pattern: shot n+2 closely resembles shot n in palette and layout while shot n+1 does not.
entries.detector_note: Represent each shot by a mean 8x8x8 HSV histogram of its unique cels; flag ABA when d(A,A') < 0.25 and both d(A,B) and d(B,A') > 0.5, with B shorter than 0.6 * A.
entries.notes: Shot-reverse-shot dialogue also produces ABAB patterns; the length asymmetry test separates most cases but not all.

entries.label: Cutting-rate envelope over time
entries.description: How the local cutting rate rises and falls across the runtime.
entries.frame_evidence: Aggregate; a curve of cuts-per-30-seconds against time.
entries.detector_note: Kernel density of cut times (Gaussian kernel, sigma 15 s, scipy.ndimage.gaussian_filter1d over a 1 Hz cut-count series); report peaks with scipy.signal.find_peaks.

entries.label: Datamosh / temporal codec smear
entries.description: Deliberate removal of keyframes so motion vectors from one shot are applied to another shot's pixels.
entries.frame_evidence: Block-structured smearing where colour from the previous shot is dragged along motion vectors, with 16x16 block boundaries visible.
entries.detector_note: Detect strong periodicity at 8 or 16 px in the horizontal and vertical gradient profiles (FFT of the mean absolute gradient per column/row) coinciding with a content change that has no valid boundary score; report block-grid strength.
entries.notes: Ordinary heavy compression also shows blocking; require the blocking to spike at a content transition and to persist while content drifts.

entries.label: Decelerating cutting (release)
entries.description: A run of shots whose lengths lengthen monotonically as tension releases.
entries.frame_evidence: A sequence of >=5 consecutive shots with monotonically increasing durations.
entries.detector_note: Mirror of accelerating_montage with positive Spearman rho.
entries.notes: Same permutation null model applies.

entries.label: Lip-sync timing against dialogue
entries.description: Whether the mouth movement matches the timing of speech energy.
entries.frame_evidence: Mouth-opening series (from the face landmarks or the mouth-region change mask) correlated against the speech-band audio envelope.
entries.detector_note: mediapipe FaceMesh mouth aperture (distance between landmarks 13 and 14, normalised by 61-291 width) per unique cel; cross-correlate against the 300-3400 Hz audio envelope over lags of +/-12 frames; report the best lag and correlation.
entries.notes: Anime mouth flaps are only loosely synced by design, so a low correlation is normal and is NOT a defect; on 3s animation the achievable lag resolution is 3 frames. FaceMesh is unreliable on stylised faces - gate on landmark confidence.

entries.label: Dissolve / cross-fade
entries.description: A transition where two shots are alpha-blended over several frames so both images are simultaneously visible.
entries.frame_evidence: A run of 6-48 frames where each consecutive pair differs moderately, spatial contrast and edge density dip in the middle, and the frame is well approximated by a*A + (1-a)*B with a ramping monotonically from 1 to 0.
entries.detector_note: Fit per-frame alpha by least squares of frame_t against the pre-transition anchor A and post-transition anchor B (numpy lstsq on downsampled 64x64 greyscale); accept when residual RMS < 0.06 of dynamic range, alpha is monotone (scipy.stats.spearmanr < -0.95) and edge density from cv2.Canny dips below both endpoints mid-transition.
entries.notes: A dissolve between two near-identical shots is indistinguishable from a slow lighting change; require the two anchors to be dissimilar (hist distance above the cut threshold) before calling it a dissolve.

entries.label: Dropped / missing frame
entries.description: A gap in the recorded motion where one or more frames are missing from an otherwise smooth move.
entries.frame_evidence: A single frame pair whose inter-frame displacement is roughly double the local median while nothing else changes.
entries.detector_note: Track the global phase-correlation shift magnitude series inside a shot; flag a pair whose shift is 1.7-2.5x the running median with no accompanying content change and no cut.
entries.notes: On animation this is indistinguishable from a deliberately dropped inbetween; report it as 'motion step' rather than asserting a technical fault.

entries.label: Duplicate frame pair
entries.description: Two consecutive frames carrying the same image, the atom of animation-on-2s and of any frame hold.
entries.frame_evidence: Consecutive frames whose mean absolute difference is at or near zero over the whole frame.
entries.detector_note: MAE on the full-resolution greyscale plus a 64-bit DCT perceptual hash Hamming distance; declare duplicate when MAE < the per-file compression noise floor (see null_model_duplicate_threshold) OR phash Hamming <= 2 with MAE below 3x the floor.
entries.notes: THE FOUNDATION ENTRY. Lossy encoding makes true duplicates non-identical; a fixed threshold of zero misses most held cels in an h264 file. Grain, dither and film weave in live action can defeat this entirely - report the noise floor alongside.

entries.label: Echo / trail ghosting
entries.description: Previous frames left visible as attenuated copies behind a moving subject.
entries.frame_evidence: The current frame contains faint, correctly displaced replicas of the subject at its positions from 1-8 frames ago.
entries.detector_note: Fit frame_t as a non-negative weighted sum of frames t-1..t-8 plus a residual (numpy.linalg.lstsq with clipping, on a 128x128 downsample); flag when two or more historical weights exceed 0.08 and the residual is small; report the decay profile.
entries.notes: Long motion blur and interlaced ghosting both load onto the same basis; require discrete taps (separated peaks in the weight vector) rather than a smooth ramp.

entries.label: Exact loop (frame-identical repeat)
entries.description: A segment of frames repeated verbatim later in the same shot.
entries.frame_evidence: Frame t and frame t+P are pixel-identical, and so are their neighbours, for a whole block.
entries.detector_note: Compute a 64-bit DCT phash per unique cel; build a self-similarity matrix over the shot (Hamming distance) and look for a strong off-diagonal stripe at a constant lag P; confirm by full-resolution MAE on the candidate lag.
entries.notes: Static shots trivially self-match at every lag; require the shot to contain motion (unique cel count > 4 and non-zero flow) before reporting a loop.

entries.label: Blink-only update
entries.description: A partial cel update confined to the eyes, typically a 2-4 frame blink on an otherwise held character.
entries.frame_evidence: A brief symmetric pair of small changed regions in the upper face, returning to the previous state within a few frames.
entries.detector_note: mediapipe FaceMesh eye-aspect-ratio (landmarks 159/145 and 386/374) dropping below 0.2 for 1-4 unique cels then recovering; require the rest of the frame to be at the duplicate noise floor.
entries.notes: On 2D art the EAR proxy is only approximate; on closed-eye stylisation it saturates. In 3D and live action this doubles as a genuine blink detector.

entries.label: Fade from black
entries.description: The image ramps up out of a fully black frame at the start of a shot or scene.
entries.frame_evidence: A monotone increasing mean-luma ramp beginning at a frame with p99 luma below ~6/255.
entries.detector_note: Same ramp fit as fade_to_black with the sign reversed; anchor the start on the last frame whose p99(Y) < 6.
entries.notes: Leader black, encoder-inserted black and true fades all look alike; cross-check the audio track for whether sound is already running.

entries.label: Fade from white
entries.description: The image resolves out of a fully white frame.
entries.frame_evidence: A frame with near-zero variance and p1 luma above 248 followed by a monotone increase in spatial variance and edge density.
entries.detector_note: Mirror of fade_to_white; track np.std(Y) and Canny edge density recovering monotonically over the run.

entries.label: Fade to black
entries.description: The image ramps down to a fully black frame, ending a shot or a scene.
entries.frame_evidence: A monotone decreasing mean-luma ramp over 4-72 frames terminating in one or more frames whose 99th-percentile luma is below ~6/255.
entries.detector_note: Track mean(Y) and p99(Y) per frame; require strictly non-increasing p99 over the run (allow 1 percent slack), a final p99 < 6, and per-frame relative decrement consistent with a linear or ease-out ramp (fit both, report better R^2).
entries.notes: A shot that simply cuts to a dark night interior is not a fade; require p99 (not mean) to reach near zero, otherwise dark scenes fire constantly.

entries.label: Fade to white
entries.description: The image ramps up to a fully white frame, a common transition for flashbacks, deaths and impacts.
entries.frame_evidence: Monotone increasing luma with collapsing spatial variance, ending in a frame where p1 luma exceeds ~248/255 and stddev(Y) is near zero.
entries.detector_note: Require p1(Y) rising above 248 and np.std(Y) falling below 3 across a monotone run; distinguish from a flash by requiring run length >= 3 frames and a monotone (not spiky) ramp.
entries.notes: An impact white flash lasting 1-2 frames is a different entry (flash_frame_transition); the separator is monotonicity and duration.

entries.label: Fast motion / undercranking
entries.description: Playback faster than real time, producing jerky accelerated movement.
entries.frame_evidence: Very high inter-frame displacement with abnormally short motion blur for the displacement, and human motion that reads as unnaturally quick.
entries.detector_note: Median flow magnitude above p95 of the file combined with blur_per_flow_ratio far BELOW the file median (short exposure relative to step); additionally test for aliasing of periodic motion (gait period below 4 unique cels).
entries.notes: Hand-drawn animation has no blur at all, so the blur cue is useless on 2D; on 2D rely on unrealistic gait periods instead and lower confidence.

entries.label: Flash / lightning false-cut guard
entries.description: A negative control that suppresses boundary detections caused by a global illumination spike rather than a change of shot.
entries.frame_evidence: A luma spike where the SPATIAL layout (normalised edge map and per-tile rank order) is preserved even though absolute brightness changed.
entries.detector_note: Recompute the boundary score on per-tile CLAHE-normalised (cv2.createCLAHE) and rank-transformed frames; if the score collapses below threshold under illumination normalisation, mark the candidate as a flash, not a cut.
entries.notes: This guard is required for any anime with impact-flash frames; without it the ASL is under-estimated by a large factor in action sequences.

entries.label: Flash-frame transition
entries.description: One to three near-uniform bright frames inserted at a cut to punctuate it.
entries.frame_evidence: An isolated spike in mean luma with collapsed spatial variance, one or two frames wide, sitting exactly on a detected shot boundary.
entries.detector_note: Detect frames with np.std(Y) < 12 and mean(Y) > mean of the 15-frame neighbourhood + 60; require run length <= 3 and a hist-distance cut on at least one side of the run.
entries.notes: Photographic camera flashes and lightning inside a continuous shot produce the identical signature; the discriminator is whether the content either side of the flash is the same shot.

entries.label: Frame-skip stutter
entries.description: A jerky look made by deleting frames rather than repeating them, so motion jumps forward.
entries.frame_evidence: A run where every inter-frame displacement is an integer multiple (2x, 3x) of the pre-effect displacement, with no duplicates.
entries.detector_note: Track persistent ORB features; test whether the per-pair displacement inside the suspect run is a near-constant multiple of the displacement in the surrounding frames of the same shot.
entries.notes: Indistinguishable from genuine acceleration unless the multiplier is close to an integer and reverts afterwards.

entries.label: Freeze frame
entries.description: Playback stopped on a single image for a sustained period, usually as a punctuation.
entries.frame_evidence: A long run of identical frames in material that was moving immediately before, with grain and noise also frozen.
entries.detector_note: Duplicate run-length >= 8 frames preceded within the same shot by non-zero motion; on live action confirm by checking that the film/sensor grain is also static (the residual after subtracting the previous frame is exactly zero, not merely small).
entries.notes: The frozen-grain test is the reliable discriminator between a freeze frame and a very still live-action shot; on animation it does not apply, where the discriminator is instead run length against the shot's own hold distribution.

entries.label: Freeze frame with graphic overlay
entries.description: A freeze used as a card for a name, stat or caption to appear over.
entries.frame_evidence: A freeze run during which new high-contrast graphic elements animate in over the still image.
entries.detector_note: Detect a freeze whose change mask is confined to a small set of components that themselves animate (grow, slide, fade) while the rest of the frame is bit-frozen; report the overlay bounding boxes.
entries.notes: Do not ask moondream what the overlay says - it confabulates text. Report geometry only, or hand the crop to the OCR path if available.

entries.label: Hair / cloth wave loop
entries.description: A looping secondary-motion wave in hair, cape, flag or foliage.
entries.frame_evidence: A localised region whose flow field oscillates with a stable period while the parent body stays still.
entries.detector_note: Per-tile flow-magnitude time series on unique cels; FFT each tile, retain tiles with a dominant frequency carrying > 0.35 of power; require the tiles to form a connected region adjacent to a static region.
entries.notes: Repeated background texture scrolling and rendering noise both produce per-tile periodicity; the adjacency-to-static-body test is what keeps this honest.

entries.label: Hard cut
entries.description: An instantaneous change of shot between frame N and frame N+1 with no blended transition.
entries.frame_evidence: One frame pair where global colour histogram, edge map and block-mean layout all change discontinuously while the frames before and after each pair are internally stable.
entries.detector_note: Per-frame 3x3-tile HSV histograms (cv2.calcHist, 16x16x8 bins) compared with cv2.compareHist HISTCMP_BHATTACHARYYA plus Edge Change Ratio from cv2.Canny(50,150) dilated 3px; declare a cut where the fused score exceeds mu+k*sigma of a rolling 121-frame window (adaptive k, default 5) AND the frame pair is not a duplicate pair and not inside a monotone dissolve ramp.
entries.notes: Full-frame flashes, lightning, camera-flash pops and hard whip-pans all fire this; must be gated by the flash and whip-pan guards. On anime a cut that lands on a duplicate-frame boundary is still a cut - never suppress cuts merely because the pair straddles a held cel.

entries.label: Hard-sync cut (picture and sound cut together)
entries.description: A cut where the audio changes on exactly the same frame as the picture, the default flat edit.
entries.frame_evidence: Coincident picture boundary and audio change point within +/-1 frame.
entries.detector_note: Coincidence of the boundary score peak and the audio novelty peak within 1 frame; report the fraction of cuts that are hard-sync versus L versus J.

entries.label: Held cel (static hold)
entries.description: One drawing held for a long run of frames with nothing at all moving.
entries.frame_evidence: A run of >= 6 consecutive duplicate frames with no global shift.
entries.detector_note: Duplicate run-length >= 6 AND cv2.phaseCorrelate shift magnitude < 0.3 px across the run.
entries.notes: Distinguish from a freeze frame in live action (separate entry) by whether the underlying material is drawn.

entries.label: Held cel with camera pan (book / harmony pan)
entries.description: A single drawing translated across the frame to fake movement without any new artwork.
entries.frame_evidence: Consecutive frames related by a near-pure translation with essentially zero residual after warping, sustained over many frames.
