entries.detector_note: cv2.phaseCorrelate for a candidate shift, warp frame t-1 by that shift (cv2.warpAffine) and measure residual MAE inside the valid overlap; declare a pan-on-a-hold when residual < 1.5x the noise floor for >=6 consecutive frames while the shift magnitude exceeds 0.5 px/frame.
entries.notes: CRITICAL: a panning held cel produces NO duplicate frames, so the naive cadence detector will call it on-1s. The warp-compensated duplicate test must run before cadence classification, and unique-cel indices must be assigned on the warped residual.

entries.label: Held cel with camera push/pull
entries.description: A single drawing scaled up or down over time to fake a dolly, again with no new artwork.
entries.frame_evidence: Consecutive frames related by a pure scale about a fixed centre with negligible residual.
entries.detector_note: Estimate scale by log-polar phase correlation (cv2.logPolar then cv2.phaseCorrelate) or by cv2.estimateAffinePartial2D on ORB matches; accept when the affine is scale+translation only (shear/rotation < 0.5 degrees) and the warped residual is at the noise floor.
entries.notes: Resampling of a scaled hold adds real pixel change; the residual threshold must be looser than for a pure pan.

entries.label: Held cel with rotation
entries.description: A single drawing rotated over time (a spinning object or a canted camera move on static art).
entries.frame_evidence: Consecutive frames related by a rotation about a fixed centre with low residual.
entries.detector_note: cv2.estimateAffinePartial2D on ORB keypoint matches; extract the rotation angle and test residual after cv2.warpAffine.

entries.label: Hit-stop (freeze on impact)
entries.description: A very short freeze of 1-6 frames landing exactly on a contact to sell weight.
entries.frame_evidence: A brief duplicate run whose first frame coincides with the peak of the motion-energy envelope and often with an impact flash.
entries.detector_note: Intersect short duplicate runs (2-6 frames) with the motion-energy envelope maximum computed on unique cels; require the run to begin within 2 unique cels of the peak and the post-run motion to reverse or scatter.
entries.notes: Anime holds a drawing constantly; without the envelope-peak coincidence test this fires on every ordinary hold.

entries.label: Hyperlapse (moving-camera time lapse)
entries.description: A time lapse in which the camera also translates substantially between captures.
entries.frame_evidence: Large consistent global displacement per frame combined with broken local flow correspondence.
entries.detector_note: Same broken-flow test as time_lapse but with a large, consistent cv2.phaseCorrelate global shift or a strong ORB-based homography between consecutive frames.

entries.label: Idle / breathing loop
entries.description: A low-amplitude repeating idle motion on an otherwise stationary character.
entries.frame_evidence: Slow periodic vertical oscillation of the shoulder/chest region of a few pixels amplitude.
entries.detector_note: mediapipe Pose shoulder landmarks 11/12 midpoint y-trajectory over unique cels, detrended (scipy.signal.detrend), FFT for a 0.2-0.6 Hz dominant component with amplitude between 0.3 and 3 percent of torso length.
entries.notes: Amplitude at this scale is comparable to landmark jitter; require the SNR against a static-background control region to exceed 3.

entries.label: Impact flash duration
entries.description: How many frames a white or coloured impact flash occupies.
entries.frame_evidence: A run of frames with elevated mean luma and collapsed variance sitting on the impact cel.
entries.detector_note: Run-length of frames exceeding the flash criteria (mean luma above neighbourhood + 60, low variance) anchored on the detected impact cel; report peak luma and the decay shape.
entries.notes: Photosensitivity-relevant; also cross-check with the flash false-cut guard so the same event is not double-reported as a cut.

entries.label: Impact frame
entries.description: The exact cel on which a contact happens, the reference point for all reaction timing.
entries.frame_evidence: The cel where a moving object's velocity abruptly drops or reverses, usually coincident with a flash, a smear or a debris burst.
entries.detector_note: Find cels where the tracked subject's velocity magnitude drops by more than 60 percent in one cel OR its direction reverses by more than 120 degrees; corroborate with a same-cel luma spike (impact flash) and with an audio-transient onset within 3 frames.
entries.notes: Occlusion at the moment of contact is common and destroys the velocity track; the flash and audio cues then carry the estimate, with wider uncertainty.

entries.label: Impact-to-reaction gap in frames
entries.description: How many frames pass between a contact and the struck party starting to react.
entries.frame_evidence: The interval between the impact cel and the first cel where the receiving subject's motion energy rises above its pre-impact baseline.
entries.detector_note: Split the frame into the aggressor and receiver regions using the connected components of the moving mask at the impact cel; compute each region's own energy series; the gap is the first cel after impact where the receiver's energy exceeds baseline + 3 sigma. Report in BOTH frames and unique cels.
entries.notes: Region attribution is the weak link: two overlapping figures at the moment of contact are one connected component. Report an attribution confidence and fall back to whole-frame energy when the components merge. On 3s animation the gap quantises to multiples of 3 - report the quantisation.

entries.label: Inbetween density between key poses
entries.description: How many intermediate drawings sit between two extreme poses, i.e. the spacing chart the animator used.
entries.frame_evidence: The sequence of unique cels between two local extremes of the pose trajectory.
entries.detector_note: Requires reliable key-pose identification on stylised drawings; mediapipe pose is not dependable enough on 2D art and we have no drawing-aware pose model. Flow-based extremes are confounded by camera moves and effects layers.
entries.notes: Marked model: the concept is real but we cannot measure it honestly today.

entries.label: Interlace combing
entries.description: Horizontal comb teeth from two interlaced fields captured at different instants.
entries.frame_evidence: Alternating-row displacement on moving edges producing a high-frequency vertical ripple.
entries.detector_note: Comb score = mean over columns of the sum of |2*row_n - row_{n-1} - row_{n+1}| restricted to high-horizontal-gradient areas; compare even-vs-odd row field difference. Report combed frame fraction.
entries.notes: Fine horizontal texture (venetian blinds, hair) raises the comb score; require the score to correlate with motion.

entries.label: Invisible / hidden cut
entries.description: A cut concealed behind a foreground wipe, a whip, a dark frame or a matched pan so the sequence reads as one take.
entries.frame_evidence: A frame or two where the image is fully occluded by a passing object or is near black, with the content on either side inconsistent in continuity terms.
entries.detector_note: By construction the pixel-level boundary signal is suppressed; detecting it requires continuity reasoning (light, wardrobe, actor position) beyond any available detector. We can flag CANDIDATE occlusion frames (full-frame low-variance or a single object covering >85 percent of the frame) but cannot confirm a cut.
entries.notes: Report candidates only; never assert a hidden cut.

entries.label: Iris in (closing circle)
entries.description: The visible image shrinks inside a closing circular (or shaped) aperture, the rest of frame going black.
entries.frame_evidence: A black annulus grows inward from the frame border; the non-black region is a shrinking disc whose radius decreases monotonically.
entries.detector_note: Per frame, threshold Y>8 to a content mask, take cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats largest component, fit cv2.minEnclosingCircle; accept iris_in when radius decreases monotonically over >=4 frames and mask circularity (4*pi*area/perimeter^2) stays > 0.85.
entries.notes: A vignette ramp or a closing-eye POV shot mimics this; the discriminator is that the outside is truly clipped to black, not merely darkened.

entries.label: Iris out (opening circle)
entries.description: The image is revealed from a growing circular aperture at the start of a shot.
entries.frame_evidence: Monotonically expanding circular content mask against black.
entries.detector_note: Mirror of iris_in with increasing radius.

entries.label: J-cut (audio arrives before the picture cut)
entries.description: The incoming shot's audio starts before its picture does.
entries.frame_evidence: An audio change point 3-45 frames before a picture cut, with no picture change at the audio change.
entries.detector_note: Mirror of the L-cut test with a negative lag; require no boundary score peak at the audio change point.
entries.notes: Same limitation: continuous music suppresses audio change points entirely.

entries.label: Jump cut
entries.description: A cut between two shots of the same subject and framing where the subject has visibly jumped position in time.
entries.frame_evidence: Background histogram and layout are nearly identical across the cut while the subject region has moved discontinuously.
entries.detector_note: At a confirmed cut, compute per-tile change on a 8x8 grid; flag jump_cut when > 70 percent of tiles are unchanged (per-tile Bhattacharyya < 0.1) but a spatially connected minority of tiles changes sharply, and phase correlation shows no global shift.
entries.notes: Indistinguishable from a fast in-shot movement plus a duplicate-frame hold unless a boundary was already confirmed. In anime, a held background with a snapping character pose triggers this constantly - require the boundary detector to fire first. | TIER CORRECTED by completeness critic: cut_on_action is landmark and the other two deterministic, but all three compare CONTENT across a cut, which needs subject correspondence across the boundary. Nothing establishes that correspondence at a tier below model

entries.label: L-cut (audio runs past the picture cut)
entries.description: The outgoing shot's audio continues over the start of the incoming shot.
entries.frame_evidence: A picture cut with no corresponding discontinuity in the audio texture, the audio change arriving later.
entries.detector_note: Compute a per-frame audio feature vector (13 MFCC-like mel-band log energies via scipy.signal.stft plus a mel filterbank built in numpy); detect audio change points by a self-similarity novelty score; an L-cut is a picture cut with no audio change point within +/-2 frames but one appearing 3-45 frames LATER.
entries.notes: Music running continuously across a whole scene means no audio change point exists at all; that is not an L-cut. Require an audio change point to be found within the search window.

entries.label: Different cadence per layer
entries.description: Character animating on 2s over a background panning on 1s, or an effect on 1s over a character on 3s.
entries.frame_evidence: The duplicate/hold periodicity measured inside one image region differs from that measured in another region of the same frame.
entries.detector_note: Compute per-tile (8x8 grid) inter-frame MAE series and per-tile MAE autocorrelation; report the modal hold length per tile and flag when at least two spatially connected tile groups have different modal periods.
entries.notes: This is the single most common reason a whole-frame cadence verdict is wrong; always run it before reporting a shot-level cadence.

entries.label: Line boil / drawing boil cycle
entries.description: Deliberate frame-to-frame wobble of outlines on an otherwise static drawing, often on a short repeating cycle of 2-4 drawings.
entries.frame_evidence: Thin high-gradient contours shift by 1-3 px each cel while filled areas stay put; the change mask is a network of thin lines.
entries.detector_note: Change mask skeletonised (skimage.morphology.skeletonize) and tested for thinness (mean local width < 3 px) and for coincidence with cv2.Canny edges of the previous cel; measure the cycle length by phash self-similarity of the edge maps.
entries.notes: Compression mosquito noise around edges produces a similar thin change mask; require the displacement to be coherent along the contour, not random per pixel.

entries.label: Linear motion (no easing)
entries.description: A move with constant velocity throughout, a common tell of unpolished CG or of a mechanical object.
entries.frame_evidence: Cumulative displacement of a tracked feature is a straight line with abrupt starts and stops.
entries.detector_note: Linear fit R^2 > 0.98 across the move together with a step change in velocity at both ends (first and last cel velocity within 15 percent of the mean).
entries.notes: Perfectly legitimate for machinery, scrolling text and vehicles at constant speed; this is an observation, not a defect.

entries.label: Long-exposure / smeared single frame
entries.description: An individual frame integrating a long slice of time, with everything moving rendered as trails.
entries.frame_evidence: A frame whose moving regions are uniformly smeared along their motion direction with far greater blur width than neighbouring frames.
entries.detector_note: Per-frame blur width inside the moving mask, compared with the shot's own distribution; flag frames above p95 by more than 3x while static regions stay sharp (so it is not a focus change or a global blur).
entries.notes: Focus pulls and camera shake both blur; the static-region-stays-sharp condition is what isolates exposure.

entries.label: Long take / oner
entries.description: An unusually long uninterrupted shot.
entries.frame_evidence: A shot whose duration exceeds a high percentile of the file's own distribution and contains internal camera or subject movement.
entries.detector_note: Shots above max(20 s, p95 of the file's shot lengths); additionally report internal motion energy so a static title card is not reported as a oner.
entries.notes: A missed cut inside the shot inflates this; cross-check with the internal boundary-score maximum.

entries.label: Loop period
entries.description: The number of frames (and unique cels) after which the animation repeats.
entries.frame_evidence: The lag of the dominant off-diagonal stripe in the shot self-similarity matrix.
entries.detector_note: argmax of the mean of the self-similarity matrix along each diagonal, excluding lags < 3; report both frames and unique-cel counts, and the prominence over a shuffled-cel null.
entries.notes: The shuffled-cel null model is mandatory - any similarity matrix has diagonal structure.

entries.label: Loop seam pop
entries.description: A visible discontinuity at the join of a loop where the last cel does not flow into the first.
entries.frame_evidence: One frame pair inside an otherwise smooth cycle whose inter-frame displacement or MAE spikes far above the cycle's own median.
entries.detector_note: Within a confirmed loop, compare the MAE and flow magnitude at the wrap pair against the distribution of the other pairs in the cycle; flag when the wrap pair exceeds p95 of the in-cycle distribution by more than 2x.
entries.notes: Only meaningful once a loop is confirmed; on a non-loop this is just a fast frame.

entries.label: Graphic match cut
entries.description: A cut whose two sides share a dominant shape, line or composition so the eye reads continuity across different content.
entries.frame_evidence: Across a confirmed cut, the binary silhouette / dominant edge structure of the last and first frames correlate strongly while colour and texture do not.
entries.detector_note: At each confirmed cut compute a 8x8 downsampled edge-orientation histogram (HOG-like, numpy) and cv2.matchShapes on the largest thresholded contour of both boundary frames; flag when shape similarity is high (matchShapes < 0.15) while HSV histogram distance stays above the cut threshold.
entries.notes: This measures shape continuity, not authorial intent. Needs a null model: compute the same score on 200 random non-adjacent frame pairs from the same file and report the percentile, otherwise the number is meaningless.

entries.label: Motion match cut
entries.description: A cut where the direction and speed of the dominant motion carry through from the outgoing to the incoming shot.
entries.frame_evidence: The dominant optical-flow vector immediately before and immediately after a cut have similar angle and magnitude.
entries.detector_note: cv2.calcOpticalFlowFarneback on the 3 unique-cel pairs before and after the cut; compare the median flow vector angle (circular difference < 25 degrees) and log-magnitude ratio (within 2x).
entries.notes: MUST be computed on unique-cel indices: on 2s animation the naive pre-cut pair may be a duplicate pair whose flow is exactly zero, which would fake a mismatch. | TIER CORRECTED by completeness critic: cut_on_action is landmark and the other two deterministic, but all three compare CONTENT across a cut, which needs subject correspondence across the boundary. Nothing establishes that correspondence at a tier below model

entries.label: Semantic / conceptual match cut
entries.description: A cut linking two shots by meaning or by an object standing in for another rather than by pixel geometry.
entries.frame_evidence: Two boundary frames whose depicted subjects are analogous (a bone and a spacecraft, a wound and a sunset).
entries.detector_note: Build a side-by-side crop of the last and first frames of the cut and ask the VLM the closed question below; only run on cuts where the graphic-match score is in the top decile, to keep the VLM budget bounded.
entries.vlm_question: This picture shows two frames side by side, left and right. Do the main objects in the left and right halves have a similar shape, size and position? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: True semantic intent is not observable; this only records that a human-legible resemblance exists.

entries.label: Median shot length
entries.description: Median shot duration, robust to a few very long takes.
entries.frame_evidence: Aggregate of the shot list.
entries.detector_note: numpy.median over shot_length_seconds; report the median/mean ratio as a skew indicator.

entries.label: Micro shot (sub-second)
entries.description: A shot shorter than roughly 12 frames, used in flash cutting and impact montages.
entries.frame_evidence: Two boundaries less than 0.5 s apart with distinct content between them.
entries.detector_note: Shot list filter length < 0.5 s; require the shot to contain at least one unique cel that is dissimilar to both neighbours so a flash frame is not counted twice.

entries.label: Mixed cadence within one shot
entries.description: A shot whose drawing rate changes partway, e.g. 3s settling into 2s or dropping to 1s at an impact.
entries.frame_evidence: The hold-length run series contains two or more contiguous regimes with different modal lengths.
entries.detector_note: Segment the hold-length sequence with a changepoint scan (cumulative sum on hold length, permutation-tested); require each regime to span >=6 frames and the modal lengths to differ.
entries.notes: Very common and usually meaningful: the cadence change is where the animator spent the money.

entries.label: Morph transition
entries.description: One subject is continuously warped into another across the transition rather than blended.
entries.frame_evidence: Mid-transition frames are sharp (no ghosting) yet the subject silhouette deforms smoothly between two different shapes.
entries.detector_note: Needs a dense correspondence / warp-field estimator robust to identity change; optical flow alone cannot separate a morph from a fast deformation, and the sharpness test alone yields false positives on any elastic squash-and-stretch.
entries.notes: Deliberately marked model: we have no reliable morph detector today.

entries.label: Motion blur present or absent for the cadence
entries.description: Whether fast-moving content carries motion blur, which interacts with how the cadence reads.
entries.frame_evidence: Directional smearing of edges on the moving subject in the same frames where flow magnitude is high.
entries.detector_note: Inside the high-flow mask, compute the structure-tensor anisotropy and the edge transition width along vs across the flow direction; report the blur/flow ratio. Hand-drawn animation on 2s typically shows zero blur at high flow.
entries.notes: Encoder ringing and low-resolution upscaling both widen edges; calibrate the width measure on a static region of the same frame.

entries.label: Easing curve of a move
entries.description: Whether a movement accelerates in, decelerates out, or both (slow-in / slow-out).
entries.frame_evidence: The displacement-versus-cel curve of a tracked feature is S-shaped rather than a straight line.
entries.detector_note: Track a persistent ORB/Lucas-Kanade feature (cv2.calcOpticalFlowPyrLK) through the move; normalise its cumulative displacement to 0..1 over 0..1 time and fit a cubic Bezier ease; report the two control-point parameters and the R^2 against a linear fit.
entries.notes: With only 4-6 unique cels in a typical 2D move the fit is badly under-determined; report the sample count and treat fewer than 6 cels as indicative only.

entries.label: Motion-energy envelope per shot
entries.description: The time series of how much the image is moving across a shot, the backbone signal for all rhythm analysis.
entries.frame_evidence: Per unique-cel-pair mean optical-flow magnitude, forming a curve over the shot.
entries.detector_note: cv2.calcOpticalFlowFarneback(pyr_scale=0.5, levels=3, winsize=15, iterations=3, poly_n=5, poly_sigma=1.2) between CONSECUTIVE UNIQUE CELS only; energy = mean magnitude over the frame, optionally with global camera motion removed by subtracting the phaseCorrelate shift; resample the per-cel series back onto the frame timeline for display.
entries.notes: MUST be computed on unique-cel indices. Computed on raw frames it is halved on 2s and thirded on 3s, because half or two-thirds of the samples are exact zeros that are artefacts, not measurements.

entries.label: Motion-accent to beat alignment
entries.description: Whether motion-energy peaks and impacts land on the musical grid, independent of where the cuts are.
entries.frame_evidence: The offset between each motion-envelope peak and the nearest beat.
entries.detector_note: Same offset statistics as cut_to_beat_alignment but using the unique-cel motion-envelope peaks as the event list, with the same shifted-null control.
entries.notes: On 3s animation motion peaks can only land on every third frame, which biases the offset distribution; correct for this quantisation before computing the z-score.

entries.label: Motion trail / streak
entries.description: A continuous drawn or rendered streak following a fast object, as opposed to discrete echoes.
entries.frame_evidence: An elongated gradient-aligned region extending backwards from the subject along its motion direction, present within the frame itself.
entries.detector_note: Inside the high-flow mask, measure the structure-tensor orientation and compare with the flow direction; a trail shows an elongated component (aspect ratio > 3) whose major axis is within 15 degrees of the motion vector and whose intensity decays monotonically away from the subject.
entries.notes: Speed lines in anime are a graphic device sitting in the same place; they will fire here and that may be the intended reading, but they are drawn, not a temporal effect.

entries.label: Mouth-flap-only update
entries.description: A partial cel update confined to the mouth region during dialogue, the cheapest form of animation.
entries.frame_evidence: The only changing region sits inside the lower third of a detected face bounding box, cycling between a small number of shapes.
entries.detector_note: mediapipe FaceMesh (or face detection) to get the face box; test that the partial-update component centroid lies within the mouth region (landmarks 61,291,13,14 convex hull dilated 20 percent) and that the number of distinct mouth-region cels in the shot is small (cluster the mouth crops by phash).
entries.notes: mediapipe FaceMesh is unreliable on stylised anime faces and on profile views; when the face box is absent fall back to the deterministic partial-update entry and do not claim it is a mouth.

entries.label: Multiplane / parallax differential pan
entries.description: Foreground, midground and background layers panning at different speeds within one held-artwork move.
entries.frame_evidence: The optical flow field is piecewise constant with two or more distinct horizontal velocities occupying spatially coherent bands.
entries.detector_note: Farneback flow on unique cels; histogram the horizontal velocity component and count modes with scipy.signal.find_peaks; require >=2 modes separated by more than 1 px/frame each covering >8 percent of frame area and forming connected regions (cv2.connectedComponents on the per-mode mask).
entries.notes: A real 3D dolly through a live-action scene produces a continuous velocity gradient, not discrete modes; the modality test is the 2D/3D discriminator.

entries.label: Musical beat grid and tempo
entries.description: An estimated steady tempo and beat phase for the passage, against which cuts can be compared.
entries.frame_evidence: Not visual; periodicity of the audio novelty curve.
entries.detector_note: Autocorrelate the novelty curve over a 60-180 BPM lag range (numpy.correlate), pick the dominant lag, then find the phase maximising the summed novelty at grid positions; report tempo, phase and a confidence from peak prominence.
entries.notes: librosa is not installed; this is a hand-rolled tempo tracker and it fails on rubato, on speech-only passages and on drone scores. Report confidence and refuse comparisons below 0.4.

entries.label: Near loop (cycle under a moving camera)
entries.description: A repeating animation cycle that is not pixel-identical because the camera or background translates through it.
entries.frame_evidence: After compensating a constant global translation, frames t and t+P match closely.
entries.detector_note: Estimate the per-frame global shift with cv2.phaseCorrelate, integrate it to a cumulative displacement, warp the candidate pair into alignment (cv2.warpAffine) and measure MAE inside the overlap; search P over 4-60.
entries.notes: This is the standard anime running-across-a-scrolling-background case; the exact-loop detector misses it entirely.

entries.label: Per-file duplicate threshold null model
entries.description: The measured noise floor that separates 'same drawing, re-encoded' from 'a genuinely new drawing'.
entries.frame_evidence: The distribution of consecutive-frame MAE over the whole file, which is bimodal on animation and unimodal on live action.
entries.detector_note: Histogram all consecutive-frame MAE values; fit a two-component split by Otsu (skimage.filters.threshold_otsu) on the log-MAE distribution; if the bimodality coefficient is below 0.55 declare the file NOT hold-based and refuse all cadence verdicts.
entries.notes: Without this every downstream cadence number is a confident fiction. Live action, film-grained transfers and heavy denoising all suppress the bimodality - that is a legitimate 'not detectable' outcome, not a failure.

entries.label: Overall temporal-analysis confidence
entries.description: A single reported figure saying how much of this domain's output can be trusted for this file.
entries.frame_evidence: Aggregate of the guard outcomes: duplicate bimodality, pulldown verdict, VFR jitter, boundary recall proxy, audio presence.
entries.detector_note: Combine cadence_verdicts_enabled, pulldown_detected, irregular_delta_fraction, flash_guard trigger rate, audio_present_flag and flow_sample_coverage into a per-file confidence vector, and emit the LIMITING factor by name.
entries.notes: Required so downstream consumers never read a cadence or ASL figure without knowing the guard state that produced it.

entries.label: Overlay / subtitle-only change guard
entries.description: A negative control that suppresses boundary detections caused only by a subtitle, caption or HUD element changing.
entries.frame_evidence: All frame change is confined to a small band (typically the lower fifth) while the rest of the frame is temporally identical.
entries.detector_note: Compute the change mask; if >92 percent of changed pixels lie in a horizontal band under 25 percent of frame height and the remainder of the frame has per-tile diff below the duplicate threshold, veto the boundary.
entries.notes: Do not ask moondream to read the band to confirm it is text - moondream confabulates on typography. Use geometry only, or the OCR judge if available.

entries.label: Partial cel update (limited animation)
entries.description: Only a small region of the drawing changes between cels while the rest is held.
entries.frame_evidence: The change mask between two unique cels is a small, spatially compact region (a mouth, an eye, a hand) surrounded by a temporally identical field.
entries.detector_note: Threshold the abs-diff at 3x the noise floor, morphological close (cv2.morphologyEx 5x5), take connected components; classify as a partial update when the total changed area is < 8 percent of frame and is contained in <= 3 components.
entries.notes: Fails on any panning shot; run only where the warp-compensated residual test says the frame is otherwise held.

entries.label: Pose-to-pose versus straight-ahead animation
entries.description: Whether the animation is built from planned key poses with inbetweens or drawn continuously frame by frame.
entries.frame_evidence: Pose-to-pose shows clear held extremes with clustered spacing; straight-ahead shows even spacing and drifting volumes.
entries.detector_note: Requires reliable pose extraction on stylised drawings to identify extremes, which mediapipe cannot deliver on 2D art; the energy-envelope proxy conflates this with cadence choice.
entries.notes: Known blind spot; the peakiness metric may be emitted but must not be labelled as this distinction.

entries.label: Pre-impact silence / drop-out
entries.description: A deliberate dip to near-silence in the frames before a big hit, to make the hit land harder.
entries.frame_evidence: Audio RMS falling below 15 percent of the local median for 4-30 frames immediately preceding a detected impact.
entries.detector_note: 20 ms RMS envelope from the extracted audio; test the 0.15-1.2 s window before each detected impact cel for a sustained dip below 0.15x the surrounding median.
entries.notes: Loudness-normalised broadcast mixes flatten this; absence is not evidence of absence.

entries.label: Push / slide transition
entries.description: The outgoing shot is pushed out of frame by the incoming shot moving in, both translating together.
entries.frame_evidence: Both the old and new content translate with the same per-frame offset; the whole frame is a rigid horizontal or vertical shift of a two-image strip.
entries.detector_note: cv2.phaseCorrelate between consecutive frames gives a near-constant integer shift; verify that the region vacated by the old content matches the incoming shot translated by the same vector (SSD < 5 grey levels).
entries.notes: A whip pan inside one continuous shot also produces a constant phase-correlation shift; the discriminator is that in a push the outgoing image content does not itself change.

entries.label: Quadruped / creature locomotion cycle
entries.description: A repeating gait for a non-bipedal body plan (gallop, trot, slither, flap).
entries.frame_evidence: Periodic silhouette deformation with a stable period but no human skeletal structure.
entries.detector_note: Requires an animal pose model we do not have; mediapipe covers humans only. A silhouette-periodicity proxy exists (see near_loop_cycle) but cannot name the gait.
entries.notes: Report periodicity if present, never a gait name.

entries.label: Reverse playback (physics tell)
entries.description: Footage played backwards where nothing else in the file reveals it, detectable only from physics running the wrong way.
entries.frame_evidence: Falling debris rises, smoke converges into a source, splashes retract, cloth un-billows.
entries.detector_note: Needs a learned arrow-of-time classifier; hand-built proxies (upward-biased particle flow, negative divergence of smoke fields) are defeated by any genuinely rising smoke, jumping subject or upward camera tilt and produce confident nonsense without a trained null.
entries.notes: Deliberately marked model. The proxy metrics may be emitted but must never be turned into a verdict.

entries.label: Reversed repeat of an earlier segment
entries.description: A stretch of frames that is an earlier stretch played backwards, the ping-pong loop.
entries.frame_evidence: Frames t..t+k match frames s+k..s in reverse order.
entries.detector_note: In the shot self-similarity matrix (phash Hamming), search for an ANTI-diagonal stripe rather than a diagonal one; confirm the best candidate at full resolution with MAE.
entries.notes: Symmetric motions (a pendulum, a blink) legitimately produce anti-diagonal structure; require pixel-level match, not just similarity.

entries.label: Rewind / scrub UI effect
entries.description: A diegetic playback effect - VHS rewind bars, a scrubbing timeline, tape noise - presented as time being manipulated on screen.
entries.frame_evidence: Horizontal tearing bands, tracking noise or an on-screen transport graphic combined with reversed or accelerated content.
entries.detector_note: Nominate on strong horizontal band artefacts (row-wise luma discontinuity periodicity) or a palindrome detection, then crop and ask the VLM.
entries.vlm_question: In this cropped picture, are there horizontal noise bars, static or tracking lines across the image like an old videotape? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Ask about bars and lines, never about any text or timecode in the graphic - moondream confabulates text; route text to the OCR path instead.

entries.label: Rhythmic flash pulsing
entries.description: Regular periodic brightness pulsing across a passage, from strobes, lightning or a designed pulse.
entries.frame_evidence: The mean-luma series shows a strong periodic component at a fixed frequency over many frames.
entries.detector_note: numpy.fft.rfft of the detrended mean-luma series over a sliding 4 s window; flag when one bin carries > 0.3 of the total power; report frequency in Hz and peak-to-trough amplitude.
entries.notes: Also the core measurement for photosensitive-epilepsy risk (3 Hz band); report the 3-30 Hz band energy separately.

entries.label: Run cycle
entries.description: A repeating running gait, distinguished from a walk by a flight phase where neither foot contacts.
entries.frame_evidence: Periodic ankle trajectories with a shorter period, larger vertical hip oscillation and a window where both ankles are above their contact baseline.
entries.detector_note: Same periodicity machinery as walk_cycle plus a flight-phase test: both ankle y-values above the running 10th-percentile baseline simultaneously for at least one cel per period; report hip vertical oscillation amplitude.
entries.notes: Same landmark limitations as walk_cycle; in 2D a running character is frequently drawn without correct ground contact at all.

entries.label: Scene grouping from shot similarity
entries.description: Consecutive shots clustered into scenes by shared palette, luminance and background layout.
entries.frame_evidence: Aggregate: a block-diagonal structure in the shot-to-shot similarity matrix.
entries.detector_note: Per-shot mean HSV histogram plus mean 8x8 luma thumbnail; build the shot-similarity matrix, run scipy.cluster.hierarchy.linkage with a contiguity constraint (only merge temporally adjacent clusters) and cut the dendrogram at the largest gap.
entries.notes: sklearn is not installed; use scipy hierarchical clustering only. Colour-graded sequences merge scenes that a human would separate.

entries.label: Settle / overshoot oscillation
entries.description: Damped oscillation after an action stops, the follow-through that sells weight.
entries.frame_evidence: After an energy peak, a short alternating-direction motion of decreasing amplitude before rest.
entries.detector_note: Track the centroid of the moving mask after the peak; test the displacement series for sign alternation with geometrically decreasing amplitude (fit an exponentially damped sinusoid with scipy.optimize.curve_fit; require R^2 > 0.7 and damping ratio in 0.05-0.6).
entries.notes: On 2s/3s animation there may only be 3-5 unique cels in the settle, too few for a stable fit; report fit_r2 and refuse below 4 samples.

entries.label: Custom shape / graphic wipe
entries.description: A transition using a designed matte shape (star, heart, logo, brush stroke, character silhouette).
entries.frame_evidence: The frame-difference mask has a recognisable non-geometric silhouette that grows or shrinks across the transition.
entries.detector_note: Detect the transition support deterministically (non-linear, non-radial growing mask), crop the mask-overlay composite mid-transition and ask the VLM what shape the boundary is.
entries.vlm_question: In this image, is the boundary between the two overlapping pictures a simple straight line or circle, or is it a decorative shape such as a star, heart, brush stroke or silhouette? Answer: straight, circle, or decorative.
entries.notes: Small VLMs answer 'decorative' too readily; require the deterministic shape-complexity metric to agree.

entries.label: Shot length dispersion
entries.description: How variable the cutting rhythm is across the file.
entries.frame_evidence: Aggregate of the shot list.
entries.detector_note: Standard deviation, coefficient of variation and interquartile range of shot_length_seconds; also the Gini coefficient of screen time by shot.

entries.label: Shot length in frames
entries.description: The duration of each individual shot measured between consecutive confirmed boundaries.
entries.frame_evidence: Distance between two boundary frame indices; evidence lives in the boundary list, not one frame.
entries.detector_note: Difference of consecutive entries of the confirmed boundary index list; also emit seconds using the ffprobe r_frame_rate, and a second value using unique-cel count for animation.
entries.notes: For anime always report BOTH the frame length and the unique-cel length; a 24-frame shot on 3s carries only 8 drawings.

entries.label: Shot / reverse-shot alternation
entries.description: A dialogue pattern alternating between two complementary framings of two characters.
entries.frame_evidence: A run of >=4 shots alternating between two clusters of similar framings, each containing a single face at mirrored horizontal positions.
entries.detector_note: Needs stable per-character identity across shots; we have no face-recognition model installed (insightface absent) and mediapipe face-mesh gives geometry, not identity. Palette clustering alone confuses reverse shots with any AB alternation.
entries.notes: Logged as a known blind spot.

entries.label: Single-frame insert
entries.description: One isolated frame of foreign content spliced into a shot (subliminal insert, glitch, horror flash).
entries.frame_evidence: Exactly one frame that is dissimilar to both its neighbours, which are themselves similar to each other.
entries.detector_note: Test d(t-1,t) and d(t,t+1) both above the cut threshold while d(t-1,t+1) is below the duplicate threshold; guard against flashes with the illumination-normalised score.
entries.notes: Codec keyframe corruption and dropped frames produce the same pattern; report a codec-artefact suspicion when the frame shows blocking.

entries.label: Slow motion by frame duplication
entries.description: Speed reduced by repeating frames, producing stepped, juddering slow motion.
entries.frame_evidence: A regular pattern of duplicate frames inside a shot that is otherwise photographic (i.e. not animation).
entries.detector_note: Duplicate run-length mode >= 2 in material classified as live action or 3D render; distinguish from animation cadence by the presence of grain/noise elsewhere and by the material classifier.
entries.notes: This is exactly the same measurement as animation-on-2s; only the material class separates the two interpretations. Report both readings when material class is uncertain.

entries.label: Slow motion by optical-flow interpolation
entries.description: Speed reduced by synthesising in-between frames, which introduces warping artefacts.
entries.frame_evidence: Smooth slow motion with no duplicates but with rubbery edge deformation, halo artefacts around fast limbs and occasional torn thin structures.
entries.detector_note: Nominate candidates deterministically (no duplicates, low flow, high flow-divergence variance near occlusion boundaries, local warping residual when frame t is predicted from t-1 and t+1) then crop the worst region per THE CROP RULE and ask the VLM.
entries.vlm_question: In this cropped picture, does any part of the object look melted, smeared or torn apart in a way that a real photograph would not look? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: The deterministic candidate score alone gives many false positives on genuine motion blur; the VLM pass is the filter, and it must run on a tight crop.

entries.label: Native slow motion (overcranked)
entries.description: Motion sampled at a higher rate and played back slower, so movement is slow but every frame is sharp and unique.
entries.frame_evidence: Low inter-frame displacement, no duplicate frames, no motion blur despite visibly fast subject action, and full temporal detail in fast phenomena (splashes, debris).
entries.detector_note: Within a shot: median flow magnitude on unique cels well below the file median, duplicate_fraction near zero, blur_per_flow_ratio low, and the high-frequency spatial energy (variance of cv2.Laplacian) stable frame to frame.
entries.notes: A genuinely slow-moving subject is the main false positive; there is no pixel-level way to separate 'slow action' from 'slowed fast action' without semantic cues. Report confidence, not a verdict, unless splash/debris cues are present.

entries.label: Smash cut
entries.description: An abrupt cut across a large energy contrast, typically loud-to-quiet or still-to-violent.
entries.frame_evidence: A confirmed cut where per-shot motion energy and audio RMS both change by a large factor within a few frames.
entries.detector_note: Extract audio with ffmpeg -f f32le, compute 20 ms RMS; at each cut compare the mean motion energy (mean |Farneback flow| over unique-cel pairs) and audio RMS of the 0.5 s before and after; flag when either ratio exceeds 6x in either direction.
entries.notes: Files with no audio track, or with music mixed at constant loudness, lose half the evidence; report which channels contributed.

entries.label: Smear / multiple-image frame
entries.description: A single drawing that depicts an object in several positions at once or as a long stretched streak to bridge a large motion.
entries.frame_evidence: One unique cel in which the moving subject appears as repeated ghosted copies or as an extreme elongated distortion, present for only 1-2 frames.
entries.detector_note: Nominate candidates deterministically (a single unique cel bracketed by high flow magnitude, containing an elongated high-gradient region with aspect ratio > 4 aligned to the motion direction), then crop the region tight per THE CROP RULE and ask the VLM the closed question below.
entries.vlm_question: In this cropped picture, is the moving object drawn as one clear solid shape, or is it stretched into a long streak or drawn as several overlapping copies? Answer: solid, streak, or copies.
entries.notes: Never ask on the full frame - the smear occupies a small area and a small VLM will describe the scene instead. Rendered motion blur in 3D gives the same answer; use the material class to separate.

entries.label: Smear-into-hold timing
entries.description: The classic anime pattern of one smeared transitional drawing followed immediately by a long held pose.
entries.frame_evidence: A single-cel high-energy smear immediately followed by a duplicate run of 4 or more frames.
entries.detector_note: Detect a snap cel (energy ratio > 4) whose next unique cel begins a hold run >= 4 frames; report the smear-to-hold ratio.
entries.notes: One of the most reliable stylistic fingerprints of hand-drawn action, and one of the cheapest to measure once unique cels are correct.

entries.label: Snap (peak-velocity cel)
entries.description: The single fastest moment of an action, often a lone drawing spanning the whole move.
entries.frame_evidence: One unique cel pair carrying a flow magnitude several times the shot median, frequently accompanied by a smear or a blur.
entries.detector_note: argmax of the unique-cel motion-energy envelope within a shot; report its magnitude relative to the shot median and its width at half maximum.
entries.notes: Farneback flow saturates on very large displacements; when the displacement exceeds roughly winsize the magnitude is under-estimated. Cross-check with ORB feature displacement for the peak cel.

entries.label: Speed ramp
entries.description: A continuous change of playback speed within a single shot, typically fast into slow or slow into fast.
entries.frame_evidence: Within one shot, the per-pair displacement of the same tracked content changes monotonically without any change in the physical action.
entries.detector_note: Track the median flow magnitude series on unique cels within a shot, detrend for the action itself is impossible, so instead test the RATIO of successive displacement of persistent ORB tracks; a ramp shows a monotone multiplicative trend (Spearman |rho| > 0.8 over >=10 pairs) together with a corresponding monotone trend in duplicate rate or blur width.
entries.notes: A subject genuinely accelerating produces the same flow trend; the corroborating cues (blur width scaling with speed, duplicate rate changing) are what make it a RAMP rather than an acceleration. Report which cues agreed.

entries.label: 3D animation stepped to 2s/3s
entries.description: CG animation deliberately rendered or retimed so it holds for 2 or 3 frames, imitating hand-drawn cadence.
entries.frame_evidence: Exact pixel duplicates in fully rendered CG imagery, including on lighting, shadows and motion blur.
entries.detector_note: Duplicate detection on CG is near-exact (very low noise floor); classify cadence with the same hold-length machinery and additionally flag that the material is CG (smooth shading gradients, sub-pixel-consistent edges) so the finding is not mislabelled 2D.
entries.notes: Some pipelines step the character but not the camera; expect layer_differential_cadence to fire alongside.

entries.label: Sustained stillness passage
entries.description: A long stretch with almost no motion and no cuts, the breathing space of an edit.
entries.frame_evidence: A run of >= 2 s with compensated motion energy below the 10th percentile of the file and no boundary.
entries.detector_note: Threshold the compensated energy envelope at the file p10, run-length encode, keep runs >= 2 s with no cut inside; report position and duration.
entries.notes: On animation a long held cel gives literally zero energy; report whether the stillness is a hold (duplicates) or genuine low motion, as these read very differently.

entries.label: Stop motion
entries.description: Physically photographed frame-by-frame animation, with characteristic per-frame lighting flicker and absent motion blur.
entries.frame_evidence: Photographic material with zero motion blur at high displacement, tiny random global luminance flicker between frames, and visible fingerprints/surface micro-changes on puppets.
entries.detector_note: Combine: blur_per_flow_ratio near zero on photographic material, per-frame mean-luma random walk with stddev 0.3-2 grey levels on a static region, and no duplicate frames. Report a composite score; corroborate with a VLM crop if the score is marginal.
entries.notes: Modern stop motion is often shot with motion-control blur and denoised, erasing both cues; and CG imitating stop motion (stepped, blur-free) is indistinguishable by construction.

entries.label: Stutter / step-print
entries.description: A deliberate juddering look made by printing each frame two or three times, or by repeating a short pattern.
entries.frame_evidence: A regular short-period duplicate pattern (AABB or AAB) inside a shot whose material is otherwise per-frame unique.
entries.detector_note: Autocorrelate the duplicate mask inside a shot; a peak at lag 2 or 3 with a hold-length mode of 2-3 in live-action/3D material, applied over a run of at least 12 frames.
entries.notes: Identical measurement to animation-on-2s and to duplicated slow motion; the interpretation depends entirely on material class and on whether the effect is local to one passage.

entries.label: 3:2 pulldown (telecine)
entries.description: 24p material distributed over 30i/30p frames in a repeating 3-2 field or frame pattern.
entries.frame_evidence: A repeating period-5 pattern of duplicated frames or of combed frames.
entries.detector_note: Autocorrelate the duplicate mask and the interlace-comb score; a strong peak at lag 5 with a 3-2 run-length signature confirms pulldown. Report the pulldown phase.
entries.notes: Mistaking pulldown for artistic on-2s/on-3s is the classic cadence error; this entry must run before the cadence classifiers and its verdict must veto them.

entries.label: Time lapse
entries.description: Extreme fast motion from long intervals between captures, so continuity between frames is largely broken.
entries.frame_evidence: Consecutive frames share the scene layout but every moving element jumps discontinuously; clouds, shadows and crowds change wholesale while the static frame stays registered.
entries.detector_note: Within a shot, per-tile change is high in sky/crowd regions while global phase correlation shows zero camera shift, and optical flow fails to find coherent correspondence (high Farneback residual / low forward-backward flow consistency).
entries.notes: Heavy noise or a strobing light also breaks flow consistency; require the static-tile fraction to be high, i.e. a locked-off camera.

entries.label: Pause and continue (time remap hold)
entries.description: Motion stops dead mid-shot for a few frames then resumes, without a cut.
entries.frame_evidence: A duplicate run embedded inside a shot with substantial motion on both sides and no boundary score at either end of the run.
entries.detector_note: Duplicate run of 3-30 frames whose preceding and following 8 frames both carry motion energy above the shot median, with no cut candidate within 3 frames.
entries.notes: In animation this is simply a hold; in live action it is a time remap. Same measurement, different label by material class.

entries.label: Time-lapse exposure flicker
entries.description: Frame-to-frame brightness pulsing from aperture stepping across a time lapse.
entries.frame_evidence: Global mean luma oscillating by several percent frame to frame with no scene reason.
entries.detector_note: Detrend the mean-luma series over the shot (scipy.signal.detrend), measure the high-frequency residual stddev and its lag-1 autocorrelation (flicker is near-zero autocorrelation, a lighting change is smooth).
entries.notes: Fluorescent-light beating and PWM LED sources produce identical flicker in ordinary footage.

entries.label: Spacing chart between extremes
entries.description: The distribution of inbetween positions between two extremes, the animator's spacing chart.
entries.frame_evidence: The set of positions of a tracked point across the cels of one move.
entries.detector_note: Needs a reliable single tracked point on a deforming drawn character across a move with only a handful of samples; Lucas-Kanade loses drawn features whose interior is flat colour, and there is no correspondence ground truth.
entries.notes: Explicitly not detectable today.

entries.label: Transition type histogram
entries.description: The counts and proportions of each transition type used in the file.
entries.frame_evidence: Aggregation over all detected boundaries; no single-frame evidence.
entries.detector_note: Tally the outcomes of every boundary classifier over the file and normalise per minute of runtime.

entries.label: Unique-cel index map
entries.description: The mapping from container frame index to the index of the distinct drawing it displays.
entries.frame_evidence: A run-length encoding of the duplicate mask across the shot.
entries.detector_note: Run-length encode the duplicate_flag series within each shot; emit per-frame unique_cel_id and per-cel hold length. Every other temporal metric in this taxonomy must consume this map rather than raw frame indices.
entries.notes: Must be rebuilt per shot: cadence changes at cuts, and a cross-shot run-length is meaningless.

entries.label: Unique drawings per second
entries.description: The effective drawing rate of a shot, independent of container frame rate.
entries.frame_evidence: Count of distinct drawings within a one-second sliding window.
entries.detector_note: unique_cel_count / shot_duration_seconds using the ffprobe frame rate; also emit a sliding 1 s series so within-shot changes are visible.
entries.notes: Typical TV anime lands at 8-12; a value of 24 in a nominally 2D shot usually means either a CG element, a pan, or grain defeating the duplicate test.

entries.label: Variable frame rate / timestamp jitter
entries.description: Non-uniform frame presentation intervals in the container, which corrupts any frame-count-based timing.
entries.frame_evidence: Container PTS deltas that are not constant.
entries.detector_note: ffprobe -show_frames -show_entries frame=pkt_pts_time -of csv; compute the delta series, its stddev and the fraction of deltas deviating more than 5 percent from the mode.
entries.notes: If irregular_delta_fraction is high, all seconds-based metrics in this domain must be computed from PTS, not from frame counts.

entries.label: Walk cycle
entries.description: A repeating bipedal walking gait, usually 8-16 unique drawings, often reused.
entries.frame_evidence: Ankle and knee landmark trajectories that are periodic and antiphase between left and right legs, with a contact-passing-contact structure.
entries.detector_note: mediapipe Pose over unique cels; take the vertical and horizontal trajectories of landmarks 27/28 (ankles) and 25/26 (knees) normalised by torso length; FFT (numpy.fft.rfft) the ankle separation signal, require a dominant frequency with >0.4 of total power and a left-right phase difference near pi.
entries.notes: mediapipe pose fails on stylised, chibi, quadruped and non-human characters, and on any figure smaller than roughly 15 percent of frame height; refuse a verdict below landmark_visibility_mean 0.5 rather than guessing.

entries.label: Whip pan transition
entries.description: A cut hidden inside a fast horizontal blur, so two shots appear joined by one violent camera swing.
entries.frame_evidence: A 2-8 frame run of extreme directional motion blur (anisotropic gradient energy) bracketing a hist-distance discontinuity.
entries.detector_note: Measure directional blur by the ratio of gradient energy along vs across the dominant direction (cv2.Sobel, structure tensor eigenvalue ratio); require ratio > 4 and phase-correlation shift > 8 percent of frame width for >=2 frames, with a cut score peak inside the blurred run.
entries.notes: In 2D animation whip pans are drawn as speed-line smears with no true blur; the structure tensor still fires but the ratio is lower - use a separate 2D threshold.

entries.label: Wing flap cycle
entries.description: A repeating up-down wing beat.
entries.frame_evidence: A periodic vertical expansion and contraction of the silhouette bounding box on either side of a body.
entries.detector_note: Segment the moving foreground by frame differencing against the shot median background (numpy.median over unique cels); track the bounding-box height and the second moment of the mask about the horizontal axis; FFT for a dominant frequency.
entries.notes: Only works with a stable camera and a separable subject; a moving camera destroys the median background.

entries.label: Clock / radial wipe
entries.description: A wipe whose boundary is a radius sweeping around a centre point.
entries.frame_evidence: The frame-difference mask grows as an angular sector about a fixed centre, its subtended angle increasing monotonically.
entries.detector_note: Convert the accumulated change mask to polar coordinates with cv2.linearPolar about the mask centroid; accept when the filled angular support grows monotonically and the radial support is full at every covered angle.
entries.notes: Rare outside broadcast graphics and retro anime eyecatches.

entries.label: Diagonal / angled wipe
entries.description: A wipe whose boundary is a straight line at an arbitrary angle.
entries.frame_evidence: The frame-difference mask is a half-plane bounded by an oblique straight line that translates along its normal each frame.
entries.detector_note: Threshold the abs-diff mask, run cv2.HoughLines on its boundary from cv2.Canny; require one dominant line whose rho advances monotonically and whose theta is stable within 3 degrees across the transition.

entries.label: Linear wipe (horizontal or vertical)
entries.description: A transition where a straight boundary sweeps across the frame replacing shot A with shot B.
entries.frame_evidence: A short window where the per-column (or per-row) difference profile shows a sharp step whose position advances monotonically frame to frame while pixels on either side of the step stay unchanged.
entries.detector_note: Compute per-column mean |frame_t - frame_{t-1}| profile; fit a step edge (argmax of the 1D gradient of the cumulative profile); accept a wipe when the step position moves monotonically by a near-constant increment across >=4 frames and the residual outside the step is < 2 grey levels.
entries.notes: A hard vertical shadow or a passing foreground object crossing frame produces a similar advancing edge; require the region behind the edge to be temporally frozen new content.

entries.label: Zero-optical-flow artefact guard
entries.description: A control that prevents reporting 'no motion' when the zero came from measuring flow between two duplicate frames.
entries.frame_evidence: An optical-flow field that is identically zero everywhere, coinciding with a duplicate frame pair.
entries.detector_note: Before any flow computation, resample the frame index list to unique-cel indices; if a flow result has max magnitude exactly 0.0 and the pair is flagged duplicate, discard the sample instead of averaging it into any envelope.
entries.notes: Without this guard every motion-energy envelope on 2s animation is halved and every anime looks half as fast as it is. This is the highest-value guard in the domain.

entries.label: Anger cross / popping-vein symbol (anime)
entries.description: The stylised cruciform vein mark drawn on the head or nearby to signal irritation or rage.
entries.frame_evidence: A small red or black plus-shaped or hash-shaped symbol on the temple, forehead or floating beside the head.
entries.detector_note: Crop the head with padding and ask qwen2.5vl; deterministic corroboration is a small high-a compact component with a cross-like skeleton (skimage.morphology.skeletonize branch-point count of 1 with 4 endpoints)
entries.vlm_question: In this cropped image of a cartoon character, is there a small red cross-shaped or popping-vein anger symbol drawn on or near the head? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: A pure symbol; must never be merged with vein_bulge.

entries.label: Stylised/anime face present
entries.description: A drawn anime-style face is present, detected by a detector tuned for drawn faces rather than photographic ones.
entries.frame_evidence: Large stylised eyes, minimal nose, a simple line mouth inside a smooth-shaded head shape.
entries.detector_note: Needs an anime face detector such as lbpcascade_animeface or a YOLO anime-face weight; neither the cascade file nor ultralytics is installed today
entries.notes: NOT INSTALLED: ultralytics and the anime cascade. Until one is added, all 2D face localisation falls back to the vlm on a whole-frame crop, which violates THE CROP RULE and is unreliable.

entries.label: 2D blink drawing count
entries.description: How many unique drawings an animated blink is made of, the animation-craft observable (a 2-drawing snap versus a 4-drawing soft blink).
entries.frame_evidence: The sequence of distinct eye drawings between the last fully-open and the next fully-open cel.
entries.detector_note: Within a template-tracked eye ROI, cluster the unique-cel crops by normalised cross-correlation (cv2.matchTemplate TM_CCOEFF_NORMED, link at 0.92) and count distinct clusters spanning the closure interval
entries.notes: Depends on a stable eye ROI across the blink; a moving head breaks the template track and inflates the drawing count. | TIER CORRECTED by completeness critic: Marked deterministic, but every one of them needs an ALIGNED FACE REGION, and the face mesh in that same shard is landmark-tier (and face_head.facemesh_fit_failure exists precisely because it fails on stylised art). Pall

entries.label: Double blink / blink burst
entries.description: Two or more blinks in rapid succession, a common surprise or disbelief beat.
entries.frame_evidence: Two EAR troughs separated by a partial reopen inside a short window.
entries.detector_note: Two or more detected blink troughs whose inter-trough interval is under 400 ms of screen time with an intervening EAR recovery above 0.6*baseline

entries.label: Natural blink
entries.description: A fast involuntary full closure and reopening of both eyelids.
entries.frame_evidence: EAR collapses toward zero for one to three unique cels and returns to baseline.
entries.detector_note: scipy.signal.find_peaks on (baseline_ear - ear_mean) with prominence 0.45*baseline and width 1-4 unique-cel samples; closure must be bilateral (ear_asymmetry under 0.25*baseline at the trough). all temporal maths run on UNIQUE-CEL indices only: consecutive frames whose 64x64 grayscale mean-abs-diff is under 0.5/255 collapse to one index, so a 24fps anime file yields 8-12 samples/sec
entries.notes: The null model is a per-shot permutation of the EAR series: a blink detector with no null reports blinks in landmark jitter. On 2D, a blink is 2-4 drawings and may be a single cel, which is at the detector width floor.

entries.label: Blink rate
entries.description: Blinks per minute across a shot, an autonomic-arousal proxy.
entries.frame_evidence: The count of blink events divided by shot duration.
entries.detector_note: blink_count from the natural-blink detector divided by shot wall duration from ffprobe timestamps; report alongside the fraction of the shot where FaceMesh actually held a fit
entries.notes: Meaningless if coverage is low; a shot where the mesh fit for 30 percent of frames will under-report rate by roughly the same factor and must be logged NOT DETECTABLE instead.

entries.label: Slow / deliberate blink
entries.description: A closure held noticeably longer than a reflex blink, reading as weariness, sensuality or resignation.
entries.frame_evidence: EAR stays under half baseline for more than about 250 ms of screen time.
entries.detector_note: Same find_peaks chain but selecting troughs whose width at half-prominence exceeds 0.25 s converted to unique-cel samples using the measured unique-cel rate, not the container fps
entries.notes: Using container fps instead of the unique-cel rate makes every anime blink look 2-3x slower than it is; this is the single most common temporal error in this domain.

entries.label: Blush on the cheeks
entries.description: Localised reddening over the cheekbones from embarrassment, attraction, cold, alcohol or exertion.
entries.frame_evidence: A warm red-pink patch over each cheekbone that is redder than the surrounding face.
entries.detector_note: Mean LAB a channel inside cheek ROIs centred on landmarks 205 and 425 minus mean a over the rest of the face mask; blush when the differential exceeds the shot baseline by more than about 3 a-units
entries.notes: The face-relative differential is essential: an absolute redness test is a skin-tone detector, not a blush detector. Warm practical lighting on one side produces a one-sided false positive.

entries.label: Blush hatch lines (anime)
entries.description: The drawn diagonal strokes or solid ovals across the nose bridge and cheeks that stand in for a blush.
entries.frame_evidence: Two to four short parallel diagonal lines on each cheek, or flat oval patches of colour.
entries.detector_note: In the cheek ROI, cv2.HoughLinesP restricted to short segments (0.02-0.08 IOD) with a consistent orientation cluster, counted per side; solid-patch variant caught by the a-channel differential above
entries.notes: Needs a face bbox on 2D art, which today only the vlm can supply reliably. Freckles and shading hatch on other parts of the face also produce line clusters.

entries.label: Asymmetric brow (single raise)
entries.description: One brow raised while the other stays or lowers, the scepticism, challenge or amusement register.
entries.frame_evidence: One brow visibly higher than the other in the same frame.
entries.detector_note: |brow_height_left - brow_height_right| exceeding 0.045 IOD sustained 2 samples with |head_roll_deg| under 12
entries.notes: Head roll produces a pure geometric asymmetry; the roll gate is mandatory.

entries.label: Brow furrow / lower (anger, effort, concentration)
entries.description: Both brows pulled down and together.
entries.frame_evidence: Reduced brow-to-eye gap plus vertical creases between the brows.
entries.detector_note: brow_height_mean below neutral by 0.05 IOD together with a reduced inter-brow distance |x(107)-x(336)| normalised by inter-ocular distance |p33-p263| so the value is scale invariant; both conditions required
entries.notes: Requiring both conditions is what separates a furrow from a squint that drags the brow landmarks down with the lid.

entries.label: Brow height primitive
entries.description: The numeric primitive for all brow observables: how far the brow sits above the eye.
entries.frame_evidence: The vertical gap between the brow arch and the upper lid.
entries.detector_note: Mean of |y(105)-y(159)| and |y(334)-y(386)| from FaceMesh brow and lid landmarks, normalised by inter-ocular distance |p33-p263| so the value is scale invariant; per-character neutral is the shot median
entries.notes: Head pitch changes apparent brow height through foreshortening; regress out head_pitch_deg before differencing.

entries.label: Inner brow raise (sadness / plea)
entries.description: The inner ends of the brows lifting into an oblique shape, the reliable sadness and concern signal.
entries.frame_evidence: The brow inner ends higher than the outer ends, forming a shallow inverted V.
entries.detector_note: Signed brow slope from (y(107)-y(70)) and (y(336)-y(300)) normalised by inter-ocular distance |p33-p263| so the value is scale invariant; inner-raise when both slopes go oblique beyond the shot-median by 0.03 IOD
entries.notes: Small movement; needs face_area_fraction above 0.05. Anime draws this as a whole-brow redraw and the slope test does work there when a brow is present.

entries.label: Brow hidden by hair
entries.description: The brows are covered by a fringe, so all brow observables are unavailable.
entries.frame_evidence: Hair mass covering the forehead down to the eyes.
entries.detector_note: Crop the forehead band and ask qwen2.5vl; used as a gate that converts every brow entry to NOT DETECTABLE for that shot
entries.vlm_question: In this cropped image of a forehead, are the eyebrows covered by hair? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: This is a gating entry: without it, hidden brows silently report as neutral brows for a whole shot.

entries.label: Brow raise (both)
entries.description: Both brows lifting in surprise, question, greeting or emphasis.
entries.frame_evidence: Both brows moving up with the forehead skin compressing into horizontal creases.
entries.detector_note: brow_height_mean exceeding neutral by more than 0.06 IOD for 2 or more unique-cel samples, corroborated by forehead_wrinkle rising
entries.notes: In 2D the brow is often drawn above or through the hairline, or is absent entirely; where the brow is not drawn this must be logged NOT DETECTABLE.

entries.label: Catchlight removed (dead / possessed eyes)
entries.description: The deliberate removal of the eye highlight to signal death, despair, brainwashing or villainy.
entries.frame_evidence: Eyes rendered as flat discs with no white highlight where earlier shots of the same character had one.
entries.detector_note: Compare catchlight_count and catchlight_area_fraction against the same character baseline from other shots; flag a drop to zero sustained across the shot
entries.notes: Requires a per-character baseline across shots, so it needs the identity/character shard; without it a simple zero-count is indistinguishable from a dark or small eye. | TIER CORRECTED by completeness critic: deterministic, while its own positive counterpart face_head.catchlight_present and lighting.catchlight_eyes are both landmark. An absence detector cannot be cheaper than the presence detector it negates - a missing catch

entries.label: Catchlight / eye highlight present
entries.description: The specular highlight in the eye, the single detail that makes an eye read as alive.
entries.frame_evidence: One or more small very bright blobs inside the iris or pupil region.
entries.detector_note: Inside the eye ROI, threshold at the 99th percentile of the ROI L channel, cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats, keep blobs between 0.2 and 6 percent of the ROI area; emit count, area and centroid offset from the iris centre
entries.notes: Compression ringing and eyelash specular both create sub-threshold blobs; the area band is doing most of the work and should be tuned per production.

entries.label: Cheek puff
entries.description: Cheeks inflated with held air, for effort, sulking or comic annoyance.
entries.frame_evidence: The cheek silhouette bulging outward beyond the jaw line with the mouth sealed.
entries.detector_note: Outward displacement of face-oval landmarks at the cheeks (205/425 and the oval points 123/352) relative to the shot-neutral face oval, normalised by inter-ocular distance |p33-p263|, with the mouth closed
entries.notes: In 2D this is a redraw the mesh cannot follow; the vlm question in expression terms is the practical fallback there.

entries.label: Chewing
entries.description: Rhythmic jaw opening and closing while eating.
entries.frame_evidence: The jaw cycling open and shut at a steady low frequency with the lips usually staying together.
entries.detector_note: scipy.signal.find_peaks or welch on jaw_drop_normalised; chewing is 3 or more regular cycles at 1-3 Hz with mar_inner staying low (lips closed) and no viseme sequence
entries.notes: Speech also cycles the jaw; the separator is that chewing keeps the lips closed and has a far more regular period. Report the regularity metric so the caller can judge.

entries.label: Chin lift / chin tuck
entries.description: A held pitch-up (haughty, defiant, looking down the nose) or pitch-down-while-eyes-up (submissive, wary, brooding).
entries.frame_evidence: The nostrils becoming visible from below, or the brow line dropping over upward-looking eyes.
entries.detector_note: Held head_pitch_deg offset from the shot median above 8 deg (lift) or below -8 deg (tuck) for 5 or more samples, reported jointly with gaze_pitch_norm so the eyes-up-head-down combination is explicit
entries.notes: Camera height changes the apparent pitch; a low-angle shot makes everyone look chin-lifted.

entries.label: Crow's feet
entries.description: Radial creases at the outer eye corners, present in genuine smiles and in squinting.
entries.frame_evidence: Short fan-shaped lines spreading laterally from the outer corner of each eye.
entries.detector_note: Radial ridge energy in an ROI lateral to landmarks 33 and 263, measured as the oriented-gradient histogram concentration around the radial direction, against the shot baseline
entries.notes: Absent by design on young characters, most 3D characters and nearly all 2D; a NOT FOUND carries no information about the expression. | TIER CORRECTED by completeness critic: Marked deterministic, but every one of them needs an ALIGNED FACE REGION, and the face mesh in that same shard is landmark-tier (and face_head.facemesh_fit_failure exists precisely because it fails on stylised art). Pall

entries.label: Blue / grey discoloration
entries.description: The face turning blue, grey or green for suffocation, cold, poison, death or supernatural effect.
entries.frame_evidence: A cold hue shift across the whole face, often with the lips going darkest.
entries.detector_note: Mean LAB b dropping (toward blue) or the face hue rotating out of the normal skin-hue band, tracked against baseline, with the lip ROI showing a larger shift than the cheek ROI
entries.notes: Indistinguishable from cold-key or moonlight lighting on colour alone; the lip-leads-the-shift test is weak evidence at best. Prefer a vlm confirmation for any dramatic claim. | TIER CORRECTED by completeness critic: Marked deterministic, but every one of them needs an ALIGNED FACE REGION, and the face mesh in that same shard is landmark-tier (and face_head.facemesh_fit_failure exists precisely because it fails on stylised art). Pall

entries.label: Cheek raise (genuine-smile marker)
entries.description: The orbicularis oculi contraction that accompanies a felt smile, raising the cheeks and narrowing the eyes.
entries.frame_evidence: The lower lids pushed up and the cheek mass rising, with crow's feet appearing.
entries.detector_note: Co-occurrence of smile amplitude with lower_lid_raise above threshold and a reduction in ear_mean of 10-30 percent, plus crows_feet ridge energy rising
entries.notes: Claiming a smile is genuine from this is a psychological inference the analyzer should not make; report the geometric co-occurrence only.

entries.label: Eye aspect ratio (EAR) primitive
entries.description: The core numeric primitive for every lid observable: the ratio of eye height to eye width.
entries.frame_evidence: The vertical gap between upper and lower lid contours versus the corner-to-corner width.
entries.detector_note: EAR = (|p159-p145| + |p158-p153|) / (2*|p33-p133|) for the right eye and (|p386-p374| + |p385-p380|) / (2*|p362-p263|) for the left, from MediaPipe FaceMesh refine_landmarks=True (478 pts): right eye 33/133/159/145/158/153/160/144, left eye 362/263/386/374/385/380/387/373, right iris 468-472, left iris 473-477, brows 70/63/105/66/107 and 300/293/334/296/336, outer lips 61/291/0/17/37/267/84/314, inner lips 78/308/13/14/82/87/312/317, nose 1/168/2/48/278, chin 152, forehead 10, cheeks 205/425/50/280; emit both eyes plus their mean and difference every unique-cel index
entries.notes: EAR has no absolute meaning without a per-character null: build the open-eye baseline as the 80th percentile of ear_mean over the shot and express everything as a fraction of that, otherwise squint and a naturally narrow eye shape are the same number.

entries.label: Eye contact with camera
entries.description: The character looks directly down the lens, breaking the fourth wall or addressing the viewer.
entries.frame_evidence: Both irises centred in the eye openings with the head near frontal.
entries.detector_note: |gaze_yaw_norm| and |gaze_pitch_norm| both under 0.12 while |head_yaw_deg| under 12 and |head_pitch_deg| under 12, sustained for 3 or more unique-cel samples
entries.notes: A character looking at a lens-adjacent object is geometrically identical; and the whole test collapses if the shot is not shot-on-axis.

entries.label: Glistening / wet eyes
entries.description: Eyes made to look wet and reflective without an actual tear, the emotional-swell shorthand.
entries.frame_evidence: Enlarged, multiplied or softened catchlights filling more of the iris than in neighbouring shots.
entries.detector_note: catchlight_area_fraction and catchlight_count elevated above the same character baseline, plus a raised 95th-percentile L inside the eye ROI
entries.notes: Needs the cross-shot character baseline; within a single shot there is nothing to compare against.

entries.label: Eye roll
entries.description: The eyes sweeping upward and around in exasperation or contempt.
entries.frame_evidence: The iris travelling up under the upper lid until mostly hidden, then returning.
entries.detector_note: gaze_pitch_norm crossing above 0.4 with an accompanying transient drop in visible iris area (see iris_visible_area), then returning to baseline inside 8 samples
entries.notes: In 2D an eye roll is often drawn as the pupil simply vanishing upward for one or two cels, which the mesh cannot see; the vlm on a crop is the practical route there.

entries.label: Sparkle / star eyes
entries.description: The exaggerated multi-highlight or star-shaped shine drawn in the eyes for awe, adoration or excitement.
entries.frame_evidence: Multiple bright shapes, sometimes stars or radiating spokes, filling much of the iris.
entries.detector_note: Crop the eye pair and ask qwen2.5vl; corroborate with catchlight_count above 3 and catchlight_area_fraction above 0.15
entries.vlm_question: In this cropped image of eyes, are the eyes filled with many bright sparkles or star shapes? Answer yes or no.

entries.label: Eyes closed (sustained)
entries.description: Both eyes held shut across many frames, as in sleep, death, meditation, a held wince or a savoured moment.
entries.frame_evidence: EAR pinned near zero for a run of frames with no reopen.
entries.detector_note: Run-length encoding of ear_mean under 0.25*baseline lasting more than 8 unique-cel samples; on 2D also validated by the eye ROI collapsing to a single dark curve (Canny edge count in the eye ROI dropping to one connected contour)
entries.notes: FaceMesh often loses the fit entirely when the eyes are shut for a long time on stylised art, converting a closed-eye hold into a mesh gap.

entries.label: Eyes hidden by fringe or shadow
entries.description: The eyes are deliberately obscured by hair, a hat brim or a shadow band, a strong dramatic convention.
entries.frame_evidence: The eye region replaced by an opaque hair mass or a hard dark band with no visible iris or catchlight.
entries.detector_note: Crop the eye band (eye landmark ring bbox expanded 60 percent, or the upper third of the face bbox when no mesh) and ask qwen2.5vl; corroborate with catchlight_present returning zero and low edge density in the eye ROI
entries.vlm_question: In this cropped image of the upper part of a face, are the eyes covered by hair or hidden in shadow so that you cannot see the eyeballs? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Frequently coincident with facemesh_fit_failure, so the landmark corroboration will be missing exactly when this fires.

entries.label: Eyes wide / startle open
entries.description: Lids retracted well beyond neutral in shock, fear or alarm.
