entries.frame_evidence: EAR spikes above the resting baseline and the white of the eye above the iris becomes visible.
entries.detector_note: ear_mean exceeding 1.25*baseline for 2 or more unique-cel samples, corroborated by upper-sclera exposure (see upper_sclera_exposure) and brow raise
entries.notes: On 2D the widen is frequently drawn as a whole-new eye design rather than a lid change, so the mesh may not track it; pair with the vlm entry expression_fear on a crop.

entries.label: Back of head / face away
entries.description: The head is present but the face is turned entirely away from camera.
entries.frame_evidence: A head-shaped hair or scalp mass with no eyes, nose or mouth anywhere on it.
entries.detector_note: Run only when a person-scale head region exists from pose landmark 0 but FaceMesh returns no fit; crop the head box with 30 percent padding and ask qwen2.5vl
entries.vlm_question: In this cropped image, is the person facing away from the camera so that no eyes, nose or mouth are visible? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Requires the body/pose shard to supply a head box; without a person detection this is indistinguishable from no-face-in-frame.

entries.label: Number of faces
entries.description: How many distinct faces are simultaneously visible.
entries.frame_evidence: Multiple separated face bounding boxes in one frame.
entries.detector_note: Non-max-suppressed union of Haar and mediapipe FaceDetection boxes (IoU 0.4 merge); count is the surviving box count, smoothed over a 5-unique-cel median to kill single-frame flicker
entries.notes: Background crowd faces inflate the count; profile and back-of-head faces are missed entirely so the count is a lower bound.

entries.label: Face partially occluded
entries.description: Part of the face is hidden by a hand, object, hair, mask, smoke or another character.
entries.frame_evidence: A face region where a contiguous foreground element covers eyes, nose or mouth.
entries.detector_note: Count FaceMesh landmarks whose per-point visibility proxy fails: project the 468 points, sample a 5x5 patch at each, and flag points whose local gradient orientation histogram is inconsistent with the fitted mesh normal; occlusion score is the flagged fraction. Cross-check with hand landmarks from mediapipe Hands overlapping the face bbox
entries.notes: MediaPipe hallucinates plausible landmark positions straight through an occluder, so a confident mesh is NOT evidence the face is unoccluded; this entry has a high false-negative rate and needs a vlm confirmation pass on the crop.

entries.label: Frontal face
entries.description: The head is turned close to square-on to camera.
entries.frame_evidence: Both eyes, both nostrils and both mouth corners visible with near-symmetric spacing.
entries.detector_note: cv2.solvePnP of the canonical 6-point face model against landmarks 1/152/33/263/61/291, cv2.Rodrigues to Euler; frontal when |yaw| under 15 deg and |pitch| under 15 deg
entries.notes: solvePnP on a 2D drawing is fitting a 3D model to a face that was never 3D; anime yaw is systematically under-estimated because stylised faces keep both eyes visible far into profile.

entries.label: Profile face
entries.description: The head is turned far enough that one side of the face is self-occluded.
entries.frame_evidence: Only one eye and one mouth corner visible; the nose breaks the silhouette of the cheek.
entries.detector_note: same solvePnP chain; profile when |yaw| exceeds 55 deg, cross-checked by the visible-landmark asymmetry ratio |x(33)-x(1)| / |x(263)-x(1)| exceeding 3.0
entries.notes: FaceMesh commonly refuses to fit past about 70 deg yaw, so hard profile reads as a detection failure rather than a profile; log the failure separately.

entries.label: Face present in frame
entries.description: At least one human or humanoid face occupies part of the frame.
entries.frame_evidence: A face-shaped region with two eye regions and a mouth region visible anywhere in the frame.
entries.detector_note: cv2.CascadeClassifier(cv2.data.haarcascades + haarcascade_frontalface_default.xml).detectMultiScale(gray, 1.1, 5, minSize=(24,24)) OR-ed with mediapipe FaceDetection(model_selection=1, min_detection_confidence=0.4); a hit from either source sets the flag
entries.notes: Haar is frontal-only and fires on high-contrast non-faces; on stylised 2D art both detectors drop out below roughly 50 percent recall, so a NOT FOUND on anime must be logged as low-confidence, never as an absence claim.

entries.label: Face scale / shot tightness
entries.description: How much of the frame the largest face occupies, which separates extreme close-up from wide shot.
entries.frame_evidence: The face bounding box area relative to the frame area.
entries.detector_note: largest face bbox area divided by (frame_w*frame_h); bands: over 0.25 extreme close-up, 0.06-0.25 close-up, 0.01-0.06 medium, under 0.01 wide
entries.notes: THE CROP RULE depends on this: any vlm-tier facial entry must only be asked on a crop where face_bbox_h_fraction after upscaling exceeds roughly 0.4 of the crop.

entries.label: Vertical shadow over the face (anime despair)
entries.description: The hard vertical gradient dropped over the upper face to signal dread, despair or menace.
entries.frame_evidence: A flat dark band with a sharp horizontal or vertical edge laid across the face, often with the eye highlights removed.
entries.detector_note: Inside the face mask, detect a bimodal L histogram (scipy.signal.find_peaks on the histogram with two separated modes) whose spatial boundary is a near-straight line via cv2.HoughLines, with an abnormally low gradient magnitude within each mode (a flat fill, not a rendered shadow)
entries.notes: A genuine hard-edged practical shadow in live action produces the same statistics, which is why this entry is 2D-only; the flat-fill test is the discriminator. | TIER CORRECTED by completeness critic: Marked deterministic, but every one of them needs an ALIGNED FACE REGION, and the face mesh in that same shard is landmark-tier (and face_head.facemesh_fit_failure exists precisely because it fails on stylised art). Pall

entries.label: Face smear / distortion drawing
entries.description: The deliberately distorted or elongated drawing of a face during a fast move, an animation-craft observable.
entries.frame_evidence: The face stretched, doubled or blurred along the motion direction for one or two drawings, then snapping back.
entries.detector_note: Anisotropy of the local gradient structure tensor inside the head bbox (skimage.feature.structure_tensor plus eigenvalue ratio); a smear is a single-cel spike in anisotropy aligned with the head displacement direction, bracketed by low-anisotropy cels
entries.notes: This measures directional blur only; it cannot separate an authored smear drawing from camera motion blur or from a defocused frame. Report the measurement, not the interpretation.

entries.label: Facial squash and stretch
entries.description: The whole head deforming non-rigidly for impact, effort or comic exaggeration.
entries.frame_evidence: The head silhouette compressing along one axis and expanding along the perpendicular one, beyond what rotation explains.
entries.detector_note: Fit a similarity transform between the current face-oval landmark set and the shot-median set (cv2.estimateAffinePartial2D); squash-stretch is a large residual after the similarity fit, with the residual field aligned to a single axis
entries.notes: Requires a landmark fit that survives the deformation, which on an extreme 2D squash it will not; the extreme cases are exactly the undetectable ones.

entries.label: Face-mesh fit failure (2D stylisation)
entries.description: A meta-observable: a face is visibly present to a human but MediaPipe FaceMesh returns no fit, which is the normal case on stylised drawings.
entries.frame_evidence: A drawn face with simplified eyes and a line mouth for which the landmark overlay is absent.
entries.detector_note: Counter comparing frames where the vlm or a face-shaped colour-region heuristic says face-present against frames where FaceMesh returned a fit; emitted as a per-shot reliability score
entries.notes: This is the single most important honesty metric in this shard: every landmark-tier entry below must be reported as NOT DETECTABLE for any shot whose facemesh_fit_rate is under about 0.6, rather than reported as NOT FOUND.

entries.label: Fangs / canines emphasised
entries.description: Prominent pointed canines, a species, monster or feral-mood signal and a recurring anime shorthand.
entries.frame_evidence: One or two triangular tooth shapes projecting well below the upper tooth line.
entries.detector_note: Crop the mouth on frames where teeth_area_fraction is high and ask qwen2.5vl
entries.vlm_question: In this cropped image of a mouth, are there sharp pointed fangs longer than the other teeth? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: A single small anime fang at one mouth corner is often only a few pixels; enforce a minimum crop upscale or the vlm sees nothing.

entries.label: Fixation (gaze hold)
entries.description: The eyes holding steady on one point for a sustained period.
entries.frame_evidence: The iris position variance staying near zero across many frames.
entries.detector_note: Rolling standard deviation of iris centre over a 6-sample window staying under 0.015 IOD; runs longer than 8 samples are fixations
entries.notes: A held drawing in 2D produces a perfect fixation by construction; this is why the unique-cel collapse must happen first, and even then a limited-animation hold is not an acted fixation.

entries.label: Flush (whole-face reddening)
entries.description: The full face going red from rage, heat, exertion, fever, drink or intense embarrassment.
entries.frame_evidence: The entire face reddening, not just the cheeks, sometimes extending to the ears and neck.
entries.detector_note: Rise in mean LAB a over the whole face mask against the shot baseline with the cheek-versus-face differential staying flat, which is what separates a flush from a blush
entries.notes: Firelight, sunset, red practicals and a red grade all raise face a; check the frame-level colour statistics outside the face mask before attributing. | TIER CORRECTED by completeness critic: Marked deterministic, but every one of them needs an ALIGNED FACE REGION, and the face mesh in that same shard is landmark-tier (and face_head.facemesh_fit_failure exists precisely because it fails on stylised art). Pall

entries.label: Forehead creases
entries.description: Horizontal lines across the forehead that accompany a brow raise.
entries.frame_evidence: Two to five parallel horizontal dark lines above the brows.
entries.detector_note: Horizontal-ridge energy (Sobel-x suppressed, Sobel-y response) summed inside the forehead ROI between the brow landmarks and landmark 10, plus a count of parallel line responses via cv2.HoughLinesP
entries.notes: Hair, fringe shadow, headwear and sharpening artefacts all add horizontal energy; only the within-shot delta correlated with brow_raise is meaningful. | TIER CORRECTED by completeness critic: Marked deterministic, but every one of them needs an ALIGNED FACE REGION, and the face mesh in that same shard is landmark-tier (and face_head.facemesh_fit_failure exists precisely because it fails on stylised art). Pall

entries.label: Frown (corners down)
entries.description: Both mouth corners pulled down.
entries.frame_evidence: The mouth line curving downward at both ends.
entries.detector_note: corner_elevation_mean below -0.02 IOD relative to the shot neutral, held 3 or more samples
entries.notes: In common usage frown also means brow-furrow; this entry is strictly the mouth. The brow sense is brow_furrow.

entries.label: Gaze aversion / look away
entries.description: The eyes break from a held target and move away, the shame, evasion or thinking beat.
entries.frame_evidence: A gaze that was centred moves off-centre and stays there while the head barely moves.
entries.detector_note: A step change in gaze_yaw_norm exceeding 0.25 that persists over 4 or more unique-cel samples with |delta head_yaw_deg| under 8 in the same window

entries.label: Gaze direction (stylised faces)
entries.description: Gaze direction read from a drawn eye where no iris landmark exists.
entries.frame_evidence: The drawn pupil or iris disc placed off-centre inside the painted eye white.
entries.detector_note: Crop the eye pair region (upper 45 percent of the face bbox, expanded 20 percent, upscaled to at least 384 px wide per THE CROP RULE) and ask qwen2.5vl
entries.vlm_question: In this cropped image of a face, which way is the character looking: at the camera, to their left, to their right, up, or down? Answer with one of those five options.
entries.notes: Small VLMs confuse the character left/right with image left/right; fix the convention in the question and re-map, and expect roughly 20 percent side errors.

entries.label: Gaze direction class
entries.description: A coarse discrete label of where a character is looking: camera, left, right, up, down, or at another character.
entries.frame_evidence: Iris placement plus head orientation resolving to one of nine cells.
entries.detector_note: Combine gaze_yaw_norm and gaze_pitch_norm with head_yaw_deg and head_pitch_deg into a 3x3 grid with dead-zone thresholds at 0.15 normalised units; falls back to a vlm crop question when iris landmarks are absent
entries.notes: For 2D this must be delegated to the vlm entry gaze_direction_2d; iris landmarks do not fit stylised eyes.

entries.label: Gaze pitch (vertical eye direction)
entries.description: Where the eyes are pointed up or down within their sockets.
entries.frame_evidence: The iris riding high under the upper lid or dropped toward the lower lid.
entries.detector_note: v = (y_iris - y_upper_lid) / (y_lower_lid - y_upper_lid) using landmarks 159/145 and 386/374; shot-median subtracted
entries.notes: Strongly coupled to lid position: a squint moves the lid landmarks and shifts v without the eye moving at all. Report jointly with EAR or it lies.

entries.label: Gaze yaw (horizontal eye direction)
entries.description: Where the eyes are pointed left or right within their sockets, independent of head direction.
entries.frame_evidence: The iris sitting off-centre toward one eye corner with more sclera exposed on the opposite side.
entries.detector_note: Iris centre landmark 468 (right) / 473 (left) expressed as a normalised offset inside the eye-corner span: u = (x_iris - x_inner) / (x_outer - x_inner); average both eyes, then subtract the shot-median to remove per-character eye-shape bias
entries.notes: Requires refine_landmarks iris points, which need a reasonably photographic eye; the mapping from u to degrees is uncalibrated so only relative direction is honest.

entries.label: Grimace
entries.description: A strained horizontal stretch of the mouth in pain, disgust or forced effort, often with teeth bared.
entries.frame_evidence: The mouth pulled wide and flat with tension lines, corners neither clearly up nor down.
entries.detector_note: mouth_width_ratio above 1.15 with |corner_elevation_mean| under 0.015 and mar_inner above 0.08, co-occurring with brow_furrow or squint in the same window
entries.notes: Without the brow or eye co-occurrence this is indistinguishable from a wide smile.

entries.label: Half-lidded eyes
entries.description: Lids resting at roughly half closure, the bedroom-eyes / bored / sultry / smug register.
entries.frame_evidence: The upper lid crosses the pupil while the lower lid is neutral, held steady.
entries.detector_note: ear_mean in the 0.4-0.65 baseline band with the upper lid landmark 159 sitting below the iris centre 468 in image y, held over 5 or more unique-cel samples and with the lower lid NOT raised
entries.notes: Distinguished from squint only by which lid moves; the iris-crossing test is what separates them and it needs refine_landmarks iris points, which are unavailable on 2D art.

entries.label: Head cock (quick tilt with a turn)
entries.description: The short combined roll-plus-yaw movement of curiosity or challenge, distinct from a sustained tilt.
entries.frame_evidence: The head tipping and turning slightly in one quick motion, then holding briefly.
entries.detector_note: Simultaneous roll and yaw step above 6 deg each occurring inside 3 samples, followed by a hold of 3 or more samples

entries.label: Head droop / hang
entries.description: A slow sustained pitch-down of the head in defeat, exhaustion, grief, sleep or death.
entries.frame_evidence: The chin sinking toward the chest and staying there without a return.
entries.detector_note: scipy.stats.linregress of head_pitch_deg over the shot with a significant downward slope and no recovery, terminal pitch more than 12 deg below the shot start
entries.notes: Distinguished from a nod purely by the absence of a return; a shot that cuts mid-nod is indistinguishable from a droop.

entries.label: Nod (yes)
entries.description: The head pitching down and up, one or more times, as affirmation or acknowledgement.
entries.frame_evidence: The chin dropping toward the chest and returning while yaw and roll stay put.
entries.detector_note: scipy.signal.find_peaks on head_pitch_deg with prominence above 4 deg and width 2-10 unique-cel samples, requiring |delta head_yaw_deg| under 6 across the same window; series sampled on UNIQUE-CEL indices, never raw container frames
entries.notes: A single slow nod and a head droop have the same downward stroke; the return-to-baseline is what makes it a nod. Camera tilt during the shot injects a false pitch signal.

entries.label: Head pose (yaw / pitch / roll) primitive
entries.description: The three-angle numeric primitive underlying every head-motion observable.
entries.frame_evidence: The apparent rotation of the face relative to camera, read from the relative placement of nose, chin, eye corners and mouth corners.
entries.detector_note: cv2.solvePnP (SOLVEPNP_ITERATIVE) fitting the canonical 6-point face model to FaceMesh landmarks 1/152/33/263/61/291 with an assumed pinhole intrinsic (f = frame_width), then cv2.Rodrigues and a ZYX Euler decomposition; emit all three angles per unique cel plus the reprojection residual as a trust metric
entries.notes: The canonical model is an averaged adult human head; a stylised or non-human skull gives a systematically biased fit. Use pnp_reprojection_error as the gate and mark high-residual shots NOT DETECTABLE.

entries.label: Head recoil / snap back from impact
entries.description: The head thrown backward or sideways by an impact, a slap or a shock.
entries.frame_evidence: The head accelerating away from a contact point with the neck extending, then returning.
entries.detector_note: A pitch or yaw impulse whose onset acceleration (second difference of the angle series) exceeds the 98th percentile of the shot, with the head translating as well as rotating (head bbox centroid displacement in the same direction)
entries.notes: Needs the impact shard to supply the contact event to distinguish recoil from a fast voluntary turn; alone it is only a fast-move detector.

entries.label: Shake (no)
entries.description: The head rotating side to side in negation, disbelief or refusal.
entries.frame_evidence: The face turning left and right about the vertical axis, repeatedly, with the chin level.
entries.detector_note: Two or more sign alternations of head_yaw_deg with amplitude above 5 deg inside 1.2 s of screen time and |delta head_pitch_deg| under 6
entries.notes: On 2D, a shake is often a smear or a 2-drawing cycle whose yaw the mesh cannot resolve; fall back to horizontal optical-flow oscillation inside the head bbox.

entries.label: Rapid head vibration (2D emphasis)
entries.description: The very fast small-amplitude head shake used in anime for panic, denial, shivering or comic fluster.
entries.frame_evidence: The head alternating between two or three drawings a few pixels apart, often with speed lines.
entries.detector_note: Within the head bbox, alternate-frame normalised cross-correlation showing an A-B-A-B pattern with a sub-head-width offset over 4 or more unique cels; measure the offset amplitude and the alternation period
entries.notes: This is one of the few places where the raw container frames matter: the effect is authored at the cel level, so run the alternation test on unique cels and report the cel period, not a Hz value.

entries.label: Head snap / sharp look
entries.description: A very fast head rotation to a new target, the alarm or attention beat.
entries.frame_evidence: The head crossing a large angle in one or two drawings, usually with motion blur or a smear.
entries.detector_note: Single-sample |delta head_yaw_deg| or |delta head_pitch_deg| above 20 deg between adjacent unique cels, with the pose stable before and after
entries.notes: At 8-12 unique drawings per second a snap can occupy a single sample, so the angular velocity is only bounded, not measured. Report the bound, not a velocity.

entries.label: Head tilt (roll hold)
entries.description: The head held canted to one side: curiosity, sympathy, coquetry or menace depending on context.
entries.frame_evidence: The eye line tipped away from horizontal while the face stays otherwise frontal.
entries.detector_note: |head_roll_deg| above 8 held for more than 5 unique-cel samples; corroborate with the angle of the line through eye corners 33 and 263 against the horizontal, which needs no PnP
entries.notes: The eye-line angle is the more robust of the two measurements and works even when PnP fails, so prefer it and report PnP roll only as a cross-check. Dutch-angle camera work produces the identical signal.

entries.label: Head turn to a new facing
entries.description: A sustained rotation of the head to a new direction that is then held, as opposed to an oscillation.
entries.frame_evidence: The face rotating through three-quarter toward profile and remaining there.
entries.detector_note: A monotonic head_yaw_deg change above 15 deg over 3-15 samples with a stable plateau afterward (rolling std under 3 deg for 4 samples)

entries.label: Visible iris area
entries.description: How much of the iris disc the lids leave uncovered, the substrate for wide-eye and half-lid reads.
entries.frame_evidence: The coloured disc of the eye partly cut by the upper or lower lid contour.
entries.detector_note: Polygon intersection (shapely-free, via cv2.fillPoly masks and numpy AND) of the iris ring polygon with the eyelid contour polygon; area ratio against the full iris ellipse
entries.notes: Iris landmarks only; 2D falls back to a colour-region area which conflates iris with painted eye white.

entries.label: Jaw opening
entries.description: How far the jaw is dropped, which is distinct from how far the lips are parted.
entries.frame_evidence: The chin dropping away from the nose while the face height grows.
entries.detector_note: |y(152) - y(1)| (chin to nose tip) normalised by inter-ocular distance |p33-p263|, minus the shot-median closed-jaw value; jaw opening and lip parting are reported separately because a mouth can be open with a closed jaw and vice versa
entries.notes: Head pitch changes chin-to-nose distance in projection; regress out head_pitch_deg first.

entries.label: Laughing
entries.description: Open-mouthed rhythmic laughter.
entries.frame_evidence: A wide open grin with the head often thrown back and the mouth pulsing at a few hertz.
entries.detector_note: Sustained grin (corner elevation plus open aperture) with a 3-6 Hz amplitude modulation on aperture_area and correlated head_pitch oscillation
entries.notes: On 2D limited animation, laughter is often a held drawing with the body shaking; the mouth modulation will be absent and the detector will miss it entirely.

entries.label: Lid droop / drifting closed
entries.description: A slow monotonic loss of lid opening as a character tires, faints or dies.
entries.frame_evidence: EAR trending downward across a shot rather than oscillating around a baseline.
entries.detector_note: scipy.stats.linregress slope of ear_mean against unique-cel index over the shot, significant negative slope with the residual RMS small relative to the drop; null model is the same regression on a circularly shifted series
entries.notes: Requires a stable shot with continuous mesh coverage; a cut mid-shot or a mesh dropout produces a spurious slope.

entries.label: Lip bite
entries.description: The lower or upper lip drawn in under the teeth.
entries.frame_evidence: Part of the lip disappearing behind a row of teeth with the visible lip area shrinking asymmetrically.
entries.detector_note: Crop the mouth and ask qwen2.5vl on candidate frames where the lower-lip visible area drops sharply while the mouth stays roughly closed
entries.vlm_question: In this cropped image of a mouth, is the person biting their lip with their teeth? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Reliably drawn in anime as a specific mouth shape but rarely with visible teeth, so the vlm will miss the 2D version; consider a 2D-specific shape-match instead.

entries.label: Inner lip aperture area
entries.description: The actual open area of the mouth aperture, the substrate for shouting, singing and yawning.
entries.frame_evidence: The area of the dark or tooth-filled region enclosed by the inner lip contour.
entries.detector_note: cv2.fillPoly the inner-lip landmark polygon into a mask, count pixels, divide by the squared inter-ocular distance to normalise

entries.label: Lip lick
entries.description: The tongue sweeping across the lips.
entries.frame_evidence: A pink tongue tip travelling horizontally along the lip line across a few frames.
entries.detector_note: Pre-select frames where a pink (high LAB a, moderate L) blob appears on or just outside the lip mask, then crop and ask qwen2.5vl
entries.vlm_question: In this cropped image of a mouth, is the tongue sticking out and touching the lips? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: The pink pre-filter also fires on the inner mouth and on lipstick; it only reduces the vlm call count, it does not decide.

entries.label: Lip press / compressed lips
entries.description: The lips pressed together and thinned, signalling suppression, resolve or withheld anger.
entries.frame_evidence: The visible red of the lips narrowing and paling while the mouth stays closed.
entries.detector_note: Vertical thickness of the outer lip band |y(0)-y(17)| normalised by inter-ocular distance |p33-p263| dropping below 0.85 of the shot neutral while mar_inner is near zero; corroborated by a drop in mean LAB a inside the lip mask
entries.notes: Lip colour drop is confounded by lighting and by lipstick; the thickness term carries the signal.

entries.label: Lip protrusion / pucker depth
entries.description: How far the lips push forward, the depth axis that separates OU from a merely narrow mouth.
entries.frame_evidence: In profile, the lips extending past the plane of the chin and nose; frontally, a shortened lip with a visible shadow ring.
entries.detector_note: FaceMesh z coordinates of p0/p13/p14/p17 relative to the mean z of the face oval; alternatively in near-profile use the horizontal distance from the lip apex to the line joining nose tip 1 and chin 152
entries.notes: MediaPipe z is a weak relative depth from a single view and is close to unusable frontally; the profile geometry route is far more trustworthy. Mark NOT DETECTABLE when |head_yaw_deg| is under 25.

entries.label: Lip purse
entries.description: The lips gathered inward and forward without protruding into a full pucker, the disapproval or consideration beat.
entries.frame_evidence: A narrowed mouth with the lips bunched and radial wrinkles at the corners.
entries.detector_note: mouth_width_ratio below 0.85 with mar_inner under 0.08 and the outer-lip perimeter shortening relative to the neutral (contour length from the outer-lip landmark polygon)
entries.notes: Shares its whole geometry with the OU viseme; only the absence of a viseme cycle and the hold duration separate a purse from speech.

entries.label: Lip-sync offset against the audio
entries.description: Whether the mouth movement leads or lags the dialogue on the soundtrack.
entries.frame_evidence: Mouth-opening peaks arriving systematically earlier or later than the loud syllables.
entries.detector_note: Extract the audio envelope with ffmpeg (astats or a decoded PCM RMS at the unique-cel rate), then cross-correlate it against the aperture_area_iod2 series with numpy.correlate; the lag at the correlation peak is the offset in milliseconds
entries.notes: Only meaningful for a shot with a single on-screen speaker and continuous dialogue. The null model is the same cross-correlation against a time-reversed envelope: if the true peak is not clearly above that, report NOT DETECTABLE rather than a number.

entries.label: Lip tremble
entries.description: A small fast oscillation of the lower lip, the pre-crying or terror signal.
entries.frame_evidence: The lower lip contour wobbling at high frequency with small amplitude.
entries.detector_note: scipy.signal.welch on the lower-lip landmark 17 vertical position; tremble when band power above 4 Hz in unique-cel time exceeds 3x the shot median with amplitude under 0.02 IOD
entries.notes: Landmark jitter occupies the same band; needs a static-face null segment from the same shot. On 2D this is drawn as a boil or a shape cycle and the frequency will be quantised to the cel rate.

entries.label: Lower lid raise
entries.description: The lower lid pushing up, present in genuine smiles, suspicion and disgust.
entries.frame_evidence: The lower lid contour rising toward the iris while the upper lid stays put.
entries.detector_note: Vertical displacement of lower-lid landmarks 145/153/144 (and 374/380/373) toward the iris centre, normalised by inter-ocular distance |p33-p263| so the value is scale invariant, measured as a delta against the shot-median neutral
entries.notes: Sub-pixel on anything but a close-up; suppress when face_area_fraction is under 0.05.

entries.label: Mouth aspect ratio (MAR) primitive
entries.description: The core numeric primitive for the mouth: openness height over width.
entries.frame_evidence: The vertical gap between the lips versus the corner-to-corner mouth width.
entries.detector_note: MAR = (|p13-p14| + |p82-p87| + |p312-p317|) / (3*|p61-p291|) from the FaceMesh inner-lip and corner landmarks; also emit the outer-lip variant using p0/p17 for cases where the inner lip is not resolved
entries.notes: MAR is scale-free but not pose-free: head pitch foreshortens the vertical term and head yaw foreshortens the horizontal one. Correct with the solvePnP Euler angles before thresholding, or a nodding head reads as chewing.

entries.label: Mouth asymmetry
entries.description: Left-right difference in the mouth shape, the substrate for smirk, sneer and one-sided speech.
entries.frame_evidence: One corner higher, wider or more retracted than the other.
entries.detector_note: |corner_elevation_left - corner_elevation_right| plus the horizontal asymmetry of the corners about the face midline defined by landmarks 1, 168 and 152
entries.notes: Yaw makes the far corner foreshorten; gate on |head_yaw_deg| under 20.

entries.label: Mouth corner elevation
entries.description: Whether the corners of the mouth sit above or below the mouth centreline, the smile-frown axis.
entries.frame_evidence: The corners of the lips curving up toward the cheeks or down toward the jaw.
entries.detector_note: Signed mean of (y_centre_of_lips - y(61)) and (y_centre_of_lips - y(291)) normalised by inter-ocular distance |p33-p263|, where y_centre is the midpoint of p0 and p17; positive is raised
entries.notes: Head roll rotates the whole mouth; de-rotate by head_roll_deg first.

entries.label: Mouth flap cycle (limited animation)
entries.description: The 2-3 shape mouth cycle used for dialogue in limited animation, which is not lip-sync at all.
entries.frame_evidence: The same two or three mouth drawings alternating regularly through a dialogue line, unrelated to the phonemes.
entries.detector_note: mouth_shape_cluster_count of 2 or 3 across the dialogue run, combined with a near-periodic alternation (high autocorrelation of the cluster-label sequence at lag 2 or 3) and a low sync_correlation_peak against the audio
entries.notes: When this fires, every viseme-tier entry for the shot must be downgraded to shape-class only: the drawings do not encode phonemes and reporting visemes from them is fabrication.

entries.label: Mouth open / closed
entries.description: The simplest mouth state: are the lips parted at all.
entries.frame_evidence: A visible dark gap, teeth or tongue between the lips.
entries.detector_note: mar_inner above 0.06 OR the inner-lip polygon (78,82,13,312,308,317,14,87) enclosing a region whose mean L is more than 20 units below the surrounding lip L; the pixel test catches 2D line-mouths where the landmark gap is degenerate
entries.notes: A 2D mouth drawn as a single stroke has zero landmark height while being narratively open; the darkness test is the one that works there.

entries.label: Drawn mouth blob geometry
entries.description: For stylised faces with no fitted mesh, the mouth as a thresholded shape whose area, aspect and orientation can still be tracked.
entries.frame_evidence: A dark or red drawn shape in the lower third of the face whose outline changes cel to cel.
entries.detector_note: Within the lower-third of the face bbox, threshold on redness (LAB a channel) or darkness, take the largest cv2.findContours component, and emit cv2.fitEllipse axes, angle and cv2.contourArea, plus Hu moments for shape matching
entries.notes: Needs a face bbox from a working 2D face detector, which is NOT INSTALLED; today the bbox must come from a vlm localisation pass, making this practically vlm-gated.

entries.label: Mouth chart size (unique mouth drawings)
entries.description: The animation-craft observable of how many distinct mouth drawings a production uses, from a 3-shape TV mouth chart to a full 10-shape feature chart.
entries.frame_evidence: The same small set of mouth drawings recurring throughout a dialogue shot.
entries.detector_note: Cluster the tracked mouth crops across the shot by normalised cross-correlation (cv2.matchTemplate TM_CCOEFF_NORMED) with single-link at 0.90; the cluster count is the chart size
entries.notes: The threshold sets the answer; report the cluster count as a function of threshold rather than a single number, or this is a hyperparameter dressed as a measurement.

entries.label: Mouth width (spread versus pucker)
entries.description: How wide the mouth is stretched horizontally, the axis that separates E from OU.
entries.frame_evidence: The mouth corners moving outward toward the cheeks or inward toward the centre.
entries.detector_note: |p61-p291| normalised by inter-ocular distance |p33-p263|, expressed as a ratio to the shot-median neutral width

entries.label: Nasolabial fold deepening
entries.description: The line from the nose wing to the mouth corner deepening in a smile, a sneer or effort.
entries.frame_evidence: A curved shadow line running from beside the nostril down past the mouth corner, darker than neutral.
entries.detector_note: Mean L along a curved sample path from landmark 48 to landmark 61 (and 278 to 291) minus the mean L of the adjacent cheek, tracked against the shot neutral
entries.notes: Directional lighting creates the same shadow without any muscle action; only change relative to the shot neutral is usable. | TIER CORRECTED by completeness critic: Marked deterministic, but every one of them needs an ALIGNED FACE REGION, and the face mesh in that same shard is landmark-tier (and face_head.facemesh_fit_failure exists precisely because it fails on stylised art). Pall

entries.label: Nose wrinkle (disgust)
entries.description: The bridge of the nose bunching upward, the core disgust action.
entries.frame_evidence: Horizontal creases across the nose bridge with the upper lip rising and the eyes narrowing.
entries.detector_note: Ridge energy (Sobel response along the horizontal) in the nose-bridge ROI between landmarks 6 and 197 rising above the shot baseline, co-occurring with upper_lip_raise and a reduced brow-to-eye distance
entries.notes: Depends entirely on whether the production renders or draws wrinkles; many 3D characters have no wrinkle map, making this a genuine absence.

entries.label: Nosebleed
entries.description: Blood from the nose, either an injury signal in drama or the comic arousal gag in anime.
entries.frame_evidence: A red trail descending from one or both nostrils over the lip and chin.
entries.detector_note: High-a (red) connected component originating within the nostril ROI (landmarks 48/278 and 2) and extending downward past the upper lip, with saturation well above the skin distribution
entries.notes: Lipstick, red facial hair and red lighting are the false-positive sources; the requirement to originate at a nostril is what makes it specific. | TIER CORRECTED by completeness critic: Marked deterministic, but every one of them needs an ALIGNED FACE REGION, and the face mesh in that same shard is landmark-tier (and face_head.facemesh_fit_failure exists precisely because it fails on stylised art). Pall

entries.label: Nostril flare
entries.description: The nostrils widening with hard breathing, anger or exertion.
entries.frame_evidence: The alae of the nose spreading outward and the nostril openings enlarging.
entries.detector_note: Alar width |x(48)-x(278)| normalised by inter-ocular distance, minus the shot-median neutral; flare when the ratio exceeds neutral by 4 percent for 2 or more unique-cel samples
entries.notes: A 3-5 percent change on a face that is a few dozen pixels wide is sub-pixel; suppress unless face_area_fraction exceeds 0.08. Yaw compresses alar width in projection and must be regressed out.

entries.label: Off-model face
entries.description: A drawing where the character's facial proportions depart from their established model sheet, a production-quality observable.
entries.frame_evidence: The same character with visibly different eye spacing, head shape or feature proportions than in surrounding shots.
entries.detector_note: Needs a per-character proportion model learned from reference frames, and a stable 2D face landmark fit to measure against; neither exists today (no anime face detector, no sklearn)
entries.notes: NOT INSTALLED. Logged as a known blind spot; a vlm comparison against a reference crop is possible in principle but small VLMs cannot reliably judge proportion drift.

entries.label: Pallor / draining of colour
entries.description: The face losing colour in shock, fear, illness or death.
entries.frame_evidence: The whole face desaturating toward grey or white relative to earlier frames of the same character.
entries.detector_note: Mean LAB a and b inside the face mask tracked across the shot, and against the character baseline; pallor is a drop in a (redness) with L stable or rising, distinguishing it from the face merely going into shadow
entries.notes: Requiring L to hold while a falls is the whole trick; without it every shadow and every grade change reads as pallor. A colour-graded cut invalidates the comparison entirely. | TIER CORRECTED by completeness critic: Marked deterministic, but every one of them needs an ALIGNED FACE REGION, and the face mesh in that same shard is landmark-tier (and face_head.facemesh_fit_failure exists precisely because it fails on stylised art). Pall

entries.label: Pinprick pupils (shock)
entries.description: The anime convention where pupils shrink to tiny dots to signal terror, rage or dissociation.
entries.frame_evidence: The iris disc replaced by a very small dark dot inside a large expanse of white or flat iris colour.
entries.detector_note: Crop each eye (eye ROI expanded 50 percent, upscaled) and ask qwen2.5vl; corroborate deterministically with the dark-region area fraction inside the eye ROI dropping below 8 percent while the eye stays open
entries.vlm_question: In this cropped image of an eye, is the pupil shrunk to a very small dot surrounded by a large amount of white? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: The deterministic corroboration is the more trustworthy half; the vlm alone confuses a small pupil with a highlight.

entries.label: Pupil diameter
entries.description: The size of the dark pupil disc inside the iris.
entries.frame_evidence: A dark circular region at the iris centre whose radius changes with light and arousal.
entries.detector_note: Inside the iris ring (468-472 / 473-477) take the LAB L channel, Otsu-threshold with cv2.threshold THRESH_OTSU, take the largest connected component with cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats, and report its equivalent radius divided by the iris radius
entries.notes: Only works on close-ups of light-coloured irises; on dark brown eyes the pupil and iris are the same luminance and the Otsu split is arbitrary. Report NOT DETECTABLE when the intra-iris L contrast is under about 12 units.

entries.label: Pupil dilation
entries.description: The pupil enlarging, read as attraction, fear, drug effect or a darkness cut.
entries.frame_evidence: The dark centre of the eye growing relative to the iris across a few frames.
entries.detector_note: Positive step in pupil_iris_ratio exceeding 0.15 sustained 3 samples, with the frame mean luminance held roughly constant so it is not a light response
entries.notes: Without the scene-luminance control this detects lighting changes, not emotion. In 2D it is usually a discrete redraw, not a continuous change.

entries.label: Saccade (fast gaze jump)
entries.description: A ballistic jump of the eyes from one fixation point to another.
entries.frame_evidence: The iris translating several of its own diameters between adjacent unique cels.
entries.detector_note: First difference of the iris-centre position normalised by inter-ocular distance |p33-p263| so the value is scale invariant; a saccade is a single-sample displacement above 0.06 IOD followed by a return to near-zero velocity, computed on UNIQUE-CEL indices only, since optical flow and any velocity between two duplicate drawings is exactly zero and that zero is an artefact
entries.notes: At 8-12 unique drawings per second an anime saccade is at or below the Nyquist limit of the sampling, so amplitude is measurable but velocity is not; report velocity as NOT DETECTABLE for 2D.

entries.label: Scream / shout mouth
entries.description: The maximally open mouth of a scream or shout, usually squared off with the tongue visible.
entries.frame_evidence: A very large aperture with visible teeth and tongue held over many frames, often with squeezed-shut eyes.
entries.detector_note: mar_inner above 0.5 and aperture_area_iod2 in the top percentile of the shot, sustained more than 4 unique-cel samples, with an absence of viseme cycling and with squint or eyes_closed co-occurring
entries.notes: Separated from yawn by the eye state and the onset speed: a scream snaps open, a yawn ramps.

entries.label: Facial skin specular character
entries.description: How the skin responds to light: matte, oily, waxy or plasticky, which is a render-quality and a story observable at once.
entries.frame_evidence: The size, softness and count of highlights on the forehead, nose and cheekbones.
entries.detector_note: Histogram of L inside the face mask: the size of the upper tail, the sharpness of the specular rolloff (gradient magnitude at the highlight boundary), and the highlight area fraction
entries.notes: Directly reusable as the waxy-skin QC metric from the existing character pipeline; a hard rolloff with a large area fraction is the waxy signature.

entries.label: Closed-mouth smile
entries.description: Corners raised with the lips still together.
entries.frame_evidence: The mouth line curving upward at both ends with no aperture and the cheeks slightly raised.
entries.detector_note: corner_elevation_mean above 0.02 IOD relative to the shot neutral with mar_inner under 0.05, held 3 or more unique-cel samples
entries.notes: A character whose neutral mouth is drawn with upturned corners smiles permanently; the neutral must be the per-character shot median, and even then a design-level smile is unfixable.

entries.label: Open smile / grin
entries.description: Corners raised with the mouth open and teeth usually showing.
entries.frame_evidence: A wide aperture with raised corners and a visible band of teeth.
entries.detector_note: corner_elevation_mean above 0.02 IOD with mar_inner above 0.10 and mouth_width_ratio above 1.05, corroborated by teeth_visible
entries.notes: Overlaps with the E viseme and with a scream; duration and the absence of a viseme cycle are the separators.

entries.label: Smirk (one-sided smile)
entries.description: A single mouth corner raised, the smug, sardonic or flirtatious register.
entries.frame_evidence: One corner of the mouth pulled up and back while the other stays level.
entries.detector_note: corner_elevation_asymmetry above 0.025 IOD with the raised corner above neutral and the other within 0.01 of neutral, gated on |head_roll_deg| under 12 and |head_yaw_deg| under 20
entries.notes: The pose gates are mandatory: a three-quarter head produces an apparent one-sided mouth in projection.

entries.label: Sneer (upper lip raise)
entries.description: One or both sides of the upper lip curled up in contempt or disgust.
entries.frame_evidence: The upper lip lifted on one side exposing the canine, with the nasolabial fold deepening.
entries.detector_note: Upper-lip landmarks 37/267 rising relative to the nose base 2 normalised by inter-ocular distance |p33-p263|, asymmetrically, together with nasolabial_deepening on the same side
entries.notes: A small motion; needs face_area_fraction above 0.06. Often stylised out entirely in 2D.

entries.label: Which visible face is speaking
entries.description: In a multi-face frame, which character the current dialogue belongs to.
entries.frame_evidence: One face's mouth articulating while the others are still.
entries.detector_note: Compare speaking_activity across all detected faces in the shot; attribute to the face with the highest shape_changes_per_sec when its margin over the runner-up exceeds 2x
entries.notes: Off-screen dialogue, a speaking character facing away, and reaction shots all break this. It must never be reported as identifying the speaker on the audio track, only as identifying the moving mouth.

entries.label: Speaking (mouth articulating)
entries.description: Whether the character is talking, judged from mouth motion alone.
entries.frame_evidence: The mouth shape changing repeatedly at speech rate over a run of frames.
entries.detector_note: shape_changes_per_sec above a threshold calibrated per production, sustained over 6 or more unique-cel samples, with the changes not fitting a chew period; on 2D, the same test on mouth-blob Hu moments
entries.notes: This is a mouth-is-moving detector, not a speech detector: chewing, blowing and a shivering mouth all trigger it. It says nothing about who is speaking on the soundtrack.

entries.label: Squint / narrowed eyes
entries.description: Both lids partly closed in suspicion, glare, scrutiny or pain, without a blink transient.
entries.frame_evidence: EAR sits at a reduced plateau rather than dipping and recovering, often with the lower lid raised.
entries.detector_note: ear_mean in the 0.35-0.7 band of baseline held for more than 6 unique-cel samples with low first-derivative energy (numpy.gradient RMS under the blink threshold), plus lower-lid raise from |y(145)-y(33)| shortening
entries.notes: A character drawn with narrow eyes as a design trait squints permanently under this rule; the per-character baseline must come from the same character, ideally the same shot.

entries.label: Swallow
entries.description: The throat bobbing as a character swallows, the nerves or tension beat.
entries.frame_evidence: The larynx rising and falling on the front of the neck across a few frames.
entries.detector_note: Track the throat ROI below chin landmark 152 down to the neck using pose landmarks 11/12 for scale; measure vertical optical flow (cv2.calcOpticalFlowFarneback) inside that ROI for a single up-then-down excursion
entries.notes: Requires an unoccluded neck, a close shot and a visible larynx; on most characters, most costumes and nearly all 2D animation this is NOT DETECTABLE and should be logged as such.

entries.label: Sweat bead / drip
entries.description: Discrete droplets forming on and running down the face.
entries.frame_evidence: Small round bright blobs on the forehead or temple, some elongating into downward trails.
entries.detector_note: Small high-L high-local-contrast blobs inside the face mask (cv2.SimpleBlobDetector or connectedComponents on a top-hat filtered L channel), tracked for downward displacement
entries.notes: Freckles, skin specularity, film grain and compression blocks all produce small bright blobs; the downward-track requirement is what promotes a blob to a drip. | TIER CORRECTED by completeness critic: Marked deterministic, but every one of them needs an ALIGNED FACE REGION, and the face mesh in that same shard is landmark-tier (and face_head.facemesh_fit_failure exists precisely because it fails on stylised art). Pall

entries.label: Sweat-drop symbol (anime)
entries.description: The single large stylised drop drawn at the temple or floating beside the head to signal awkwardness, exasperation or panic.
entries.frame_evidence: One oversized teardrop shape, often outlined and semi-transparent, attached to or beside the head.
entries.detector_note: Crop the head with 40 percent padding and ask qwen2.5vl; deterministic corroboration is a single large outlined ellipse via cv2.findContours with high circularity in the temple region
entries.vlm_question: In this cropped image of a cartoon character, is there a single large exaggerated sweat drop drawn on or next to the head? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: A pure symbol with no physical referent; it must be reported as a stylistic marker, never merged with the physical sweat entries.

entries.label: Sweat sheen on the skin
entries.description: A broad specular film on the forehead, nose and cheeks from heat, exertion or fear.
entries.frame_evidence: Bright soft highlights spread across the high points of the face with the skin looking wet rather than matte.
entries.detector_note: Ratio of the 95th-percentile L to the median L inside the face mask, plus the area fraction above a specular threshold, tracked against the character shot baseline
entries.notes: Wholly confounded with lighting changes, oily skin, makeup and a change of key light; only a within-shot rise with stable frame luminance is evidence. | TIER CORRECTED by completeness critic: Marked deterministic, but every one of them needs an ALIGNED FACE REGION, and the face mesh in that same shard is landmark-tier (and face_head.facemesh_fit_failure exists precisely because it fails on stylised art). Pall

entries.label: Comic tear burst / waterfall tears
entries.description: The exaggerated anime convention of tears spraying or streaming as thick jets from the eyes.
entries.frame_evidence: Two large stylised streams or fans of drawn droplets projecting from the eyes.
entries.detector_note: Crop the face and ask qwen2.5vl; deterministic corroboration is a large bright low-chroma region attached to the eye ROI extending well beyond the face oval
entries.vlm_question: In this cropped image of a cartoon face, are large exaggerated streams of tears spraying out of the eyes? Answer yes or no.

entries.label: Falling tear drop
entries.description: A discrete tear detaching and falling from the eye or jaw.
entries.frame_evidence: A small bright blob moving downward across frames, separate from the face.
entries.detector_note: Small bright connected components (area under 0.01 of the face bbox) below the eye whose centroid displaces downward monotonically over 3 or more unique cels; cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats plus nearest-neighbour linking
entries.notes: Rain, sparks, dust motes and bokeh produce identical tracks; requires the drop to originate inside the eye ROI to be attributable. | TIER CORRECTED by completeness critic: Marked deterministic, but every one of them needs an ALIGNED FACE REGION, and the face mesh in that same shard is landmark-tier (and face_head.facemesh_fit_failure exists precisely because it fails on stylised art). Pall

entries.label: Tear streak on the cheek
entries.description: One or more tear trails running down the face.
entries.frame_evidence: A thin near-vertical bright or glossy line descending from the inner or outer eye corner across the cheek.
entries.detector_note: skimage.filters.frangi vesselness on the cheek ROI restricted to near-vertical ridge orientations, thresholded and filtered to components longer than 0.15 IOD starting within the eye-corner neighbourhood
entries.notes: Frangi also lights up on hair strands, scars, rain, blood and rim-light edges on the cheekbone; the requirement that the component originate at an eye corner is what makes it specific. | TIER CORRECTED by completeness critic: Marked deterministic, but every one of them needs an ALIGNED FACE REGION, and the face mesh in that same shard is landmark-tier (and face_head.facemesh_fit_failure exists precisely because it fails on stylised art). Pall

entries.label: Tears welling in the eyes
entries.description: Fluid pooling along the lower lid before any tear falls.
entries.frame_evidence: A bright glossy band along the lower lid with elevated specular highlights and a wobbling meniscus.
entries.detector_note: Within the lower-lid ROI, the fraction of pixels above the 97th percentile L of the face plus the temporal variance of that fraction (a wobbling meniscus flickers); compared against the character shot baseline
entries.notes: Any wet or strongly lit eye produces lower-lid specularity; without a baseline this is a shininess detector. In 2D it is usually drawn as explicit highlight shapes and is better served by the vlm.

entries.label: Gritted / bared teeth
entries.description: Both rows of teeth pressed together and exposed by retracted lips, the strain, rage or defiance signal.
entries.frame_evidence: Two horizontal white bands separated by a thin dark line, framed by widely stretched lips.
entries.detector_note: teeth_area_fraction above 0.4 with mar_inner low (under 0.12) and mouth_width_ratio above 1.1; the combination of wide-and-nearly-closed-yet-full-of-teeth is the signature
entries.notes: Geometrically identical to the SS viseme; only duration and the absence of a viseme cycle separate them.

entries.label: Teeth visible
entries.description: Any teeth showing inside the mouth aperture.
entries.frame_evidence: A bright near-white low-chroma band inside the dark mouth opening.
entries.detector_note: Inside the inner-lip mask, count pixels with LAB L above the face median and |a| and |b| both low (near-neutral chroma); report the fraction of aperture area
entries.notes: Bright specular highlights on wet lips and a bright background seen through an open mouth both trip the chroma test; require the pixels to be inside the filled inner-lip polygon, not merely near it.

entries.label: Tongue protruding past the lips
entries.description: The tongue stuck out beyond the mouth, for cheek, disgust, exhaustion or a comedic beat.
entries.frame_evidence: A pink shape extending outside the lip contour onto the chin or lower face.
entries.detector_note: Pink-mask connected component whose bounding box extends beyond the outer-lip polygon by more than 0.03 IOD; measure the protrusion length and direction
entries.notes: Reliable when a face mask exists; robust on 2D too because the pink-outside-the-lip-line test does not need a mesh, only a mouth region.

entries.label: Tongue tip position
entries.description: Where the tongue tip sits inside the mouth, the discriminator between the L, TH, DD and vowel visemes.
entries.frame_evidence: The leading edge of the pink mass relative to the teeth and lip contours.
entries.detector_note: Needs a trained mouth-interior segmentation model to separate tongue from oral cavity and place the tip; no such model is installed and there is no sklearn to fit a light one
entries.notes: NOT INSTALLED. This is the single missing measurement that would resolve the model-tier visemes; worth flagging as the highest-value model to add for this domain.

entries.label: Tongue visible inside the mouth
entries.description: The tongue body visible within an open mouth.
entries.frame_evidence: A pink or red mass filling the lower part of the mouth aperture.
entries.detector_note: Inside the inner-lip mask, fraction of pixels with high LAB a (pink/red) and mid L, excluding the lip band itself
entries.notes: The inside of the mouth is also red; separating tongue from oral cavity by colour alone is unreliable, so treat this as an aperture-is-pink measurement and say so.

entries.label: Turn to face camera
entries.description: The head rotating from an off-axis facing to look directly at the lens, a deliberate dramatic move.
entries.frame_evidence: The face swinging around until frontal with the gaze settling on the lens.
entries.detector_note: A head_turn event whose final |head_yaw_deg| and |head_pitch_deg| are both under 12, followed by eye_contact_camera going true within 4 samples

entries.label: Upper sclera visible (fear tell)
entries.description: White of the eye showing above the iris, the strong fear and shock signal.
entries.frame_evidence: A band of bright pixels between the upper lid edge and the top of the iris.
entries.detector_note: Inside the eye ROI from the eye landmark ring, threshold on LAB L above the iris-ring top (landmarks 469-472 / 474-477): count high-L low-chroma pixels between lid landmark 159/386 and the iris top; report the band height normalised by inter-ocular distance |p33-p263| so the value is scale invariant
entries.notes: Needs the refined iris landmarks, so live action and quality 3D only; stylised 2D eyes have painted whites that break the chroma test.

entries.label: Bulging vein on temple or forehead
entries.description: A raised vessel visible on the temple or forehead under strain or rage.
entries.frame_evidence: A branching raised ridge with its own highlight and shadow on the side of the forehead.
entries.detector_note: Crop the temple region and ask qwen2.5vl; deterministic pre-filter is skimage.filters.frangi ridge response in the temple ROI above the shot baseline
entries.vlm_question: In this close cropped image of a forehead or temple, is there a raised bulging vein visible on the skin? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Rarely modelled in 3D and rarely drawn realistically; expect near-universal NOT FOUND.

entries.label: Viseme: AA (open A as in father)
entries.description: The wide-open jaw-dropped mouth shape. viseme vocabulary is the Preston-Blair 10 extended toward the Oculus OVR 15 set: sil, aa, E, ih, oh, ou/W, PP(M-B-P), FF(F-V), TH, DD/nn/tt, kk, CH/SH/JJ, SS, RR, L
entries.frame_evidence: A large open aperture, jaw clearly dropped, lips neither spread nor rounded.
entries.detector_note: mar_inner above 0.35 with jaw_drop_normalised above 0.5 and mouth_width_ratio within 0.15 of neutral; aperture_eccentricity moderate (0.4-0.8)
entries.notes: Visemes are many-to-one with phonemes and this is a GEOMETRY classifier, not a speech recogniser: it can only report the mouth SHAPE class, never the spoken sound. Any claim beyond shape is an overclaim. AA is geometrically indistinguishable from a shout, a yawn peak and a scream on shape alone; disambiguation needs the duration and the audio track.

entries.label: Viseme: CH / SH / JJ (postalveolar, protruded)
entries.description: The forward-protruded slightly-rounded mouth of SH, CH and J.
entries.frame_evidence: The lips pushed forward into a small rounded rectangle with the teeth close together.
entries.detector_note: Needs a trained mouth-crop classifier; geometrically it sits between OU and DD and the landmark thresholds overlap both
entries.notes: NOT INSTALLED. Reported as unresolved between OU and the consonant class.

entries.label: Viseme: DD / NN / TT (alveolar consonants)
entries.description: The narrow slightly-open mouth of D, T and N, where the visible articulation is mostly the tongue behind the teeth.
entries.frame_evidence: A small aperture with teeth close together and little lip shaping.
entries.detector_note: The visible geometry of DD, NN, TT and kk is nearly identical and is not separable from landmarks; needs a trained viseme classifier on mouth crops, which we do not have
entries.notes: NOT INSTALLED: no viseme classifier and no sklearn to train a light one. Logged as a known blind spot; these consonants are correctly reported as a single unresolved neutral-consonant class.

entries.label: Viseme: E (spread, as in bet)
entries.description: The horizontally stretched half-open mouth. viseme vocabulary is the Preston-Blair 10 extended toward the Oculus OVR 15 set: sil, aa, E, ih, oh, ou/W, PP(M-B-P), FF(F-V), TH, DD/nn/tt, kk, CH/SH/JJ, SS, RR, L
entries.frame_evidence: A wide flattened aperture with the corners pulled outward and the teeth often showing.
entries.detector_note: mouth_width_ratio above 1.08 with mar_inner in 0.10-0.28 and aperture_eccentricity above 0.85 (a wide flat ellipse)
entries.notes: Visemes are many-to-one with phonemes and this is a GEOMETRY classifier, not a speech recogniser: it can only report the mouth SHAPE class, never the spoken sound. Any claim beyond shape is an overclaim. Overlaps heavily with a closed-teeth smile; the two are separated only by duration and by whether the shape recurs at speech rate.

entries.label: Viseme: FF (F, V lip-on-teeth)
entries.description: The lower lip drawn under the upper teeth for F and V.
entries.frame_evidence: The upper teeth visibly resting on or biting the lower lip with the mouth barely open.
entries.detector_note: Crop the mouth (inner-lip bbox expanded 80 percent, upscaled to at least 256 px per THE CROP RULE) and ask qwen2.5vl; the landmark geometry cannot see teeth-on-lip at all
entries.vlm_question: In this cropped image of a mouth, are the upper front teeth resting on or touching the lower lip? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Visemes are many-to-one with phonemes and this is a GEOMETRY classifier, not a speech recogniser: it can only report the mouth SHAPE class, never the spoken sound. Any claim beyond shape is an overclaim. Frame-rate cost: a vlm call per frame is unaffordable, so this can only be run on candidate frames pre-selected by low mar_inner during speech.

entries.label: Viseme: IH / EE (narrow spread, as in bit and see)
entries.description: A narrow spread mouth with a small aperture. viseme vocabulary is the Preston-Blair 10 extended toward the Oculus OVR 15 set: sil, aa, E, ih, oh, ou/W, PP(M-B-P), FF(F-V), TH, DD/nn/tt, kk, CH/SH/JJ, SS, RR, L
entries.frame_evidence: The lips slightly parted and stretched wide with a thin slot between them.
entries.detector_note: mouth_width_ratio above 1.05 with mar_inner in 0.05-0.12; separated from E only by aperture height
entries.notes: Visemes are many-to-one with phonemes and this is a GEOMETRY classifier, not a speech recogniser: it can only report the mouth SHAPE class, never the spoken sound. Any claim beyond shape is an overclaim. The IH/E boundary is a threshold choice, not a physical one; report the pair jointly when confidence is close.

entries.label: Viseme: KK / GG (velar consonants)
entries.description: The near-neutral mouth of K and G, articulated at the back of the tongue where nothing is visible.
entries.frame_evidence: A mouth shape barely distinguishable from the surrounding vowels.
entries.detector_note: The articulation is behind the tongue body and produces no reliable external evidence in any medium; this is a genuine physical blind spot, not a tooling gap
entries.notes: Even a perfect viseme model cannot recover velars from vision alone. Always logged NOT DETECTABLE, which is the honest answer.

entries.label: Viseme: L (tongue tip to alveolar ridge)
entries.description: The L shape, with the tongue tip raised behind the upper teeth inside a moderately open mouth.
entries.frame_evidence: A visible tongue body inside an open mouth with the tip touching the roof.
entries.detector_note: Crop the mouth on frames where the aperture is open and contains a pink region and ask qwen2.5vl
entries.vlm_question: In this cropped image of an open mouth, is the tongue raised so its tip touches the roof of the mouth behind the upper teeth? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Visemes are many-to-one with phonemes and this is a GEOMETRY classifier, not a speech recogniser: it can only report the mouth SHAPE class, never the spoken sound. Any claim beyond shape is an overclaim. Small VLMs are unreliable on tongue position; treat any positive as low confidence.

entries.label: Viseme: OH (rounded open, as in go)
entries.description: The rounded medium-open mouth. viseme vocabulary is the Preston-Blair 10 extended toward the Oculus OVR 15 set: sil, aa, E, ih, oh, ou/W, PP(M-B-P), FF(F-V), TH, DD/nn/tt, kk, CH/SH/JJ, SS, RR, L
entries.frame_evidence: A roughly circular aperture with the corners drawn inward.
entries.detector_note: mouth_width_ratio below 0.92 with mar_inner in 0.18-0.40 and aperture_eccentricity below 0.5 (near-circular)
entries.notes: Visemes are many-to-one with phonemes and this is a GEOMETRY classifier, not a speech recogniser: it can only report the mouth SHAPE class, never the spoken sound. Any claim beyond shape is an overclaim.

entries.label: Viseme: OU / W (pucker, as in boot and we)
entries.description: The tightly rounded protruded mouth. viseme vocabulary is the Preston-Blair 10 extended toward the Oculus OVR 15 set: sil, aa, E, ih, oh, ou/W, PP(M-B-P), FF(F-V), TH, DD/nn/tt, kk, CH/SH/JJ, SS, RR, L
entries.frame_evidence: A small circular aperture with the lips pushed forward and the corners strongly drawn in.
entries.detector_note: mouth_width_ratio below 0.80 with mar_inner in 0.06-0.20 and, where available, lip_z_protrusion above the shot neutral
entries.notes: Visemes are many-to-one with phonemes and this is a GEOMETRY classifier, not a speech recogniser: it can only report the mouth SHAPE class, never the spoken sound. Any claim beyond shape is an overclaim. Without a usable protrusion measurement OU and a whistle or a kiss are the same shape.

entries.label: Viseme: PP (M, B, P bilabial closure)
entries.description: The full lip closure that produces M, B and P, the most reliably detectable viseme.
entries.frame_evidence: The lips pressed fully together for a single frame in the middle of otherwise moving speech.
entries.detector_note: aperture_area_iod2 dropping to near zero for 1-3 unique-cel samples while the surrounding window has speaking_activity true; the transient closure inside continuous speech is the signature, not the closure itself
entries.notes: Visemes are many-to-one with phonemes and this is a GEOMETRY classifier, not a speech recogniser: it can only report the mouth SHAPE class, never the spoken sound. Any claim beyond shape is an overclaim. This is the one viseme worth trusting from geometry alone, because closure inside speech is unambiguous. It cannot distinguish M from B from P.

entries.label: Viseme: rest / silence (sil)
entries.description: The neutral closed mouth between utterances. viseme vocabulary is the Preston-Blair 10 extended toward the Oculus OVR 15 set: sil, aa, E, ih, oh, ou/W, PP(M-B-P), FF(F-V), TH, DD/nn/tt, kk, CH/SH/JJ, SS, RR, L
entries.frame_evidence: Lips together at neutral width with no aperture and no corner displacement.
entries.detector_note: mar_inner under 0.04 and mouth_width_ratio within 0.06 of the shot neutral and aperture_area near zero, held over 2 or more unique-cel samples
entries.notes: Visemes are many-to-one with phonemes and this is a GEOMETRY classifier, not a speech recogniser: it can only report the mouth SHAPE class, never the spoken sound. Any claim beyond shape is an overclaim.

entries.label: Viseme: RR (R, slightly rounded and retracted)
entries.description: The R shape, mildly rounded with the tongue bunched or curled.
entries.frame_evidence: A small rounded mouth with less protrusion than OU and no full closure.
entries.detector_note: Needs a trained classifier; R varies more by accent and by animator than any other viseme and has no stable geometric signature
entries.notes: NOT INSTALLED, and even with a model this is the lowest-reliability viseme in the set.

entries.label: Viseme sequence over a line
entries.description: The ordered string of viseme classes across a spoken line, the thing an animator actually authored.
entries.frame_evidence: A run of frames whose mouth shapes cycle through distinguishable classes at speech rate.
entries.detector_note: Per-unique-cel argmax over the viseme confidence vector, median-filtered with a width-3 kernel to remove single-sample flicker, emitted as a run-length-encoded sequence with per-symbol durations
entries.notes: Visemes are many-to-one with phonemes and this is a GEOMETRY classifier, not a speech recogniser: it can only report the mouth SHAPE class, never the spoken sound. Any claim beyond shape is an overclaim. unresolved_fraction is the honesty metric: on a 3-shape anime mouth chart it will exceed 0.6 and the sequence should be reported as shape-classes, not visemes.

entries.label: Viseme: SS / ZZ (sibilant, teeth together)
entries.description: The narrow mouth with the teeth nearly touching for S and Z.
entries.frame_evidence: A thin horizontal slot with both rows of teeth visible and close together.
entries.detector_note: Crop the mouth on frames with low mar_inner and high white-pixel fraction inside the aperture, and ask qwen2.5vl
entries.vlm_question: In this cropped image of a mouth, are both the upper and lower teeth visible and nearly touching, with only a narrow gap between them? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Visemes are many-to-one with phonemes and this is a GEOMETRY classifier, not a speech recogniser: it can only report the mouth SHAPE class, never the spoken sound. Any claim beyond shape is an overclaim. Overlaps completely with a gritted-teeth expression on shape; only speech context separates them.

entries.label: Viseme: TH (tongue between teeth)
entries.description: The tongue tip protruding between the teeth for the TH sounds.
entries.frame_evidence: A small pink tongue tip visible between the upper and lower teeth.
entries.detector_note: Crop the mouth and ask qwen2.5vl on candidate frames where mar_inner is low but non-zero and the aperture contains high-a-channel (pink) pixels
entries.vlm_question: In this cropped image of a mouth, is the tip of the tongue visible between the teeth? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Visemes are many-to-one with phonemes and this is a GEOMETRY classifier, not a speech recogniser: it can only report the mouth SHAPE class, never the spoken sound. Any claim beyond shape is an overclaim. Almost never drawn in 2D animation at all, so a NOT FOUND on anime is expected and uninformative.

entries.label: Mouth shape change rate
entries.description: How fast the mouth shape is changing, the substrate for speaking-versus-silent and for fast versus laboured speech.
entries.frame_evidence: The mouth outline differing substantially from one unique cel to the next, repeatedly.
entries.detector_note: Mean per-sample L2 distance of the normalised inner-lip landmark vector (or the Hu-moment vector on 2D), reported as changes per second using the measured unique-cel rate
entries.notes: This is the most robust speech-related measurement in the whole group because it needs no class labels at all; prefer it over any viseme claim when unresolved_fraction is high.

entries.label: Wince / flinch squeeze
entries.description: A fast asymmetric or bilateral hard squeeze of the lids in reaction to pain or an impact.
entries.frame_evidence: A brief deep EAR trough with simultaneous brow lowering and nose wrinkle, faster onset than a natural blink.
entries.detector_note: EAR trough with closure velocity above the 90th percentile of that shot combined with brow_height dropping and nose_wrinkle rising in the same 3-cel window; requires the co-occurrence, not the EAR alone
entries.notes: Without the brow and nose co-occurrence this is just a fast blink; reporting a wince from EAR alone is the classic overclaim in this domain.

entries.label: Wink / one-eye close
entries.description: One eye closes while the other stays open.
entries.frame_evidence: A large EAR asymmetry with one eye at baseline and the other near zero.
entries.detector_note: ear_asymmetry exceeding 0.5*baseline sustained for 2 or more unique-cel samples while the open eye stays above 0.7*baseline
entries.notes: Head roll and extreme yaw both produce a genuine EAR asymmetry from foreshortening alone; gate this on |head_roll_deg| under 20 and |head_yaw_deg| under 25 or it fires constantly during turns.

entries.label: Yawn
entries.description: A slow wide opening and closing of the mouth with the eyes usually squeezing shut.
entries.frame_evidence: A very large aperture held for a long time with the head often tilting back and the eyes closing.
entries.detector_note: mar_inner above 0.45 sustained for more than 0.6 s of screen time, with ear_mean dropping below 0.5*baseline in the same window and a slow symmetric open-hold-close envelope
entries.notes: The duration plus eye-closure co-occurrence is what separates a yawn from a shout; either alone is not enough.

entries.label: Backdraft / inrush before eruption
entries.description: Air and smoke drawn inward toward an opening immediately before a violent outward eruption.
entries.frame_evidence: A short window of inward (negative divergence) flow toward an aperture, immediately followed by strong outward flow.
entries.detector_note: Detect a sign flip in the mean flow divergence within an ROI: sustained negative divergence for >= 3 unique cels followed within 5 cels by a large positive divergence; report both magnitudes and the gap.
entries.notes: Rare and usually stylised; the ROI must be supplied or come from a detected opening, which we cannot detect automatically.

entries.label: Blood dripping from an object
entries.description: Drops falling from a blade, hand, or edge.
entries.frame_evidence: Red pendant drops forming at an edge, detaching, and falling on gravity-consistent arcs.
entries.detector_note: drip_pendant and drip_detach_event restricted to the red mask, with a ballistic-arc check on the falling child blob.
entries.notes: Depends on drop-scale resolution; usually only works in close-ups.

entries.label: Blood trickle
entries.description: A thin line of blood running down a surface, skin, or face.
entries.frame_evidence: A narrow dark-red line extending downward over successive cels from a fixed origin point.
entries.detector_note: Runoff-rivulet tip tracking restricted to a red-hue mask (H in [0,10] or [170,179] OpenCV units, S > 120, V moderate); report the tip descent rate and the line width.
entries.notes: Red hair, red fabric, red paint and rust all pass the colour test; the extension-over-time requirement is what makes it a trickle. Stylised black or monochrome blood is entirely missed.

entries.label: Spreading blood pool
entries.description: A pool of blood growing on a floor or surface.
entries.frame_evidence: A dark red region on the ground whose area increases monotonically across the shot with a smooth advancing boundary.
entries.detector_note: Red mask on a ground-plane region; fit area against the unique-cel index and require a positive slope with r2 > 0.8; measure boundary smoothness from contour curvature statistics.
entries.notes: Requires a stable camera. A pool that appears fully formed in one cel (slope undefined) is the common animation treatment and is a legitimate distinct finding.

entries.label: Blood soaking through fabric
entries.description: A red stain expanding through clothing from a wound.
entries.frame_evidence: A red region on a garment growing outward with a diffuse, feathered boundary rather than a sharp one.
entries.detector_note: Within a mediapipe-pose torso or limb ROI, track red-mask area growth and measure boundary sharpness (mean gradient magnitude along the contour); soaking shows growth with a low boundary gradient.
entries.notes: Red garment patterns inside the ROI will be counted as stain; the growth term must be non-zero for this to mean anything.

entries.label: Arterial blood spray
entries.description: A pulsed jet of blood ejected under pressure.
entries.frame_evidence: A narrow red arc or cone leaving a point on a body, appearing in rhythmic bursts rather than continuously.
entries.detector_note: Red-mask cone or arc from an apex, with a burst temporal profile: FFT of the masked area series over unique cels showing a dominant low-frequency peak; report the pulse period.
entries.notes: Needs enough unique cels for the pulse FFT; most such shots are too short. Stylised spray is often a single held drawing and will show no pulse at all.

entries.label: Blowing sand / spindrift sheet
entries.description: A low sheet of granular material streaming across a surface in wind.
entries.frame_evidence: A thin low-lying textured layer with fast, strongly unidirectional horizontal flow hugging the ground or a dune.
entries.detector_note: Detect a horizontally elongated band above a surface with flow resultant length > 0.8, direction within 25 deg of horizontal, and internal texture decorrelating rapidly across unique cels.
entries.notes: A fast horizontal camera move over textured ground produces the same field; homography stabilisation is mandatory.

entries.label: Nucleate boiling bubbles
entries.description: Small bubbles forming repeatedly at fixed nucleation sites on a heated vessel bottom.
entries.frame_evidence: Bubbles appearing at the same few pixel locations again and again, each rising and vanishing.
entries.detector_note: Build a per-pixel event map by accumulating bubble-track origins over the shot; nucleation sites are pixels whose origin count is > 5 sigma above the map mean. Requires bubble tracking as above.
entries.notes: Almost never depicted with true nucleation-site repetition in animation; expect NOT FOUND. Needs a fixed camera and a long shot.

entries.label: Rolling boil
entries.description: Vigorous, continuous, whole-surface agitation of a heated liquid.
entries.frame_evidence: The entire liquid surface churns with high-frequency, high-magnitude, spatially incoherent motion, plus dense bubbles and steam above.
entries.detector_note: Inside the liquid region require flow magnitude above the frame 90th percentile, flow coherence below 0.3, and temporal decorrelation between unique cels > 0.6; combine into a boil_intensity score.
entries.notes: Requires the liquid region to be known; a churning crowd or foliage in wind has the same statistics. Consider a VLM confirmation crop on the pot.

entries.label: Bow wave
entries.description: The raised, foaming water pushed ahead of and around the front of a moving hull or body.
entries.frame_evidence: A bright crescent of disturbed water hugging the leading edge of a moving object, moving locked to it.
entries.detector_note: Whitewater mask (V>0.75, S<0.20) intersected with a dilated band ahead of the tracked object; require its centroid displacement to correlate with the object's displacement at r > 0.8 across the window.
