entries.notes: A missing bow wave on a fast-moving hull is itself a finding but absence cannot be asserted without a confident object track, which we have no detector for.

entries.label: Visible breath in cold air
entries.description: A short puff of condensed vapour exhaled from a mouth or nostrils.
entries.frame_evidence: A small, brief, low-contrast light puff originating at a face's mouth region and dispersing within a few frames.
entries.detector_note: Use mediapipe face mesh to locate the mouth (landmarks 13/14/61/291) and define an ROI extending forward from it; inside that ROI detect a transient low-contrast bright region with positive divergence lasting 3-15 unique cels.
entries.notes: Requires a detectable face; mediapipe face mesh fails on stylised anime faces at many angles and on profile views. Cigarette smoke from the same mouth is indistinguishable by this test.

entries.label: Bubble bursting at the surface
entries.description: A bubble reaching the liquid surface and popping.
entries.frame_evidence: A blob arriving at the waterline disappears within one or two cels, leaving a brief small ring or ripple at that spot.
entries.detector_note: Detect track termination within 5px of the waterline, then check the same ROI for a short-lived expanding ring (radial gradient peak radius increasing over 2-4 cels).
entries.notes: Requires both the bubble tracker and the waterline; usually only resolvable in close-ups.

entries.label: Static bubble cluster / froth
entries.description: A raft of bubbles sitting on a liquid surface without a bulk flow.
entries.frame_evidence: A patch of packed circles with visible rims and highlights, drifting slowly with the surface rather than rising.
entries.detector_note: cv2.HoughCircles on a contrast-enhanced crop of the surface; require >= 6 circles with radii within a factor of 3 of one another and near-zero net vertical motion.
entries.notes: HoughCircles on froth is fragile; treat the count as an order of magnitude, not a census.

entries.label: Rising bubble column
entries.description: A stream of gas bubbles ascending through a liquid.
entries.frame_evidence: Small ring-like or highlighted circular blobs moving consistently upward along a roughly vertical path, often growing as they rise.
entries.detector_note: Blob detection restricted to a water region, linked into tracks; require the mean track direction within 25 deg of up and mean upward speed > 1px per unique cel; measure blob radius growth along each track.
entries.notes: Requires the water region for context; in an unlabelled frame this fires on any upward-moving speckle. Bubbles that grow while rising is a physically correct detail worth reporting separately.

entries.label: Glowing burn edge advancing
entries.description: The thin glowing line at the boundary between burnt and unburnt material.
entries.frame_evidence: A narrow orange line separating a black char region from an intact region, moving into the intact region cel by cel.
entries.detector_note: Detect a thin (< 6px) fire-coloured contour lying between the char mask and the unburnt region; track its position normal to itself and report the advance rate.
entries.notes: Depends on charring_blackening providing the char mask; NOT DETECTABLE without it, or in stylised 2D where the char is drawn as a flat shape with no glowing rim.

entries.label: Fire burning out
entries.description: A flame diminishing toward extinction.
entries.frame_evidence: Fire mask area and mean luminance both decline monotonically over many cels until the mask disappears.
entries.detector_note: Fit an exponential decay to fire_mask_area_frac over the shot with scipy.optimize.curve_fit; report tau, the fit r2 and the extinction cel where the area first falls below 30px.
entries.notes: An instantaneous extinction (tau near zero) is common in animation and is a legitimate result, but check for a shot boundary first.

entries.label: Campfire coal bed
entries.description: A bed of glowing embers beneath or between flames, without its own flicker.
entries.frame_evidence: A low-lying orange-red region with high brightness but much lower temporal variation than the flames above it.
entries.detector_note: Fire-coloured pixels whose per-cel luminance std is below 40% of the flame region's std, located below the flame mask centroid; report area and the std ratio.
entries.notes: Shares its statistics with molten_metal_glow; separated only by spatial context under a flame.

entries.label: Candle guttering / near-extinction
entries.description: A candle flame shrinking, flattening and thrashing as it nearly goes out.
entries.frame_evidence: Flame area drops sharply and the orientation swings wildly across a few cels, sometimes vanishing and returning.
entries.detector_note: On a tracked candle flame, detect a window where area falls below 40% of its running median while orientation std more than doubles; report whether the flame recovers or the track ends.
entries.notes: A candle passing behind an object produces the same area drop; require the surrounding cast light to drop in step.

entries.label: Candle flame teardrop
entries.description: A small, single, roughly teardrop-shaped flame on a wick.
entries.frame_evidence: A small isolated fire region (typically < 0.5% of the frame) with a rounded base, a pointed top, and low flicker amplitude.
entries.detector_note: Fire components with area below a small threshold, aspect ratio 1.3-2.5, a single skeleton branch and flicker amplitude below 15% of the mean; require a dark vertical wick line at the base.
entries.notes: Small warm practicals, LED candles and lens flares are shape-compatible; the wick check helps only in close-ups.

entries.label: Caustics animation rate
entries.description: How fast the caustic network reorganises over time.
entries.frame_evidence: The bright web changes topology between unique cels while the underlying surface stays fixed.
entries.detector_note: Normalised cross-correlation of the top-hat caustic map between consecutive unique cels; rate = 1 - NCC. Also measure the frame-to-frame change in branch_point_density and the autocorrelation peak period.
entries.notes: A tiling looped caustics texture (very common in cheap CG) gives an exact repeat - report caustic_loop_period_cels when the autocorrelation shows a strong peak, that is itself a finding.

entries.label: Caustics network
entries.description: The bright interlaced web of focused light cast through a rippled water surface onto a submerged or nearby surface.
entries.frame_evidence: A cellular network of thin bright curved lines over a diffuse surface, with characteristic polygonal cells.
entries.detector_note: Top-hat filter (cv2.morphologyEx MORPH_TOPHAT, elliptical kernel ~7px) to isolate thin bright ridges; skeletonise with skimage.morphology.skeletonize and measure branch-point density and mean cell area via skimage.measure.label on the inverted skeleton.
entries.notes: Cracked mud, spiderwebs, veins and lace produce similar skeleton statistics on a single frame; the animation rate entry is what makes it caustics.

entries.label: Effect animation cadence (1s / 2s / 3s)
entries.description: How many container frames each unique drawing of the effect is held for.
entries.frame_evidence: The effect region is near-identical across runs of 2 or 3 consecutive container frames.
entries.detector_note: Within the effect region bbox compute the mean absolute difference between consecutive container frames; a run of near-zero differences is a hold. Report the modal hold length and the full histogram.
entries.notes: THIS ENTRY IS A PREREQUISITE for every temporal metric in this domain. Effects are frequently animated on a different cadence from the characters - effect_vs_scene_cadence_delta captures that, and each region must be deduped on its own.

entries.label: Looping effect cycle
entries.description: A fire, water, or smoke effect that repeats a fixed short sequence of drawings.
entries.frame_evidence: The effect region's content at cel n is near-identical to cel n+P for a fixed period P across the shot.
entries.detector_note: Build the unique-cel similarity matrix for the effect ROI (normalised cross-correlation or perceptual-hash Hamming distance); a loop shows strong off-diagonal bands at a constant offset P.
entries.notes: Applies to 3D too: a cached or tiled fluid sim loops identically. A short shot cannot distinguish a loop from a coincidence - require at least 3 repeats.

entries.label: Flat cel-shaded fluid fill
entries.description: Fire, water or smoke drawn as flat colour regions bounded by hard ink lines rather than as a gradient volume.
entries.frame_evidence: The effect region has very few distinct colour values, hard high-contrast boundaries, and near-zero internal texture.
entries.detector_note: Inside the effect mask count distinct quantised colours (np.unique on the frame reduced to 5 bits per channel), measure internal Laplacian variance (near zero) and boundary gradient magnitude (high); a cel fill is few colours, flat interior, hard edge.
entries.notes: This entry exists so that a low internal_decorrelation or zone_count == 1 elsewhere is read as a style, not a defect. Heavy banding in compressed CG can mimic a low colour count.

entries.label: Stylised smoke puff ring
entries.description: Smoke or dust drawn as a ring or cluster of scalloped circular lobes.
entries.frame_evidence: The smoke silhouette is composed of arcs of similar radius joined into a scalloped outline, rather than a fractal boundary.
entries.detector_note: Fit circles to segments of the effect contour (RANSAC over contour chunks); a stylised puff has many high-quality circle fits of similar radius, while real smoke has a high box-counting fractal dimension and poor circle fits.
entries.notes: The fractal-dimension contrast between drawn and simulated smoke is the strongest single 2D-vs-3D discriminator in this domain.

entries.label: Stylised water speed lines
entries.description: Motion or force conveyed by drawn parallel lines within or around a fluid effect.
entries.frame_evidence: Long, thin, near-perfectly parallel and unnaturally straight lines overlaid on or emanating from the fluid region.
entries.detector_note: cv2.HoughLinesP with a long minLineLength; require an orientation std < 8 deg and near-perfect straightness (contour deviation from the fitted line < 1px), which real fluid streaks do not achieve.
entries.notes: Rain streaks are also near-parallel; separated by the straightness residual and by persistence within a single cel.

entries.label: Ink-outlined water shapes
entries.description: Water, splashes or waves delineated by explicit black or coloured outlines.
entries.frame_evidence: Closed dark contours enclosing the water regions, of near-constant width, following the effect's silhouette.
entries.detector_note: Detect closed dark contours (V below the 10th percentile) of near-constant width via the distance transform along the contour, enclosing regions classified as water candidates; report the width consistency.
entries.notes: Line art detection is confounded by heavy shadows and by dark backgrounds behind bright effects.

entries.label: Charring / blackening of material
entries.description: A surface darkening permanently where it has burned.
entries.frame_evidence: A region's luminance falls monotonically and does not recover, with the darkened area expanding outward from the fire contact zone.
entries.detector_note: Per-pixel luminance monotonic-decrease test across unique cels on a homography-stabilised surface; char area = pixels whose luminance dropped > 30% and never rose again; require adjacency to the fire mask.
entries.notes: A moving shadow produces a large luminance drop that recovers; the irreversibility ratio is what separates them. Requires a stable camera.

entries.label: Chimney smoke
entries.description: Smoke rising from a roof stack or chimney.
entries.frame_evidence: A plume with a small, static, elevated source point on a building silhouette, drifting with the wind.
entries.detector_note: Detect the plume deterministically (smoke_plume_column) and send a crop centred on the plume base to the VLM to identify the source.
entries.vlm_question: Is the smoke in this crop coming out of a chimney or a rooftop pipe? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Base localisation is deterministic and reliable; only the source identification needs the VLM.

entries.label: Exhaled smoke puff
entries.description: A dense puff of smoke expelled from a mouth.
entries.frame_evidence: A puff originating at a face's mouth region, expanding forward and dispersing over 10-40 frames.
entries.detector_note: Same ROI construction as breath_vapour_cold from mediapipe face-mesh mouth landmarks, but requiring a longer lifetime (> 10 unique cels), a larger peak area and a slower dispersion than a cold-breath puff.
entries.notes: The separation from cold breath is a duration and size heuristic with no validated threshold; treat the class label as uncertain and report the raw numbers.

entries.label: Condensation beads on a cold surface
entries.description: Fine water droplets forming on a chilled container (a glass, a can, a pipe).
entries.frame_evidence: A dense field of tiny specular points appearing on a curved surface, often coalescing into runoff over time.
entries.detector_note: As droplet_beading_on_surface but with a temporal onset requirement: bead count rising from near zero over the shot; anchor to a surface region whose homography is stable.
entries.notes: Usually static set dressing rather than an animated event; the count slope will be ~0 and this will read as beading, not condensation. That distinction is the point.

entries.label: Fogging on glass
entries.description: A translucent misted layer forming on a cold or hot glass surface.
entries.frame_evidence: A bounded region progressively losing high-frequency detail and gaining brightness while its outline stays fixed in screen space.
entries.detector_note: Within a screen-static region, track Laplacian variance decreasing monotonically while mean V increases, over >= 8 unique cels; report both slopes and the region mask.
entries.notes: A rack-focus, a dissolve, or a fade produces the same detail loss globally; require the effect to be spatially bounded and the rest of the frame to stay sharp. | TIER CORRECTED by completeness critic: Marked deterministic but gated on masks whose own entries are vlm: fluids_fire.ice_surface_present is vlm and scene_semantics.material_glass_transparent is vlm. A detector cannot be more certain than its own precondition

entries.label: Drip detachment
entries.description: The frame at which a hanging drop separates and begins to fall freely.
entries.frame_evidence: A connected blob splits into an attached remnant and a free blob that then accelerates downward.
entries.detector_note: Detect a connected-component split (skimage.measure.label count in the ROI increments) followed by downward acceleration of the child blob over the next >=3 unique cels.
entries.notes: In 2D animation the drip is often drawn as a stretched teardrop with no true split; expect NOT FOUND even when a drip is clearly depicted.

entries.label: Pendant drop before detachment
entries.description: A drop hanging from an edge, growing and necking before it falls.
entries.frame_evidence: A small bulb attached to a surface edge whose area grows across several frames while its attachment neck narrows.
entries.detector_note: Track a blob touching an edge contour; measure area(t) increasing and the minimum width of the connecting neck decreasing (distance-transform minimum along the connection path).
entries.notes: Subtle and small; below ~10px the neck measurement is pure noise. Gate on blob area >= 30px.

entries.label: Line of drips from an edge
entries.description: Multiple drips falling from along a roof line, ledge, or branch.
entries.frame_evidence: Several short vertical streaks starting at different points along one horizontal edge, at irregular intervals.
entries.detector_note: Detect drip detach events whose origin points all lie within 5px of one fitted horizontal line (cv2.fitLine on the origins); report the count and the inter-event interval distribution.
entries.notes: A perfectly regular interval across all origins is an animation-loop tell worth flagging.

entries.label: Ballistic droplet trajectories
entries.description: Droplets following parabolic, gravity-consistent paths.
entries.frame_evidence: Tracked droplet centroids across a short window fit a downward-curving parabola with a consistent vertical acceleration.
entries.detector_note: Link droplet blobs frame-to-frame by nearest-neighbour within a motion gate; fit y = a*t^2 + b*t + c per track with np.polyfit on UNIQUE-cel time; report mean a and the fraction of tracks with r2 > 0.9 and a > 0.
entries.notes: Anti-gravity droplets (a <= 0) are a genuine and valuable CG/2D finding. Track linking fails when droplet density is high; report track_count so low-confidence cases are visible. The time axis MUST be the unique-cel index.

entries.label: Beading droplets on a surface
entries.description: Discrete rounded drops resting on a hydrophobic surface (skin, glass, paint, leaves).
entries.frame_evidence: Many small circular highlights each with a bright specular dot and a small shadow, sitting on a solid surface and moving with it.
entries.detector_note: Blob detection restricted to a surface region, requiring an internal V>240 specular point offset from the blob centroid and blob motion locked to the surface homography.
entries.notes: Freckles, acne, rivets and beaded jewellery pass the blob-plus-specular test on stills. Consider a VLM confirmation crop when the count matters.

entries.label: Discrete airborne droplets
entries.description: Individually resolvable liquid drops travelling through air.
entries.frame_evidence: Small isolated blobs (5-200px) with rounded contours, distinct from the background, moving independently of the main fluid mass.
entries.detector_note: skimage.feature.blob_log or cv2.SimpleBlobDetector on the frame-difference image; keep blobs with circularity (4*pi*A/P^2) > 0.5 and inter-frame displacement > 2px; count and size-histogram them.
entries.notes: Snow, sparks, confetti, dust and compression artefacts all pass a blob-plus-circularity test; use colour (low saturation, near-background hue) and ballistic-arc fitting to narrow it.

entries.label: Droplet motion-blur streaks
entries.description: Fast droplets rendered as elongated streaks rather than round blobs.
entries.frame_evidence: Elongated bright ellipses whose long axis aligns with their frame-to-frame displacement direction.
entries.detector_note: For each droplet blob compute skimage regionprops orientation and eccentricity; compare orientation against the track displacement angle; a streak has eccentricity > 0.85 and angular agreement < 20 deg.
entries.notes: A high streak_fraction with poor orientation agreement suggests a baked-in blur texture rather than real motion blur - worth flagging.

entries.label: Water on the camera lens
entries.description: Drops sitting on the lens or a protective glass, distorting the image locally.
entries.frame_evidence: Circular regions of inverted or blurred imagery fixed in screen space while the whole scene moves behind them.
entries.detector_note: Find regions whose local content is static in screen space (low temporal variance) while the global homography indicates camera motion, and whose local blur (Laplacian variance) is far below the frame median.
entries.notes: Dirty-lens dust, a vignette, and a soft-focus filter all produce screen-static low-detail regions.

entries.label: Impact dust cloud
entries.description: A burst of dust thrown up where something heavy strikes the ground.
entries.frame_evidence: A brown-grey low-contrast cloud appearing at a ground contact point and expanding outward and upward over a few cels.
entries.detector_note: Low-saturation warm-grey candidate region (S < 0.30, hue biased warm relative to the smoke test) with a burst onset, a ground-plane base, positive divergence, and area growth followed by decay.
entries.notes: Colour is the only weak separator from smoke and it fails under coloured lighting or a heavy grade. Report the steam_vs_smoke ambiguity flag alongside.

entries.label: Airborne dust motes
entries.description: Individual illuminated dust particles drifting slowly through a light beam or air.
entries.frame_evidence: Sparse tiny bright points drifting slowly and irregularly, often only visible against a dark background or in a shaft of light.
entries.detector_note: skimage.feature.blob_log with sigma 1-2 on a contrast-enhanced dark region; require slow (< 1.5px per unique cel) non-ballistic tracks and a lifetime > 5 cels.
entries.notes: Sensor noise, dead pixels and compression sparkle all present as tiny bright points; the track-lifetime requirement removes most of them but not all.

entries.label: Footstep dust puff
entries.description: A small dust burst at a foot's contact with dry ground.
entries.frame_evidence: A small transient light cloud at the ankle-ground contact point on the frame the foot lands.
entries.detector_note: mediapipe pose ankle landmarks 27/28 give the ROI and the landing cel (vertical-velocity minimum); look inside that ROI for a transient low-contrast bright region lasting 3-12 unique cels.
entries.notes: Same mediapipe limitations as footstep_water_splash: unreliable on stylised or distant figures. Report NOT DETECTABLE below landmark confidence 0.5.

entries.label: Eddy shedding behind obstacle
entries.description: Alternating vortices peeling off downstream of a fixed obstruction in a current.
entries.frame_evidence: Small counter-rotating swirls appearing alternately on either side of a static obstacle and drifting downstream.
entries.detector_note: Curl map downstream of a motion-identified static obstacle; track sign alternation of successive curl blobs and estimate the shedding period by FFT of the signed curl integrated over a downstream window.
entries.notes: Very rarely animated correctly in 2D and usually absent in cheap CG; expect mostly NOT FOUND. Requires long stable shots for the FFT to mean anything.

entries.label: Static glowing embers
entries.description: Small hot points that glow without flame, embedded in burnt material.
entries.frame_evidence: Isolated small orange-red bright points inside a dark region, pulsing gently rather than flickering violently.
entries.detector_note: Small (< 60px) fire-coloured blobs inside a low-luminance surround, with per-cel luminance std between 2% and 15% of their mean and near-zero displacement across unique cels.
entries.notes: Warm out-of-focus practicals and bokeh points are indistinguishable without context.

entries.label: Rising embers
entries.description: Glowing particles carried upward on the thermal column of a fire.
entries.frame_evidence: Small warm points drifting upward with a slight lateral wander, fading as they rise.
entries.detector_note: Track small fire-coloured blobs; require the mean track direction within 40 deg of up and blob luminance declining along each track; report the count, the mean rise speed and the lateral wander std.
entries.notes: Embers rising in perfectly straight parallel lines with no wander are a particle-system tell captured by ember_lateral_wander_std.

entries.label: Vehicle exhaust smoke
entries.description: Smoke or vapour emitted from an exhaust pipe.
entries.frame_evidence: Puffs emerging from a fixed point on a moving object and being left behind in world space as the object advances.
entries.detector_note: Needs a vehicle or exhaust anchor we cannot produce (no object detector installed). The smoke region itself is detectable, but attributing it to an exhaust is not.
entries.notes: Log as not-detectable. A VLM crop could confirm it if a candidate ROI were supplied by other means.

entries.label: Radial debris ejection
entries.description: Solid fragments thrown outward from a blast on radial trajectories.
entries.frame_evidence: Many non-glowing blobs moving away from a common centre with initially high speed, later curving downward under gravity.
entries.detector_note: Blob tracks in the post-flash window with radial agreement to the blast centre > 0.7; fit each track's vertical component for a downward acceleration term and report the fraction with a > 0.
entries.notes: debris_gravity_fraction near zero (all debris flying in straight lines forever) is a strong CG particle tell and a valuable finding.

entries.label: Expanding fireball
entries.description: A rapidly growing roughly spherical mass of burning gas.
entries.frame_evidence: A fire-coloured region expanding radially at high rate from a point, with strong positive flow divergence and a rolling internal texture.
entries.detector_note: Fire mask area growing > 30% per unique cel for >= 3 cels, with mean flow divergence in the top decile and radial flow agreement to the mask centroid > 0.6.
entries.notes: A fast whip-pan toward a fire produces apparent expansion; the homography-corrected area is required.

entries.label: Explosion flash frame
entries.description: The one or two frames of near-total overexposure at the instant of detonation.
entries.frame_evidence: Global mean luminance spikes far above the shot baseline and a large fraction of pixels clip to maximum, for 1-3 frames only.
entries.detector_note: Per-frame global mean V and clipped-pixel fraction (V >= 250); flag frames where the mean exceeds the shot median by > 3 robust standard deviations and the excursion lasts <= 3 frames.
entries.notes: Lightning, camera flashes, welding arcs and white-flash transitions are identical. This one is measured on ALL container frames, not unique cels, because a flash is often a single inserted drawing.

entries.label: Shockwave ring
entries.description: A thin refractive or dust ring expanding outward from a detonation.
entries.frame_evidence: A faint high-contrast circular arc expanding much faster than the fireball, distorting or brightening what it passes over.
entries.detector_note: Ring detection (cv2.HoughCircles on the Canny of the temporal-difference image) around the fireball centre, requiring an expansion rate at least 2x the fireball's radial growth rate.
entries.notes: Lasts 2-4 frames at most and is often subtle; below 720p and at heavy compression it is usually NOT DETECTABLE.

entries.label: Post-explosion smoke ball
entries.description: The dark churning cloud that replaces the fireball as combustion ends.
entries.frame_evidence: The fire-coloured mask collapses over a few cels while a dark, low-saturation, still-expanding region takes its place at the same location.
entries.detector_note: Detect fire mask area falling while a co-located low-saturation dark region's area rises; report the crossover cel and the spatial overlap (IoU) between the two masks around it.
entries.notes: Depends on both masks; if the shot cuts at the flash this is NOT DETECTABLE.

entries.label: Fire-correlated cast light
entries.description: Surrounding surfaces illuminated by the fire, brightening and dimming in step with it.
entries.frame_evidence: The luminance of nearby non-fire surfaces rises and falls at the same times as the flame's own luminance.
entries.detector_note: Build the per-unique-cel mean luminance series for the fire mask and for an annulus around it (excluding fire pixels); detrend both, then report the Pearson correlation and the lag of the maximum cross-correlation.
entries.notes: A near-zero correlation with an obvious fire present is a strong compositing or animation finding. Requires >= 12 unique cels and a stabilised camera; global exposure changes inflate the correlation, hence the detrend.

entries.label: Flicker-driven shadow movement
entries.description: Shadows cast by firelight shifting and wavering with the flame.
entries.frame_evidence: Shadow boundaries near a fire move slightly in step with flame shape changes while the objects casting them are still.
entries.detector_note: Track the sub-pixel displacement of high-contrast shadow edges (1D cv2.phaseCorrelate on strips perpendicular to the edge) and correlate that displacement series against the flame's orientation or centroid series across unique cels.
entries.notes: Requires still objects and a still camera; sub-pixel displacements are below the compression noise floor at low bitrates.

entries.label: Fire spread rate
entries.description: How fast the burning region grows across the frame.
entries.frame_evidence: The fire mask's total area and its bounding perimeter grow across successive cels.
entries.detector_note: Fit fire_mask_area_frac against the unique-cel index over the shot; report the slope, and separately the advance rate of the mask's leading contour along the growth direction.
entries.notes: A camera push-in inflates the apparent area growth; normalise the area by the homography scale before fitting.

entries.label: Fire present with no cast illumination
entries.description: A visible fire that does not light anything around it - a compositing or animation shortcut.
entries.frame_evidence: A large bright flame sits against surroundings whose luminance neither rises with it nor flickers in step.
entries.detector_note: Take fire_cast_light_flicker's correlation and amplitude, plus the annulus mean luminance versus a matched control annulus far from the fire; flag when the fire mask exceeds 2% of the frame yet the correlation is below the null distribution's 95th percentile.
entries.notes: The null distribution must be built from control annuli in the same shot; without it the correlation number is meaningless. Legitimate in flat-lit 2D styles - report the measurement, not a verdict.

entries.label: Flame colour temperature zones
entries.description: A flame showing distinct colour bands - blue or white at the base, yellow in the body, deep orange or red at the tips.
entries.frame_evidence: Hue varies systematically with height inside a single flame region rather than being one flat colour.
entries.detector_note: Inside the fire mask fit hue and saturation against normalised height with np.polyfit degree 1; report the slopes, the number of distinguishable hue clusters (histogram peak count) and the r2.
entries.notes: zone_count == 1 is precisely what a flat cel-shaded 2D flame produces and is a legitimate finding, not a detector failure.

entries.label: Flame flicker frequency
entries.description: The oscillation rate of a flame's brightness and shape.
entries.frame_evidence: The mean luminance inside the fire mask oscillates over successive unique cels.
entries.detector_note: Build the per-unique-cel mean luminance series inside the fire mask, then scipy.signal.welch to find the dominant frequency; convert cel index to seconds using the measured unique-cel rate, not the container fps.
entries.notes: THE anime trap: computing this on all 24 container frames when only 8-12 are unique drawings halves or thirds the reported frequency. Requires >= 16 unique cels for a usable spectrum.

entries.label: Flame height variation
entries.description: How much the flame's vertical extent changes over time.
entries.frame_evidence: The topmost fire-mask row rises and falls across successive cels while the base stays fixed.
entries.detector_note: Per unique cel record the fire mask's bounding box top and bottom; height = bottom - top; report the coefficient of variation and the base row's stability.
entries.notes: A moving camera moves the base row; stabilise first. A flame_height_cv near zero on a supposedly live fire is a strong tell for a static or cycled element.

entries.label: Flame lean under wind
entries.description: A flame tilted consistently off vertical by airflow.
entries.frame_evidence: The flame's principal axis is persistently rotated away from vertical in one direction rather than oscillating symmetrically.
entries.detector_note: Per unique cel compute the fire mask's skimage regionprops orientation; report the mean deviation from vertical and test whether the distribution's mean differs from zero by more than 2 standard errors.
entries.notes: Perspective and an off-centre flame base bias the principal axis; report the significance test rather than the raw mean alone.

entries.label: Flame tongue / lick
entries.description: An individual elongated flame finger extending from the main flame body.
entries.frame_evidence: A protrusion from the fire mask with high eccentricity and a tapering tip, appearing and retracting within a few cels.
entries.detector_note: Skeletonise the fire mask and count skeleton branches whose length exceeds 1.5x the mask's mean inscribed radius; track branch lifetime across unique cels.
entries.notes: Skeleton branch counts are unstable at low resolution and under motion blur; report the median over the window, not per-cel values.

entries.label: Flame present
entries.description: Visible combustion flame anywhere in the frame.
entries.frame_evidence: A bright, warm-hued region (yellow through deep orange) whose interior luminance fluctuates strongly frame to frame.
entries.detector_note: Fire candidate mask: HSV with H in [0,35] OpenCV units, S > 90, V > 180, plus R > G > B in BGR order; then require the region's per-cel mean luminance std across a 7-unique-cel window to exceed 4% of its mean. Colour alone is not sufficient.
entries.notes: Sunsets, orange signage, tungsten practicals, skin under warm light and orange clothing all pass the colour test; the flicker requirement is the load-bearing part. Static composited flame elements defeat it.

entries.label: Flame transparency
entries.description: Background detail remaining visible through the flame body.
entries.frame_evidence: Edges from the background persist inside the fire region rather than being fully occluded.
entries.detector_note: Correlate the Canny edge map inside the fire mask against the same region from a clean background plate (temporal median of the shot with fire cels excluded); a high correlation indicates transparency.
entries.notes: Requires enough fire-free cels in the shot to build a clean plate; NOT DETECTABLE if the fire is present throughout.

entries.label: Directed flame jet
entries.description: A sustained projected stream of burning fuel.
entries.frame_evidence: A long fire-coloured cone leaving a point source with high axial flow, persisting for many cels.
entries.detector_note: Fire mask with an apex-anchored cone geometry (as in spray_cone_nozzle) plus sustained duration > 10 unique cels and axial flow magnitude in the frame's top decile.
entries.notes: Magical fire-breath effects in animation satisfy the same geometry, which is correct behaviour for this taxonomy - it detects the depiction, not the cause.

entries.label: Visible matte edge on a fluid element
entries.description: A composited fire, smoke, or water element showing a hard rectangular or unnaturally clean boundary.
entries.frame_evidence: The effect region's boundary contains long perfectly straight segments or a sudden opacity cliff inconsistent with a soft fluid edge.
entries.detector_note: Fit lines to the effect's boundary contour; flag straight segments longer than 40px with residual < 1px, and measure the boundary opacity gradient (a matte cliff sits far above the fluid's interior gradient distribution).
entries.notes: An effect legitimately cropped by the frame edge produces straight boundary segments; exclude contour segments within 3px of the frame border.

entries.label: Specific liquid identity (water vs milk vs alcohol vs juice)
entries.description: Which specific liquid a body of fluid actually is, beyond its colour.
entries.frame_evidence: Colour, opacity and viscosity cues that a human reads instantly but that overlap heavily between real liquids under arbitrary lighting and grading.
entries.detector_note: No installed classifier covers liquid material identity, and colour plus opacity statistics are not separable across grades and lighting. A VLM crop question gives an answer but with no measurable reliability on this task.
entries.notes: Logged as a blind spot on purpose. If a VLM is asked anyway, record the answer as an unvalidated hint and never as a finding.

entries.label: Unclassifiable fluid region
entries.description: A region with clear fluid-like motion statistics that cannot be assigned to any specific fluid class.
entries.frame_evidence: Coherent non-rigid deformation with soft boundaries and no colour, shape, or anchor evidence that discriminates between water, smoke, dust, cloth, or foliage.
entries.detector_note: No method available today separates generic non-rigid deformation into fluid classes without either an anchor or a trained classifier we do not have. The entry exists so the analyzer logs the region and its numbers rather than guessing a class.
entries.notes: Deliberately unsupported. Emitting a confident class here is precisely the overclaim to avoid; log the region as a known blind spot.

entries.label: Apparent fluid temperature
entries.description: Whether a liquid is depicted as hot, warm, or cold independently of steam or ice being present.
entries.frame_evidence: There is no direct pixel evidence for temperature; only secondary cues (steam, condensation, ice, glow) which are separately catalogued entries.
entries.detector_note: Temperature is not observable. The analyzer should instead report the co-occurrence of steam_release_wisp, condensation_droplets_cold_surface, ice_surface_present and molten_metal_glow, and leave the inference to a human.
entries.notes: Included so the taxonomy explicitly refuses this rather than inventing a heuristic. Any number reported here would have no null model and no ground truth.

entries.label: Fluid temporal jitter / boiling noise
entries.description: An effect whose detail changes randomly every frame with no coherent motion - denoiser or sampling instability.
entries.frame_evidence: The effect region decorrelates strongly between consecutive frames while its optical flow magnitude is near zero.
entries.detector_note: Compute region decorrelation (1 - NCC) between consecutive unique cels alongside the Farneback mean magnitude; jitter is high decorrelation with near-zero coherent flow. Compare against a static control region for the noise floor.
entries.notes: Film grain and heavy compression produce the same signature everywhere; the control-region comparison is mandatory and is exactly the null model the project lesson demands.

entries.label: Foam dissipation over time
entries.description: Foam gradually shrinking and fading after the event that created it.
entries.frame_evidence: The white foam mask area declines across a shot and its texture coarsens as bubbles pop.
entries.detector_note: Track foam_area_frac across unique cels and fit an exponential decay with scipy.optimize.curve_fit; report the time constant and the fit quality.
entries.notes: Requires a stable camera and a shot long enough (>=15 unique cels) for the fit; otherwise NOT DETECTABLE.

entries.label: Foam / whitewater texture
entries.description: Aerated white liquid with a fine cellular bubble texture.
entries.frame_evidence: A bright desaturated region carrying dense small-scale structure rather than a flat fill.
entries.detector_note: Inside the V>0.75, S<0.20 mask compute skimage.feature.local_binary_pattern uniformity and the high-frequency FFT energy ratio; foam has both high, a flat white fill has both low.
entries.notes: A high foam_flatness_score is exactly how 2D cel foam (flat white shapes) reads - that is a correct and useful distinction, not a failure.

entries.label: Footstep splash in shallow water
entries.description: Water thrown up by a foot striking a puddle or shallow water.
entries.frame_evidence: A burst of bright droplets and a radial ring appearing at a foot's contact point in the frame the foot lands.
entries.detector_note: Use mediapipe pose ankle landmarks 27/28 to define a contact ROI; detect the landing cel as the local minimum of ankle vertical velocity, then apply splash_impact_moment inside that ROI.
entries.notes: mediapipe pose is unreliable on stylised anime bodies, on partial figures and at long-shot scale; when pose confidence for 27/28 is below 0.5 report NOT DETECTABLE rather than NOT FOUND.

entries.label: Fountain jet arc
entries.description: Liquid ejected upward or at an angle following a ballistic arc before falling.
entries.frame_evidence: A bright arced band leaving a nozzle, curving over an apex and descending, persistent across the shot.
entries.detector_note: Fit a parabola to the skeleton of the persistent bright thin region with np.polyfit degree 2; require the quadratic coefficient sign to indicate downward curvature and the fit r2 > 0.85.
entries.notes: Any arced bright line (a cable, a rainbow, a drawn effect line) fits a parabola; require internal flow along the arc via Farneback to confirm it is moving liquid.

entries.label: Freezing front advancing
entries.description: A liquid surface converting to ice with a visible advancing boundary.
entries.frame_evidence: A boundary sweeping across a liquid region, behind which the surface becomes brighter, more textured and stops flowing.
entries.detector_note: Track the boundary between a low-temporal-variance (frozen) region and a high-temporal-variance (liquid) region using per-pixel temporal std over a sliding 5-cel window; the boundary contour's advance rate is the metric.
entries.notes: Fires on any region that simply stops moving (an object coming to rest, a shot going still). Confirm the appearance change (brightness/texture) as well as the motion stop.

entries.label: Frost crystal growth
entries.description: Branching ice crystals spreading across a surface.
entries.frame_evidence: Thin bright dendritic branches extending outward from seed points across successive frames.
entries.detector_note: Skeletonise the thresholded bright thin structures per unique cel; measure total skeleton length and branch-point count increasing monotonically; report the growth rate.
entries.notes: Cracks propagating look identical in skeleton statistics; polarity (bright branches vs dark cracks) is the only cheap separator and it inverts with lighting.

entries.label: Low-lying ground fog
entries.description: A shallow horizontal layer of mist sitting on the ground.
entries.frame_evidence: A band of reduced contrast with a flat top boundary hugging the ground plane, drifting slowly laterally.
entries.detector_note: Contrast-reduction band with a flat upper boundary (line fit residual < 8px), slow lateral flow and no expanding source; distinguish from smoke_ceiling_layering by its position at the bottom of the frame.
entries.notes: Overlaps with the atmospherics domain; emit the same band bbox in both so downstream logic can deduplicate.

entries.label: Heat haze / refractive shimmer
entries.description: Air distortion above a hot surface that wobbles the image behind it.
entries.frame_evidence: A band above a hot surface where background edges wobble laterally frame to frame while the background itself is static.
entries.detector_note: Compute a dense flow field on a static background; a haze band shows small-amplitude (<3px), high-frequency, spatially incoherent flow confined to a horizontal band, with zero net displacement integrated over the shot.
entries.notes: Video compression breathing and film gate weave produce similar small incoherent flow; measure the same statistic on a control band elsewhere in the frame as a null.

entries.label: Ice cracking / fracture propagation
entries.description: New fracture lines appearing and extending through ice.
entries.frame_evidence: Dark thin lines that did not exist in the previous unique cel appear and lengthen across the ice region.
entries.detector_note: Difference the Canny edge maps of consecutive unique cels inside the ice mask; new-edge pixel count and the connected length of new edges per cel are the metrics; require the new edges to persist in following cels.
entries.notes: Any newly revealed texture (a camera move, a dissolve) creates new edges; the persistence requirement and a stabilised camera are mandatory.

entries.label: Ice surface present
entries.description: A solid frozen water surface (sheet ice, ice cubes, a frozen pond).
entries.frame_evidence: A bright, low-saturation, high-specular region with internal fracture lines and no surface flow.
entries.detector_note: Deterministic pre-filter (high V, low S, specular blob density, near-zero internal flow on unique cels), then a VLM crop confirmation.
entries.vlm_question: Is the bright surface in this crop ice? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Snow, glass, white plastic and blown highlights all pass the pre-filter.

entries.label: Dripping icicle
entries.description: Meltwater forming and falling from an icicle tip.
entries.frame_evidence: A small bright blob appears at an icicle's lowest point, grows, then detaches and falls.
entries.detector_note: Apply drip_pendant and drip_detach_event with the ROI anchored to the icicle tip from icicle_present.
entries.notes: Depends on icicle_present; NOT DETECTABLE without it. Very small in wide shots.

entries.label: Icicle present
entries.description: A tapered pendant ice spike hanging from an edge.
entries.frame_evidence: An elongated bright shape attached at its wide top to a horizontal edge, tapering to a point at the bottom.
entries.detector_note: Within the ice candidate mask find components with high eccentricity, principal axis within 20 deg of vertical, width monotonically decreasing downward, and the top touching a horizontal edge contour.
entries.notes: Stalactites, fangs, drips of white paint and certain hair strands satisfy the same shape rule. | TIER CORRECTED by completeness critic: Marked deterministic but gated on masks whose own entries are vlm: fluids_fire.ice_surface_present is vlm and scene_semantics.material_glass_transparent is vlm. A detector cannot be more certain than its own precondition

entries.label: Ignition / first flame
entries.description: The frame at which flame first appears at a location.
entries.frame_evidence: A fire-coloured region with non-zero area appears where the previous unique cels had none, then grows.
entries.detector_note: Track fire_mask_area_frac per unique cel; ignition is the first cel where a new connected fire component exceeds 30px and its area is monotonically non-decreasing over the next 3 unique cels.
entries.notes: A cut to a new shot containing fire also produces a first appearance; run shot-boundary detection first and reset the state at every cut.

entries.label: Lava crust cracking
entries.description: The dark cooled skin on a lava flow splitting to reveal the glowing interior.
entries.frame_evidence: Bright thin lines appearing and widening within a dark crust region across successive cels.
entries.detector_note: Inside the lava mask, difference the bright-thin-structure map (top-hat) between unique cels; measure the new-bright-line length and its widening rate, requiring persistence.
entries.notes: Depends on lava_flow; the same statistic on a general fire mask fires on ordinary flame movement.

entries.label: Lava flow
entries.description: Molten rock advancing as a slow, self-luminous, high-viscosity mass.
entries.frame_evidence: A glowing orange-red region with very slow coherent motion, a dark crust in patches, and almost no flicker.
entries.detector_note: Fire-coloured mask AND low flicker (per-cel luma std < 5% of mean) AND slow coherent flow (magnitude below the frame median, coherence > 0.6) AND a bimodal luminance histogram (glowing channels plus dark crust).
entries.notes: The bimodality term is what separates lava from a plain orange glow; without visible crust it collapses into molten_metal_glow.

entries.label: Lava fountain / spatter
entries.description: Blobs of molten material ejected upward and falling back.
entries.frame_evidence: Glowing blobs on ballistic arcs above a lava source, larger and slower than sparks.
entries.detector_note: Ballistic-arc fitting on glowing blob tracks (as in droplet_ballistic_arc) with a size floor (> 30px) and a low-flicker requirement to exclude sparks.
entries.notes: Small spatter is indistinguishable from spark showers; the size floor is a judgement call, so report the size distribution.

entries.label: Liquid rope coiling
entries.description: A viscous stream buckling into a coil where it meets a surface.
entries.frame_evidence: The stream's lower end traces a small repeating circular path at the landing point.
entries.detector_note: Track the stream's lowest skeleton point; test for periodic circular motion via the autocorrelation of its x and y series and a phase offset near 90 degrees between them.
entries.notes: Requires many unique cels and a close, stable shot; essentially never present in animation. Expect NOT FOUND.

entries.label: Melting progression
entries.description: A solid shrinking as it turns to liquid, with the liquid pool growing.
entries.frame_evidence: A solid region's area declines monotonically across the shot while a wet or pooled region below or around it grows.
entries.detector_note: Segment the solid by its high-V low-S signature and the pool by its specular/dark signature; fit both areas against the unique-cel index with np.polyfit degree 1 and require opposite-signed slopes.
entries.notes: Needs a static camera and a long shot. Anything leaving frame produces a negative area slope - the anticorrelation with a growing pool is what makes this specific.

entries.label: Molten metal / glowing melt
entries.description: A metal or mineral hot enough to emit visible light while flowing.
entries.frame_evidence: A region that is simultaneously very bright, strongly orange-yellow, and flowing with a viscous, slow, coherent motion.
entries.detector_note: Intersect the fire-colour mask (H in 0-30 OpenCV units, S > 100, V > 200) with a low-flicker requirement (temporal luminance std of the region below the flame threshold) and slow coherent flow.
entries.notes: The low-flicker requirement is exactly what separates molten material from flame; sunsets and orange lamps pass the colour test alone.

entries.label: Mud splatter on a surface
entries.description: Discrete dark irregular marks deposited by thrown mud.
entries.frame_evidence: New irregular dark patches appear on a surface between cels and then stay put, moving with the surface.
entries.detector_note: On a homography-stabilised surface, detect new persistent dark components with irregular (low circularity) contours that appear within one or two cels and do not subsequently move relative to the surface.
entries.notes: Identical in signature to blood splatter and to paint; colour is the only separator and it is unreliable under a grade.

entries.label: Viscous mud flow
entries.description: A thick brown slurry moving slowly with a rounded, blunt leading edge.
entries.frame_evidence: A brown mass with slow coherent motion and a smooth, high-radius-of-curvature front.
entries.detector_note: Brown hue band (H 10-25 OpenCV units, S 40-150) with flow coherence > 0.6, flow magnitude below the frame median, and a leading contour whose mean curvature is low; report the front advance rate.
entries.notes: Brown is a very common scene colour; without motion the colour test is worthless. Report the flow terms alongside the mask.

entries.label: Muzzle flash
entries.description: The brief bright star-shaped flame at a firearm's muzzle.
entries.frame_evidence: A small very bright fire-coloured burst lasting 1-2 frames at a fixed point relative to a held object, with a matching illumination spike on nearby surfaces.
entries.detector_note: Single-frame-lifetime high-V fire-coloured blob with radial spikes (polar-unwrap angular maxima >= 3), plus a same-frame luminance rise on the surrounding region; measured on all container frames, not just unique cels.
entries.notes: A lens flare or a single-frame sparkle effect will pass. A flash with no surround_luma_rise is a compositing finding.

entries.label: Oil slick iridescence
entries.description: Thin-film interference colours swirling on an oil-on-water surface.
entries.frame_evidence: Smooth rainbow-like hue bands within a small region, with hue varying continuously across space and shifting over time.
entries.detector_note: Within a candidate region measure hue circular variance (high) together with low luminance variance and a smooth spatial hue gradient (small |grad H| percentiles); require the hue field to change between unique cels.
entries.notes: Lens flares, chromatic aberration fringes and soap bubbles share this signature. Heavy 4:2:0 chroma subsampling destroys the hue detail.

entries.label: Viscous liquid pour
entries.description: A thick liquid (oil, honey, syrup) pouring in a slow, wide, non-breaking stream.
entries.frame_evidence: A pour stream that is wider, slower and does not break into droplets, sometimes coiling where it lands.
entries.detector_note: pour_stream_continuous plus a low flow magnitude (below the frame median), no breakup row detected, and a stream width slope near zero or positive.
entries.notes: The distinction from water is a set of thresholds on continuous quantities, not a classification; report the numbers and let downstream logic decide.

entries.label: Blue gas flame
entries.description: A clean-burning gas flame that is blue rather than orange.
entries.frame_evidence: A small flickering region whose hue sits in the blue band while still showing flame-rate luminance oscillation.
entries.detector_note: Run the flame flicker test on a blue-hue mask (H in 95-130 OpenCV units, S > 100) instead of the warm mask; require flicker amplitude above the noise floor measured on a static control region.
entries.notes: The default fire mask misses this entirely, which is why it needs its own entry. Blue LED practicals and blue screens do not flicker at flame rates but can be animated to.

entries.label: Continuous pour stream
entries.description: An unbroken column of liquid falling from a tilted vessel or a tap.
entries.frame_evidence: A narrow, near-vertical, temporally persistent band connecting a source and a receiving surface, with strong downward flow inside it.
entries.detector_note: Find a thin connected region (skeleton length / mean width > 6) that persists across the window, is oriented within 30 deg of vertical, and has mean downward flow well above the frame median.
entries.notes: A transparent stream over a busy background often fails to threshold at all; use the flow-magnitude channel rather than intensity for glass-clear liquids.

entries.label: Puddle present
entries.description: A shallow standing pool of water on a ground surface.
entries.frame_evidence: An irregular darker patch on the ground that is more specular than its surround and carries reflected content.
entries.detector_note: On a ground-plane region find components darker than the local median but containing a higher specular-highlight density, and whose content correlates with a vertically flipped patch of the scene above (reuse the reflection correlation test).
entries.notes: Shadows are also darker patches; the specular density and reflection correlation are the separators, and both are weak on matte-shaded 2D backgrounds.

entries.label: Sinking into a viscous medium
entries.description: A body slowly descending into mud, quicksand, tar, or slime.
entries.frame_evidence: An object's visible height above the medium's surface decreases monotonically while its horizontal position stays roughly fixed.
entries.detector_note: For a human, use mediapipe pose to measure the visible landmark count and the lowest visible landmark index over the shot; sinking shows a monotonic loss of lower-body landmarks with a stable horizontal centroid.
entries.notes: Occlusion by any foreground object produces the same landmark loss, and mediapipe on partially buried, stylised figures is unreliable.

entries.label: Rain density
entries.description: How heavy the rain is, as visible streak coverage.
entries.frame_evidence: The proportion of the frame occupied by rain streaks and the count of streaks per unit area.
entries.detector_note: Rain line count per megapixel and total rain-line pixel area fraction from the same Hough pass; report per unique cel and take the shot median.
entries.notes: Sensitive to the Hough threshold; report the threshold used with the metric so runs are comparable.

entries.label: Rain impact rings on standing water
entries.description: Many small concentric ripples appearing where raindrops strike a puddle or pool.
entries.frame_evidence: A scatter of tiny expanding rings appearing and vanishing across a water surface, several per frame.
entries.detector_note: Apply ripple_concentric with a small radius range (2-15px) and a high permitted count; report the event rate per unique cel per unit water area.
entries.notes: Below about 480p these rings are 2-3px and undetectable. Rain in the air over a glassy puddle is a common CG omission - that absence is a genuine finding.

entries.label: Rain micro-splashes on ground
entries.description: Tiny upward bursts where raindrops hit a hard surface.
entries.frame_evidence: A shimmering carpet of very small transient bright specks on a ground plane, each lasting one or two frames.
entries.detector_note: Count single-cel-lifetime bright blobs (< 20px) on a ground-plane region; a high count with near-zero persistence and no coherent flow direction scores the entry.
entries.notes: Indistinguishable from sensor noise or heavy grain by these statistics alone; measure a control region under shelter if one exists.

entries.label: Airborne rain streaks
entries.description: Falling rain rendered as elongated streaks through the air.
entries.frame_evidence: Many thin near-parallel elongated bright or dark lines with a shared orientation, changing position every frame.
entries.detector_note: cv2.HoughLinesP on the temporal-difference image; require >= 20 lines, orientation std < 15 deg, and line length 5-60px; measure the fraction of lines that do not persist between unique cels (rain is transient).
entries.notes: Film scratches, dust on the print and hatching in 2D art are also parallel lines but persist or are static; the transience requirement handles it. Very light rain falls below the Hough threshold entirely.

entries.label: Reflection wobble / distortion
entries.description: The reflected image is broken up and displaced by surface ripples.
entries.frame_evidence: Vertical smearing and lateral jitter of reflected features that changes between frames while the source object above stays still.
entries.detector_note: Compute per-row horizontal displacement between the flipped source strip and the reflection strip via 1D cv2.phaseCorrelate per row; wobble amplitude = std of that displacement profile; wobble rate = its temporal change across unique cels while the source rows are static.
entries.notes: If the source object is itself moving the statistic is meaningless; a source-static check must pass first.

entries.label: Missing or inconsistent reflection
entries.description: An object that should reflect in a visible water surface has no reflection, or one that contradicts its position.
entries.frame_evidence: A prominent object stands at the waterline yet the strip below it correlates no better with the flipped object than with an unrelated patch.
entries.detector_note: For each object anchored at the waterline, compare reflection_correlation against a null distribution built from 20 randomly offset flipped patches of the same size from the same shot; flag when the true correlation does not exceed the null 95th percentile.
entries.notes: This is the entry that needs the null model most: raw correlation numbers on textured water are meaningless without it. Stylised 2D art legitimately omits reflections - report the measurement, not a verdict.

entries.label: Refraction offset at the waterline
entries.description: A partially submerged straight object appears bent or laterally displaced where it crosses the surface.
entries.frame_evidence: An object's edge line has a visible kink exactly at the waterline row, with the submerged portion offset sideways and often magnified.
entries.detector_note: Fit separate lines (cv2.fitLine) to the object's dominant edge above and below the waterline row; report the angle difference and the lateral offset at the junction; require the junction to lie within 4px of the detected waterline.
entries.notes: Only works on objects with a long straight edge. Motion blur and low resolution destroy the fit. Absence of a kink is a legitimate CG shortcut and a real finding.

entries.label: Concentric ripple rings
entries.description: Circular waves expanding outward from a point disturbance on a calm surface.
entries.frame_evidence: Two or more near-concentric bright/dark arcs sharing a centre, with radii increasing monotonically across frames.
entries.detector_note: cv2.HoughCircles(minDist small, param2 low) on the Canny map of the water mask across a short window; group circles by centre proximity (<8px) and fit radius(t) by least squares; require dr/dt > 0.
entries.notes: HoughCircles is noisy on textured water; the monotonic-radius fit (r2 > 0.8) is the real discriminator. In 2D animation ripples are often drawn as ellipses in perspective and Hough will miss them entirely.

entries.label: Wind chop / surface texture
entries.description: Fine, high-frequency, non-directional surface roughness driven by wind rather than a point impact.
entries.frame_evidence: Dense small-scale luminance variance across the whole water region with no dominant ring or wave structure.
entries.detector_note: Band-pass energy of the water region: ratio of high-frequency FFT energy (radial bins above 0.25 Nyquist) to total, plus cv2.Laplacian(region, cv2.CV_64F).var(); temporally the texture decorrelates fast (normalised cross-correlation between unique cels < 0.5).
entries.notes: Sensor noise and heavy film grain raise the same statistic; measure grain on a static non-water region and subtract it as a floor.

entries.label: River current streaklines
entries.description: Elongated surface streaks that trace the current of a flowing river or channel.
entries.frame_evidence: Anisotropic elongated bright/dark bands aligned with the flow axis, persisting and translating over several frames.
entries.detector_note: skimage.filters.frangi or a bank of oriented cv2.getGaborKernel responses inside the water mask; streak orientation histogram compared against the Farneback dominant direction; agreement within 20 deg scores the entry.
entries.notes: Wood grain, brushed metal and hatching in 2D art produce identical Gabor anisotropy; the flow-agreement term is what separates them.

entries.label: Runoff rivulet on a surface
entries.description: A thin stream of liquid running down a solid vertical or sloped surface.
entries.frame_evidence: A narrow darker or more specular line on a surface, extending downward over successive frames with a moving leading tip.
entries.detector_note: Track the tip of a thin dark/specular line: threshold the difference against a running median background of the surface, skeletonize, and follow the lowest skeleton endpoint's downward displacement per unique cel.
entries.notes: Requires a static or homography-stabilised surface. Scratches and painted lines are static and will be rejected by the tip-motion requirement.

entries.label: Shoreline swash / run-up
entries.description: Thin water sheet running up and retreating down a beach or bank.
entries.frame_evidence: A moving boundary line between wet (darker, more specular) and dry substrate that advances then reverses within a short window.
entries.detector_note: Track the wet/dry boundary as the largest luminance step contour in a rectified strip; fit boundary position over time and detect a sign change in its velocity (advance followed by retreat).
entries.notes: Requires a roughly static camera; pan/tilt must be stabilised first or the boundary motion is the camera.

entries.label: Fluid scale mismatch (miniature look)
entries.description: Water or fire whose droplet size, speed and detail scale contradict the depicted size of the scene.
entries.frame_evidence: Droplets are enormous relative to the depicted objects, and the fluid moves too slowly or too fast for its apparent scale.
entries.detector_note: Emit the deterministic supporting numbers (droplet median area relative to a reference object's size, mean vertical acceleration in px per cel squared), then ask a VLM on a crop containing both the fluid and a scale reference.
entries.vlm_question: Does the water in this crop look like real full-size water, or like a small-scale miniature? Answer real, miniature, or unclear.
entries.notes: Genuinely hard: the physical judgement needs a scale reference we cannot reliably identify. Expect low confidence and log it as such.

entries.label: Particle popping / sudden appearance
entries.description: Simulation particles appearing or vanishing abruptly instead of fading in or out.
entries.frame_evidence: Individual droplets, sparks or smoke puffs appear at full opacity in one frame with no precursor in the previous frame.
entries.detector_note: For each tracked particle examine its first and last few cels: a popped particle reaches > 80% of its peak area and brightness within one cel; report the fraction of tracks that pop rather than fade.
entries.notes: On 2s/3s animation everything appears in one unique cel by construction, so this is only meaningful when cel_effect_hold_cadence reports 1s. Report NOT DETECTABLE otherwise.

entries.label: Billboard sprite flatness
entries.description: Volumetric-looking smoke or fire that is actually flat cards always facing the camera.
entries.frame_evidence: During a camera move the effect's internal parallax is zero while the surrounding geometry parallaxes normally.
entries.detector_note: Estimate the scene homography from background features during a camera move, then measure the residual flow inside the effect region after applying it; a billboard shows near-zero residual parallax while true volume shows depth-dependent residual.
entries.notes: Requires a real camera move; on a locked-off shot this is NOT DETECTABLE. Smoke genuinely far away also has near-zero parallax.

entries.label: Volumetric ray-march banding
entries.description: Concentric or planar stepping artefacts inside volumetric smoke or fog from too few ray-march samples.
entries.frame_evidence: Regularly spaced faint luminance bands within a smoke or god-ray region, at a constant spatial period.
entries.detector_note: Take a 1D FFT along the estimated view direction through the volumetric region; banding shows a sharp isolated spatial-frequency peak well above the surrounding spectrum.
entries.notes: Distinct from codec banding, which aligns to luminance quantisation levels rather than to a view direction; check whether the peak moves with the camera.

entries.label: Water/solid interpenetration
entries.description: Simulated liquid visibly passing through a solid object instead of colliding with it.
entries.frame_evidence: Liquid pixels appear on the far side of an object's silhouette with no occlusion boundary, and flow vectors cross the object edge unchanged.
entries.detector_note: Deterministically find flow vectors inside the water mask that cross a strong static object edge without a magnitude discontinuity, then crop that boundary and ask a VLM. The deterministic part alone has too many false positives from transparency and reflection.
entries.vlm_question: Does the liquid in this crop pass through the solid object instead of flowing around it? Answer yes, no, or unclear.
entries.notes: Under-constrained and a genuine weak spot; even a strong VLM struggles on tight crops without depth context.

entries.label: Gentle simmer
entries.description: Occasional isolated bubbles breaking a mostly calm heated surface.
entries.frame_evidence: Sparse, intermittent small disturbances against an otherwise quiet liquid surface.
entries.detector_note: Same statistics as rolling boil but with boil_intensity in a low band and a burst-like temporal profile: count discrete surface-disturbance events per unique cel via connected components on the thresholded temporal difference.
entries.notes: The boundary between simmer and rolling boil is a threshold choice; report the continuous boil_intensity and let downstream logic bin it.

entries.label: Viscous filaments / strings
entries.description: Thin strands connecting two separating masses of a sticky substance.
entries.frame_evidence: One or more very thin bright or dark lines spanning the gap between two blobs that are moving apart.
entries.detector_note: After a connected-component split, run a ridge filter (skimage.filters.meijering) in the gap between the child components and count ridges whose endpoints lie on the two components.
entries.notes: Sub-pixel filaments vanish under compression, and any background line crossing the gap is counted. Low confidence by construction.

entries.label: Slime ooze / stretch
entries.description: A highly viscous, elastic substance stretching and sagging under gravity.
entries.frame_evidence: A mass with a smooth glossy surface elongating downward and thinning in the middle over many cels without breaking.
entries.detector_note: Track a region's bounding-box aspect ratio increasing while its minimum internal width (distance-transform minimum along the skeleton) decreases, with the region remaining connected throughout.
entries.notes: Requires the substance to be segmentable, which usually means a distinctive colour; on a busy background this is NOT DETECTABLE.

entries.label: Liquid smear / multiple frame
entries.description: A single drawing that stretches or multiplies the fluid to imply extreme speed.
entries.frame_evidence: One frame shows an anomalously elongated or repeated version of the effect shape between two normal frames.
entries.detector_note: Detect a single unique cel whose effect-region eccentricity or area exceeds the neighbouring cels' by > 2.5x and which is not repeated in the following cels.
entries.notes: Compression ghosting and dropped frames produce similar single-frame anomalies; verify by inspecting the flagged cel.

entries.label: Backlit volumetric smoke
entries.description: Smoke illuminated from behind or within, revealing light shafts and internal density variation.
entries.frame_evidence: Bright ray-like structures within a smoke region converging toward a light source, with strong luminance variation inside the smoke.
entries.detector_note: Inside the smoke mask run cv2.HoughLinesP on the top-hat map and test whether the lines converge on a common point (least-squares intersection residual small); report the convergence point and the internal luminance std.
entries.notes: Overlaps with the lighting domain's crepuscular-ray entries; report the same convergence point in both so they can be reconciled.

entries.label: Turbulent billowing smoke
entries.description: Smoke rolling in large mushrooming eddies rather than rising smoothly.
entries.frame_evidence: Large-scale curling structures inside the smoke mass, with alternating-sign curl regions and rapidly changing internal texture.
entries.detector_note: Inside the smoke mask count curl-sign-alternating regions above a magnitude threshold and measure internal texture decorrelation between unique cels; billowing scores high on both.
entries.notes: 2D cel smoke drawn as flat overlapping circles gives near-zero internal decorrelation with a high visual billow - the metric and the appearance disagree, which is itself worth recording.

entries.label: Smoke layering under a ceiling
entries.description: Smoke accumulating in a flat horizontal stratum at the top of an enclosed space.
entries.frame_evidence: A horizontally elongated smoke band with a sharp flat lower boundary near the top of frame, descending slowly over the shot.
entries.detector_note: Fit a horizontal line to the smoke mask's lower boundary (residual < 6px indicates a flat layer) and track that line's vertical position across unique cels.
entries.notes: Very rarely animated; expect NOT FOUND. A horizontal haze gradient in an exterior can mimic it.

entries.label: Smoke colour (black vs white)
entries.description: Whether the smoke is dark (rich, sooty combustion) or light (steam-like, cool combustion).
entries.frame_evidence: The smoke region's mean luminance sits clearly below or clearly above the local background luminance.
entries.detector_note: Mean V inside the smoke mask minus the mean V of a surrounding annulus; report the signed difference and the within-mask luminance spread.
entries.notes: Backlighting inverts the sign; record the estimated light direction if available or mark the reading as lighting-dependent.

entries.label: Smoke dissipation rate
entries.description: How fast smoke thins and disappears into the background.
entries.frame_evidence: The smoke region's opacity (its difference from the clean background) declines while its area grows.
entries.detector_note: With a clean plate (temporal median over smoke-free cels), compute mean |frame - plate| inside the smoke mask per unique cel and fit an exponential decay; report tau alongside the area growth slope.
entries.notes: Requires smoke-free cels for a clean plate. Smoke that vanishes abruptly (tau near zero, no fade) is an animation shortcut and a legitimate finding.

entries.label: Contrast loss behind smoke
entries.description: Background detail measurably washing out where smoke passes in front of it.
entries.frame_evidence: A region's local contrast drops relative to a clean plate exactly where the smoke mask is, and recovers when the smoke leaves.
entries.detector_note: With a clean plate, compute local contrast (skimage.filters.rank.entropy or local std) inside vs outside the smoke mask, and confirm recovery in cels after the smoke moves on.
entries.notes: A smoke element composited over a plate WITHOUT any contrast reduction (drop ratio ~1.0) is a compositing finding: the smoke reads as a decal, not a volume.

entries.label: Smoke plume column
entries.description: A coherent vertical column of smoke rising from a source.
entries.frame_evidence: A tall region with a stable base, upward internal flow, and width increasing with height.
entries.detector_note: On the smoke candidate mask fit width against height with np.polyfit degree 1 (expect a positive slope), require mean upward flow, and check base-centroid stability across unique cels.
entries.notes: A negative width slope (a plume that narrows as it rises) is physically wrong and worth flagging as a finding.

entries.label: Smoke present
entries.description: Visible combustion smoke anywhere in the frame.
entries.frame_evidence: A low-saturation grey region with soft boundaries that reduces local contrast where it overlaps the background, and drifts and expands over time.
entries.detector_note: Deterministic pre-filter: S < 0.20, local entropy below the shot median, soft gradient boundary, positive flow divergence, area changing across unique cels. Confirm with a VLM crop, because steam, fog, dust and haze share every one of those numbers.
entries.vlm_question: Is there smoke in this crop? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Do not report smoke on the deterministic statistics alone; that is exactly the overclaim this taxonomy is meant to avoid. Record the pre-filter numbers even when the VLM says no.

entries.label: Thin smoke wisp
entries.description: A narrow, sinuous ribbon of smoke, typical of a cigarette, an extinguished wick, or a smouldering point.
entries.frame_evidence: A thin curving semi-transparent line rising from a small source, wavering laterally as it goes.
entries.detector_note: skimage.filters.meijering or frangi ridge filter on the smoke candidate region; keep ridges with width < 8px and length > 40px whose lower endpoint is stable across cels (the source) while the upper part wanders.
entries.notes: Hair strands, wires and thin scratches produce the same ridges; the source-stability plus upper-wander asymmetry is the discriminator.

entries.label: Smoke or steam with no visible source
entries.description: A vapour effect whose emission point is not attached to any object or fire in frame.
entries.frame_evidence: A plume's base sits in empty space or drifts freely rather than remaining anchored to a surface or a fire region.
entries.detector_note: Take the plume base from smoke_plume_column and test whether it lies within 10px of the fire mask, a surface contour, or any strong static edge; report the distance to the nearest candidate anchor.
entries.notes: An off-screen source is a perfectly legitimate composition; this measures anchoring, not correctness. Report the distance and let a human judge.

entries.label: Sparks bouncing off surfaces
entries.description: Spark particles rebounding from a floor or wall rather than passing through it.
entries.frame_evidence: A spark track shows an abrupt direction change at a surface with a reduced outgoing speed.
entries.detector_note: On spark tracks detect direction discontinuities > 60 deg accompanied by a speed drop > 20%; report the count and whether the discontinuity points lie on a common line (cv2.fitLine residual).
entries.notes: Requires resolvable multi-cel spark tracks; at typical spark speeds and 2s animation this is often only 2 samples per track and the fit is meaningless.

entries.label: Spark shower
entries.description: A burst of many bright hot particles ejected from an impact, grinding, or short circuit.
entries.frame_evidence: A dense fan of very bright small streaks radiating from a single point over a handful of frames.
entries.detector_note: Detect a burst of high-V small elongated blobs whose orientations all point away from a common apex (angular residual to the radial direction < 20 deg for > 70% of blobs); require the event to last < 20 unique cels.
entries.notes: Fireworks, muzzle flash debris and lens-flare artefacts share this signature. The bounded duration separates a shower from a sustained spray.

entries.label: Specular glitter / sun path
entries.description: The scattered field of bright specular points where a light source reflects off a rippled surface.
entries.frame_evidence: Many small blown-out points clustered along an axis pointing toward the light, twinkling on and off between frames.
entries.detector_note: Threshold V>250 inside the water mask, label with skimage.measure.label, keep components < 40px area; fit a principal axis to the component centroids (PCA) and measure per-component temporal on/off rate across unique cels.
entries.notes: Christmas lights, bokeh and sensor hot pixels also produce small blown points; the elongated axis plus the twinkle rate is the discriminator.

entries.label: Rebound column / Worthington jet
entries.description: The narrow vertical liquid column that shoots up after the crown collapses.
entries.frame_evidence: A tall thin bright vertical structure rising from the impact centre several frames after impact, often with a droplet pinching off the top.
entries.detector_note: Track the maximum vertical extent of connected bright pixels above the impact centre across the post-impact window; a jet is a single-peaked rise-and-fall profile with width/height < 0.3.
entries.notes: Frequently omitted entirely in 2D and in low-budget CG - a legitimate NOT FOUND. Do not confuse with a vertical spark or a rising ember.

entries.label: Splash crown / coronet
entries.description: The ring of upward liquid spikes around an impact point.
