entries.frame_evidence: A radially symmetric ring of thin upward-pointing bright spikes surrounding a central depression, 1-4 frames after impact.
entries.detector_note: In the post-impact ROI, polar-unwrap around the impact centre (cv2.warpPolar) and count angular maxima in the radial-extent profile; a crown scores >= 5 maxima with roughly even angular spacing.
entries.notes: Needs the impact centre from splash_impact_moment. Off-axis camera angles break the radial symmetry assumption; report angular regularity rather than gating on it.

entries.label: Splash impact frame
entries.description: The single frame in which an object first contacts a liquid surface.
entries.frame_evidence: An abrupt appearance of high-frequency bright structure at the contact point, with the object's downward motion arrested in the same window.
entries.detector_note: Detect the frame where the local Laplacian variance in a small ROI at the object's leading point jumps > 4x its trailing 5-cel median, coincident with a sign change or magnitude drop in the object's tracked vertical velocity.
entries.notes: Requires an object track. In 2D animation the impact is often a single smear or impact-flash drawing, which spikes the same statistic for the wrong reason - inspect the flagged frame.

entries.label: Liquid sheet / lamella
entries.description: A thin continuous curved sheet of liquid thrown out by an impact or a swipe through liquid.
entries.frame_evidence: A smooth curved bright region with a thin, sometimes scalloped free edge, semi-transparent to the background.
entries.detector_note: Detect regions where background structure is still correlated through the region (against a temporal-median clean plate) bounded by a smooth low-curvature-variance contour from cv2.findContours.
entries.notes: Transparency estimation without a clean plate is unreliable; when no static background is available downgrade this to a VLM crop check.

entries.label: Nozzle spray cone
entries.description: A widening conical spray from a hose, aerosol, or sprinkler.
entries.frame_evidence: A triangular haze widening away from a point source, with flow vectors diverging from that apex.
entries.detector_note: Locate the flow-divergence source by finding the point minimising the angular residual of flow vectors to radial directions; fit the region's opening angle from the convex hull; require monotonic width increase with distance from the apex.
entries.notes: Shares its signature with a smoke jet and with an explosion's early frames; the sustained duration over the shot separates spray from a one-shot burst.

entries.label: Spray / atomised mist
entries.description: A diffuse cloud of very small airborne water droplets.
entries.frame_evidence: A soft, low-contrast, bright, fast-expanding haze with no distinct particle edges.
entries.detector_note: Region with positive flow divergence, contrast (skimage.filters.rank.entropy) below the shot median, brightness above it, and area growth over the window; expansion rate from the convex hull area of the thresholded region.
entries.notes: Statistically near-identical to light-coloured smoke and to dust; only context (proximity to a splash or a water region) separates them. Flag the ambiguity rather than asserting water.

entries.label: Standing wave / rapids
entries.description: A wave that holds a fixed spatial position while water flows through it.
entries.frame_evidence: A bright crest structure that does not translate across frames while the surface texture around it clearly does.
entries.detector_note: Compare the crest ridge track velocity (near zero) against the local Farneback mean magnitude (clearly non-zero) inside the same ROI; flag when |crest_speed| < 0.2 * flow_mag_mean.
entries.notes: A duplicated cel makes both terms zero and the ratio undefined; skip frames that are not unique cels.

entries.label: Pressurised steam jet
entries.description: A fast, narrow, high-velocity vapour jet from a kettle spout, valve, or pipe.
entries.frame_evidence: A narrow high-speed white plume leaving a small aperture with a straight initial section before it breaks up.
entries.detector_note: Cone/jet detection with a small apex aperture, high flow magnitude near the apex (top decile of the frame), and an initially low opening angle (< 20 deg) that widens with distance.
entries.notes: Shares its signature with a spray cone and with a smoke jet; the anchor (kettle, pipe) must come from a VLM or be supplied.

entries.label: Steam wisp above hot liquid
entries.description: Thin white vapour curling upward from a hot surface or vessel.
entries.frame_evidence: A faint, low-contrast, low-saturation plume immediately above a liquid or vessel, moving upward and dissipating within the frame.
entries.detector_note: Above a candidate vessel/liquid region, detect a low-contrast bright region with mean upward flow, positive divergence, and monotonically decreasing opacity (difference from a running background median) with height.
entries.notes: Pixel statistics cannot separate steam from smoke. Assignment to steam rests entirely on the spatial anchor (a hot liquid or vessel below) - record which anchor was used.

entries.label: Steam / smoke ambiguity flag
entries.description: An explicit flag that a detected vapour region cannot be classified as steam, smoke, dust, or fog on pixel evidence.
entries.frame_evidence: A low-contrast diffuse expanding region with no unambiguous source anchor in frame.
entries.detector_note: When a vapour region is detected without a confident source anchor, emit this flag and send a tight crop of the region plus its base to the VLM.
entries.vlm_question: Is the cloudy substance in this crop smoke from something burning, steam from something hot, or dust? Answer smoke, steam, dust, or unclear.
entries.notes: This entry exists so the analyzer records a known blind spot instead of guessing. A small VLM will still guess confidently - treat its answer as a hint, not ground truth.

entries.label: Stream breakup into drops
entries.description: A falling stream destabilising and separating into discrete droplets (Plateau-Rayleigh).
entries.frame_evidence: The lower part of a stream shows periodic bulges then separates into a chain of individual drops.
entries.detector_note: Along the stream skeleton measure width(row); detect periodicity via FFT of the width profile, then detect the row below which the mask becomes disconnected (label count > 1 per row band).
entries.notes: Requires enough resolution that individual drops span >3px; usually NOT DETECTABLE below 720p or in stylised 2D.

entries.label: Stream narrowing under gravity
entries.description: A falling stream thins as it accelerates downward.
entries.frame_evidence: The stream's measured width decreases monotonically from source to landing point.
entries.detector_note: Measure the stream mask width per row from the distance transform; fit width vs row with np.polyfit degree 1; report slope and r2. A physically plausible pour has a negative slope.
entries.notes: A constant-width stream (slope ~0) is a common 2D and cheap-CG simplification and is a genuine finding. Perspective foreshortening can invert the sign.

entries.label: Mirror reflection in still water
entries.description: A near-perfect inverted image of the scene above the waterline.
entries.frame_evidence: The region below the waterline is an approximate vertical mirror of the region above it, usually darker and slightly desaturated.
entries.detector_note: Take the strip above the waterline, cv2.flip(strip,0), and run cv2.matchTemplate(TM_CCOEFF_NORMED) against the strip below; report the peak correlation and the vertical offset of the peak.
entries.notes: Needs a reliable waterline row. A high correlation from a symmetric composition (an archway, a symmetric face) is a real false positive; require the luma ratio below 1.0 as a second condition.

entries.label: Meniscus / surface tension curve
entries.description: The curved liquid edge where a liquid meets a container wall or an object.
entries.frame_evidence: A thin curved bright or dark line hugging the container wall, curving up or down over a few pixels at the liquid edge.
entries.detector_note: Too small and too context-dependent for a reliable pixel rule; crop the liquid-container junction (from the waterline row plus the container edge) and ask a VLM. Emit the crop coordinates so the finding is auditable.
entries.vlm_question: In this close-up, does the liquid surface curve upward where it touches the container wall? Answer yes, no, or unclear.
entries.notes: Almost never drawn in 2D animation; frequently omitted in CG. A no answer at low resolution means nothing - gate on crop size >= 96px.

entries.label: Torch flame trailing a moving source
entries.description: A carried flame stretched and dragged behind the direction of travel.
entries.frame_evidence: The flame's principal axis leans opposite to the tracked motion of its base, and its elongation increases with the base's speed.
entries.detector_note: Track the fire mask base centroid; correlate mean_lean_deg against the base velocity direction across the shot; report the correlation coefficient and the elongation-vs-speed slope.
entries.notes: A flame that does not respond to its carrier's motion (correlation near zero) is a common animation shortcut and a good finding.

entries.label: Turbidity / suspended particulate
entries.description: Water carrying visible suspended sediment or particles that reduce clarity.
entries.frame_evidence: Submerged detail loses contrast rapidly with depth, and small drifting specks are visible in the water volume.
entries.detector_note: Measure contrast falloff with the depth proxy plus small-blob count (skimage.feature.blob_log, sigma 1-3) inside the water region whose motion is decoupled from the surface flow field.
entries.notes: Compression mosquito noise around edges is counted as particulate at low bitrates; measure the blob count on a clean static region as a floor.

entries.label: Underwater / submerged camera
entries.description: The camera is beneath the water surface.
entries.frame_evidence: Global blue-green colour cast, reduced contrast with distance, suspended particulate, and often caustic light bands and rising bubbles.
entries.detector_note: Pre-filter deterministically (global hue mean in the cyan band, saturation elevated, contrast falling with an image-space depth proxy), then confirm with a VLM crop question. Emit the pre-filter numbers regardless.
entries.vlm_question: Was this picture taken underwater? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: A heavy teal colour grade produces the same deterministic signature; the VLM confirmation is load-bearing.

entries.label: Vehicle spray from wet road
entries.description: A rooster tail or sheet of water thrown by wheels on a wet surface.
entries.frame_evidence: A bright fan of spray trailing a moving vehicle's wheels, locked to the vehicle's motion.
entries.detector_note: Needs a vehicle or wheel detector to anchor the ROI; we have no object detector installed (no ultralytics/YOLO). Without an anchor the spray region is indistinguishable from generic dust or mist.
entries.notes: Log as not-detectable. Would become deterministic given any wheel bbox source.

entries.label: Kelvin wake (V pattern)
entries.description: The V-shaped pair of wave arms trailing a body moving through water.
entries.frame_evidence: Two roughly straight bright lines diverging behind a moving object at a near-constant half-angle.
entries.detector_note: cv2.HoughLinesP on the Canny edges of the water mask behind the moving object; keep line pairs whose apex lies within 30px of the object's trailing point and whose half-angle is 15-25 deg; require the apex to track the object across frames.
entries.notes: Needs an already-localised moving object; without one this fires on any two lines. In 2D animation wakes are frequently drawn at physically wrong angles - report the measured angle, do not gate on 19.47 deg.

entries.label: Water body present
entries.description: A region of the frame is liquid water (sea, lake, river, pool, puddle, vessel contents).
entries.frame_evidence: A large contiguous region with low-frequency luminance structure, blue/green-shifted hue relative to the scene mean, and specular highlights inconsistent with a matte surface.
entries.detector_note: Segment candidate regions deterministically (HSV hue 85-130 in OpenCV units OR high specular-highlight density via V>240 blobs), then confirm semantics with vlm_inspector.py on a tight crop of the largest candidate region. Do NOT call hue alone 'water'.
entries.vlm_question: Is there liquid water visible in this crop? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Blue sky, blue cloth, blue-graded night scenes and glass all fire the deterministic pre-filter. The pre-filter is a recall stage only; precision comes from the VLM.

entries.label: Depth colour gradient
entries.description: Water darkens and shifts hue with depth or distance from shore.
entries.frame_evidence: A monotonic luminance and hue gradient across the water region, typically light near the shoreline and dark toward deep water.
entries.detector_note: Fit a linear model of V and H against the distance-transform from the water mask boundary (scipy.ndimage.distance_transform_edt); report slope and r2.
entries.notes: A vignette or a graded sky reflection produces the same gradient; the distance-transform anchoring reduces but does not eliminate this.

entries.label: Flow field coherence
entries.description: How laminar versus turbulent the water motion is inside the region.
entries.frame_evidence: Neighbouring surface patches move in near-identical directions (laminar) or in scattered, conflicting directions (turbulent).
entries.detector_note: On the Farneback field inside the mask compute per-pixel angular deviation from the local 15px mean direction; coherence = 1 - circular_variance. Also emit curl std from np.gradient(vy,axis=1)-np.gradient(vx,axis=0).
entries.notes: Needs a null model: run the same statistic on a time-shuffled frame pair from the same shot; report the measured value only as a ratio to that null.

entries.label: Water flow direction
entries.description: The dominant translation direction of a moving body of water within its region.
entries.frame_evidence: Consistent displacement of surface texture across a frame pair in one dominant direction.
entries.detector_note: cv2.calcOpticalFlowFarneback(prev,next,None,0.5,3,15,3,5,1.2,0) restricted to the water mask; dominant direction = circular mean of arctan2(vy,vx) weighted by |v|; report resultant length R as directionality.
entries.notes: MUST be computed between consecutive UNIQUE cels (dedupe with mean abs frame diff < 0.5/255) or 2s/3s animation returns an artefactual zero. Camera motion must be subtracted using a background-plate homography (cv2.estimateAffinePartial2D on ORB matches outside the water mask).

entries.label: Waterfall base mist
entries.description: The diffuse aerated cloud rising from where a falling water sheet lands.
entries.frame_evidence: A soft-edged low-contrast bright haze at the foot of a falling-water region, with upward and outward slow motion.
entries.detector_note: Below the fall region, detect a zone of reduced local contrast (skimage.filters.rank.entropy drop > 25% vs the shot median) with positive flow divergence and a small upward component; anchor spatially to the fall region base.
entries.notes: Indistinguishable from generic fog/haze without the spatial anchor to a fall region; if fluids_fire.waterfall_curtain is NOT FOUND this must be reported NOT DETECTABLE, not NOT FOUND.

entries.label: Waterfall curtain
entries.description: A continuous falling sheet of water from a lip or edge.
entries.frame_evidence: A vertically elongated bright region with strongly downward-biased optical flow and vertical streak texture.
entries.detector_note: Region with flow direction within 20 deg of straight down, magnitude above the shot's 90th percentile, and vertical Gabor response dominating horizontal by >2x; require aspect ratio height/width > 1.5.
entries.notes: Vertical rain and vertical wipes/whip-pans produce the same signature; check that the region is spatially static while its content moves.

entries.label: Waterline on a body or object
entries.description: The line where an object enters the water surface.
entries.frame_evidence: A horizontal discontinuity across an object's silhouette where texture, colour and sharpness change abruptly.
entries.detector_note: Within an object bbox, find the row with maximum horizontally-summed gradient magnitude and a step change in mean saturation between the strips above and below it; validate that the same row aligns with the surrounding water-mask boundary within 5px.
entries.notes: Fails on foamy or splashing entry where the boundary is genuinely diffuse; also needs an object bbox, which for humans can come from mediapipe pose but for anything else has no source.

entries.label: Backlit wave translucency
entries.description: Light passing through the thin part of a wave, making it glow green or blue from within.
entries.frame_evidence: The upper interior of a crest is brighter and more saturated than both the water below it and the sky behind it.
entries.detector_note: Inside a detected crest ROI compare mean saturation and V against the water region mean and against the region directly above the crest; flag when crest saturation exceeds both by > 15%.
entries.notes: Depends entirely on fluids_fire.wave_crest having found a crest; NOT DETECTABLE when it has not.

entries.label: Breaking wave / whitewater
entries.description: A wave crest collapsing into aerated white foam.
entries.frame_evidence: A high-luminance, low-saturation, high-texture band appearing at the crest line and expanding downward over 3-10 frames.
entries.detector_note: Mask V>0.75 and S<0.20 inside the water region; require the mask area to grow monotonically over a short window and its Laplacian variance to exceed the surrounding water by 3x; anchor the onset at the crest ridge from wave_crest.
entries.notes: Snow, clouds, white cloth and blown highlights are all bright and desaturated; the monotonic growth anchored to a crest is what makes this specific.

entries.label: Wave crest
entries.description: The raised leading edge of a travelling surface wave.
entries.frame_evidence: An elongated bright ridge (or dark trough shadow) running roughly perpendicular to the flow direction, with a sharper luminance gradient on its leading face.
entries.detector_note: Ridge detection via skimage.feature.hessian_matrix_eigvals on the smoothed water region; keep ridges whose orientation is within 60-120 deg of the Farneback dominant direction; measure crest length and asymmetry of the cross-ridge profile.
entries.notes: Distinguishing crest from trough requires knowing the light direction; without it, polarity is a coin flip. Report crest_profile_asymmetry rather than asserting which side is the crest.

entries.label: Wave travel speed
entries.description: Propagation speed of a wave front in pixels per unique cel.
entries.frame_evidence: A crest ridge occupying successively displaced positions across a short frame window.
entries.detector_note: Track the crest ridge centroid across unique cels with cv2.matchTemplate on a strip perpendicular to the crest; speed = displacement / delta_unique_index; convert to px/sec using the unique-cel rate, not the container fps.
entries.notes: Reporting px/sec from container fps on 2s/3s anime overestimates by 2-3x. Always divide by measured unique-cel cadence.

entries.label: Melting wax run-down
entries.description: Candle wax liquefying and running down the candle body.
entries.frame_evidence: Smooth translucent lobes forming at the candle rim and creeping downward over many frames, with a specular sheen.
entries.detector_note: Runoff-rivulet tracking restricted to a vertical candle-body region below a detected flame; require a slow tip descent rate (< 1px per unique cel) and increasing lobe area.
entries.notes: Extremely slow; requires a long static shot. Anchoring to a flame from the fire detector is what distinguishes it from a generic rivulet.

entries.label: Wet fabric darkening
entries.description: Clothing or hair becoming visibly darker and clinging where soaked.
entries.frame_evidence: Regions of a garment drop in luminance and gain saturation relative to the dry parts of the same garment, with a soft irregular boundary.
entries.detector_note: Use mediapipe pose landmarks 11/12/23/24 to define torso and limb ROIs, then look for a bimodal luminance distribution within a single garment ROI with a soft boundary between the modes; report the mode separation.
entries.notes: Shadow, fold shading and printed garment patterns all create bimodal luminance in a garment ROI. Consider a VLM crop for confirmation on a torso crop.

entries.label: Wet surface sheen
entries.description: A ground or object surface made glossier by water without a standing pool.
entries.frame_evidence: Elevated specular highlight coverage and increased contrast between highlight and base compared to the same material dry.
entries.detector_note: Specular-highlight area fraction (V > 240) and the ratio of the region's 95th to 50th luminance percentile on the surface region; report both against the shot distribution.
entries.notes: Has no dry reference within a single shot, so this is a relative statistic only. Polished floors, ice and metal read identically.

entries.label: Whirlpool / vortex
entries.description: A rotating funnel or spiral in a liquid surface.
entries.frame_evidence: Concentric spiral streaks around a centre, with tangential rather than radial surface motion, often with a darker depression at the core.
entries.detector_note: Curl of the Farneback field (np.gradient(vy,axis=1)-np.gradient(vx,axis=0)); locate curl extrema, then verify the flow near that point is predominantly tangential (mean |dot(v, r_hat)| / mean |cross(v, r_hat)| < 0.4) over a >20px radius.
entries.notes: Camera roll produces a global curl field indistinguishable from a giant vortex; stabilise rotation first. Isolated curl peaks from flow noise are common - require persistence over >=3 unique cels.

entries.label: Wildfire front line
entries.description: An extended, roughly linear advancing line of flame across terrain.
entries.frame_evidence: A long, thin, connected fire region with a high length-to-width ratio, advancing perpendicular to its own axis.
entries.detector_note: Fire mask components with skeleton length / mean width > 10; measure the advance of the component's centroid along the direction perpendicular to its principal axis.
entries.notes: Requires a wide shot; in close coverage the front fills the frame and the aspect test fails.

entries.label: Active picture aspect ratio
entries.description: Aspect ratio of the picture after removing detected bars, plus the nearest standard ratio.
entries.frame_evidence: Whether the real image is 1.78, 1.85, 2.39 or 4:3 inside its container.
entries.detector_note: active_width_px/active_height_px; snap to the nearest of [1.33,1.37,1.66,1.78,1.85,2.00,2.20,2.35,2.39,2.76] and report the residual.

entries.label: Banding origin confirmation
entries.description: Whether a high banding_score is genuine posterisation or the flat-fill style of the artwork.
entries.frame_evidence: Stepped contours in what should be a smooth gradient.
entries.detector_note: When banding_score is high AND unique_colour_count_5bit is also high (so it is not simply cel art), crop the highest-scoring 512x512 smooth region and ask qwen2.5vl.
entries.vlm_question: Does this image show smooth continuous shading, or visible stepped bands of colour? Answer only 'smooth' or 'banded'.
entries.notes: THE CROP RULE: send the tight smooth-region crop, never the whole frame. Deterministic metrics decide WHERE to crop; the VLM only adjudicates.

entries.label: Bar purity / bleed
entries.description: Whether detected bars are truly clean black or carry bleed, noise or leftover picture.
entries.frame_evidence: Faint image ghosting or compression noise inside what should be a solid mask.
entries.detector_note: Within the bar rows: max, mean and std of Y, plus the count of pixels > 16.
entries.notes: Dirty bars are a real deliverable defect and are invisible on any normal viewing monitor.

entries.label: Black clipping fraction
entries.description: Fraction of pixels at or below the crushed-black threshold.
entries.frame_evidence: Shadow areas that have gone to a featureless solid black.
entries.detector_note: float((Y <= 2).mean()); also report at thresholds 0, 2, 8, 16.
entries.notes: Letterbox bars dominate this metric; exclude the bar rows found by letterbox_bar_geometry first.

entries.label: Effective black level
entries.description: The p0.1 luma value: whether true black is actually reached or the image is lifted.
entries.frame_evidence: A washed-out frame whose darkest pixel is grey, not black.
entries.detector_note: float(np.percentile(Y_excluding_bars, 0.1)).

entries.label: Blur intent confirmation
entries.description: Whether a low sharpness reading is intentional depth of field or an out-of-focus/soft-source defect.
entries.frame_evidence: A soft frame where either the subject is sharp and the background is not, or nothing is sharp.
entries.detector_note: Trigger when laplacian_variance is in the shot's bottom decile AND dof_score is ambiguous; crop the region around focus_centroid at 512x512 and ask qwen2.5vl.
entries.vlm_question: Is the main subject in this image sharp and in focus? Answer only yes or no.
entries.notes: Small VLMs are unreliable at fine focus judgement; treat the answer as one vote alongside edge_width_blur_extent, never as the verdict.

entries.label: Depth-of-field edge halo
entries.description: Bright or dark halo hugging the subject silhouette, the tell of a post-process 2.5D blur rather than optical DOF.
entries.frame_evidence: A thin sharp outline of background stuck to the character's edge where the blur was masked.
entries.detector_note: Along strong closed contours, compare the mean local sharpness in a 3px band inside versus a 3-10px band outside; a sharp thin outer band inside an otherwise blurred region flags a matte-blurred composite.
entries.notes: This is the discriminator shallow_depth_of_field_score lacks, but it also fires on any sharpening halo; pair it with sharpening_overshoot.

entries.label: BRISQUE perceptual quality score
entries.description: Learned no-reference image quality score from natural-scene-statistics features.
entries.frame_evidence: An overall 'how degraded does this look' number.
entries.detector_note: cv2.quality.QualityBRISQUE_create(model_path, range_path) EXISTS in cv2 4.13 contrib, but the brisque_model_live.yml and brisque_range_live.yml files are NOT shipped with the pip wheel and are not on this machine.
entries.notes: Even with the model files, BRISQUE is trained on NATURAL photographs; its natural-scene-statistics prior is invalid for flat-shaded 2D animation and would report every anime frame as heavily distorted.

entries.label: Camera move class
entries.description: Categorical label derived from the decomposed global transform: static, pan, tilt, zoom, roll, or compound.
entries.frame_evidence: Whether the shot is locked off or the camera is moving, and how.
entries.detector_note: Threshold the decomposed pan/tilt/zoom/roll against per-shot noise floors measured from the frames with the LOWEST residual motion; classify by which components exceed 3x their noise floor.
entries.notes: Needs the per-shot noise floor as its null model; without it a locked-off tripod shot on a noisy source reports a constant micro-pan.

entries.label: Camera shake / handheld energy
entries.description: High-frequency component of the global translation trajectory across a short window.
entries.frame_evidence: The frame jittering rather than moving smoothly.
entries.detector_note: Accumulate pan/tilt over 9-15 unique cels; subtract a Savitzky-Golay smoothed trajectory (scipy.signal.savgol_filter, window 9, order 2); shake = RMS of the residual.
entries.notes: Sub-pixel estimation error looks exactly like micro-shake; the noise floor must come from a known locked-off segment.

entries.label: Canny edge density
entries.description: Fraction of pixels classified as edges by Canny at auto-tuned thresholds.
entries.frame_evidence: How busy and linework-heavy the frame is.
entries.detector_note: v=np.median(Y); lo=int(max(0,0.66*v)); hi=int(min(255,1.33*v)); ed=cv2.Canny(Y,lo,hi); ed.mean()/255.
entries.notes: Report the thresholds used alongside the density or the number is not reproducible across shots.

entries.label: Cel hold length (ones/twos/threes)
entries.description: Number of consecutive frames a single drawing is held for.
entries.frame_evidence: The same drawing repeated twice (on 2s) or three times (on 3s).
entries.detector_note: Run-length encode the duplicate flag stream; report the modal and mean run length over the shot.
entries.notes: Mixed cadence within one shot (a character on 2s over a BG panning on 1s) means a single hold number for the frame is a lie; measure holds REGIONALLY when the residual motion map shows independent layers.

entries.label: Shading step count
entries.description: Number of discrete luminance steps within a single-hue surface: 2-tone cel shading versus continuous shading.
entries.frame_evidence: A character's arm shaded with exactly two flat tones and a hard terminator.
entries.detector_note: Within each connected same-hue region, count distinct luminance modes via a smoothed histogram peak search; report the mean modes per region.

entries.label: Changed pixel fraction
entries.description: Fraction of pixels whose value changed by more than the codec noise floor.
entries.frame_evidence: How much of the frame area is actually in motion or changing.
entries.detector_note: (cv2.absdiff(a,b) > max(6, 3*noise_sigma)).mean(); threshold derived from the shot's static-region noise.
entries.notes: The threshold MUST be derived from the measured noise floor; a fixed threshold reports pure grain as motion on a noisy source.

entries.label: Per-channel mean and std
entries.description: First and second moments of each of B, G and R separately.
entries.frame_evidence: Which primary carries the frame's energy.
entries.detector_note: bgr.reshape(-1,3).mean(0) and .std(0).

entries.label: Chroma bleed at luma edges
entries.description: Spatial offset and softness of chroma edges relative to luma edges, the 4:2:0 signature.
entries.frame_evidence: Coloured fringes lagging a half-pixel behind hard graphic edges, worst on red.
entries.detector_note: Sobel magnitude on Y versus on Cr and Cb; measure the edge-width ratio and the cross-correlation lag between the luma and chroma edge profiles across strong vertical edges.
entries.notes: Tells you about the DELIVERY CODEC, not the production; a 4:2:0 h264 proxy of a 4:4:4 master shows this strongly.

entries.label: Colour banding score
entries.description: Density of long constant-value runs inside smooth low-gradient regions: the posterisation signature.
entries.frame_evidence: Visible stepped contours across a sky or a soft gradient.
entries.detector_note: Mask smooth regions (Sobel magnitude < 4 after a 5x5 blur); inside the mask count runs of identical value along x and y with length >= 8; score = banded_run_pixels / smooth_pixels.
entries.notes: Deliberate flat cel fill in 2D animation produces INFINITE runs and scores maximum. Gate this metric on unique_colour_count_5bit being high, or 2D animation reports 100% banding.

entries.label: Correlated colour temperature estimate
entries.description: Estimated CCT in kelvin from the grey-world illuminant, via the McCamy approximation.
entries.frame_evidence: Whether the frame reads warm tungsten or cool daylight/moonlight.
entries.detector_note: Grey-world mean RGB -> linearise -> sRGB-to-XYZ matrix -> xy chromaticity; n=(x-0.3320)/(0.1858-y); CCT=449n^3+3525n^2+6823.3n+5520.33.
entries.notes: Grey-world fails on any frame dominated by one saturated surface; report duv and refuse to emit a CCT when duv is large (the point is far off the Planckian locus).

entries.label: Hasler-Susstrunk colourfulness
entries.description: The standard no-reference colourfulness metric M3 on opponent axes.
entries.frame_evidence: How chromatically rich the frame reads without reference to any target.
entries.detector_note: rg = R-G; yb = 0.5*(R+G)-B; M = sqrt(rg.std()**2+yb.std()**2) + 0.3*sqrt(rg.mean()**2+yb.mean()**2).
entries.notes: Published rule of thumb: <15 not colourful, >60 extremely colourful.

entries.label: Complementary hue opposition
entries.description: Mass concentrated at two hue modes roughly 180 degrees apart (the teal-and-orange signature).
entries.frame_evidence: Skin-tone warm subjects against a cyan-shifted background.
entries.detector_note: For each pair of hue modes compute angular separation; score = combined mass of the best pair weighted by cos-similarity to 180 degrees.

entries.label: Trackable feature count and spread
entries.description: Number of trackable corners and how evenly they cover the frame, which bounds how well global motion can be estimated.
entries.frame_evidence: How many distinct trackable corners the frame offers.
entries.detector_note: cv2.goodFeaturesToTrack(Y, maxCorners=2000, qualityLevel=0.01, minDistance=7, blockSize=7); cross-check with cv2.ORB_create(nfeatures=2000).detect; dispersion = std of keypoint coords / frame diagonal.
entries.notes: Directly gates global_motion_homography: below ~30 corners the camera-motion estimate must be marked low-confidence, which is exactly what happens on flat anime backgrounds.

entries.label: Shot boundary cut score
entries.description: Fused dissimilarity score used to detect a hard cut between two frames.
entries.frame_evidence: The picture changing completely from one frame to the next.
entries.detector_note: score = w1*(1-hist_correl) + w2*min(phash_hamming/32,1) + w3*min(absdiff_mean/40,1) + w4*(1-ssim); compare against 6*MAD of the score over a 30-frame rolling window rather than a fixed threshold.
entries.notes: A FIXED cut threshold fails on anime: a fast action cel change can exceed a slow dissolve. The rolling-MAD null is mandatory. Whip pans and full-frame flashes are the classic false positives.

entries.label: 8x8 blocking artefact score
entries.description: Excess of gradient energy on the 8- and 16-pixel codec grid relative to off-grid positions.
entries.frame_evidence: Visible square blocks in gradients and dark areas on a heavily compressed source.
entries.detector_note: col_diff = |Y[:,1:]-Y[:,:-1]|.mean(axis=0); blockiness = mean(col_diff[7::8]) / mean(col_diff[off-grid]); repeat for rows and for a 16px grid.
entries.notes: Measures the DELIVERY encode; a re-encoded or rescaled file shifts or destroys the grid alignment, so a score near 1.0 does not mean the master was clean.

entries.label: Depth layer count
entries.description: Number of distinct depth planes in the frame.
entries.frame_evidence: Foreground, midground and background separating as distinct planes.
entries.detector_note: Needs monocular depth estimation (MiDaS / Depth-Anything ONNX). onnxruntime 1.24.3 and torch 2.10 are installed but NO depth weights are present on this machine, so this is not runnable today.
entries.notes: The blur-based proxy (focus_map_tiles) is NOT a depth measure; a deep-focus frame has real depth layers and zero blur separation.

entries.label: Near-grey pixel fraction
entries.description: Fraction of pixels whose chroma is below a near-grey threshold.
entries.frame_evidence: How much of the frame is effectively monochrome.
entries.detector_note: lab = cv2.cvtColor(bgr, cv2.COLOR_BGR2LAB); C = hypot(a-128, b-128); (C < 6).mean().

entries.label: Spatial detail density map
entries.description: Per-tile high-frequency energy over a 16x16 grid, describing where detail lives.
entries.frame_evidence: Detailed foreground against an empty painted background.
entries.detector_note: Tile the high-pass map into 16x16 and report the tile matrix, its entropy and its centroid.

entries.label: Dissolve / cross-fade score
entries.description: Sustained elevated but sub-cut change with monotone histogram blending across several frames.
entries.frame_evidence: Two images visibly superimposed while one fades into the other.
entries.detector_note: Over a 15-frame window, test whether each frame is well modelled as alpha*A + (1-alpha)*B for the window endpoints: fit alpha per frame by least squares and check monotonicity and the residual.
entries.notes: Blended pulldown frames produce the same linear-mix signature over 1-2 frames; require length >= 4.

entries.label: Dominant colour palette (k-means)
entries.description: The k dominant colours of the frame with their pixel-mass weights, in Lab and sRGB.
entries.frame_evidence: The five swatches a colourist would pull off the frame.
entries.detector_note: Downsample to 128px, convert to Lab float32, cv2.kmeans(Z, K=5, None, (cv2.TERM_CRITERIA_EPS+cv2.TERM_CRITERIA_MAX_ITER,20,1.0), 3, cv2.KMEANS_PP_CENTERS).
entries.notes: sklearn is NOT installed; use cv2.kmeans. Cluster in Lab not BGR, or perceptually distinct colours merge. Fix the RNG seed or the palette order jitters frame to frame.

entries.label: Dominant edge orientation
entries.description: Peak of the orientation histogram and its concentration.
entries.frame_evidence: The direction the frame's lines mostly run.
entries.detector_note: argmax of the smoothed orientation histogram plus its normalised prominence.

entries.label: Edge orientation entropy
entries.description: Entropy of the orientation histogram: structured architecture versus organic clutter.
entries.frame_evidence: A city frame with strong H/V bias versus a forest with uniform orientation.
entries.detector_note: -sum(p*log2(p)) on the normalised orientation histogram, max 4.17 bits for 18 bins.

entries.label: Edge orientation histogram
entries.description: 18-bin (10-degree) histogram of gradient orientation weighted by magnitude, over 0-180 degrees.
entries.frame_evidence: Whether the frame's structure is predominantly horizontal, vertical or diagonal.
entries.detector_note: ang = (np.rad2deg(np.arctan2(gy,gx)) % 180); np.histogram(ang, bins=18, range=(0,180), weights=mag).

entries.label: Mean edge rise width
entries.description: Average 10-90 percent rise distance across detected edges: an absolute, resolution-aware blur measure.
entries.frame_evidence: How many pixels an edge takes to go from dark to light.
entries.detector_note: Canny edges; for each edge pixel walk the gradient normal until the profile flattens; report the mean and p10 rise width in pixels (Crete-style blur extent).
entries.notes: Unlike Laplacian variance this is comparable across shots and resolutions, which is why it should be the primary blur metric.

entries.label: Effective unique drawing rate
entries.description: Unique cels per second of runtime, versus the container frame rate.
entries.frame_evidence: A 24fps file that only shows 12 new drawings a second.
entries.detector_note: unique_cel_count_in_window / (window_frames / container_fps) using ffprobe's r_frame_rate for the container rate.

entries.label: Exact duplicate frame flag
entries.description: Whether the frame is byte-for-byte or near-byte identical to its predecessor.
entries.frame_evidence: A held drawing repeated across consecutive frames.
entries.detector_note: np.array_equal(a, b) for exact; else float(cv2.absdiff(a,b).mean()) < 0.15 AND (cv2.absdiff(a,b) > 2).mean() < 1e-4 for near-duplicate under lossy codec noise.
entries.notes: THE ANCHOR ENTRY FOR ANIME. 24fps anime carries 8-12 unique drawings per second; every temporal metric in this shard must be computed between UNIQUE-CEL indices, not raw neighbours, or two thirds of measurements are structural zeros.

entries.label: Face bounding box geometry
entries.description: Position and area fraction of each detected face, a shot-size and headroom proxy.
entries.frame_evidence: How large in frame the face is and where it sits.
entries.detector_note: Min/max over the 468 face-mesh landmark coordinates; area_fraction = bbox_area/(w*h); headroom = bbox_top_y normalised.

entries.label: Detected face count
entries.description: Number of faces returned by the mediapipe face detector / face mesh in this frame.
entries.frame_evidence: How many faces are visible and resolvable.
entries.detector_note: mediapipe.solutions.face_mesh.FaceMesh(static_image_mode=True, max_num_faces=8, refine_landmarks=True, min_detection_confidence=0.5); len(results.multi_face_landmarks).
entries.notes: Mediapipe face mesh is trained on PHOTOGRAPHIC faces and fails or mislands on stylised 2D anime faces (huge eyes, no nose bridge). On 2D content a zero count is NOT evidence of no face - see face_landmark_failure_2d.

entries.label: Face landmark failure on stylised art
entries.description: Explicit flag that mediapipe returned no face or a low-confidence mesh on a frame that plainly contains a drawn face.
entries.frame_evidence: An obvious anime face in frame with zero landmarks returned.
entries.detector_note: When face_count==0 but skin_chroma_fraction and flat_fill_fraction are both high, escalate a tight centre-of-saliency CROP to qwen2.5vl for confirmation.
entries.vlm_question: Is there a drawn cartoon or anime face in this image? Answer only yes or no.
entries.notes: This entry exists so the analyzer does not silently report 'no faces' on an entire anime episode. THE CROP RULE applies: send a tight crop, never the full frame.

entries.label: Face yaw / pitch / roll
entries.description: Head orientation estimated by solving PnP against the canonical face model.
entries.frame_evidence: Whether the head is turned, tilted or looking to camera.
entries.detector_note: cv2.solvePnP with the mediapipe canonical face metric landmarks and an assumed pinhole intrinsic (f = image width); cv2.Rodrigues then cv2.RQDecomp3x3 for Euler angles.
entries.notes: The assumed focal length is a guess; ABSOLUTE angles carry maybe 10 degrees of error, RELATIVE change across a shot is far more reliable.

entries.label: Fade to/from black or white
entries.description: Monotone ramp of mean luminance toward 0 or 255 with collapsing contrast.
entries.frame_evidence: The picture sinking to black or blooming to white over several frames.
entries.detector_note: Linear fit of luminance_mean over a 15-frame window with rms_contrast falling toward zero; report slope, r2 and the terminal luma.

entries.label: Fixed pattern / row-column noise
entries.description: Structured noise aligned to rows or columns, as opposed to random grain.
entries.frame_evidence: Faint horizontal banding or vertical striping across a flat area.
entries.detector_note: Row means and column means of the high-pass residual; compare their variance to the expected variance under independence (residual_std/sqrt(N)); report the excess ratio.

entries.label: Flat colour fill fraction
entries.description: Fraction of the frame occupied by regions of near-constant colour larger than a size threshold.
entries.frame_evidence: Big areas of a single unmodulated colour, the definitive cel-animation signature.
entries.detector_note: Quantise to 5 bits/channel, cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats on each colour, sum areas of components > 0.1% of frame with internal std < 2.
entries.notes: The single most reliable 2D-versus-live-action discriminator alongside unique_colour_count_5bit; heavy grain or a film-grain overlay destroys it.

entries.label: Flow coherence
entries.description: Resultant vector length divided by summed magnitude: how unidirectional the motion is.
entries.frame_evidence: A whole-frame pan (coherent) versus scattered independent movers (incoherent).
entries.detector_note: |sum(flow_vectors)| / sum(|flow_vectors|), over pixels with mag > 0.5px.
entries.notes: Coherence near 1 is the primary signature of camera motion rather than subject motion.

entries.label: Flow curl and shear
entries.description: Curl (whole-frame rotation) and shear components of the flow Jacobian.
entries.frame_evidence: The picture rotating about a point, or leaning and skewing rather than translating.
entries.detector_note: du=np.gradient(flow[...,0]); dv=np.gradient(flow[...,1]); curl=dv_dx-du_dy; shear_normal=du_dx-dv_dy; shear_tangential=du_dy+dv_dx.

entries.label: Flow direction histogram
entries.description: Magnitude-weighted 36-bin circular histogram of flow direction.
entries.frame_evidence: Whether the frame's motion is unified in one direction or fragmented.
entries.detector_note: np.histogram(np.rad2deg(ang), bins=36, range=(0,360), weights=mag) with mag>0.5px gating.

entries.label: Flow divergence (zoom/expansion)
entries.description: Divergence of the flow field: positive means expansion toward camera or a dolly/zoom in.
entries.frame_evidence: The whole picture expanding outward from a focus of expansion.
entries.detector_note: du_dx = np.gradient(flow[...,0], axis=1); dv_dy = np.gradient(flow[...,1], axis=0); div = du_dx + dv_dy; report mean and the radial-fit focus of expansion.

entries.label: Flow magnitude statistics
entries.description: Mean, median, std, p95 and max of |v| over the flow field.
entries.frame_evidence: The overall amount of motion between the two drawings.
entries.detector_note: mag, ang = cv2.cartToPolar(flow[...,0], flow[...,1]); mean/median/std/p95/max of mag in pixels per unique-cel step.
entries.notes: Report in px per UNIQUE CEL and also normalise by frame diagonal, or the number is not comparable across resolutions.

entries.label: Flow occlusion / forward-backward failure
entries.description: Fraction of pixels where forward and backward flow disagree, marking occlusions and flow failure.
entries.frame_evidence: Areas revealed or covered between the two frames where no correspondence exists.
entries.detector_note: Compute flow a->b and b->a; fb_error = |flow_ab(x) + flow_ba(x + flow_ab(x))|; occluded = fb_error > 0.01*(|f_ab|^2+|f_ba|^2) + 0.5.
entries.notes: THIS IS THE NULL MODEL FOR ALL FLOW METRICS: high occlusion fraction means the flow numbers above are not measurements. Anime flat fills and large hold-then-jump cel changes both blow this up.

entries.label: Focus centroid
entries.description: Sharpness-weighted centre of mass, i.e. where in frame the sharpest region sits.
entries.frame_evidence: The subject plane the lens is actually focused on.
entries.detector_note: Weighted centroid of the tile focus map, normalised to 0-1 in x and y; also its distance from frame centre.

entries.label: Tile-wise focus map
entries.description: Per-tile sharpness over an 8x8 grid, plus the fraction of tiles that are in focus.
entries.frame_evidence: A frame where one plane is sharp and everything else is soft.
entries.detector_note: Split into 8x8 tiles; per tile cv2.Laplacian(...).var(); in_focus = tiles > 0.35*tiles.max().
entries.notes: Empty sky tiles are unmeasurable, not out of focus; mask tiles whose luma std is below ~3.

entries.label: Edge row/column garbage
entries.description: Anomalous outermost rows or columns: half-pixel resize edges, green lines, black borders.
entries.frame_evidence: A one-pixel dark or coloured line pinned to the frame edge.
entries.detector_note: Compare each of the outer 4 rows/columns to the mean of rows 8-16 inward with cv2.absdiff; flag rows whose deviation exceeds 4x the interior row-to-row variation.

entries.label: Frame index and timing metadata
entries.description: The frame's index, presentation timestamp, container frame rate and resolution.
entries.frame_evidence: Not visual - the coordinates every other metric is reported against.
entries.detector_note: cv2.VideoCapture.get(cv2.CAP_PROP_POS_FRAMES / CAP_PROP_POS_MSEC); cross-check against ffprobe -show_frames -select_streams v for pkt_pts_time and key_frame.
entries.notes: cv2's frame positions drift on variable-frame-rate sources; ffprobe's pts is authoritative and the two must be reconciled before any per-second metric is emitted.

entries.label: Render engine / capture device identification
entries.description: Which renderer, camera or generative model produced the frame.
entries.frame_evidence: Characteristic sampling noise, tonemap and aliasing signatures.
entries.detector_note: No forensic model is installed and no reliable open method exists for this across the 2D/3D/live-action mix; spectral and noise features correlate weakly but have no validated null.
entries.notes: Explicitly logged as not-detectable so the analyzer never guesses provenance from spectral slope alone.

entries.label: 2D-drawn versus 3D-rendered versus live-action
entries.description: Which of the three production modes the frame belongs to, driving which metrics are even meaningful.
entries.frame_evidence: Flat fills and ink outlines, versus continuous shading with rendered specular, versus photographic grain and depth of field.
entries.detector_note: Fuse flat_fill_fraction, unique_colour_count_5bit, ink_line_fraction, spectral_alpha, gradient_shading_fraction and flat_region_noise_sigma into a scored rule; emit the per-class score AND the winning class.
entries.notes: This is a HAND-TUNED RULE, not a trained classifier, and cel-shaded 3D deliberately defeats it. It must be validated against a labelled null set of known-2D and known-live-action clips before any downstream metric is gated on it.

entries.label: GLCM texture features
entries.description: Haralick contrast, homogeneity, energy and correlation from the grey-level co-occurrence matrix.
entries.frame_evidence: The statistical texture of surfaces: rough gravel versus smooth flat fill.
entries.detector_note: skimage.feature.graycomatrix(Y//4, distances=[1,2,4], angles=[0,pi/4,pi/2,3pi/4], levels=64, symmetric=True, normed=True) then graycoprops for contrast/homogeneity/energy/correlation.
entries.notes: Expensive at full resolution; compute on a 512px-max downscale and record the scale. skimage.feature.local_binary_pattern(P=8,R=1,method='uniform') is the cheaper fallback descriptor if GLCM cost bites.

entries.label: Exposure drift across a shot
entries.description: Slow monotone trend in mean luminance across a shot, distinct from a single-frame flash.
entries.frame_evidence: The whole shot gradually brightening as an auto-exposure hunts or a light ramps.
entries.detector_note: np.polyfit(frame_index, luminance_mean, 1) over the shot; report slope per second, r2 and the total excursion.

entries.label: Global similarity transform
entries.description: RANSAC similarity transform between adjacent unique cels, decomposed into pan, tilt, zoom and roll.
entries.frame_evidence: The camera move underlying the whole frame's motion.
entries.detector_note: p0 = cv2.goodFeaturesToTrack(a); p1,st,_ = cv2.calcOpticalFlowPyrLK(a,b,p0,None,winSize=(21,21),maxLevel=3); M,inl = cv2.estimateAffinePartial2D(p0[st==1], p1[st==1], method=cv2.RANSAC, ransacReprojThreshold=3.0); zoom=hypot(M[0,0],M[1,0]); roll=degrees(atan2(M[1,0],M[0,0])); pan=M[0,2]; tilt=M[1,2].
entries.notes: Confidence is bounded by corner_count: on a flat anime background the transform is unconstrained and returns near-identity regardless of the truth. Refuse to emit below ~30 inliers.

entries.label: Global homography
entries.description: Full 8-DOF projective transform between frames, capturing perspective change a similarity cannot.
entries.frame_evidence: The plane of the scene shifting perspective as the camera moves through space.
entries.detector_note: cv2.findHomography(src, dst, cv2.RANSAC, 3.0, maxIters=2000, confidence=0.995); decompose the top-left 2x2 by SVD for scale/rotation/shear and read the bottom row for the perspective terms.
entries.notes: A homography fitted to a NON-planar scene is a wrong model that still fits; always report the inlier ratio and prefer the affine when the perspective terms are within noise.

entries.label: Gradient magnitude statistics
entries.description: Mean, std and p95 of the Sobel gradient magnitude field.
entries.frame_evidence: Overall edge strength independent of any binarisation threshold.
entries.detector_note: mag = cv2.magnitude(cv2.Sobel(Yf,cv2.CV_32F,1,0), cv2.Sobel(Yf,cv2.CV_32F,0,1)); mean/std/p95.

entries.label: Smooth shading gradient fraction
entries.description: Fraction of the frame carrying smooth, low-amplitude luminance ramps typical of 3D shading.
entries.frame_evidence: Continuously curving falloff across a surface rather than a hard two-tone cel shadow.
entries.detector_note: Regions where the Sobel magnitude is low-but-nonzero (1-6) and the second derivative is near constant over >0.1% of frame; sum their area fraction.
entries.notes: Cel-shaded 3D deliberately suppresses this and reads as 2D; that is a real ambiguity, not a bug.

entries.label: Grain spectral slope
entries.description: Slope of the noise residual's radial power spectrum: white sensor noise versus clumped film grain.
entries.frame_evidence: Fine even digital noise versus coarse organic grain clumps.
entries.detector_note: Radial average of |FFT(high-pass residual)|**2 in flat tiles; np.polyfit(log f, log P, 1).
entries.notes: A film-grain PLUGIN and real film grain give the same slope; this measures the grain, not its origin.

entries.label: Detected hand count and landmarks
entries.description: Number of hands detected and the count of visible hand landmarks.
entries.frame_evidence: Hands present and resolvable enough to land 21 keypoints on.
entries.detector_note: mediapipe.solutions.hands.Hands(static_image_mode=True, max_num_hands=4, min_detection_confidence=0.5); len(results.multi_hand_landmarks) and per-hand landmark visibility.
entries.notes: Mediapipe hands is the ONLY hand signal available (no YOLO installed) and it fails on drawn hands, motion-blurred hands and hands smaller than roughly 40px.

entries.label: Dark-channel haze estimate
entries.description: Dark channel prior value: high dark-channel means atmospheric haze, fog or a milky lift.
entries.frame_evidence: Distant parts of frame washed toward a bright uniform grey.
entries.detector_note: dark = cv2.erode(bgr.min(axis=2), np.ones((15,15),np.uint8)); report dark.mean() and its p90.
entries.notes: Any large bright uniform surface (snow, a white wall, an anime sky fill) reads as haze; needs a background-region null.

entries.label: High-frequency energy ratio
entries.description: Fraction of spectral energy above half Nyquist, a resolution-aware sharpness measure.
entries.frame_evidence: How much genuine fine detail survives at the pixel scale.
entries.detector_note: sum(P[f>0.25]) / sum(P[f>0]) on the radial spectrum.

entries.label: Histogram correlation
entries.description: Correlation, chi-square and Bhattacharyya distance between adjacent frames' colour histograms.
entries.frame_evidence: Whether the two frames share a palette and tonal distribution.
entries.detector_note: 3D HSV histogram (h=32,s=8,v=8) normalised; cv2.compareHist with cv2.HISTCMP_CORREL, HISTCMP_CHISQR, HISTCMP_BHATTACHARYYA.
entries.notes: Insensitive to spatial rearrangement: a whip pan within one location keeps correlation high, which is why cut_score must fuse it with phash and absdiff.

entries.label: Horizon / dutch tilt angle
entries.description: Signed deviation of the dominant near-horizontal line family from true horizontal.
entries.frame_evidence: A canted frame where the world's horizontals run downhill.
entries.detector_note: cv2.HoughLinesP(edges, 1, np.pi/360, threshold=80, minLineLength=w//6, maxLineGap=10); keep segments within 30 degrees of horizontal; report the length-weighted median angle.
entries.notes: A frame with no long horizontals gives a meaningless angle; refuse to emit unless the supporting line length exceeds ~0.5 frame widths.

entries.label: Left-right symmetry
entries.description: Similarity between the frame and its horizontal mirror.
entries.frame_evidence: A deliberately centred, mirrored composition.
entries.detector_note: skimage.metrics.structural_similarity(Y, np.fliplr(Y)) and 1 - mean|Y - fliplr(Y)|/255.
entries.notes: Needs a NULL: compute the same score against 20 random horizontal shifts of the mirrored frame; only an excess above that null is symmetry.

entries.label: Circular mean hue
entries.description: The chroma-weighted mean hue angle, computed correctly on the circle.
entries.frame_evidence: The single dominant colour direction of the frame's cast.
entries.detector_note: z = np.sum(w*np.exp(1j*np.deg2rad(H_deg))); mean_hue = np.rad2deg(np.angle(z)) % 360.
entries.notes: Never average hue linearly; 359 and 1 degrees are adjacent.

entries.label: Circular hue variance
entries.description: 1 minus the resultant vector length: how spread the frame's hues are around the wheel.
entries.frame_evidence: A monochromatic teal frame versus a full-spectrum carnival frame.
entries.detector_note: R = abs(z)/sum(w); circular_variance = 1 - R.

entries.label: Hue histogram (10-degree bins)
entries.description: Chroma-weighted 36-bin circular histogram of hue.
entries.frame_evidence: The literal palette distribution of the frame around the colour wheel.
entries.detector_note: np.histogram(H_deg, bins=36, range=(0,360), weights=chroma_mask_weights) with weights = S*V so grey pixels do not vote.
entries.notes: Unweighted hue histograms are dominated by noise in dark/grey areas; always weight by chroma.

entries.label: Hue mode count
entries.description: Number of prominent peaks in the smoothed circular hue histogram.
entries.frame_evidence: How many distinct colour families the frame is actually built from.
entries.detector_note: Circularly wrap the 36-bin hist, smooth with a 3-bin kernel, scipy.signal.find_peaks with prominence >= 5% of mass.

entries.label: Ink outline fraction
entries.description: Fraction of pixels belonging to dark, thin, closed outlines drawn over flat fills: the cel-ink signature.
entries.frame_evidence: Black character outlines sitting on top of flat colour areas.
entries.detector_note: mask = (Y < p15) & (Canny dilated) & (local flat-fill neighbourhood on both sides); measure fraction and mean run thickness via cv2.distanceTransform on the mask.
entries.notes: Live-action frames with dark thin structures (wires, railings, hair) also fire; gate on flat_fill_fraction being high.

entries.label: Interlacing / combing score
entries.description: Alternating-line displacement energy indicating interlaced or badly deinterlaced source.
entries.frame_evidence: Horizontal comb teeth along the edges of moving objects.
entries.detector_note: comb = mean(|2*Y[1:-1] - Y[:-2] - Y[2:]| along rows) restricted to columns with motion; compare the even-field-only and odd-field-only downscales with cv2.absdiff.
entries.notes: Fine horizontal texture (venetian blinds, hair) mimics combing; require the effect to be localised to MOVING regions from the flow field.

entries.label: Iris landmark availability
entries.description: Whether the refined iris landmarks resolved, and the resulting eye-opening ratio.
entries.frame_evidence: Eyes open enough and large enough in frame to land iris points on.
entries.detector_note: FaceMesh(refine_landmarks=True) gives landmarks 468-477; eye aspect ratio from the vertical/horizontal lid landmark distances.
entries.notes: The eyelid metric governs blink and gaze work; on 2D animation it is unavailable because face mesh does not land.

entries.label: Low-key / high-key index
entries.description: Signed ratio of shadow mass to highlight mass, classifying the frame as low-key or high-key.
entries.frame_evidence: A noir frame is mostly shadow with a small bright accent; a commercial frame is the reverse.
entries.detector_note: shadow=(Y<64).mean(); high=(Y>192).mean(); key_balance=(high-shadow)/(high+shadow+1e-6).

entries.label: Lab a*/b* colour cast
entries.description: Mean a* (green-magenta) and b* (blue-yellow) offsets from neutral.
entries.frame_evidence: The direction and strength of the overall grade cast.
entries.detector_note: lab = cv2.cvtColor(bgr, cv2.COLOR_BGR2LAB); a_mean = lab[...,1].mean()-128; b_mean = lab[...,2].mean()-128.

entries.label: Laplacian variance (sharpness)
entries.description: Variance of the Laplacian response, the standard cheap focus measure.
entries.frame_evidence: Whether the frame carries crisp high-frequency detail at all.
entries.detector_note: cv2.Laplacian(Y, cv2.CV_64F, ksize=3).var().
entries.notes: SCALE DEPENDENT and CONTENT DEPENDENT: a sharp frame of a blank wall scores low. Always normalise per-shot against the shot's own maximum, and never compare across resolutions without resizing to a fixed height first.

entries.label: Matte bar geometry (letterbox and pillarbox)
entries.description: Thickness in pixels of the black mattes on all four edges and the resulting active picture area.
entries.frame_evidence: Solid black strips banding the top and bottom, or columns down the sides, of the image.
entries.detector_note: A bar row satisfies Y[r].max()<=16 and Y[r].std()<=2; count contiguous bar rows inward from the top and bottom edges, then apply the same test column-wise on Y.T for pillarboxing.
entries.notes: A genuinely dark shot (night, fade) produces a FALSE full-frame bar reading; require the bar boundary to be stable across the shot before cropping to it.

entries.label: Bar versus dark-content check
entries.description: Whether a detected black band is a real matte bar or simply a very dark part of the picture.
entries.frame_evidence: A black strip at the top of frame that may be a matte or may be a dark ceiling.
entries.detector_note: Trigger when letterbox bars are detected on fewer than 80% of a shot's frames; crop the band plus 40px of picture below it and ask qwen2.5vl.
entries.vlm_question: Is the black strip along the edge of this image a solid uniform black bar with a perfectly straight edge? Answer only yes or no.
entries.notes: Cheap and worth it: a wrong bar crop corrupts every subsequent composition metric in the shot.

entries.label: Straight line segment count
entries.description: Number of straight segments found by the fast line detector, with their length distribution.
entries.frame_evidence: How much of the image is built from hard straight lines.
entries.detector_note: fld = cv2.ximgproc.createFastLineDetector(length_threshold=20, distance_threshold=1.41, canny_th1=50, canny_th2=150); lines = fld.detect(Y).

entries.label: Contour straightness and complexity
entries.description: Chord-to-arc ratio and polygonal complexity over traced contours: how straight and how intricate the frame's shapes are.
entries.frame_evidence: Rigid manmade geometry versus flowing organic silhouettes.
entries.detector_note: cv2.findContours(binary, cv2.RETR_LIST, cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE); per contour cv2.arcLength vs endpoint distance, cv2.approxPolyDP(eps=0.02*perimeter) vertex count, and isoperimetric complexity perimeter**2/(4*pi*area).

entries.label: Line weight variance
entries.description: Variation in outline thickness along a stroke, distinguishing tapered hand inking from uniform digital strokes.
entries.frame_evidence: A brush line that swells and tapers versus a constant 2px vector line.
entries.detector_note: Skeletonise the ink mask (cv2.ximgproc.thinning), sample cv2.distanceTransform values along the skeleton, report std/mean of thickness.
entries.notes: Rescaling and codec ringing both smear thickness; only meaningful at or near native resolution.

entries.label: Global luminance delta
entries.description: Signed change in mean luma between adjacent frames.
entries.frame_evidence: The picture getting brighter or darker frame to frame.
entries.detector_note: float(Yb.mean()) - float(Ya.mean()); also the p95 and p5 deltas separately.

entries.label: Luminance entropy
entries.description: Shannon entropy of the luma histogram in bits, a tonal-information measure.
entries.frame_evidence: A frame that is nearly one flat tone carries almost no tonal information.
entries.detector_note: skimage.measure.shannon_entropy(Y, base=2) or -sum(p*log2(p)) on the normalised 256-bin hist.
entries.notes: Anime flat fills legitimately score low; do not read low entropy as a defect.

entries.label: Flash frame / luminance spike
entries.description: A single-frame excursion in mean luminance far outside the local trend.
entries.frame_evidence: One frame that is suddenly much brighter or darker than its neighbours.
entries.detector_note: Over a 9-frame window compute the median and MAD of luminance_mean; flag frames where |Y_mean - median| > 6*MAD AND the frames either side return to trend.
entries.notes: Uses a MAD null so a legitimately rising exposure ramp does not fire. Frames flagged here must be excluded from grade statistics.

entries.label: Luminance and chroma flicker
entries.description: Periodic frame-to-frame luminance or colour-cast oscillation measured in static regions.
entries.frame_evidence: A steady pulsing of brightness, or colour breathing, across frames that should be identical.
entries.detector_note: Over pixels where the residual motion mask is zero, take per-frame mean luma and per-frame lab_a/lab_b means; FFT each series over the shot; report the peak frequency, amplitude and SNR against the series noise floor.
entries.notes: Must be measured in STATIC regions only or subject motion is misread as flicker.

entries.label: Directional brightness gradient
entries.description: Signed difference in mean luma between opposite thirds of the active picture, vertically and horizontally.
entries.frame_evidence: A sky-bright/ground-dark frame, or side-key lighting with one side carrying the light.
entries.detector_note: vertical = Y[:h//3].mean()-Y[2*h//3:].mean(); horizontal = Y[:,:w//3].mean()-Y[:,2*w//3:].mean(), on the bar-cropped frame.

entries.label: Luminance histogram (256 bins)
entries.description: The full 256-bin luma histogram, emitted as a vector for downstream shape analysis.
entries.frame_evidence: The literal tone distribution of the frame.
entries.detector_note: cv2.calcHist([Y],[0],None,[256],[0,256]); normalise by pixel count.

entries.label: Mean luminance
entries.description: Average perceptual brightness of the frame in Rec.601 luma.
entries.frame_evidence: The frame reads overall dark, mid, or bright to the eye.
entries.detector_note: Y = cv2.cvtColor(bgr, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY) (Rec.601 luma); float(Y.mean()); report on 0-255 and normalised 0-1.
entries.notes: Rec.601 luma is not linear light; do not call this 'exposure' in stops without linearising.

entries.label: Luminance percentile ladder
entries.description: Luma value at p0.1/p1/p5/p25/p50/p75/p95/p99/p99.9, the printing-style level ladder; p50 is the median.
entries.frame_evidence: Where the shadows sit, where the highlights sit, and how far apart they are.

entries.label: Luminance histogram shape moments
entries.description: Third and fourth moments of the luma distribution: tonal skew toward shadow or highlight, and peakedness.
entries.frame_evidence: A night frame with a few practicals skews strongly positive.
entries.detector_note: scipy.stats.skew(Y.ravel()) and scipy.stats.kurtosis(Y.ravel(), fisher=True).

entries.label: Luminance standard deviation
entries.description: Spread of the luma histogram, the simplest global contrast proxy.
entries.frame_evidence: A flat foggy frame has low spread; a hard-lit frame has high spread.
entries.detector_note: float(Y.std()) on the float32 luma array.
entries.notes: Identical to rms_contrast up to normalisation; keep both only for reporting continuity.

entries.label: Michelson contrast
entries.description: (Imax-Imin)/(Imax+Imin) on robust percentile extremes, plus the interpretable p95/p05 ratio.
entries.frame_evidence: The peak-to-trough tonal swing of the frame.
entries.detector_note: hi=np.percentile(Y,99); lo=np.percentile(Y,1); (hi-lo)/(hi+lo+1e-6); ratio = np.percentile(Y,95)/max(np.percentile(Y,5),1.0).
entries.notes: Use percentiles not true min/max, or a single hot pixel sets the value.

entries.label: Independent motion blobs
entries.description: Connected components of the residual motion mask, with their bounding boxes and areas.
entries.frame_evidence: Distinct things moving separately within the frame.
entries.detector_note: Threshold the residual, cv2.morphologyEx OPEN then CLOSE with a 5x5 ellipse, cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats; keep components > 0.05% of frame area.
entries.notes: Blobs are not objects: one character often fragments into 3-4 blobs (head, hands, coat hem) because flat interiors carry no flow.

entries.label: Per-blob velocity
entries.description: Mean flow vector inside each motion blob after global compensation.
entries.frame_evidence: How fast and in what direction each independent mover is going.
entries.detector_note: Mean of (flow - global_flow_model) over each blob mask; report speed in px per unique cel and direction in degrees.

entries.label: Blur directionality
entries.description: Anisotropy of the gradient structure tensor: whether blur is directional (motion) or isotropic (defocus).
entries.frame_evidence: Streaks running one way across a moving limb versus an evenly soft background.
entries.detector_note: Structure tensor from cv2.Sobel products smoothed with cv2.GaussianBlur; eigenvalues l1>=l2; anisotropy=(l1-l2)/(l1+l2); dominant angle = 0.5*atan2(2*Jxy, Jxx-Jyy).

entries.label: Motion blur streak length
entries.description: Estimated blur kernel length in pixels from the cepstral/autocorrelation notch spacing.
entries.frame_evidence: How far a moving object smeared within one exposure.
entries.detector_note: Log power spectrum of a patch, inverse FFT to the cepstrum, find the first off-centre peak along the dominant blur angle; length = distance to that peak.
entries.notes: Unreliable on textured or low-contrast patches; only run it inside high-anisotropy regions and report the confidence.

entries.label: Parallax layer count
entries.description: Number of distinct coherent global-velocity layers, the multiplane/parallax signature.
entries.frame_evidence: Background, midground and foreground sliding at three different speeds.
entries.detector_note: Cluster the flow vectors of tracked corners by velocity using cv2.kmeans over (vx,vy) for K=1..4 and pick K by the elbow in compactness; require each cluster to be spatially contiguous.
entries.notes: Two layers is also what a single moving subject on a static BG produces; the discriminator is that a parallax layer is spatially BANDED (usually by depth/height), not a compact blob.

entries.label: Negative space fraction
entries.description: Fraction of frame occupied by low-detail, low-saliency emptiness.
entries.frame_evidence: Large empty sky or wall giving the subject room.
entries.detector_note: Fraction of 16x16 tiles with both detail energy below the 20th percentile and saliency below the 20th percentile of the shot.
entries.notes: Percentile thresholds must be taken over the SHOT, not the frame, or every frame has 20% negative space by construction.

entries.label: Noise sigma estimate
entries.description: Estimated additive noise standard deviation via robust wavelet detail statistics.
entries.frame_evidence: The grain or sensor-noise level sitting on top of the picture.
entries.detector_note: skimage.restoration.estimate_sigma(rgb, channel_axis=-1, average_sigmas=False); ALSO the flat-tile version: take the 10% of 32x32 tiles with the lowest gradient energy and use sigma = 1.4826*MAD of their high-pass residual.
entries.notes: Fine texture is indistinguishable from noise on a SINGLE frame; the trustworthy version is the temporal one (temporal_noise_sigma) measured on static regions across a unique-cel pair.

entries.label: Noise spatial uniformity
entries.description: Variation of the local noise estimate across the frame: uniform grain versus patchy denoising.
entries.frame_evidence: Smeared, plasticky patches where a denoiser worked hard next to grainy patches where it did not.
entries.detector_note: Per-tile MAD-based sigma; report std/mean across tiles and the min/max ratio.
entries.notes: Strong evidence of temporal denoising or AI upscaling when the ratio is extreme.

entries.label: Dense optical flow field
entries.description: Per-pixel motion vectors between adjacent unique cels.
entries.frame_evidence: Where and how fast every part of the picture moved.
entries.detector_note: cv2.calcOpticalFlowFarneback(prev_gray, next_gray, None, pyr_scale=0.5, levels=3, winsize=15, iterations=3, poly_n=5, poly_sigma=1.2, flags=0); cross-check with cv2.DISOpticalFlow_create(cv2.DISOPTICAL_FLOW_PRESET_MEDIUM).calc.
entries.notes: Temporal metric: must be computed on UNIQUE-CEL index pairs, never raw frame pairs, or held drawings inject artefactual zeros. Farneback is also blind to motion inside FLAT FILL regions - an anime character sliding across a flat colour area yields zero flow in its interior and flow only at its outline.

entries.label: Oversaturated pixel fraction
entries.description: Fraction of pixels with S above 0.95 and V above 0.5, i.e. pinned chroma.
entries.frame_evidence: Neon or heavily graded regions where hue detail has been crushed out.
entries.detector_note: ((S > 0.95) & (V > 0.5)).mean() on the HSV planes.

entries.label: Absolute frame difference
entries.description: Mean, p95 and max of the per-pixel absolute difference between adjacent unique cels.
entries.frame_evidence: How much of the picture literally changed between the two drawings.
entries.detector_note: d = cv2.absdiff(a_gray, b_gray); float(d.mean()), np.percentile(d,95), int(d.max()).
entries.notes: Temporal metric: must be computed on UNIQUE-CEL index pairs, never raw frame pairs, or held drawings inject artefactual zeros.

entries.label: Peak signal-to-noise ratio
entries.description: PSNR in dB between adjacent frames, dominated by codec noise on held cels.
entries.frame_evidence: How close to identical the two frames are on a log scale.
entries.detector_note: cv2.PSNR(a, b) or skimage.metrics.peak_signal_noise_ratio(a, b, data_range=255).
entries.notes: On held anime cels PSNR measures the CODEC, not the animation; useful precisely for calibrating the near-duplicate threshold.

entries.label: Structural similarity (SSIM)
entries.description: SSIM between adjacent unique cels, plus the SSIM map for localising change.
entries.frame_evidence: Structural rather than pixelwise similarity between the two frames.
entries.detector_note: skimage.metrics.structural_similarity(a_gray, b_gray, full=True, data_range=255, gaussian_weights=True, sigma=1.5); or cv2.quality.QualitySSIM_create(a).compute(b).
entries.notes: Temporal metric: must be computed on UNIQUE-CEL index pairs, never raw frame pairs, or held drawings inject artefactual zeros.

entries.label: Per-channel clipping fraction
entries.description: Clipping measured separately in B, G and R, which catches single-channel saturation.
entries.frame_evidence: A red flare where only the red channel has pinned while G and B still hold detail.
entries.detector_note: for c in range(3): (bgr[...,c] >= 254).mean() and (bgr[...,c] <= 1).mean().
entries.notes: Single-channel clipping is the usual cause of hue shifts inside bright areas.

entries.label: Per-channel gamma estimate
entries.description: Exponent that maps each channel's normalised histogram to a uniform reference, a proxy for tone-curve shape.
entries.frame_evidence: One channel visibly lifted or crushed relative to the other two.
entries.detector_note: For each channel: g = log(mean(c/255) + 1e-6)/log(0.5) under a mid-grey-scene assumption; also fit c_out = c_in**g by least squares between the channel CDF and the luma CDF.
entries.notes: This has NO null model on a single frame - it assumes an average scene reflectance of mid grey. Only the CHANNEL SPREAD (a relative quantity) is trustworthy; the absolute gamma is not.

entries.label: Perceptual hash distance
entries.description: Hamming distance between the pHash of adjacent frames, a robust coarse-change measure.
entries.frame_evidence: Whether the frames depict essentially the same picture.
entries.detector_note: h = cv2.img_hash.pHash(frame); dist = cv2.norm(h1, h2, cv2.NORM_HAMMING); also cv2.img_hash.blockMeanHash and cv2.img_hash.colorMomentHash for cross-checks.
entries.notes: The imagehash python package is not installed; cv2.img_hash (contrib) is present and is the right tool.

entries.label: Number of people in frame
entries.description: How many distinct human figures are present.
entries.frame_evidence: Two, three or a crowd of separate people in the shot.
entries.detector_note: Requires a multi-person detector: ultralytics/YOLO is NOT installed, and mediapipe Pose is single-person only. cv2.HOGDescriptor_getDefaultPeopleDetector() exists but is a 2008-era detector with an unusable false-positive rate on stylised content.
entries.notes: Marked as a blind spot deliberately - the single-person Pose solution would silently report 1 for a crowd.

entries.label: Visible pose landmark count
entries.description: Number of the 33 body landmarks returned above a visibility threshold.
entries.frame_evidence: How much of a body is visible and resolvable in frame.
entries.detector_note: mediapipe.solutions.pose.Pose(static_image_mode=True, model_complexity=2); count landmarks with .visibility > 0.5.
entries.notes: mediapipe Pose is SINGLE-PERSON: in a two-shot it returns one skeleton, often stitched across both people. Never use it as a person counter.

entries.label: Telecine / pulldown cadence
entries.description: Detected repeating duplicate pattern such as 3:2 pulldown or 2:2, indicating a frame-rate conversion.
entries.frame_evidence: A regular repeating rhythm of duplicated and blended frames.
entries.detector_note: Autocorrelate the pair-absdiff time series over lags 2-10; a strong peak at lag 5 with the 3:2 duplicate mask indicates telecine; also detect BLENDED (not duplicated) frames where absdiff is uniformly half of its neighbours.
entries.notes: Blended pulldown frames are NOT duplicates and will pass the unique-cel test while carrying half-motion; they must be excluded from flow measurement separately.

entries.label: Quantised unique-colour count
entries.description: Number of distinct colours surviving a 5-bit-per-channel quantisation.
entries.frame_evidence: Flat cel artwork uses a handful of colours; a photographic frame uses thousands.
entries.detector_note: q = (bgr >> 3); len(np.unique(q.reshape(-1,3), axis=0)); also the count covering 90% of pixels.
entries.notes: One of the strongest cheap 2D-versus-3D/live-action discriminators, but compression noise inflates the count on lossy sources.

entries.label: Radial power spectrum
entries.description: Azimuthally averaged log power spectrum as a function of normalised spatial frequency.
entries.frame_evidence: The frame's energy distribution from coarse structure to fine detail.
entries.detector_note: F = np.fft.fftshift(np.fft.fft2(Yf * hann2d)); P = |F|**2; bin by radius into 64 rings with np.bincount on the integer radius map.
entries.notes: Always apply a 2D Hann window first or the frame border injects a false cross of energy through the origin.

entries.label: Radial symmetry about centre
entries.description: Consistency of the image under rotation by 360/n degrees about the frame centre, for n in 2..8.
entries.frame_evidence: An explosion, iris or radial burst centred in frame.
entries.detector_note: cv2.warpAffine with cv2.getRotationMatrix2D(centre, 360/n, 1.0); SSIM against the original within an inscribed circular mask.

entries.label: Non-global (residual) motion energy
