entries.description: Motion energy remaining after compensating the global transform: what moved independently of the camera.
entries.frame_evidence: A character moving within a panning frame.
entries.detector_note: warped = cv2.warpAffine(a, M, (w,h)); res = cv2.absdiff(warped, b) masked to the valid warp region; energy = res.mean() and the >threshold area fraction.
entries.notes: Parallax in a 3D scene creates real residual with no independent mover; on 2D multiplane backgrounds the same is true, which is itself a useful multiplane signal.

entries.label: Mosquito / ringing artefact score
entries.description: High-frequency oscillation hugging hard edges, the DCT ringing signature.
entries.frame_evidence: Shimmering fuzz around sharp text or a hard silhouette against a flat background.
entries.detector_note: In an 8px band outside strong Canny edges but inside otherwise flat regions, measure high-pass residual variance and normalise by the flat-region baseline variance.
entries.notes: Very hard to separate from sharpening_overshoot; the discriminator is that ringing OSCILLATES (multiple sign changes) while overshoot is a single lobe.

entries.label: RMS contrast
entries.description: Standard deviation of normalised luma, the standard global contrast definition.
entries.frame_evidence: How far the frame's tones spread away from its own average tone.
entries.detector_note: Yn = Y.astype(np.float32)/255.0; float(Yn.std()).

entries.label: Rolling shutter skew
entries.description: Time-varying horizontal skew from a CMOS rolling shutter during fast pans.
entries.frame_evidence: Vertical poles leaning during a whip pan.
entries.detector_note: Would require separating rolling-shutter skew from genuine perspective shear and from a dutch-tilted subject, which needs either camera metadata (absent) or a calibrated straight-edge reference in frame (not guaranteed).
entries.notes: flow_shear captures the raw signal but cannot attribute it; logged as a known blind spot rather than reported.

entries.label: Rule-of-thirds saliency mass
entries.description: Fraction of saliency mass falling within a radius of the four thirds intersections.
entries.frame_evidence: The subject sitting on a thirds power point rather than dead centre.
entries.detector_note: sal = cv2.saliency.StaticSaliencySpectralResidual_create().computeSaliency(bgr)[1]; sum sal within r=0.1*diagonal of each of (1/3,1/3),(2/3,1/3),(1/3,2/3),(2/3,2/3) divided by total.
entries.notes: Spectral-residual saliency is a low-level attention proxy, NOT a subject detector; on flat anime it fires on line art rather than on the character.

entries.label: Spatial saliency centroid
entries.description: Centre of mass of the saliency map with its dispersion and entropy: where the eye is pulled and how contested the frame is.
entries.frame_evidence: The visual centre of gravity of the frame.
entries.detector_note: Weighted centroid of the spectral-residual saliency map; dispersion = sqrt of the mass-weighted variance / diagonal; entropy = -sum(p log2 p) on a 32x32 pooled, sum-normalised map.

entries.label: Saturation statistics
entries.description: Mean, median, std and percentiles of the HSV S channel across the frame.
entries.frame_evidence: Whether the image reads muted and desaturated or vivid and punchy.
entries.detector_note: hsv = cv2.cvtColor(bgr, cv2.COLOR_BGR2HSV); S = hsv[...,1]/255.0; mean/median/std/p05/p95.
entries.notes: HSV S is undefined for near-black pixels; mask V<16 before computing or shadows drag the mean.

entries.label: Split-tone shadow/highlight hue
entries.description: Separate mean hue of the darkest and brightest tonal thirds: the split-toning signature.
entries.frame_evidence: Cool blue shadows against warm amber highlights.
entries.detector_note: Mask Y<p33 and Y>p66; compute chroma-weighted circular mean hue and mean chroma in each; report the angular difference.

entries.label: Shallow depth-of-field score
entries.description: Contrast between the sharpest and softest tiles, the bokeh/DOF signature.
entries.frame_evidence: A sharp subject cut out against a smoothly dissolved background.
entries.detector_note: log(tile_focus_p95 / max(tile_focus_p20, eps)) on the masked tile focus map.
entries.notes: 3D renders fake this with a post depth-of-field pass and 2D anime with a gaussian on the BG layer; the METRIC cannot tell them apart, only the depth-edge halo can.

entries.label: Sharpening halo / overshoot
entries.description: Amplitude of the bright-dark overshoot pair straddling hard edges, the unsharp-mask signature.
entries.frame_evidence: White outlines glowing along contrast edges.
entries.detector_note: Sample the intensity profile normal to Canny edges; measure max(profile)-plateau_high and plateau_low-min as a fraction of the edge step; report the mean overshoot ratio.
entries.notes: 2D cel line art has genuine dark outlines that are not overshoot; require a matched BRIGHT overshoot on the light side before flagging.

entries.label: Skin-tone chroma fraction
entries.description: Fraction of pixels falling inside the classic YCbCr skin-chroma box.
entries.frame_evidence: How much of the frame is plausibly bare skin.
entries.detector_note: ycrcb = cv2.cvtColor(bgr, cv2.COLOR_BGR2YCrCb); mask = (133<=Cr<=173) & (77<=Cb<=127); mask.mean().
entries.notes: This is a CHROMA RULE, not a skin detector: wood, sand, orange walls and warm-graded anything all fire. Cross-check against face_count_mediapipe before ever reporting it as skin.

entries.label: Spectral anisotropy
entries.description: Angular variation of spectral energy: directional blur, scan lines or anisotropic detail.
entries.frame_evidence: Detail present horizontally but missing vertically (or the reverse).
entries.detector_note: Bin the power spectrum by angle into 36 sectors over 0-180; anisotropy = (max-min)/(max+min); dominant angle = argmax.

entries.label: Periodic spectral peaks (moire/halftone)
entries.description: Isolated off-DC peaks in the spectrum indicating a repeating pattern, screen door, halftone or moire.
entries.frame_evidence: A regular interference pattern crawling over a fine texture.
entries.detector_note: Suppress the radial trend, then find local maxima >6 sigma above the local spectral background; report their frequency, angle and prominence.
entries.notes: Genuine architectural repetition (bricks, screens, fabric) is a real periodic peak; the metric cannot tell it from an artefact.

entries.label: 1/f spectral slope
entries.description: Exponent alpha of the P(f) ~ f^-alpha fit, the natural-image statistic.
entries.frame_evidence: Whether the frame's frequency falloff looks like a photograph (alpha ~2) or like flat graphics.
entries.detector_note: np.polyfit(np.log(f[1:]), np.log(radial_power[1:]), 1); alpha = -slope, fit over f in 0.02-0.4 cycles/px.
entries.notes: Flat-fill 2D animation departs strongly from natural alpha~2; that is content, not degradation.

entries.label: Strobing / judder score
entries.description: Per-cel motion displacement large enough to break the eye's fusion, the strobing signature.
entries.frame_evidence: A pan that steps in visible jumps instead of moving smoothly.
entries.detector_note: flow_mag_median per unique-cel step expressed in frame-widths per second; flag when a coherent pan exceeds roughly 1/7 frame width per 1/24s.
entries.notes: A perceptual rule of thumb, not a measurement of perception; report it as a risk score and never as a defect verdict.

entries.label: Temporal noise sigma
entries.description: Noise standard deviation measured as the frame-to-frame variation of STATIC pixels.
entries.frame_evidence: Grain that dances between frames while the picture beneath it holds still.
entries.detector_note: Over pixels where the residual motion mask is zero across a 5-frame window, sigma = std over time, then take the spatial median of that map.
entries.notes: The ONLY trustworthy noise estimate, because it separates grain from texture in a way a single frame cannot. Requires unique-cel indexing: across a held anime cel the temporal sigma is CODEC noise only.

entries.label: Tenengrad gradient energy
entries.description: Mean squared Sobel gradient magnitude above a threshold, a focus measure less noise-sensitive than Laplacian.
entries.frame_evidence: Amount of well-defined edge energy in the frame.
entries.detector_note: gx=cv2.Sobel(Y,cv2.CV_64F,1,0,ksize=3); gy=cv2.Sobel(Y,cv2.CV_64F,0,1,ksize=3); g2=gx**2+gy**2; float(g2[g2>thr].mean()) with thr set from the shot's median.

entries.label: On-screen text / typography presence
entries.description: Presence, location and extent of rendered text (titles, subtitles, credits, signage).
entries.frame_evidence: Legible glyphs composited over the picture.
entries.detector_note: rapidocr is NOT installed on this interpreter. A deterministic PROXY exists (cv2.MSER_create + stroke-width consistency + horizontal alignment of components) which localises text-like regions but cannot read them.
entries.notes: moondream MUST NOT be asked about text - it confabulates glyphs that are not there. Do not substitute a VLM here.

entries.label: True lens focal length
entries.description: Physical focal length and sensor size behind the framing.
entries.frame_evidence: Perspective compression of depth relative to subject size.
entries.detector_note: Requires EXIF/camera metadata (not present in a decoded frame) or a calibrated scene; the PnP intrinsic used in face_pose_angles is an assumption, not a measurement.
entries.notes: Any 'this is a 35mm lens' claim from pixels alone is a fabrication; kept here so the analyzer refuses to make it.

entries.label: Unique cel index
entries.description: Monotone index assigned to each distinct drawing, collapsing held frames.
entries.frame_evidence: The sequence of actual new drawings underneath the frame rate.
entries.detector_note: Run exact_duplicate_flag across the shot; increment the index only on a non-duplicate; emit a mapping frame_index -> cel_index.
entries.notes: Under lossy compression 'identical' cels differ by a few DCT LSBs; use the near-duplicate test, and validate the threshold against a known live-action clip where the near-duplicate rate must be near zero.

entries.label: Resolution ceiling / upscale evidence
entries.description: Cutoff frequency beyond which spectral energy collapses, revealing the true source resolution.
entries.frame_evidence: A 1080p file whose detail actually stops at 720p worth of frequency.
entries.detector_note: Find the knee where radial_power drops more than 2 decades below its mid-band trend; native_height_est = frame_height * knee_freq / 0.5.
entries.notes: Heavy defocus or motion blur produces the same cliff; only claim upscaling when the cliff is stable ACROSS a shot's sharpest frames.

entries.label: Vanishing point estimate
entries.description: RANSAC intersection of the dominant non-parallel line family, giving a perspective convergence point.
entries.frame_evidence: Receding parallels that converge at a point on or off the frame.
entries.detector_note: Take FLD segments as homogeneous lines (cross product of endpoints); RANSAC for the point minimising algebraic distance; report normalised position and inlier count.
entries.notes: Meaningless below ~8 inlier segments. 2D anime backgrounds often have a HAND-DRAWN, geometrically inconsistent perspective, so a low inlier ratio is a legitimate style signal, not a failure.

entries.label: Top-bottom symmetry
entries.description: Similarity between the frame and its vertical mirror, the reflection signature.
entries.frame_evidence: A landscape reflected in still water.
entries.detector_note: structural_similarity(Y, np.flipud(Y)); also search the best horizontal axis row by sliding the flip.

entries.label: Radial luminance falloff
entries.description: Slope of mean luma against normalised radius from frame centre: optical or added vignette.
entries.frame_evidence: Corners measurably darker than the centre by a smooth radial ramp.
entries.detector_note: Bin pixels by r = hypot((x-cx)/cx,(y-cy)/cy) into 20 rings; np.polyfit(ring_r, ring_mean_Y, 1) slope; also corner_centre_ratio = mean(corner 10% boxes)/mean(centre 20% box).
entries.notes: A dark subject sitting centre-frame inverts this; require the radial fit r2 to exceed ~0.6 before calling it a vignette.

entries.label: White clipping fraction
entries.description: Fraction of pixels at or above the blown-highlight threshold.
entries.frame_evidence: Skies, practicals or bloom areas that have gone featureless white.
entries.detector_note: float((Y >= 254).mean()); also report at 240, 250, 255.

entries.label: Effective white level
entries.description: The p99.9 luma value: whether the frame reaches full white or is capped.
entries.frame_evidence: A frame whose brightest pixel tops out at 230, indicating a limited-range decode.
entries.detector_note: float(np.percentile(Y, 99.9)); compare with 235 to flag a limited-range (16-235) decode.
entries.notes: A 16-235 range decoded as 0-255 (or the reverse) is the single most common false 'grading' finding.

entries.label: Worn accessories and carried bags
entries.description: Jewellery, watches, badges, backpacks, satchels, holsters - things attached to the body that move with it.
entries.frame_evidence: Small high-contrast regions locked to a body zone across cels, with their own secondary sway.
entries.detector_note: Object detection restricted to the person mask; require centroid correlation with the parent body zone above 0.9.

entries.label: Ageing of the same character across shots
entries.description: The same identity rendered at different apparent ages within one piece - a time-jump tell.
entries.frame_evidence: A face embedding matches across shots while the age band, hair colour or skin texture changes.
entries.detector_note: Face embedding similarity above the identity threshold combined with an age-band change of two or more steps, or a grey-hair fraction jump.
entries.notes: Needs the missing per-face identity embedding; see gaps.face_identity_embedding.

entries.label: Extra or missing anatomy
entries.description: Limb, digit or feature counts that violate the body plan - extra arms, a third leg, two pupils.
entries.frame_evidence: The pose skeleton has more chains than the body plan allows, or a limb emerges from an implausible attachment point.
entries.detector_note: Compare the detected landmark topology against the body-plan prior; report every violation with its location. Do not merge with hand_object.finger_count_anomaly - this is the whole-body case.

entries.label: Animal blink
entries.description: An animal eye closing, including the sideways sweep of a nictitating membrane in birds and reptiles.
entries.frame_evidence: A small dark specular point on the head vanishes for one to three cels and returns.
entries.detector_note: Track the brightest small specular blob inside the head crop (the catchlight); a blink is a disappearance lasting 1-3 unique cels with the head pose otherwise unchanged.
entries.notes: The user asked explicitly for natural eye open/close. face_head.blink_natural is human-only and MediaPipe EAR does not fit an animal eye.

entries.label: Ear position and flick
entries.description: Ears forward, flattened back, or flicking - the main non-facial affect channel for most animals.
entries.frame_evidence: Two small protrusions on the head silhouette change angle or disappear into the head outline.
entries.detector_note: No landmark model covers animal ears. Crop the head region from the animal box at >= 128px and ask the VLM. Report a null when the crop is smaller than that.
entries.vlm_question: In this cropped animal head, are the ears pointing up/forward, flattened back against the head, or to the side?

entries.label: Animal grooming or preening
entries.description: Repetitive head-to-body contact motion: licking, preening, scratching.
entries.frame_evidence: The head repeatedly travels to and from a point on the animal's own body with a regular period.
entries.detector_note: Deterministic prior: head-end of the skeleton oscillating toward the body mask interior at 0.5-3 Hz. Confirm with a VLM crop question.
entries.vlm_question: Is this animal licking, preening or scratching itself?

entries.label: Person touching an animal
entries.description: Petting, leading, feeding or restraining an animal.
entries.frame_evidence: A human hand landmark sits within a few pixels of the animal mask boundary for a sustained run.
entries.detector_note: Minimum distance between any hand landmark and the animal mask contour, normalised by shoulder width; contact = below 0.15 for >= 3 unique cels. Verify with the contact-shadow cue.

entries.label: Leash, rein or tether between person and animal
entries.description: A thin line linking a hand to an animal, and whether it is slack or taut.
entries.frame_evidence: A thin elongated structure whose two endpoints lie on a hand and on an animal, sagging or straight.
entries.detector_note: Line/curve detection between the hand landmark and the animal bbox; classify slack vs taut from the sagitta of the fitted curve relative to the endpoint distance.
entries.notes: The taut/slack alternation is what sells pulling; a rigid straight tether that never sags is a CG tell.

entries.label: Animal mouth open or panting
entries.description: An open animal mouth, including rhythmic panting.
entries.frame_evidence: A dark aperture in the head silhouette that opens and closes at a steady rate, often with a visible tongue.
entries.detector_note: Head crop plus a deterministic aperture-area oscillation test on the darkest connected component inside the crop; panting = oscillation 2-6 Hz.
entries.vlm_question: Is this animal's mouth open? Is its tongue out?
entries.notes: face_head is human-only; every mouth entry there assumes a mediapipe face mesh that will not fit an animal.

entries.label: Animal present and coarse class
entries.description: Any non-human animal in frame, classified to a coarse body plan (quadruped, bird, fish, insect, reptile, other).
entries.frame_evidence: A non-human body silhouette with a limb count, body axis and head position that do not fit the human pose prior.
entries.detector_note: COCO-class detector (yolo/detr) for bird,cat,dog,horse,sheep,cow,elephant,bear,zebra,giraffe; anything outside the set falls back to a VLM body-plan question. Gate: mediapipe pose must NOT fit the same box.
entries.vlm_question: How many non-human animals are in this image, and for each, is it a four-legged animal, a bird, a fish, an insect, a reptile, or something else?
entries.notes: scene_semantics.animal_presence_any only asks yes/no. Every downstream animal metric needs the body plan first.

entries.label: Animal carrying a rider
entries.description: A person coupled to and moving with an animal - horse, camel, elephant.
entries.frame_evidence: A human pose sits above the animal mask with its hip landmark inside the animal's upper silhouette and its centroid locked to the animal's over time.
entries.detector_note: Require a mediapipe pose whose hip midpoint lies within the animal bbox upper third, and whose camera-compensated centroid correlates with the animal centroid at r > 0.9 over >= 10 cels.
entries.notes: Also gives the classic tell for bad CG: a rider whose bounce does not match the gait period.

entries.label: Tail carriage and posture
entries.description: Static tail position (high, level, tucked) as distinct from a tail swing.
entries.frame_evidence: A thin appendage extending from the rear of the animal mask, held at a stable angle over many cels.
entries.detector_note: Skeletonise the animal mask, take the branch furthest from the head end, and report its mean angle to the body axis and its angular variance over the shot.
entries.notes: body_action.tail_swing covers motion only. A tucked, still tail is a strong state signal and reads as 'no detection' today.

entries.label: Per-animal track identity
entries.description: A stable id for each animal across the shot so gait and behaviour are attributed to one body.
entries.frame_evidence: The same animal silhouette recurs at nearby positions across consecutive cels.
entries.detector_note: IoU + appearance-embedding tracker over the animal detections; break the track on an occlusion longer than 6 unique cels and report the break rather than bridging it.
entries.notes: Without this, quadruped_gait_classification cannot say WHICH animal is trotting in a two-animal frame.

entries.label: Archive or different-format insert
entries.description: A shot from a different source: different resolution ceiling, grain, aspect, cadence or codec signature.
entries.frame_evidence: One shot's native-resolution estimate, grain spectral slope and cadence all differ sharply from the surrounding shots.
entries.detector_note: Per-shot vector of native_resolution_estimate, grain_spectral_slope, pulldown cadence and active aspect; an insert is a single-shot outlier on three or more of them.

entries.label: Per-frame audio level and spectral flux
entries.description: Loudness and spectral change aligned to each video frame, so any visual event can be checked against sound.
entries.frame_evidence: Not visible - the audio track resampled to the frame grid.
entries.detector_note: Per-frame RMS, short-term LUFS and spectral flux from the audio stream, indexed by frame number so audio-visual offsets are exact.
entries.notes: editing_time has an onset track and a beat grid but no continuous level, so 'the music swells here' is unmeasurable.

entries.label: Silence, dropout and clipping in the audio
entries.description: Frames where the audio is silent, clipped, or drops out entirely.
entries.frame_evidence: Not visible - an audio-track property reported on the frame grid.
entries.detector_note: Per-frame peak and RMS; silence = below -60 dBFS, clipping = sample peaks at full scale, dropout = a silence run bounded by non-silence within one shot.

entries.label: Global audio-video sync offset
entries.description: The whole file's sound running ahead of or behind the picture.
entries.frame_evidence: Every measured impact and every lip closure lands consistently early or late.
entries.detector_note: Cross-correlate the impact-frame series and the lip-closure series against the audio onset track over the whole file; report the single best global offset and its consistency.
entries.notes: editing_time.audio_visual_impact_sync_offset is per event. A GLOBAL constant offset is a delivery defect and needs one number for the whole file.

entries.label: Figure present in the background
entries.description: A person or shape standing in the background that no in-frame subject reacts to.
entries.frame_evidence: A small person-like detection at low contrast, static, in the depth background, with no subject gaze directed at it.
entries.detector_note: Person detection below the principal size threshold with near-zero motion, in the defocused or distant depth band, and outside every subject's gaze cone.
entries.notes: The horror staple, and a real defect check too - a crew member standing in the back of a plate.

entries.label: Something moves in the background
entries.description: A localised motion in the depth background while the foreground subject is still.
entries.frame_evidence: A small isolated residual-motion blob far from the subject, in a region that is otherwise static.
entries.detector_note: Residual (camera-compensated) motion blobs outside every subject mask, in the upper depth band, above the shot's own background motion floor.
entries.notes: Directly measurable and currently unreachable: motion_blob_segmentation exists but is never partitioned into subject and background.

entries.label: Background warping as the camera moves
entries.description: Static scenery that bends, breathes or reorganises during a camera move - geometry that was never real.
entries.frame_evidence: Straight architectural lines curve and straighten as the camera pans; the background's structure is not rigid.
entries.detector_note: Fit a homography to the background between cels and report the residual after warping; a rigid scene has a small structured residual, a hallucinated one has a large smooth non-rigid residual.

entries.label: Ball or game object track
entries.description: A small roughly circular object with an independent ballistic or bouncing trajectory.
entries.frame_evidence: A compact high-circularity blob moving independently of every person, with a parabolic or bouncing path.
entries.detector_note: Circular blob detection with circularity > 0.8 and area within a plausible band; track it; require the track to be independent of every person mask for at least part of its life.
entries.notes: object_dynamics covers ballistics generically but nothing identifies the sports object or separates it from debris.

entries.label: Possession and possession change
entries.description: Which person is in contact with or controlling the game object, and when that changes.
entries.frame_evidence: The ball track's distance to a person's hand or foot goes to near zero and its velocity becomes that person's velocity.
entries.detector_note: Minimum ball-to-extremity distance normalised by body height; possession = below 0.1 with velocity correlation above 0.8; a change is a transfer between two different tracks.

entries.label: Bandage, cast or dressing on a body
entries.description: A high-luminance low-chroma wrap on a limb or head.
entries.frame_evidence: A bright near-neutral band across a limb, with a texture distinct from both skin and the character's clothing.
entries.detector_note: Bright low-saturation region inside the person mask that crosses a limb axis perpendicular; confirm with VLM.
entries.vlm_question: Is this person wearing a bandage, a cast or a medical dressing? Where?

entries.label: Bird flapping versus gliding
entries.description: Whether a flying animal is beating its wings or holding them fixed and gliding.
entries.frame_evidence: The silhouette's width oscillates periodically (flap) or stays constant while the body translates (glide).
entries.detector_note: Track the animal mask's width perpendicular to the travel axis per unique cel; run scipy.signal.periodogram. Flap = dominant peak with amplitude > 15% of mean width; glide = amplitude < 5% over >= 8 cels.
entries.notes: body_action.wing_flap_cycle only covers the flap. Gliding, hovering and soaring are separate and very common.

entries.label: Limp or unconscious body
entries.description: A body with no voluntary muscle tone: head unsupported, limbs hanging, motion driven only by an external force.
entries.frame_evidence: The head lolls with the torso rather than stabilising, and limb motion lags the torso with no anticipation.
entries.detector_note: Head-to-torso angular stabilisation ratio near zero, limb phase lag positive on every chain, and zero anticipation events over the shot.
entries.notes: body_action.ragdoll_tumble covers the tumble; a carried or lying unconscious body is different and more common.

entries.label: Subject growing or shrinking
entries.description: A subject's real size changing relative to the scene, as distinct from moving closer to camera.
entries.frame_evidence: The subject's height grows while its ground-contact point stays at the same depth and the background scale is unchanged.
entries.detector_note: Subject height in pixels rises while the ground-plane row of its foot contact stays fixed and the global scale term of the camera model is near 1.
entries.notes: This is exactly the measurement that separates a giant from a dolly-in, and it is missing.

entries.label: Boiling over or spilling from a vessel
entries.description: Liquid or foam crossing the vessel rim and running down the outside.
entries.frame_evidence: The foam or liquid mask crosses the detected rim contour and new rivulets appear on the exterior.
entries.detector_note: Rim contour from the vessel mask; fire when foam/liquid mask pixels appear outside the rim and are connected to the interior mass, followed by runoff rivulets.

entries.label: Bowing stroke cycle
entries.description: A long thin implement drawn back and forth across a fixed body at a musical rate.
entries.frame_evidence: A thin line translates along its own perpendicular with regular direction reversals.
entries.detector_note: Track the bow's principal axis and its lateral position; report reversal rate, stroke length and the dwell at each reversal.

entries.label: Food browning during cooking
entries.description: A cooking surface darkening and shifting warm over time - the visual proof that heat is being applied.
entries.frame_evidence: The food region's mean luminance falls and its hue rotates toward orange-brown monotonically across many cels.
entries.detector_note: On a homography-stabilised food ROI, fit luminance and hue against cel index; browning = negative luminance slope with hue rotation toward 20-35 deg and r2 > 0.6, sustained over >= 20 cels.
entries.notes: Same machinery as fluids_fire.charring_blackening but slower and without a fire mask adjacency requirement.

entries.label: Bruising or swelling progression
entries.description: A body region darkening, purpling or growing over a sequence.
entries.frame_evidence: A skin region's hue rotates toward purple and its local silhouette bulges, monotonically over many cels.
entries.detector_note: Per-zone skin hue and local contour deviation from the character's clean baseline, with a monotonicity requirement. Needs identity tracking.

entries.label: Hair and cloth behaving buoyantly
entries.description: Hair and fabric floating outward and settling slowly, with heavy damping and no gravity droop.
entries.frame_evidence: Hair spreads away from the head rather than hanging, and its settle takes many times longer than in air.
entries.detector_note: Hair region's mean radial extent from the head centre stays high with the head static, and the settle time constant after a motion is above 1 second.
entries.notes: object_dynamics.hair_sway_lag assumes air. Buoyant hair is the single most-failed underwater CG element.

entries.label: Camera moving through a crowd
entries.description: Bodies passing close to the lens on both sides while the camera advances.
entries.frame_evidence: Large fast-moving out-of-focus person-shaped masses transit the frame edges while the centre advances.
entries.detector_note: Strong positive flow divergence (forward motion) combined with recurring large defocused masks crossing the left and right thirds.

entries.label: Carbonation in a drink
entries.description: Fine bubbles rising continuously through a transparent liquid, with a foam head.
entries.frame_evidence: A dense field of tiny bright points inside a vessel, all travelling upward, with a bright band at the surface.
entries.detector_note: Sub-5px bright blob field inside the vessel mask with mean vertical velocity upward and size CV low; foam head = a bright horizontal band at the liquid surface.

entries.label: Infant carried by an adult
entries.description: An infant body whose motion is locked to an adult's torso.
entries.frame_evidence: A small body overlapping an adult's chest or hip whose centroid tracks the adult's across cels.
entries.detector_note: Centroid correlation between the small-person box and the adult torso midpoint > 0.9 with a persistent bbox overlap.

entries.label: Character transformation sequence
entries.description: A subject changing form, costume or scale within a continuous shot or a dedicated stock sequence.
entries.frame_evidence: The same tracked subject's silhouette, palette and proportions change substantially while the identity track holds.
entries.detector_note: Identity track maintained across a run in which the person mask's shape descriptor and dominant palette both change beyond the shot's own variability; require the track never to break.
entries.notes: The magical-girl case: the taxonomy has auras, glow and dissolve shaders but no entry for the transformation itself.

entries.label: Energy charge-up on a subject or prop
entries.description: Light and particles converging inward toward a point before a release.
entries.frame_evidence: Flow vectors in the effect region point inward toward a common centre while the region's luminance climbs.
entries.detector_note: Negative flow divergence in the effect region with a rising mean luminance, followed by a sign reversal at the release cel.
entries.notes: anime_2d.aura_energy_charge_convergence covers 2D only; the same measurement works on any medium.

entries.label: Breathing rate and depth
entries.description: The rise and fall of the chest and shoulders - present, absent, fast, or heaving.
entries.frame_evidence: A low-amplitude periodic vertical oscillation of the shoulder landmarks with no other body motion.
entries.detector_note: Shoulder-midpoint vertical series after camera compensation; periodogram in the 0.1-1.0 Hz band; report rate and amplitude relative to shoulder width.
entries.notes: body_action.idle_breathing_micromotion detects motion but does not report a RATE, and 'not breathing' is a deliberate storytelling state.

entries.label: Child-to-adult height pairing
entries.description: Two people whose height ratio marks one as a child - and the framing consequences (eyeline offset, look up/down).
entries.frame_evidence: Two standing figures on the same ground plane with a height ratio below 0.8.
entries.detector_note: Both subjects' ankle landmarks on a fitted ground line; ratio of head-top to ankle heights. Pair with interaction_social.height_level_asymmetry.

entries.label: Repetitive chopping or slicing
entries.description: A blade descending on a board at a regular rate with the material dividing under it.
entries.frame_evidence: The tool tip's vertical position oscillates with a sharp bottom, and the material region below gains new boundaries.
entries.detector_note: hand_object.tool_tip_trajectory periodicity plus a rising count of connected components in the board ROI across cels.
entries.notes: hand_object.cut_with_blade is a single VLM-tier event; repetitive food prep is a rate.

entries.label: Burn-length continuity of a cigarette or candle
entries.description: A burning object getting longer, or not getting shorter, across a sequence.
entries.frame_evidence: The measured length of the thin bright body between the hand and the ember changes non-monotonically.
entries.detector_note: Track the elongated component between the grip point and the detected ember; report its length per cel; flag any increase beyond noise.
entries.notes: The user named cigarettes explicitly. hand_object covers holding and lifting one but nothing measures the thing burning down.

entries.label: Visible clock or timer continuity
entries.description: A clock face or digital time display that runs backward, freezes, or jumps.
entries.frame_evidence: The hand angles or the digits on a detected clock are inconsistent with the elapsed running time.
entries.detector_note: Detect the clock region; for an analogue face measure the hand angles by line fitting, for a digital display OCR the digits; compare the implied elapsed time with the actual elapsed frames.

entries.label: Everyone looks the same way off-screen
entries.description: Two or more subjects turning their gaze or heads toward the same off-frame point within a short window.
entries.frame_evidence: Multiple head-yaw traces move toward the same frame edge within a few cels of each other.
entries.detector_note: Cluster the per-subject gaze rays' off-frame intersection points; fire when >= 2 subjects agree within 15 deg inside a 6-cel window.
entries.notes: interaction_social.reaction_to_offscreen_event covers a body reaction; the synchronised LOOK is the more common and earlier cue.

entries.label: Conducting or beat-keeping gesture
entries.description: A hand tracing a repeating beat pattern in the air, phase-locked to the audio beat grid.
entries.frame_evidence: The wrist path repeats a closed figure at the musical tempo.
entries.detector_note: Wrist trajectory autocorrelation period compared against editing_time.musical_beat_grid; report the phase offset.

entries.label: Bright-source count and distribution
entries.description: How many distinct bright sources or highlights the frame contains, and how they are spread.
entries.frame_evidence: Multiple separated bright blobs against a darker field.
entries.detector_note: Threshold at the 99th luminance percentile, label connected components above a minimum area, and report count, area distribution and spatial dispersion.
entries.notes: lighting.light_source_count_estimate is marked unsupported for the physical setup; the IMAGE-side count is trivially measurable and useful.

entries.label: Reflection in the eyes
entries.description: What is reflected in the subject's eye - a light source, a screen, a figure.
entries.frame_evidence: Structured (non-round) content inside the catchlight rather than a plain highlight.
entries.detector_note: Crop the iris from iris landmarks at >= 24px; a plain catchlight is a compact blob, structured content shows multiple components or an elongated shape. Report shape, not identity.
entries.notes: lighting.catchlight_count_and_shape reports shape; nothing asks whether the shape is a WINDOW, a RING LIGHT or a FIGURE, which is what sells a look.

entries.label: Cough, sneeze or convulsive spasm
entries.description: A sharp involuntary whole-body impulse with a fast forward head snap and recovery.
entries.frame_evidence: A single-cel head and torso jerk with a large acceleration spike and no external contact.
entries.detector_note: Head + torso acceleration spike above 4 robust sigma with no contact event and no camera impulse in the same cel; followed by a return within 5 cels.

entries.label: Chest compression or resuscitation
entries.description: Rhythmic vertical hand pressure on a supine body's chest.
entries.frame_evidence: Two stacked hands oscillate vertically at about 2 Hz over a horizontal body that does not otherwise move.
entries.detector_note: Bimanual stacked-hand configuration over a supine person mask with vertical oscillation in the 1.5-2.5 Hz band.

entries.label: Non-standard limb count on a creature
entries.description: A body plan with a limb count that is neither bipedal nor quadrupedal: six legs, tentacles, multiple heads, wings plus arms.
entries.frame_evidence: The mask skeleton has more terminal branches than any human or quadruped prior allows.
entries.detector_note: Skeletonise the subject mask and count terminal branches longer than 15% of the body length as a prior; adjudicate the actual body plan with a VLM.
entries.vlm_question: Describe this creature's body plan: how many legs, how many arms, does it have wings, a tail, tentacles, more than one head?
entries.notes: Cross-check with the creature body-plan lock: a front-facing anchor hides a tail, so a per-view agreement gate is required before trusting a count.

entries.label: Creature scale relative to a human
entries.description: Whether the creature reads as smaller than, comparable to, or vastly larger than a person in the same frame.
entries.frame_evidence: The creature's height in pixels versus a detected human's height in the same depth plane.
entries.detector_note: Requires a human pose in frame on a shared ground plane; ratio = creature bbox height / human bbox height, reported only when both feet contacts are visible.
entries.notes: Null when there is no human reference. Absolute scale stays unsupported, as scene_semantics already says.

entries.label: Crew, rig or equipment in frame
entries.description: A boom mic, light stand, crew member, camera or rig shadow appearing where it should not.
entries.frame_evidence: An object intruding at a frame edge or a distinctive shadow shape that belongs to no scene element.
entries.detector_note: VLM question over the frame edges and the top band, plus a deterministic prior: a dark elongated intrusion from the top edge that moves with the dialogue rhythm is a boom.
entries.vlm_question: Is there any filming equipment visible in this image - a microphone boom, a light, a stand, a camera, a crew member, or a reflection of one?
entries.notes: post_fx.paint_out_and_rig_removal detects the FIX. Nothing detects the problem.

entries.label: Cross-cutting between two locations
entries.description: Alternation between two distinct settings, implying simultaneity.
entries.frame_evidence: Shots alternate between two clusters in embedding space, ABAB, over several cycles.
entries.detector_note: Cluster shots by frame embedding; cross-cutting = an alternating cluster sequence with at least two full ABAB cycles and low within-cluster distance.
entries.notes: editing_time.shot_reverse_shot_pattern covers two ANGLES of one place; two PLACES is a different structure and a very common one.

entries.label: Crowd applause, cheering or raised arms
entries.description: Many subjects raising arms or clapping roughly together.
entries.frame_evidence: A large fraction of the crowd's upper regions show synchronised vertical motion above the head line.
entries.detector_note: Above-head-line motion energy as a fraction of crowd area, with cross-subject phase coherence; report the fraction participating and the synchrony.

entries.label: Background person looking at camera
entries.description: A background figure whose gaze is aimed at the lens - almost always an error.
entries.frame_evidence: A non-principal subject's head is frontal with gaze near zero yaw toward the camera.
entries.detector_note: Run gaze estimation on all detections below the principal size threshold; fire when a background subject holds camera-directed gaze for >= 4 unique cels.
entries.notes: interaction_social.mutual_gaze covers subject-to-subject; face_head.eye_contact_camera is not applied to background extras.

entries.label: Subject lost and found in a crowd
entries.description: The tracked principal disappearing behind other bodies and reappearing.
entries.frame_evidence: The principal's track breaks while its last position is overlapped by other subject masks, then resumes nearby.
entries.detector_note: Track break with a same-cel overlap by another subject mask above 60%, followed by a re-identification within 20 cels and 20% of frame width.

entries.label: Objects held above a crowd
entries.description: Signs, phones, weapons, umbrellas or torches held above head height by many people.
entries.frame_evidence: A field of small distinct shapes above the crowd head line, moving with individual bodies.
entries.detector_note: Detect the crowd head line from the detection tops; count connected components above it that track with individual subjects.

entries.label: Pedalling or rowing cadence
entries.description: A cyclic lower-limb or upper-limb motion driven by a machine rather than by ground contact.
entries.frame_evidence: Knee angle oscillates periodically with no footfall events and no vertical centre-of-mass bob.
entries.detector_note: Knee-angle periodogram with the constraint that foot_ground_contact never fires and com_vertical_trajectory amplitude is below a walking threshold.
entries.notes: body_action.locomotion_gait assumes ground contact; a cyclist would currently be scored as a failed walk.

entries.label: Speaking to someone who is never shown
entries.description: A subject articulating and gaze-holding toward a fixed off-frame point over a sustained run, with no reverse shot in the scene.
entries.frame_evidence: Sustained speaking activity with gaze locked off-frame and no cut to a second subject in the scene group.
entries.detector_note: Combine speaking_activity, gaze_toward_offscreen stability, and the absence of a shot/reverse-shot partner within the scene grouping.

entries.label: Trail through vegetation, dust or water
entries.description: A body's passage leaving a temporary disturbance that recovers - parted grass, a wake, a dust trail.
entries.frame_evidence: A disturbance region trails behind the subject and relaxes back over several seconds.
entries.detector_note: Region behind the subject's path with elevated motion energy that decays exponentially after passage; report the decay time constant.

entries.label: Kneading, folding or shaping a soft mass
entries.description: Two hands repeatedly deforming a plastic mass that holds its new shape.
entries.frame_evidence: A soft region changes outline under bimanual contact and does not spring back.
entries.detector_note: Bimanual role-differentiated contact plus a region whose shape changes and whose post-contact outline is stable (no elastic return within 5 cels).
entries.notes: object_dynamics.soft_body_contact_deform assumes a rebound; plastic deformation is the opposite test.

entries.label: Small aerial drone in the scene
entries.description: A hovering multi-rotor machine as scene content (not the camera platform).
entries.frame_evidence: A small rigid body holding station with blurred discs at its corners.
entries.detector_note: gaps.hover_stationary_flight plus detection of two or more rotor blur discs (low-variance circular regions with high internal blur) at symmetric offsets from the body.
entries.notes: object_dynamics.rotor_blur_disc exists but is attached to nothing.

entries.label: Drum or percussion strike
entries.description: An implement striking a membrane, with the membrane or cymbal responding.
entries.frame_evidence: A stick tip decelerates hard at a surface and the surface shows a short high-frequency wobble afterward.
entries.detector_note: hand_object.tool_impact_frame restricted to a detected circular surface, plus a post-impact oscillation in the surface region lasting 2-8 cels.

entries.label: Dust settling after destruction
entries.description: The slow clearing phase after an impact or collapse: haze decreasing, contrast returning.
entries.frame_evidence: Dark-channel haze falls monotonically over many cels with slow downward particulate motion.
entries.detector_note: Track frame_metrics.haze_dark_channel over the shot after a detected impact; settling = a monotonic decrease over >= 30 cels with downward mean particle velocity.

entries.label: Elderly or infirm gait markers
entries.description: Reduced stride, wider base, stooped trunk, shuffling contact, or a walking aid.
entries.frame_evidence: Short stride relative to leg length, forward trunk lean held throughout, low foot clearance in swing.
entries.detector_note: From the existing gait primitives: stride_length_norm below 0.5 leg lengths, torso_pitch_lean above 15 deg sustained, and swing-phase ankle clearance below 3% of body height.
entries.notes: body_action.limp_gait_asymmetry covers injury; age gait is symmetric and slow, a different signature.

entries.label: Elemental effect (ice, wind, stone, plant)
entries.description: A non-fire, non-water elemental effect: spikes of ice forming, a wind vortex, stone erupting, vines growing.
entries.frame_evidence: New geometry grows outward from a point along a directional axis over a short run.
entries.detector_note: Growth detection: a new mask region expanding from an origin with a directional bias, gated by a VLM class question. The growth measurement is deterministic; the element is not.
entries.vlm_question: What kind of effect is appearing here - ice, wind, stone, plants, lightning, or something else?

entries.label: Semantic drift inside one shot
entries.description: How far the content of a shot travels from its own first frame - the honest measure of whether a shot 'changes'.
entries.frame_evidence: Not visible directly; shows as a rising distance from the shot's opening embedding.
entries.detector_note: Cosine distance from the shot's first unique cel embedding to each subsequent one; report the max, the slope and whether it is monotonic.

entries.label: Empty frame becoming occupied
entries.description: A shot that begins with no subject and gains one without a cut.
entries.frame_evidence: Zero person detections for a sustained opening run, then a persistent detection, with no cut boundary between.
entries.detector_note: Subject-count time series within one shot: a transition from 0 to >= 1 sustained for 6 cels, with the cut boundary list confirming a single shot.
entries.notes: Pairs with gaps.teleport_appear_disappear: entry from a border is staging, entry mid-frame is a defect or an effect.

entries.label: Impact ripple on a shield or barrier
entries.description: A concentric disturbance expanding across a curved barrier surface from a hit point.
entries.frame_evidence: Concentric rings expand from a point across a translucent curved region and decay.
entries.detector_note: Polar-unwrap around the hit point inside the barrier region; a ripple shows a radial luminance wave with an expanding radius and decaying amplitude.

entries.label: Energy projectile
entries.description: A self-luminous object travelling through the scene with a trailing tail and a cast glow.
entries.frame_evidence: A saturated emissive blob on a smooth path with a fading tail behind it and a matching brightening of nearby surfaces.
entries.detector_note: Track a high-V high-S blob; require a tail (elongated luminance falloff behind the travel vector) and a correlated luminance rise on the surrounding surfaces.
entries.notes: anime_2d covers drawn beams; a travelling energy bolt in 3D or live-action comp has no entry.

entries.label: Bubbles from a mouth or regulator
entries.description: A stream of rising bubbles anchored to a subject's head, pulsing with breathing.
entries.frame_evidence: Bubbles emerge from a point on the head and rise, in bursts rather than continuously.
entries.detector_note: fluids_fire.bubbles_rising_column anchored within a head-width of the face landmark; report burst periodicity as a breathing rate.

entries.label: Expression contradicts the body
entries.description: A face reading one way while the posture reads another - deliberate in performance, an error in animation.
entries.frame_evidence: A high-arousal expression on a body whose motion energy and posture openness are at rest levels.
entries.detector_note: Compare the expression arousal against body motion energy and posture openness percentiles within the shot; report the disagreement magnitude, never a verdict.
entries.notes: A finding to be inspected, not a defect: this is exactly how deadpan comedy and dissociation are staged.

entries.label: Facial expression category
entries.description: A named expression rolled up from the primitives: neutral, happy, sad, angry, fearful, surprised, disgusted, contemptuous.
entries.frame_evidence: A configuration of brow, eye and mouth measurements that matches a known pattern.
entries.detector_note: A trained expression classifier over the face crop, ALWAYS reported alongside the underlying primitive values (brow height, EAR, MAR, corner elevation) so the reader can see the evidence.
entries.vlm_question: What emotion does this face show: neutral, happy, sad, angry, afraid, surprised, disgusted?
entries.notes: face_head has 140 excellent primitives and no roll-up. Every consumer of this taxonomy will want the label; better it is defined here than invented downstream.

entries.label: Expression change event
entries.description: The frame at which an expression shifts from one category to another.
entries.frame_evidence: The primitive vector moves across a decision boundary and stays there.
entries.detector_note: Change-point detection on the smoothed primitive vector; report the onset cel, the transition duration and the before/after classes.
entries.notes: The TIMING of a reaction is what an editor cares about; the static class is much less useful.

entries.label: Expression valence and arousal
entries.description: A continuous two-axis read of affect, more robust than a discrete category on stylised faces.
entries.frame_evidence: The primitive vector's position on a pleasant/unpleasant and calm/excited plane.
entries.detector_note: A regression head over the face crop or a rule map from the primitives; report both axes with confidence, and prefer this over the discrete class for drawn faces.

entries.label: Eyecatch, bumper or interstitial card
entries.description: A short graphic interstitial with a logo or title over a plain field, separating segments.
entries.frame_evidence: A very short shot dominated by a graphic on a flat field, with a hard cut on both sides and no continuity with either neighbour.
entries.detector_note: A shot under 3 seconds whose background uniformity is high, whose embedding distance to both neighbours is large, and which contains a text or logo region.

entries.label: Face covering, mask or helmet
entries.description: Whether the face is covered, and by what - mask, helmet visor, scarf, hand, hair.
entries.frame_evidence: The face box is present but the lower or upper face landmarks have low confidence with a hard-edged region over them.
entries.detector_note: Compare per-region landmark confidence against the whole-face mean; a covering shows a spatially contiguous confidence collapse with a strong edge at its border.
entries.vlm_question: Is this person's face covered, and by what?
entries.notes: face_head.face_occluded_partial says occluded but never says by what, and a helmet visor behaves very differently from hair.

entries.label: Per-face identity embedding
entries.description: A face-recognition vector for every detected face, so a character can be followed across cuts.
entries.frame_evidence: Not visible - a derived representation of a detected face.
entries.detector_note: A face embedding model over each detected face crop above a minimum size; report the vector, the crop size and the model id. Refuse below the size floor rather than returning a weak vector.
entries.notes: Nothing in fifteen shards can answer 'is this the same character as in the previous shot'. hand_object.hand_identity_across_cut and interaction_social.subject_track_identity both silently assume this exists.

entries.label: Figure entering the extreme frame edge
entries.description: A partial body or face at the very border of frame, deliberately half-cropped.
entries.frame_evidence: A subject detection whose bbox is more than 40% outside the frame, held rather than transiting.
entries.detector_note: Subject bbox clipping fraction above 0.4 sustained for >= 5 unique cels with low lateral velocity - held, not passing through.
entries.notes: camera.framing_limb_cropped_at_edge treats cropping as a framing property; a HELD partial figure at the edge is a staging device.

entries.label: Filmed-screen refresh banding
entries.description: The rolling horizontal light/dark band across a screen photographed by a camera at a mismatched shutter.
entries.frame_evidence: A wide horizontal luminance band inside the screen region that translates vertically at a constant rate across frames.
entries.detector_note: Row-mean luminance profile inside the screen quad per frame (container frames, not unique cels); a travelling band shows a strong low-frequency peak whose phase advances linearly.
entries.notes: lighting.rolling_shutter_light_banding covers the whole frame; a screen inside the frame bands independently and is a very strong live-action tell.

entries.label: Fish or aquatic body undulation
entries.description: The travelling lateral wave along a swimming body, as opposed to limb-driven locomotion.
entries.frame_evidence: The body's midline curvature alternates sign and the curvature maximum travels from head to tail.
entries.detector_note: Skeletonise the body mask, sample curvature along the arclength, and cross-correlate the curvature profile between cels to detect a posterior-travelling phase shift.
entries.notes: body_action.serpentine_slither covers the ground case; a swimming body also has buoyancy and drag, so its beat frequency and settle differ.

entries.label: Flashback or memory treatment on a shot
entries.description: A shot rendered in sepia, monochrome, bleached or heavily soft-focus to mark it as a memory.
entries.frame_evidence: A shot whose saturation, CCT and softness differ sharply from its neighbours and that returns afterward.
entries.detector_note: Per-shot saturation, CCT and Laplacian variance compared against both neighbouring shots; a treatment run differs from both and reverts.

entries.label: Flashback or dream signalled by treatment
entries.description: A run of shots that differ systematically in grade, grain, aspect or frame rate from their neighbours.
entries.frame_evidence: A contiguous group of shots whose colour statistics, grain sigma or cadence differ sharply from the shots on both sides.
entries.detector_note: Segment the piece by shot; detect a contiguous run whose median saturation, CCT, grain sigma or cadence differs from both flanking runs beyond a robust threshold, then returns.

entries.label: Flock, swarm or school
entries.description: Many small similar bodies moving as a correlated group.
entries.frame_evidence: Dozens of small blobs of similar size whose velocity vectors are more aligned with each other than with the background.
entries.detector_note: Blob detection (MOG2 or DoG) with size within 2x of the median; require count >= 12, size CV < 0.6, and mean pairwise velocity cosine > 0.5 after camera compensation.
entries.notes: Distinguish from rain/snow/particles by size regularity and by turning coherence: a flock turns together, precipitation does not.

entries.label: Water flooding into a space
entries.description: A rising or advancing water boundary taking over a previously dry area.
entries.frame_evidence: A water-textured region's boundary advances monotonically across static scenery.
entries.detector_note: Track the water mask boundary on the stabilised plate; flooding = monotonic area growth with a coherent advancing front and a rising specular fraction behind it.

entries.label: Food present and its preparation state
entries.description: Food in frame and whether it is raw, cooking, cooked or plated.
entries.frame_evidence: A textured organic region inside or on a vessel, with a colour that changes over the shot.
entries.detector_note: Region proposal from vessel detection plus a VLM state question. The colour-change-over-time test below is the deterministic half.
entries.vlm_question: Is there food in this image? Is it raw, being cooked, or finished and plated?
entries.notes: scene_semantics.food_or_drink_present is a yes/no. The kitchen reel needs state and change.

entries.label: Foot tapping or leg bouncing
entries.description: A seated or standing subject's leg oscillating rapidly with no locomotion.
entries.frame_evidence: One ankle or knee oscillates vertically at 3-8 Hz while the hips stay fixed.
entries.detector_note: Ankle or knee vertical spectrum with a peak in 3-8 Hz and hip displacement near zero; report which side.

entries.label: Footprints, tracks or trails left behind
entries.description: Persistent marks left in snow, sand, mud or dust by a passing body or vehicle.
entries.frame_evidence: New dark marks appear on the ground at each footfall and remain in place as the subject moves on.
entries.detector_note: On the stabilised ground plane, detect new persistent regions appearing within a foot-width of each footfall event and persisting for >= 20 cels.
entries.notes: Their ABSENCE on snow or sand is one of the loudest CG tells, and nothing currently looks.

entries.label: Forced perspective scale illusion
entries.description: Two subjects staged so their apparent sizes contradict their ground positions.
entries.frame_evidence: A subject that is lower in frame (nearer) appears smaller than one higher in frame (further) on the same ground plane.
entries.detector_note: Fit the ground line from foot contacts; flag when apparent height and estimated depth are anti-correlated across three or more subjects.

entries.label: Foreground / background mask split
entries.description: A binary partition of the frame into subject-ish foreground and everything else, as a primitive for dozens of other entries.
entries.frame_evidence: Not visible - a derived mask.
entries.detector_note: Salient-object segmentation or a motion-plus-depth consensus mask; report the area fraction and the boundary length. Many existing entries ('inside the candidate region', 'the cloth', 'the crack mask') silently assume this.
entries.notes: This is the single largest hidden prerequisite in the whole taxonomy.

entries.label: Cut hidden behind a foreground transit
entries.description: A cut concealed inside a moment when a foreground object covers the frame.
entries.frame_evidence: A cut boundary falls inside the window during which a large foreground mask covers more than 80% of the frame.
entries.detector_note: Intersect the cut-boundary list with gaps.passing_traffic_or_train transit windows and with whip-pan windows; report cuts that fall inside them.
entries.notes: editing_time.invisible_cut is marked unsupported wholesale. The cover-transit case is fully measurable and is how most of them are actually done.

entries.label: Matte box, filter edge or blanking intrusion
entries.description: A dark corner or edge intrusion from hardware rather than a designed vignette.
entries.frame_evidence: A hard-edged dark region entering a corner with a sharp boundary, asymmetric between corners.
entries.detector_note: Compare the four corner luminance profiles; a hardware intrusion has a hard gradient (edge width below 4px) and is present in fewer than all four corners.
entries.notes: post_fx.mechanical_vignette_hard_cut assumes all four corners; a matte box usually hits one or two.

entries.label: Per-frame semantic embedding
entries.description: A dense semantic vector per frame, for shot clustering, near-duplicate search and drift measurement.
entries.frame_evidence: Not visible - a derived representation of the whole frame.
entries.detector_note: CLIP or DINOv2 image embedding per unique cel; store the vector and the model id. Everything downstream that says 'similar shot' should use this rather than a histogram.
entries.notes: The shards have pHash, SSIM and histogram correlation only. None of those can group two shots of the same location at different exposures.

entries.label: Frame is a solid colour, slate or test pattern
entries.description: A frame with no pictorial content: black, white, a colour card, bars, a countdown leader, a placeholder.
entries.frame_evidence: Near-zero spatial variance, or the specific geometry of colour bars or a leader countdown.
entries.detector_note: Spatial std below a threshold for a solid; for bars, test for full-height vertical stripes with uniform interiors; for a leader, a rotating radial sweep plus a large central numeral.
entries.notes: The analyser must not report a lighting ratio for a black slate. This is the gate that stops it.

entries.label: Malformed or nonsense lettering
entries.description: Text-shaped marks that are not real words - a generative-model and background-art tell.
entries.frame_evidence: Stroke-consistent character-like components that OCR either fails on or returns non-lexical strings for.
entries.detector_note: OCR the text region; gibberish = high per-character confidence but a non-lexical token, or wildly inconsistent glyph heights within one baseline.
entries.notes: scene_semantics.gibberish_or_fake_text is vlm-tier only; the OCR-confidence-versus-lexicality test is a cheap deterministic prior worth running first.

entries.label: Gore and injury intensity level
entries.description: A graded severity of visible injury content, for gating and for reporting.
entries.frame_evidence: Blood area fraction, wound count, and whether internal anatomy is visible.
entries.detector_note: Combine blood mask area fraction, gaps.wound_appearance_event count and a VLM severity question into a 0-3 band. Report the components, never the band alone.
entries.vlm_question: Rate the visible injury content: none, minor (small wounds or blood), moderate (heavy blood), severe (major trauma or internal anatomy visible).
entries.notes: Needed as a gate for downstream publishing, and the pipeline has no such measurement anywhere.

entries.label: Unkeyed green or blue screen visible
entries.description: A raw backing colour still present in a delivered frame.
entries.frame_evidence: A large contiguous region of saturated pure green or blue with a very low texture energy.
entries.detector_note: Hue within the keying bands, saturation above 0.6, contiguous area above 10% of frame, and texture energy near zero.

entries.label: Crater or ground fissure forming
entries.description: The ground itself deforming: a crater, a crack running across the floor, a sinkhole.
entries.frame_evidence: A dark irregular region grows outward along the ground plane from an impact point, with radial branching.
entries.detector_note: On the stabilised ground plane, detect a growing dark region whose skeleton branches radiate from a common origin; report growth rate and branch count.

entries.label: Hairstyle, length and colour
entries.description: The hair region's extent, colour and silhouette class - and its continuity.
entries.frame_evidence: A coloured region above and around the face landmarks with a distinct silhouette from the body.
entries.detector_note: Hair segmentation model (or a colour-clustered region anchored to the face box superior arc); report area relative to head area, dominant hue, and the lowest hair pixel relative to the shoulders.
entries.notes: Hair motion is covered in three shards; hair identity is covered nowhere, and it is the single most common character-consistency defect.

entries.label: Which hand holds what, across a cut
entries.description: An object changing hands, or appearing in an empty hand, across a cut.
entries.frame_evidence: The handedness label of the hand holding a matched object differs across the cut.
entries.detector_note: hand_object.handedness_label plus object matching across the cut; report a swap or an appearance with no handoff action in between.
entries.notes: The single most common continuity error in coverage, and directly measurable from entries that already exist.

entries.label: HDR transfer function and peak level
entries.description: Whether the source is SDR, HLG or PQ, and what peak level it actually reaches.
entries.frame_evidence: Not visible - container metadata plus a measurement.
entries.detector_note: Read the transfer characteristics, colour primaries and matrix coefficients from the container; measure the actual peak nits reached under the declared transfer.
entries.notes: Nothing in the taxonomy distinguishes an HDR source, yet every luminance threshold in every shard assumes SDR.

entries.label: Vehicle lamps: headlights, brake lights, indicators
entries.description: Emissive lamps on a vehicle and their state changes - the cheapest read on what a vehicle is doing.
entries.frame_evidence: Saturated red or white blobs at fixed positions on the vehicle mask, switching state.
entries.detector_note: Small saturated blob detection anchored to the vehicle mask; classify by hue (red rear / white-amber front); report per-lamp on/off series and blink period for indicators.
entries.notes: Brake lights are the direct visual confirmation of object_dynamics.vehicle_pitch_brake_accel and are not covered.

entries.label: Moving external light sweeping an interior
entries.description: A bar or patch of light travelling across walls and faces from an unseen passing source.
entries.frame_evidence: A bright region translates smoothly across static surfaces while the camera and subjects are still.
entries.detector_note: Detect a bright connected region whose centroid translates monotonically over static geometry with the global motion model near identity; report speed and direction.
entries.notes: lighting.moving_shadow_sweep covers the shadow half of the same phenomenon; the light half is absent.

entries.label: Holographic or volumetric projection
entries.description: A semi-transparent emissive image floating in space, usually with scanlines and an edge falloff.
entries.frame_evidence: A region where the background remains partly visible through a coloured emissive structure, with horizontal banding.
entries.detector_note: Alpha-like behaviour: the region's pixels correlate with both a foreground pattern and the background behind it as the camera moves; plus horizontal periodic banding in its power spectrum.
entries.notes: cg_3d.shader_hologram covers the shader; this covers the object existing as scene content.

entries.label: Hovering flight
entries.description: A flying body holding station in the air: high-frequency wing motion with near-zero body translation.
entries.frame_evidence: The body centroid is static within a few pixels while a blurred or oscillating wing region persists beside it.
entries.detector_note: Camera-compensated body centroid displacement < 2px per cel for >= 6 cels, combined with local high-frequency residual motion energy in an annulus around the body above the frame median.
entries.notes: Insects, hummingbirds, drones and hovering mecha all read the same way here - that is a feature, not a defect.

entries.label: HUD reticle locking onto a target
entries.description: An overlay graphic that follows a moving subject in the scene rather than sitting still on the frame.
entries.frame_evidence: A geometric overlay element whose position correlates with a tracked subject and not with the camera.
entries.detector_note: Detect thin-stroke synthetic overlay elements (uniform width, saturated, aliasing-free), then correlate their centroid with subject tracks versus with the global motion model.
entries.notes: scene_semantics.ui_or_graphic_overlay only says an overlay exists; whether it TRACKS is the interesting bit.

entries.label: Telescopic or hydraulic extension
entries.description: A segment lengthening or shortening along its own axis rather than rotating.
entries.frame_evidence: A rigid element's length along its principal axis changes while its angle stays fixed.
entries.detector_note: PCA on the segment mask per cel; report principal-axis length change with the axis angle held within 5 deg.

entries.label: Face or character identity flickering
entries.description: A character's face subtly changing identity from frame to frame - the defining diffusion-video failure.
entries.frame_evidence: The face embedding distance between consecutive frames of one continuous track is far above the distance seen in real footage.
entries.detector_note: Per-frame face embeddings on one unbroken track; report the mean and max consecutive-frame distance and compare against a reference distribution from a known-real clip.
entries.notes: post_fx.generative_frame_provenance is one model-tier catch-all. This pipeline generates video; the specific failure modes deserve their own entries.

entries.label: Machine indicator light pattern
entries.description: Small saturated point lights on a machine blinking in a pattern.
entries.frame_evidence: Sub-1%-of-frame saturated blobs on the machine turning on and off at a regular cadence.
entries.detector_note: Small saturated blob detection restricted to the machine mask; per-blob luminance series and its periodicity; report period and duty cycle per blob.

entries.label: Infant or very young child present
entries.description: A body with infant proportions, usually carried, held or lying rather than standing.
entries.frame_evidence: A very small body with a head occupying a quarter or more of its total height, with limbs short relative to torso.
entries.detector_note: Person detection plus head_body_ratio > 0.2 and absolute height below 60% of any adult in frame; confirm with VLM.
entries.vlm_question: Is there a baby or toddler in this image? Is it being held or carried?
entries.notes: MediaPipe pose is trained on adult proportions and mis-fits infants; expect landmark confidence to drop and do not read that as absence.

entries.label: Erratic insect flight path
entries.description: The high-curvature, direction-reversing path of a flying insect, distinct from a bird's smooth arc.
entries.frame_evidence: A small blob whose track direction changes sharply many times per second.
entries.detector_note: Track small blobs; compute per-cel heading change; erratic = mean absolute heading change > 40 deg/cel with a low net displacement to path length ratio (< 0.3).

entries.label: Insert of a still image or photograph
entries.description: A shot that is a photograph, painting or document rather than live footage - zero motion, often with a frame or border.
entries.frame_evidence: A shot with essentially zero residual motion for its whole length, often with a rectangular border and a different grain character.
entries.detector_note: A shot whose camera-compensated residual motion energy is at the noise floor for its entire length, with the unique-cel count equal to one or the camera model showing only a scale/translation ramp on a static plate.
entries.notes: Distinguishes a genuine still insert from editing_time.freeze_frame, which is a stopped MOVING image.

entries.label: Inset reaction panel or cut-in
entries.description: A smaller framed image inserted over the main image - the eye close-up box, the reaction inset.
entries.frame_evidence: A bordered sub-rectangle appears over the main artwork with its own independent content.
entries.detector_note: Detect a rectangular sub-region with a constant-colour border whose interior content is uncorrelated with the region it covers, appearing and disappearing within a shot.
entries.notes: Extremely common in anime and manga-derived layout, and it breaks every whole-frame metric while it is on screen.

entries.label: Musical instrument present
entries.description: An instrument held or played by a subject, to a coarse class (string, keyboard, percussion, wind, brass).
entries.frame_evidence: A rigid object coupled to the body in a play posture, with a characteristic silhouette.
entries.detector_note: Object detection restricted to the person's contact zone; VLM for the class. The play-posture prior is the deterministic gate: both hands in fixed asymmetric relation to the object.
entries.vlm_question: Is this person holding or playing a musical instrument? What kind?
entries.notes: Entirely absent from all fifteen shards.

entries.label: Unsteady or intoxicated motion
entries.description: Locomotion with a wide base, irregular stride timing and a wandering path.
entries.frame_evidence: Stride intervals vary far more than a normal walk, the path curves erratically, and the trunk sways laterally.
entries.detector_note: Stride-interval coefficient of variation above 0.25, lateral COM sway above 8% of body height, and a low path-efficiency ratio.

entries.label: Jump-scare event
entries.description: A sudden large subject appearance filling the frame, usually with a luminance and audio spike in the same frames.
entries.frame_evidence: A large new mask appears within one or two frames, mean luminance and audio energy spike together, and the shot's motion energy jumps an order of magnitude.
entries.detector_note: Coincidence within 3 frames of: a subject-mask area jump above 20% of frame, a motion-energy z-score above 4, and an audio onset peak. Measured on container frames.
entries.notes: All the components exist in separate shards; nothing composes them into the event that a viewer would name.

entries.label: Key press on a keyboard instrument
entries.description: Individual keys depressing under fingers, in a pattern.
entries.frame_evidence: Narrow horizontal elements in a regular row change their vertical position or shading one at a time.
entries.detector_note: Detect the regular key lattice by its periodic spectral peak, then per-key luminance/position series; a press is a single-key excursion.
entries.notes: hand_object.typing_on_keyboard covers a computer keyboard's HAND motion only, not the keys responding.

entries.label: Striking an object with a limb or implement
entries.description: The contact instant at which a person's foot, hand or implement changes an object's velocity.
entries.frame_evidence: The object's velocity direction reverses or turns sharply in the same cel that an extremity reaches it.
entries.detector_note: Coincidence of a ball-track velocity discontinuity with the minimum extremity distance; report the impulse direction change and the pre/post speed ratio.
entries.notes: body_action.front_kick etc. detect the LEG motion; nothing checks whether a struck object responded.

entries.label: Animated or moving text
entries.description: Text that scales, slides, rotates or types on, as a graphic element.
entries.frame_evidence: A text region translates, scales or grows character by character while the plate behind it is static.
entries.detector_note: Track the text region's affine transform per cel against a static background; type-on shows the region's width growing in quantised steps.

entries.label: Leaning on a wall, rail or furniture
entries.description: The body's weight partly carried by contact with a static object.
entries.frame_evidence: The trunk axis is tilted well off vertical while the feet stay planted and a body region touches a static surface.
entries.detector_note: Trunk tilt beyond 12 deg from the ground normal with stable foot contact and a body-to-static-surface contact zone; the centre of mass must fall outside the base of support.
entries.notes: A body whose COM is outside its base of support and is not falling is either leaning or is a physics error - the same test answers both.

entries.label: Off-screen event implied by a light change
entries.description: A global or directional illumination change with no visible cause in frame - a door opening, an explosion, a car passing, a light switching.
entries.frame_evidence: Scene luminance or key azimuth changes sharply while nothing in frame moves enough to explain it.
entries.detector_note: A luminance or key-azimuth step with residual (non-global) motion energy below the shot median in the same window; report the direction of the new light.
entries.notes: lighting.practical_offscreen_implied covers a static pool of light; this covers the EVENT.

entries.label: Missing limb or dismemberment
entries.description: A body plan that is missing a limb, either as a character trait or as an event.
entries.frame_evidence: Pose landmarks for one limb chain are persistently absent while the rest of the body tracks cleanly, with no occluder present.
entries.detector_note: Persistent per-chain landmark absence with high confidence elsewhere, plus a check that no foreground object overlaps the expected limb region. An EVENT is a transition from present to absent within a shot.
entries.notes: Currently reads as tracker dropout and would be filtered out as noise.

entries.label: Liquid level continuity across a cut
entries.description: The level in the same vessel jumping between shots without anyone drinking.
entries.frame_evidence: The measured level fraction differs across a cut by more than the measurement noise, with no drinking action between.
entries.detector_note: Compare gaps.liquid_level_in_vessel across the cut for a matched vessel; flag when the delta exceeds 8% of interior height and no hand_object.drink_from_vessel fired in the interval.

entries.label: Liquid level inside a vessel
entries.description: The height of the liquid surface within a glass, cup or bottle - a per-frame measurement and a continuity anchor.
entries.frame_evidence: A horizontal boundary inside the vessel silhouette with different optical behaviour above and below it.
