entries.detector_note: Inside the vessel mask, find the strongest horizontal edge; report its height as a fraction of the vessel's interior height, per unique cel.
entries.notes: This is THE canonical continuity error (the glass that refills between angles) and nothing in the fifteen shards measures it.

entries.label: Manga-style panel split within one frame
entries.description: One frame divided into two or more angled panels by white or black gutters.
entries.frame_evidence: Straight gutters at non-orthogonal angles dividing the frame into independent images.
entries.detector_note: Detect long straight uniform-colour bands crossing the frame at arbitrary angles, then verify the regions they separate have uncorrelated content.
entries.notes: gaps.split_screen_or_multipanel covers orthogonal splits; manga panels are angled and gutter-coloured and need their own test.

entries.label: Backscatter particles in water
entries.description: Suspended particulate lit by the camera or sun, drifting slowly and out of focus.
entries.frame_evidence: Many small soft-edged bright points drifting slowly in all directions, denser near the light.
entries.detector_note: Small blob field with low edge sharpness, slow near-isotropic velocities, and a density gradient toward the brightest region.

entries.label: Giant-machine weight cues
entries.description: The set of cues that sell a very large machine: slow angular rates, ground impact dust at each step, camera shake locked to footfalls, long settle.
entries.frame_evidence: Each footfall coincides with a dust puff, a camera shake impulse and a low-frequency settle oscillation.
entries.detector_note: Cross-correlate the footfall event series with camera_shake_energy peaks and dust-puff onsets; large scale = all three phase-locked within 2 frames, with limb angular rates in the bottom decile.
entries.notes: cg_3d.physics_scale_reads_miniature is marked unsupported; this makes the measurable half of it measurable.

entries.label: Progressive mechanical damage
entries.description: A machine accumulating dents, missing panels, sparks and exposed internals over a sequence.
entries.frame_evidence: New dark cavities and spark emitters appear on the machine mask and persist.
entries.detector_note: Per-track appearance delta with a monotonicity requirement, plus spark-emitter detection anchored inside the machine mask.

entries.label: Mechanical transformation or unfolding
entries.description: A machine reconfiguring: panels rotating out, segments sliding, silhouette changing class.
entries.frame_evidence: The silhouette's Hu moments change drastically over a short run while the mask area stays roughly conserved.
entries.detector_note: Track mask area and Hu moments per cel; a transform = normalised Hu-moment distance in the top percentile with area conserved within 25% and the subject track unbroken.
entries.notes: editing_time.morph_transition is a shot transition, not a subject transforming inside a continuous shot.

entries.label: Medical equipment in frame
entries.description: Drips, monitors, masks, stretchers, syringes - the props that mark a medical scene.
entries.frame_evidence: Recognisable clinical objects, often with an emissive monitor showing a periodic trace.
entries.detector_note: Prop-inventory VLM question plus a deterministic bonus: a screen region containing a periodic horizontal trace (a vitals waveform) is measurable from its spectral peak.
entries.vlm_question: Is there medical equipment in this image - an IV drip, a heart monitor, an oxygen mask, a stretcher, a syringe?

entries.label: Brief expression flash
entries.description: An expression appearing and vanishing within a few frames.
entries.frame_evidence: A large excursion in the primitive vector lasting 2-5 frames and fully returning.
entries.detector_note: Excursion above 2 robust sigma in the primitive vector with a full return within 5 container frames; measured on container frames, not unique cels.
entries.notes: Must be measured on container frames: on 2s or 3s a genuine 3-frame flash may not survive unique-cel indexing at all, and that itself is a finding.

entries.label: Microphone held or stood at the mouth
entries.description: A handheld or stand-mounted object held close to the mouth for a sustained period.
entries.frame_evidence: An elongated object whose tip stays within a head-width of the mouth landmark across many cels.
entries.detector_note: Distance from a detected elongated held object's tip to the mouth landmark, normalised by face width; sustained below 0.6 for >= 10 cels.

entries.label: Walking aid, wheelchair or crutch
entries.description: A mobility device coupled to a person's gait.
entries.frame_evidence: A rigid line or wheeled frame whose ground contact alternates with the person's footfalls.
entries.detector_note: Object detection for wheelchair/cane/crutch/walker plus phase-locking of the device's ground contact to the footfall series.
entries.vlm_question: Is this person using a cane, crutches, a walker or a wheelchair?

entries.label: Montage sequence
entries.description: A run of short shots from many different settings, unified by pace rather than by continuity.
entries.frame_evidence: A run with a short average shot length and a high number of distinct embedding clusters relative to its shot count.
entries.detector_note: Over a sliding window of 8 shots: cluster count over shot count above 0.7 with the window ASL below the piece median. Report the window bounds.

entries.label: Flock shape reorganisation
entries.description: The envelope of a flock or swarm changing shape while the members stay grouped.
entries.frame_evidence: The convex hull of the blob cluster stretches, folds or rotates between cels without the members dispersing.
entries.detector_note: Convex hull of the swarm blobs per cel; track hull area, elongation and principal-axis angle; reorganisation = axis rotation > 20 deg or elongation change > 30% while member count stays within 20%.

entries.label: An object changing into another object
entries.description: A prop whose identity or class changes while its track continues.
entries.frame_evidence: A tracked object's shape descriptor and colour change substantially without the track breaking or the camera cutting.
entries.detector_note: Track the object; measure Hu-moment and palette distance across the run; adjudicate whether the change is a morph, a rotation, or a tracking error with a VLM.
entries.vlm_question: Compare the object at the start and end of this sequence. Is it the same object seen differently, or has it become something else?

entries.label: Object appears, vanishes or changes count
entries.description: Props, limbs, windows or people whose count changes between frames without an occlusion.
entries.frame_evidence: The count of a repeated element differs between consecutive cels with no entry or exit at a border.
entries.detector_note: Count stable repeated elements (windows, buttons, fingers, people) per cel and report any change not explained by an occlusion or a border crossing.

entries.label: Debris or fluid arriving from off-screen
entries.description: Material entering from a frame edge with high speed, implying an unseen impact or attack.
entries.frame_evidence: New fast-moving particles or a fluid spatter cross a frame border inward with no visible emitter.
entries.detector_note: Particle/spatter tracks whose first observation lies within 5% of a frame border with inward velocity and no emitter within the frame.

entries.label: Out-of-gamut and illegal colour fraction
entries.description: Pixels outside the target colour space or outside broadcast-legal limits.
entries.frame_evidence: Not visible without a scope; shows as flat saturated patches at delivery.
entries.detector_note: Convert to the delivery space and count pixels outside gamut and outside the legal RGB/luma range; report per channel.

entries.label: Foreground element transiting the frame
entries.description: A large object crossing between camera and subject - a passing car, a train, a pillar - briefly occluding everything.
entries.frame_evidence: A large high-speed region crosses the frame, occluding the subject for a short run, then reveals it again.
entries.detector_note: A moving mask exceeding 25% of frame width crossing the frame in under 15 cels while the subject track goes missing and returns at a consistent position.
entries.notes: Also the deterministic detector for a hidden cut behind a foreground wipe - editing_time.invisible_cut is marked unsupported, but this half of it IS measurable.

entries.label: Perceptual distance between frames
entries.description: A perceptual (not pixel) distance between two frames, which tolerates grain and grade but not content change.
entries.frame_evidence: Not visible - a pairwise derived number.
entries.detector_note: LPIPS or a DISTS-style metric between consecutive unique cels and across cut boundaries. Use it to separate a real cut from a flash or a grain change.

entries.label: Picture-in-picture or inset panel
entries.description: A smaller independent image inset inside the main frame, usually with a border.
entries.frame_evidence: A rectangular sub-region with its own cuts and its own motion, bounded by a constant border.
entries.detector_note: A rectangular region whose interior shows independent cut boundaries (SSIM collapses not present in the host frame) and whose border pixels are temporally constant.

entries.label: Placeholder, proxy or missing-asset frame
entries.description: Untextured grey geometry, magenta missing-texture surfaces, or a watermarked proxy render.
entries.frame_evidence: Large regions of pure neutral grey with shading but no texture, or saturated magenta fills.
entries.detector_note: Regions with normal shading gradients but near-zero chroma variance and near-zero texture energy (grey proxy), or pixels within a tight band of pure magenta covering a contiguous surface.
entries.notes: A production-critical check that would catch an unfinished render shipping as a deliverable.

entries.label: Portal, rift or gateway
entries.description: A bounded region showing different scene content from its surroundings, with a distinct edge treatment.
entries.frame_evidence: A closed contour whose interior colour statistics and motion are inconsistent with everything around it.
entries.detector_note: Detect a closed region whose interior palette distance to the surrounding ring is large and whose interior motion is uncorrelated with the surrounding flow; adjudicate with a VLM.
entries.vlm_question: Is there a portal, doorway or opening in this image showing a different place through it?

entries.label: Held postural configurations
entries.description: Named static postures: arms crossed, hands on hips, hands in pockets, arms behind back, hugging self.
entries.frame_evidence: The wrist and elbow landmarks sit in a stable named configuration relative to the torso for many cels.
entries.detector_note: Classify from normalised wrist and elbow positions in the torso frame; require the configuration to hold for >= 8 unique cels before naming it.
entries.notes: interaction_social.open_vs_closed_body_orientation gives an openness score but never names the posture that produced it.

entries.label: Pouring into a vessel and the level rising
entries.description: The receiving half of a pour: the liquid level in the target vessel rising while a stream is present.
entries.frame_evidence: A stream connects two vessels and the lower vessel's internal horizontal boundary climbs.
entries.detector_note: hand_object.liquid_stream_present combined with a monotonically rising gaps.liquid_level_in_vessel in the target; the two must be simultaneous.
entries.notes: A stream with no rising level is a classic composited-element error.

entries.label: Damage persistence across shots
entries.description: Whether destruction that happened stays visible in later shots of the same location.
entries.frame_evidence: A location reused across shots shows fewer damage features in a later shot than in an earlier one.
entries.detector_note: Match locations with scene_semantics.location_reuse_across_shots, then compare damage-feature counts (holes, debris area, dust) in shot order; a decrease is the finding.
entries.notes: The 'the set repaired itself' error - a hard one for humans, an easy one for a machine, and completely uncovered.

entries.label: Prop state continuity across a cut
entries.description: A prop whose STATE (open/closed, lit/unlit, full/empty, worn/held) changes across a cut with no action between.
entries.frame_evidence: The same prop is present on both sides of a cut with a different binary state.
entries.detector_note: Match props across the cut by position and appearance, then compare a per-prop state vector (aperture, emissive, fill level, grip). Report only when no action window explains the change.
entries.notes: object_dynamics.prop_position_jump_across_cut covers position only. State is the more common error and the more visible one.

entries.label: Quadruped footfall contact events
entries.description: Which of the four feet is on the ground on each cel - the substrate under any gait claim.
entries.frame_evidence: A limb tip's vertical motion goes to zero and stays there for several cels while the body continues forward.
entries.detector_note: Animal-pose keypoints (e.g. an AP-10K style model) then per-limb-tip vertical velocity zero-crossings. Without animal keypoints, fall back to the four lowest extremities of the animal mask.
entries.notes: body_action.quadruped_gait_classification is marked model but has no contact primitive under it. Gait names are worthless without the support pattern.

entries.label: Implement swing and follow-through
entries.description: A held implement swept through an arc with a peak tip speed and a follow-through past contact.
entries.frame_evidence: The tool's long axis sweeps a wide arc with the tip speed peaking near the object contact.
entries.detector_note: hand_object.tool_swing_arc plus a requirement that the tip-speed peak lies within 2 cels of a ball-track velocity discontinuity.

entries.label: Reflection on glasses or a visor
entries.description: Bright reflected content on lenses, sometimes hiding the eyes entirely.
entries.frame_evidence: Two bright patches over the eye regions with content that moves with the head rather than with the eyes.
entries.detector_note: Compare eye-region luminance against the surrounding face; a lens reflection is a high-luminance patch bounded by the lens edge whose interior structure is head-locked.

entries.label: Subject missing from a reflective surface
entries.description: A polished surface that reflects the scene but not the subject standing in front of it.
entries.frame_evidence: A surface shows environment reflections while the region where the subject's reflection should fall is empty.
entries.detector_note: Given a detected reflective surface and a subject on the same ground plane, predict the reflection region geometrically and test whether it contains subject-like content.
entries.vlm_question: There is a mirror or polished surface in this image. Is the person in front of it reflected in it?
entries.notes: cg_3d.ssr_missing_offscreen_object covers the SSR case; the general 'no reflection' case is broader and is also a deliberate storytelling device.

entries.label: Reflection disagrees with the subject
entries.description: The reflection showing something different from the subject - a horror device and a CG defect.
entries.frame_evidence: The reflected instance's pose, appearance or presence diverges from the mirrored expectation.
entries.detector_note: Warp the subject region by the estimated mirror transform and compare against the reflection region; report the residual. Adjudicate large residuals with a VLM before calling them intentional.
entries.vlm_question: Compare the person and their reflection in this image. Do they match in pose, clothing and appearance?

entries.label: Road or ground surface flow speed
entries.description: The apparent speed of the ground passing the camera - the honest speedometer of a driving shot.
entries.frame_evidence: Strong coherent downward or outward flow in the lower frame region, with lane markings streaking.
entries.detector_note: Mean flow magnitude in the lower-third ground region after removing camera rotation; report in frame-heights per second. Compare against object_dynamics.wheel_rotation_rate for the skating-wheel check.

entries.label: Robotic or mechanical subject
entries.description: A subject that is a machine rather than an organism: rigid segments, visible joints, no skin.
entries.frame_evidence: A humanoid or animal silhouette whose surface is uniformly hard-specular with visible panel seams and no skin chroma.
entries.detector_note: Person/creature detection whose mask has near-zero skin-chroma fraction, high straight-line-segment density inside the mask, and a high specular ratio; adjudicate with a VLM.
entries.vlm_question: Is this figure a robot, a mech, a suit of armour, or a living being?

entries.label: Scoreboard, timer or countdown overlay
entries.description: A persistent graphic showing numbers that change monotonically.
entries.frame_evidence: A fixed-position overlay region whose interior changes while its border stays pixel-identical.
entries.detector_note: Find frame regions with zero inter-cel change on their border and non-zero change inside; report position, size and change rate. OCR the interior if an OCR engine is available.
entries.notes: This detector also catches clocks, HUD counters and burned-in timecode.

entries.label: Screen content scrolling or cutting
entries.description: The image inside a screen scrolling, playing video, or cutting to a new image.
entries.frame_evidence: Optical flow inside the screen quad is coherent and independent of the flow outside it.
entries.detector_note: Compute flow restricted to the screen quad after removing the global model; scrolling = coherent uniform flow, playing = high residual energy, cut = an SSIM collapse inside the quad only.

entries.label: Screen inside the frame and its content state
entries.description: A monitor, phone, TV or projection surface visible in the scene, and whether its content is changing.
entries.frame_evidence: A bright rectangular region, usually brighter than its surround, whose interior changes independently of the rest of the frame.
entries.detector_note: Find bright quadrilaterals (approxPolyDP, 4 corners, extent > 0.8); classify as a screen when the interior inter-cel change energy exceeds the exterior's by 3x while the quad corners stay static.
entries.notes: scene_semantics.emissive_screen_device says a screen exists. Whether it is ON, and whether its content MOVES, is a different and very visible thing.

entries.label: Self-touch and fidgeting
entries.description: Repetitive self-directed micro-actions: scratching, hair tucking, nail biting, adjusting glasses, rubbing hands.
entries.frame_evidence: A hand makes short repeated excursions to a fixed point on the subject's own body or clothing.
entries.detector_note: Hand landmark repeatedly entering a small region of the subject's own body mask, more than twice within 3 seconds, with low transport amplitude.
entries.notes: hand_object.self_directed_actions has only two entries. Self-adaptors are the densest behaviour in any conversation scene.

entries.label: Servo-stepped mechanical motion
entries.description: Motion that moves in discrete increments with hard stops, the signature of a machine as opposed to a body.
entries.frame_evidence: Joint angle traces are piecewise-constant with abrupt transitions and no ease-in or ease-out.
entries.detector_note: Fit the tracked angle series; measure the fraction of cels with near-zero derivative bracketed by single-cel jumps; stepped = > 40% zero-derivative cels with jump magnitude above 3 deg.
entries.notes: The inverse of editing_time.motion_easing_curve, and an intentional style, not a defect.

entries.label: Shadow standing in for an unseen figure
entries.description: A human- or creature-shaped shadow on a surface with no corresponding body in frame.
entries.frame_evidence: A dark region with a recognisable limbed silhouette whose shape changes over time, with no person detected.
entries.detector_note: Dark-region segmentation with a silhouette-shape prior (limb-count from skeleton branches) fired only when no person or animal is detected in the frame.
entries.vlm_question: Is there a shadow of a person or creature in this image whose body is not itself visible?
entries.notes: lighting.offscreen_object_shadow is the closest entry and is about an OBJECT. A figure's shadow used as the subject is a distinct staging choice.

entries.label: Shadow does not match the subject's action
entries.description: The shadow doing something the body is not - a horror device and a compositing error.
entries.frame_evidence: The shadow silhouette's shape change is uncorrelated with the subject's pose change.
entries.detector_note: Correlate the shadow mask's shape-descriptor time series against the subject's pose-derived silhouette series; a low correlation with both present is the finding.
entries.vlm_question: Does the shadow in this image match what the person is doing?

entries.label: Shadow enters frame before its owner
entries.description: A cast shadow arriving in frame ahead of the body that casts it - a standard approach reveal.
entries.frame_evidence: A dark shape enters from a frame edge and grows for several cels before any subject enters.
entries.detector_note: Report the cel index of the first shadow-region intrusion at a frame edge and the cel index of the first subject detection; fire when the gap exceeds 3 unique cels.

entries.label: Shadow growing as a proxy for approach
entries.description: A cast shadow enlarging monotonically, implying something coming closer to the light or the wall.
entries.frame_evidence: The shadow region's area grows monotonically while the light source and surface stay fixed.
entries.detector_note: Track the shadow mask area and its principal-axis length across cels; growth = monotonic increase over >= 6 cels with the surface homography stable.

entries.label: Shivering or trembling
entries.description: High-frequency low-amplitude oscillation of the whole body, distinct from a hand tremor.
entries.frame_evidence: Every landmark oscillates in phase at 5-12 Hz with tiny amplitude and no net displacement.
entries.detector_note: Landmark position spectra after camera compensation: a common peak in the 5-12 Hz band across torso and limb landmarks with amplitude below 2% of body height.
entries.notes: hand_object.hand_tremor_microjitter covers the hand only, and would call a shivering body a tracking defect.

entries.label: Screen direction continuity across cuts
entries.description: A subject travelling left-to-right in one shot and right-to-left in the next, without a turn.
entries.frame_evidence: The subject's screen travel direction reverses across a cut with no visible pivot.
entries.detector_note: Compare scene_semantics.subject_travel_direction for the matched identity across the cut; a reversal beyond 120 deg with no pivot_turn event is the finding.
entries.notes: The other half of the 180-degree rule and the measurable half - the shards mark axis crossing unsupported and stop there.

entries.label: Singing versus speaking
entries.description: Sustained open vowel shapes with long holds, distinct from the fast consonant transitions of speech.
entries.frame_evidence: The mouth holds a wide-open shape for far longer than any speech viseme, with a slow return.
entries.detector_note: Viseme dwell-time distribution: singing shows a long tail of open-vowel dwells (> 500 ms) and a lower viseme transition rate than speech at the same audio energy.
entries.notes: face_head.speech_sync assumes dialogue timing throughout.

entries.label: Sizzling oil spatter
entries.description: Small bright droplets ejected upward from a hot cooking surface at a high, irregular rate.
entries.frame_evidence: Sub-pixel-to-few-pixel bright specks appear above the pan surface with short ballistic lives.
entries.detector_note: Airborne-particle detection restricted to a band above the detected vessel rim; require lifetimes of 1-3 cels, upward initial velocity and a Poisson-like irregular emission interval.
entries.notes: Distinct from fluids_fire.spark_shower: spatter is not emissive and does not decay in luminance.

entries.label: Gliding locomotion (skating, skiing, boarding)
entries.description: Forward travel that continues while the feet are not cycling - a glide phase far longer than any run allows.
entries.frame_evidence: The centroid translates steadily while the ankle landmarks stay fixed relative to the hips for many cels.
entries.detector_note: Camera-compensated horizontal centroid speed above a threshold with ankle-to-hip relative motion near zero for >= 8 unique cels.
entries.notes: body_action.foot_slide_artifact would currently flag every skating shot as a defect. This is the legitimate case and must gate it.

entries.label: Skid, drag or scrape marks
entries.description: A continuous linear mark left by a sliding contact.
entries.frame_evidence: A new elongated dark streak on the ground aligned with a sliding object's path.
entries.detector_note: New persistent elongated region on the stabilised ground whose principal axis matches a tracked object's path within 10 deg.

entries.label: Exposed-skin fraction of the subject
entries.description: How much of the visible body is bare skin versus covered.
entries.frame_evidence: Skin-chroma pixels as a fraction of the person mask, zoned by body part.
entries.detector_note: frame_metrics.skin_tone_pixel_fraction restricted to the person mask and split by pose-landmark zones; report per zone, not globally.
entries.notes: Needed for wardrobe change detection and for content gating; the existing global skin fraction cannot tell a face from a bare arm.

entries.label: Sleeping or resting
entries.description: Eyes closed for a long sustained run with a still body and slow breathing.
entries.frame_evidence: Sustained eye closure over seconds, minimal body motion, a slow periodic chest rise.
entries.detector_note: face_head.eyes_closed_sustained beyond 3 seconds AND body motion energy below the shot's stillness threshold AND a detected breathing rate below 0.4 Hz.
entries.notes: Distinguishes sleep from a long blink and from a still corpse - the breathing rate is the discriminator.

entries.label: Subject revealed gradually by light
entries.description: A subject emerging from darkness as illumination rises or a light source approaches.
entries.frame_evidence: The subject region's mean luminance and detail density rise monotonically while the frame's overall exposure does not.
entries.detector_note: Subject-region luminance and Laplacian variance rising monotonically over >= 10 cels with the background luminance flat; report the ramp duration.

entries.label: Water surface seen from below
entries.description: The bright circular window of the sky seen through the surface, ringed by total internal reflection.
entries.frame_evidence: A bright roughly circular region at the top of frame surrounded by a darker mirrored ring.
entries.detector_note: Detect a bright high-eccentricity-low region in the upper frame with a sharp luminance drop at its boundary and mirrored content outside it.

entries.label: Spell circle, sigil or rune array
entries.description: A geometric emissive figure appearing in space, often rotating, often in perspective.
entries.frame_evidence: A bright thin-line figure with high radial or rotational symmetry, growing or rotating in place.
entries.detector_note: Detect thin bright structure with high radial symmetry score (frame_metrics.radial_symmetry_score restricted to the region) and track its rotation via log-polar phase correlation.

entries.label: Split screen or multi-panel frame
entries.description: One frame carrying two or more independent images separated by hard boundaries.
entries.frame_evidence: Straight full-height or full-width boundaries with uncorrelated content and independent motion on either side.
entries.detector_note: Find full-span straight edges with a large discontinuity in both colour statistics and flow; require the panels' flow fields to be uncorrelated over >= 5 cels.
entries.notes: The remix workflow produces split-screens routinely, and every global metric in every shard is wrong on one.

entries.label: Steam rising off food or a vessel
entries.description: A low-contrast rising vapour column anchored to a food or drink vessel.
entries.frame_evidence: A faint semi-transparent plume rising from a vessel rim, visible mainly against a darker background.
entries.detector_note: fluids_fire.steam_release_wisp gated to a region above a detected vessel rim, with a low-contrast (delta L < 12) requirement so it is not mistaken for smoke.
entries.notes: The single most requested 'is the food hot' cue, and it is invisible on a bright background - report the null.

entries.label: Stereoscopic or 360 source format
entries.description: Side-by-side or over-under stereo pairs, anaglyph, or an equirectangular 360 projection.
entries.frame_evidence: Two near-identical halves with a small horizontal disparity, or extreme barrel curvature with poles stretched at top and bottom.
entries.detector_note: Test the two halves for a high correlation at a small horizontal offset (stereo); test for equirectangular by extreme horizontal stretching in the top and bottom rows and left-right edge continuity.
entries.notes: camera.format_aspect covers letterboxing only. A stereo or 360 source silently breaks every geometric detector in the set.

entries.label: Storyboard, animatic or rough-line frame
entries.description: Unfinished production art standing in for a finished shot: pencil lines, no colour, timing notes.
entries.frame_evidence: Near-monochrome sketchy linework with low fill saturation and a high line-weight variance.
entries.detector_note: High ink_line_fraction with low flat_fill_fraction and near-zero saturation, plus a high line_weight_variance indicating hand lines rather than clean-up.
entries.notes: A delivery check: an animatic frame surviving into a finished cut is a hard fail and nothing currently catches it.

entries.label: Building or structure collapse
entries.description: Large-scale architecture failing: walls falling, roofs dropping, a silhouette losing its upper mass.
entries.frame_evidence: A large static structure's silhouette loses area from the top downward while a debris and dust field expands below.
entries.detector_note: Segment the large static background structure by its zero-motion mask in earlier cels; collapse = a monotonic loss of that mask's area with downward motion of the lost region and a rising dust mask.
entries.notes: object_dynamics.stack_collapse is prop-scale. Nothing covers the environment itself failing.

entries.label: Strum or pluck event
entries.description: A fast hand pass across strings, with the strings visibly responding.
entries.frame_evidence: The strumming hand crosses the instrument body quickly and the string region shows a one-to-two-cel blur.
entries.detector_note: Wrist speed peak inside the instrument bbox coincident with a local high-frequency energy spike in the string region.
entries.notes: The 'strings do not vibrate' error is one of the most common animation misses and is directly measurable.

entries.label: Stuck, dead or hot pixel
entries.description: A single pixel or tiny cluster with a constant value regardless of content.
entries.frame_evidence: A persistent bright or dark point in exactly the same coordinates across every frame of the file.
entries.detector_note: Per-pixel temporal variance across the whole file; a dead pixel is a variance near zero at a location whose 8-neighbourhood has normal variance.

entries.label: Apparent age band of a subject
entries.description: A coarse age band for each person: infant, child, adolescent, adult, elderly.
entries.frame_evidence: Head-to-body proportion, facial feature spacing, skin texture and posture, taken together.
entries.detector_note: Head-height-to-body-height ratio from pose landmarks is the deterministic prior (infant ~1:4, adult ~1:7.5); the band itself needs a trained age estimator or a VLM. Always report the ratio alongside the band.
entries.vlm_question: Roughly how old is this person: a baby, a young child, a teenager, an adult, or elderly?
entries.notes: Report as apparent, never as fact; the ratio is the evidence and the band is the inference.

entries.label: Character damage or dishevelment state
entries.description: Progressive dirt, blood, tears, sweat and hair disorder on a character - and whether it persists correctly.
entries.frame_evidence: New dark or red patches and raised high-frequency texture appear on a character and do not disappear in later frames.
entries.detector_note: Per-character appearance delta against the character's first clean appearance in the sequence: added dark/red mask area and hair-region edge entropy increase. Requires identity tracking.
entries.notes: The 'damage resets after the cut' error is invisible to every current entry. Monotonicity is the whole test.

entries.label: Duplicate instances of one character
entries.description: Two or more simultaneous instances of the same identity in one frame.
entries.frame_evidence: Two person detections whose appearance embeddings match above the identity threshold, both fully visible.
entries.detector_note: Face or body identity embeddings on all detections in a frame; report any within-frame pair above the same-identity threshold, with a strict distance and both detections above a size floor.
entries.notes: Covers afterimage clones, split-screen twins, and the generative-model failure where one character reappears in the background.

entries.label: Subject visible in a reflection
entries.description: A second instance of a subject appearing in a mirror, window, water or polished surface.
entries.frame_evidence: A region containing a subject-like appearance that moves in mirrored correlation with the real subject.
entries.detector_note: Detect a second person/subject instance whose motion is the horizontal mirror of the primary's within a bounded region; require an appearance-embedding match above the identity threshold.
entries.notes: interaction_social.partner_implied_by_reflection covers an OFF-SCREEN partner only. The subject's own reflection is a different and much more common shot.

entries.label: Semi-transparent subject
entries.description: A character rendered partly see-through - a ghost, a hologram, a fading-out body.
entries.frame_evidence: The background structure remains visible and correlated inside the subject mask.
entries.detector_note: Correlate the subject region against the background plate recovered from neighbouring cels (temporal median under camera compensation); transparency = correlation above 0.4 inside the mask.

entries.label: Burned-in caption band timing
entries.description: A subtitle band's appearance, dwell and disappearance timing.
entries.frame_evidence: A text region in the lower safe area appears and disappears at intervals independent of the picture cuts.
entries.detector_note: scene_semantics.burned_in_subtitle_band plus per-block onset/offset timing; report dwell distribution and any block shorter than 700 ms.
entries.notes: The pipeline writes subtitles; nothing in the taxonomy measures whether they are readable for long enough.

entries.label: Ground yielding under a load
entries.description: Snow compressing, sand sinking, a mattress or cushion depressing under a body.
entries.frame_evidence: The contact region's local surface height or shading changes at contact and partially recovers on release.
entries.detector_note: On the stabilised surface, measure the local shading gradient change inside the contact patch at the contact cel and its recovery fraction after release.

entries.label: Persistent skin marking
entries.description: A tattoo, scar, birthmark or painted marking on skin, and whether it stays put.
entries.frame_evidence: A fixed dark or coloured pattern inside a skin region that deforms with the body rather than sliding over it.
entries.detector_note: Detect stable high-contrast structure inside the skin mask; verify it is body-locked by tracking it against the pose warp rather than against the frame.
entries.notes: Sliding tattoos are a standard LoRA and CG defect and nothing here would catch it.

entries.label: Object floating with no support
entries.description: A prop suspended in air with no contact and no ballistic trajectory - hovering, orbiting or rising slowly.
entries.frame_evidence: An object with no contact point whose vertical acceleration is not gravity, often with a slow drift or orbit.
entries.detector_note: Object track with no contact and vertical acceleration inconsistent with the file's own gravity estimate from other props; require >= 8 cels.
entries.notes: object_dynamics.floating_no_ground_contact is a vlm flag for a DEFECT. Intentional levitation needs the same measurement with the opposite verdict.

entries.label: Subject appearing or vanishing in place
entries.description: A person or creature present in one cel and absent in the next, with no cut and no exit path.
entries.frame_evidence: A subject track terminates or begins mid-frame, far from any frame border and with no occluder.
entries.detector_note: Track termination or initiation with the bbox centre more than 15% of frame size from any border, no cut boundary within 2 cels, and no occluding foreground mask.
entries.notes: Also the correct detector for tracker failure - the null model matters, so report the occluder test alongside.

entries.label: Overall temporal incoherence
entries.description: A single roll-up of how much the frame content churns beyond what the motion explains.
entries.frame_evidence: High residual change after compensating for all measured motion, sustained across the shot.
entries.detector_note: Warp each cel to the next by the measured flow and compute the residual; a real clip's residual is grain-level, a hallucinated one's is structural. Report the residual's spectral slope as well as its magnitude.

entries.label: On-screen text appearing, changing or leaving
entries.description: The event of text arriving or departing - a title card, a subtitle, a chyron, a caption.
entries.frame_evidence: A text-like region's presence changes between cels while the underlying picture does not cut.
entries.detector_note: Run the MSER stroke-width text proxy per cel; report onset and offset cels of each stable text region, gated against editing_time cut boundaries.
entries.notes: scene_semantics.text_region_presence is per-frame. The TIMING of a title or subtitle is what an editor actually needs.

entries.label: Text orientation, skew and mirroring
entries.description: Whether visible text is upright, rotated, perspective-skewed on a surface, or mirrored.
entries.frame_evidence: The dominant stroke orientation of the text region differs from horizontal, or the glyph shapes are laterally reversed.
entries.detector_note: Fit the text baseline angle from the component centroid line; mirroring is detected by comparing OCR confidence on the region against its horizontal flip.
entries.notes: Mirrored text is the giveaway for a reflection shot and for a flipped plate - a real and cheap defect check.

entries.label: Pattern drift on clothing or surfaces
entries.description: A repeating pattern that slides, reorganises or changes scale on a surface that is not moving that way.
entries.frame_evidence: A patterned region's texture phase advances independently of the surface's tracked motion.
entries.detector_note: Track the surface by homography, then measure the pattern's phase via cross-correlation in the surface's own frame; drift = a phase advance in the stabilised frame.
entries.notes: The same test also catches cg_3d texture swimming, which is why it should be a shared primitive.

entries.label: Thought bubble or imagined-scene inset
entries.description: An imagined or remembered image shown inside a soft-edged or bubble-shaped region.
entries.frame_evidence: A region with a soft, cloudy or scalloped boundary containing different scene content.
entries.detector_note: Detect a closed region whose boundary is high-curvature and non-rectangular containing content uncorrelated with its surround; adjudicate with a VLM.
entries.vlm_question: Is part of this image showing a thought, memory or imagined scene inside a bubble or soft-edged panel?

entries.label: Point of view through a vehicle windscreen
entries.description: A framing where a static interior border surrounds a moving exterior.
entries.frame_evidence: The frame's outer region is static (dashboard, pillars, mirror) while an inner region shows strong forward flow.
entries.detector_note: Split the frame into a static-mask and a moving-mask by temporal variance; fire when the static mask forms a connected border around a high-flow interior.

entries.label: Thruster, jet or rocket plume
entries.description: A directed high-velocity emission from a machine, distinct from ambient smoke.
entries.frame_evidence: A bright cone anchored to a fixed point on the vehicle, with flow directed outward along the cone axis and a hot core.
entries.detector_note: Fire/emissive mask anchored to the machine mask boundary; require flow divergence positive along one dominant axis and the anchor point stable in the machine's local frame.
entries.notes: fluids_fire covers flame and smoke but nothing anchored to and moving with a vehicle.

entries.label: Title card, chapter card or credit roll
entries.description: A frame whose subject IS text on a plain field, or scrolling credits.
entries.frame_evidence: A near-uniform background with a large centred text region and near-zero non-text content; credits show uniform vertical scroll.
entries.detector_note: Text region area over total non-background area above 0.6 with background colour variance low; credits add a uniform vertical flow of the text region only.

entries.label: Tracking markers or witness points visible
entries.description: Crosses, dots or tape markers left on a set or a suit.
entries.frame_evidence: Small high-contrast regular geometric marks in a repeated pattern on a surface or costume.
entries.detector_note: Template-match small cross and dot patterns; require three or more instances with similar scale and a consistent surface attachment across cels.

entries.label: Reused transformation or stock sequence
entries.description: The same animated sequence inserted more than once in a piece.
entries.frame_evidence: A run of frames whose perceptual hashes match an earlier run within a small distance.
entries.detector_note: Sliding-window perceptual-hash matching across the whole file; report matched runs longer than 12 frames with their two time positions.
entries.notes: editing_time.exact_loop_repeat is within-shot. Cross-shot bank reuse is the anime economics tell and is separately measurable.

entries.label: A tall element toppling
entries.description: A tree, mast, pole or column rotating about its base and falling.
entries.frame_evidence: A tall vertical component's principal axis rotates through a large angle with its base fixed.
entries.detector_note: Track the tall component's principal axis angle with its lowest point held fixed within 5px; fire on a monotonic rotation beyond 40 deg with an accelerating rate.
entries.notes: object_dynamics.topple_tipping covers small props with a tipping edge; a felling has a different scale, duration and accelerating profile.

entries.label: Motorcycle or bicycle lean angle
entries.description: The roll of a two-wheeled vehicle into a turn, which must agree with its path curvature.
entries.frame_evidence: The vehicle's vertical axis tilts from frame-vertical while it follows a curved path.
entries.detector_note: Principal axis angle of the vehicle mask relative to the fitted ground normal, correlated against the track's path curvature; disagreement is the finding.

entries.label: Colour absorption with depth underwater
entries.description: The progressive loss of red and then green with distance through water - the strongest underwater cue.
entries.frame_evidence: Distant parts of the frame are markedly more blue-green than near parts, beyond any aerial-perspective norm.
entries.detector_note: Fit per-channel mean against the depth proxy (distance transform from the nearest in-focus region, or a depth map when available); underwater = a red-channel slope far steeper than blue's.
entries.notes: fluids_fire.underwater_view is a vlm yes/no. This is the measurement that separates a real underwater plate from a blue grade.

entries.label: Motion damped by water drag
entries.description: Limb and object motion that decelerates without contact and never overshoots.
entries.frame_evidence: Every motion has a long slow tail; there is no snap and no follow-through oscillation.
entries.detector_note: Measure the deceleration profile of limb tips: underwater motion shows an exponential decay to rest with no velocity sign reversal (no overshoot) and a time constant above 0.4 s.
entries.notes: The inverse of body_action.follow_through_overshoot; its ABSENCE is the finding.

entries.label: Vehicle leaving the ground
entries.description: All wheels off the surface with a ballistic body trajectory.
entries.frame_evidence: The wheel contact points lift off the fitted ground line and the body follows a parabola.
entries.detector_note: Fit the ground line; airborne = all detected wheel-bottom points above it for >= 3 cels with the body centroid following a parabolic fit.

entries.label: Vehicle crash deformation
entries.description: A vehicle's silhouette permanently changing at an impact.
entries.frame_evidence: The vehicle mask's outline changes abruptly at the impact cel and does not return.
entries.detector_note: Track the vehicle mask's shape descriptor; a crash = a single-cel discontinuity above threshold coincident with a deceleration spike, with no recovery over the following 15 cels.
entries.notes: object_dynamics.dent_permanent_deformation is prop-scale; a vehicle crash also has body roll, debris and glass and should roll them up.

entries.label: Expulsion from the mouth
entries.description: Material ejected from the mouth with a forward torso fold.
entries.frame_evidence: A fluid mask emerges from the mouth region with downward-forward velocity, coincident with a deep torso flexion.
entries.detector_note: fluids_fire stream detection anchored to the mouth landmark plus torso_pitch_lean beyond 40 deg in the same window.

entries.label: Breach or hole punched through a surface
entries.description: A new opening in a wall, door or vehicle panel, with debris ejected in the direction of travel.
entries.frame_evidence: A new region of different content appears inside a previously uniform surface, ringed by radial cracks or debris.
entries.detector_note: On a homography-stabilised surface, detect a new interior region whose appearance differs from the surface statistics, with a debris burst in the same cel.

entries.label: Wardrobe continuity across a cut
entries.description: The same character's clothing changing between shots that are meant to be continuous.
entries.frame_evidence: Per-zone garment colour histograms for the matched identity differ across the cut beyond the grade-drift allowance.
entries.detector_note: Match identities across the cut, then compare per-zone colour histograms after normalising for the shot grade delta measured on a neutral reference.
entries.notes: The classic continuity error. Must be measured AFTER removing the grade difference or every graded cut fires.

entries.label: Garment inventory on a subject
entries.description: What the subject is wearing, as a coarse open set: top, outer layer, headwear, eyewear, mask, gloves, footwear.
entries.frame_evidence: Distinct colour and texture regions bounded by the body silhouette in the expected anatomical zones.
entries.detector_note: Human parsing / clothing segmentation model over the person mask, mapped to body zones from pose landmarks. VLM fallback for stylised art.
entries.vlm_question: List what this person is wearing: headwear, eyewear, top, jacket, gloves, footwear, anything covering the face.
entries.notes: There is no clothing entry anywhere in the fifteen shards beyond material_fabric_cloth. Costume is one of the most-observed things in any frame.

entries.label: Persistent watermark, bug or burn-in
entries.description: A graphic that is identical in every frame regardless of the picture underneath - channel bug, watermark, timecode burn.
entries.frame_evidence: A region whose inter-frame difference is essentially zero across an entire shot boundary.
entries.detector_note: Per-pixel temporal variance across the whole file; a watermark is a connected region with variance near zero that survives cuts. Report its bbox and opacity estimate.
entries.notes: Critical for provenance and for licensing checks, and completely absent.

entries.label: Subject reflected in wet ground or a puddle
entries.description: A vertically mirrored, distorted copy of a subject below it on a wet surface.
entries.frame_evidence: A dim vertically flipped copy of the subject appearing directly below its ground contact point.
entries.detector_note: Vertically flip the subject region about the estimated ground line and cross-correlate with the region below it; report peak correlation and vertical offset.
entries.notes: The rainy-street shot's single most defining element, and no shard measures it - fluids covers reflection distortion in water, not the SUBJECT'S reflection.

entries.label: Blowing, whistling or spitting
entries.description: A sustained pucker with directed airflow - blowing out a candle, whistling, spitting.
entries.frame_evidence: A held tight pucker with an effect at a distance: a flame guttering, dust moving, a droplet leaving the mouth.
entries.detector_note: Sustained lip_protrusion above threshold for >= 4 cels, paired with an effect in the region in front of the mouth (flame amplitude change, particle emission, or a droplet track).
entries.notes: The candle-blowout is a scene beat the whole taxonomy currently misses; face_head has the pucker but nothing checks the world responding.

entries.label: Interior reflected in a night window
entries.description: The doubled image of an interior superimposed on a dark exterior through glass.
entries.frame_evidence: A dark region carries a faint second image that moves with the interior, not with anything beyond the glass.
entries.detector_note: Within a dark quad region, test for two superimposed motion layers (bimodal flow histogram) where one layer's motion matches an in-frame interior subject.

entries.label: Windscreen wiper sweep
entries.description: A blade sweeping across glass at a regular rate, clearing water behind it.
entries.frame_evidence: An elongated dark element rotates about a fixed pivot at the frame's lower edge with a regular period, and the region behind it briefly clears.
entries.detector_note: Rotating elongated component about a fixed pivot; period from the angle series; verify the trailing region's droplet density drops after each pass.
entries.notes: The defining element of the rainy-drive shot; also a strong per-frame timing reference.

entries.label: Wound appearing on a body
entries.description: A new injury mark appearing on a character at a specific frame.
entries.frame_evidence: A new red or dark region appears inside the person mask, body-locked, at a cel that often coincides with an impact.
entries.detector_note: Body-locked appearance test: warp the person region by the pose delta between cels and find new red/dark components that persist for >= 5 cels; report the cel index and the body zone.
entries.notes: fluids_fire covers blood as a fluid. Nothing covers the injury as an event on a body, which is what an action reel needs.

entries.label: Zero-gravity or weightless motion
entries.description: Bodies and objects drifting with constant velocity and no downward acceleration.
entries.frame_evidence: Free objects follow straight constant-speed paths and rotate at a constant rate with no settle.
entries.detector_note: Fit each free object's trajectory; zero-g = vertical acceleration within noise of zero across >= 10 cels for two or more independent objects, with rotation rate constant.
entries.notes: object_dynamics.gravity_direction_consistency assumes gravity exists. Its absence is a legitimate and detectable scene state.

entries.label: Tonal zone occupancy
entries.description: How the frame's pixels distribute across eleven print zones - the photographer's read of exposure.
entries.frame_evidence: Not visible - a histogram summary.
entries.detector_note: Bin luminance into 11 zones on a log scale and report the fraction in each, plus the modal zone.
entries.notes: More interpretable than the raw 256-bin histogram already present, and directly comparable across shots.

entries.label: Ash flick
entries.description: A quick thumb or index tap on the cigarette to shed ash.
entries.frame_evidence: A 1-3 unique-cel high-frequency finger oscillation against the held cylinder with the hand otherwise stationary.
entries.detector_note: Index or thumb tip displacement in the hand-local frame exceeding 0.15 hand-widths across one unique cel while the wrist is static, repeated within 3 cels.
entries.notes: Needs 12+ unique cels per second to resolve; on 3s anime the whole flick can occupy one drawing and is unmeasurable.

entries.label: Bimanual role-differentiated action
entries.description: One hand stabilises while the other acts, the normal pattern for cutting, writing and opening jars.
entries.frame_evidence: One wrist near-static on an object while the other moves substantially, both within the same object region.
entries.detector_note: Over a 6-unique-cel window, one wrist speed below 0.02 shoulder-widths per cel and the other above 0.06, with both hand bboxes within 2 hand-widths of each other.
entries.notes: Also matches one hand simply resting near where the other works; the shared-object requirement is only a proximity proxy.

entries.label: Bimanual symmetric action
entries.description: Both hands do the same thing at the same time, mirrored about the body midline.
entries.frame_evidence: Left and right wrist trajectories mirrored about the torso midline over several unique cels.
entries.detector_note: Correlate left wrist displacement with the x-mirrored right wrist displacement about the shoulder midline; symmetric when corr > 0.8 over 5+ unique cels.
entries.notes: A camera pan drives both wrists together and fakes symmetry; camera compensation is mandatory.

entries.label: Opening or closing a book or lid
entries.description: A hinged flat object rotates about an edge under hand control.
entries.frame_evidence: A quadrilateral region whose aspect and skew change progressively about a fixed edge while a hand stays on its free edge.
entries.detector_note: Fit a homography between the quad in successive unique cels (cv2.findHomography on approxPolyDP corners); a hinge is indicated when one edge stays fixed within 3px while the opposite edge sweeps.
entries.notes: Requires a reasonably rectilinear object with visible corners; fails on soft covers and on heavily stylised 2D art.

entries.label: Laying a brick
entries.description: A rectangular block is carried, positioned onto a course, and tapped down.
entries.frame_evidence: A rectangular object transported, lowered onto a horizontal line of similar rectangles, released, then tapped.
entries.detector_note: Candidate from set_object_down where the object is a strong rectangle (approxPolyDP 4 vertices, aspect 1.8-2.5) landing collinear with other rectangles; confirm with a VLM crop.
entries.vlm_question: Is a brick or block being placed onto a wall in this image? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: The collinearity test is what separates this from setting down any box; it needs at least two previously-laid units visible.

entries.label: Buttoning clothing
entries.description: Both hands work at a small point on the torso, one feeding a button and the other guiding fabric.
entries.frame_evidence: Two hands close together at chest or cuff, both in pinch grips, with small opposed movements and near-zero net travel.
entries.detector_note: Gate on two pinch grips within 1.5 hand-widths of each other over the torso, then ask a VLM on the crop.
entries.vlm_question: Are the two hands fastening a button on clothing? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Buttoning, unbuttoning, adjusting a tie and fiddling with a zip are visually near-identical at normal shot scales.

entries.label: Pressing a physical button
entries.description: A fingertip drives into a small control and stops, sometimes with visible travel.
entries.frame_evidence: Single extended fingertip approaching a small device region, decelerating to zero, and holding for a cel or two.
entries.detector_note: One fingertip extended (flexion ratio > 0.9) with others flexed, tip speed profile showing approach then a dwell of at least 1 unique cel, and the tip inside a device ROI.
entries.notes: Cannot see whether the button actually moved; button travel is typically sub-pixel. A device ROI must be supplied since no object detector is installed.

entries.label: Catching an object
entries.description: An incoming object is intercepted and its motion is arrested by the hand.
entries.frame_evidence: An independently-moving object converging on the hand, then sharing the hand motion from one cel onward.
entries.detector_note: Requires tracking a fast small object before contact, which needs a detector we do not have; Farneback flow on a blurred ball gives no stable ROI to seed.
entries.notes: Logged as a blind spot; the post-catch half is measurable by coupling but the pre-catch half is not, and reporting only the second half would be misleading.

entries.label: Cigarette held between the lips
entries.description: The cigarette rests in the mouth with the hand withdrawn.
entries.frame_evidence: A thin cylinder protruding from the mouth region while both hands are elsewhere.
entries.detector_note: Crop the face lower third (from FaceLandmarker or the pose head box) and ask; check separately that no wrist is within 0.8 head-widths.
entries.vlm_question: Is there a cigarette in the person mouth? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Anime often draws this as a couple of strokes; small VLMs miss it on stylised art more often than they false-positive.

entries.label: Cigarette held in the hand
entries.description: A cigarette is present between the fingers.
entries.frame_evidence: A thin pale cylinder held between index and middle finger, often with a lit tip or smoke wisp.
entries.detector_note: Crop 2.5x the hand bbox and ask a VLM; the deterministic tool-axis fit can flag a thin elongated object but cannot identify it.
entries.vlm_question: Is the person holding a cigarette between their fingers? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Pens, chopsticks, matches and thin brushes all produce the same thin-cylinder geometry; the VLM is the only discriminator we have.

entries.label: Lifting a cigarette to the mouth
entries.description: The full drag cycle: cigarette-holding hand rises to the lips, dwells, and lowers.
entries.frame_evidence: Hand-to-mouth minimum with a thin cylinder ending at the lips, followed by retreat and often an exhale.
entries.detector_note: Gate on hand_object.hand_to_mouth_transport (landmark) to pick the candidate window, then ask a VLM on the mouth-plus-hand crop at the distance minimum.
entries.vlm_question: Is the person putting a cigarette to their lips? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Drinking from a straw and eating from a fork produce the same landmark trajectory; the VLM crop is what separates them.

entries.label: Hand-object contact onset
entries.description: The primitive event where the hand first touches the object, the anchor for every manipulation.
entries.frame_evidence: The hand silhouette meets the object silhouette with no gap, the hand decelerates, and the object begins to share the hand motion within a cel or two.
entries.detector_note: Composite: (a) minimum gap between fingertip landmarks and the nearest strong edge from cv2.Canny inside a 1.5x hand ROI falls below 3px, (b) wrist speed drops below 25 percent of reach peak, (c) object-follows-hand correlation rises above 0.6 within 3 unique cels. Require 2 of 3.
entries.notes: Silhouette adjacency is not contact: a hand passing in front of an object satisfies (a) alone. The coupling term is what carries the evidence, so never fire on (a)+(b) in a static-object shot without a null from a non-hand ROI.

entries.label: Contact with no deceleration
entries.description: The hand reaches contact at full speed and stops instantly, a physics violation typical of snapped CG constraints or missing inbetweens.
entries.frame_evidence: Wrist speed goes from near-peak to near-zero across a single unique cel at the contact frame.
entries.detector_note: speed[t-1] > 0.6 * reach_peak AND speed[t] < 0.1 * reach_peak on adjacent unique cels at the contact index.
entries.notes: In 2D this is often a legitimate stylistic snap on 2s, not an error; report it, do not moralise about it.

entries.label: Contact shadow where hand meets object
entries.description: A darkening in the crevice between hand and held object, the cheapest visual proof of contact.
entries.frame_evidence: A thin low-luminance band along the hand-object boundary that moves with the grip.
entries.detector_note: Sample luminance along the normal to the hand-object boundary; a contact shadow is a local minimum within 3px of the boundary at least 12 levels below both sides, persisting across unique cels.
entries.notes: Needs a boundary estimate, so it inherits the hand-mask error; flat-lit anime has no contact shadows by design and must report NOT DETECTABLE rather than a defect.

entries.label: Coupling break mid-carry
entries.description: The object stops following the hand although no release was animated, a common CG constraint failure.
entries.frame_evidence: Coupling collapses for a few unique cels while the aperture stays closed and the hand keeps a holding pose.
entries.detector_note: Detect coupling dropping below null_mean + 2*null_std for 2 or more unique cels while landmark aperture_norm stays below its holding median plus 0.05.
entries.notes: Heavy motion blur destroys flow inside the object ROI and fakes a break; gate on hand_object.hand_motion_blur.

entries.label: Opening or closing a curtain
entries.description: A hand drags a fabric panel laterally, bunching or spreading it and changing the light behind.
entries.frame_evidence: A vertically-oriented textured region translating sideways with its fold frequency changing, plus a global luminance change in the window area.
entries.detector_note: Track the vertical-edge density profile (column-wise sum of cv2.Sobel dx magnitude) inside a window ROI across unique cels; a draw shows the density front translating laterally while mean window luminance rises or falls monotonically.
entries.notes: Direction of the luminance change tells open from closed only if the light is genuinely behind the curtain; a night interior inverts it.

entries.label: Cutting with a knife
entries.description: A bladed tool is drawn through a target, usually with repeated sawing or a single press.
entries.frame_evidence: A straight elongated tool with its tip descending into a target region, plus repeated short reciprocation along the blade axis.
entries.detector_note: Candidate from tool_long_axis plus reciprocating tip motion, then confirm on a crop centred on the tool tip and target.
entries.vlm_question: Is the person cutting something with a knife or blade? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Actual separation of the cut material is usually sub-pixel and hidden by the hand, so the evidence is the motion pattern, not the cut.

entries.label: Grasping and turning a door handle
entries.description: The hand closes on a handle and rotates it before the door moves.
entries.frame_evidence: Hand closes at a fixed point on a vertical surface, then wrist roll occurs with the hand centroid nearly stationary.
entries.detector_note: Hand centroid static within 0.05 shoulder-widths while the hand-local axis (landmark 5->17) rotates by more than 15 degrees over 2-4 unique cels.
entries.notes: In-plane hand rotation is measurable, but a handle turned toward or away from camera produces no in-plane rotation at all.

entries.label: Door, lid or drawer opening
entries.description: A large planar element moves aside under hand control, revealing new content behind it.
entries.frame_evidence: A large region translating or rotating with a hand attached, and previously hidden pixels appearing along its leading edge.
entries.detector_note: Segment the moving region with a flow-magnitude threshold on Farneback flow, verify a hand landmark lies inside it, and measure the newly-revealed area (pixels whose local structure was absent in the previous unique cel).
entries.notes: Does not distinguish door from drawer from curtain from lid; treat as a generic reveal primitive and let a VLM name it.

entries.label: Pulling a drawer out
entries.description: A rectangular element translates toward camera or laterally along a straight track while gripped.
entries.frame_evidence: A rectangle growing along one axis with a straight-line hand path and no rotation.
entries.detector_note: Use door_open_swing as a candidate, then ask a VLM on a 1.5x crop of the moving region.
entries.vlm_question: Is a drawer being pulled open in this image? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Pure translation with no hinge separates a drawer from a door geometrically, but only when the camera is roughly perpendicular.

entries.label: Drinking from a vessel
entries.description: A cup, glass or bottle is raised to the mouth and tilted.
entries.frame_evidence: Hand-to-mouth minimum with a bulky object at the lips and a head-back tilt during the dwell.
entries.detector_note: hand_to_mouth_transport minimum coincident with a head pitch change (angle of the nose-to-shoulder-midpoint vector rising by more than 5 degrees from its pre-reach baseline) and a dwell of 2+ unique cels at the minimum.
entries.notes: Landmark evidence is the trajectory plus the head tilt only: it cannot tell a cup from a bottle from a bowl, and a shot drunk fast shows no tilt at all. Confirm the vessel with a VLM crop before calling it drinking.

entries.label: Bringing food to the mouth
entries.description: Food, with or without a utensil, is transported to the mouth and released there.
entries.frame_evidence: Hand-to-mouth minimum where the carried object shrinks or disappears after the dwell.
entries.detector_note: Gate on hand_to_mouth_transport, then compare the grip-ROI template before and after the dwell (a real bite reduces the object), and confirm identity with a VLM crop.
entries.vlm_question: Is the person putting food into their mouth? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: The object-shrinks test fails for a spoon (utensil returns unchanged in silhouette) and for anything occluded by the jaw.

entries.label: Wrong number of fingers
entries.description: The rendered or drawn hand shows more or fewer than the expected number of digits.
entries.frame_evidence: A clear, unoccluded open hand crop in which the visible digits do not number five.
entries.detector_note: Select unique cels where the hand is open (high mean extension) and large (bbox > 5 percent of frame width), crop 2x, and ask a VLM; require agreement on 2 of 3 sampled cels.
entries.vlm_question: How many fingers are visible on this hand? Answer with a single number.
entries.notes: Only ask on an open, front-facing, unoccluded hand: on a fist or a foreshortened hand the true answer is not five and the finding would be false. Small VLMs miscount even good crops, hence the agreement requirement.

entries.label: Per-finger flexion profile
entries.description: The flexion ratio of each of the five digits, the raw substrate for every grasp label.
entries.frame_evidence: Fingertip-to-wrist distances relative to each finger fully-extended length in the same frame.
entries.detector_note: For each finger f, ratio = ||tip - wrist|| / (sum of its segment lengths from landmarks); segment lengths taken as the per-frame max over the shot to normalise for scale.
entries.notes: Foreshortening reduces the ratio without any real flexion; this is the single largest error source in the grasp taxonomy above.

entries.label: Finger individuation
entries.description: Whether fingers move independently or as a block, which separates skilled manipulation from a generic open/close.
entries.frame_evidence: Divergent per-finger flexion trajectories across a window rather than five parallel curves.
entries.detector_note: Variance of the five flexion signals after removing their common mean; individuation index = residual variance / total variance over unique cels.
entries.notes: CG hands driven by a single curl slider give an individuation index near zero, which is a genuinely useful finding, but so does a low-quality landmark track.

entries.label: Finger rig pop
entries.description: A rigged finger snaps between poses in a single frame with no inbetween, or a joint flips.
entries.frame_evidence: A single-frame discontinuity in one finger flexion signal while the rest of the hand is smooth.
entries.detector_note: Per-finger flexion second difference over unique cels; a pop is an isolated spike above 4 MADs in one finger while the others stay within 1 MAD.
entries.notes: Landmark noise produces the same isolated spikes, so require the frame either side to be clean and the hand to be large in frame.

entries.label: Fingers wrap behind the object
entries.description: Some fingers disappear behind the object silhouette, proving the hand is around the object rather than beside it.
entries.frame_evidence: Finger contours terminating at the object edge on one side and reappearing on the other, or fingertips simply absent behind the object.
entries.detector_note: Crop the hand-plus-object bbox with 1.5x padding and ask a VLM; the deterministic alternative needs an object mask we cannot produce.
entries.vlm_question: Do any of the fingers pass behind the object so that their tips are hidden? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: A classic tell for pasted-on CG props and for flat anime hands drawn in front of an object they should be holding.

entries.label: Fingertip pad flattening on contact
entries.description: The finger pad visibly compresses where it presses the object, a soft-body cue absent in most rigid CG hands.
entries.frame_evidence: The fingertip contour flattens against the object edge instead of remaining a smooth convex arc.
entries.detector_note: Crop tightly to a single contact fingertip (about 6 percent of frame width) and ask a VLM; deterministic contour curvature is unreliable at the pixel scales involved.
entries.vlm_question: Is the fingertip squashed flat where it touches the object, or does it keep a rounded shape? Answer squashed or rounded.
entries.notes: Live action almost always shows flattening; its absence in CG is a finding, but low-resolution crops make the VLM guess. Require the crop to be at least 96px on the short side.

entries.label: Flame appears in the hand
entries.description: A small flickering light source materialises at the top of a held object.
entries.frame_evidence: A small warm high-luminance blob near the fingertips persisting across cels with frame-to-frame shape flicker.
entries.detector_note: Persistent (>4 unique cels) small warm bright component near a fingertip, with area or centroid varying more than 10 percent per cel (the flicker signature) and a local luminance halo gradient.
entries.notes: A practical bulb, a phone screen or a lit cigarette tip can all pass; the flicker variance is the only real discriminator and 2D animation quantises it.

entries.label: Visible gap between hand and held object
entries.description: The object travels with the hand while a clear gap separates them, the opposite failure to interpenetration.
entries.frame_evidence: Background pixels visible between the finger contours and the object edge while coupling is high.
entries.detector_note: After a coarse hand mask (grabCut seeded from the landmark hull) and an object ROI, measure the minimum inter-contour distance with cv2.distanceTransform; flag when min gap > 4px sustained while coupling > 0.8.
entries.notes: Foreshortening and depth separation make a legitimate gap; this is a candidate-generator for a VLM check, not a verdict.

entries.label: Forearm pronation / supination proxy
entries.description: Rotation of the hand about the forearm axis, needed for pouring, screwing and turning.
entries.frame_evidence: The apparent width of the hand changes and the thumb crosses from one side of the hand to the other while the wrist stays put.
entries.detector_note: Track the signed offset of the thumb MCP 2 from the line through landmarks 5 and 17, normalised by palm width; a sign change is a pronation/supination crossing.
entries.notes: A proxy only. True forearm rotation needs 3D and the mediapipe z is not accurate enough to supply it; never report degrees from this.

entries.label: Fused or melted fingers
entries.description: Digits merge into an undifferentiated mass or lose their joint structure, the signature generative-image hand failure.
entries.frame_evidence: A hand crop where the finger boundaries are absent or the digits bend in anatomically impossible ways.
entries.detector_note: Crop the hand at 2.5x and ask a VLM; a deterministic proxy is the count of distinct convexity defects in the hand contour (cv2.convexityDefects) being under 3 on an open hand, which can gate which crops get asked.
entries.vlm_question: Are the fingers on this hand clearly separate and normally shaped, or are they merged, twisted or malformed? Answer normal or malformed.
entries.notes: Project history: the VLM hand judge has previously scored obviously melted hands as clean at 1.00 confidence on full frames. Only ever ask on a tight crop, and treat a single clean verdict as weak evidence.

entries.label: Gesticulation rate over the shot
entries.description: How much the hands move overall while talking, a character-behaviour statistic.
entries.frame_evidence: Total camera-compensated wrist path length per second across the shot.
entries.detector_note: Sum of wrist displacements over unique cels divided by shot duration, normalised by shoulder width; report both hands separately.
entries.notes: Must be computed on unique cels and then divided by real elapsed seconds, not by frame count, or 2s and 3s animation reports a third of the true rate.

entries.label: Beat gestures during speech
entries.description: Rhythmic small hand movements that punctuate speech rather than depict anything.
entries.frame_evidence: Repeated small vertical hand excursions with no object contact and no configuration change, while the mouth is moving.
entries.detector_note: Wrist vertical position band-passed at 1-4 Hz over unique cels with amplitude 0.05-0.25 shoulder-widths, hand configuration stable (aperture variance low), and no coupled object ROI.
entries.notes: Correlating with actual speech would need mouth-opening from FaceLandmarker; without it, a bouncing hand while silent scores the same.

entries.label: Clapping
entries.description: The two palms meet repeatedly.
entries.frame_evidence: Inter-wrist distance showing periodic sharp minima near zero with both hands open.
entries.detector_note: find_peaks on the negated inter-wrist distance (normalised by shoulder width) with minima below 0.25 and a regular period; both hands must be extended.
entries.notes: Hands crossing in front of each other from a side view produce the same minima; a contact frame is often the one that is blurred or skipped.

entries.label: Counting on fingers
entries.description: The number of extended fingers changes in steps, enumerating items.
entries.frame_evidence: Extended-finger count stepping by one and holding for a beat, repeatedly.
entries.detector_note: Per-cel extended-finger count from the five flexion ratios thresholded at 0.85; counting when the count changes by exactly 1 at least twice with plateaus of 2+ unique cels between changes.
entries.notes: Foreshortened fingers read as flexed; the count is only meaningful with the palm roughly facing camera (check hand bbox aspect near 1.0).

entries.label: Finger snap
entries.description: Middle finger slips off the thumb in a fast snap.
entries.frame_evidence: A one-to-two frame transition from a thumb-middle contact pose to an extended-middle pose, usually motion blurred.
entries.detector_note: The event lasts under 60 ms; at 8-12 unique drawings per second in animation and with heavy blur in live action, no installed detector resolves the transition reliably, and audio is out of scope here.
entries.notes: Deliberate blind spot. A pre-snap pose can be detected as a lateral pinch but firing snap on that alone would be an overclaim.

entries.label: Fist clench
entries.description: The hand closes into a tight fist with nothing in it.
entries.frame_evidence: All fingertips drawn to the palm with no object silhouette in or crossing the fist.
entries.detector_note: All five flexion ratios below 0.55 AND no elongated object axis intersecting the hand hull (see tool_axis_through_grip returning nothing).
entries.notes: An object entirely inside the fist (a coin, a key) is invisible and reads as an empty fist; that is a genuine limit, not a bug.

entries.label: Hand to face / facepalm / chin rest
entries.description: The hand contacts the actor own face or head.
entries.frame_evidence: Hand region overlapping the face bbox with the wrist decelerating to rest and staying.
entries.detector_note: Hand bbox IoU with the face bbox above 0.15 and wrist speed below 0.02 shoulder-widths per unique cel for 3+ cels; report which face third (upper/mid/lower) is contacted.
entries.notes: A hand passing in front of the face gives the same IoU for a cel or two; the dwell requirement filters most of it.

entries.label: Handshake
entries.description: Two people clasp right hands and pump vertically.
entries.frame_evidence: Two hands from different skeletons merged into one region at mid-torso height, oscillating vertically together.
entries.detector_note: Wrists from two pose skeletons within 0.4 shoulder-widths, moving with correlated vertical oscillation (corr > 0.8) over 4+ unique cels.
entries.notes: Requires two tracked skeletons; PoseLandmarker in this build tracks a limited number of people and association across frames is not guaranteed.

entries.label: OK ring sign
entries.description: Thumb and index form a closed ring with the other fingers extended.
entries.frame_evidence: A visible enclosed loop between thumb and index while middle, ring and little fingers stay straight.
entries.detector_note: Pinch aperture below 0.15 palm-widths while middle/ring/pinky flexion ratios all exceed 0.85; optionally confirm an enclosed contour hole with cv2.findContours hierarchy inside the hand mask.
entries.notes: Geometrically identical to a precision pinch holding a small object; the extended-fingers condition is the only separator.

entries.label: Open palm-up presentation
