entries.description: A flat open hand offered palm-up, the classic explanatory or offering gesture.
entries.frame_evidence: Extended fingers with the palm surface facing the camera-up direction and the hand held away from the body.
entries.detector_note: All flexion ratios > 0.88 and the palm normal (cross of 0->5 and 0->17) pointing image-upward; wrist at least 0.6 shoulder-widths from the torso midline.
entries.notes: Palm normal is derived from weak relative-z and flips readily; treat as low-confidence unless it holds over 3+ unique cels.

entries.label: Pointing
entries.description: Index finger extended along the forearm direction to indicate something.
entries.frame_evidence: One extended finger with the others flexed, the finger axis roughly continuing the forearm line.
entries.detector_note: Index flexion ratio > 0.92 with middle/ring/pinky below 0.75, and the angle between the index vector (5->8) and the forearm vector (elbow 13 -> wrist 15) under 35 degrees.
entries.notes: A pointing pose held while gesturing about something else is still labelled pointing; this entry measures the pose, not the referent.

entries.label: Pointing direction in image space
entries.description: The 2D screen direction the pointing finger indicates.
entries.frame_evidence: The extended index vector orientation in the frame.
entries.detector_note: Angle of landmark 5->8 in image coordinates, plus a ray cast to the frame border; report the angle, not a referent object.
entries.notes: What is being pointed AT requires a scene object detector we do not have; a pointing ray toward camera degenerates to a dot.

entries.label: Stop / palm-out
entries.description: Flat hand held vertically with the palm facing away from the body toward camera or another actor.
entries.frame_evidence: Extended fingers pointing image-up with the palm plane roughly perpendicular to the view direction.
entries.detector_note: Finger extension high, hand major axis within 30 degrees of vertical, and the palm plane roughly frontal (hand bbox aspect near the fully-open reference rather than edge-on).
entries.notes: Cannot distinguish palm-toward-camera from back-of-hand-toward-camera without reliable handedness, which is itself shaky.

entries.label: Thumbs up
entries.description: Fist with the thumb extended upward.
entries.frame_evidence: All four fingers flexed into the palm with the thumb extended roughly opposite image-down.
entries.detector_note: Four-finger flexion ratio < 0.6, thumb IP angle > 160 degrees, and the thumb vector (2->4) within 40 degrees of image-up.
entries.notes: Camera roll rotates image-up; if a horizon or gravity estimate exists, use it instead.

entries.label: Waving
entries.description: An open hand oscillates laterally, typically above waist height.
entries.frame_evidence: Open hand with 2-6 lateral direction reversals over a short window with the elbow relatively fixed.
entries.detector_note: FFT of the wrist x-position (camera-compensated) over unique cels showing a dominant 1.5-4 Hz component with amplitude above 0.15 shoulder-widths, while all fingers are extended.
entries.notes: Requires enough unique cels: a 2 Hz wave at 8 drawings per second is only 4 samples per cycle and aliases badly.

entries.label: Adducted-thumb grip
entries.description: Object held between fingers and palm with the thumb tucked in rather than opposing, as when carrying a folder under a flat hand.
entries.frame_evidence: Thumb lying flat against the index metacarpal with no visible thumb-index web opening.
entries.detector_note: Thumb tip 4 within 0.25 palm-widths of index MCP 5 AND thumb CMC-MCP-IP nearly collinear (angle > 165 deg).
entries.notes: Common false positive: any fist seen from the ulnar side hides the thumb entirely.

entries.label: Grasp aperture (thumb-index distance)
entries.description: The continuous scalar distance between thumb tip and index tip normalised by hand size, the base signal for every open/close event.
entries.frame_evidence: Pixel gap between the thumb tip and index tip in the frame, divided by the wrist-to-middle-MCP distance.
entries.detector_note: ||landmark4-landmark8|| / ||landmark0-landmark9||, smoothed with scipy.signal.savgol_filter(window=5, poly=2) over unique-cel indices.
entries.notes: Aperture is a projection: rotating the hand shrinks it with no finger motion at all. Report aperture together with the hand bbox aspect ratio so a projection collapse can be recognised.

entries.label: Grasp closure event
entries.description: The instant the fingers close onto an object, aperture falling and then holding flat.
entries.frame_evidence: A monotone fall in aperture across 2-5 unique cels terminating in a plateau, with the hand centroid decelerating at the same time.
entries.detector_note: Negative-going zero crossing of d(aperture_norm)/dt followed by |d/dt| < 0.02 for 3 unique cels; require hand centroid speed to drop below 25 percent of its reach peak in the same window.
entries.notes: On 2s/3s animation the closure can occupy a single unique cel, giving a rate that is a differencing artefact; report closure_rate only when at least 3 unique cels span the event.

entries.label: Hook grip
entries.description: Fingers flexed into a hook to carry a handle or bag with the thumb not opposing.
entries.frame_evidence: Four fingers flexed in parallel with the thumb extended or idle, the load hanging below the fingers.
entries.detector_note: Four-finger flexion ratio < 0.7 while thumb tip 4 to index MCP 5 distance stays above 0.6 hand-widths (thumb NOT opposing), and the wrist-to-hand vector points downward in image space.
entries.notes: Gravity direction is assumed to be image-down; canted or rotating camera invalidates the load-hangs-below cue.

entries.label: Intrinsic-plus / lumbrical grip
entries.description: MCP joints flexed with the interphalangeal joints straight, the grip used to hold a plate or a stack of books against the palm heel.
entries.frame_evidence: Fingers bent sharply at the knuckle line but straight beyond it, forming an L profile in side view.
entries.detector_note: MCP angle (landmarks 0-5-6) below 120 deg while PIP angle (5-6-7) and DIP angle (6-7-8) both above 160 deg, for at least three fingers.
entries.notes: Needs a near-profile view of the hand; from the front the angles are unresolvable.

entries.label: Lateral (key) pinch
entries.description: Thumb pad presses a flat object against the radial side of the flexed index finger, as when turning a key or holding a card.
entries.frame_evidence: Thumb lying across the side of the index middle phalanx with a thin flat object sandwiched between them.
entries.detector_note: Thumb tip 4 closest to index PIP/MCP segment (6-5) rather than to index tip 8, perpendicular distance < 0.18 palm-widths, index flexed but not fully closed.
entries.notes: Reliably confusable with pad pinch at low resolution; needs a hand at least about 60px wide.

entries.label: Object slips within the grip
entries.description: The held object translates or rotates relative to the hand while still being held.
entries.frame_evidence: The object ROI drifts by several pixels against the fingertip landmarks across consecutive unique cels without a release.
entries.detector_note: Track the object ROI with cv2.calcOpticalFlowPyrLK on cv2.goodFeaturesToTrack seeds, express the mean displacement in the hand frame (origin landmark 0, axes from 0->9 and 5->17), and threshold the residual against the shot noise floor from a static background ROI.
entries.notes: Needs the static-background null or camera motion is read as slip; and on 2D cels a redrawn hand shifts the frame origin, producing slip that is a drawing difference, not a physical one.

entries.label: Open-palm platform carry
entries.description: An object rests on a flat open hand with no finger closure, as with a tray, plate or offered item.
entries.frame_evidence: Flat extended fingers, palm facing up, object silhouette sitting on top of the palm outline.
entries.detector_note: All finger flexion ratios > 0.9 (extended), palm normal (from landmarks 0,5,17 cross product) pointing toward image-up, and the hand plane roughly horizontal in image space.
entries.notes: Palm normal from a 2.5D landmark set is noisy; a flat hand held vertically (a stop gesture) can score up depending on camera roll.

entries.label: Power grasp, cylindrical
entries.description: All four fingers wrap a shaft or handle with the thumb closing over or alongside them, the whole palm loading the object.
entries.frame_evidence: Fingertips curled toward the palm centre with a shaft-shaped object crossing the palm and emerging on both sides of the fist.
entries.detector_note: All four fingertip-to-wrist distances (landmarks 8,12,16,20 to 0) below 0.62 of their fully-extended reference, MCP-PIP-DIP flexion consistent across fingers, and thumb tip 4 within 0.35 hand-widths of index PIP 6.
entries.notes: A closed empty fist scores identically; requires an object crossing the palm (see tool_axis_through_grip) to separate grasp from fist.

entries.label: Power grasp, spherical
entries.description: Fingers splayed and curved around a ball-like object, thumb abducted, contact spread across the finger pads.
entries.frame_evidence: Fingertips at roughly equal radius from a common centre outside the palm, with visible inter-finger spread rather than a tight fist.
entries.detector_note: Fit a circle to fingertips 4,8,12,16,20 (scipy.optimize.least_squares); flag when fit residual < 0.12 hand-widths, radius between 0.35 and 0.9 hand-widths, and adjacent-fingertip spacing above the closed-fist reference.
entries.notes: An open cupped hand with nothing in it fits the same circle; needs an object mask or a VLM cross-check to be a grasp.

entries.label: Precision pinch, pad to pad
entries.description: Thumb pad opposes the index pad to hold a small object, the classic two-jaw precision grip.
entries.frame_evidence: Thumb tip and index tip nearly touching with the remaining fingers curled clear, a small object bridging the gap.
entries.detector_note: ||landmark4 - landmark8|| normalised by palm width below 0.22, middle/ring/pinky tips flexed away, and the thumb-index contact point at least 0.5 palm-widths from the palm centroid.
entries.notes: The same geometry appears in the OK gesture and in an empty pinch; object presence is a separate entry.

entries.label: Aperture preshaping before contact
entries.description: The hand opens to a size proportional to the target object before contact, the signature of a planned rather than pasted-on grasp.
entries.frame_evidence: Aperture rises to a peak during the reach and then closes onto the object, the peak scaling with object width.
entries.detector_note: Requires object width from a detector we do not have (no ultralytics/YOLO installed); the aperture half is landmark-derived but the scaling test needs the object bbox to correlate against.
entries.notes: Logged as a known blind spot. This is the single best cue that a CG grasp was hand-animated rather than snapped, so its absence matters.

entries.label: Regrasp / grip adjustment
entries.description: The hand partly reopens and recloses on an object it never let go of.
entries.frame_evidence: A shallow aperture bump that does not reach the free-hand open value, while the object stays coupled to the hand throughout.
entries.detector_note: Detect aperture local maxima with scipy.signal.find_peaks(prominence=0.05) that stay below 0.6 of the shot aperture_max, while object-hand coupling remains above 0.7.
entries.notes: A useful realism signal: CG shots often show zero regrasps across long carries, which is itself a finding.

entries.label: Grasp release event
entries.description: The fingers open and the object stops moving with the hand.
entries.frame_evidence: Aperture rises from a plateau while the held-object ROI stops tracking the wrist translation.
entries.detector_note: Positive d(aperture_norm)/dt above 0.03 per unique cel, coincident with the object-follows-hand correlation dropping below its shot median minus 2 MADs (see hand_object.object_follows_hand_coupling).
entries.notes: An open hand that simply rotates away produces the aperture rise without a real release; the coupling term is what makes this meaningful.

entries.label: Tip pinch
entries.description: Very tip of thumb and index oppose to pick up a needle, thread or crumb.
entries.frame_evidence: Only the distal fingertip points meet, with a visible gap between the finger pads behind them.
entries.detector_note: Crop 3x the thumb-index bbox and ask a VLM; the landmark tier cannot resolve tip-versus-pad contact at typical fingertip pixel sizes.
entries.vlm_question: Are the very tips of the thumb and finger touching each other, rather than the flat pads? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: THE CROP RULE applies hard here: on a full frame this is invisible to any VLM.

entries.label: Tripod / three-jaw chuck grip
entries.description: Thumb, index and middle finger converge on one object, the grip used for pens, chopsticks and small tools.
entries.frame_evidence: Three fingertips converging within a small disc while ring and little fingers are curled out of the way.
entries.detector_note: Circumradius of the triangle formed by landmarks 4, 8, 12 below 0.3 palm-widths, ring 16 and pinky 20 flexion ratio below 0.75.
entries.notes: Foreshortening on a hand pointed at camera collapses the triangle and produces false positives; gate on hand_bbox aspect near 1.

entries.label: Grasp type changes within a shot
entries.description: The classified grasp switches category (for example power to precision) while the same object is held.
entries.frame_evidence: The dominant grasp label over a sliding window changes while the coupled object ROI persists.
entries.detector_note: Majority-vote grasp label over a 5-unique-cel window; report a transition when the label is stable for 3 cels either side of the switch.
entries.notes: Label churn from tracker noise dominates unless the stability gate is enforced on both sides of the transition.

entries.label: Grip force / effort
entries.description: How hard the hand is squeezing the object.
entries.frame_evidence: Would require fingertip pad flattening, nail-bed blanching and tendon prominence at a resolution we almost never have.
entries.detector_note: No available detector; the visual correlates need macro-scale skin detail and are absent by construction in 2D and in most CG skin shaders.
entries.notes: Logged deliberately as a blind spot so nobody reads a grasp label as an effort measurement.

entries.label: Hammering
entries.description: A weighted tool is swung down onto a target and rebounds, usually repeatedly.
entries.frame_evidence: Repeated arcs of the tool tip terminating in an abrupt reversal at the same screen location.
entries.detector_note: Combine tool_swing_arc and tool_impact_frame; hammering when 2+ impacts occur within 1.5 hand-widths of the same point with a regular inter-impact interval.
entries.notes: Anime replaces the descent with 1-2 smear drawings, so strike_speed_peak is a differencing artefact; report strike_count only.

entries.label: Hand animated on a different cadence than the body
entries.description: The hand updates on a different number of frames than the face or body, a common limited-animation economy.
entries.frame_evidence: Hand ROI change events occurring on a different frame lattice than face ROI change events.
entries.detector_note: Compare the change-event index sets of the hand ROI and the face ROI over the shot; report the fraction of frames where one changed and the other did not.
entries.notes: Camera pans make every ROI change every frame and destroy the test; restrict to locked-off or compensated shots.

entries.label: Number of visible hands
entries.description: How many distinct hands are visible, which bounds every bimanual entry downstream.
entries.frame_evidence: Two or more separated hand landmark clusters, or two wrist landmarks whose hand regions do not overlap.
entries.detector_note: Count HandLandmarker results after NMS on palm bboxes (IoU>0.5 merged); cross-check against PoseLandmarker wrists 15/16 present in frame bounds.
entries.notes: Crowd shots and mirrors inflate the count; hands of different people are not separated by this entry.

entries.label: Hand held-cel duration
entries.description: How many display frames a single hand drawing is held for, the 1s/2s/3s cadence of the hand itself.
entries.frame_evidence: Byte-identical or near-identical hand ROI across consecutive frames.
entries.detector_note: Per-frame mean absolute difference of the hand ROI against the previous frame; run-length encode the near-zero runs (threshold from the frame-wide noise floor) and report the modal run length.
entries.notes: This entry is the prerequisite for every temporal entry in this domain: it defines the unique-cel index everything else is computed on.

entries.label: Hand hold stillness
entries.description: How still a supposedly static hand actually is, separating a live hold from a frozen one.
entries.frame_evidence: Near-zero but non-zero wrist displacement across unique cels during a hold.
entries.detector_note: Std of camera-compensated wrist position over a hold window, compared with the static-background null; a real hand holds at a few times the null, a frozen CG or held cel sits at exactly the null.
entries.notes: MUST be on unique cels: a 2s hold gives literally identical pixels between duplicate frames, and that exact zero is a file artefact, not a stillness measurement.

entries.label: Same hand continuity across a cut
entries.description: Whether the hand shown in a cutaway insert belongs to the same character as the wide shot.
entries.frame_evidence: Skin tone, sleeve, jewellery and hand shape matched either side of a cut.
entries.detector_note: Would need a hand re-identification embedding; insightface is not installed and would be the wrong model anyway.
entries.notes: The two histogram metrics are computable deterministically and are worth logging, but they are far from an identity decision and must not be reported as one.

entries.label: Hand mesh self-intersection
entries.description: Fingers pass through each other or through the palm.
entries.frame_evidence: A finger silhouette crossing another finger with no shading break, or a fingertip visible inside the palm mass.
entries.detector_note: Crop the hand at 3x and ask a VLM; there is no deterministic route without a depth or normal pass from the render.
entries.vlm_question: Do any of the fingers pass through or into another finger or the palm? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: If an AOV depth or normal pass is available this becomes trivially deterministic, but from a delivered picture it is not.

entries.label: Hand motion blur / streak
entries.description: The hand region is blurred or streaked by fast motion, degrading every fine-motor measurement in that frame.
entries.frame_evidence: Hand ROI is markedly lower in high-frequency energy than the face ROI in the same frame, with a directional gradient histogram peak.
entries.detector_note: cv2.Laplacian(hand_roi, cv2.CV_64F).var() compared with the face-ROI variance in the same frame; directionality from the angular histogram of cv2.Sobel gradients (blur axis = the minimum-energy direction).
entries.notes: Shallow depth of field defocuses a hand that is not moving at all; the face-ratio null does not separate defocus from motion blur, only from a globally soft image.

entries.label: Hand/object depth order flips
entries.description: The object is drawn in front of the fingers in one cel and behind them in the next, without any rotation to justify it.
entries.frame_evidence: Finger contours occluding the object edge in cel n and being occluded by it in cel n+1.
entries.detector_note: Crop the grip region on two consecutive unique cels and ask about occlusion order on each, then compare answers.
entries.vlm_question: In this image, is the object in front of the fingers or behind them? Answer in front or behind.
entries.notes: Very common 2D cel-paint error and worth catching, but a small VLM answers this near chance on ambiguous flat art; require agreement across two crops per cel.

entries.label: Hand occluded by body or object
entries.description: An arm is visible but its hand is hidden behind the torso, another actor, or a prop.
entries.frame_evidence: Forearm silhouette terminates at an occluding edge rather than at a hand, with the wrist landmark predicted but low-visibility.
entries.detector_note: PoseLandmarker elbow 13/14 visibility>0.7 while wrist 15/16 visibility<0.4, AND HandLandmarker returns no hand within the extrapolated forearm ray.
entries.notes: Indistinguishable from a hand that is simply out of frame; pair with hand_out_of_frame before concluding occlusion.

entries.label: Hand off-model in proportion
entries.description: The hand is drawn or rigged noticeably too large, too small or with wrong finger proportions for the character.
entries.frame_evidence: Hand-to-shoulder ratio or finger-to-palm ratio departing from the character established value in the same production.
entries.detector_note: Build a per-character distribution of hand_to_shoulder_ratio over the episode, then flag frames beyond 3 MADs; requires a character identity grouping supplied externally.
entries.notes: Needs a per-character null distribution to mean anything at all; without it the threshold is invented and the numbers are noise.

entries.label: Handing an object to another person
entries.description: An object transfers from one person hand to another, with a brief interval where both hold it.
entries.frame_evidence: Two hands from different people converging on one object, a shared-hold window, then the object following the receiving hand.
entries.detector_note: Candidate when two wrists from different pose skeletons come within 1.5 hand-widths and object coupling switches from one wrist to the other; confirm on a crop of both hands.
entries.vlm_question: Is one person passing an object into another person hand? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Multi-person pose association is fragile in crowded frames; the coupling switch is the real evidence and it needs an object ROI seed.

entries.label: Hand crosses the frame border
entries.description: The hand leaves or enters the visible frame, truncating any manipulation evidence.
entries.frame_evidence: Hand bbox clipped by an image edge, or the forearm axis exiting the frame with no hand region inside it.
entries.detector_note: Test hand bbox intersection with a 2px border band; also extrapolate the pose forearm vector (13->15) and check whether the projected wrist falls outside image bounds.
entries.notes: This entry exists mainly to explain NOT-FOUND results for other hand entries in the same shot.

entries.label: Hand present in frame
entries.description: At least one human hand is visible somewhere in the frame.
entries.frame_evidence: A hand-shaped skin/glove region with a wrist joining a forearm, or a mediapipe hand landmark set returned with confidence above threshold.
entries.detector_note: mediapipe.tasks.python.vision.HandLandmarker (num_hands=4, min_hand_detection_confidence=0.3) per frame; fall back to PoseLandmarker wrist landmarks 15/16 with visibility>0.5 when HandLandmarker returns nothing.
entries.notes: HandLandmarker is trained on photographic hands; on 2D anime cels detection rate typically collapses below 0.2 even when a hand is clearly drawn. Always log hand_det_rate for the shot so a FOUND/NOT-FOUND verdict can be discounted.

entries.label: Hand size relative to body
entries.description: Apparent hand size normalised by shoulder width, used both as a perspective cue and as an off-model check.
entries.frame_evidence: Hand bbox diagonal measured against the shoulder-to-shoulder pixel distance in the same frame.
entries.detector_note: hand_bbox_diag / ||pose[11]-pose[12]||; expected human ratio approx 0.28-0.42 for a hand at torso depth.
entries.notes: A hand reaching toward camera legitimately breaks the ratio; only flag when the wrist depth ordering says the hand is near the torso plane.

entries.label: Hand silhouette flickers between cels
entries.description: The drawn hand shape changes more between adjacent cels than the motion justifies, the classic off-model wobble.
entries.frame_evidence: Large silhouette dissimilarity between consecutive unique cels despite a small hand centroid displacement.
entries.detector_note: Align consecutive hand ROIs by their centroids, then compare shapes with cv2.matchShapes (Hu moments) or IoU of thresholded masks; flag high dissimilarity paired with sub-half-hand-width centroid motion.
entries.notes: Fast rotation legitimately changes the silhouette without moving the centroid; treat as a candidate generator for a VLM look, not a verdict.

entries.label: Hand smear / multiple drawing
entries.description: A single drawing in which the hand is elongated, ghosted or drawn several times to imply speed.
entries.frame_evidence: The hand region in one cel is far more elongated or has far more repeated parallel edges than in the cels either side.
entries.detector_note: Per unique cel, hand-ROI elongation from PCA eigenvalue ratio plus parallel-edge count from the Hough angle histogram peak sharpness; a smear is a single-cel outlier above 2.5 MADs of the shot.
entries.notes: Motion blur in live action produces elongation too, which is why this entry is scoped to 2D; the parallel-edge count is what distinguishes a drawn multiple from a blur.

entries.label: Object transferred between own hands
entries.description: An object moves from one of the actor hands to the other.
entries.frame_evidence: The object coupling switches from one wrist to the other with a brief overlap where both hands touch it.
entries.detector_note: Compute per-hand coupling with the object ROI; a transfer is a crossing of the two coupling curves with both above 0.5 for at least one unique cel.
entries.notes: Needs an object ROI seed and both hands tracked; at the crossover the object is usually maximally occluded, which is exactly where the ROI tracker fails.

entries.label: Hand travels to the mouth
entries.description: The generic hand-to-mouth trajectory underlying smoking, drinking, eating and nail-biting.
entries.frame_evidence: Wrist landmark approaching the mouth landmark until their separation reaches a local minimum, then retreating.
entries.detector_note: Distance between pose wrist 15/16 and mouth landmarks (pose 9/10 midpoint, or FaceLandmarker upper-lip vertex) normalised by head width; find local minima below 0.6 head-widths with scipy.signal.find_peaks on the negated signal.
entries.notes: Does not identify what is in the hand; pair with the cigarette/cup/food entries. Head turn changes the projected distance without any hand motion.

entries.label: Hand landmark dropout run
entries.description: A run of consecutive unique cels in which the hand tracker loses a hand that is still visually present.
entries.frame_evidence: Landmark set absent for k consecutive unique cels while the hand region remains present by frame-difference and by pose wrist visibility.
entries.detector_note: Run-length encode HandLandmarker misses over unique-cel indices while pose wrist visibility>0.6; report the longest run and the duty cycle.
entries.notes: Compute on unique-cel indices only; on 2s/3s animation a per-frame dropout rate is inflated by duplicate frames that the tracker also fails on.

entries.label: Hand tremor / micro-jitter
entries.description: Small high-frequency hand oscillation, whether performed (nervousness, cold, age) or an animation artefact.
entries.frame_evidence: Wrist position showing low-amplitude energy above about 5 Hz that survives camera compensation.
entries.detector_note: numpy.fft.rfft of the camera-compensated wrist position over unique cels; report energy above 5 Hz relative to total, with a null taken from a static background point tracked the same way.
entries.notes: Landmark jitter is itself high-frequency, which is precisely why the static-point null is required; without it every hand tremors.

entries.label: Left vs right hand
entries.description: Which anatomical hand a detected hand region is.
entries.frame_evidence: Thumb lies on the anatomically left or right side of the palm given the palm normal implied by landmark ordering.
entries.detector_note: HandLandmarkerResult.handedness category_name plus score; sanity-check by cross product of (landmark 5 - landmark 0) x (landmark 17 - landmark 0) z-sign against the reported label.
entries.notes: Handedness flips frame to frame on palm-edge-on views; a flip count is often a tracker artefact, not a re-posed hand.

entries.label: Held object changes identity across a cut
entries.description: The object in hand before and after a cut is not the same object, a continuity break.
entries.frame_evidence: Two grip crops either side of a cut showing different colour, shape or type of object.
entries.detector_note: Take the last pre-cut and first post-cut grip crops (2x hand bbox), stack them side by side, and ask a VLM the closed question below.
entries.vlm_question: Are the two objects being held in the left and right halves of this image the same kind of object with the same colour? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Do not ask moondream for any labels or text on the object; keep the question purely about sameness.

entries.label: Occlusion of the held object by the hand
entries.description: How much of the object the hand covers, which bounds what any downstream object-level entry can see.
entries.frame_evidence: The proportion of the object silhouette hidden behind fingers and palm.
entries.detector_note: Needs instance segmentation of both hand and object (no ultralytics/YOLO, no SAM installed); the hand hull from landmarks gives only a crude numerator and no object mask at all.
entries.notes: Reported as a blind spot on purpose: several manipulation entries are unreadable precisely when this fraction is high, and we cannot currently measure when that is.

entries.label: Held object appears or vanishes
entries.description: The manipulated object exists in one unique cel and is gone in the next with no motion to explain it.
entries.frame_evidence: A structured region in the grip area present in cel n and replaced by background in cel n+1 without any occluder crossing.
entries.detector_note: Template-match the grip ROI (cv2.matchTemplate, TM_CCOEFF_NORMED) from cel n into a 2x search window in cel n+1; flag when the best score falls below 0.45 while the hand landmarks remain tracked with the same pose.
entries.notes: Compute across UNIQUE cels only. Also fires on a lighting change or a hard cut; gate on shot boundaries from a histogram-difference cut detector.

entries.label: Held object changes size
entries.description: The object grows or shrinks relative to the hand across a shot with no camera move to justify it.
entries.frame_evidence: Object bbox diagonal divided by hand bbox diagonal trending across the shot.
entries.detector_note: Track the object ROI scale with cv2.TrackerCSRT or by ECC alignment (cv2.findTransformECC, MOTION_EUCLIDEAN with a scale term) and regress the object/hand size ratio over unique cels.
entries.notes: Perspective change during transport legitimately alters the ratio; only a monotone drift with a static camera is evidence.

entries.label: Turning a knob or dial
entries.description: A pinch or palmar grip rotates a small round control in place.
entries.frame_evidence: Hand centroid fixed on a small circular feature while the hand-local axis rotates.
entries.detector_note: Same rotation test as door_handle_grasp_turn but with a small hand-object footprint (grip region under 1 hand-width) and rotation typically under 90 degrees.
entries.notes: Indistinguishable from a key turn or a lid start without a VLM naming the object.

entries.label: Lift-off
entries.description: The object leaves its support and begins to travel with the hand.
entries.frame_evidence: The object ROI starts translating in step with the wrist while its previous contact edge with the support opens into a gap.
entries.detector_note: Cross-correlate object-ROI optical flow (cv2.calcOpticalFlowFarneback, pyr_scale=0.5, levels=3, winsize=15) with wrist displacement over a 5-unique-cel window; lift-off at the first cel where correlation exceeds 0.7 after being below 0.2.
entries.notes: Object ROI must be seeded (by a VLM crop question or manual hint) because no object detector is installed; without a seed this entry degrades to model tier.

entries.label: Lighter flick / thumb roll
entries.description: The thumb rolls down a lighter wheel or presses its lever, usually once or twice.
entries.frame_evidence: An isolated thumb-tip arc across the top of a small held object with the other fingers static.
entries.detector_note: Thumb tip 4 displacement in the hand-local frame above 0.2 hand-widths across 1-2 unique cels while fingertips 8/12/16/20 move less than 0.05; optionally followed by a flame appearance.
entries.notes: Needs a hand at least 80px wide plus good landmarks, so effectively a live-action or photoreal-CG entry only.

entries.label: Liquid stream between vessels
entries.description: A visible falling stream connecting the pouring vessel to its target.
entries.frame_evidence: A thin, near-vertical, temporally-persistent high-gradient ribbon running from the vessel lip downward.
entries.detector_note: In the region below the vessel lip, look for a connected component with width under 3 percent of frame width, height over 4x its width, near-vertical PCA axis, persisting 3+ unique cels; verify downward flow with Farneback inside it.
entries.notes: Clear liquid on a busy background is nearly invisible to gradient methods; and in 2D the stream is a drawn shape whose internal flow is zero, so the flow check must be dropped for animation.

entries.label: Load phase pause before lift
entries.description: A short dwell where the hand is on the object but nothing has moved yet, the moment weight is taken up.
entries.frame_evidence: Two or more unique cels in which both hand and object are near-static, between contact onset and lift-off.
entries.detector_note: Count unique cels between the contact frame and lift-off where both wrist speed and object ROI displacement are below 0.02 shoulder-widths.
entries.notes: Absence of a load phase on a heavy-looking object is a weight-reading finding; it is also simply what happens when a shot is cut tight.

entries.label: Purpose of the manipulation
entries.description: Why the hand is doing what it is doing, as opposed to what it is doing.
entries.frame_evidence: Nothing in a frame or short window carries intent; it is inferred from narrative context spanning shots.
entries.detector_note: Out of scope for a frame-by-frame analyzer; a VLM asked this question will confabulate a plausible story with high confidence.
entries.notes: Explicitly logged as unsupported so the taxonomy cannot be read as supporting intent claims.

entries.label: Match ignition flare
entries.description: The sudden bright bloom when a match catches.
entries.frame_evidence: A small region near the fingertips jumping several stops in luminance within one unique cel, with a warm hue shift.
entries.detector_note: Per unique-cel pair, find connected components where V (from cv2.cvtColor to HSV) rises by more than 60 levels and hue falls in 10-45 deg; require the component centroid within 1.5 hand-widths of a fingertip landmark and area under 2 percent of frame.
entries.notes: Muzzle flashes, sparks, camera flashes and cuts to a brighter shot all trip this; the hand-proximity gate is doing most of the work.

entries.label: Striking a match
entries.description: A rapid short linear drag of a small object across a striking surface.
entries.frame_evidence: Small object translating fast along a straight path over 1-3 unique cels, immediately followed by a luminance flare at its tip.
entries.detector_note: Detect a short high-speed linear tip trajectory (tool_tip_trajectory) whose end coincides within 2 unique cels with hand_object.match_ignition_flare.
entries.notes: Without the flare this is indistinguishable from any quick small-object move; the two must co-occur.

entries.label: Mitten hand (fingers not drawn)
entries.description: A stylistic or economy choice where the hand is a rounded mass with no individuated fingers.
entries.frame_evidence: A hand-sized blob with a smooth convex contour and no internal line work, attached to a wrist.
entries.detector_note: Hand ROI contour solidity (area / convex hull area) above 0.93 with internal edge density from cv2.Canny below the shot median for hand regions, sustained over several unique cels.
entries.notes: A closed fist also has high solidity and low internal detail; require the region to persist as a mitten across many cels including open-hand poses.

entries.label: Object-follows-hand coupling
entries.description: The core primitive: how strongly the object ROI motion matches the hand motion, which is what distinguishes held from merely adjacent.
entries.frame_evidence: Object ROI displacement vectors parallel and proportional to wrist displacement over a short window.
entries.detector_note: Per unique-cel pair compute mean flow in the object ROI and in the hand ROI (Farneback), then coupling = cosine similarity times min(|vo|,|vh|)/max(|vo|,|vh|); build the null from three random background ROIs of the same area in the same frames.
entries.notes: A detector with no null model produces confident numbers that mean nothing: the background-ROI null is mandatory, because a panning camera drives every ROI pair to coupling 1.0.

entries.label: Fingers pass through the object
entries.description: Finger geometry intersects the held object instead of resting on it, the signature CG collision failure.
entries.frame_evidence: A fingertip visibly sunk inside the object surface, or an object edge cutting across a finger mid-length.
entries.detector_note: Crop to the grip region at 2x the hand bbox and ask a VLM; occurs at a scale a full-frame question cannot resolve.
entries.vlm_question: Does any finger sink into or pass through the surface of the object it is holding? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Small VLMs over-report this on any tight grip; treat single-frame yes as weak and require 2 of 3 sampled unique cels.

entries.label: Weight or material of the held object
entries.description: How heavy or what material the manipulated object is.
entries.frame_evidence: Only indirectly present through arm posture, load-phase duration and transport speed, none of which identify weight on their own.
entries.detector_note: No installed detector estimates mass or material from a picture; the kinematic correlates (load phase, deceleration) are logged separately and must not be relabelled as weight.
entries.notes: A VLM will confidently name a material; that is a guess from appearance priors, not a measurement, and is excluded here on purpose.

entries.label: Held object shadow tracks the object
entries.description: The cast shadow of a manipulated object follows it, a compositing-integrity check.
entries.frame_evidence: A dark region on the support surface translating in step with the object, with a consistent offset.
entries.detector_note: Track the shadow blob (low-luminance, low-saturation region near the object) and correlate its displacement with the object displacement; report the offset stability.
entries.notes: Fails entirely in soft or flat lighting, and a missing shadow is the most common CG comp error precisely because it is easy to overlook.

entries.label: Turning a book page
entries.description: A hand lifts and sweeps a page over, momentarily revealing a curved sheet.
entries.frame_evidence: A large curved-edge region sweeping across a bright rectangular field while the hand travels along its free edge.
entries.detector_note: Use hand_object.page_turn_wipe as the cheap candidate generator, then confirm on a 2x book-region crop with a VLM.
entries.vlm_question: Is the person turning a page of a book? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Turning a page, closing a book and sliding a sheet of paper all look alike to the deterministic stage; the VLM disambiguates but only on a tight crop.

entries.label: Page-turn wipe pattern
entries.description: The distinctive moving curved boundary a turning page sweeps across the spread.
entries.frame_evidence: A high-gradient arc translating laterally across a bright quadrilateral over 2-6 unique cels, with the region behind it changing content.
entries.detector_note: Inside the detected bright quad, track the strongest cv2.Canny contour by its centroid x per unique cel; require monotone lateral travel of more than 25 percent of the quad width plus a rise in mean absolute difference behind the boundary.
entries.notes: Any wiping motion across a bright rectangle (a hand, a cloth, a shadow) reproduces the pattern.

entries.label: Plugging something in
entries.description: A held connector is aligned to a receptacle and pushed in along its own axis.
entries.frame_evidence: A small held object approaching a fixed point along its own long axis, then a short insertion travel and a stop.
entries.detector_note: Candidate from tool axis aligned with the tip velocity vector within 15 degrees plus an abrupt stop, then confirm with a VLM crop.
entries.vlm_question: Is a plug or connector being pushed into a socket in this image? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: The final insertion is nearly always occluded by the hand, so the evidence is the approach, not the seating.

entries.label: Tilting a vessel to pour
entries.description: A held container rotates past horizontal so its contents can leave.
entries.frame_evidence: The held object major axis rotating progressively, usually 40-120 degrees, while the hand keeps a stable grip.
entries.detector_note: tool_long_axis angle change over unique cels while the grasp is stable (aperture flat); require monotone rotation exceeding 30 degrees with the object still coupled to the hand.
entries.notes: A rotationally symmetric vessel gives a weak axis; and a bottle rotating away from camera shows little in-plane rotation.

entries.label: Hand-over-hand pulling
entries.description: Alternating grips on a rope or line drawn toward the body.
entries.frame_evidence: Two hands alternating between grip and release along a common linear structure, each releasing as the other closes.
entries.detector_note: Anti-phase aperture signals for the two hands (correlation below -0.5 over 8+ unique cels) with both hands lying near a common fitted line.
entries.notes: Needs both hands tracked simultaneously, which mediapipe manages in live action and rarely in animation.

entries.label: Pushing an object along a surface
entries.description: A hand shoves an object which slides rather than being lifted.
entries.frame_evidence: Object translating in the hand direction while staying in contact with a horizontal support line and never rising off it.
entries.detector_note: High coupling with the object trajectory constrained to a line, and the object-to-support gap (distance from the object lower contour to the fitted support edge) staying under 2px throughout.
entries.notes: Requires a visible support edge to fit; on a cluttered table the edge fit fails.

entries.label: Ballistic reach peak velocity
entries.description: The single fastest part of a reach, normally around 40-50 percent of the way to the target in natural motion.
entries.frame_evidence: A pronounced single maximum in the wrist speed profile between rest and contact.
entries.detector_note: scipy.signal.find_peaks on the camera-compensated wrist speed profile over unique cels; report peak value and its normalised time within the reach interval.
entries.notes: Human reaches are bell-shaped with time_to_peak_frac around 0.4; linear CG interpolation gives a flat profile and a skew near zero, which is exactly the finding worth logging.

entries.label: Corrective submovement
entries.description: A secondary velocity bump near the target as the hand corrects its aim.
entries.frame_evidence: A small second peak in the wrist speed profile inside the final third of the reach.
entries.detector_note: find_peaks with prominence >= 0.15 of the primary peak, restricted to the last 35 percent of the reach interval on unique cels.
entries.notes: Requires at least about 8 unique cels in the reach; on 3s animation a 0.4s reach has only 3 samples and this entry must report NOT DETECTABLE rather than zero.

entries.label: Reach deceleration before contact
entries.description: The slowdown as the hand homes in on the object, longer than the acceleration phase in real motion.
entries.frame_evidence: Wrist speed falling steadily over several unique cels immediately before the contact frame.
entries.detector_note: Integrate the falling limb of the speed profile; compute decel_accel_ratio = duration_after_peak / duration_before_peak over unique cels.
entries.notes: A ratio near or below 1.0 with a hard stop at contact is the classic snap-to-target CG signature.

entries.label: Reach onset
entries.description: The frame at which the hand starts moving toward a target after being at rest.
entries.frame_evidence: Wrist speed rises from near zero past a threshold and keeps rising for several unique cels.
entries.detector_note: Wrist landmark 15/16 speed in shoulder-widths per unique cel; onset when speed crosses 0.05 and stays above it for 3 consecutive unique cels; camera motion removed first by subtracting the global affine from cv2.estimateAffinePartial2D on background features.
entries.notes: MUST run on unique-cel indices: on an animation held for 3 frames the per-frame speed is zero twice out of three and onset is reported late or twice.

entries.label: Reach path curvature
entries.description: How much the hand path bows away from a straight line between start and target.
entries.frame_evidence: The traced wrist trajectory across the reach, compared with the chord joining its endpoints.
entries.detector_note: Max perpendicular deviation of the wrist polyline from its endpoint chord, normalised by chord length; computed on unique-cel wrist positions after camera compensation.
entries.notes: Perfectly straight paths (curvature < 0.02) are a strong CG-interpolation tell but also occur in a genuinely constrained reach along a surface.

entries.label: Swiping a touchscreen
entries.description: A fingertip slides across the screen surface while maintaining contact.
entries.frame_evidence: Fingertip translating steadily within the screen quadrilateral over 3+ unique cels, with screen content shifting in the same direction.
entries.detector_note: Fingertip path constrained inside the screen quad with near-constant speed; cross-check with mean optical flow inside the screen region being parallel to the fingertip motion.
entries.notes: The screen-flow cross-check is the only thing separating a swipe from a finger passing in front of a screen.

entries.label: Tapping a touchscreen
entries.description: A fingertip contacts a bright flat rectangular surface briefly and lifts.
entries.frame_evidence: Fingertip touching a bright rectangle, dwell of 1-3 unique cels, then retreat, often with a UI change under the finger.
entries.detector_note: Extended-index tip trajectory with a dwell minimum inside a bright quadrilateral found by cv2.findContours on an adaptive threshold with 4-vertex cv2.approxPolyDP; optionally require a pixel change in the screen region within 2 cels of the dwell.
entries.notes: Screens in shot are usually blown out or replaced in post; the UI-change confirmation fails on composited screen inserts. Do not attempt to read what is on the screen with moondream.

entries.label: Screwing / unscrewing
entries.description: Repeated axial rotation of a tool or lid about an axis pointing away from the hand.
entries.frame_evidence: Cyclic wrist rotation with the hand centroid fixed, alternating between a driving turn and a return.
entries.detector_note: Hand-local axis angle (landmark 5->17) oscillating with an asymmetric sawtooth over unique cels while the centroid is static; count cycles with find_peaks.
entries.notes: Cannot determine tightening versus loosening: the in-plane sense of rotation depends on which way the fastener faces the camera.

entries.label: Setting an object down
entries.description: A carried object is lowered onto a surface and released.
entries.frame_evidence: Downward transport, contact with a surface, coupling drop, then the hand rising away while the object stays.
entries.detector_note: Object ROI vertical velocity going to zero on a horizontal edge, coupling falling below the null band, and the wrist continuing to move for 2+ unique cels while the object stays static.
entries.notes: The object must remain visible after release; if the hand withdraws across it the ROI is lost and this reports nothing.

entries.label: Exhaled smoke plume
entries.description: A low-contrast expanding cloud emerging from the mouth after a drag.
entries.frame_evidence: A region in front of the face whose local contrast falls and whose area grows monotonically over several unique cels.
entries.detector_note: In a mouth-anchored ROI, track mean local std (cv2.blur of squared deviation) and the area above a soft-threshold; require monotone area growth over 4+ unique cels and a drop in ROI edge density from cv2.Canny.
entries.notes: Steam, breath in cold air, fog and lens flare all match; and in 2D smoke is drawn as hard-edged shapes that raise rather than lower edge density, inverting the test.

entries.label: Stirring
entries.description: A held implement is moved in repeated loops inside a container.
entries.frame_evidence: The hand or tool tip tracing a closed loop repeatedly over 6+ unique cels with a stable wrist position.
entries.detector_note: Unwrap the angle of the tip position about its own trajectory centroid; stirring when the unwrapped angle advances monotonically past 2*pi with radius variance below 25 percent.
entries.notes: Requires enough unique cels to sample a loop: at 8 drawings per second a fast stir aliases into an apparent reversal.

entries.label: Stylised hand defeats the landmark tracker
entries.description: A drawn hand is clearly visible to a human but returns no landmarks, marking the whole landmark tier as not-detectable for that shot.
entries.frame_evidence: A VLM confirms a hand on the crop while HandLandmarker detection rate over the shot is near zero.
entries.detector_note: Sample 5 unique cels where pose says a wrist is present but HandLandmarker failed; crop 2.2x the predicted hand box and ask qwen2.5vl; treat a yes-majority as a landmark-tier blind spot flag for the shot.
entries.vlm_question: Is there a human hand in this image? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: This is the honesty gate for the whole domain on anime: without it, every landmark entry silently reports NOT FOUND instead of NOT DETECTABLE.

entries.label: Flipping a switch
entries.description: A finger or thumb throws a small lever, often with an accompanying lighting change.
entries.frame_evidence: A single fingertip making a short sharp stroke at a wall or panel point, sometimes followed by a global luminance step.
entries.detector_note: Short (1-2 unique cel) fingertip excursion under 0.3 hand-widths at a static hand position, optionally correlated with a global mean-luminance step of more than 8 levels within 3 unique cels.
entries.notes: The luminance step is the strong evidence and it is absent for any switch that does not control the visible light.

entries.label: Throwing an object
entries.description: The hand accelerates, opens, and the object continues on its own ballistic path.
entries.frame_evidence: Peak wrist speed followed within 1-2 unique cels by aperture opening and by the object continuing while the hand decelerates.
entries.detector_note: Wrist speed peak, then aperture rise, then object ROI velocity exceeding hand velocity for 2+ unique cels (coupling goes negative in the magnitude-ratio term).
entries.notes: The thrown object usually leaves frame or blurs to nothing within 2 cels, so the post-release evidence window is very short.

entries.label: Thumb opposition present
entries.description: The thumb is positioned across from the fingers rather than alongside them, the anatomical precondition of most grasps.
entries.frame_evidence: Thumb tip on the palmar side of the plane formed by the finger metacarpals.
entries.detector_note: Sign of dot(landmark4 - landmark0, palm_normal) where palm_normal = cross(landmark5-landmark0, landmark17-landmark0); opposition when the thumb sits palmar by more than 0.1 palm-widths.
entries.notes: Depends on mediapipe relative-z, which is weakly supervised and unreliable when the hand is small in frame.

entries.label: Tool axis jitter
entries.description: Frame-to-frame instability of the tool orientation beyond what the hand motion explains.
entries.frame_evidence: The fitted axis angle oscillating by several degrees between consecutive unique cels while the hand pose is steady.
entries.detector_note: Std of d(tool_axis_deg) across unique cels, minus the std of the hand-axis (landmark 0->9) angle change over the same cels, as the residual jitter.
entries.notes: Line-fitting noise alone is 1-3 degrees at typical resolutions; report the fit residual so the jitter can be judged against it.

entries.label: Tool axis passes through the grip
entries.description: The fitted tool axis actually intersects the hand, which is what separates a held tool from a background line.
entries.frame_evidence: The elongated object crosses the fist silhouette and emerges on both sides, or terminates inside it.
entries.detector_note: Test the perpendicular distance from the hand centroid (landmark 9) to the fitted axis line, normalised by hand width; require < 0.5 and the line segment to overlap the landmark convex hull.
entries.notes: This is the cheap gate that stops tool entries firing on architectural lines behind an actor.

entries.label: Tool impact frame
entries.description: The frame where the swinging tool meets its target and reverses or stops.
entries.frame_evidence: Tip speed maximum immediately followed by a reversal or near-zero, coincident with a local pixel disturbance at the tip.
entries.detector_note: Tip speed sign reversal or drop below 20 percent of peak within one unique cel, AND a spike in mean |frame difference| inside a small disc at the tip location relative to the shot median.
entries.notes: Impact frames are the most likely to be motion-blurred or replaced by a smear cel, so the tip fit may be missing exactly at the event.

entries.label: Tool long axis
entries.description: The dominant orientation of an elongated held object, the primitive for every tool-use entry.
entries.frame_evidence: An elongated bright/dark region extending from the fist, whose principal direction can be fitted.
entries.detector_note: Within a hand-anchored ROI, cv2.Canny then cv2.HoughLinesP (minLineLength = 0.6 * hand width) and take the angle mode; or PCA (numpy.linalg.eigh of the coordinate covariance) on the thresholded object ROI, reporting eigenvalue ratio as elongation.
entries.notes: Background linear structure (table edges, door frames) contaminates the Hough mode; restrict to the ROI attached to the fist and require the line to intersect the hand hull.

entries.label: Tool swing arc
entries.description: A tool swung about the wrist or elbow, describing an arc rather than a translation.
entries.frame_evidence: Tool tip path fitting a circular arc whose centre lies near the wrist or elbow landmark.
entries.detector_note: Least-squares circle fit to the tip trajectory (scipy.optimize.least_squares); require fit residual below 8 percent of radius and the centre within 1.5 forearm lengths of the wrist landmark.
entries.notes: Needs at least 5 unique cels of the swing; a 2-frame anime smear swing is not measurable this way and must be logged NOT DETECTABLE.

entries.label: Tool tip trajectory
entries.description: The path traced by the working end of the tool, which is the thing the action is actually about.
entries.frame_evidence: The far endpoint of the fitted axis segment tracked across unique cels.
entries.detector_note: Take the axis endpoint farther from the hand centroid per cel, smooth with savgol, and report path length, peak speed and curvature; camera-compensated by the background affine.
entries.notes: Tip identity swaps end-for-end when the tool passes through a vertical, producing a spurious jump; enforce temporal continuity on the endpoint choice.

entries.label: Transport phase carrying an object
entries.description: The interval where hand and object move together across the frame.
entries.frame_evidence: A sustained run of unique cels with high hand-object coupling and non-zero hand speed.
entries.detector_note: Run-length of cels with coupling>0.7 and wrist speed>0.03 shoulder-widths per unique cel; report duration and mean speed.
entries.notes: Camera motion that moves hand and object together also produces perfect coupling; subtract the global affine first or the whole shot reads as transport.

entries.label: Spreading mortar with a trowel
entries.description: A flat tool drags a viscous material across a surface, leaving a changed texture band.
entries.frame_evidence: A flat-bladed tool sweeping along a line with a persistent texture change trailing behind it.
entries.detector_note: Trailing-change test: after a tool tip passes a location, the local texture energy (skimage.feature.graycomatrix contrast, or local std) must change and stay changed for 5+ unique cels.
entries.notes: The trailing-persistence test is the general primitive for any material-depositing action (mortar, paint, icing) and cannot name which.

entries.label: Tying a knot or lace
entries.description: Two hands manipulate flexible strands through a loop-forming sequence.
entries.frame_evidence: Two pinch grips exchanging positions around a small region, with thin flexible elements changing topology between cels.
entries.detector_note: Needs a fine articulated hand-object model plus thin-structure tracking; neither the landmark tier nor a small VLM resolves strand topology at these scales.
entries.notes: Logged as a blind spot. A VLM will happily say yes to tying on almost any two-handed close-up, so a vlm tier here would be an overclaim.

entries.label: Typing
entries.description: Multiple fingers oscillate vertically over a flat surface in an alternating pattern.
entries.frame_evidence: Several fingertips moving up and down out of phase with the wrists nearly stationary.
entries.detector_note: Per-fingertip vertical displacement in the hand-local frame; typing when 3+ fingertips show oscillation of 0.05-0.25 hand-widths at 2-8 Hz (FFT via numpy.fft.rfft over unique cels) with pairwise phase differences above 0.3 rad.
entries.notes: Needs a good hand landmark track at 12+ unique cels per second; anime keyboard shots are typically a couple of blurred drawings and must be logged NOT DETECTABLE.

entries.label: Utensil to mouth
entries.description: A fork, spoon or chopsticks travel to the mouth in a tripod or power grip.
entries.frame_evidence: A thin tool axis extending from a tripod grip and terminating at the lips.
entries.detector_note: Tripod grasp plus tool axis whose far endpoint reaches within 0.3 head-widths of the mouth landmark, confirmed by a VLM crop.
entries.vlm_question: Is there a fork, spoon or chopsticks touching the person mouth? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Chopsticks give two nearly-parallel axes and often break the single-axis fit.

entries.label: Wiping a surface
entries.description: A hand or cloth sweeps back and forth over a surface, usually removing something.
entries.frame_evidence: Repeated reciprocating hand travel over a planar region with progressive texture change behind it.
entries.detector_note: Reciprocation count from sign changes in the hand velocity along its dominant PCA axis, combined with the trailing-change test.
entries.notes: Without the texture change this is just a waving hand near a surface.

entries.label: Wrist radial / ulnar deviation
entries.description: Side-to-side wrist angle, prominent in hammering, pouring and writing.
entries.frame_evidence: Lateral offset of the hand axis from the forearm axis in the frame.
entries.detector_note: Signed angle between the forearm vector (13->15) and the hand vector (0->9) projected into the palm plane estimated from landmarks 0, 5, 17.
entries.notes: Same projection caveat as wrist flexion; the two are not separable without real 3D.

entries.label: Wrist flexion / extension angle
entries.description: The angle between forearm and hand in the sagittal sense.
entries.frame_evidence: Angle formed by elbow, wrist and middle-finger MCP in the frame.
entries.detector_note: Angle at pose wrist 15 between the vectors to elbow 13 and to hand landmark 9 (or pose index 19); report in degrees, sign from the palm normal.
entries.notes: This is a projected angle, not an anatomical one; out-of-plane rotation makes it read arbitrarily.

entries.label: Writing with a pen
entries.description: A tripod-gripped implement makes small rapid strokes on a surface, leaving marks.
entries.frame_evidence: Tripod grip, small high-frequency tip excursions confined to a band, and progressive dark-pixel accumulation along the tip path.
entries.detector_note: Tripod grasp gate (landmark) plus accumulation test: difference the writing-surface ROI across unique cels and check that newly-dark pixels lie within 5px of the tracked tip path and never disappear.
entries.notes: The VLM inspector is blind to ink; this accumulation test is the only handle we have, and it fails when the hand occludes the writing or the paper is blown out.

entries.label: Angled (L-shaped) conversational stance
entries.description: Subjects oriented at roughly a right angle rather than squared off, the relaxed-talk geometry.
entries.frame_evidence: Two bodies whose chest directions meet at about 90 degrees, both partly toward a shared space.
entries.detector_note: Angle between torso facing vectors in [60, 120] degrees while distance_shoulder_units < 3.

entries.label: Approach
entries.description: One subject deliberately moves toward the other, closing the gap.
entries.frame_evidence: One body's feet and centroid translate toward the other while the other stays put.
entries.detector_note: Closing trend AND the mover's centroid displacement > 3x the other's; direction cosine between mover velocity and the A->B vector > 0.7.
entries.notes: A camera dolly toward a static pair mimics approach: gate on background flow (cv2.calcOpticalFlowFarneback median vector outside both subject masks) being near zero.

entries.label: Attack initiation (who moves first)
entries.description: Which subject begins the exchange.
entries.frame_evidence: One body committing forward while the other is still static.
entries.detector_note: First subject in the shot whose limb speed crosses the strike threshold; report the lead in unique cels over the other subject's first crossing.

entries.label: Averted gaze
entries.description: A subject actively looks away from the partner while remaining oriented toward him.
entries.frame_evidence: Body still facing the partner but eyes and head angled off to the side or down.
entries.detector_note: Torso facing_cos > 0.6 toward the partner while gaze_error > 40 degrees, over >= 3 unique cels.

entries.label: Back to back
entries.description: Subjects oriented away from each other, backs adjacent, typical of a defensive pair or a rift beat.
entries.frame_evidence: Two bodies close together with both facing vectors pointing outward in opposite directions.
entries.detector_note: Torso facing vectors with dot product < -0.7 while distance_shoulder_units < 1.2.
entries.notes: Highly sensitive to the front/back ambiguity above; verify with a VLM crop when the beat matters.

entries.label: Beckoning gesture
entries.description: A hand gesture calling the other subject closer.
entries.frame_evidence: A raised hand with fingers curling repeatedly toward the gesturer, aimed at the partner.
entries.detector_note: HandLandmarker aperture oscillating (>= 2 open-close cycles in <= 10 unique cels) with the palm oriented toward the gesturer and the arm raised toward the partner.
entries.notes: Palm orientation from HandLandmarker is unstable at small hand sizes; the cycle count carries most of the signal.

entries.label: Block / parry
entries.description: The defender interposes a limb or object on the attack line.
entries.frame_evidence: A forearm raised into the path of the incoming limb, the two limbs meeting short of the body.
entries.detector_note: Defender's forearm segment (13-15 or 14-16) intersecting the attacker's limb ray, with the attacker's limb speed dropping > 60% at that point rather than at the defender's torso.
entries.notes: Requires both skeletons through the collision, which is exactly where pose detection is least reliable.

entries.label: Blocking the other's path
entries.description: A subject stands in the line the other is travelling along, obstructing it.
entries.frame_evidence: One figure planted directly between the other and its direction of travel, arms out or braced.
entries.detector_note: A's centroid lies within 1 shoulder-span of the ray from B's centroid along B's velocity, at a distance < 4 shoulder-units, and A's own speed is near zero.

entries.label: Bow toward the partner
entries.description: A subject bends at the waist toward the other, a greeting or deference beat.
entries.frame_evidence: The torso pitching forward around the hips while the feet stay planted, head lowered toward the partner.
entries.detector_note: Shoulder-midpoint to hip-midpoint vector rotating forward by > 25 degrees while ankle positions stay within 0.05 frame-diagonals, and the bend direction is toward the partner.
entries.notes: Bending to pick something up has the same torso signature; the reach-to-ground check (wrist near the ground line) should veto it.

entries.label: Camera-motion compensation for interaction metrics
entries.description: Removal of global camera motion before any relative-motion claim about two subjects.
entries.frame_evidence: The whole frame translating or scaling while the subjects hold their relative positions.
entries.detector_note: cv2.goodFeaturesToTrack + cv2.calcOpticalFlowPyrLK on background pixels (outside all subject masks), then cv2.estimateAffinePartial2D with RANSAC; subtract the fitted global transform from every subject velocity.
entries.notes: When subjects fill the frame there are too few background features and the fit is garbage; report the inlier fraction and suppress motion findings below a threshold.

entries.label: Carry / lift
entries.description: One subject bears the other's weight off the ground.
entries.frame_evidence: One body horizontal or elevated with its feet clear of the ground line, supported by the other's arms.
entries.detector_note: B's ankle landmarks (27,28) above the estimated ground line (the lowest 5th percentile of A's foot landmarks over the shot) while masks intersect, sustained >= 4 unique cels.
entries.notes: Ground-line estimation fails on stairs, water, flying shots and low-angle framings.

entries.label: Catch
entries.description: A flying object's track terminates at a subject's hand which then moves with it.
entries.frame_evidence: The blob arriving at a hand, the hand closing, and the blob thereafter sharing the hand's motion.
entries.detector_note: Flight track ending within 0.2 shoulder-spans of a wrist landmark, followed by blob-hand velocity correlation > 0.8 over the next 3 unique cels.
entries.notes: Also fires when an object passes behind a hand; the velocity correlation is the discriminator and it needs >= 3 cels.

entries.label: Flat-shaded contact ambiguity (2D)
entries.description: In flat cel art there is no occlusion cue at a contact boundary, so screen adjacency can never be resolved to real contact.
entries.frame_evidence: Two drawn characters whose outlines meet with identical flat fills on both sides of the boundary.
entries.detector_note: No pixel evidence exists to separate 'touching' from 'one drawn in front of the other'; the shading model that would carry it is absent by design in most cel styles.
entries.notes: Explicit and permanent blind spot for 2D: every physical_contact FOUND on drawn footage is really 'silhouettes adjacent', and must be logged with that qualification. Character-outline colour changes (a contact line drawn by the artist) exist in some styles but are not general.

entries.label: Chase
entries.description: A pursuit at speed: one subject flees, the other pursues, both moving fast.
entries.frame_evidence: Two figures running in the same direction with the gap roughly held or closing, limbs at full stride.
entries.detector_note: Following geometry PLUS both subjects' centroid speeds above the shot's 80th percentile PLUS gait cadence (ankle-landmark oscillation frequency) in the running range; report gap trend.
entries.notes: In a locked-camera chase both subjects are near-stationary in frame and the background streams instead; measure speed relative to the BACKGROUND flow, not to the frame.

entries.label: Choke / hands at the throat
entries.description: Hands closed around the partner's neck.
entries.frame_evidence: One or two hands clamped at the base of the other character's head, faces close, arms extended.
entries.detector_note: Both of A's wrists within 0.35 head-widths of B's neck point (midpoint of landmark 0 and the 11-12 midpoint) for >= 3 unique cels.
entries.notes: A two-handed collar grab has the same geometry; a VLM crop check is warranted before reporting this specific label.

entries.label: Circle / ring formation
entries.description: Subjects arranged around a common centre, all facing inward.
entries.frame_evidence: Figures ringing an open central space, backs outward.
entries.detector_note: Fit a circle to the centroids by algebraic least squares (numpy.linalg.lstsq on the Kasa formulation); require radial residual < 15% of radius and most facing vectors pointing at the fitted centre.
entries.notes: With <= 4 subjects a circle fit is under-constrained and will always succeed; require >= 5 or report low confidence.

entries.label: Circling / orbiting the other subject
entries.description: One subject moves around the other at roughly constant radius, as in a stand-off or a sizing-up.
entries.frame_evidence: The moving subject sweeping across frame while the gap to the stationary subject stays constant.
entries.detector_note: distance_shoulder_units std < 0.3 while the bearing angle atan2(dy,dx) of the A->B vector changes monotonically by > 40 degrees over the window.
entries.notes: A camera arc around a static pair produces the same bearing sweep; gate on background parallax.

entries.label: Combat vs dance vs play
entries.description: Whether a fast contact-rich exchange is a fight, a dance, or roughhousing.
entries.frame_evidence: Similar kinematics: fast limbs, close distance, repeated contact, differing only in facial expression and context.
entries.detector_note: Crop the two-subject union bbox, upscale to 640px, ask qwen2.5vl; escalate contested shots to the Qwen3-VL judge.
entries.vlm_question: Are the two characters in this image fighting each other? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Kinematics genuinely cannot separate these classes; anything the geometry says here is a guess. The VLM answer is itself unreliable on stylised art and should be reported with its own confidence, not merged into the geometry.

entries.label: Contact shadow / occlusion seam
entries.description: The darkening where two bodies genuinely touch, the rendered cue that separates real contact from screen adjacency.
entries.frame_evidence: A narrow band of reduced luminance running along the boundary where the two silhouettes meet.
entries.detector_note: Sample a 5-px band along the mask-intersection boundary (cv2.dilate minus cv2.erode of the union mask); compare its mean luminance against the same band's value 10 px away on each body; flag a drop > 8% as a contact seam.
entries.notes: THE discriminator for the screen-adjacency false positive in the physical_contact group. Fails under flat frontal lighting, on dark clothing where the drop is unmeasurable, and on any render with contact shadows disabled.

entries.label: Contact duration and count
entries.description: How many distinct contact events occur in a shot and how long each lasts.
entries.frame_evidence: Repeated cycles of silhouettes touching and separating.
entries.detector_note: Run-length encode the contact_flag series over unique cels; emit event count, durations, and the inter-event gaps.
entries.notes: Report durations in both cels and seconds; the cel count alone is meaningless across 1s/2s/3s footage.

entries.label: Gentle vs forceful contact
entries.description: Whether the contact is a light touch or a violent impact.
entries.frame_evidence: A slow-approaching hand that comes to rest, versus a fast limb with a flash and a recoiling target.
entries.detector_note: Composite: approach speed at the last pre-contact cel, presence of an impact frame, and the target's post-contact displacement; threshold on the composite rather than on any single term.
entries.notes: The force_score is an ordinal, not physics. Calibrate its threshold on hand-labelled clips or it is an arbitrary number.

entries.label: Impact frame (contact instant)
entries.description: The single cel where a collision is registered by the image itself.
entries.frame_evidence: A luminance spike, an impact flash, radial speed lines, a squash of both silhouettes, or debris particles at the contact point.
entries.detector_note: On unique cels: spike detection on mean luminance (delta > 3 sigma of the shot) OR a local divergence peak in cv2.calcOpticalFlowFarneback flow at the contact centroid; corroborate with a sudden edge-density jump (cv2.Canny count) in the contact ROI.
entries.notes: Cuts, lightning, muzzle flashes and camera flashes all produce luminance spikes; the finding is 'an impact-like discontinuity', and attribution to the contact point requires the contact centroid to already exist.

entries.label: Contact patch slipping
entries.description: A gripped or supported contact point sliding across the other body, the rig artefact that betrays a fake attachment.
entries.frame_evidence: A hand that stays visually on a shoulder but drifts across it relative to the shoulder's own surface features.
entries.detector_note: Seed cv2.calcOpticalFlowPyrLK features inside the contact patch on both bodies; the slip is the residual displacement between the two feature sets after removing the receiving body's rigid motion.
entries.notes: Needs trackable surface texture on both bodies; on untextured clothing or flat cel fills the LK tracker has nothing to lock onto and returns a confident zero.

entries.label: Body region of contact
entries.description: Which part of the receiving subject is being touched: head, torso, arm, hand, leg.
entries.frame_evidence: The overlap patch located over the receiving character's head, chest, limb, etc.
entries.detector_note: Assign the contact centroid to the nearest of B's landmark clusters (head 0-10, torso 11/12/23/24, arms 13-22, legs 25-32) by Euclidean distance in image space.
entries.notes: Ambiguous when the contact centroid falls between clusters; report the margin so weak assignments can be filtered.

entries.label: Distance-to-contact transition
entries.description: The pair transitions from a measurable gap to zero gap within one continuous shot.
entries.frame_evidence: A frame where clear background separates two bodies, followed within a few cels by silhouettes touching.
entries.detector_note: distance_shoulder_units crossing below the touching threshold (mask gap == 0 px after 3px dilation) inside one shot, without an intervening cut.
entries.notes: Requires the shot-boundary list; a cut mid-approach produces a false instantaneous transition.

entries.label: Contact release / separation
entries.description: Contact ends and the bodies separate.
entries.frame_evidence: Background pixels reappearing between the two silhouettes after a period of adjacency.
entries.detector_note: Mask intersection returning to empty for >= 2 consecutive unique cels after a contact run; report the run length.

entries.label: Contact deformation / squash
entries.description: The bodies visibly deform at the contact point, the animation signature of force.
entries.frame_evidence: A flattened cheek, a compressed torso, or a stretched limb across the two cels bracketing contact.
entries.detector_note: Compare the contact-ROI silhouette's second moments (cv2.moments -> eccentricity) between the pre-contact and impact cels; flag an eccentricity increase > 25% localised to the contact ROI.
entries.notes: Only meaningful when the ROI silhouette is cleanly segmentable; on busy backgrounds this measures the background.

entries.label: Zero-gap silhouette contact
entries.description: The two subjects' image regions touch, the necessary condition for any physical contact event.
entries.frame_evidence: No background pixels remaining between the two bodies at the point of nearest approach.
entries.detector_note: PoseLandmarker(output_segmentation_masks=True): dilate each mask by 3 px with cv2.dilate and test for non-empty intersection; report the contact centroid.
entries.notes: Screen-space adjacency is not 3D contact: a subject passing in front of another at a different depth reads as touching. This is the dominant false positive in the whole contact group.

entries.label: Counter-attack
entries.description: The defender's own strike immediately following a block or dodge.
entries.frame_evidence: A defensive motion flowing directly into an outgoing limb toward the first attacker.
entries.detector_note: A strike-extension event by the defender starting within 6 unique cels of a block or dodge event, with the roles reversed.
entries.notes: Roles depend on identity tracks; during a clinch the tracks are the least trustworthy.

entries.label: Cowering / shrinking away
entries.description: A subject compacts his posture, lowering and drawing in, near another subject.
entries.frame_evidence: A crouched body with arms drawn up and head tucked, close to a standing figure.
entries.detector_note: Bounding-box aspect ratio dropping toward square, head-to-hip distance shrinking > 25% from the shot median, wrists inside the torso quad, while another subject is within 2 shoulder-units.
entries.notes: Also fires on sitting down, picking something up and being carried.

entries.label: Cradle / bridal carry
entries.description: One subject holds the other horizontally across the arms.
entries.frame_evidence: A horizontal body supported at the back and knees by a standing figure.
entries.detector_note: B's shoulder-hip axis within 30 degrees of horizontal, B's centroid above A's hips, A's elbows flexed under B's torso.

entries.label: Crowd converging on a point
entries.description: A crowd's motion field points inward toward a common location.
entries.frame_evidence: Bodies from several sides all heading toward one spot in frame.
entries.detector_note: Negative mean divergence of the dense flow field; locate the sink by finding the minimum of the divergence map after scipy.ndimage.gaussian_filter smoothing.
entries.notes: A camera zoom-in produces a global convergent field; the homography compensation is mandatory, not optional.

entries.label: Crowd density distribution
