entries.description: Where in frame the crowd is dense versus sparse.
entries.frame_evidence: Regions of tightly packed figures against regions of open ground.
entries.detector_note: A real density map needs a crowd-counting CNN. An honest proxy is local edge density (cv2.Canny + box filter) normalised per shot, which measures texture, not people.
entries.notes: Do not report the edge-density proxy as a headcount; foliage and architecture score as dense crowds.

entries.label: Crowd flow coherence vs turbulence
entries.description: Whether the crowd moves as one body or churns in conflicting directions.
entries.frame_evidence: A uniformly streaming crowd versus a milling, colliding mass.
entries.detector_note: Resultant length R of the magnitude-weighted orientation histogram (R near 1 = coherent, near 0 = turbulent); also report the mean absolute flow divergence via numpy.gradient of the flow field.

entries.label: Crowd flow direction
entries.description: The dominant direction a crowd is moving, without needing any individual to be resolved.
entries.frame_evidence: A mass of bodies whose collective texture translates coherently across the frame.
entries.detector_note: cv2.calcOpticalFlowFarneback (or cv2.DISOpticalFlow_create(PRESET_MEDIUM)) between UNIQUE cels; build a 36-bin orientation histogram weighted by magnitude over the crowd ROI; report the circular mean and resultant length R.
entries.notes: Camera motion adds a global vector: subtract the dominant homography (cv2.estimateAffinePartial2D on background features) first. On 2s animation, flow between duplicate frames is exactly zero and that zero is an artefact. All temporal deltas must be indexed on UNIQUE CELS (dedupe consecutive frames by mean abs diff < 0.5/255 before differencing); on 2s/3s animation a raw per-frame delta of zero is a duplicate-frame artefact.

entries.label: Crowd fleeing from a point
entries.description: A crowd's motion field points outward from a common location, the panic signature.
entries.frame_evidence: Bodies radiating away from a single spot, often after an impact or explosion.
entries.detector_note: Positive mean divergence with a localised source maximum in the smoothed divergence map; corroborate with a preceding luminance spike (an explosion) in the same ROI.

entries.label: Crowd population estimate
entries.description: Estimated headcount when subjects exceed what per-person landmarking can resolve.
entries.frame_evidence: A field of repeated head-and-shoulder silhouettes filling a large fraction of frame area.
entries.detector_note: Needs a person detector (YOLO/RT-DETR) or a crowd-density CNN (CSRNet-class); neither is installed. cv2.HOGDescriptor with getDefaultPeopleDetector exists but is pedestrian-upright-photoreal only and is not trustworthy here.
entries.notes: Logged as NOT DETECTABLE today. Do not substitute contour counting: cel-shaded crowds merge into one connected component.

entries.label: Defocus disparity between subjects
entries.description: One subject is sharp and the other blurred, proving they sit at different depths and therefore are not in contact.
entries.frame_evidence: Crisp edges on one body against visibly soft edges on the other in the same frame.
entries.detector_note: Variance of the Laplacian (cv2.Laplacian(roi, cv2.CV_64F).var()) inside each subject's mask, normalised by the ROI's own contrast; a ratio above ~3 indicates a depth separation.
entries.notes: Only meaningful on shallow-depth-of-field live action and CG that renders DOF; a deep-focus or 2D image gives a ratio near 1 and the test is silent, which must not be read as 'same depth'.

entries.label: Speaking toward the frame edge
entries.description: A lone subject's mouth is active while his gaze is aimed off-screen, implying an unseen interlocutor.
entries.frame_evidence: A single character talking with the face angled toward an empty frame edge.
entries.detector_note: Mouth activity above the shot noise floor with gaze bearing exiting the frame and subject_count == 1.
entries.notes: Cannot distinguish talking to someone off-screen from talking to oneself or to an object.

entries.label: Dialogue implied without lip movement
entries.description: Speech is happening but the drawing does not animate the mouth (off-model shortcut, back-turned shot, held cel).
entries.frame_evidence: A static held drawing, or a back-of-head shot, over a stretch where the scene grammar implies talk.
entries.detector_note: Cannot be established from pixels alone; it requires the audio track or subtitles, which this analyzer does not read.
entries.notes: Explicit blind spot: absence of mouth motion is NOT evidence of silence in limited animation.

entries.label: Disengage from an exchange
entries.description: A combatant breaks contact and increases distance out of striking range.
entries.frame_evidence: One fighter stepping back with the other not following, the gap opening past arm's length.
entries.detector_note: Distance crossing above 2 shoulder-units after a contact/strike run, with strike-event rate falling to zero for >= 6 unique cels.

entries.label: Dismissive / go-away wave
entries.description: A hand sweeping outward away from the partner.
entries.frame_evidence: A hand flicking away from the body along the line toward the partner, once or twice.
entries.detector_note: Wrist lateral excursion > 0.5 shoulder-spans with the outward stroke faster than the return, over <= 6 unique cels.
entries.notes: Kinematically almost identical to a greeting wave; the two are only separable in context.

entries.label: Closing distance
entries.description: The gap between two subjects is shrinking over the window.
entries.frame_evidence: Successive cels show the background gap between the two bodies narrowing.
entries.detector_note: scipy.stats.linregress over distance_shoulder_units against UNIQUE-CEL index; slope < -0.05 units/cel with p < 0.05.
entries.notes: All temporal deltas must be indexed on UNIQUE CELS (dedupe consecutive frames by mean abs diff < 0.5/255 before differencing); on 2s/3s animation a raw per-frame delta of zero is a duplicate-frame artefact.

entries.label: Opening distance
entries.description: The gap between two subjects is growing over the window.
entries.frame_evidence: Successive cels show background opening up between the two bodies.
entries.detector_note: linregress slope > +0.05 units/cel with p < 0.05 on unique-cel indices.
entries.notes: All temporal deltas must be indexed on UNIQUE CELS (dedupe consecutive frames by mean abs diff < 0.5/255 before differencing); on 2s/3s animation a raw per-frame delta of zero is a duplicate-frame artefact.

entries.label: Held distance
entries.description: Two subjects maintain a near-constant separation, e.g. walking together or a stand-off.
entries.frame_evidence: The gap between the bodies stays visually identical across many cels even as both bodies move.
entries.detector_note: std(distance_shoulder_units) < 0.15 over >=8 unique cels while at least one subject's centroid displacement exceeds 0.05 frame-diagonal (i.e. they are moving, together).

entries.label: Dodge / slip
entries.description: The defender moves the target region off the attack line without blocking.
entries.frame_evidence: The head or torso ducking or leaning aside as the limb passes through empty space.
entries.detector_note: Defender's head or torso centroid displacing > 0.5 head-widths perpendicular to the attack line within 3 unique cels of the strike peak, and no contact detected.

entries.label: Drag
entries.description: One subject pulls the other along the ground.
entries.frame_evidence: A body low in frame translating horizontally, connected by an arm to an upright walking figure.
entries.detector_note: Sustained wrist-to-wrist or wrist-to-limb contact while B's hip-midpoint stays in the bottom third of B's own historic range and both centroids translate together over >= 6 unique cels.

entries.label: Embrace / hug
entries.description: Two subjects wrap arms around each other with torsos in contact.
entries.frame_evidence: Two silhouettes merged into one mass with arms visible crossing behind the partner's back.
entries.detector_note: Torso masks intersecting, each subject's wrists lying on the FAR side of the partner's torso centreline (a sign test on the wrist position relative to the partner's shoulder-hip axis), for >= 3 unique cels.
entries.notes: During an embrace the two pose skeletons frequently merge into one detection or swap limbs between subjects; treat the identity output as unreliable inside the contact window.

entries.label: Embrace, VLM adjudication
entries.description: A VLM ruling on whether two characters are hugging, used because pose landmarking degrades inside an embrace.
entries.frame_evidence: Two merged bodies with arms around each other.
entries.detector_note: Crop the merged silhouette bbox with 15% padding, upscale to 512px, ask qwen2.5vl.
entries.vlm_question: Are the two characters in this image hugging each other with their arms around each other? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Wrestling, carrying and a tackle all read as a hug to a small VLM; use with the combat entries as a disambiguator.

entries.label: One subject encircled by others
entries.description: Several subjects surround a single one, the geometry of confrontation or ambush.
entries.frame_evidence: A lone figure at the centre with others arrayed around and facing inward.
entries.detector_note: A subject whose bearing coverage (the angular spread of the other subjects' bearings around it, binned into 8 sectors) exceeds 5 occupied sectors, all within 4 shoulder-units.
entries.notes: Screen-space bearing coverage is a 2D projection; subjects behind and in front of the target collapse onto the same sector, so this under-reports at flat camera angles.

entries.label: Escort / flanking formation
entries.description: Two subjects travel abreast of and slightly behind a third.
entries.frame_evidence: One figure ahead with two others holding station on its left and right rear quarters.
entries.detector_note: With >= 3 subjects: two subjects holding roughly constant bearing and distance to a third over >= 10 unique cels, bearings on opposite sides of the leader's velocity vector.

entries.label: Evasive change of direction
entries.description: The pursued subject makes a sharp lateral direction change.
entries.frame_evidence: A body planting hard and the trajectory kinking within two or three cels.
entries.detector_note: Heading change of the centroid velocity > 45 degrees within <= 3 unique cels while speed stays above half its pre-change value.
entries.notes: All temporal deltas must be indexed on UNIQUE CELS (dedupe consecutive frames by mean abs diff < 0.5/255 before differencing); on 2s/3s animation a raw per-frame delta of zero is a duplicate-frame artefact.

entries.label: Attack exchange alternation
entries.description: The back-and-forth rhythm of a fight: A attacks, B attacks, A attacks.
entries.frame_evidence: Alternating bursts of limb speed between the two bodies.
entries.detector_note: Run-length encode the per-subject strike-event series on unique cels; count role alternations and report the inter-strike interval distribution against a shuffled null.
entries.notes: NULL MODEL REQUIRED: two subjects flailing independently also alternate; the null is a random shuffle of the interval sequence.

entries.label: Exclusion (a subject turned away from the group)
entries.description: In a group, one subject faces away while the others face inward.
entries.frame_evidence: A ring of inward-facing figures with one whose back is to the rest.
entries.detector_note: With >= 3 subjects: one subject whose facing vector has a negative dot product with the direction to the group centroid while the majority are positive.
entries.notes: Inherits the front/back facing ambiguity, which is the exact quantity this entry depends on.

entries.label: Offering gesture (arm extended toward partner)
entries.description: One subject extends an arm toward the other, palm-forward or holding something out.
entries.frame_evidence: A straightened arm reaching into the gap, hand at the far end near the partner.
entries.detector_note: Elbow angle > 150 degrees with the wrist displaced toward the partner by > 0.6 shoulder-spans from the shoulder, held >= 3 unique cels.

entries.label: Eyeline match across a cut
entries.description: Two consecutive shots whose gaze bearings are complementary, implying the subjects are looking at each other.
entries.frame_evidence: Shot A: a face looking frame-right. Shot B: a face looking frame-left, at similar height.
entries.detector_note: Compare the last unique cel of shot N against the first of shot N+1: gaze bearings of opposite screen sign and head heights within 0.15 frame height. Requires the shot-boundary list as input.
entries.notes: This is the standard shot/reverse-shot grammar; a mismatch is either a deliberate crossed-line or a continuity error, and the detector cannot tell which.

entries.label: Facing each other
entries.description: Both subjects' torsos are oriented toward one another, the geometry of confrontation or conversation.
entries.frame_evidence: Two bodies squared up with chests aimed at each other across the gap.
entries.detector_note: cos(angle between A's torso facing vector and the A->B vector) > 0.6 AND the same for B toward A, over >=2 unique cels.
entries.notes: MediaPipe pose/face landmarkers are trained on photoreal humans; on 2D cel art recall drops hard (large eyes, missing nose shading, non-anatomical proportions), so a NOT-FOUND on drawn footage is usually detector failure, not absence. Log pose_detect_confidence_mean alongside every verdict.

entries.label: Facing the same way
entries.description: Both subjects face a common direction, as when watching something together or walking abreast.
entries.frame_evidence: Two bodies in matching profile or matching three-quarter view, both chests aimed off the same side of frame.
entries.detector_note: Dot product of the two torso facing vectors > 0.7 while neither points at the other (facing_cos < 0.3).

entries.label: Raised fist
entries.description: A clenched fist raised toward the partner.
entries.frame_evidence: A closed hand lifted above shoulder height, arm cocked, aimed toward the other character.
entries.detector_note: HandLandmarker aperture below the closed threshold, wrist above the shoulder line, and the forearm vector oriented toward the partner.
entries.notes: A raised fist is also a celebration; the target-bearing check is the only cue and it is weak.

entries.label: Fleeing away from another subject
entries.description: A subject moves at speed along the vector away from another subject.
entries.frame_evidence: A running figure with its back to a second figure and the gap opening.
entries.detector_note: Centroid velocity direction cosine to the away-vector > 0.8 with speed above the shot 70th percentile and the gap opening.

entries.label: Focus pull from one subject to the other
entries.description: The plane of focus shifts from one subject to the other, a directorial transfer of attention within one shot.
entries.frame_evidence: One body sharpening over several frames while the other softens, with no cut.
entries.detector_note: Track the per-subject Laplacian variance across unique cels; flag a crossing where sharpness_ratio inverts sign and both curves change monotonically over >= 4 cels.
entries.notes: Camera motion changing subject scale also changes measured sharpness; normalise by subject pixel area before comparing.

entries.label: Following (one subject behind another)
entries.description: One subject travels behind another along a similar path.
entries.frame_evidence: Two figures moving the same way, one consistently trailing in the direction of travel.
entries.detector_note: Both centroid velocity vectors aligned (cos > 0.8), a stable offset along the travel direction, and the follower's path matching the leader's earlier path (compare the follower's position at cel t to the leader's at t-k for the best lag k).
entries.notes: Two people happening to walk the same way down a street satisfy this; the path-match residual at a positive lag is what makes it 'following' rather than 'co-moving'.

entries.label: Foreground dominance framing
entries.description: One subject is framed much larger and nearer camera than the other, a compositional power cue.
entries.frame_evidence: One body occupying a third or more of the frame with the other small in the background.
entries.detector_note: Ratio of subject mask areas > 4, with the larger subject's bbox touching a frame edge.
entries.notes: This is framing, not interaction; report it as context for the other findings.

entries.label: Gaze directed at the partner's hands or held object
entries.description: A subject looks at what the other is holding or doing rather than at his face.
entries.frame_evidence: A face angled downward toward the other character's hands.
entries.detector_note: Gaze ray lands within 1.5 hand-widths of the partner's wrist landmarks (15/16) and > 2 head-widths from the partner's head.

entries.label: Gaze break
entries.description: Eye contact is established and then broken, a beat-level transition.
entries.frame_evidence: Two faces locked, then one face swinging away over the following cels.
entries.detector_note: Transition from mutual_gaze true to false with gaze_error rising past 35 degrees within <= 4 unique cels; log which subject broke it.
entries.notes: All temporal deltas must be indexed on UNIQUE CELS (dedupe consecutive frames by mean abs diff < 0.5/255 before differencing); on 2s/3s animation a raw per-frame delta of zero is a duplicate-frame artefact.

entries.label: Off-screen gaze continuity across a cut
entries.description: A subject's off-screen gaze bearing is consistent with the subject revealed in the next shot.
entries.frame_evidence: Shot A: a subject looking frame-left. Shot B: the object or person that was off frame-left.
entries.detector_note: Compare the last unique cel of shot N (gaze exit edge) with the first cels of shot N+1 (whether the newly revealed content sits on the corresponding side); requires the shot-boundary list.
entries.notes: This is film grammar inference, not measurement; the match flag is weak evidence and should never be reported as a verified interaction.

entries.label: Gaze following (A looks, then B looks)
entries.description: One subject looks somewhere and the other subsequently turns to look the same way.
entries.frame_evidence: A head turns toward frame-left; a few cels later the second head turns to the same bearing.
entries.detector_note: Cross-correlate the two gaze-yaw time series on unique-cel indices; report peak correlation at positive lag 1-8 cels with the follower's final bearing within 20 degrees of the leader's.
entries.notes: MUST be scored against a null: circularly shift one subject's series 200 times and report the percentile of the observed peak. Without that null the correlation is meaningless.

entries.label: Per-subject gaze ray
entries.description: The estimated direction each subject is looking, the substrate of every gaze relation.
entries.frame_evidence: Iris position within the eye opening combined with head orientation.
entries.detector_note: FaceLandmarker(output_face_blendshapes=True, output_facial_transformation_matrixes=True): head rotation from the matrix, eye offset from eyeLookInLeft/eyeLookOutLeft/eyeLookUpLeft/eyeLookDownLeft blendshapes; combine into a ray.
entries.notes: Anime eyes are drawn with a stylised iris and no sclera shading in many styles; blendshape-derived eye offset is near-meaningless there. Mark 2D gaze rays low-confidence by default.

entries.label: True 3D gaze target
entries.description: Where a subject is actually looking in scene space, not merely in screen bearing.
entries.frame_evidence: A subject's eyes aimed at a specific depth-separated object.
entries.detector_note: Requires a calibrated gaze estimator (Gaze360/ETH-XGaze class) plus monocular depth; neither model is installed and screen-space rays cannot resolve depth ambiguity.
entries.notes: Logged as a permanent blind spot: all gaze findings in this shard are SCREEN-BEARING findings only.

entries.label: Gaze aimed off-screen
entries.description: A subject looks at something outside the frame, implying an unseen participant.
entries.frame_evidence: A face turned hard toward a frame edge with the eyes at the corner of the socket.
entries.detector_note: Gaze ray exits the frame boundary within its first 0.3 frame-diagonals of travel and no subject or salient object lies along it inside the frame.

entries.label: Glance / quick flick of the eyes
entries.description: A short look toward the partner or an object, returning to the original direction.
entries.frame_evidence: Two or three cels where the pupils shift off-centre and then return.
entries.detector_note: Gaze yaw excursion > 20 degrees and return to within 8 degrees of baseline inside <= 5 unique cels.
entries.notes: At 8-12 unique drawings per second, a real glance can be a single cel; the detector cannot resolve anything faster.

entries.label: Collar or clothing grab
entries.description: One subject grabs the other's clothing at the chest or collar.
entries.frame_evidence: A fist bunched at the other character's upper chest, that character's torso pulled forward and tilted.
entries.detector_note: A's hand landmarks inside B's upper-torso quad (between 11,12 and the shoulder-hip midline top third) with B's torso lean angle changing > 8 degrees toward A within 3 unique cels.

entries.label: Wrist grab
entries.description: One subject seizes the other's wrist, arresting its motion.
entries.frame_evidence: One hand closed around the other character's wrist, the grabbed arm's motion stopping abruptly.
entries.detector_note: A's hand landmarks within 0.12 shoulder-spans of B's wrist AND B's wrist speed dropping by > 70% within 2 unique cels of the contact onset.
entries.notes: The motion-arrest test is what separates a grab from a hand simply passing near a wrist.

entries.label: Greeting wave
entries.description: A raised hand oscillating laterally toward the partner.
entries.frame_evidence: A hand held above shoulder height swinging side to side, face toward the partner.
entries.detector_note: Wrist above shoulder line, lateral oscillation with >= 2 zero crossings in <= 10 unique cels, torso facing the partner.
entries.notes: All temporal deltas must be indexed on UNIQUE CELS (dedupe consecutive frames by mean abs diff < 0.5/255 before differencing); on 2s/3s animation a raw per-frame delta of zero is a duplicate-frame artefact.

entries.label: Group clustering
entries.description: Multiple subjects converging into a tight spatial cluster.
entries.frame_evidence: Several figures whose mutual gaps shrink until they form one compact mass.
entries.detector_note: Mean pairwise distance across all tracked subjects decreasing with linregress slope < 0 (p<0.05) and ending below 2.5 shoulder-units.
entries.notes: Caps out at num_poses=6; larger groups fall under the crowd entries and are not detectable today.

entries.label: Group dispersal / scatter
entries.description: Subjects moving apart from a common centre, as in a panic scatter or a break-up.
entries.frame_evidence: Figures radiating outward from a shared point, gaps widening in all directions.
entries.detector_note: Mean pairwise distance increasing AND the mean radial velocity component (relative to the group centroid) positive for >= 60% of subjects.

entries.label: Group leader / front position
entries.description: Which subject occupies the leading position of a moving group.
entries.frame_evidence: One figure consistently ahead of the group centroid along the direction of travel.
entries.detector_note: Project each subject's centroid onto the group's mean velocity vector; the leader is the argmax sustained over >= 8 unique cels.
entries.notes: Depends on the identity tracks, which are the weakest link; report leader_stability_fraction so churn is visible.

entries.label: Synchronised group motion
entries.description: Subjects moving in step with one another, e.g. marching or a dance.
entries.frame_evidence: Several bodies whose limbs reach the same phase of the same cycle in the same cels.
entries.detector_note: Cross-correlate per-subject limb-angle time-series (e.g. knee angle) on unique-cel indices; report the mean peak correlation at zero lag against a circular-shift null of 200 permutations.
entries.notes: NULL MODEL MANDATORY: any two walking figures correlate somewhat. The percentile against the shifted null is the finding, not the raw correlation.

entries.label: Group spacing uniformity
entries.description: Whether the group is evenly spaced (formal, marching) or irregular (casual, crowd).
entries.frame_evidence: Equal gaps between every adjacent pair, versus a ragged distribution.
entries.detector_note: Nearest-neighbour distance distribution across subjects: report mean, std, and the coefficient of variation.

entries.label: Fighting guard stance
entries.description: Hands raised in a protective position with a bladed or braced stance.
entries.frame_evidence: Both fists near face height, elbows tucked, feet staggered.
entries.detector_note: Both wrists above the shoulder-hip midline and within 1 head-width of the head, elbow angles < 110 degrees, and ankle separation > 0.8 shoulder spans with one foot forward.

entries.label: Guarding / interposing between two others
entries.description: A third subject positions himself between two others, shielding one from the other.
entries.frame_evidence: One figure standing on the line joining two others, facing the threatening one, arms spread.
entries.detector_note: With >= 3 subjects: C's centroid within 1 shoulder-span of the segment A-B, with C's facing vector toward A and C's arms abducted (wrist-to-torso-axis distance > 0.6 shoulder-spans on both sides).
entries.notes: Requires three simultaneous tracks, which is where the untracked-identity problem bites hardest.

entries.label: Hand entering frame to touch the subject
entries.description: A limb from off-screen enters the frame and contacts the visible subject.
entries.frame_evidence: A hand or arm crossing a frame edge and landing on the subject's shoulder, arm, or face.
entries.detector_note: HandLandmarker hand whose wrist cannot be matched to the visible pose's wrists, whose track originates at a frame border, and which reaches the subject's mask.
entries.notes: The subject's own hand re-entering after leaving frame produces the same signature; check whether the visible pose already accounts for both wrists.

entries.label: Hand holding
entries.description: The two subjects' hands are joined and moving together.
entries.frame_evidence: Two hands overlapping into a single blob that translates as one unit across cels.
entries.detector_note: A's wrist within 0.15 shoulder-spans of B's wrist for >= 4 unique cels AND their velocity vectors correlated > 0.8 over that window.
entries.notes: Two hands that merely cross in screen space at similar velocity (both subjects walking) will pass the correlation test; require the small distance AND the correlation, and report both.

entries.label: Hand near the partner's body
entries.description: One subject's hand is within touching distance of the other's body, the geometric precondition for touch.
entries.frame_evidence: A hand overlapping or adjacent to the other character's torso, arm, or head.
entries.detector_note: Min distance from A's wrist/index landmarks (15,16,19,20) to any of B's landmarks, normalised by B's shoulder span; threshold < 0.35.
entries.notes: MediaPipe pose/face landmarkers are trained on photoreal humans; on 2D cel art recall drops hard (large eyes, missing nose shading, non-anatomical proportions), so a NOT-FOUND on drawn footage is usually detector failure, not absence. Log pose_detect_confidence_mean alongside every verdict.

entries.label: Hands meet then separate (handoff shell)
entries.description: The pure kinematic shell of an exchange: hands converge, dwell, diverge, without identifying any object.
entries.frame_evidence: Two hands approaching to touching distance, holding briefly, then withdrawing to their own bodies.
entries.detector_note: Wrist-to-wrist distance profile with a V shape: falls below 0.2 shoulder-spans, dwells >= 2 unique cels, then rises above 0.5 within 8 cels.
entries.notes: Identical to a handshake without oscillation and to a hand-hold that ends; report the shell, not the interpretation.

entries.label: Hands-only participant
entries.description: A participant present only as hands or a limb entering frame, with no torso to landmark.
entries.frame_evidence: A hand or forearm crossing the frame edge and acting on an object or on the visible subject's body.
entries.detector_note: mediapipe HandLandmarker(num_hands=4) returns a hand whose wrist (landmark 0) cannot be matched to any detected pose's wrist (15/16) within 0.08 of frame diagonal.
entries.notes: Very common in inserts (a hand passing a cup). Without a torso the analyzer must not claim who the hand belongs to.

entries.label: Handshake
entries.description: Two subjects clasp hands at roughly waist height and shake vertically.
entries.frame_evidence: Two forearms extended into the gap with the hands merged, small vertical oscillation over cels.
entries.detector_note: Wrist-to-wrist distance < 0.15 shoulder-spans at a height between the two subjects' hip and shoulder levels, with a vertical oscillation of the joined point (>= 1 up-down cycle in <= 8 unique cels).
entries.notes: Without the oscillation this is indistinguishable from a hand-hold or a handoff; report the cycle count.

entries.label: Head aimed at the partner
entries.description: Head yaw points at the other subject even when the torso does not, the 'looking over at him' geometry.
entries.frame_evidence: The face turned toward the partner while the chest stays aimed elsewhere.
entries.detector_note: Head yaw from mediapipe FaceLandmarker facial_transformation_matrixes (decompose R to yaw/pitch/roll); compare the head ray against the A->B vector; require |head_yaw - torso_yaw| > 20 degrees for the 'head only' case.
entries.notes: FaceLandmarker on anime faces returns a plausible mesh with unreliable pose; head yaw on cel art should be treated as low-confidence and cross-checked with a VLM crop.

entries.label: Headbutt
entries.description: A head-first strike into the partner.
entries.frame_evidence: One head driving forward into the other's face or chest, torso pitched forward.
entries.detector_note: A's head landmark 0 velocity toward B exceeding 3x its torso velocity, terminating inside B's head or torso mask.
entries.notes: Rare enough that the false-positive rate from a fast lean-in will dominate; treat every hit as a candidate for VLM review.

entries.label: Eye-level asymmetry (standing vs kneeling)
entries.description: One subject's head is markedly higher than the other's, so the interaction is up/down rather than level.
entries.frame_evidence: One character's head near the top of frame and the other's near mid-frame, with folded legs or a seated silhouette.
entries.detector_note: Head y (landmark 0) difference normalised by mean body height > 0.35; classify posture from knee angle (23-25-27) < 100 degrees for kneeling/seated.

entries.label: Hit flash / impact whiteout
entries.description: The single white or inverted cel used to sell an impact in drawn animation.
entries.frame_evidence: One cel where a large fraction of the frame goes uniformly bright or the values invert.
entries.detector_note: Mean luminance jumping > 3 sigma above the shot mean for exactly 1-2 unique cels with the frame's luminance variance collapsing (a flat frame), then returning.
entries.notes: Also fires on lightning, cuts to white, and photographic flashes; it is an event marker, not proof of a hit. Pose detection returns nothing on the flash cel, so the impact geometry must be stitched from the cels either side.

entries.label: Huddle
entries.description: A tight inward-facing cluster with heads close together.
entries.frame_evidence: Several heads converging into a small area with bodies leaning in.
entries.detector_note: Head landmarks (index 0) of >= 3 subjects within a radius of 1.5 shoulder-spans, with torsos leaning toward the head-cluster centroid.

entries.label: Identity-swap risk flag
entries.description: A moment where two tracks cross or overlap enough that downstream per-subject claims become unreliable.
entries.frame_evidence: Two subject boxes overlapping while their left-right screen order inverts between adjacent unique cels.
entries.detector_note: From pose centroids: flag when bbox IoU > 0.15 AND sign(x_A - x_B) flips between consecutive unique cels; mark all pairwise outputs in that window with confidence_penalty = 1.0.
entries.notes: A quality flag rather than a finding; its purpose is to stop the analyzer reporting confident nonsense during crossings.

entries.label: Debris or blood particles at the contact point
entries.description: Small high-contrast elements spraying from the contact location.
entries.frame_evidence: A cluster of small blobs radiating from the point where the bodies met, in the cels after impact.
entries.detector_note: In the contact ROI on the post-impact unique cel, count small connected components (cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats, area below a percentile) whose centroids' displacement vectors radiate from the contact centroid.
entries.notes: Snow, rain, sparks and confetti in the background produce the same statistic; require the radial origin to coincide with an independently detected contact centroid.

entries.label: Directed speed lines between subjects
entries.description: Drawn radial or parallel lines aimed from one subject at the other, a 2D-only force cue.
entries.frame_evidence: A burst of straight high-contrast lines converging on the contact point or streaming along the attack line.
entries.detector_note: cv2.HoughLinesP on the Canny map of the gap ROI; test for a common convergence point by clustering the line normals, and for parallelism by the orientation histogram's resultant length.
entries.notes: Backgrounds with architecture (railings, tiles, rain) generate the same Hough response; require the lines to be transient across unique cels, i.e. absent in the neighbouring cels.

entries.label: Selected interacting pair
entries.description: Which pair of subjects the analyzer treats as the interacting dyad in a multi-subject frame.
entries.frame_evidence: The two subjects that are closest, mutually oriented, and co-moving relative to everyone else.
entries.detector_note: Score each pair = w1*(1/normalised_distance) + w2*mutual_facing_cos + w3*motion_correlation; pick argmax and log the runner-up score so ambiguity is visible.
entries.notes: If selection_margin is small the shot has no single dyad; downstream dyadic findings should be suppressed, not guessed.

entries.label: Per-finding confidence roll-up
entries.description: The combined confidence for any dyadic finding, propagating detection, tracking and threshold uncertainty.
entries.frame_evidence: Not a visual feature: an audit value attached to every other entry in this domain.
entries.detector_note: Multiply the per-subject pose confidence, the identity-track stability over the window, the null percentile where one exists, and a threshold-margin term; emit all factors, never just the product.
entries.notes: Exists so a FOUND verdict in this domain is never reported without the identity-tracking weakness attached to it.

entries.label: Interaction with an off-screen subject
entries.description: The visible subject is clearly interacting with someone outside the frame.
entries.frame_evidence: A subject speaking, gesturing, or reaching toward a frame edge with nothing visible there.
entries.detector_note: Composite: mouth activity or a directed gesture present, gaze/pointing bearing exiting the frame, and no second subject detected in frame. Report as a composite score with each term logged.
entries.notes: Absence of a second subject can be detector failure rather than a real absence; report pose_detect_confidence so the two cases are separable downstream.

entries.label: Interception
entries.description: One subject moves to a point ahead of another's path, cutting it off.
entries.frame_evidence: A figure crossing into the space the other is heading toward.
entries.detector_note: Extrapolate B's velocity to a predicted position k cels ahead; interception when A's centroid closes on that predicted point faster than on B's current position.
entries.notes: Linear extrapolation over more than ~5 cels is unreliable in animation, where trajectories are keyframed and abrupt.

entries.label: Interpersonal distance (shoulder-width units)
entries.description: The same gap expressed in the subjects' own body-scale units, which cancels camera distance.
entries.frame_evidence: Two bodies separated by roughly N shoulder-widths of clear background.
entries.detector_note: distance_px / mean(shoulder_span_px_a, shoulder_span_px_b), where shoulder_span is |L11 - L12| in pixels.
entries.notes: Breaks when a subject is in strong perspective foreshortening (shoulders edge-on shrink the denominator and inflate distance).

entries.label: Interpersonal distance (frame-relative)
entries.description: The centre-to-centre distance between two subjects expressed in frame-diagonal units.
entries.frame_evidence: The visible gap between two bodies measured across the frame.
entries.detector_note: Euclidean distance between hip-midpoints (mean of landmarks 23,24) of the two poses, divided by sqrt(W^2+H^2); emit alongside the shoulder-normalised version.
entries.notes: Frame-relative distance conflates 'they moved apart' with 'the camera pushed in'; always pair with the shoulder-normalised metric and with a camera-motion flag.

entries.label: Joint attention on a third target
entries.description: Both subjects look at the same off-body target, the geometry of 'they are both watching that'.
entries.frame_evidence: Two faces aimed along converging lines toward a common point in the frame or off-screen.
entries.detector_note: Intersect the two gaze rays in image space; joint attention if the intersection lies inside the frame (or plausibly beyond an edge) and both angular residuals < 20 degrees, while neither ray lands on the other subject.
entries.notes: 2D ray intersection is not 3D intersection; two people looking at different objects along the same screen bearing produce a false positive. Confidence should scale with the intersection angle (near-parallel rays are unresolvable).

entries.label: Joint attention, VLM adjudication
entries.description: A VLM ruling on whether both characters are looking at the same thing.
entries.frame_evidence: Two characters and a candidate target visible together in one crop.
entries.detector_note: Crop the convex hull of both subjects plus the candidate target region, pad 10%, ask qwen2.5vl on the crop.
entries.vlm_question: Are both characters in this image looking at the same thing? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Ask only when a candidate target is already in the crop; an unbounded question invites confabulation.

entries.label: Kick landing
entries.description: A leg strike making contact with the partner.
entries.frame_evidence: An extended leg terminating at the partner's body with impact effects at the contact point.
entries.detector_note: Ankle landmark (27/28) speed > 3x the torso ROI mean via cv2.calcOpticalFlowFarneback inside the ankle ROI, knee angle extending, terminal ankle position inside B's mask.
entries.notes: All temporal deltas must be indexed on UNIQUE CELS (dedupe consecutive frames by mean abs diff < 0.5/255 before differencing); on 2s/3s animation a raw per-frame delta of zero is a duplicate-frame artefact.

entries.label: Kiss
entries.description: Mouth-to-mouth or mouth-to-body contact between subjects.
entries.frame_evidence: Two heads tilted into each other with faces merged at the mouths and no gap between the head silhouettes.
entries.detector_note: Detect the geometric precondition first (head landmark 0 distance < 0.6 head-widths with heads counter-rotated), then crop the two heads only, upscale to 448px, and ask qwen2.5vl on that crop.
entries.vlm_question: Are these two characters kissing, with their lips touching? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: In profile the geometry of a kiss, a whisper, and a bite are the same; the VLM is the only separator and it is not reliable on stylised art. Gate on the geometric precondition to keep the query count sane. | TIER CORRECTED by completeness critic: All landmark, i.e. inferred from 2D landmark proximity and silhouette overlap. The same shard marks interaction_social.cel_flat_contact_ambiguity as unsupported and provides a whole contact_verification_cues group precis

entries.label: Knockback
entries.description: The struck subject is driven backwards along the attack line.
entries.frame_evidence: A body translating away from the attacker over several cels immediately after an impact frame.
entries.detector_note: Post-impact centroid displacement > 0.5 shoulder-units within 4 unique cels, direction cosine to the attack vector > 0.7, with the victim's feet leaving their pre-impact ground positions.

entries.label: Knockdown
entries.description: A struck subject goes to the ground.
entries.frame_evidence: A body's centroid dropping to the bottom of its own historic range and its torso axis going horizontal.
entries.detector_note: Hip-midpoint descending > 0.3 body heights while the torso axis rotates past 60 degrees from vertical, held >= 3 unique cels.

entries.label: Leading (one subject ahead, other follows)
entries.description: The complement of following, attributing the front role.
entries.frame_evidence: One figure ahead, glancing back or setting the pace for the one behind.
entries.detector_note: Same path-match machinery as following, with the role assignment from the sign of the lag; corroborate with the leader's occasional head-turn back toward the follower.

entries.label: Line / queue formation
entries.description: Subjects arranged along a straight line.
entries.frame_evidence: Figures evenly spaced along one screen axis or a receding perspective line.
entries.detector_note: Fit a line to the subject centroids with numpy.polyfit degree 1; require R^2 > 0.9 with >= 3 subjects and roughly uniform spacing (spacing std / mean < 0.3).
entries.notes: Any two subjects are collinear by definition; require >= 3.

entries.label: Listener head shake (negation beat)
entries.description: The non-speaking subject shakes his head left-right.
entries.frame_evidence: The head rotating side to side across 4-10 cels with the mouth closed.
entries.detector_note: Head yaw oscillation of amplitude > 8 degrees with at least two zero crossings within 10 unique cels, mouth activity low.

entries.label: Listener nod (agreement beat)
entries.description: The non-speaking subject nods, a backchannel response.
entries.frame_evidence: The head dipping down and returning across 3-6 cels while the mouth stays closed.
entries.detector_note: Head pitch (FaceLandmarker transformation matrix) oscillation: one down-up cycle of amplitude > 6 degrees within <= 8 unique cels, with mouth activity below threshold.
entries.notes: Camera shake and walking bob produce the same pitch oscillation; subtract the global background flow first.

entries.label: Listener reaction shot
entries.description: A shot that cuts to the non-speaking subject to show his response.
entries.frame_evidence: A single-subject shot with a closed mouth and changing facial expression, framed close, following a speaking shot.
entries.detector_note: Shot with subject_count == 1, mouth-activity near zero, and non-zero facial change (mean abs delta of the 478 face landmarks over unique cels above the shot noise floor), immediately following a shot with a detected speaker.
entries.notes: Needs the shot-boundary list and shot ordering; on its own a frame cannot be a reaction shot.

entries.label: Looking down at the other
entries.description: The taller or elevated subject's head pitches down toward the lower one.
entries.frame_evidence: A face tilted forward, chin dropped, aimed at a head below it.
entries.detector_note: Head pitch < -10 degrees while the partner's head is lower by > 0.2 body heights.

entries.label: Looking up at the other
entries.description: The lower subject's head pitches up toward the taller one.
entries.frame_evidence: A face tilted back with the chin raised, aimed at a head above it.
entries.detector_note: Head pitch from FaceLandmarker transformation matrix > +10 degrees while the partner's head is higher in frame by > 0.2 body heights.

entries.label: Looming over the other subject
entries.description: One subject occupies a dominating position above and close to the other.
entries.frame_evidence: A large figure filling the upper frame with a smaller one beneath it, close in.
entries.detector_note: Head-height delta > 0.35 body heights, distance_shoulder_units < 1.5, and the upper subject's apparent scale larger than the lower subject's.

entries.label: Camera angle asymmetry on the pair
entries.description: The camera looks up at one subject and down at the other across a shot pair.
entries.frame_evidence: One shot with the horizon low and the subject towering, the reverse shot with the horizon high.
entries.detector_note: Requires camera-pose estimation across shots; no calibration, no depth, and no installed structure-from-motion. (Project note: COLMAP was deliberately not built.)
entries.notes: Explicit blind spot. Vanishing-point heuristics on architecture would work only on shots that happen to contain strong architectural lines, which is not a general detector.

entries.label: Lunge / sudden distance collapse
entries.description: A rapid single-beat collapse of the gap, the opening move of a grab, tackle or strike.
entries.frame_evidence: Two or three cels in which the gap goes from open to zero, often with smear frames or speed lines in 2D.
entries.detector_note: Per-unique-cel |delta distance_shoulder_units| > 1.0 in a single cel step, or > 2.5 over 3 cels, ending in overlap.
entries.notes: On 2s/3s animation a single cel step is 2-3 frames of screen time; report rates per cel AND per second so the number is interpretable.

entries.label: Mesh interpenetration at contact
entries.description: A CG-specific defect where one character's geometry passes through the other's instead of deforming against it.
entries.frame_evidence: A hand or limb whose silhouette terminates abruptly inside the other body with no occlusion boundary or contact shadow.
entries.detector_note: Crop the contact ROI at high zoom (per THE CROP RULE) and ask the Qwen3-VL judge via vlm_inspector.py; qwen2.5vl on the same crop is the cheap first pass. VLM bounding boxes come back normalised 0-1000 and must be rescaled to the crop.
entries.vlm_question: Is one character's hand or limb passing through the other character's body instead of resting on it? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Small VLMs score clean contacts as clipping and vice versa; this needs a hand-labelled calibration set before its positives mean anything. A pure-geometry version would need the source scene, which the analyzer never has.

entries.label: Monologue (one speaker, silent listener)
entries.description: One subject speaks continuously while the other never takes a turn on screen.
entries.frame_evidence: One mouth active across a long run, the other closed throughout.
entries.detector_note: Speaker index constant with zero alternations over >= 20 unique cels while both subjects remain tracked.
entries.notes: On 2D cel art this depends on interaction_social.mouth_flap_2d, which is model-tier (no anime face detector installed); report NOT DETECTABLE for drawn footage rather than a zero.

entries.label: 2D mouth-flap state
entries.description: The discrete open/mid/closed mouth drawing used by limited animation for dialogue.
entries.frame_evidence: A small dark mouth shape switching between three canonical drawings on 2s or 3s.
entries.detector_note: The area math is trivial (skimage.filters.threshold_otsu on a mouth ROI, area quantised on UNIQUE-CEL indices), but SEEDING the mouth ROI on drawn faces needs an anime face detector (lbpcascade_animeface / YOLO-anime class) that is NOT installed; mediapipe FaceLandmarker does not reliably land on cel-art faces.
entries.notes: This is the load-bearing blind spot for 2D dialogue: without a seeded mouth ROI, every turn-taking entry below is photoreal-only. A workable hybrid is one VLM crop per shot to seed the ROI, then deterministic tracking of that ROI across unique cels. Optical flow between duplicate frames is exactly zero and that zero is an artefact, not a measurement.

entries.label: Mouth open state per subject
entries.description: Whether each subject's mouth is open, the atomic unit of speech inference.
entries.frame_evidence: Visible gap between the lips, drawn as a filled shape in 2D.
entries.detector_note: FaceLandmarker blendshape 'jawOpen' > 0.25, corroborated by the inner-lip vertical distance (landmarks 13 to 14 of the 478-mesh) normalised by inter-ocular distance.
entries.notes: On anime the mouth is often drawn as a solid dark shape with no lip landmarks; use the 2D-specific entry instead.

entries.label: Mutual gaze (eye contact)
entries.description: Both subjects' gaze rays land on each other's head region at the same time.
entries.frame_evidence: Two faces turned toward each other with both sets of pupils aimed across the gap.
entries.detector_note: Angular error between A's gaze ray and the vector from A's head to B's head < 15 degrees, and symmetrically for B, sustained over >= 2 unique cels.
entries.notes: In 2D this must fall back to the VLM entry; landmark gaze on cel art has no validated error model here.

entries.label: Eye contact, VLM adjudication
entries.description: A VLM ruling on eye contact, the primary detector for 2D where iris landmarks are unreliable.
entries.frame_evidence: Two faces close enough in one crop to read both sets of eyes.
entries.detector_note: Crop the bounding box of the two head regions only (from pose landmarks 0-10 per subject) with 25% padding and upscale to 512px; ask qwen2.5vl. THE CROP RULE: never ask this on the full frame.
entries.vlm_question: Are these two characters looking directly at each other? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: The most common VLM failure here is answering yes for any two faces pointed roughly inward; establish the false-positive rate on a hand-labelled set before enabling.

entries.label: Mutual vs one-sided contact
entries.description: Whether both subjects are actively reaching into the contact or only one is.
entries.frame_evidence: Both characters' arms extended into the shared space, versus one passive arm hanging at the side.
entries.detector_note: Compare each subject's hand-to-partner distance and hand motion energy over the pre-contact window; one-sided if one subject's hand motion is below the shot noise floor.

entries.label: Head nod toward the partner
entries.description: A single acknowledging head dip aimed at the other subject.
entries.frame_evidence: One downward-upward head motion with the face oriented at the partner.
entries.detector_note: One head-pitch cycle of amplitude 5-15 degrees within <= 6 unique cels while head bearing points at the partner.

entries.label: Object arriving from off-screen
entries.description: A projectile or thrown item enters the frame from an edge toward the subject.
entries.frame_evidence: A small fast blob entering at a border on a straight path toward the visible subject.
entries.detector_note: Camera-compensated frame differencing; a fast blob whose track's first detection is within 3% of a frame border and whose fitted line points at the subject's mask.
entries.notes: Foreground scenery passing in a moving-camera shot behaves identically; the camera compensation is what separates them.

entries.label: Object occupying the space between two hands
entries.description: A distinct region held between the two subjects' hands, the substrate of a handoff.
entries.frame_evidence: A small non-skin, non-background blob bridging one character's hand and the other's.
entries.detector_note: Reliable detection needs a general object detector (YOLO-class) which is not installed. A crude proxy: a connected component in the gap ROI that is neither background (frame-median model) nor either subject's segmentation mask.
entries.notes: Marked model because the proxy fires on clothing, hair and shadows; report it as a candidate only.

entries.label: Object handoff between subjects
entries.description: An object passes from one subject's hand to the other's.
entries.frame_evidence: A held blob moving with hand A, a cel where both hands touch it, then the blob moving with hand B.
entries.detector_note: Requires object tracking (detector + tracker) to attribute the blob to a hand before and after; cv2.TrackerCSRT can follow a seeded blob but nothing installed can seed it reliably.
entries.notes: The geometric shell (hands meeting then separating) IS detectable at landmark tier; only the object attribution is not. Emit the shell separately so the blind spot is explicit.

entries.label: Object thrown between subjects
entries.description: A small object travels ballistically from one subject toward the other.
entries.frame_evidence: A small blob on a smooth arcing path across consecutive cels, leaving one hand and heading toward the other subject.
entries.detector_note: Detect small fast movers by background-subtracted frame differencing (cv2.absdiff on registered cels), filter blobs by area and speed, then fit a parabola to the centroid track with numpy.polyfit; require fit residual below threshold and endpoints near the two subjects' hands.
entries.notes: Camera motion must be compensated first (cv2.estimateAffinePartial2D between cels) or every static object appears to fly. Motion-blurred or smear-drawn projectiles break the centroid track.

entries.label: Handoff, VLM adjudication
entries.description: A VLM ruling on whether one character is giving something to the other.
entries.frame_evidence: Two hands meeting with something between them.
entries.detector_note: Crop the hands-and-gap ROI (union of both wrists plus 30% padding), upscale to 448px, ask qwen2.5vl on the crop.
entries.vlm_question: Is one person handing an object to the other person in this image? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: This is the only route to handoff detection today; expect it to answer yes for any two adjacent hands.

entries.label: One faces the other's back
entries.description: Asymmetric orientation: A is turned toward B, B is turned away.
entries.frame_evidence: One character's chest aimed at the other character's shoulder blades.
entries.detector_note: facing_cos_a > 0.6 while facing_cos_b < -0.3.

entries.label: One-sided gaze
entries.description: A looks at B while B looks elsewhere.
entries.frame_evidence: One face aimed at the partner, the partner's face aimed off-axis or down.
entries.detector_note: gaze_error_a < 15 degrees while gaze_error_b > 35 degrees, sustained >= 2 unique cels.

entries.label: Open vs closed body posture toward the partner
entries.description: Whether a subject's arms and torso are open toward the partner or crossed/shielded.
entries.frame_evidence: Arms crossed over the chest and shoulders drawn in, versus arms loose at the sides with the chest exposed.
entries.detector_note: Wrists (15,16) inside the torso quad (11,12,24,23) and elbows abducted -> closed; wrist-to-hip distance > 0.5 shoulder span with chest normal toward partner -> open.
entries.notes: Cannot distinguish crossed arms from holding an object against the chest; that separation needs the object detector we lack.

entries.label: Over-the-shoulder framing
entries.description: A foreground subject's shoulder/head occupies a frame edge while the background subject faces camera-ward.
entries.frame_evidence: A large out-of-focus or cropped shoulder and back-of-head in the corner, a second full face beyond it.
entries.detector_note: One pose with a large scale and bbox clipped by a frame edge and its head landmarks (0,7,8) showing back-of-head (nose visibility low, both ears similar visibility), plus a second smaller frontal pose.
entries.notes: Shallow depth of field blurs the foreground shoulder past landmarking in live action; this fails silently there.

entries.label: Pace matching (walking together)
entries.description: Two subjects walk at matched speed and, sometimes, matched gait phase.
entries.frame_evidence: Two figures moving abreast with their strides visibly in or out of phase.
entries.detector_note: Speed ratio within [0.85, 1.15] over >= 10 unique cels; separately cross-correlate the two ankle-oscillation series and report the phase lag against a circular-shift null.
entries.notes: Gait phase requires enough temporal resolution; at 8 unique drawings per second a full stride is 4-6 samples and the phase estimate is coarse. All temporal deltas must be indexed on UNIQUE CELS (dedupe consecutive frames by mean abs diff < 0.5/255 before differencing); on 2s/3s animation a raw per-frame delta of zero is a duplicate-frame artefact.

entries.label: Pair centroid convergence
entries.description: Both subjects move toward a common midpoint, i.e. mutual approach rather than one-sided.
entries.frame_evidence: Both bodies translating inward toward the space between them.
entries.detector_note: Both centroid velocity vectors have positive dot product with the vector to the pair midpoint, and both magnitudes exceed 0.2 shoulder-units/cel.

entries.label: Null model for pair-interaction metrics
entries.description: The permutation baseline every correlation-based interaction claim in this domain is scored against.
entries.frame_evidence: Not a visual feature: the distribution of the same statistic under randomised pairing or randomised time offset.
entries.detector_note: For each correlation/synchrony metric, recompute it 200 times with one subject's time series circularly shifted (and, where >= 3 subjects exist, with pair identities permuted); report the observed value's percentile.
entries.notes: A detector with no null model produces confident numbers that mean nothing. Any entry emitting a correlation, a synchrony score, or an alternation count MUST carry its percentile or be reported as NOT DETECTABLE.

entries.label: Off-screen partner visible in a reflection
entries.description: A second subject appears only as a reflection in a mirror, window, or water.
entries.frame_evidence: A person-shaped region inside a bounded reflective surface, often mirrored and lower contrast.
entries.detector_note: Crop candidate reflective regions (low-saturation, high-planarity rectangles are not detectable reliably, so in practice: crop any secondary person-like detection) and ask qwen2.5vl on the crop.
entries.vlm_question: Is the person in this image a reflection in a mirror or window, rather than a real person? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Pose landmarkers happily detect reflections as real subjects, so this entry exists mainly to catch a systematic false-positive source in the subject-count entries.

entries.label: Off-screen partner implied by a cast shadow
entries.description: A second figure's shadow falls into frame while the figure itself is off-screen.
entries.frame_evidence: A human-shaped dark region on the ground or wall with no corresponding body in frame.
entries.detector_note: Would need a shadow segmenter plus a human-shape classifier on the shadow mask; neither is installed. A crude proxy (dark connected component with a vertical aspect ratio that moves coherently) is far too generic to be trustworthy.
entries.notes: Logged as a blind spot: the proxy fires on every dark object in a moving scene.

entries.label: Back pat
entries.description: Repeated hand contact on the partner's back, usually during or after an embrace.
entries.frame_evidence: A hand striking lightly against the far side of the other character's torso, repeatedly.
entries.detector_note: Wrist on the far side of B's torso axis with >= 2 contact-retreat cycles; require torso overlap (an embrace context).
entries.notes: Almost entirely occluded during a hug; expect low recall.

entries.label: Head pat
entries.description: A repeated light hand contact on top of the partner's head.
entries.frame_evidence: A hand descending onto the other character's crown and lifting, twice or more.
entries.detector_note: A's wrist above B's landmark 0 within 0.4 head-widths horizontally, with >= 2 vertical approach-retreat cycles over <= 10 unique cels.
entries.notes: Very common in anime and usually drawn on 3s; the cycle count must be computed on unique cels or it is halved.

entries.label: Space intrusion (one-sided closure)
entries.description: One subject enters the other's near zone while the other does not reciprocate or retreats.
entries.frame_evidence: One body advancing into the frame space the other occupies, the other's posture unchanged or shrinking.
entries.detector_note: Approach event by A into distance_shoulder_units < 1.0 with B's centroid displacement < 0.5x A's, or B showing a simultaneous retreat/recoil.
entries.notes: Reads as intrusion only with a social prior; the analyzer should log the asymmetric geometry and not the intent.

entries.label: Deference posture toward the other
entries.description: Bowing, kneeling, or head-lowering directed at the other subject.
entries.frame_evidence: One figure lowered or bent toward a standing figure, head below the other's chest.
entries.detector_note: Bow or kneel detected (knee angle < 100 degrees or torso pitch > 25 degrees) with the bend direction toward the other subject and the head below the other's shoulder line.
entries.notes: The social reading is an inference; the analyzer should report the geometry and label it as a posture, not a meaning.

entries.label: Piggyback / shoulder carry
entries.description: One subject rides on the other's back or shoulders.
entries.frame_evidence: One torso stacked above and behind the other, arms over the carrier's shoulders.
entries.detector_note: B's hip-midpoint above A's shoulder line, B's wrists forward of A's shoulders (11/12), masks intersecting.
entries.notes: Pose landmarkers frequently fuse the two stacked bodies into one skeleton with impossible limb lengths; validate limb-length consistency and discard fused detections.

entries.label: Pointing off-screen
entries.description: A subject points at something outside the frame.
entries.frame_evidence: An extended arm aimed at a frame edge with nothing in the frame along its ray.
entries.detector_note: Pointing ray exits the frame with no subject or salient blob within 0.15 frame-diagonals of the ray inside frame.

entries.label: Pointing at another subject
entries.description: One subject points a finger or hand at another.
entries.frame_evidence: An extended arm with an index finger aimed along the line toward the other character.
entries.detector_note: Elbow angle > 150 degrees; pointing ray from the elbow (13/14) through the index landmark (19/20), or from HandLandmarker landmarks 5->8; angular error to the A->B vector < 15 degrees, held >= 2 unique cels.
entries.notes: An extended arm holding something reads as a point; the index-finger extension check from HandLandmarker is what separates them, and it needs a large enough hand in frame.

entries.label: Posture openness asymmetry between subjects
entries.description: One subject's posture is expansive while the other's is contracted.
entries.frame_evidence: One figure with arms and stance wide, the other with limbs pulled in.
entries.detector_note: Compare per-subject convex-hull area of landmarks normalised by shoulder span squared; report the ratio.
entries.notes: Convex-hull area is view-dependent: a subject in profile always scores lower than one facing camera.

entries.label: Intimate zone
entries.description: The two subjects are inside touching range of each other.
entries.frame_evidence: Bodies overlapping or with a gap narrower than roughly half a shoulder width.
entries.detector_note: distance_shoulder_units < 0.75 sustained over >=2 unique cels; equivalently pair_bbox_iou > 0.1 with similar apparent scale.
entries.notes: Zone thresholds are conventions, not measurements. Report the continuous distance as primary and the zone label as derived.

entries.label: Personal zone
entries.description: Conversational close range: about arm's length between subjects.
entries.frame_evidence: A gap of roughly one to two shoulder widths, both subjects fully separated but close.
entries.detector_note: 0.75 <= distance_shoulder_units < 2.5 over >=2 unique cels.
entries.notes: Same convention caveat as the intimate zone.

entries.label: Public zone
entries.description: Subjects share the frame but are far apart, typical of address, standoff, or establishing shots.
entries.frame_evidence: Two small figures at opposite regions of a wide frame with landscape between them.
entries.detector_note: distance_shoulder_units >= 5.5; also flag when both subjects occupy < 5% of frame area each.

entries.label: Social zone
entries.description: Formal or group range where subjects are clearly separated but co-present.
entries.frame_evidence: Two to roughly five shoulder widths of clear ground between subjects.
entries.detector_note: 2.5 <= distance_shoulder_units < 5.5 over >=2 unique cels.

entries.label: Pull / yank
entries.description: One subject applies force that drags the other toward him.
entries.frame_evidence: A gripped arm or garment with the gripped subject's body accelerating toward the gripper.
entries.detector_note: Contact maintained while B's centroid accelerates toward A and A's elbow angle decreases (flexion) over the same cels.

entries.label: Punch landing
entries.description: A closed-fist strike making contact with the partner.
entries.frame_evidence: A fist at the end of an extended arm coincident with the partner's body, with an impact flash or deformation.
entries.detector_note: Wrist speed peak > 4x torso mean, elbow angle extending past 150 degrees at the peak cel, terminal wrist position inside B's mask, plus an impact-frame luminance spike.
entries.notes: In 2D the contact frame is frequently a white flash with no readable bodies; the pose detector returns nothing on it. Detect the flash separately and stitch the pre/post cels.

entries.label: Pursuit gap closing or opening
entries.description: Whether the pursuer is gaining or losing ground.
entries.frame_evidence: The separation between two running figures narrowing or widening over the shot.
entries.detector_note: linregress of distance_shoulder_units against unique-cel index inside a detected chase window; report slope, sign and predicted intercept cel.

entries.label: Push / shove
entries.description: One subject applies force that displaces the other away.
entries.frame_evidence: Extended arms against the other's chest, followed by that subject accelerating backwards.
entries.detector_note: Contact at B's torso by A's hands, A's elbow angle increasing (extension) across the contact cels, and B's centroid acceleration away from A exceeding 3x its pre-contact value within 3 unique cels.
entries.notes: Requires the acceleration to be measured on unique cels; All temporal deltas must be indexed on UNIQUE CELS (dedupe consecutive frames by mean abs diff < 0.5/255 before differencing); on 2s/3s animation a raw per-frame delta of zero is a duplicate-frame artefact.

entries.label: Raised palm / stop gesture
entries.description: An open palm held toward the partner, arresting or warding.
entries.frame_evidence: A flat hand presented face-on toward the other character, fingers up.
entries.detector_note: HandLandmarker: all fingers extended (fingertip-to-wrist distances near maximum), palm normal within 30 degrees of the A->B vector, held >= 3 unique cels with low wrist speed.

entries.label: Ranged attack trajectory between subjects
entries.description: A projectile or beam travelling from one subject toward another.
entries.frame_evidence: A streak, bolt or small fast blob on a straight line from one figure to the other.
entries.detector_note: Camera-compensated frame differencing to isolate fast movers, then a straight-line fit (numpy.polyfit) whose endpoints lie near subject A's hands and subject B's body; alternatively a persistent high-contrast streak detected by Hough.
entries.notes: A beam drawn as a single long streak exists in one cel and has no trajectory to fit; handle the streak case separately from the moving-blob case.

entries.label: Collective reaction to an off-screen event
entries.description: Several visible subjects react at once toward the same off-screen direction.
entries.frame_evidence: All heads snapping toward the same frame edge within a cel or two of each other.
entries.detector_note: Head-yaw derivative of >= 2 subjects exceeding threshold in the SAME direction within a 3-unique-cel window; report the synchrony against a shuffled-onset null.
entries.notes: A whip pan makes every head appear to turn at once; subtract the global background flow before differencing head yaw.

entries.label: Reach and grasp toward the partner
entries.description: The receiving subject extends and closes a hand at the exchange point.
entries.frame_evidence: A second arm entering the gap, fingers opening then closing at the meeting point.
entries.detector_note: Reaching arm extension plus a hand-aperture drop from mediapipe HandLandmarker (mean fingertip-to-wrist distance, landmarks 4/8/12/16/20 to 0) falling > 25% within 3 unique cels at the meeting point.
entries.notes: HandLandmarker needs the hand to be reasonably large in frame; at wide framings it returns nothing.

entries.label: Recoil / flinch back
entries.description: A fast involuntary-looking increase in distance, typically a reaction to the partner's action.
entries.frame_evidence: Torso pitching away from the partner with the rear foot planting, over 2-4 cels.
entries.detector_note: Opening trend with peak rate > 0.8 shoulder-units/cel AND torso lean angle (shoulder-midpoint to hip-midpoint vector) tilting away from the partner by > 10 degrees within the same window.
entries.notes: Distinguishing recoil from a normal step back needs the trigger event; without it, report kinematics only.

entries.label: Facing relation, VLM adjudication
entries.description: A VLM ruling on who faces whom, used when landmark front/back disambiguation is low-confidence.
entries.frame_evidence: Two characters whose orientation is obvious to a human but whose skeletons are ambiguous.
entries.detector_note: Crop the union bbox of both subjects with 15% padding, upscale to at least 640px, ask qwen2.5vl; escalate to the Qwen3-VL judge in vlm_inspector.py for contested shots.
entries.vlm_question: In this image, are the two characters facing each other, facing the same direction, or facing away from each other? Answer with exactly one of: facing each other, same direction, facing away.
entries.notes: Small VLMs default to 'facing each other' for any two-shot; run a null check on shots known to be same-direction before trusting the positive rate.

entries.label: Restrain / pin
entries.description: One subject holds the other immobile, typically against the ground or a wall.
entries.frame_evidence: One body pressed flat with the other above it, the pinned subject's limbs static under contact.
entries.detector_note: Sustained contact while the pinned subject's landmark motion energy falls below 20% of the pinner's for >= 6 unique cels.
entries.notes: A held drawing gives both subjects zero motion; require the pinner to be moving so the ratio is defined.

entries.label: Retreat / backing away
entries.description: One subject moves away from the other, opening the gap.
entries.frame_evidence: One body translating away, often still facing the partner (backing up rather than turning to leave).
entries.detector_note: Opening trend with the mover's velocity direction cosine to the B->A vector < -0.7; check head yaw to separate backing-away-facing from turning-and-leaving.
entries.notes: Same camera-motion confound as approach.

entries.label: Salute or other codified gesture
entries.description: A culturally codified directed gesture (salute, prayer bow, specific hand sign).
entries.frame_evidence: A hand brought to the brow, or palms pressed together, aimed at the other subject.
entries.detector_note: Crop the gesturing subject's upper body, upscale to 448px, ask qwen2.5vl.
entries.vlm_question: Is this character performing a formal salute with a hand raised to the forehead? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Codified gestures are a long tail; one closed question per gesture type is the only workable form, so coverage is limited to whatever list is enumerated.

entries.label: Both subjects on the same ground plane
entries.description: Whether the two subjects' feet rest on a common ground line, a weak depth-consistency check for proxemic distance.
entries.frame_evidence: Two sets of feet meeting the floor at heights consistent with one receding plane.
entries.detector_note: Fit a line to all detected foot landmarks (29-32) across subjects and across the shot; a subject whose feet sit far off that line is at a different depth or elevation. Report the per-subject residual.
entries.notes: Assumes a single flat floor and a roughly level camera; stairs, slopes, low angles and floating characters break it. The residual is a flag for 'proxemic distance may be wrong', not a depth measurement.

entries.label: Object held by both subjects
entries.description: Both subjects grip the same object at once, as in a tug-of-war or a joint carry.
entries.frame_evidence: One elongated object with a hand from each character at opposite ends.
entries.detector_note: Needs object detection to establish the object's extent; the landmark shell (two wrists at a fixed separation moving as a rigid pair) is detectable but does not prove an object.
entries.notes: The rigid-pair shell is a genuinely useful proxy; report it as 'rigid link between hands', not as 'shared object'.

entries.label: Shielding another with the body
entries.description: One subject covers another with his own body, e.g. bending over a fallen figure.
entries.frame_evidence: One body arched over or pressed in front of another, the covered one largely occluded.
entries.detector_note: Sustained mask overlap where the near subject occludes > 50% of the far subject's landmark set while the near subject's torso is oriented away from the far one (facing the threat direction).
entries.notes: Heavy occlusion means the covered subject's pose is mostly missing; the finding rests on the disappearance itself, which is also what a subject leaving frame looks like.

entries.label: Shot / reverse-shot pattern
entries.description: The alternating single-subject shot structure that carries most screen dialogue.
entries.frame_evidence: Alternating shots of two different subjects at mirrored framings and complementary eyelines.
entries.detector_note: Over a shot sequence: alternating single-subject shots whose subject appearance histograms differ and whose gaze bearings have opposite screen sign; requires shot boundaries and at least a coarse subject appearance signature (cv2.calcHist on the torso ROI in HSV).
entries.notes: Without ReID the 'same subject returns' claim rests on a colour histogram, which fails on similarly-dressed characters.

entries.label: Side-by-side adjacency
entries.description: Two subjects standing or moving abreast, shoulders roughly level and aligned.
entries.frame_evidence: Two bodies at the same depth with their shoulder lines colinear and a small horizontal gap.
entries.detector_note: Hip-midpoint y-difference < 0.15 of mean body height, distance_shoulder_units < 2.0, and both shoulder-line normals pointing within 30 degrees of each other.
entries.notes: MediaPipe pose/face landmarkers are trained on photoreal humans; on 2D cel art recall drops hard (large eyes, missing nose shading, non-anatomical proportions), so a NOT-FOUND on drawn footage is usually detector failure, not absence. Log pose_detect_confidence_mean alongside every verdict.

entries.label: Overlapping speech / interruption
entries.description: Both subjects' mouths move in the same window, the visual sign of talking over each other.
entries.frame_evidence: Two mouths open and changing shape in the same cels.
entries.detector_note: Both mouth-activity binaries true for >= 3 consecutive unique cels; flag the onset cel as the interruption point.
entries.notes: Laughing, eating and shouting crowds all trigger this; it is a co-activity finding, not a speech finding. On 2D cel art this depends on interaction_social.mouth_flap_2d, which is model-tier (no anime face detector installed); report NOT DETECTABLE for drawn footage rather than a zero.

entries.label: Slap
entries.description: An open-hand strike to the partner's face or body.
entries.frame_evidence: An arm swinging across frame, an impact cel with the head snapping aside, often a flash or impact star in 2D.
entries.detector_note: High wrist speed (> 4x the torso ROI mean speed) terminating within 0.3 head-widths of B's head, followed within 2 unique cels by B's head yaw or position changing > 15 degrees / 0.1 head-widths.
entries.notes: The strike itself is often drawn as a smear or skipped entirely between two cels; the reliable evidence is the before/after pair, not the contact frame.

entries.label: Which subject is speaking
entries.description: Attributing the current speech activity to one of the visible subjects.
entries.frame_evidence: One character's mouth moving across successive cels while the other's stays static.
entries.detector_note: Per-subject mouth-open variance over a 10-unique-cel window; the speaker is the subject whose variance exceeds 3x the other's and exceeds the shot's own noise floor.
entries.notes: Purely visual: an off-screen or non-moving-mouth speaker is invisible to this. Do not call it 'dialogue' without audio. On 2D cel art this depends on interaction_social.mouth_flap_2d, which is model-tier (no anime face detector installed); report NOT DETECTABLE for drawn footage rather than a zero.

entries.label: Shouting vs murmuring
entries.description: How forcefully a subject appears to be speaking.
entries.frame_evidence: A wide-open mouth with a strained face and forward head thrust, versus a barely-parted mouth.
entries.detector_note: Crop to the speaker's head with 20% padding, upscale to 448px, ask qwen2.5vl.
entries.vlm_question: Is this character shouting with a wide open mouth? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: The jawOpen blendshape gives a cheaper continuous proxy on photoreal faces; the VLM is for cel art where blendshapes fail.

entries.label: Squared-off (confrontational) stance
entries.description: Both subjects fully frontal to each other with feet planted, a confrontation geometry.
entries.frame_evidence: Two bodies chest-on with shoulder lines parallel and both sets of feet spread and planted.
entries.detector_note: mutual_facing_score > 0.85, shoulder lines parallel within 15 degrees, and ankle separation (27-28) > 0.8x shoulder span on both subjects.

entries.label: Stagger and recovery
entries.description: The struck subject loses and regains balance.
entries.frame_evidence: The torso tilting off vertical then righting over several cels, feet shuffling.
