entries.detector_note: Torso axis (shoulder-mid to hip-mid) deviating from vertical by > 20 degrees and returning to within 8 degrees within 10 unique cels, with foot repositioning.
entries.notes: Cannot distinguish a stagger from a deliberate lean or a dance step without the preceding impact.

entries.label: Straggler / subject lagging the group
entries.description: A subject falling behind the group's motion.
entries.frame_evidence: One figure trailing the moving mass with a growing gap.
entries.detector_note: Subject whose projection onto the group velocity vector is the minimum AND whose distance to the group centroid grows with a positive linregress slope over >= 8 unique cels.

entries.label: Strike extension (the attack itself)
entries.description: The limb accelerates toward the opponent.
entries.frame_evidence: A limb whipping across frame toward the other body, often with a smear or multiple-image drawing in 2D.
entries.detector_note: Limb endpoint speed > 4x the torso ROI mean speed with velocity direction cosine toward the opponent > 0.7; measure the ROI speeds with cv2.calcOpticalFlowFarneback inside the limb ROIs.
entries.notes: On smear frames the limb has no pose landmark at all; fall back to the flow-magnitude peak in the region between the two bodies.

entries.label: Strike wind-up (anticipation)
entries.description: The preparatory motion before a strike: the limb draws back away from the target.
entries.frame_evidence: An arm or leg pulled back and the torso coiled, one to three cels before the attack.
entries.detector_note: Limb endpoint (wrist 15/16 or ankle 27/28) velocity directed AWAY from the opponent immediately before a velocity reversal, with the torso rotating opposite to the coming strike.
entries.notes: Animation anticipation is often a single held cel; at 3s that is one sample and the velocity is undefined. All temporal deltas must be indexed on UNIQUE CELS (dedupe consecutive frames by mean abs diff < 0.5/255 before differencing); on 2s/3s animation a raw per-frame delta of zero is a duplicate-frame artefact.

entries.label: Subject silhouette overlap
entries.description: The degree to which two subjects' image regions overlap, the raw substrate of contact and occlusion.
entries.frame_evidence: Two person regions sharing pixels, with one silhouette's outline interrupted by the other's.
entries.detector_note: Axis-aligned bbox per pose from min/max of visible landmarks; IoU plus overlap_area/min_area. Refine with PoseLandmarkerOptions(output_segmentation_masks=True) and use numpy mask AND / OR.
entries.notes: Overlap is NOT contact: a far subject standing behind a near one overlaps completely without touching.

entries.label: Subject count in frame
entries.description: How many distinct human/humanoid subjects are resolvable in the frame.
entries.frame_evidence: Two or more separated person-shaped regions each carrying an independent head-torso-limb landmark set.
entries.detector_note: mediapipe.tasks.python.vision.PoseLandmarker with PoseLandmarkerOptions(num_poses=6, min_pose_detection_confidence=0.4); count results whose mean landmark .visibility over indices 11,12,23,24 exceeds 0.5.
entries.notes: MediaPipe pose/face landmarkers are trained on photoreal humans; on 2D cel art recall drops hard (large eyes, missing nose shading, non-anatomical proportions), so a NOT-FOUND on drawn footage is usually detector failure, not absence. Log pose_detect_confidence_mean alongside every verdict. Count is a LOWER BOUND: heavily occluded and back-turned subjects are dropped.

entries.label: Subject count, VLM fallback (drawn art)
entries.description: A VLM headcount used where pose landmarking fails on stylised 2D characters.
entries.frame_evidence: Characters clearly readable as separate people to a human eye but carrying no valid pose skeleton.
entries.detector_note: Crop to the union of motion-energy blobs (dilated |frame diff| mask), upscale to 768px, ask qwen2.5vl. Per THE CROP RULE, ask on the tight crop, never the full frame.
entries.vlm_question: How many separate people or characters are in this image? Answer with a single number: 0, 1, 2, 3, or more than 3.
entries.notes: Small VLMs miscount past 3 and count reflections and background posters; treat >3 as 'many', not as a number.

entries.label: Who is in front of whom
entries.description: The near-far ordering of two overlapping subjects.
entries.frame_evidence: One subject's contour continuing unbroken across the overlap while the other's is cut off at the boundary.
entries.detector_note: Compare per-subject apparent scale (shoulder 11-12 pixel span) and the visibility drop pattern: the occluded subject loses .visibility on landmarks inside the overlap region while the occluder keeps his.
entries.notes: Fails when the two subjects are at genuinely similar depth, and when a 2D layout gives a distant character the same line weight as a near one.

entries.label: Subject enters frame
entries.description: A new subject crosses the frame border into the scene during the shot.
entries.frame_evidence: A partial body appearing at a frame edge over consecutive cels and growing toward completeness.
entries.detector_note: New pose track whose first-detection bbox touches an image border (within 2% of width/height) and whose visible-landmark count rises monotonically over the next 3 unique cels.
entries.notes: A subject 'entering' by a cut is not an entry; gate on shot boundaries from the scene-cut detector.

entries.label: Subject leaves frame
entries.description: A subject crosses out of frame, ending on-screen participation in the interaction.
entries.frame_evidence: A body shrinking against a frame edge until only a limb, then nothing, remains.
entries.detector_note: Track terminates with final bbox touching an image border and visible-landmark count falling monotonically over the preceding 3 unique cels.
entries.notes: Occlusion by scenery produces the same signature; a subject vanishing mid-frame is occlusion, not exit.

entries.label: Apparent size disparity between subjects
entries.description: One subject is drawn/rendered much larger than the other, from depth or from actual body-size difference.
entries.frame_evidence: Two subjects whose head heights differ by more than a factor of ~1.5 in the same frame.
entries.detector_note: Ratio of head-to-hip pixel length (landmark 0 to midpoint of 23/24) between the two subjects; also shoulder span ratio.
entries.notes: Cannot separate 'child next to adult' from 'adult far behind adult' without depth; report the ratio, not the cause.

entries.label: Per-subject identity track
entries.description: A stable ID for each subject across frames so that 'A touched B' means the same A throughout.
entries.frame_evidence: The same subject's bounding box moving continuously frame to frame without swapping labels with a neighbour.
entries.detector_note: Needs a ReID embedder or a proper multi-object tracker (ByteTrack/OC-SORT + appearance features); not installed. Interim: greedy Hungarian assignment on pose-centroid distance between unique cels, bridged by cv2.TrackerCSRT_create() over gaps <=5 cels.
entries.notes: This is the single biggest dependency in the domain: every 'A does X to B' entry inherits its identity-swap error. Greedy centroid assignment swaps whenever two subjects cross, which is exactly during hugs, fights and handoffs.

entries.label: Sustained stare
entries.description: One subject holds gaze on the other for an unusually long run.
entries.frame_evidence: A face held aimed at the partner across many cels with minimal head motion.
entries.detector_note: gaze_error < 20 degrees for >= 12 consecutive unique cels with head-yaw std < 5 degrees.
entries.notes: A held drawing (an anime still-frame beat) is not a stare; check that the cel index actually advances, otherwise you are measuring one drawing many times.

entries.label: Tackle / takedown
entries.description: One subject drives into the other and both go to the ground.
entries.frame_evidence: Two bodies colliding and the merged mass dropping in frame over several cels.
entries.detector_note: Contact onset followed by both subjects' hip-midpoints descending > 0.25 frame height within 8 unique cels while remaining in contact.

entries.label: Three-or-more shot
entries.description: Three or more resolvable subjects share the frame, so interaction is triadic or group-level.
entries.frame_evidence: Three or more separated torso regions with independent shoulder lines.
entries.detector_note: subject_count >= 3 from PoseLandmarker(num_poses=6); emit the full pairwise distance matrix for downstream pair selection.
entries.notes: num_poses=6 is a hard ceiling; anything denser is reported by the crowd entries, not here.

entries.label: Torso facing vector
entries.description: The direction a subject's chest points, per subject, as the substrate for all facing relations.
entries.frame_evidence: The visible chest plane and shoulder line indicating which way the body is turned.
entries.detector_note: Normal of the shoulder line (L11 -> L12) in image space, disambiguated front/back by the z-sign of landmarks 11/12 in PoseLandmarkerResult.pose_world_landmarks.
entries.notes: Front/back ambiguity is the dominant error: a back-turned subject and a front-facing one give nearly identical 2D shoulder lines, and world-landmark z is weak on stylised art.

entries.label: Hand on the partner's arm
entries.description: A hand contacting the partner's forearm or upper arm, e.g. a steadying or restraining touch.
entries.frame_evidence: Fingers wrapped around or resting on the other character's arm.
entries.detector_note: A's wrist within 0.25 shoulder-spans of B's elbow (13/14) or the 11-13 / 12-14 segment (point-to-segment distance).

entries.label: Hand to the partner's face
entries.description: A hand contacting the partner's cheek, chin, or forehead.
entries.frame_evidence: A palm or fingertips against the far character's face, faces close.
entries.detector_note: A's wrist/index landmarks within 0.3 head-widths of B's head landmarks (0,7,8) with a mask-contact confirmation.
entries.notes: Cannot separate a caress from a slap-in-progress by geometry alone; pair with the impact-frame entry.

entries.label: Hand on shoulder
entries.description: A hand placed on the partner's shoulder, a reassurance or restraint beat.
entries.frame_evidence: Fingers curled over the far character's deltoid, arm extended across the gap.
entries.detector_note: A's wrist within 0.25 shoulder-spans of B's landmark 11 or 12, with A's elbow angle (13/14) > 100 degrees (extended arm), sustained >= 2 unique cels.

entries.label: Opposed pulling on a shared link
entries.description: Both subjects pull in opposite directions against a rigid link between their hands.
entries.frame_evidence: Two bodies leaning away from each other with arms taut toward a common point.
entries.detector_note: Constant wrist separation (std < 0.1 shoulder-spans) while both torso lean angles tilt away from the link point and the centroid distance oscillates.

entries.label: Dialogue turn-taking (alternating mouth movement)
entries.description: Speech activity alternating between two subjects, the visual signature of conversation.
entries.frame_evidence: Runs of cels where A's mouth moves and B's does not, followed by runs of the reverse.
entries.detector_note: Binarise each subject's mouth-activity series on unique cels, then count sign alternations of (activity_a - activity_b); require >= 2 alternations with runs of >= 3 cels each.
entries.notes: NULL MODEL REQUIRED: shuffle the run lengths 200 times and report the percentile, otherwise chewing, laughing or breathing produce the same alternation statistic. On 2D cel art this depends on interaction_social.mouth_flap_2d, which is model-tier (no anime face detector installed); report NOT DETECTABLE for drawn footage rather than a zero.

entries.label: Turn away from the partner
entries.description: A subject rotates his body or head away from the other, a disengagement beat.
entries.frame_evidence: The face swinging from partner-ward to profile or to the back of the head over a few cels.
entries.detector_note: Same as turn-toward with the opposite sign; head-yaw component from FaceLandmarker facial_transformation_matrixes yaw where a face is resolvable.
entries.notes: All temporal deltas must be indexed on UNIQUE CELS (dedupe consecutive frames by mean abs diff < 0.5/255 before differencing); on 2s/3s animation a raw per-frame delta of zero is a duplicate-frame artefact.

entries.label: Pause between turns
entries.description: A gap where neither subject's mouth moves, between two turns.
entries.frame_evidence: Several cels with both mouths closed and held, between speech runs.
entries.detector_note: Both activity binaries false for >= 3 unique cels bounded by activity on either side; report duration in cels and in seconds using the source fps.
entries.notes: Held drawings inflate gaps; report both the cel count and the wall-clock duration so the inflation is visible. On 2D cel art this depends on interaction_social.mouth_flap_2d, which is model-tier (no anime face detector installed); report NOT DETECTABLE for drawn footage rather than a zero.

entries.label: Turn toward the partner
entries.description: A subject rotates his body or head to face the other, a re-engagement beat.
entries.frame_evidence: The shoulder span widening or the face rotating from profile toward the partner across a few cels.
entries.detector_note: d(torso_yaw)/d(unique cel) with sign toward the partner, total change > 25 degrees over <= 6 cels; corroborate with shoulder_span_px increasing (rotating to frontal).
entries.notes: All temporal deltas must be indexed on UNIQUE CELS (dedupe consecutive frames by mean abs diff < 0.5/255 before differencing); on 2s/3s animation a raw per-frame delta of zero is a duplicate-frame artefact.

entries.label: Two-shot (exactly two subjects)
entries.description: Frame contains exactly two resolvable subjects, the canonical dyadic-interaction setup.
entries.frame_evidence: Two person regions, both with visible torsos, no third head blob above the crowd-density threshold.
entries.detector_note: subject_count == 2 held over >=3 consecutive unique cels to suppress single-cel detector flicker.
entries.notes: Mirror reflections and posters of people are counted as subjects by pose landmarkers.

entries.label: Unique-cel indexing for all pair metrics
entries.description: The de-duplicated frame index on which every temporal interaction metric in this domain must be computed.
entries.frame_evidence: Consecutive frames that are byte-for-byte or near-identical drawings, held for 2 or 3 frame times.
entries.detector_note: Mean absolute difference between consecutive decoded frames; a frame is a duplicate when MAD < 0.5/255 over the non-letterbox region. Emit the unique-cel index array and the held-duration per cel.
entries.notes: Mandatory dependency for every 'short' and 'shot' entry here. Optical flow between two duplicate frames is exactly zero and that zero is an artefact, not a measurement. Compression noise can defeat the MAD test on heavily compressed sources; raise the threshold per-source and log which threshold was used.

entries.label: Wedge / V formation
entries.description: Subjects arranged in a wedge with one leading point.
entries.frame_evidence: One figure ahead and two flanking lines trailing behind it.
entries.detector_note: Centroids fitting two lines meeting at an apex; test by fitting a line to each half after sorting by projection onto the group's principal axis (numpy.linalg.svd on centred centroids).
entries.notes: Needs >= 5 subjects to be distinguishable from a line or a cluster.

entries.label: Weapon or tool aimed at another subject
entries.description: One subject points a held object at the other.
entries.frame_evidence: A rigid elongated shape extending from a hand along the line toward the other character.
entries.detector_note: Requires object detection to identify the held item; the landmark shell (extended arm bearing at the partner) is available but cannot establish that anything is held.
entries.notes: The elongated-blob proxy (a high-eccentricity component attached to the hand region) is worth logging as a candidate, never as a weapon claim.

entries.label: Weapon or limb clash
entries.description: Two attacking limbs or objects meet, producing a contact away from either body.
entries.frame_evidence: A bright impact point in the space between the two bodies with sparks or a flash, and both limbs stopping there.
entries.detector_note: Luminance spike localised in the gap ROI (between the two subject masks) combined with a flow-magnitude collapse at the spike location on the following unique cel.
entries.notes: Any bright flash in the gap qualifies; without object detection the analyzer cannot say the flash is a clash rather than a spell, a muzzle flash or a lens flare.

entries.label: Reach overlap (in striking range)
entries.description: The subjects are close enough that a limb can reach the other.
entries.frame_evidence: The gap between bodies smaller than one extended arm's length.
entries.detector_note: distance_shoulder_units < (arm_length_a + arm_length_b) / mean_shoulder_span, where arm length is the summed 11-13-15 segment length; report the margin.
entries.notes: Ignores held weapons entirely, since object extent is not detectable today.

entries.label: Ambient occlusion in crevices
entries.description: Soft darkening where surfaces meet at concave angles, from a render's AO pass or from real ambient shadowing.
entries.frame_evidence: Corners, folds, nostrils, under-collar and where limbs meet the body carry a soft gradient darkening.
entries.detector_note: Detect concave junction candidates as local minima of L that coincide with local maxima of cv2.cornerEigenValsAndVecs concavity or with skeleton branch points of the subject mask, then measure the depth and radial falloff of the darkening.
entries.notes: Painted or drawn shading in the same places is indistinguishable; on 2D this is a style read, not an AO measurement, and excessive uniform AO (the dirty-render look) needs a separate model to call.

entries.label: Ambient-only / no discernible key
entries.description: The subject is lit by an even ambient wash with no directional key producing modelling.
entries.frame_evidence: The subject shows very low luminance variance across its surface with no terminator anywhere on it.
entries.detector_note: Inside the subject mask compute std(L)/mean(L) and the 95th percentile of cv2.Sobel magnitude after cv2.GaussianBlur(sigma=3); ambient-only when the normalised std is below 0.10 and no gradient ridge longer than 15 percent of the mask diameter is found by skimage.morphology.skeletonize on the thresholded gradient.
entries.notes: Indistinguishable from flat cel colour fill in 2D; on anime this fires constantly and is only meaningful together with lighting.cel_shade_two_tone being absent.

entries.label: Flat drawn rim band (anime)
entries.description: A hand-drawn rim rendered as a single flat value with a hard ink-like inner edge rather than a falloff.
entries.frame_evidence: The edge highlight is one uniform colour with a step boundary and no gradient inside it.
entries.detector_note: Inside the rim band, count unique quantised colours after cv2.pyrMeanShiftFiltering(sp=5, sr=15); flag flat when the band is covered above 85 percent by two or fewer clusters and the inner boundary gradient measured by cv2.Sobel exceeds 40 L units over 2 px.
entries.notes: Heavy compression flattens gradients into bands and mimics this; measure on the highest-quality decode available, never on a re-encoded proxy.

entries.label: Drawn hair highlight band (anime)
entries.description: The stylised flat band or zigzag of lighter colour drawn across anime hair to stand in for a specular.
entries.frame_evidence: A continuous lighter band with a hard edge follows the hair mass contour, often in a jagged or scalloped shape.
entries.detector_note: Within a hair region (colour cluster above the face, from the mediapipe face bbox), find the brightest colour cluster and test that it forms an elongated band (regionprops eccentricity above 0.85) with hard boundaries and covers 5 to 30 percent of the hair region.
entries.notes: Bleached streaks and hair accessories look identical; also fires on the highlight of a helmet or hat sitting where the hair region was estimated.

entries.label: Anisotropic specular streak (brushed metal, hair)
entries.description: A highlight stretched perpendicular to the surface grain, characteristic of brushed metal, satin and hair shading.
entries.frame_evidence: The highlight is a long thin band rather than a round spot, aligned consistently with a surface direction.
entries.detector_note: For each specular component, compare regionprops major and minor axis lengths and test whether the major axis is perpendicular to the dominant local texture orientation found from the structure tensor (skimage.feature.structure_tensor and its eigenvectors).
entries.notes: Needs enough resolution to resolve the surface grain; at typical delivery sizes the structure tensor on brushed metal returns noise.

entries.label: Atmospheric haze / aerial perspective
entries.description: Distant parts of the scene are lifted in black level and desaturated by intervening atmosphere.
entries.frame_evidence: Background layers are paler, lower in contrast and less saturated than foreground layers.
entries.detector_note: Compute the dark-channel prior (min over RGB in a 15 px window, as used in haze removal) and correlate its value with a depth proxy from image row position or from a segmentation-based foreground/background split; report the black-level lift and contrast reduction of the background relative to the foreground.
entries.notes: The row-position depth proxy is wrong for any non-landscape composition; without a depth estimate this is a weak measurement and should be reported with its proxy named.

entries.label: Auto-exposure pumping
entries.description: The camera repeatedly hunting exposure up and down, usually after something bright enters or leaves the frame.
entries.frame_evidence: Overall brightness overshoots then settles, oscillating over a second or two, most visible on a static background.
entries.detector_note: On the per-unique-cel mean linear luminance series, fit a damped-oscillation or step-with-overshoot model and fire when there is at least one overshoot above 10 percent followed by a settle, with the same uniform-ratio spatial condition as lighting.exposure_shift_step; report the settle time and overshoot magnitude.
entries.notes: Photographic capture only; an animated file cannot pump unless the plate was photographed. Genuine lighting changes (a passing car) mimic the envelope, so the spatial-uniformity gate is required.

entries.label: Bioluminescent / ambient glow from many small sources
entries.description: Many small dim emitters (fireflies, glowing plankton, embers) collectively lighting a dark scene.
entries.frame_evidence: Dozens of small saturated glowing points in an otherwise very dark frame, with a faint matching tint on nearby surfaces.
entries.detector_note: Count local maxima via scipy.ndimage.maximum_filter peak detection on a dark frame (median L below 0.2); fire when more than 15 peaks of area under 0.05 percent each share a hue within 25 degrees and the frame background carries the same hue at low chroma.
entries.notes: Star fields, bokeh lights and sensor hot pixels all produce point arrays; the shared-hue and background-tint conditions do most of the work.

entries.label: Lifted black level (milky blacks)
entries.description: The darkest values in the frame sit well above zero, giving a washed or faded look.
entries.frame_evidence: No pixels approach black and the darkest areas read grey, often with a colour cast in the shadows.
entries.detector_note: np.percentile(min-channel, 0.5) above 25/255 while the frame contains regions that should be shadowed (shadow-candidate mask non-empty or key_fill_stops above 1.0); report the lift in code values and the LAB chroma of the lifted floor.
entries.notes: Haze, fog and a genuinely bright bounce-filled set all lift the floor legitimately; cross-check lighting.atmospheric_haze_depth before calling it a grade.

entries.label: Blob shadow (simplified ellipse under a 3D character)
entries.description: A generic soft ellipse used in place of a real projected shadow, common in game-engine and low-budget CG output.
entries.frame_evidence: A smooth dark ellipse under the character that does not match the character's silhouette and does not change shape as they move.
entries.detector_note: Fit an ellipse to the ground shadow component with cv2.fitEllipse; fire when the IoU between the component and its fitted ellipse exceeds 0.90 while the IoU between the component and the vertically projected subject silhouette is below 0.35, and the eccentricity stays within 0.05 over the shot.
entries.notes: A genuinely round object legitimately casts an elliptical shadow; the silhouette-projection mismatch term is the one that carries the finding.

entries.label: Blown / clipped highlights
entries.description: Highlight areas that have reached the top of the range and lost all detail.
entries.frame_evidence: Regions of flat maximum white with no texture, often with hard boundaries where the clip begins.
entries.detector_note: Count pixels with R, G and B all above 250/255; report the fraction, the number and size of connected clipped components, and the fraction of clipped pixels that lie inside components larger than 0.1 percent of frame area (large flat clips being the meaningful kind).
entries.notes: A practical source or a specular is supposed to clip; distinguish by whether the clipped region coincides with a detected source blob, and report the two counts separately or every night interior reads as overexposed.

entries.label: Blue hour / twilight
entries.description: The period after sunset where ambient sky light is soft, cool and directionless while practicals become visible.
entries.frame_evidence: An overall deep blue cast with soft shadowless ambient light and lit windows or street lamps punching through.
entries.detector_note: Frame median L between 0.12 and 0.35, mean LAB b below -10, shadow-candidate area below 2 percent (soft ambient, no hard shadows), and at least 2 warm clipped components (LAB b above 15) present as practicals.
entries.notes: Day-for-night grading imitates this deliberately and will be indistinguishable; check lighting.day_for_night.

entries.label: Ground bounce fill
entries.description: Light reflecting off the floor, sand, snow or water filling the underside of a subject.
entries.frame_evidence: The under-chin, under-jaw and underside of arms are lifted relative to what a pure top key would leave.
entries.detector_note: Compare the measured chin ROI luminance against the value predicted by the fitted Lambertian light model from lighting.key_elevation_angle; fire when the residual on downward-facing mesh regions is positive by more than 0.4 stops, and report the hue of that residual.
entries.notes: Depends entirely on the quality of the Lambertian fit, which uses generic head normals; the residual for a very non-average face will be large for reasons unrelated to bounce.

entries.label: Coloured bounce light
entries.description: Light reflecting off a coloured surface and tinting the subject nearby, such as a red wall warming a cheek.
entries.frame_evidence: The side of the subject facing a strongly coloured surface carries that surface's hue at reduced chroma.
entries.detector_note: For each large saturated surface region, sample the subject region within 20 percent of frame width on the facing side and test whether its LAB hue angle has shifted toward the surface hue relative to the subject's opposite side, with the shift decaying with distance.
entries.notes: The absence of this effect is the more useful finding for CG review, but absence is also produced by a neutral set; only claim absence when a strongly saturated adjacent surface exists.

entries.label: Cast shadow direction conflicts with the key direction
entries.description: The shadow points somewhere incompatible with the light direction read off the subject shading.
entries.frame_evidence: The face is lit from camera-left while the character's ground shadow also falls to camera-left.
entries.detector_note: Compare lighting.shadow_bearing_deg against 180 degrees minus lighting.key_azimuth_deg projected to the ground plane; flag when the absolute circular difference exceeds 45 degrees and both source measurements had acceptable confidence.
entries.notes: The projection from a 3D light azimuth to an image-plane shadow bearing needs the ground-plane orientation, which is unknown; treat conflicts under 60 degrees as unreliable.

entries.label: Cast shadow direction
entries.description: The bearing from an object to its own cast shadow, which points directly away from the light.
entries.frame_evidence: The shadow blob extends from the object base toward one side of the frame.
entries.detector_note: Pair each shadow component with the nearest subject-mask component sharing a boundary, then report the angle from the subject mask's lowest contact point to the shadow component centroid; aggregate with a circular mean over all pairs in the frame.
entries.notes: Pairing is the weak link: with several objects and overlapping shadows the association is ambiguous and the circular std is the only honest confidence signal.

entries.label: Cast shadow length relative to the object
entries.description: How long the shadow is compared to the height of the object casting it, which encodes the light elevation.
entries.frame_evidence: A long raking shadow versus a short pooled one under the object.
entries.detector_note: Take the shadow component's major-axis length from skimage.measure.regionprops and divide by the paired subject mask bounding-box height; also derive an implied light elevation as arctan(1/ratio) under a flat-ground assumption.
entries.notes: The flat-ground assumption fails on stairs, slopes and walls, and camera perspective foreshortens the shadow; the implied elevation is a rough indicator only.

entries.label: Multiple cast shadows from one object
entries.description: One object throws two or more distinct shadows, revealing two or more strong light sources.
entries.frame_evidence: Two separate shadow shapes fan out from the same object base at different angles.
entries.detector_note: Group shadow components whose nearest contact point is the same subject mask, then fire when two or more grouped components have centroid bearings differing by more than 25 degrees and each exceeds 0.2 percent of frame area.
entries.notes: A single shadow broken by a step or an object in the ground plane splits into two components and fakes this; require both lobes to touch the same contact region.

entries.label: Cast shadow present
entries.description: A shadow thrown by an object onto another surface, as distinct from the object's own form shadow.
entries.frame_evidence: A darker region on a surface whose colour matches the surrounding lit surface but at lower luminance.
entries.detector_note: Shadow-candidate mask by the illumination-invariant ratio test: convert to HSV and LAB, keep pixels where V is below the local (51 px cv2.blur) mean by 25 to 70 percent while hue differs from the local mean hue by under 10 degrees and LAB chroma is within 15 percent; clean with cv2.morphologyEx OPEN then keep components above 0.3 percent of frame area.
entries.notes: This classical test confuses dark albedo (a black rug, dark hair, wet asphalt) with shadow constantly; precision on real footage is poor and every downstream shadow metric inherits that. Run a null by scoring the same test on a deliberately shadow-free flat-lit frame from the same production.

entries.label: Cast shadow edge softness
entries.description: How diffuse the boundary of a cast shadow is, encoding the apparent size of the source.
entries.frame_evidence: The shadow boundary is either a crisp line or a broad gradient smear.
entries.detector_note: Sample normals across the shadow component contour and reuse the logistic-profile 10-to-90 rise measurement from lighting.penumbra_width, reported per shadow component rather than globally.
entries.notes: Motion blur on a moving shadow widens the edge along the motion axis only; measure width on the contour segments perpendicular to the optical-flow direction.

entries.label: Catchlight count and shape
entries.description: How many sources are reflected in the eye and what shape they are, which reveals the lighting setup.
entries.frame_evidence: One round spot, a rectangular softbox reflection, a ring, or two separate spots inside the iris.
entries.detector_note: Count catchlight components per iris and report each component's regionprops eccentricity, extent and solidity to distinguish round from rectangular from ring shapes.
entries.notes: At typical broadcast resolutions the iris is a handful of pixels and shape descriptors are meaningless; require an iris diameter above 25 px before emitting shape metrics.

entries.label: Catchlight in the eyes
entries.description: The reflection of the key source in the eye, which reveals the source shape and position.
entries.frame_evidence: A small bright spot inside the iris or pupil area of one or both eyes.
entries.detector_note: Use mediapipe face_mesh with refine_landmarks=True to get iris landmarks 468-472 and 473-477; inside each iris disc find the brightest connected component above the iris mean plus 3 std, and report its area, position within the iris in clock terms, and peak luminance.
entries.notes: Needs a face large enough that the iris spans at least 12 px; below that the iris landmarks are noise. Anime eyes carry a drawn catchlight that is a style constant rather than a light reading.

entries.label: Caustics projected onto a wall, ceiling or face
entries.description: Water or glass caustics thrown onto a nearby surface as a moving bright pattern, a strong mood device.
entries.frame_evidence: A rippling bright pattern swims across a wall, ceiling or a character's face with no matching geometry on that surface.
entries.detector_note: Same skeleton prefilter as lighting.caustics_water_surface but restricted to regions identified as a face ROI or a low-texture planar region, with the additional requirement that the underlying surface structure is static across unique cels; crop the region and ask qwen2.5vl.
entries.vlm_question: Is there a moving rippling water-light pattern falling on the surface in this crop? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Distinct from lighting.dappled_light_moving mainly by the closed-cell topology; when the pattern is coarse the two entries will both fire and both should be logged.

entries.label: Caustics on or under water
entries.description: The bright interlocking net of light focused by a rippling water surface.
entries.frame_evidence: A shifting web of bright curved lines forming irregular polygonal cells over a surface.
entries.detector_note: Prefilter: skeletonise the top-decile luminance mask (skimage.morphology.skeletonize) and measure branch density and loop count via skimage.graph or Euler number; caustic candidates have high branch density with many closed loops and strong frame-to-frame deformation on unique cels; crop and ask qwen2.5vl.
entries.vlm_question: Does this crop show the rippling net-like pattern of light made by water? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Cracked mud, veins, lightning and marbling all skeletonise similarly; the deformation-over-time term helps but 2D drawn caustics are often animated on threes and deform in steps.

entries.label: Correlated colour temperature estimate
entries.description: A numeric Kelvin estimate of the dominant illuminant.
entries.frame_evidence: The chromaticity of near-specular highlights and of neutral-looking surfaces in the frame.
entries.detector_note: Estimate the illuminant with a grey-edge/grey-world hybrid on non-clipped pixels, convert the resulting RGB to CIE 1931 xy through sRGB primaries, then apply McCamy approximation n = (x - 0.3320)/(0.1858 - y), CCT = 449 n^3 + 3525 n^2 + 6823.3 n + 5520.33.
entries.notes: Only meaningful with a near-neutral surface present; on a graded, single-hue or heavily stylised frame the Kelvin number is fiction. Report Duv alongside and suppress the Kelvin value when Duv exceeds 0.02, since the chromaticity is then nowhere near the Planckian locus.

entries.label: Three-tone cel shading with a highlight tone
entries.description: Cel shading that adds a third, brighter tone for direct highlight in addition to base and shadow.
entries.frame_evidence: Three distinct flat values appear on one continuous surface, the brightest confined to a small area facing the light.
entries.detector_note: Same clustering as lighting.cel_shade_two_tone with exactly 3 clusters above 5 percent coverage, the brightest occupying under 25 percent of the region and being spatially compact by regionprops solidity.
entries.notes: Line art and outlines add a fourth very dark cluster; exclude clusters whose pixels are mostly within 2 px of a cv2.Canny edge.

entries.label: Two-tone cel shading
entries.description: The anime convention of rendering a surface with exactly one base colour and one shadow colour separated by a hard boundary.
entries.frame_evidence: Skin or clothing shows precisely two flat values with a step boundary and no intermediate tone.
entries.detector_note: Inside a skin or garment region found by colour clustering (cv2.pyrMeanShiftFiltering then np.unique on the quantised image), count clusters covering more than 5 percent of the region; two-tone when exactly 2 clusters cover above 90 percent and the boundary between them has a Sobel slope above 30 L units over 2 px.
entries.notes: Gradient banding from 8-bit encoding also produces discrete steps; the discriminator is that cel tones are 2 or 3 large regions, banding is many thin parallel ones.

entries.label: Character lit against the background light direction
entries.description: The character element is lit from a direction the background plate does not support, the classic composite tell.
entries.frame_evidence: Background shadows fall to one side while the character shading and edge light imply the opposite side.
entries.detector_note: Deterministic prefilter: compare lighting.key_azimuth_deg on the face with lighting.global_light_direction_estimate computed on the background-only region (subject mask inverted); when they disagree by more than 60 degrees, crop a box containing the character plus 30 percent context and send it to the qwen2.5vl judge.
entries.vlm_question: In this image, is the light on the person coming from the same side as the light on the background behind them? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Ask on a crop that contains both the character and enough background; asked on a full wide frame the VLM answers from scene gist and is near chance.

entries.label: Chiaroscuro
entries.description: Strong dramatic modelling where a hard-edged pool of light carves the subject out of deep surrounding darkness.
entries.frame_evidence: A high key-to-fill ratio combines with a sharp terminator and a large fraction of the frame in near-black.
entries.detector_note: Composite rule: lighting.key_fill_stops above 3.0 AND lighting.terminator_sharpness in the hard band AND lighting.dark_pixel_frac above 0.5; report a single chiaroscuro score as the normalised product of the three.
entries.notes: A composite of three thresholded measures inherits all three failure modes; always emit the components alongside the score so a reader can see which term carried it.

entries.label: Colour-cycling light
entries.description: A source whose hue rotates over time, as in disco, emergency or party lighting.
entries.frame_evidence: The scene tint moves through hues over a short window while overall luminance stays roughly constant.
entries.detector_note: Track the LAB a,b centroid of the frame per unique cel and measure the angular travel of atan2(b,a) over the shot; fire when the unwrapped hue travel exceeds 90 degrees while the mean L coefficient of variation is under 0.15.
entries.notes: A camera panning past differently coloured practicals gives the same hue travel; gate on low global optical flow.

entries.label: Heavily gelled / saturated coloured lighting
entries.description: The scene is lit by a strongly saturated non-white source that pushes everything toward one hue.
entries.frame_evidence: The whole frame or a large region is dominated by one saturated hue with little hue variation across materials.
entries.detector_note: Compute the circular variance of hue over pixels above the 20th luminance percentile with chroma above 8; fire when the circular variance is under 0.15 (highly concentrated) and the mean chroma exceeds 25.
entries.notes: A monochrome grade, an underwater shot and a sunset all satisfy this; it describes the image, and the cause is separated by the time-of-day entries.

entries.label: Contact shadow
entries.description: The tight dark line right where an object meets a surface, which anchors the object to the ground.
entries.frame_evidence: A narrow darkening band a few pixels wide hugging the base of feet, furniture legs or a resting prop.
entries.detector_note: Take a 15 px band immediately below the subject mask's lowest boundary (or below mediapipe pose ankle landmarks 27/28/31/32) and test whether mean L there is below the mean L of the same-surface region 40 px further away by more than 0.4 stops, with the darkening decaying monotonically with distance.
entries.notes: Requires the contact point to be visible; occluded feet, grass and water make this untestable and it should log NOT DETECTABLE.

entries.label: Global luminance contrast and dynamic range
entries.description: How far the frame spans from its darkest meaningful value to its brightest.
entries.frame_evidence: The spread between the low and high percentiles of the luminance histogram.
entries.detector_note: np.percentile(L, [1, 5, 50, 95, 99]) on linear luminance; report the 99/1 ratio in stops, the 95/5 ratio in stops, and the RMS contrast std(L)/mean(L).
entries.notes: A single specular clip or one black letterbox bar dominates the extreme percentiles; crop off any detected letterbox before measuring.

entries.label: Cool key light
entries.description: The dominant light on the subject is blue biased.
entries.frame_evidence: Lit planes carry a blue-cyan cast, typical of moonlight, screen light or a cool grade.
entries.detector_note: Same highlight-tercile LAB measurement as lighting.warm_key with the opposite condition: mean b below -8.
entries.notes: Cannot be separated from a cool colour grade by pixel measurement alone; this measures the image, not the fixture.

entries.label: Crushed blacks
entries.description: Shadow areas driven to the bottom of the range so that shadow detail is unrecoverable.
entries.frame_evidence: Large regions at or near value zero with no texture and a histogram spike at the black point.
entries.detector_note: Fraction of pixels with max(R,G,B) below 6/255, plus the height of the histogram bin at 0 relative to its neighbours (a spike ratio above 3 indicates clipping rather than a natural rolloff), plus the Laplacian std inside those regions compared with the frame noise floor.
entries.notes: Deliberate low-key and chiaroscuro produce crushed blacks by intent; this is an exposure observation, never automatically a defect.

entries.label: Moving dappled light
entries.description: Broken light patches that shift and swim across a subject, from leaves in wind or a moving vehicle under trees.
entries.frame_evidence: Many small bright patches on a face or wall that change shape and position over a short window while the surface itself stays still.
entries.detector_note: On unique cels compute the temporal std of L per pixel inside a motion-compensated subject ROI; fire when the high-variance pixels form many small components (count above 15, median area under 0.3 percent) while the ROI structural similarity (skimage.metrics.structural_similarity on a gradient image) stays above 0.7, meaning the surface did not move.
entries.notes: This is one of the strongest cases for the unique-cel rule: on duplicated cels the temporal std is exactly zero and the detector silently reports no dapple.

entries.label: Day-for-night treatment
entries.description: Footage shot in daylight and graded to read as night, which leaves characteristic contradictions.
entries.frame_evidence: A dark blue frame that nonetheless carries hard sun shadows, a bright sky region and daylight-shaped highlight falloff.
entries.detector_note: Fire when the frame reads night by level and hue (median L below 0.3, LAB b below -8) while simultaneously showing sun-like evidence: hard shadow edges, shadow bearings consistent within 15 degrees frame-wide, and an upper region whose luminance still exceeds the lower region by 0.5 stops.
entries.notes: A genuine moonlit exterior produces frame-wide consistent hard shadows too; the sky-still-brighter term is the strongest discriminator and it fails when no sky is in frame.

entries.label: Daylight exterior
entries.description: The scene is lit by open daylight outdoors.
entries.frame_evidence: High overall luminance, a bright upper region consistent with sky, and a cool-neutral illuminant estimate.
entries.detector_note: Deterministic prefilter: frame median L above 0.45, upper-third mean L above lower-third by 0.5 stops, estimated CCT between 5000 and 8000 K; then confirm with qwen2.5vl on a downsampled full frame since this is a scene-gist question rather than a detail question.
entries.vlm_question: Is this scene taking place outdoors in daylight? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: This is the rare case where the full frame is the right VLM input, because the question is about the scene as a whole rather than a defect; the crop rule does not apply to gist questions.

entries.label: Double rim in two colours
entries.description: Two separate back lights of different hue rim opposite sides of the subject, the modern stylised look.
entries.frame_evidence: The left silhouette edge glows one hue (for example cyan) and the right edge glows a contrasting hue (for example magenta).
entries.detector_note: Split the rim band from lighting.rim_light into left and right halves by the mask centroid column, compute the mean LAB a and b of pixels above the band luminance median in each half, and fire when the hue angle atan2(b,a) differs by more than 60 degrees and both halves exceed a chroma of 12.
entries.notes: Chromatic aberration produces exactly this signature at very small band widths; require band width above 3 px and a hue delta that survives on a 2x downsample.

entries.label: Flat drawn drop shadow (anime)
entries.description: The single flat-value ellipse or shape drawn under a 2D character as a shorthand ground shadow.
entries.frame_evidence: A uniform-value shape under the character with a hard ink edge and no gradient or penumbra.
entries.detector_note: Ground-region shadow component whose interior std(L) is below 3 units, whose edge slope exceeds 30 L units over 2 px, and which contains one or two quantised colours after mean-shift filtering.
entries.notes: Correct behaviour for the medium, not a defect; it exists as an entry so 2D output is not scored against 3D shadow expectations.

entries.label: Emissive effect element (magic, energy, glowing prop)
entries.description: An FX element that emits light into the scene, such as a glowing weapon, spell or energy field.
entries.frame_evidence: A saturated bright shape with a soft additive halo whose colour also appears on nearby surfaces and faces.
entries.detector_note: Find high-saturation high-value components, then test that the same hue appears at reduced chroma on surfaces within 3 blob radii (the spill test) using LAB hue-angle matching within 20 degrees and a monotone chroma falloff.
entries.notes: The spill test is what distinguishes an emitter that is lighting the scene from a bright element merely composited over it, which is a useful 2D compositing quality read in itself.

entries.label: Explosion / large blast light
entries.description: A large short-lived warm source that momentarily becomes the key for the whole scene.
entries.frame_evidence: A frame-wide warm luminance surge with the light direction snapping to the blast position for a handful of frames.
entries.detector_note: Global mean L rises above 1.5 stops within 2 unique cels, mean LAB b rises above 10 units, and lighting.global_light_direction_estimate changes by more than 60 degrees for the duration of the surge, then returns.
entries.notes: A cut to a bright shot produces the same global step; require the pre-surge and post-surge frames to be similar (histogram correlation above 0.85) so a cut is excluded.

entries.label: Exposure step inside a shot
entries.description: A discrete change in exposure level during a continuous shot, from an iris pull, an ND change or a grade edit.
entries.frame_evidence: The whole frame steps brighter or darker in one or two frames while the composition is unchanged.
entries.detector_note: On unique cels, look for a change in mean linear luminance above 0.25 stops within 2 cels that is spatially uniform (the per-tile ratio has a coefficient of variation below 0.15) and persists for at least 5 cels, with histogram correlation across the step above 0.7.
entries.notes: The uniform-ratio test is what separates an exposure change from a lighting change; a light turning on is spatially non-uniform, an iris pull is uniform.

entries.label: Broad versus short lighting
entries.description: Whether the lit side of a turned head is the side facing the camera (broad) or the side turned away (short).
entries.frame_evidence: On a three-quarter head, the wider visible cheek is either the bright one or the dark one.
entries.detector_note: Estimate head yaw from the ratio of distances landmark 1 to 234 versus 1 to 454; identify which cheek polygon has the larger projected area, then report broad when the larger-area cheek is also the brighter one, short when it is the darker one.
entries.notes: Meaningless at yaw below 10 degrees; emit NOT DETECTABLE rather than a coin-flip label.

entries.label: Butterfly / paramount lighting
entries.description: A high frontal key that drops a small symmetric butterfly-shaped shadow directly under the nose.
entries.frame_evidence: Cheeks are near-equally lit and a compact symmetric shadow sits centred beneath the nose above the lip.
entries.detector_note: Cheek ratio below 0.25 log2, forehead brighter than chin by 0.3 to 0.8 stops, and the darkest connected component in the philtrum ROI (landmarks 2/97/326/164) is centred within 5 percent of the face midline with area 0.5 to 3 percent of the face bbox.
entries.notes: Anime faces frequently draw no under-nose shadow at all, so this pattern is close to undetectable on 2D and should log NOT DETECTABLE rather than NOT FOUND when lighting.cel_shade_two_tone is active.

entries.label: Loop lighting
entries.description: A moderate off-axis key that drops a small loop of nose shadow onto the cheek without touching the shadow-side cheek edge.
entries.frame_evidence: A short comma of shadow runs from the nostril diagonally down the cheek and stops before reaching the lip corner.
entries.detector_note: Cheek ratio between 0.2 and 0.6 log2 plus a dark component in the nose ROI whose major axis, from skimage.measure.regionprops, points 20 to 60 degrees below horizontal and whose length is under 20 percent of face width.
entries.notes: Loop and Rembrandt are a continuum; the discriminator is whether the nose shadow merges with the cheek shadow, which is a connectivity test on the thresholded mask.

entries.label: Rembrandt triangle
entries.description: A small isolated lit triangle on the shadow-side cheek, bounded by the nose shadow and the cheekbone.
entries.frame_evidence: A bright quadrilateral patch roughly eye-width sits inside the otherwise shadowed cheek, below the shadow-side eye.
entries.detector_note: Take the shadow-side cheek ROI (whichever of the 234/93/132 or 454/323/361 polygons is darker), threshold with skimage.filters.threshold_otsu inside the ROI, run cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats, and require exactly one bright component of area 2 to 12 percent of the face bbox whose centroid lies below the shadow-side eye centre.
entries.notes: Specular sweat, a freckle cluster or an anime cheek blush blob can all satisfy the area test; require the patch to be contiguous with the lit side through the cheekbone or it is a false positive.

entries.label: Split lighting on a face
entries.description: The portrait lighting pattern where the face is divided into a fully lit half and a fully shadowed half.
entries.frame_evidence: A hard vertical edge runs through the bridge of the nose with one half several stops darker.
entries.detector_note: Cheek LAB ratio above 1.5 log2 and the terminator column, from the max of cv2.Sobel(L, dx=1) summed over face rows, within 8 percent of the nose-bridge column (mediapipe landmark 168).
entries.notes: Requires a near-frontal face; gate on head yaw below 15 degrees or the pattern name is meaningless.

entries.label: Single-frame white flash (anime impact flash)
entries.description: One or two frames of near-uniform white or coloured fill used as an impact or transition device.
entries.frame_evidence: A single frame where almost the entire image is one near-clipped value with negligible spatial variance.
entries.detector_note: Fire when a frame has mean L above 0.9 with std below 8/255 over more than 90 percent of pixels, and the frames immediately before and after are normal-contrast frames with histogram correlation above 0.6 to each other.
entries.notes: Also applies to black flash frames with the test inverted; count these per minute for photosensitivity reporting.

entries.label: Flat lighting with little modelling
entries.description: The lighting produces almost no sense of three-dimensional form on the subject.
entries.frame_evidence: The subject shows small luminance variation across surfaces that should turn away from the light.
entries.detector_note: Compute the residual of the Lambertian light-vector fit over the mediapipe face mesh; flat when the fitted light magnitude is low relative to the constant ambient term (ambient/(ambient+directional) above 0.75).
entries.notes: This is the intended state for most anime faces, so on 2D it is a style descriptor rather than an observation about a light.

entries.label: Flicker amplitude
entries.description: How deep the luminance oscillation is, as a fraction of the mean level.
entries.frame_evidence: The peak-to-trough swing of frame or region luminance across the flicker cycle.
entries.detector_note: On the same per-unique-cel series, report (p95 - p05) / mean and the RMS of the detrended signal divided by the mean, both computed over a rolling 1 second window.
entries.notes: Camera or subject motion changes frame-mean luminance without any flicker; measure inside a motion-compensated ROI or gate on global flow below 1 px.

entries.label: Flicker frequency
entries.description: The dominant rate at which scene or source luminance oscillates.
entries.frame_evidence: Frame-mean luminance oscillates periodically over a short window.
entries.detector_note: Build the per-UNIQUE-CEL frame mean L series, detrend with scipy.signal.detrend, run scipy.signal.welch(nperseg=64) and report the peak frequency, converting cel index to seconds using the measured unique-cel rate rather than the container fps.
entries.notes: The single most important place the twos-and-threes lesson bites: computing this on container fps gives a frequency that is a property of the animation schedule, not the light. Nyquist also caps what is measurable at half the unique-cel rate.

entries.label: Fog or smoke scattering light
entries.description: Airborne particulate that becomes visible where light passes through it, revealing the beam and reducing contrast.
entries.frame_evidence: Low-contrast luminous regions with no texture that brighten near lights and drift slowly across the frame.
entries.detector_note: Identify regions with low local Laplacian variance and elevated black level (dark-channel value above 0.25) whose luminance correlates with distance from a detected source blob; confirm slow non-rigid motion via cv2.calcOpticalFlowFarneback on unique cels with a small coherent flow field.
entries.notes: Defocused background, overexposed sky and a plain wall all read as low-texture with a lifted black level; the source-distance correlation is what makes the finding about light rather than about focus.

entries.label: Dappled foliage shadow
entries.description: The irregular broken shadow pattern cast by leaves, with soft-edged bright pools between dark patches.
entries.frame_evidence: Many small irregular shadow blobs of similar scale scattered over a surface with soft edges.
entries.detector_note: Blob statistics on the shadow mask: fire when component count exceeds 20, median component area is between 0.02 and 0.5 percent of frame area, component solidity from regionprops is below 0.75, and the size distribution has a low coefficient of variation.
entries.notes: Camouflage print, leopard spots and mottled walls are the standing false positives; the temporal companion lighting.dappled_light_moving is far more specific.

entries.label: Whole-frame light direction estimate
entries.description: A scene-level estimate of where the dominant light is coming from when no face is available.
entries.frame_evidence: Shading gradients across the whole image consistently brighten toward one side of the frame.
entries.detector_note: Downsample L to 64x36, blur with cv2.GaussianBlur(sigma=6), take cv2.Sobel dx and dy, and report the mean gradient vector direction weighted by gradient magnitude; also report the luminance centroid offset from the frame centre.
entries.notes: This measures composition as much as lighting; a bright sky at the top of every exterior frame will bias it upward, so it needs the per-shot median of a random-crop null before any claim is made.

entries.label: Glow / bloom around a bright source
entries.description: A soft halo of light spreading around a bright source, from lens scatter, atmosphere or a render bloom pass.
entries.frame_evidence: A smooth radially decaying brightness surrounds a clipped source and washes over adjacent darker objects.
entries.detector_note: Fit an exponential or power-law decay to the radial mean luminance profile around each source blob with scipy.optimize.curve_fit; report the decay radius normalised by frame height and whether the glow crosses object boundaries (a bloom tell, since real occluders should cut a scene light but not a post bloom).
entries.notes: The crossing-occluder-boundary test is the interesting part: it separates a post-process bloom from genuine atmospheric scatter, but it needs a reliable occluder edge.

entries.label: Patterned shadow (window bars, blinds, gobo)
entries.description: A shadow carrying a regular geometric pattern thrown by blinds, window frames, grilles or a lighting gobo.
entries.frame_evidence: Parallel dark stripes or a lattice lies across a wall, floor or face at a consistent spacing and angle.
entries.detector_note: Inside a shadow candidate region compute the 2D FFT of L (np.fft.rfft2 after windowing) and fire on a dominant off-DC peak with magnitude above 6x the local spectral median; report the stripe period in pixels and the angle from the peak orientation.
entries.notes: Fabric weave, brick, fences and interlacing all produce strong periodic spectra; require the pattern to appear only inside the darker class and to vanish in the lit neighbourhood.

entries.label: God rays / crepuscular shafts
entries.description: Visible beams of light through atmosphere radiating from a source or an aperture.
entries.frame_evidence: Elongated brighter wedges converging toward a common point, superimposed on the scene without occluding it.
entries.detector_note: Prefilter deterministically: high-pass the luminance, run cv2.HoughLinesP, and test whether 4 or more detected lines converge to a common vanishing point within 5 percent of frame diagonal via least-squares intersection; crop the convergent region plus the shafts and ask qwen2.5vl.
entries.vlm_question: Are there visible beams or shafts of light going through the air in this image? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Architectural perspective lines converge to a vanishing point too and dominate the Hough prefilter; the deterministic side must exclude lines that coincide with strong structural edges in cv2.Canny.

entries.label: Golden hour
entries.description: Low warm sun near the horizon producing long shadows, warm key and strong rim.
entries.frame_evidence: Strongly warm highlights, very long cast shadows, and frequent lens flare or haze toward a low sun.
entries.detector_note: Composite: highlight LAB b above 18, lighting.shadow_length_ratio above 2.0 (implied elevation below 27 degrees), and a warm-to-cool gradient across the frame measured as LAB b differing by more than 8 units between the sun-side and opposite thirds.
entries.notes: A warm interior with a low practical satisfies all three; needs lighting.daylight_exterior to have fired for the label to mean golden hour rather than warm low light.

entries.label: Hair highlight repositioning across cels
entries.description: Whether the drawn hair highlight moves consistently with head rotation or jumps arbitrarily between drawings.
entries.frame_evidence: The highlight band sits in a different place on the hair from one drawing to the next without matching head motion.
entries.detector_note: Across unique cels, track the highlight band centroid in head-local coordinates (normalised by the mediapipe face bbox and derotated by the head yaw proxy); flag jumps above 15 percent of head width that are not explained by yaw change.
entries.notes: Highlight placement is a legitimate artistic choice per drawing and varies between key animators; this is an observation of variance, never a defect verdict on its own.

entries.label: Hair light
entries.description: A dedicated light picking out the top of the head so hair separates from a dark background.
entries.frame_evidence: The crown of the head carries a bright cap or band that is not present on the shoulders or face.
entries.detector_note: Define a hair ROI as the region above mediapipe landmark 10 extended up by 0.5 x face height inside the subject mask; hair light when mean L(hair ROI) exceeds mean L(shoulder ROI from pose landmarks 11/12 band) by >0.8 stops and the hair-ROI bright pixels form a band along the upper contour.
entries.notes: Blonde or grey hair is intrinsically brighter than dark clothing, which fakes this every time; the band-shape test on the upper contour is what makes it a lighting read rather than an albedo read.

entries.label: Halation (warm bleed around highlights)
entries.description: A red-orange fringe blooming around bright highlights, a film-stock characteristic often emulated digitally.
entries.frame_evidence: Bright window frames, lamps and skin highlights carry a warm reddish halo on their dark side.
entries.detector_note: In an annulus 3 to 15 px outside clipped components, measure the mean LAB a and b relative to the local background; halation when a exceeds the background by more than 5 units with a matching b rise, and the effect scales with the core brightness across multiple components in the frame.
entries.notes: Chromatic aberration produces a hue fringe too, but it is directional (radial from frame centre) and antisymmetric; halation is isotropic around the source, which is the discriminator.

entries.label: Hard light quality
entries.description: A small or distant source producing crisp shadow edges and tight speculars.
entries.frame_evidence: Shadow boundaries transition from lit to shadow within a few pixels and highlights are small and intense.
entries.detector_note: Sample 200 points along detected shadow boundaries (from a shadow candidate mask), take a 21 px profile normal to the boundary, fit a logistic to each profile with scipy.optimize.curve_fit, and report the median transition width in pixels normalised by frame height; hard when the normalised width is under 0.004.
entries.notes: Resolution, upscaling and codec smoothing all widen every edge; normalise by the sharpest object edge in the same frame or the number is a measurement of the encode, not the light.

entries.label: Harsh overhead sun
entries.description: A high, small, hard sun producing short crisp shadows, deep eye sockets and clipped highlights.
entries.frame_evidence: Very short hard-edged shadows directly beneath objects, blown highlights and racoon-eye shadows on faces.
entries.detector_note: shadow_length_ratio below 0.6 (implied elevation above 59 degrees), shadow edge width normalised below 0.005, blown-highlight fraction above 0.5 percent, and eye-socket depth above 0.8 stops on any detected face.
entries.notes: A hard overhead studio light gives the same numbers; combine with lighting.daylight_exterior for the sun attribution.

entries.label: Full environment light estimation
entries.description: Recovering the number, direction, size, colour and intensity of every light in the scene as an environment map.
entries.frame_evidence: The complete lighting rig implied by all shading, shadows and speculars in the frame taken together.
entries.detector_note: Requires a learned lighting-estimation model (a spherical-harmonic or environment-map regressor). Not installed. The Lambertian face fit in this shard recovers a single dominant direction plus an ambient term and nothing more.
entries.notes: Log as NOT DETECTABLE. Anything reported here as a light direction should be read as one dominant direction, not as the rig.

entries.label: High-key lighting
entries.description: An overall bright, low-contrast scheme where most of the image sits in the upper luminance range with minimal dark area.
entries.frame_evidence: The frame histogram is bunched high with almost no pixels in the lower quarter and shadows are open.
entries.detector_note: cv2.calcHist on L; high-key when the luminance median is above 0.62 of full scale, less than 5 percent of pixels are below 0.15, and the interquartile range is under 0.30.
entries.notes: An overexposed shot and a deliberately high-key shot are numerically identical; the discriminator is lighting.blown_highlights_clipped, which should be low for true high key.

entries.label: Warm interior at night
entries.description: An indoor scene lit by warm household practicals against dark windows.
entries.frame_evidence: Warm pools of light on walls and faces with dark blue or black windows and no daylight spill.
entries.detector_note: Warm illuminant (CCT below 3500 K where the estimate is valid), multiple lighting.practical_source_in_frame hits, and at least one dark region above 3 percent of frame area bounded by straight edges (window candidate) with median L below 0.1.
entries.notes: The window test is crude geometry and will hit any dark rectangular object; it is a supporting term only.

entries.label: Separating surface colour from illumination
entries.description: Decomposing the image into reflectance and shading so that a dark object can be told apart from a shadowed one.
entries.frame_evidence: Any dark region in the frame: is it a black coat or a shadow falling on a white one.
entries.detector_note: Requires an intrinsic-image decomposition network (for example an IID or Retinex-style learned model). Not installed. Classical Retinex via a large-kernel cv2.GaussianBlur ratio gives an unstable approximation that is not trustworthy for reporting.
entries.notes: Log as NOT DETECTABLE. Every illuminant estimate, colour-temperature figure and bounce measurement in this shard is technically confounded by this gap and their notes say so individually.

entries.label: Key azimuth angle estimate
entries.description: A continuous estimate of the horizontal bearing of the dominant light relative to the camera axis.
entries.frame_evidence: The lateral offset of the shading terminator and of the nose shadow encodes the light bearing.
entries.detector_note: Horizontal component of the same least-squares Lambertian light-vector solve over mediapipe face-mesh vertices; report azimuth as atan2(lx, lz) in degrees, 0 = camera axis, positive = camera left.
entries.notes: Front-back ambiguity is real: a strong backlight and a strong frontal light can both fit; disambiguate with lighting.key_backlight before trusting the sign of lz.

entries.label: Backlight / key from behind
entries.description: The main light is behind the subject so the subject body is darker than its surround and the edges glow.
entries.frame_evidence: The subject interior sits well below the background luminance while a bright band hugs the outer contour.
entries.detector_note: Subject mask from mediapipe selfie_segmentation or the largest saliency blob; erode the mask by 6 px for interior, take the 5 px annulus between mask and its erosion for the edge band; backlight when mean L(interior) < mean L(background ring dilated 30 px) and mean L(edge band) exceeds mean L(interior) by more than 1.5 stops.
entries.notes: A dark costume against a bright wall reads identically; the edge_band_gain term is what separates true backlight from plain value contrast, so never fire on the ratio alone.

entries.label: Key direction changes during a shot
entries.description: The dominant light direction rotates or jumps while the shot is still running, from a moving light, a moving subject or a lighting cue.
entries.frame_evidence: The face terminator or cheek ratio slides steadily or steps between the start and the end of the shot.
entries.detector_note: Compute lighting.key_azimuth_deg per UNIQUE-CEL frame index (dedup by mean abs frame difference below 0.5/255 against the previous frame), fit a linear trend with scipy.stats.linregress, and flag when the total swing exceeds 25 degrees or a single-step jump exceeds 20 degrees between consecutive unique cels.
entries.notes: Subject head rotation moves the terminator without any light moving; subtract head yaw from mediapipe before attributing the swing to the light.

entries.label: Two subjects lit from different directions
entries.description: Two or more characters in the same frame are lit by keys pointing in materially different directions.
entries.frame_evidence: One face has its bright side camera-left while another face in the same frame has its bright side camera-right.
entries.detector_note: Run mediapipe face_mesh with max_num_faces=5, compute the cheek LAB ratio and azimuth per face, and flag when any pair differs by more than 45 degrees in azimuth or has opposite-signed cheek ratios above 0.5 log2 each.
entries.notes: Legitimate blocking (one character by a window, one by a lamp) produces the same signal; this is an observation, not a defect verdict.

entries.label: Key elevation angle estimate
entries.description: A continuous estimate of how high above or below the subject the dominant light sits.
entries.frame_evidence: The vertical position of the shading terminator on the face and body encodes the light height.
entries.detector_note: Fit a Lambertian shading model over the mediapipe face-mesh vertices: for each of the 468 landmarks take a 5 px LAB L patch, approximate the surface normal from the canonical face mesh topology, and solve least-squares for the light vector via np.linalg.lstsq; report elevation as arcsin of the y component.
entries.notes: The canonical mesh normals are a generic head, not this head, so the residual is the honest confidence; a fit with residual above the shuffled-normal null (recompute with randomly permuted normals) must be reported as unmeasured.

entries.label: Key-to-fill ratio
entries.description: The luminance ratio between the lit side and the shadow side of the subject, the numeric spine of lighting contrast.
entries.frame_evidence: The measurable brightness step between the lit cheek or torso plane and the shadowed one.
entries.detector_note: mediapipe face_mesh cheek polygons, or pose-derived torso ROI when no face; ratio = mean L(bright ROI) / mean L(dark ROI) on linearised luminance (undo sRGB gamma with np.where(c<=0.04045, c/12.92, ((c+0.055)/1.055)**2.4)); report in stops as log2.
entries.notes: Only valid on linear luminance; measuring the ratio on gamma-encoded pixels understates high ratios badly. On graded footage the ratio is the grade as much as the lighting.

entries.label: Frontal key light
entries.description: The dominant light sits close to the camera axis so the subject is lit flat from the front with minimal visible modelling shadow.
entries.frame_evidence: Face and torso luminance is near-symmetric left-to-right and the nose casts little or no lateral shadow.
entries.detector_note: mediapipe face_mesh (refine_landmarks=True); build left-cheek polygon from landmarks 234/93/132/58 and right-cheek from 454/323/361/288, convert frame to LAB, compare mean L; frontal when abs(log2(L_left/L_right)) < 0.25 AND the nose-side patch (landmarks 1/2/98/327) is within 10 percent of the cheek mean.
entries.notes: Fails on profile or heavily occluded faces; a flat-shaded anime face is frontal-looking by drawing convention, not by lighting intent, so 2D hits need the cel-shade entries as context.

entries.label: Side key (90 degree)
entries.description: The key comes from roughly 90 degrees off the camera axis so one half of the subject is lit and the other half falls into shadow.
entries.frame_evidence: A near-vertical terminator runs down the centre of the face or body with a large luminance step across it.
entries.detector_note: Same mediapipe cheek ROIs as lighting.key_frontal; side key when abs(log2(L_left/L_right)) > 1.0 and the terminator, found as the max column of cv2.Sobel(L, dx=1) summed over face rows, lies within 20 percent of the face-bbox mid-column.
entries.notes: A face turned three-quarters away produces the same cheek ratio for a different reason; gate on face yaw from mediapipe landmark 1 vs 234/454 midpoint.

entries.label: Three-quarter key
entries.description: The classic 45-degree key that lights most of the subject while leaving a shaped shadow on the far side.
entries.frame_evidence: One cheek is clearly brighter, the far cheek retains detail rather than going black, and the nose shadow angles down and across.
entries.detector_note: Cheek LAB ratio in the band 0.35 to 1.0 log2, with far-cheek mean L above 25 percent of near-cheek mean L (shadow retains detail) and a nose-shadow blob detected as the darkest connected component inside the nose ROI (landmarks 1/2/98/327/331) whose centroid is offset laterally by >8 percent of face width.
entries.notes: Overlaps lighting.face_loop_lighting and lighting.face_rembrandt_triangle by construction; report all that fire rather than forcing exclusivity.

entries.label: Top light
entries.description: The key sits high above the subject so upward-facing planes are lit and the eye sockets and under-chin go dark.
entries.frame_evidence: Forehead and shoulder tops read bright while eye sockets, under-nose and under-chin sit in deep shadow.
entries.detector_note: Forehead ROI from mediapipe landmarks 10/109/338/151 vs chin ROI from 152/148/377/400; top light when mean L(forehead) exceeds mean L(chin) by >0.8 stops AND the eye-socket ROI (33/133/159/145 and mirror 362/263/386/374) is below the face median L by >0.6 stops.
entries.notes: A hat brim or fringe produces the same eye-socket darkness with no top key; the forehead term must also fire.

entries.label: Underlight / uplight
entries.description: The key sits below the subject so the lighting gradient inverts and shadows are thrown upward.
entries.frame_evidence: Chin, under-nose and lower lip are brighter than the forehead, and the nose shadow points up onto the brow.
entries.detector_note: Same forehead and chin ROIs as lighting.key_toplight with the sign reversed: uplight when mean L(chin) exceeds mean L(forehead) by >0.5 stops and the darkest blob inside the nose ROI sits ABOVE the nose tip (landmark 1) in image rows.
entries.notes: Snow, water or a lit page can bounce enough to invert the gradient without any deliberate uplight; that is still a true observation of the light, so log it and let lighting.bounce_from_ground_up carry the cause.

entries.label: Kicker (three-quarter back light)
entries.description: A rim that comes from behind and to one side only, sculpting one edge and the cheekbone rather than the full outline.
entries.frame_evidence: The bright edge band covers only one side of the silhouette and continues a short way onto the cheek or shoulder plane.
entries.detector_note: Same edge-band extraction as lighting.rim_light, then bin the band by contour angle into 12 sectors; kicker when the rim gain is concentrated in fewer than 5 adjacent sectors and the inner 15 px of the mask on that side also shows a luminance rise.
entries.notes: Distinguishing a kicker from a plain rim is a threshold on angular concentration; the boundary is arbitrary, so publish the concentration number alongside the label.

entries.label: Gradual light ramp (dimmer or dawn)
entries.description: A slow monotone change in illumination level across the shot rather than a step.
entries.frame_evidence: Frame luminance drifts steadily in one direction across many seconds without oscillation.
entries.detector_note: scipy.stats.linregress on the per-unique-cel mean L series over the shot; fire when the absolute slope exceeds 0.15 stops per second with r-squared above 0.7 and no step larger than 0.2 stops between consecutive cels.
entries.notes: A camera move from a dark to a bright part of the set produces the same monotone drift; check that global flow is low or that the ramp is spatially uniform across tiles.

entries.label: Number of lights in the setup
entries.description: How many distinct sources are lighting the scene, including those invisible and outside frame.
entries.frame_evidence: Multiple shadow lobes, multiple catchlights and multiple specular positions collectively imply a count.
entries.detector_note: No reliable route today. The available partial cues (catchlight component count, shadow lobe count, tile-level chromaticity clusters) each undercount badly and disagree with each other; combining them without a trained model produces a confident number with no null model behind it.
entries.notes: Log as NOT DETECTABLE. The individual cues are still emitted by lighting.catchlight_count_and_shape and lighting.cast_shadow_multiple_from_one_object; the aggregate count is what is refused.

entries.label: Light switched on or off
entries.description: A discrete lighting state change inside a shot where a source turns on or off.
entries.frame_evidence: A one-way step in frame luminance that persists, with a source blob appearing or vanishing, and no cut.
entries.detector_note: On unique cels detect a step in mean L above 0.6 stops that persists for at least 10 cels, verify no shot cut via histogram correlation above 0.7 across the step and global flow below 2 px, and report the sign and the transition duration in cels.
entries.notes: A door opening, a character walking into frame carrying a lamp, or a hard exposure cut all produce persistent steps; the no-cut verification is essential.
