entries.label: Light wrap on the composite edge
entries.description: Background colour bleeding a few pixels into the subject edge, either an intentional comp treatment or its absence a comp tell.
entries.frame_evidence: The outermost 2 to 6 pixels of the subject carry a tint pulled from the background immediately behind them.
entries.detector_note: For sampled contour points, take the LAB a and b of the inner 3 px band and of the outer background 10 px band; report the correlation of inner-band chroma against local background chroma around the contour, and the exponential decay length of that influence inward.
entries.notes: Chroma subsampling in 4:2:0 already bleeds colour 2 px across every edge and will read as a weak wrap everywhere; report only decay lengths above 3 px as evidence of a deliberate wrap.

entries.label: Lighting continuity break across a cut
entries.description: Two shots presented as the same moment differ materially in light direction, colour or level.
entries.frame_evidence: Across the cut the key jumps to the other side of the face, or the colour temperature or exposure level shifts noticeably.
entries.detector_note: At each detected cut (histogram correlation drop below 0.5 or a large frame-difference spike), compare the last stable pre-cut frame with the first stable post-cut frame on key_azimuth_deg, cct_kelvin, mean linear luminance and shadow bearing; flag deltas above 40 degrees, 800 K, 0.5 stops or 40 degrees respectively.
entries.notes: A cut to a different location or angle is supposed to change all four; without shot-grouping knowledge the analyzer cannot know the two shots are the same moment, so this must be reported as an observation with the deltas, not as an error.

entries.label: Lightning flash
entries.description: A very brief cool-white full-scene flash, often doubled, that momentarily overrides all other lighting.
entries.frame_evidence: One or two frames of near-white cool overexposure across the whole frame, with the scene otherwise dark before and after.
entries.detector_note: Detect global L surges above 2 stops lasting 1 to 4 unique cels with mean LAB b at or below 0 (cool or neutral) against a dark baseline (pre-flash median L below 0.3); count the number of surges within a 1 second window to catch the double flash.
entries.notes: Photosensitivity relevance: also emit the flash rate so a downstream harmful-flash check can use it. A white flash-frame transition in anime is identical in pixels.

entries.label: Low-key lighting
entries.description: A predominantly dark scheme where small lit areas sit in a large field of shadow.
entries.frame_evidence: The histogram is heavily weighted low with a small isolated bright lobe and large connected dark regions.
entries.detector_note: Low-key when the luminance median is below 0.30, more than 55 percent of pixels are below 0.25, and the top 5 percent of pixels occupy fewer than 12 percent of the frame while forming compact components in cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats.
entries.notes: Underexposure, a night exterior and a low-key interior all satisfy this; pair with lighting.crushed_blacks and lighting.night_exterior to attribute.

entries.label: Mains-frequency flicker (50 or 60 Hz beat)
entries.description: Whole-frame luminance pulsing from a discharge source beating against the shutter, appearing as a slow beat frequency.
entries.frame_evidence: Frame luminance oscillates at a steady low beat rate with a very regular period and constant scene content.
entries.detector_note: Welch spectrum of the per-frame (NOT per-cel, this is a capture artefact) mean L with a sharp peak, high peak-to-median power ratio above 20, and period regularity CV under 0.1; report the beat frequency and the implied alias against the container fps.
entries.notes: Photographic capture only. The actual 50 or 60 Hz is far above the frame rate, so what is measured is always an alias; do not report an absolute mains frequency.

entries.label: Missing contact shadow (object appears to float)
entries.description: An object resting on a surface has no darkening at its contact point, so it reads as pasted on.
entries.frame_evidence: The base of the subject meets the ground with no darkening whatsoever and identical luminance either side of the contact line.
entries.detector_note: Invert lighting.contact_shadow: fire when the contact band darkening is under 0.05 stops while the frame elsewhere shows a cast shadow (so the scene demonstrably has directional light) and the feet or object base are unoccluded.
entries.notes: A genuinely soft-lit scene has near-zero contact shadow legitimately; requiring evidence of directional light elsewhere in the frame is what keeps this from firing on every overcast shot.

entries.label: Mixed colour temperature in one frame
entries.description: Two or more sources of clearly different colour temperature light different parts of the same frame.
entries.frame_evidence: One side of the room or subject is warm while another is cool, with a visible transition between them.
entries.detector_note: Tile the frame 8x8, estimate the local illuminant chromaticity per tile on non-clipped mid-luminance pixels, and fire when the tile chromaticity distribution is bimodal with cluster centres separated by more than 0.03 in CIE xy and each cluster covering more than 15 percent of tiles.
entries.notes: Two differently coloured painted surfaces produce the same tile-level bimodality; the illuminant estimate cannot separate surface colour from light colour without an intrinsic-image model.

entries.label: Monochrome / near-desaturated lighting
entries.description: The frame carries almost no chroma, either from a black-and-white treatment or from very low light.
entries.frame_evidence: Chroma is near zero across the whole frame while luminance structure is normal.
entries.detector_note: Mean LAB chroma sqrt(a^2+b^2) below 4 over more than 95 percent of pixels while the luminance IQR exceeds 0.15.
entries.notes: A grey wall filling the frame also has near-zero chroma; the luminance-IQR condition keeps it from firing on flat grey plates.

entries.label: Moonlight key
entries.description: A cool, hard, distant key at night, conventionally rendered blue with visible shadows.
entries.frame_evidence: Hard-edged shadows and directional modelling in a dark, blue-cast frame, with no visible warm practical explaining them.
entries.detector_note: Dark frame (median L below 0.3) plus a directional key (key_fill_stops above 1.0) plus hard shadow edges plus cool highlights (LAB b below -5) plus no warm clipped source in frame.
entries.notes: Physically, real moonlight is neutral-to-warm and the blue is a cinematic convention; this detector measures the convention, which is the correct thing to log for a film image.

entries.label: Shadow sweeping across a subject
entries.description: A shadow travels across a face or surface over several frames, from a passing object, vehicle or light.
entries.frame_evidence: The boundary between lit and shadowed area translates steadily across the subject over a short frame window.
entries.detector_note: On UNIQUE-CEL indices, track the shadow-mask centroid over 5 to 15 frames and require a consistent displacement with cv2.calcOpticalFlowFarneback showing near-zero motion for the underlying texture (the surface stays put while the shading moves).
entries.notes: The texture-static condition is what separates a moving shadow from a moving object; computing this on duplicated cels yields zero flow that is an artefact of the twos and threes, not a static surface.

entries.label: Muzzle flash
entries.description: A one to three frame intense warm flash localised at a weapon that also lights the shooter and surroundings.
entries.frame_evidence: A very brief bright warm burst near a character's hands with a matching one-frame lift on the face and nearby walls.
entries.detector_note: On unique cels find frames where the frame max L jumps above the 3-cel rolling max by more than 40 percent for at most 3 cels, with the new energy concentrated in a component under 2 percent of frame area located within 20 percent of frame width of a mediapipe wrist landmark, and a simultaneous global mean L lift above 5 percent.
entries.notes: Cannot be told apart from a small explosion, a camera flash or a sparking impact by pixels; the wrist proximity gate is the only weapon-specific evidence and it fails when hands are not visible.

entries.label: Night exterior
entries.description: An outdoor scene at night, lit by practicals, moonlight or ambient city glow.
entries.frame_evidence: Low overall luminance with isolated bright point sources and large dark regions, and no bright sky.
entries.detector_note: Prefilter: frame median L below 0.25, more than 3 compact clipped components, upper-third not brighter than lower-third; confirm with qwen2.5vl on the full frame.
entries.vlm_question: Is this scene taking place outdoors at night? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: A dark interior satisfies every deterministic term; the indoor/outdoor split is entirely on the VLM.

entries.label: Nose shadow direction
entries.description: The bearing of the shadow the nose casts on the face, the single most reliable read of key direction on a human face.
entries.frame_evidence: A dark wedge extends from the nose base toward one side and downward, or upward under uplight.
entries.detector_note: Threshold the nose and upper-lip ROI (mediapipe 1/2/98/327/331/164) at the ROI 25th percentile of LAB L, take the largest component, and report the vector from landmark 1 to the component centroid as an angle plus a length normalised by face width.
entries.notes: Nostril openings are dark and sit exactly in this ROI; exclude components whose area is under 0.3 percent of the face bbox or that contain the nostril landmarks 218/438.

entries.label: Shadow cast by an off-screen object
entries.description: A shadow shape enters the frame with no visible object in frame that could have cast it.
entries.frame_evidence: A recognisable shadow silhouette lies across a wall or floor while the caster is outside the frame.
entries.detector_note: Prefilter: a shadow component above 2 percent of frame area that touches a frame border and has no adjacent subject mask; crop that component with 20 percent context and ask the qwen2.5vl judge.
entries.vlm_question: In this image, is there a shadow of a person or object whose body is not visible in the picture? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: A high-value storytelling beat but also the hardest shadow case; dark set dressing and vignetting both trip the prefilter, so the VLM confirm is mandatory.

entries.label: Overcast / heavy diffusion daylight
entries.description: A large diffuse sky source producing soft toplight with weak shadows and low contrast.
entries.frame_evidence: Even, slightly cool illumination, very soft or absent shadows, and a flat luminance histogram with no clipping.
entries.detector_note: Daylight-level median L, shadow area under 3 percent or all shadow edge widths above 0.02 normalised, key_fill_stops below 1.0, dr_stops_p95_p5 under 3.5, and lighting.key_toplight firing weakly on faces.
entries.notes: Studio softbox lighting is numerically identical to overcast; the entry describes the light quality, not the location.

entries.label: Partial silhouette / half-lost figure
entries.description: Part of the subject falls into unreadable darkness while another part stays lit.
entries.frame_evidence: One region of the body or face carries no recoverable detail while an adjacent region is normally exposed.
entries.detector_note: Tile the subject mask into 16 blocks, compute per-block std(L) and mean(L), and fire when at least 25 percent of blocks are below mean L 25/255 with std under 4 while at least 25 percent are above mean L 90/255.
entries.notes: Crushed encoding can manufacture the dark blocks; cross-check with lighting.crushed_blacks so the cause is attributed correctly.

entries.label: Penumbra width
entries.description: The physical width of the soft transition band at a shadow edge, which encodes the apparent size of the source.
entries.frame_evidence: The measurable gradient band between full shadow and full light along a cast shadow boundary.
entries.detector_note: For each sampled shadow-boundary normal profile, report the 10-to-90 percent rise distance in pixels; also report how that width grows with distance from the contact point, which is the source-size signature.
entries.notes: Only meaningful on a real cast shadow; on cel animation the penumbra is a drawing decision and may be exactly zero everywhere.

entries.label: Peter-panning (shadow detached from the object base)
entries.description: The cast shadow is offset from the point where the object touches the ground, so the object appears to hover.
entries.frame_evidence: A visible gap of lit ground separates the character's feet from the start of their shadow.
entries.detector_note: Measure the minimum distance in pixels from the paired shadow component to the subject mask's lowest contact point; fire when that gap exceeds 1.5 percent of frame height while the shadow is otherwise consistent in direction with the scene.
entries.notes: A jumping or airborne character legitimately has a detached shadow; gate on the pose ankles being at or near the estimated ground line and on low vertical velocity.

entries.label: Candle / open flame practical
entries.description: A small warm flame source lighting the scene, with characteristic flicker and steep falloff.
entries.frame_evidence: A small teardrop clipped highlight with a strongly warm surround and a rapid drop-off into darkness.
entries.detector_note: Prefilter deterministically: a source blob under 0.5 percent of frame area, warm (LAB b of the annulus above 20), with lighting.flicker_amplitude above 0.03 in the 6 to 15 Hz band; crop the blob plus 4x its radius and ask the qwen2.5vl judge.
entries.vlm_question: Is the bright source in this crop a candle flame or open fire? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Identifying the fixture TYPE is a semantic task; the deterministic side can only say warm, small, flickering. moondream is unreliable here, use qwen2.5vl.

entries.label: Firelight / campfire / burning practical
entries.description: A large unsteady warm source, usually below the subject, with strong low-frequency flicker.
entries.frame_evidence: Warm uplight on faces that pulses irregularly, with the brightest area low in frame.
entries.detector_note: Combine lighting.key_underlight (chin brighter than forehead) with a warm face ROI (LAB b above 18) and a flicker spectrum from scipy.signal.welch on the per-unique-cel face mean L showing energy concentrated below 12 Hz with amplitude above 0.05 of the mean.
entries.notes: Anime animates fire flicker on twos or threes, so the apparent flicker frequency is quantised by the drawing rate; report the cel rate alongside the frequency or the number is meaningless.

entries.label: Fluorescent tube / overhead office light
entries.description: A broad greenish overhead source producing even flat toplight, characteristic of institutional interiors.
entries.frame_evidence: Long bright rectangles in the ceiling with a slightly green cast on skin and even top-down illumination.
entries.detector_note: Bright elongated rectangular components in the upper third (regionprops extent above 0.8, aspect above 4), combined with a scene-wide green bias measured as mean LAB a below -3 on neutral-looking mid-grey pixels and lighting.key_toplight firing on faces.
entries.notes: Any green grade produces the same LAB a bias; the ceiling-rectangle geometry is the load-bearing part of this detector.

entries.label: Vehicle headlights
entries.description: A pair of intense moving sources, usually with visible beams and a raking sweep across the scene.
entries.frame_evidence: Two bright blobs at similar height separated horizontally, with a lit cone ahead of them, translating across the frame.
entries.detector_note: Prefilter: exactly two clipped blobs of similar area within 5 percent of frame height of each other, moving coherently across unique cels; crop the pair plus surroundings and ask qwen2.5vl.
entries.vlm_question: Are the two bright lights in this crop the headlights of a vehicle? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Two street lamps, two windows or a pair of eyes-glow effects all pass the geometric prefilter.

entries.label: Practical demonstrably lights the subject
entries.description: A visible source and the subject's illumination change together, proving the source is actually the key rather than decorative.
entries.frame_evidence: When the visible fixture brightens or dims, the light on the face moves in step within the same frame window.
entries.detector_note: On unique cels, compute the Pearson correlation between the source blob's mean L and the face ROI mean L over a 15 cel window with a lag search of plus or minus 2 cels; report the correlation and best lag.
entries.notes: Needs actual variation in the source; on a perfectly steady practical the correlation is undefined and the entry must log NOT DETECTABLE, not NOT FOUND.

entries.label: Household lamp / incandescent practical
entries.description: A steady warm domestic fixture such as a table lamp, sconce or bare bulb lighting the scene.
entries.frame_evidence: A steady warm clipped source with a shade-shaped falloff pool on a nearby wall or table.
entries.detector_note: Prefilter: source blob with warm annulus (LAB b above 15), flicker amplitude below 0.01, and a cone or pool of elevated luminance on an adjacent surface; crop and ask the qwen2.5vl judge.
entries.vlm_question: Is the light source in this crop a lamp or light bulb fixture? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Sodium street lamps, torches and firelight all read as warm steady sources deterministically; the type split is entirely on the VLM.

entries.label: Neon / LED sign practical
entries.description: A highly saturated narrow-band source, typically magenta, cyan or green, lighting the scene and often visible as tube shapes.
entries.frame_evidence: Extremely saturated clipped strokes or letters with a coloured glow spilling onto nearby surfaces.
entries.detector_note: Find components where HSV S exceeds 0.75 and V exceeds 0.9 covering 0.02 to 3 percent of frame; require a stroke-like shape (regionprops eccentricity above 0.9 or skeleton length over area ratio high) and a coloured halo whose hue matches the core within 15 degrees.
entries.notes: Saturated graphics, UI overlays and subtitle karaoke colours pass the colour test; the halo-hue-match requirement is what ties it to actual emission into the scene.

entries.label: Off-screen practical implied by its pool of light
entries.description: A source outside the frame whose presence is evident only from the light pool, spill or beam it throws inside it.
entries.frame_evidence: A bright pool or wedge anchored at a frame edge, falling off inward, with no emitter visible.
entries.detector_note: Fit a 2D quadratic to the low-frequency luminance field (L downsampled to 32x18, cv2.GaussianBlur); fire when the fitted maximum lies outside the frame bounds and the luminance falls monotonically inward from one border with a gradient above 0.15 of mean L per frame width.
entries.notes: Vignetting produces the opposite sign and a bright sky at the top of frame produces the same one; require the gradient direction to be inconsistent with a simple sky or vignette model.

entries.label: Screen glow (monitor, phone, TV) on a face
entries.description: A face or room lit by a display, giving cool blue-white light from a broad low-intensity panel that changes with the content.
entries.frame_evidence: A face lit from below-front by a cool wash whose colour and level shift over a few seconds as the screen content changes.
entries.detector_note: On UNIQUE-CEL indices track the face-ROI mean LAB a, b and L; screen glow when the face is cool (b below -5), the key azimuth is near-frontal and slightly low, and the face-ROI chroma has a temporal std above 3 LAB units over a 2 second window with no corresponding change in the background.
entries.notes: The temporal colour wobble is the real signature; a static blue key gives no wobble and reads as ordinary cool light. Colour-graded night interiors also drift and can mimic it.

entries.label: Practical light source visible in frame
entries.description: The emitting fixture itself is inside the frame, not merely implied by its effect.
entries.frame_evidence: A compact region at or near clipping with a surrounding glow falloff sits inside the picture.
entries.detector_note: Threshold L above the 99.5th percentile, run cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats, keep components between 0.01 and 5 percent of frame area whose surrounding 30 px annulus shows a monotone radial luminance falloff fitted by scipy.optimize.curve_fit on an inverse-square or exponential model.
entries.notes: Specular highlights on chrome and water pass the same test; the radial falloff exponent and the blob's colour saturation are the separators, and a genuine emitter usually clips.

entries.label: Torch or lantern carried by a character
entries.description: A hand-held warm source that moves with the character, so its lighting pool travels with them.
entries.frame_evidence: A bright warm blob near a hand with a surrounding pool of light that translates as the hand moves.
entries.detector_note: Track mediapipe pose wrist landmarks 15/16 (or hands landmarks) across unique cels and test whether the brightest local blob within 15 percent of frame width of the wrist moves with correlation above 0.8 against the wrist trajectory.
entries.notes: Fails when the hand is occluded or out of frame; also fires on a reflective object held in the hand, so the warm-annulus and falloff terms must hold too.

entries.label: TV flicker in a dark room
entries.description: A room lit only by a television, where overall room luminance and colour jump on cuts in the unseen programme.
entries.frame_evidence: The whole room brightness steps at irregular intervals of roughly one to five seconds with colour shifts, while nothing in the room moves.
entries.detector_note: On unique cels, compute frame mean L and mean LAB a,b; fire on step changes above 15 percent in L or 5 units in chroma that are global (present in more than 70 percent of frame tiles), with global optical flow below 0.5 px, at irregular intervals (inter-step interval CV above 0.5).
entries.notes: Auto-exposure pumping produces global steps too; the discriminator is that AE steps follow a large scene change while TV flicker does not, and TV flicker carries chroma steps.

entries.label: Precise shadow region segmentation
entries.description: Pixel-accurate separation of shadow from dark surface colour, which everything downstream about shadows depends on.
entries.frame_evidence: The exact boundary of every shadow region in the frame, including on textured and dark-albedo surfaces.
entries.detector_note: Requires a trained shadow-detection network (BDRAR, MTMT or a modern segmentation model). None is installed; the deterministic chroma-ratio heuristic used by lighting.cast_shadow_present is a low-precision stand-in and its errors propagate into shadow direction, length, softness and every consistency check built on them.
entries.notes: Log as NOT DETECTABLE. This is the single largest blind spot in this domain: roughly a third of the entries here are gated on a shadow mask that is a heuristic, and their confidence should be reported as inherited-low.

entries.label: Pulsing / breathing light
entries.description: A slow smooth sinusoidal rise and fall in level, typical of alarm lights, magical effects and heartbeat cues.
entries.frame_evidence: Region luminance swells and recedes smoothly over roughly half a second to several seconds.
entries.detector_note: Welch spectrum peak below 3 Hz with spectral flatness under 0.4 and a low crest factor (peak/RMS under 1.6, indicating a smooth rather than pulsed waveform), measured on the source-blob ROI where a blob exists.
entries.notes: Needs a shot long enough to hold at least 3 cycles; on shots shorter than that report NOT DETECTABLE.

entries.label: Rim hue differs from key hue
entries.description: The rim light is a materially different colour temperature from the key, for example a cool rim over a warm key.
entries.frame_evidence: The edge band is visibly bluer or warmer than the lit planes of the subject face and body.
entries.detector_note: Compare the mean LAB b of the rim band against the mean LAB b of the lit interior region (interior pixels above the interior L median); fire when the b delta exceeds 8 units, and report the implied direction of colour-temperature offset.
entries.notes: Any global grade with split toning shifts highlights toward one hue and will move the rim with them; check lighting.split_toning_warm_cool before attributing this to a separate fixture.

entries.label: Rim light
entries.description: A bright outline separating the subject from the background, produced by a light behind and to the side.
entries.frame_evidence: A thin continuous bright band hugs part of the subject silhouette and is brighter than both the subject interior and the adjacent background.
entries.detector_note: Subject mask from mediapipe selfie_segmentation; band = mask XOR cv2.erode(mask, 5x5, iters=1); rim when the band mean L exceeds the eroded-interior mean L by >1.0 stop over a contiguous arc covering at least 8 percent of the contour length measured on the cv2.findContours perimeter.
entries.notes: Matting fringe, JPEG ringing and white clothing edges all produce a bright annulus; require the band to be brighter than the background too, not just the interior.

entries.label: Rim light with no source in the scene
entries.description: A rim or edge light appears on a subject in a scene that offers nothing behind them to produce it.
entries.frame_evidence: A bright silhouette edge sits against a flat dark background containing no visible or implied light source.
entries.detector_note: Prefilter with lighting.rim_light firing while the background region contains no pixels above the 99.5th luminance percentile of the frame; crop the subject plus surrounding background and put the question to qwen2.5vl.
entries.vlm_question: In this image, is there any visible light source behind the person that could explain the bright glow on the edge of their body? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Stylised lighting deliberately breaks this rule, so a hit is a note about the image, not an error; off-screen sources are legitimate and the VLM cannot see them.

entries.label: Rolling-shutter light banding
entries.description: Horizontal luminance bands drifting vertically, caused by a mains-frequency source beating against a rolling-shutter sensor.
entries.frame_evidence: Broad horizontal light and dark bars slide up or down the frame while the scene content stays still.
entries.detector_note: Compute the per-row mean L profile per frame, take the 1D FFT along rows and look for a dominant low spatial frequency peak whose phase advances monotonically across consecutive frames.
entries.notes: Live-action capture only; an animated file cannot exhibit this, so on a 2D or CG source a hit means the plate was photographed or the artefact was deliberately simulated. | TIER CORRECTED by completeness critic: All three deterministic while frame_metrics.rolling_shutter_skew - the primitive they all rest on - is marked unsupported. A direct, load-bearing contradiction: whoever writes the code will implement it three times or ze

entries.label: Self shadow / form shadow
entries.description: The part of an object that is dark because it faces away from the light rather than because something blocks the light.
entries.frame_evidence: A gradient-bounded dark region on the object itself that follows the object's own curvature.
entries.detector_note: On the face, take the mediapipe mesh region whose fitted Lambertian n.l is negative and confirm that region is darker than the predicted lit region by more than 0.7 stops; on the body use the pose-derived torso and limb ROIs and compare the two sides of each limb.
entries.notes: The separation between form shadow and cast shadow is exactly the thing the pixel test cannot make; the landmark route works only where a mesh exists.

entries.label: Banded shading ramp
entries.description: A shading gradient broken into visible discrete steps by quantisation or a stepped toon ramp.
entries.frame_evidence: Parallel bands of constant value march across what should be a smooth gradient, most visible on skies and walls.
entries.detector_note: In a low-texture region (Laplacian std below noise floor x 2) take the L profile along the gradient direction; count monotone plateaus of length above 4 px separated by steps of 1 to 4 L units using scipy.signal.find_peaks on the derivative.
entries.notes: Distinguishing render banding from codec banding is not possible from pixels alone; report the observation, not the cause.

entries.label: Shadow acne / shadow-map shimmer
entries.description: High-frequency crawling stipple or flickering stair-stepped edges from an under-resolved shadow map.
entries.frame_evidence: The shadow boundary crawls, sparkles or steps in blocks and changes pattern frame to frame even when nothing moves.
entries.detector_note: On UNIQUE-CEL indices with near-zero global optical flow, compute the temporal std of L restricted to a 5 px band around the shadow contour; fire when that band std exceeds 3x the temporal std of the interior region, and confirm high spatial frequency energy at the contour via a high-pass FFT.
entries.notes: Codec noise concentrates at edges too; require the effect to persist at multiple bitrates or on the highest-quality decode before calling it a render artefact.

entries.label: Shadow colour tint
entries.description: The hue the shadows carry, typically the fill or sky colour, most often cool blue under warm sun.
entries.frame_evidence: The dark regions read visibly blue, purple or green rather than a neutral darker version of the lit colour.
entries.detector_note: Compare mean LAB a and b of pixels in the lower luminance tercile against the upper tercile within the same material region; report the delta in a and b and the implied hue angle of the shadow tint.
entries.notes: This is the same measurement as lighting.split_toning_warm_cool from a different angle; they will co-fire and that is correct, one is about lighting physics and one about grade.

entries.label: Shadow geometry physically consistent with the scene
entries.description: Whether every shadow in the frame is geometrically consistent with a single scene geometry and light placement.
entries.frame_evidence: Shadow shapes, lengths and convergence across many objects at different depths in one frame.
entries.detector_note: Requires scene depth, ground-plane orientation and object geometry, none of which are recoverable from a single frame with the installed stack; monocular depth would need a model that is not installed, and even with depth the shadow-caster association problem remains open.
entries.notes: Log as NOT DETECTABLE. The weaker two-dimensional proxies (lighting.cast_shadow_conflicts_with_key and lighting.cast_shadow_direction circular std) are what is actually available, and they only catch gross violations.

entries.label: No shadow anywhere in a directionally lit scene
entries.description: The scene shows clear directional key modelling but contains no cast shadow of any kind.
entries.frame_evidence: Faces and objects have strong lit and shadow sides while every ground and wall surface is uniformly lit.
entries.detector_note: Fire when lighting.key_fill_stops exceeds 1.5 and lighting.hard_light holds on the terminator, but the shadow-candidate mask covers under 0.5 percent of the frame outside the subject mask across the whole shot.
entries.notes: Perfectly legitimate when the ground is out of frame or the subject is against sky; require at least 20 percent of the frame to be a plausible receiving surface below the subject.

entries.label: Detail retained in the shadow side
entries.description: Whether the shadow side still carries readable texture and form or has gone to a featureless black.
entries.frame_evidence: The dark half of the subject either shows visible fabric, skin or hair structure, or is a flat void.
entries.detector_note: Inside the shadow-side ROI compute the std of cv2.Laplacian(L, cv2.CV_32F) and the fraction of pixels below L=8/255; retention is high when Laplacian std exceeds the noise floor estimated from a flat patch by 3x.
entries.notes: Codec noise in dark regions is itself high-frequency and inflates the Laplacian std; the flat-patch noise floor is the required null.

entries.label: Full silhouette
entries.description: The subject is rendered as a solid dark shape with no interior detail against a much brighter field.
entries.frame_evidence: The subject region is near-uniformly dark with almost no internal luminance variance while the surround is bright.
entries.detector_note: Subject mask interior mean L below 15 percent of the background mean L, interior std(L) under 6 units on 0-255, and the interior 95th percentile below the background 5th percentile.
entries.notes: Requires a subject mask; when segmentation fails on a stylised 2D figure, fall back to skimage.filters.threshold_otsu on the whole frame and treat the dark class as the candidate shape.

entries.label: Skin sheen / sweat specular
entries.description: Broad low-level specular across skin from oil or sweat, giving a wet or glistening look.
entries.frame_evidence: The forehead, nose bridge and cheekbones carry elevated, desaturated brightness beyond the diffuse shading.
entries.detector_note: In the mediapipe forehead, nose-bridge (168/6/197) and cheekbone ROIs, measure the fraction of pixels whose saturation is below the face-median saturation while their L is above the face 85th percentile; report that fraction and its spatial concentration on the classic sheen zones.
entries.notes: Overlaps directly with the waxy-skin failure mode seen in generated stills; sheen and plastic-render waxiness are the same measurement with different causes and this entry must not claim to distinguish them.

entries.label: Smooth continuous shading (3D render)
entries.description: Continuous-tone shading across a surface characteristic of a rendered or photographed object rather than cel fills.
entries.frame_evidence: Luminance across a surface varies smoothly with no step boundaries and many intermediate values.
entries.detector_note: Histogram of L inside a surface region has entropy above 5.0 bits with no bin exceeding 15 percent, and the profile derivative has no peak above 15 L units per pixel after gaussian smoothing.
entries.notes: Toon-shaded 3D deliberately mimics 2D and will be classified as cel; that is a correct observation of the image and should not be corrected by asset-type assumptions.

entries.label: Soft light quality
entries.description: A large or heavily diffused source producing broad gradual shadow transitions and wide speculars.
entries.frame_evidence: Shadow edges spread over many pixels and highlights are large, dim and diffuse.
entries.detector_note: Same boundary-profile fit as lighting.hard_light with the opposite verdict: soft when the median normalised transition width exceeds 0.015 and no shadow boundary in the frame is sharper than 0.008.
entries.notes: Defocus makes hard light look soft; require an in-focus reference edge (a face landmark edge or text edge) to be sharp in the same frame before calling the light soft.

entries.label: Specular highlight present
entries.description: A mirror-like reflection of the source on a glossy surface, distinct from diffuse shading.
entries.frame_evidence: A small very bright spot whose position depends on the viewing angle, on skin, metal, glass or wet surfaces.
entries.detector_note: Candidate speculars are pixels in the top 1 percent of L whose saturation is markedly lower than the surrounding region (specular reflections take the source colour, diluting surface chroma); keep compact components under 0.2 percent of frame area with a steep radial falloff.
entries.notes: Small emitters and bright white objects both pass; the saturation-drop-relative-to-surround test is the only cheap separator and it fails on already-white surfaces.

entries.label: Specular highlight travel
entries.description: A highlight sliding across a surface as the object, camera or light moves, which reveals surface curvature and light position.
entries.frame_evidence: The bright spot on a curved object migrates across the surface over a short window while the object outline barely changes.
entries.detector_note: Track specular component centroids across unique cels with nearest-neighbour association, and report the centroid displacement relative to the displacement of the host object's mask centroid; travel is present when the ratio exceeds 2.
entries.notes: Association breaks when a highlight splits or is briefly occluded; report track length so short unreliable tracks can be discounted. In 2D the highlight is drawn and may pop rather than travel.

entries.label: Warm highlights against cool shadows (split toning)
entries.description: Highlights and shadows carry opposing hues, either from real warm key plus cool ambient or from a grade.
entries.frame_evidence: Bright areas skew orange while dark areas skew blue within the same surface.
entries.detector_note: Split pixels into luminance terciles, compute mean LAB a,b per tercile, and report the hue-angle difference between the top and bottom tercile plus the chroma of each; fire when the hue difference exceeds 60 degrees and both chromas exceed 6.
entries.notes: Confounded by content (a blue sky in the shadows tercile of a backlit shot); restrict to a single material region where possible.

entries.label: Strobe lighting
entries.description: Rapid on-off pulsing where the scene alternates between lit and dark at a high regular rate.
entries.frame_evidence: Frame luminance alternates between two well-separated levels at a regular short period.
entries.detector_note: Bimodality test on the per-unique-cel mean L series (dip test proxy: fit two Gaussians via a 2-means split on the 1D series and require the separation to exceed 2x the within-cluster std) combined with a regular alternation period from scipy.signal.find_peaks; report pulses per second.
entries.notes: Emit strobe_rate_hz unconditionally so a photosensitive-content check can use it; note that the true strobe rate may exceed what the unique-cel rate can represent and would then be aliased.

entries.label: Terminator sharpness on a curved surface
entries.description: How abruptly shading falls off across the lit-to-unlit boundary on a rounded form such as a cheek or a sphere.
entries.frame_evidence: The gradient across the boundary on the face or a rounded prop is either a step or a long ramp.
entries.detector_note: Extract an L profile along the horizontal line through the mediapipe nose tip across the face bbox, smooth with scipy.ndimage.gaussian_filter1d(sigma=2), and report the maximum absolute derivative and the width over which 80 percent of the total drop occurs.
entries.notes: Hair, glasses and beard boundaries crossing the profile line create false steps; take the median over 5 parallel profile lines.

entries.label: Visible volumetric cone from a source
entries.description: A single lamp, torch or headlight whose beam is visible in the air as a cone or wedge.
entries.frame_evidence: A triangular brighter region widening away from a visible source blob, with soft edges and no texture of its own.
entries.detector_note: Anchored at a detected source blob, sample luminance along rays at 2 degree increments; a cone is present when a contiguous angular sector shows elevated luminance above the surrounding sectors with a width that grows linearly with radius and a low Laplacian variance inside it.
entries.notes: A lit floor pool in front of a lamp gives the same radial signature; the low-texture interior condition is what separates air from a lit surface, and it fails on a plain floor.

entries.label: Warm key light
entries.description: The dominant light on the subject is orange or amber biased.
entries.frame_evidence: Lit planes of the face and objects carry a yellow-orange cast relative to the shadowed planes.
entries.detector_note: Take the top luminance tercile of the subject region excluding clipped pixels, convert to LAB, and fire when mean b exceeds 12 and mean a exceeds 2; report the chromaticity of that highlight set as the illuminant estimate.
entries.notes: Skin is intrinsically warm, so measuring on a face alone always reads warm; prefer a neutral-looking surface region, and always report which region carried the measurement.

entries.label: Wet surface specular (rain, road, skin)
entries.description: A surface made reflective by water, producing elongated streaked reflections of lights.
entries.frame_evidence: Vertically streaked bright reflections below light sources on the ground and high-contrast mottled speculars.
entries.detector_note: Below each detected source blob, test for an elongated bright region whose major axis is near-vertical (within 20 degrees), whose length exceeds 3x its width, and whose hue matches the source within 20 degrees.
entries.notes: A mirror, polished floor or still water gives the same signature without rain; this measures reflectivity, not wetness.

entries.label: White balance drifts inside a shot
entries.description: The overall colour cast changes during a continuous shot, from auto white balance hunting or a practical change.
entries.frame_evidence: Neutral surfaces drift from warm to cool or back across the shot without any scene change.
entries.detector_note: Track the estimated illuminant chromaticity per unique cel; fire when the total CIE xy travel exceeds 0.02 with a monotone or single-reversal trajectory while histogram correlation between the first and last frame exceeds 0.7 (same scene).
entries.notes: Content entering frame (a red coat walking in) moves the grey-world estimate; use a static background tile set as the reference region.

entries.label: Anime hair clump secondary motion
entries.description: The characteristic pointed hair clumps of 2D character design moving as semi-independent flaps.
entries.frame_evidence: Individual hair spikes change angle relative to the head between key cels while their roots stay put.
entries.detector_note: Hair contour from the mediapipe face-mesh-anchored band; find elongated protrusions via cv2.convexityDefects on the contour and track each protrusion tip's angle about its root across unique cels.
entries.notes: Clump correspondence between cels is fragile when the head turns; only report the aggregate fraction, never per-clump identity across a turn. mediapipe face-mesh and pose are unreliable on stylised 2D faces and on non-human characters, which is exactly where this entry matters most; report unmeasurable on low mesh confidence rather than reporting zero.

entries.label: Anticipation windup
entries.description: A brief motion opposite to the main action, taken before the action itself.
entries.frame_evidence: The prop moves a short distance the wrong way, then reverses into the full move.
entries.detector_note: In the 6 unique cels before a detected large move, look for a displacement whose direction is >120 degrees from the main move's direction and whose magnitude is 5-25% of it.
entries.notes: Absence is meaningful for a stylistic report (no anticipation = stiff animation) but must not be reported as an error. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification.

entries.label: Apex / hang frame
entries.description: The top of a ballistic arc where vertical velocity passes through zero.
entries.frame_evidence: One or more cels where the object stops climbing and has not yet begun to fall, often held slightly longer than physics allows.
entries.detector_note: Sign change of the first difference of the y-track; report the number of unique cels within 10% of the peak height as a hang-time measure.
entries.notes: A hang of >2 unique cels against a fitted parabola is deliberate stylisation (floaty hang), worth logging as a style trait not an error. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification.

entries.label: Wrong-gravity / miniature look
entries.description: A prop whose fall acceleration is inconsistent with its apparent physical size, reading as a toy or as slow-motion.
entries.frame_evidence: A large object drifting down too slowly, or a small one snapping down too fast, relative to its screen size.
entries.detector_note: Convert the fitted px/cel^2 to px/s^2 using fps and the unique-cel ratio, normalise by the prop's silhouette height in px, and compare against the dimensionless g*h/v^2 band expected for the VLM-declared object class.
entries.notes: Only meaningful once the object class and thus a real-world size prior is known; without that prior the number is unanchored. Also fires legitimately on intentional slow motion. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification.

entries.label: Ballistic parabolic arc
entries.description: A free-flying prop following a parabolic path under constant downward acceleration.
entries.frame_evidence: The centroid trail rises, flattens and falls with a symmetric curve about the apex.
entries.detector_note: numpy.polyfit(t, y, 2) and numpy.polyfit(t, x, 1) on the unique-cel track; report the quadratic coefficient (2a = gravity in px/cel^2), the residual RMS and R^2.
entries.notes: Needs >=5 unique cels of unoccluded flight; a camera that moves during the arc must be compensated first or the fit measures the camera. All temporal terms are computed on UNIQUE-CEL indices (duplicate-frame runs collapsed via mean abs frame diff < 0.5/255); raw-fps sampling reports zero motion on held cels. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification.

entries.label: Bend / flex of an elongated body
entries.description: A long rigid-ish prop curving under load instead of staying straight.
entries.frame_evidence: The medial axis of an elongated silhouette bows away from the line joining its ends.
entries.detector_note: skimage.morphology.medial_axis on the ROI mask, order the skeleton points, fit a quadratic and report the max curvature and the mid-point deviation from the endpoint chord.
entries.notes: Skeletonisation of a mask with holes or a fringed edge produces spurious branches; prune branches shorter than 15% of the main path first. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification.

entries.label: Bounce sequence with decaying apex
entries.description: Repeated impacts against a surface, each rebound reaching a lower apex than the previous one.
entries.frame_evidence: The vertical position track shows successive local minima at the surface line separated by successively shorter arcs.
entries.detector_note: scipy.signal.find_peaks on the negated y-track for contacts and on y for apexes; the restitution estimate is sqrt(h_{n+1}/h_n) per bounce pair.
entries.notes: A physically consistent sequence has both the apex heights AND the intervals shrinking by the same ratio; only the heights shrinking is a classic hand-animated error worth reporting. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification.

entries.label: Burn-through hole
entries.description: Material consumed from the inside outward, leaving a growing hole with a hot or charred rim.
entries.frame_evidence: A hole opens in the middle of a surface and expands, its edge ringed by bright orange or darkened pixels.
entries.detector_note: Detect an interior hole via cv2.findContours with RETR_CCOMP (child contours), track its area growth, and measure the mean hue in a 5 px dilation ring (orange band H in [5,25] in OpenCV units) or a luminance drop for charring.
entries.notes: A pre-existing hole in a moving object also grows in projection when it rotates toward camera; require the rim signature. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification.

entries.label: Cape / cloak trailing lag
entries.description: A cape following the wearer's motion with a delay and a trailing arc.
entries.frame_evidence: The cape's mass is displaced opposite the direction of travel and reaches its extreme after the body does.
entries.detector_note: Define the body ROI from mediapipe pose shoulders (11/12) and hips (23/24) and the cape ROI as the region below and behind that box; cross-correlate their velocity signals across unique cels for the lag, and measure the cape's mean offset direction against the body velocity.
entries.notes: The cape ROI is a heuristic band, not a segmentation; it will include background whenever the character is against a busy plate. mediapipe also loses the pose entirely on stylised or non-human characters.

entries.label: Chain link articulation
entries.description: Whether a chain bends at its links or as a smooth continuous curve.
entries.frame_evidence: Individual links visibly hinge against each other along the bend.
entries.detector_note: Would need a link detector or per-link instance segmentation to identify individual links and their relative angles; nothing installed can segment repeated small link geometry reliably.
entries.notes: Logged as a known blind spot. At typical delivery resolutions the links are a few pixels and no available detector resolves them.

entries.label: Cloth passing through the body
entries.description: Garment geometry poking through the character it clothes.
entries.frame_evidence: Skin or an inner surface appears on the wrong side of the garment for a few frames.
entries.detector_note: Crop tightly around the garment-body boundary (elbow, knee, shoulder from mediapipe pose landmarks) on candidate cels flagged by a local flow discontinuity, and query the VLM.
entries.vlm_question: Is a piece of the body or skin poking through the clothing in this image? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Small VLMs are unreliable on this and over-answer yes on any busy crop; require agreement across 2 consecutive cels and treat as a lead, not a finding. THE CROP RULE applies.

entries.label: Curtain / drape pendular sway
entries.description: A hanging cloth swinging as a whole about its top attachment.
entries.frame_evidence: The free lower edge swings side to side while the top edge stays fixed.
entries.detector_note: Track the lower-edge horizontal centroid over unique cels; fit a damped sinusoid and check that the upper-edge centroid variance stays below 10% of the lower edge's.
entries.notes: Requires the top edge to be visible in frame; a cropped curtain gives no anchor and the metric is unanchored. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification.

entries.label: Flag / banner flutter
entries.description: A wind-driven travelling wave running along a fixed-edge cloth.
entries.frame_evidence: Ripple crests visibly move from the attached edge toward the free edge, cel after cel.
entries.detector_note: Sample columns across the cloth ROI, build a per-column vertical-centroid signal, then measure the phase lag between adjacent columns' oscillations (numpy.correlate or scipy.signal.csd) to recover a travelling-wave speed and direction.
entries.notes: The single most useful cloth defect this catches is a phase lag of exactly zero across all columns: the whole cloth oscillating in unison is a rigid parented flap, not cloth. All temporal terms are computed on UNIQUE-CEL indices (duplicate-frame runs collapsed via mean abs frame diff < 0.5/255); raw-fps sampling reports zero motion on held cels. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification.

entries.label: Frozen cloth during body motion
entries.description: Cloth that does not move at all while the body it belongs to clearly does.
entries.frame_evidence: The garment silhouette is pixel-identical across cels while the wearer translates or turns.
entries.detector_note: Body ROI from the mediapipe pose torso box (landmarks 11/12/23/24); garment ROI as the band below and around it; ratio of mean |Farneback flow| in the garment ROI to the body ROI after global camera compensation, flagged below 0.1 over >=5 unique cels.
entries.notes: Legitimately fires on stiff materials (armour, leather) and on tight clothing; the finding must be phrased as no-secondary-motion, not as a defect. All temporal terms are computed on UNIQUE-CEL indices (duplicate-frame runs collapsed via mean abs frame diff < 0.5/255); raw-fps sampling reports zero motion on held cels. mediapipe face-mesh and pose are unreliable on stylised 2D faces and on non-human characters, which is exactly where this entry matters most; report unmeasurable on low mesh confidence rather than reporting zero.

entries.label: Pinned constraint point
entries.description: The point at which a cloth is attached, around which everything else moves.
entries.frame_evidence: One spot on the cloth is motionless across the window while the surrounding fabric displaces.
entries.detector_note: Per-cel dense Farneback flow inside the cloth ROI; find local minima of |v| that persist across >=5 unique cels while the ROI's mean |v| is high.
entries.notes: A flat untextured region gives zero flow through the aperture problem and reads as a false pin; require local texture (Laplacian variance) above a floor at the candidate point. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification.

entries.label: Cloth settling after motion
entries.description: Cloth continuing to move briefly and then coming to rest after the body stops.
entries.frame_evidence: The garment ripples for a few cels past the body's last movement, then goes still.
entries.detector_note: Body motion-stop cel from the mediapipe pose torso centroid velocity; then count unique cels until the pose-anchored garment ROI's mean |Farneback flow| falls below its static floor.
entries.notes: A lag of zero (cloth stops on the same cel as the body) is the reportable finding: real cloth always overruns. mediapipe face-mesh and pose are unreliable on stylised 2D faces and on non-human characters, which is exactly where this entry matters most; report unmeasurable on low mesh confidence rather than reporting zero.

entries.label: Cloth sim jitter / crawl
entries.description: High-frequency noise in a cloth simulation, seen as a crawling or buzzing surface.
entries.frame_evidence: Wrinkle lines shimmer and change every frame without any coherent travelling direction.
entries.detector_note: Temporal high-pass of the per-pixel flow field inside the cloth ROI; report the fraction of flow energy above 0.35 cycles/cel and the spatial incoherence (local flow-direction entropy).
entries.notes: Video compression noise is also high-frequency; measure the same statistics on a static region of the same frame as a null and report the ratio. entries.label: Clothing sway with gait
entries.description: Loose garment motion driven by, and phase-locked to, the wearer's step cycle.
entries.frame_evidence: The garment's swing peaks alternate with the footfalls.
entries.detector_note: Get the step cycle from mediapipe pose ankles (27/28) vertical signal; get the garment signal from a hip-anchored ROI; report the coherence and phase offset between the two via scipy.signal.coherence.
entries.notes: A garment period that is not the gait period or half of it is a strong tell of an unlinked cloth sim or a cycled cel. Fails when the legs are off-frame.

entries.label: Constant-velocity glide
entries.description: A prop translating at effectively unchanging speed, the signature of an unaccelerated or floating body.
entries.frame_evidence: Equal-length displacement steps between every consecutive unique cel for the whole window.
entries.detector_note: Coefficient of variation of |v[k]| over the unique-cel track below 0.15 for >=6 cels, with |a| below the tracker noise floor measured on a static background patch.
entries.notes: A too-perfect CV (<0.02) is often a linear keyframe interpolation, i.e. an animation smell rather than physics. entries.label: Contact frame identification
entries.description: The specific cel on which two bodies actually touch.
entries.frame_evidence: The gap between the two silhouettes closes to zero and at least one of them changes velocity on that cel.
entries.detector_note: Per-cel minimum distance between the two ROI contours via cv2.pointPolygonTest sampling; contact = the argmin cel, confirmed by a |dv| spike on the same or the next unique cel.
entries.notes: Occlusion makes two objects at different depths appear to touch; a contact with no velocity change on either body should be reported as apparent-only. entries.label: Interpenetration at contact
entries.description: One solid body visibly passes into another instead of stopping at its surface.
entries.frame_evidence: The two silhouettes overlap in a region where an occlusion boundary should be, with no consistent depth ordering.
entries.detector_note: Crop a 1.6x box around the detected contact point on the contact cel and the following two unique cels and query the VLM; deterministic mask overlap only pre-filters candidate crops.
entries.vlm_question: Does one solid object pass through or sink into the other object in this image, instead of stopping at its surface? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Ordinary occlusion looks identical to interpenetration in a single 2D projection; small VLMs answer yes far too often, so treat a lone yes as low confidence and require agreement on >=2 consecutive crops. THE CROP RULE applies: never ask this on the full frame.

entries.label: Conveyor / tread translation
entries.description: A surface texture translating continuously along a fixed path while the body stays put.
entries.frame_evidence: Belt markings or tread lugs slide steadily along the belt line with a stationary housing.
entries.detector_note: Dense Farneback flow inside the belt ROI showing uniform velocity along the belt axis while the housing ROI shows near-zero flow.
entries.notes: The aperture problem makes an untextured belt read as stationary; require texture (Laplacian variance) above a floor. entries.label: Crack propagation
entries.description: A fracture line growing across a surface over successive cels.
entries.frame_evidence: A thin dark line appears and lengthens, branching or not, without the body separating yet.
entries.detector_note: Ridge/line response via skimage.filters.frangi or Canny on the ROI, binarise, skimage.morphology.skeletonize, and track total skeleton length per unique cel; require monotonic growth.
entries.notes: Any drawn line art (hatching, panel lines, wrinkles) produces skeleton length; the discriminator is MONOTONIC GROWTH from near-zero on a previously clean surface. All temporal terms are computed on UNIQUE-CEL indices (duplicate-frame runs collapsed via mean abs frame diff < 0.5/255); raw-fps sampling reports zero motion on held cels. entries.label: Crumble / disintegration
entries.description: A body progressively erodes into small particles rather than splitting into large shards.
entries.frame_evidence: The silhouette loses area from its edges cel by cel while a fine particle field grows below it.
entries.detector_note: Monotonic ROI mask area decay combined with a rising count of small (<0.5% of parent area) components in the region below; report the area half-life in cels.
entries.notes: Dissolve transitions and fade-outs erode area identically; require the small-component field to be present and to move downward. entries.label: Dangling accessory secondary motion
entries.description: Small hanging items (earrings, tags, charms, straps) reacting to the wearer's motion.
entries.frame_evidence: A small element below an attachment point swings a beat after the body moves.
entries.detector_note: Anchor small ROIs at mediapipe face-mesh ear points or pose shoulder/hip landmarks; measure each small ROI's residual motion after registering out the parent's motion, and its lag by cross-correlation.
entries.notes: At delivery resolution these elements are often under 10 px across and below the tracker's reliable scale; report unmeasurable rather than zero.

entries.label: Debris cloud expansion
entries.description: The outward-expanding field of fragments and dust following a break.
entries.frame_evidence: Many small elements spreading roughly radially from a common origin over several cels.
entries.detector_note: Fit a common origin to the small components' velocity vectors (least-squares intersection of back-projected lines) and report the mean radial speed and the isotropy of the angular histogram.
entries.notes: Gravity biases the later cels downward, lowering isotropy legitimately; measure isotropy on the first 3 cels only. entries.label: Falling debris shower
entries.description: Many small elements falling together through the frame.
entries.frame_evidence: A field of small blobs all moving downward with similar speeds and slight spread.
entries.detector_note: cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats on the diff mask plus dense flow; require >=10 small components with a downward-dominant flow histogram and a positive mean vertical acceleration.
entries.notes: Rain, snow and falling leaves all match; separation needs shape and terminal-velocity statistics that overlap heavily. Report as a falling-particle field, and let a VLM name it. entries.label: Dent (permanent deformation)
entries.description: An impact leaves a lasting concavity in a body that does not spring back.
entries.frame_evidence: The silhouette gains a persistent inward notch at the impact point after the impact cel.
entries.detector_note: cv2.convexHull minus cv2.contourArea gives a convexity-defect measure per cel; flag a step increase at the contact cel that persists for >=8 following unique cels.
entries.notes: Rotation of a non-convex object changes its defect area without any dent; gate on a low measured rotation rate over the same window. entries.label: Domino / chain-reaction propagation
entries.description: A toppling event triggering the next along a line, with a travelling front.
entries.frame_evidence: Successive elements start falling in sequence, each a fixed short interval after its neighbour.
entries.detector_note: Per-element motion-onset cel along a fitted spatial line; report the onset-cel gradient (front speed) and the linearity of onset time versus position.
entries.notes: Requires each element to be separable; a dense row at low resolution merges into one blob. entries.label: Open / closed state change
entries.description: Whether an aperture is open or shut, and when that changes.
entries.frame_evidence: A dark or through-visible gap appears or vanishes at the panel edge.
entries.detector_note: Crop the panel-and-frame region on the first and last cel of the shot and ask the VLM; the deterministic pipeline can time the motion but cannot name the open/closed semantics.
entries.vlm_question: Is the door in this image open or closed? Answer open or closed.
entries.notes: THE CROP RULE applies. Reflective or glazed doors confuse small VLMs; a single answer is not authoritative, so ask on 3 cels and take the majority.

entries.label: Door / lid swing about a hinge
entries.description: A panel rotating about a fixed edge rather than translating.
entries.frame_evidence: One edge of the panel stays put while the opposite edge sweeps an arc and the panel foreshortens.
entries.detector_note: Track the panel's four corners (cv2.goodFeaturesToTrack constrained to the ROI, matched across cels); fit a single fixed pivot as the least-squares point equidistant-over-time from each tracked corner, and report the residual.
entries.notes: Needs a textured or high-contrast panel for corner tracking; a flat door on a flat wall gives nothing to track. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification.

entries.label: Exhaust puff
entries.description: A discrete burst of exhaust from a pipe.
entries.frame_evidence: A small dark or pale cloud emerging at a fixed point on the vehicle and falling behind it.
entries.detector_note: Detect a repeated small blob birth at a body-fixed offset from the vehicle ROI, then track its detachment and drift; report the emission period.
entries.notes: A body-fixed emission point is the key discriminator against passing background elements. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. entries.label: Floating bob oscillation
entries.description: A floating body rising and falling with the water surface.
entries.frame_evidence: The object oscillates vertically about a mean level while its waterline stays roughly constant.
entries.detector_note: Vertical centroid signal per unique cel with scipy.signal.periodogram; require the oscillation to be coherent with the surrounding water-surface motion (coherence via scipy.signal.coherence against a nearby water ROI signal).
entries.notes: An object bobbing at a period unrelated to the water it sits in is the reportable defect; needs a water ROI that is actually animated. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification. The water surface line is only estimated as the dominant near-horizontal cv2.HoughLines edge; it is unreliable on choppy, foamy, close-up or overhead water, and every metric here must be reported unmeasurable when that line fit is weak rather than defaulted.

entries.label: Object floating (no ground contact)
entries.description: A prop that should rest on a surface but hovers above it.
entries.frame_evidence: A visible gap between the object's base and the surface, with no contact shadow bridging it.
entries.detector_note: Crop the object's lower third plus the surface beneath it and query the VLM; the deterministic pre-filter is a persistent gap between the ROI's lowest contour point and the nearest strong horizontal edge below it.
entries.vlm_question: Is this object resting on the ground, or is it floating above the surface with a gap underneath? Answer resting or floating.
entries.notes: Perspective legitimately puts a distant object's base above a nearer ground line, which is the dominant false positive. THE CROP RULE applies.

entries.label: Fluttering (non-ballistic) fall
entries.description: Light objects (leaves, paper, feathers) descending on a swaying, non-parabolic path.
entries.frame_evidence: The object drifts side to side as it falls, with an oscillating horizontal position.
entries.detector_note: Fit a parabola to the fall; a poor quadratic fit combined with a clear periodic residual in x (periodogram peak) marks flutter rather than ballistic fall.
entries.notes: This is one of the few places where a LOW fit quality is the positive finding; make sure the reporting logic does not treat it as a failed measurement. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification.

entries.label: Follow-through overshoot
entries.description: A prop travels past its resting position at the end of a move and eases back.
entries.frame_evidence: The position track passes the final settled value, then returns to it.
entries.detector_note: Compare the extreme position in the last third of the move against the settled position from object_dynamics.settle_to_rest; report the overshoot as a fraction of total travel.
entries.notes: Requires the settle point to be found first; a shot that cuts before the settle makes this unmeasurable. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification.

entries.label: Fragment area conservation
entries.description: Whether the pieces produced by a break plausibly account for the body that broke.
entries.frame_evidence: The visible fragment area is far less, or far more, than the silhouette that vanished.
entries.detector_note: Sum the fragment component areas over the 3 cels after the break and compare against the parent ROI area on the cel before it; report the ratio.
entries.notes: Fragments overlap, leave frame, and foreshorten, so the ratio is only a coarse sanity signal; a ratio near 0.1 or above 3 is worth reporting, anything between is noise. No null model exists for the expected ratio, so do not threshold tightly. entries.label: Free fall from rest
entries.description: A dropped prop with near-zero initial velocity accelerating straight down.
entries.frame_evidence: The object's vertical steps grow cel over cel while its horizontal position barely changes.
entries.detector_note: Quadratic fit with the linear term constrained near zero; require |dx| total < 0.15 * |dy| total and a positive quadratic coefficient.
entries.notes: A constant-speed fall (zero quadratic term) is the most common animation error this catches. entries.label: Gear meshing rotation
entries.description: Two toothed wheels rotating in contact, in opposite directions, at radius-inverse rates.
entries.frame_evidence: Adjacent circular elements turning against each other at their touching edge.
entries.detector_note: cv2.HoughCircles for both wheels, per-wheel log-polar phase-correlation rotation rates, then check the sign is opposite and the rate ratio matches the inverse radius ratio within tolerance.
entries.notes: Gears that turn the SAME way, or whose ratio does not match their radii, is the classic decorative-machinery error this catches. Needs both gears near-frontal and resolvable. cv2.HoughCircles returns every circle in the frame: which circles are actually wheels or gears must be confirmed by object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification before any of these numbers mean anything.

entries.label: Glass crack web
entries.description: The radial-plus-concentric fracture pattern characteristic of impacted glass.
entries.frame_evidence: Lines radiating from a single point crossed by roughly concentric arcs.
entries.detector_note: Skeletonise the crack mask, fit a common origin to the straight branches (least-squares intersection), and report the fraction of skeleton pixels lying on radials through that origin.
entries.notes: Stylised 2D glass breaks are drawn as a few clean radials with no concentrics; a low concentric score is not a failure of the shot. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification.

entries.label: Gravity consistency between props
entries.description: Whether every independently flying prop in one shot falls with the same acceleration.
entries.frame_evidence: Two or more airborne objects in the same shot whose arcs have visibly different curvature-per-second.
entries.detector_note: Compare the fitted quadratic coefficients from object_dynamics.ballistic_arc_parabola across all tracked projectiles in a shot; report the spread relative to the median.
entries.notes: Objects at different depths legitimately show different px/cel^2; only comparable when their apparent sizes imply a similar depth. Report as advisory, not a defect. entries.label: Gravity direction consistency
entries.description: Whether everything unsupported in a shot falls in the same direction.
entries.frame_evidence: Two falling objects whose paths curve toward different parts of the frame.
entries.detector_note: Compare the acceleration-vector direction from each tracked projectile's quadratic fit across the shot; report the angular spread and the deviation from frame-down.
entries.notes: A dutch-tilted or rolling camera legitimately rotates frame-down; estimate the horizon from cv2.HoughLines and report the deviation relative to that, not to the frame axis.

entries.label: Frozen hair ('helmet hair')
entries.description: Hair that does not move at all while the head does.
entries.frame_evidence: The hair silhouette is rigidly identical relative to the head across a window of strong head motion.
entries.detector_note: Register every cel on the mediapipe face-mesh bounding box (cv2.phaseCorrelate on the face crop), then measure the residual Farneback flow inside the hair band above and around that box; near-zero residual under high absolute head motion is frozen hair.
entries.notes: Short, tied-back or covered hair legitimately shows no residual; the finding needs the hair mass to be large relative to the head box. mediapipe face-mesh and pose are unreliable on stylised 2D faces and on non-human characters, which is exactly where this entry matters most; report unmeasurable on low mesh confidence rather than reporting zero.

entries.label: Hair passing through the head or shoulders
entries.description: Hair geometry intersecting the body it should rest on.
entries.frame_evidence: Strands visibly cross into the face, ear or shoulder surface.
entries.detector_note: Crop the head-and-shoulders region on cels flagged by large hair-ROI displacement toward the body, and query the VLM.
entries.vlm_question: Does any hair pass through the face, ear, or shoulder in this image instead of resting on top of it? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Very high false-positive rate on stylised hair that is DESIGNED to overlap the face. THE CROP RULE applies; do not run on 2D sources.

entries.label: Strand separation / clumping
entries.description: Whether hair reads as separated strands and clumps or as one solid shape.
entries.frame_evidence: Visible internal boundaries inside the hair mass versus a flat filled silhouette.
entries.detector_note: Hair band ROI from the mediapipe face-mesh bounding box dilated upward and outward; measure interior Canny edge density and the skimage.morphology.skeletonize branch count, normalised by ROI area.
entries.notes: This measures drawing/render style more than dynamics; a flat anime hair shape scores near zero by design and that is correct, not a defect. mediapipe face-mesh and pose are unreliable on stylised 2D faces and on non-human characters, which is exactly where this entry matters most; report unmeasurable on low mesh confidence rather than reporting zero.

entries.label: Hair sway lag behind head
entries.description: Hair mass following head motion with a delay.
entries.frame_evidence: The hair silhouette is still travelling in the previous direction when the head has already changed direction.
entries.detector_note: Head ROI from the mediapipe face-mesh bounding box; hair ROI as the dilated band above and around it minus the face box; cross-correlate their per-unique-cel velocity signals and report the lag at peak correlation.
entries.notes: The hair ROI is a geometric heuristic and will swallow background on a busy plate. A measured lag of exactly zero across a whole shot means the hair is rigidly parented, which is the finding worth reporting.

entries.label: Hanging sign / lamp sway
entries.description: A suspended object rocking gently about its hanging point.
entries.frame_evidence: A small persistent rotational oscillation of an object whose top point is fixed.
entries.detector_note: Orientation signal from cv2.moments about the object's own centroid, plus a fixed-top-point check; report amplitude and period of the angular oscillation.
entries.notes: Amplitudes under about 1.5 degrees are inside the orientation estimator's noise on small ROIs. entries.label: Held prop slipping in the hand

entries.label: Impact hold (anime)
entries.description: The impact cel is deliberately held for extra frames to punch the hit.
entries.frame_evidence: The same drawing repeats for several frames exactly at the moment of contact.
