entries.notes: This is the one place raw frame indices matter rather than unique cels; the metric IS the duplication.

entries.label: Shockwave ring
entries.description: An expanding ring or disc of displaced air/energy radiating from an impact.
entries.frame_evidence: A visible annulus centred on the impact point whose radius grows every cel.
entries.detector_note: Radial intensity profile around the contact point per cel; track the radius of the profile's peak and require near-linear growth with a decaying peak amplitude.
entries.notes: Stylised 2D rings are often drawn as an ellipse or a partial arc; the radial-symmetry gate should be loose (>0.5) for anime. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification.

entries.label: Inflation / deflation
entries.description: A body's volume growing or shrinking as it fills or empties.
entries.frame_evidence: The silhouette area grows or shrinks smoothly while the object stays in place and its outline stays convex.
entries.detector_note: Monotonic ROI mask area change with a stationary centroid and a high, stable convexity ratio (contourArea/convexHullArea > 0.9).
entries.notes: Depth approach produces the same area growth; gate on centroid stability and on texture scale not changing. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification.

entries.label: Jiggle / secondary wobble
entries.description: The damped oscillation of a soft or loosely attached element after the main motion stops.
entries.frame_evidence: The silhouette edge of the element oscillates back and forth with shrinking amplitude after the body halts.
entries.detector_note: Build a 1D signal from the ROI edge offset (or contour centroid) per unique cel after the settle point, detrend, then scipy.signal.periodogram for the frequency and an exponential fit to the envelope from scipy.signal.hilbert for the damping.
entries.notes: Needs >=8 unique cels of post-stop signal; on anime at 8 drawings/sec that is a full second of screen time and is often simply not there. Report as not-measurable rather than as no-wobble. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification.

entries.label: Launch / release frame
entries.description: The exact cel at which a previously static or carried prop becomes free-flying.
entries.frame_evidence: The first cel where the prop's speed rises above the local noise floor and its path becomes independent of whatever held it.
entries.detector_note: First unique cel k where |v[k]| exceeds 3x the pre-launch residual motion AND the prop-to-holder ROI distance starts increasing monotonically.
entries.notes: Motion blur on the launch cel can bias the centroid backward, shifting the reported index by one. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification.

entries.label: Limited-animation prop stepping
entries.description: A prop moved in discrete positional jumps rather than an interpolated path.
entries.frame_evidence: The object holds still for several frames then jumps a large distance, repeatedly.
entries.detector_note: Histogram the inter-frame (not unique-cel) displacements: a bimodal distribution with a large zero mode and a large single non-zero mode marks stepping; report the step size and the step interval.
entries.notes: This is a style trait of limited animation, not a defect, and the report must say so. Do NOT compute this on unique-cel indices, since the holds are the signal. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification.

entries.label: Missed contact (visible gap on the impact cel)
entries.description: An impact is clearly intended but the two bodies never actually meet on any cel.
entries.frame_evidence: The reaction (flash, recoil, dust) fires while a visible gap still separates the silhouettes.
entries.detector_note: At the cel where an impact reaction is detected, measure the minimum contour gap; flag when it exceeds 2% of the frame diagonal while a flash/recoil/puff was found.
entries.notes: Depth separation makes many true contacts look gapped in 2D projection, so this must be reported as suspicion and confirmed on a crop by a VLM, never asserted alone. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification.

entries.label: Missing contact shadow
entries.description: An object touching a surface with no darkening at the contact, which destroys the sense of weight.
entries.frame_evidence: The object's base meets the surface with no ambient-occlusion darkening or cast shadow at all.
entries.detector_note: Sample a band immediately below the object's base contour and compare its mean luminance against the same surface further away; a contact shadow shows a >8% local darkening.
entries.notes: Flat-lit 2D animation legitimately has no contact shadows at all; only report on sources where other objects in the same shot DO show contact darkening. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification.

entries.label: Momentum transfer to a second body
entries.description: A struck object starts moving on or just after the cel the striker reaches it.
entries.frame_evidence: A previously static silhouette begins to translate within one or two cels of the contact.
entries.detector_note: Cross-check the struck ROI's motion-onset cel against the detected contact cel; require onset within +/-1 unique cel and an onset direction within 45 degrees of the striker's incoming velocity.
entries.notes: An onset that PRECEDES contact is a genuine, very reportable animation error (the target reacts before it is hit). No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification.

entries.label: Multi-object collision ordering
entries.description: In a pile-up or crowd of props, which contacts happen in what order.
entries.frame_evidence: Several near-simultaneous contacts whose sequence determines whether the outcome makes sense.
entries.detector_note: Reliable ordering needs per-object identity maintained through mutual occlusion and through motion blur; no installed tracker holds identity through a dense multi-object collision, and a wrong association produces a confidently wrong ordering.
entries.notes: Deliberately unsupported. Individual pairwise contacts are still logged by object_dynamics.contact_frame; only the global ordering is refused.

entries.label: Multiple-image / afterimage (2D)
entries.description: The same object drawn several times in one cel at successive positions along its path.
entries.frame_evidence: Two or more ghosted copies of one silhouette, evenly spaced along the motion axis.
entries.detector_note: Autocorrelation of the ROI along the estimated motion axis showing >=2 secondary peaks at regular spacing, with each copy's shape correlation to the primary above 0.6.
entries.notes: Repeating background patterns inside the ROI generate the same autocorrelation peaks; require the copies to be absent from the neighbouring cel. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification.

entries.label: Prop held static over a panning background
entries.description: A foreground prop cel held motionless while the background plate pans behind it.
entries.frame_evidence: The background slides steadily while the prop is pixel-identical frame to frame.
entries.detector_note: Global background shift from cv2.phaseCorrelate exceeding 2 px/frame while the prop ROI's mean abs frame difference stays at the duplicate-frame floor.
entries.notes: Standard and correct in cel animation when the prop is meant to be camera-locked; report as an observation, never a defect. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification.

entries.label: Jitter / sim instability
entries.description: A prop that should be still or smoothly moving instead vibrates with high-frequency zero-mean displacement.
entries.frame_evidence: The centroid track carries a per-cel wobble of a few pixels with no directional bias and no visible cause.
entries.detector_note: High-pass the centroid track (subtract a scipy.signal.savgol_filter smooth of window 7), then report residual RMS and the fraction of residual power above 0.3 cycles/cel.
entries.notes: Tracker noise is itself high-frequency; subtract the jitter measured on a co-visible static object before claiming a sim defect. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification.

entries.label: Perceived weight / mass of a prop
entries.description: Whether a prop's motion reads as heavy or as weightless.
entries.frame_evidence: A large object accelerating instantly, stopping dead, or drifting like foam.
entries.detector_note: There is no calibrated way to map image-space acceleration to perceived mass without a known object scale, a known frame rate mapping, and a human-judged null; every available proxy (accel magnitude, settle time, squash depth) is confounded by style and by camera distance.
entries.notes: Deliberately marked unsupported. The component measurements (accel, settle, squash, follow-through) ARE logged individually; the aggregate weight judgement is not, because a confident weight score with no null model would be exactly the failure mode this taxonomy is meant to avoid.

entries.label: Material identification from motion
entries.description: Inferring what a prop is made of (metal, wood, rubber, glass, cloth) from how it moves and breaks.
entries.frame_evidence: The way it bends, rings, shatters or deforms on impact.
entries.detector_note: Would need a material or object classifier; nothing installed classifies materials, and asking a small VLM about material on a motion-blurred crop returns the object's colour, not its physics.
entries.notes: Logged as a blind spot. The downstream physics checks that WOULD need a material prior (restitution plausibility, gravity scale) are therefore reported without a plausibility verdict.

entries.label: Motion-blur consistency with speed
entries.description: Whether a prop's rendered blur length matches how fast it is actually moving.
entries.frame_evidence: A fast object rendered razor sharp, or a slow one heavily smeared.
entries.detector_note: Estimate the blur length from the ROI's directional power-spectrum falloff (or the autocorrelation width along the motion axis) and regress it against the measured per-cel displacement across all tracked props in the shot; report the residual per object.
entries.notes: Needs several moving objects in one shot to fit the regression; with a single object there is no null model and the absolute blur length means nothing. Anime has no motion blur by convention, so restrict to 3D/live sources. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification.

entries.label: Arced vs straight path
entries.description: Whether a moving prop travels on a curved (animator-preferred) or dead-straight (machine-interpolated) path.
entries.frame_evidence: The centroid trail across the window bows away from the chord joining its endpoints, or does not.
entries.detector_note: Max perpendicular deviation of the centroid track from the endpoint chord, normalised by chord length.
entries.notes: A bow ratio under 0.01 over a long move is a strong linear-interpolation tell. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification.

entries.label: Approach / recede scale change
entries.description: A prop growing or shrinking in the frame because it is moving toward or away from camera.
entries.frame_evidence: The tracked silhouette's area changes monotonically while its shape and texture stay self-similar.
entries.detector_note: Per-cel ROI mask area from cv2.findContours plus the scale term recovered by log-polar cv2.phaseCorrelate; report the growth rate and whether area scales as the square of the linear scale.
entries.notes: Separates a genuine depth move from a 2D zoom-on-the-cel cheat: a real approach keeps texture detail growing, a scaled cel goes soft. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification.

entries.label: Object-shadow motion sync
entries.description: Whether a prop's cast shadow moves with the prop.
entries.frame_evidence: The shadow shape translates by the geometrically implied amount as the object moves.
entries.detector_note: Identify the dark region adjacent to the object base and cross-correlate its per-cel displacement against the object's; report the ratio and the lag.
entries.notes: Shadow segmentation by darkness alone grabs any nearby dark texture; only trustworthy on a plain light-toned floor. A lag of >=1 cel is a genuine and reportable compositing error. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification.

entries.label: Planted prop sliding (prop foot-slide)
entries.description: A prop that should be locked to a surface drifting across it.
entries.frame_evidence: The object translates relative to fixed background features while nothing pushes it.
entries.detector_note: After global camera compensation via cv2.phaseCorrelate on the background, measure the object's residual displacement relative to two static background features over the window.
entries.notes: The entire measurement rests on the camera compensation; if the background residual exceeds 1 px the slide number is meaningless and must be suppressed. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification.

entries.label: Trajectory occlusion gap
entries.description: A flying prop disappearing behind an occluder and reappearing where the arc predicts, or not.
entries.frame_evidence: The object vanishes at one edge of an occluder and reappears at the other.
entries.detector_note: Extrapolate the fitted parabola across the occlusion gap and compare the predicted reappearance position and cel against the observed one.
entries.notes: The error grows quadratically with the gap length, so a long occlusion makes any discrepancy unattributable; suppress above a gap of about 8 unique cels. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification.

entries.label: Overlapping action (appendage lag)
entries.description: Attached or trailing parts reach their extremes later than the body that drives them.
entries.frame_evidence: The tip of a trailing element is still moving in the old direction when the body has already reversed.
entries.detector_note: Cross-correlate the driver ROI's velocity signal against the trailing ROI's velocity signal over unique cels (numpy.correlate on z-scored series) and report the lag at maximum correlation.
entries.notes: A lag of zero across every attached element is the signature of a rigidly parented prop, a genuine and reportable stiffness finding. All temporal terms are computed on UNIQUE-CEL indices (duplicate-frame runs collapsed via mean abs frame diff < 0.5/255); raw-fps sampling reports zero motion on held cels. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification.

entries.label: Drawer / sliding panel
entries.description: A panel translating along a single fixed axis without rotating.
entries.frame_evidence: The element extends or retracts along one direction with a constant orientation and a growing or shrinking visible length.
entries.detector_note: LK track of ROI corners showing pure translation (rotation from log-polar phase correlation below 2 deg) confined to one direction over the window, with a monotonic change in visible extent.
entries.notes: Camera dolly along the same axis is indistinguishable without background compensation. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification.

entries.label: Pendulum swing
entries.description: A body swinging on a fixed pivot with a regular period.
entries.frame_evidence: The object traces a repeated arc about a fixed point above it.
entries.detector_note: Fit a fixed pivot to the object's track (least-squares circle fit, scipy.optimize.least_squares), then take the angular signal and report period, amplitude and damping.
entries.notes: A period that does not scale as sqrt(length) between two pendulums in the same shot is a reportable inconsistency, but the comparison needs both to be visible and in-plane. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification.

entries.label: Penetration into a surface
entries.description: A projectile that enters and stays lodged in a surface instead of rebounding.
entries.frame_evidence: The object's visible length shortens at the contact point and then stops changing, with the remainder protruding.
entries.detector_note: Track the visible extent of the projectile ROI along its travel axis across contact; require a monotonic shortening that halts, with the residual stub static for >=4 unique cels.
entries.notes: Only works when the projectile is elongated and side-on; a head-on penetration is pure occlusion and unmeasurable this way. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification.

entries.label: Piston reciprocation
entries.description: A component moving back and forth along a fixed line with a repeating period.
entries.frame_evidence: An element slides in and out along one axis, reversing at both ends.
entries.detector_note: Project the component centroid onto its dominant motion axis (PCA of the track) and run scipy.signal.periodogram on the 1D signal; report period, amplitude and waveform symmetry.
entries.notes: A looped cel-animation cycle produces a perfectly periodic signal too; period constancy alone does not prove mechanical motion. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification.

entries.label: Ponytail / braid pendulum swing
entries.description: A discrete hank of hair swinging as a damped pendulum from a fixed root.
entries.frame_evidence: An elongated hair element pivots about a point at the head while its tip traces an arc.
entries.detector_note: Anchor on the mediapipe face-mesh head box; isolate the elongated component adjacent to it, take skimage.morphology.medial_axis, fit a pivot as the least-squares intersection of the axis lines across cels, then report the tip angular signal's period, amplitude and damping.
entries.notes: Needs the hank to be separable from the rest of the hair mass, which is only reliable on high-contrast 2D designs. mediapipe face-mesh and pose are unreliable on stylised 2D faces and on non-human characters, which is exactly where this entry matters most; report unmeasurable on low mesh confidence rather than reporting zero.

entries.label: Pre-break stress cue
entries.description: The visual warning before a break: bulging, stress lines, flexing or a glowing seam.
entries.frame_evidence: The intact body shows local distortion or line detail concentrated where it is about to fail.
entries.detector_note: Crop the parent ROI on the 4 unique cels before a detected break cel and ask the VLM; there is no reliable deterministic signature for anticipatory stress.
entries.vlm_question: Does this object look like it is under strain or about to break apart, showing bulging or stress lines? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Only run when a break was already detected downstream, otherwise the false-positive rate on ordinary textured objects is very high. THE CROP RULE applies.

entries.label: Projectile motion-blur streak
entries.description: A fast projectile rendered as an elongated smear rather than a discrete shape.
entries.frame_evidence: A single cel contains a thin bright or dark ridge, much longer than wide, oriented along the travel direction.
entries.detector_note: cv2.HoughLinesP on the Canny edges of the ROI; require an elongated component (cv2.minAreaRect aspect > 4) whose orientation matches the Farneback flow direction within 15 degrees.
entries.notes: Genuine thin props (arrows, poles, blades) at rest look identical on a single frame; the flow-agreement gate is what separates them. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification.

entries.label: Projectile trail / wake particles
entries.description: A tail of small elements (sparks, dust, vapour) shed along a projectile's path.
entries.frame_evidence: Small blobs strung out behind the moving object, each older element further from it and usually fainter.
entries.detector_note: cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats on the diff mask behind the prop; require component centroids to fall within a corridor around the fitted trajectory with monotonically decreasing intensity by distance.
entries.notes: Compression blocking around a fast object creates spurious components; enforce a minimum area of ~8 px. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification.

entries.label: Prop passing through the hand
entries.description: A held object intersecting the fingers instead of being gripped by them.
entries.frame_evidence: Fingers appear on both sides of, or inside, the prop's surface.
entries.detector_note: Crop tightly on the mediapipe hand bounding box union the prop ROI and query the VLM.
entries.vlm_question: Is the object passing through the hand or fingers instead of being held by them? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Small VLMs are weak on hands generally and this crop is exactly where they confabulate; treat only repeated yes across cels as a lead. THE CROP RULE applies.

entries.label: Prop identity / class label
entries.description: Naming what a prop actually is, so the physics priors for it can be selected.
entries.frame_evidence: The object's appearance on a clean crop.
entries.detector_note: Crop the tracked ROI with 1.4x padding on its sharpest cel (highest Laplacian variance) and ask the VLM for a single-word class.
entries.vlm_question: What single object is shown in this image? Answer with one or two words only.
entries.notes: Every physics-plausibility entry in this domain depends on this label, so its error rate propagates everywhere; log the label as an assumption, not a fact. moondream should not be trusted for fine classes and must never be asked about any text on the prop. THE CROP RULE applies.

entries.label: Prop pop-in / disappearance
entries.description: A prop that appears or vanishes between cels without entering or leaving frame.
entries.frame_evidence: A silhouette present on one cel is simply absent on the next, mid-frame.
entries.detector_note: Track ROI presence across unique cels; flag a presence-to-absence transition where the ROI is >20 px from every frame edge and no occluder ROI overlaps it on the transition cel.
entries.notes: Occlusion by a fast-moving foreground element is the main false positive; the occluder-overlap test only works when the occluder is itself segmented. All temporal terms are computed on UNIQUE-CEL indices (duplicate-frame runs collapsed via mean abs frame diff < 0.5/255); raw-fps sampling reports zero motion on held cels. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification.

entries.label: Prop position jump across a cut
entries.description: A continuity break where a prop's position or state changes across an edit.
entries.frame_evidence: The same prop sits somewhere different in the shot after the cut than it did before.
entries.detector_note: Detect the cut (histogram-difference shot boundary), crop the same semantic prop region either side, and ask the VLM to compare; nothing installed can re-identify an arbitrary prop across a camera change.
entries.vlm_question: In these two images of the same scene, is the object in the same place and the same state in both? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Requires a side-by-side or sequential crop pair, which small VLMs handle poorly; qwen2.5vl is the minimum viable judge here and moondream must not be used. High false-positive rate on any camera-angle change.

entries.label: Prop scale inconsistency
entries.description: The same prop drawn or rendered at inconsistent size relative to its surroundings.
entries.frame_evidence: The object's size relative to a hand, a doorway or a character changes between shots without a depth change.
entries.detector_note: Crop the prop with a same-frame reference object and ask the VLM; a deterministic ratio of prop height to a mediapipe-derived body height can pre-filter candidates when a person is present.
entries.vlm_question: Is this object the right size compared to the person or objects next to it? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: The deterministic pre-filter only exists when a human is co-visible; otherwise this is a pure VLM judgement with no null model. THE CROP RULE applies.

entries.label: Rebound / velocity reversal
entries.description: A body's direction of travel flips at a contact instead of stopping or passing through.
entries.frame_evidence: The motion vector before and after the contact cel point in substantially opposed directions.
entries.detector_note: Angle between the mean pre-contact and post-contact velocity vectors > 110 degrees, with post-contact speed > 0.2 * pre-contact speed.
entries.notes: Needs at least 2 unique cels on each side of the contact; short cuts on impact (a very common edit) leave nothing to measure. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification.

entries.label: Ricochet / deflection angle
entries.description: A projectile bouncing off a surface at an angle rather than stopping in it.
entries.frame_evidence: The trajectory kinks sharply at a surface, continuing away from it on a new heading.
entries.detector_note: Fit lines to the pre- and post-contact track segments; report the incidence and reflection angles against the local surface normal estimated from the cv2.HoughLines segment at the contact point.
entries.notes: A mirror error near zero means physically plausible reflection; large errors are worth reporting but stylised action deliberately breaks this. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification.

entries.label: Positional pop / teleport
entries.description: A prop jumps discontinuously to a new position between two consecutive unique cels.
entries.frame_evidence: One inter-cel displacement is many times larger than every neighbouring step, with no motion blur bridging it.
entries.detector_note: Flag |v[k]| > 6 * median(|v|) over the shot AND > 0.08 * frame diagonal, with no elongated blur ridge at the midpoint (checked by the smear detector).
entries.notes: Legitimate fast action plus a hard cut both trigger this; must be suppressed inside one cel of a detected shot boundary. All temporal terms are computed on UNIQUE-CEL indices (duplicate-frame runs collapsed via mean abs frame diff < 0.5/255); raw-fps sampling reports zero motion on held cels.

entries.label: In-plane rotation (spin)
entries.description: A prop rotating about an axis perpendicular to the screen, keeping its silhouette area roughly constant.
entries.frame_evidence: The same silhouette reappears rotated about its own centroid across cels, area near-constant.
entries.detector_note: Centre the ROI on its centroid, cv2.warpPolar(..., flags=cv2.WARP_POLAR_LOG) both cels, then cv2.phaseCorrelate the log-polar images; the angular shift is the per-cel rotation. Validate with cv2.moments second-order orientation of the binarised silhouette.
entries.notes: Radially symmetric props (balls, discs) give a meaningless or unstable angle; gate on ROI eccentricity from cv2.moments. Requires a prop ROI: moving-blob proposals from cv2.createBackgroundSubtractorMOG2 after global camera compensation (cv2.phaseCorrelate), or an operator/VLM-seeded cv2.TrackerCSRT box. Object identity is NOT established by this tier.

entries.label: Acceleration / deceleration profile
entries.description: Whether a moving prop is speeding up, holding speed, or slowing down across the move.
entries.frame_evidence: Inter-cel displacement of the prop grows, holds, or shrinks monotonically over the window.
entries.detector_note: First difference of the centroid track gives v[k]; second difference gives a[k]; classify by sign of a robust (Theil-Sen) slope fit to |v[k]| and report the fraction of cels with a>0 vs a<0.
entries.notes: Perspective (approach/recede) fakes acceleration in image space; cross-check against object_dynamics.object_scale_change_perspective. All temporal terms are computed on UNIQUE-CEL indices (duplicate-frame runs collapsed via mean abs frame diff < 0.5/255); raw-fps sampling reports zero motion on held cels.

entries.label: Linear translation
entries.description: A prop moves across the frame along a straight path without changing orientation.
entries.frame_evidence: The same silhouette/texture patch occupies successively offset positions over a frame window with constant shape.
entries.detector_note: cv2.goodFeaturesToTrack inside the prop ROI then cv2.calcOpticalFlowPyrLK across unique cels; take the median point displacement as the centroid track; least-squares line fit of (x,y) and report R^2 plus per-cel speed.
entries.notes: Requires a prop ROI: moving-blob proposals from cv2.createBackgroundSubtractorMOG2 after global camera compensation (cv2.phaseCorrelate), or an operator/VLM-seeded cv2.TrackerCSRT box. Object identity is NOT established by this tier. All temporal terms are computed on UNIQUE-CEL indices (duplicate-frame runs collapsed via mean abs frame diff < 0.5/255); raw-fps sampling reports zero motion on held cels.

entries.label: Out-of-plane tumble
entries.description: A prop rotating about an axis in the screen plane so its projected silhouette cyclically flattens and fills.
entries.frame_evidence: Silhouette aspect ratio and area oscillate periodically while the centroid follows a smooth path.
entries.detector_note: Per-cel cv2.minAreaRect on the ROI mask; build the aspect-ratio and area signals, then scipy.signal.periodogram for a dominant period; require an area minimum coincident with an aspect-ratio extreme.
entries.notes: In 2D the tumble is drawn, not projected, so the area signal is often a stylised 2-pose flip with no smooth cycle; expect a low periodogram peak on anime. All temporal terms are computed on UNIQUE-CEL indices (duplicate-frame runs collapsed via mean abs frame diff < 0.5/255); raw-fps sampling reports zero motion on held cels. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification.

entries.label: Articulated arm / joint chain motion
entries.description: A chain of rigid links rotating about successive joints.
entries.frame_evidence: Straight segments pivot about identifiable points, each carrying the next segment with it.
entries.detector_note: Would need a part/keypoint detector for the specific mechanism; mediapipe only supplies human, hand and face topologies, and nothing installed detects arbitrary articulated machinery.
entries.notes: Logged as a blind spot. A generic skeletonisation of the arm mask can sometimes suggest joints but has no null model and would produce confident nonsense.

entries.label: Rolling (roll without slip)
entries.description: A round prop whose rotation is locked to its translation along a surface.
entries.frame_evidence: Surface markings on a circular object rotate exactly one radius-arc per unit of horizontal travel.
entries.detector_note: cv2.HoughCircles for the radius r, log-polar cv2.phaseCorrelate for the per-cel rotation dtheta, LK track for the per-cel translation dx; report the slip ratio dx/(r*dtheta).
entries.notes: Ratio near 1.0 is rolling, near 0 is a spinning-in-place skid, >1 is a skating error. Featureless or flat-shaded wheels defeat the log-polar phase correlation. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification. cv2.HoughCircles returns every circle in the frame: which circles are actually wheels or gears must be confirmed by object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification before any of these numbers mean anything.

entries.label: Rope catenary sag
entries.description: A slack line hanging between two supports in a catenary curve.
entries.frame_evidence: A thin curved element sagging between two higher attachment points.
entries.detector_note: Extract the thin structure via skimage.filters.frangi and skeletonize, order the skeleton, then fit both a parabola and a cosh (scipy.optimize.curve_fit) and report the sag depth and which model fits better.
entries.notes: Perspective turns a real catenary into an arbitrary projected curve; the sag ratio is only comparable across cels of the same shot with a static camera. entries.label: Rope stretching (inextensibility violation)
entries.description: A rope, chain or cable whose total length visibly changes over the shot.
entries.frame_evidence: The line's arc length grows or shrinks between cels with no coil or slack entering frame.
entries.detector_note: Skeleton arc length per unique cel, normalised by a static reference length in the frame; report the coefficient of variation.
entries.notes: Perspective foreshortening changes projected arc length legitimately; only reportable for a static camera and an in-plane rope. Chains legitimately shorten when coiling. entries.label: Rope snapping taut
entries.description: A slack line pulling straight in one or two cels as load comes on.
entries.frame_evidence: The curve between the two ends flattens to a straight segment abruptly.
entries.detector_note: Per-cel max deviation of the rope skeleton from its endpoint chord; flag a drop to <10% of the previous value within 2 unique cels.
entries.notes: Requires the whole span to be visible; a rope leaving frame gives a truncated chord and a meaningless deviation. entries.label: Rotational / cyclic periodicity of a mechanism
entries.description: Any machine element repeating its state on a fixed cycle.
entries.frame_evidence: The same configuration of the mechanism reappears at regular cel intervals.
entries.detector_note: Self-similarity matrix of the ROI across unique cels (normalised cross-correlation of every cel pair), then find the dominant off-diagonal ridge spacing.
entries.notes: This also detects looped animation and cycled backgrounds, which is useful in itself but must not be reported as machinery. entries.label: Propeller / rotor blur disc
entries.description: A rotating blade array rendered as a translucent disc or a strobing blade set.
entries.frame_evidence: A circular region of reduced contrast and radial streaking at the hub location.
entries.detector_note: Inside a Hough circle at the hub, compare radial-profile variance against angular-profile variance; a blur disc has low angular variance and a distinct contrast drop against the surround.
entries.notes: A genuinely stopped rotor with visible blades gives the opposite signature and should be reported separately (rotor visible but aircraft flying is a common error). entries.label: Rubber-hose / noodle deformation
entries.description: A limb or prop drawn with continuous curvature and no rigid joints, bending like a hose.
entries.frame_evidence: An elongated element whose medial axis curves smoothly along its whole length with no straight segments.
entries.detector_note: Fit piecewise-linear segments to the medial axis and report the fraction of the length whose local curvature exceeds a threshold; rubber-hose is high sustained curvature with no dominant hinge point.
entries.notes: A style trait, not a defect; only meaningful when the analyzer is asked to characterise animation style. entries.label: Sail / canopy billow
entries.description: A large cloth filling with wind into a stable curved volume.
entries.frame_evidence: The cloth's outline bows into a sustained convex curve and holds it, rather than rippling.
entries.detector_note: Fit a quadratic to the cloth's free-edge contour and track the fitted curvature over cels; billow is a large sustained curvature with low temporal variance.
entries.notes: Requires a mostly unoccluded side-on view; a head-on sail projects flat and reads as unbilled. entries.label: Screen shake at impact
entries.description: The whole frame jolts as a reaction to an impact.
entries.frame_evidence: Every element in the frame translates together for a few cels after the contact.
entries.detector_note: cv2.phaseCorrelate between consecutive full frames gives the global shift; flag a burst of >4 px shifts with alternating sign within 5 cels of a detected contact.
entries.notes: Handheld camera work produces continuous low-level shake; require the burst to exceed 3x the shot's baseline global-shift RMS.

entries.label: Settle to rest
entries.description: A prop's residual motion decays until it is stationary and stays stationary.
entries.frame_evidence: Frame-to-frame difference inside the prop ROI falls to the static-background noise level and remains there.
entries.detector_note: Mean abs diff inside the tracked ROI across unique cels, compared against the same statistic measured on a hand-picked static background patch; flag the first cel of a run of >=4 cels below 1.5x that floor.
entries.notes: Compression noise raises the floor on dark ROIs; the floor must be measured per-shot, never hard-coded. entries.label: Shatter into fragments
entries.description: A body breaks apart into many separate pieces in one or two cels.
entries.frame_evidence: One silhouette is replaced by a scatter of smaller silhouettes moving outward.
entries.detector_note: cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats on the foreground mask across cels; flag a >=4x jump in component count within the parent ROI's bounding box, with the new components' centroids moving radially outward.
entries.notes: Fast camera motion or a cut fragments the mask too; require the radial-outward test to pass on >=60% of new components. All temporal terms are computed on UNIQUE-CEL indices (duplicate-frame runs collapsed via mean abs frame diff < 0.5/255); raw-fps sampling reports zero motion on held cels. entries.label: Simulation cadence mismatch
entries.description: A prop's motion updating on a different cadence than the rest of the shot.
entries.frame_evidence: The prop steps forward on every frame while the characters step on 2s, or vice versa.
entries.detector_note: Compute the unique-cel run-length histogram separately for the prop ROI and for the rest of the frame; flag a modal hold length that differs by a factor of 2 or more.
entries.notes: This is exactly the metric the ones-vs-twos rule demands and it is genuinely useful in 2D/3D hybrid work, where a 3D prop composited into a 2D scene runs on 1s. Needs a static enough camera that the background does not force every frame unique. entries.label: Sinking
entries.description: A body descending through a fluid, progressively occluded by the surface.
entries.frame_evidence: The visible portion of the object shrinks from the bottom up as it passes below the surface line.
entries.detector_note: Track the ROI's visible area and its top edge against the detected horizontal surface line; sinking is monotonic area loss with a stationary or descending top edge and no fragment scatter.
entries.notes: Distinguishing sinking from an object simply leaving frame at the bottom requires the surface line to be found; a calm surface with no contrast defeats the line detection. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification. The water surface line is only estimated as the dominant near-horizontal cv2.HoughLines edge; it is unreliable on choppy, foamy, close-up or overhead water, and every metric here must be reported unmeasurable when that line fit is weak rather than defaulted.

entries.label: Skirt / hem flutter
entries.description: Fine oscillation of a garment's free lower edge.
entries.frame_evidence: The hem line ripples with small, fast, spatially varying displacements.
entries.detector_note: Anchor a band ROI below mediapipe pose hips (23/24); extract the lower contour per unique cel and measure the RMS of its high-spatial-frequency component and its temporal variance.
entries.notes: Confused by patterned fabric edges and by low-resolution sources where the hem is 2 px thick.

entries.label: Slide with friction decay
entries.description: A prop sliding along a surface and losing speed at a roughly constant or exponential rate.
entries.frame_evidence: Contact stays on one surface line while the inter-cel step shrinks monotonically to zero.
entries.detector_note: Fit both a linear (Coulomb) and an exponential (viscous) model to |v[k]| by scipy.optimize.curve_fit; report the better-fitting model and its decay constant.
entries.notes: Fewer than 5 unique cels of decay makes the two models indistinguishable; report model_choice as null below that. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification.

entries.label: Smear frame (2D)
entries.description: A single drawing that stretches or multiplies a moving element to carry the eye between poses.
entries.frame_evidence: One cel shows the object as an elongated, distorted or multi-imaged shape unlike its neighbours.
entries.detector_note: Flag a unique cel whose ROI aspect ratio and contour perimeter jump >2x above both neighbouring cels' values and whose interior contains repeated near-parallel edges (autocorrelation peak along the motion axis).
entries.notes: Fires on motion blur in live action too; restrict to 2d sources. A smear cel is one to two frames long, so a shot-level scan will miss it if it samples sparsely. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification.

entries.label: Soft-body deformation on contact
entries.description: A non-rigid body conforming to whatever it presses against.
entries.frame_evidence: The silhouette flattens locally against the contact surface and its outline elsewhere bulges out.
entries.detector_note: Compare the local contour curvature inside the contact arc against the object's own median curvature; a soft contact shows near-zero curvature over the contact arc and increased curvature adjacent to it.
entries.notes: Needs a clean silhouette; soft bodies are often motion-blurred or partly occluded at the moment of contact. entries.label: Speed lines / action lines (2D)
entries.description: Drawn straight or radial line bundles around a prop that stand in for its velocity.
entries.frame_evidence: A fan of parallel or converging thin strokes filling the space behind or around the object.
entries.detector_note: cv2.HoughLinesP over the annulus around the prop ROI; require >=8 segments whose angular histogram has one dominant mode (parallel case) or whose extensions converge on a common point within 0.05 of the frame diagonal (radial case).
entries.notes: Backgrounds with strong architectural line structure (fences, rain, hatching) are the dominant false positive; require the lines to be absent in the neighbouring non-action cel. entries.label: Spin-axis wobble / precession
entries.description: The rotation axis of a spinning prop itself drifts or nutates instead of holding steady.
entries.frame_evidence: The silhouette's principal-axis angle drifts with a slow secondary oscillation superimposed on the fast spin.
entries.detector_note: Unwrap the per-cel orientation from cv2.moments (0.5*atan2(2*mu11, mu20-mu02)), detrend the linear spin term, then look for a low-frequency residual peak via scipy.signal.welch.
entries.notes: Orientation from moments has a pi ambiguity; unwrap before detrending or the residual is pure artefact. entries.detector_note: Track the element's long-axis extent from cv2.minAreaRect per unique cel; scipy.signal.periodogram on the length signal for period and amplitude.
entries.notes: Coil spacing (the more legible cue) is below the resolvable scale at normal delivery resolutions. entries.label: Squash on impact

entries.frame_evidence: On the contact cel the silhouette is visibly wider and shorter than on the approaching cels.
entries.detector_note: cv2.minAreaRect on the ROI mask per cel; report the aspect ratio relative to the pre-contact median and require the compression axis to align with the incoming velocity within 30 degrees.

entries.label: Squash-stretch volume preservation

entries.label: Throw release from hand
entries.description: The moment a hand-carried prop separates from the hand and becomes ballistic.
entries.frame_evidence: The prop ROI and the hand stop moving together and their separation begins to grow.
entries.detector_note: mediapipe pose wrist landmarks 15/16 (or hands landmark 0) give a hand point per cel; track the prop ROI centroid; release is the first cel where the prop-hand distance exceeds 1.5x its carried median and keeps growing for >=3 cels.

entries.frame_evidence: Two diverging bright lines opening rearward from the object's contact with the surface.
entries.detector_note: cv2.HoughLinesP behind the object restricted to the surface region; require two lines symmetric about the travel axis with an opening angle stable across cels, anchored at the object.
entries.notes: A wake that is not anchored to the object (it lags or leads) is the reportable defect. Choppy water hides the lines entirely. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification. The water surface line is only estimated as the dominant near-horizontal cv2.HoughLines edge; it is unreliable on choppy, foamy, close-up or overhead water, and every metric here must be reported unmeasurable when that line fit is weak rather than defaulted.

entries.label: Water entry splash
entries.description: The crown and spray thrown up when a body enters a liquid surface.
entries.frame_evidence: A bright irregular structure erupts upward at the entry point on the cel after contact.
entries.detector_note: At the cel after a surface-line crossing, detect a new high-luminance, high-edge-density region above the surface line whose area peaks within 3 unique cels and then decays.
entries.notes: The classic error this catches is a splash whose peak area does not scale with the entry speed at all, but that comparison needs several entries in one shot to calibrate. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification. The water surface line is only estimated as the dominant near-horizontal cv2.HoughLines edge; it is unreliable on choppy, foamy, close-up or overhead water, and every metric here must be reported unmeasurable when that line fit is weak rather than defaulted.

entries.label: Waterline / submersion depth
entries.description: How deep a floating body sits in the fluid.
entries.frame_evidence: The horizontal line across the object where it meets the surface, and its height on the object's silhouette.
entries.detector_note: Intersect the detected surface line with the object ROI; report the submerged fraction of the silhouette height and its stability across cels.
entries.notes: A waterline that changes with no change in load is a reportable inconsistency; heavy foam or spray makes the line undetectable. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification. The water surface line is only estimated as the dominant near-horizontal cv2.HoughLines edge; it is unreliable on choppy, foamy, close-up or overhead water, and every metric here must be reported unmeasurable when that line fit is weak rather than defaulted.

entries.label: Wheel spin vs ground speed (skating wheels)
entries.description: Whether the wheels rotate at the rate the vehicle's travel demands.
entries.frame_evidence: The vehicle slides forward while the wheels turn too slowly, too fast, or not at all.
entries.detector_note: Compare r*dtheta from object_dynamics.wheel_rotation_rate against the vehicle's ground displacement per unique cel, both in image pixels; report the ratio.
entries.notes: The single most common vehicle animation error. Requires a side-on or near-side-on view; a three-quarter view foreshortens the wheel and biases the radius. cv2.HoughCircles returns every circle in the frame: which circles are actually wheels or gears must be confirmed by object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification before any of these numbers mean anything.

entries.label: Static (non-rotating) wheel
entries.description: A wheel that never turns while the vehicle moves.
entries.frame_evidence: Hub markings and spokes hold exactly the same angle for the whole travelling shot.
entries.detector_note: Measured |rotation_deg_per_cel| below 1 degree for >=8 unique cels while the vehicle's ground speed exceeds 2 px/cel.
entries.notes: A radially symmetric or fully blurred wheel produces the same reading; require a resolvable spoke or hub feature (measured spoke_count_estimate >= 3). cv2.HoughCircles returns every circle in the frame: which circles are actually wheels or gears must be confirmed by object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification before any of these numbers mean anything.

entries.label: Wheel rotation rate
entries.description: How fast a wheel spins about its own axle.
entries.frame_evidence: Spokes, hub markings or tread rotate about the wheel centre between cels.
entries.detector_note: cv2.HoughCircles to find the wheel, cv2.warpPolar about the circle centre, then cv2.phaseCorrelate the polar images of consecutive unique cels to recover the angular shift per cel.
entries.notes: A featureless or blurred wheel returns a meaningless phase-correlation peak; gate on a response above 0.15 and report unmeasurable otherwise. All temporal terms are computed on UNIQUE-CEL indices (duplicate-frame runs collapsed via mean abs frame diff < 0.5/255); raw-fps sampling reports zero motion on held cels. cv2.HoughCircles returns every circle in the frame: which circles are actually wheels or gears must be confirmed by object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification before any of these numbers mean anything.

entries.label: Spoke strobing / reverse rotation
entries.description: Temporal aliasing that makes a spoked wheel appear to slow, stop, or turn backward.
entries.frame_evidence: The spokes appear to rotate opposite the vehicle's travel direction.
entries.detector_note: Sign disagreement between the measured wheel rotation direction and the vehicle's travel direction, with a high spoke-count periodicity in the polar image (FFT of the angular profile).
entries.notes: In live action this is a real optical artefact and correct; in 3D it means the render frame rate beat the wheel rate. The analyzer should report it, not judge it. cv2.HoughCircles returns every circle in the frame: which circles are actually wheels or gears must be confirmed by object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification before any of these numbers mean anything.

entries.label: Whip crack (tip acceleration)
entries.description: The travelling loop of a whip that accelerates the tip far beyond the handle's speed.
entries.frame_evidence: A wave runs down the line and the far end blurs or streaks while the hand barely moves.
entries.detector_note: Track the skeleton endpoint furthest from the held end; report the ratio of tip speed to handle speed per unique cel and the peak of that ratio.
entries.notes: The tip is usually motion-blurred to invisibility at the crack cel, so the peak is systematically underestimated; report as a lower bound. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification.

entries.label: Wire / cable snap and recoil
entries.description: A line under tension breaking and its ends whipping back.
entries.frame_evidence: The continuous line becomes two components whose free ends accelerate away from the break point.
entries.detector_note: Skeleton component count jumping from 1 to 2 with both new endpoints moving away from the last common point at high speed over the following cels.
entries.notes: Occlusion of the middle of a rope produces the same component split; require both ends to MOVE, not merely to exist. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification.

entries.label: Wrinkle formation and propagation
entries.description: Fold lines appearing in cloth as it compresses, and travelling as the compression moves.
entries.frame_evidence: New short parallel line features appear inside the garment area and shift position between cels.
entries.detector_note: Canny or skimage.filters.frangi edge density inside the cloth ROI per unique cel; report the density change and the dominant edge orientation, plus the flow of the edge map (Farneback on the edge images) as a propagation direction.
entries.notes: Printed fabric patterns and shadow noise dominate the edge density in low-light shots; report the CHANGE, never the absolute value. In 2D, wrinkles are drawn only on key poses so the density steps rather than flows. No installed detector segments this object class (no ultralytics/YOLO, no instance segmentation): the ROI must come from a motion-blob proposal, a cv2.TrackerCSRT seed, or object_dynamics.prop_identity_classification. This tier covers the MEASUREMENT only, not the identification.

entries.label: Additive stock element (screen-blended plate)
entries.description: A photographed smoke, dust, spark or flare plate composited in screen or add mode over the shot.
entries.frame_evidence: A translucent element that only ever lightens what is behind it, never darkens it, sometimes with a faint rectangular boundary where its plate ends.
entries.detector_note: Motion-compensate the neighbouring unique cel and check that the element's residual is strictly non-negative over its whole area; separately look for a straight-line discontinuity in the residual field that would mark a plate boundary.
entries.notes: Genuine additive phenomena (real sparks, real fire) are also strictly non-negative, so this identifies the blend mode and not the provenance; only the rectangular plate boundary is a real tell.

entries.label: AI upscale face and eye artefacts
entries.description: Faces regenerated by a face-restoration model, giving over-smooth skin with unnaturally crisp eyes and teeth.
entries.frame_evidence: On a tight face crop the skin is poreless while the iris and eyelash edges are hyper-defined, often with mismatched left and right eyes.
entries.detector_note: Crop the face using the mediapipe FaceMesh bounding box expanded 20 percent, upscale to at least 448px, and ask the qwen2.5vl judge; report the deterministic small_scale_variance inside the cheek ROI as supporting evidence.
entries.vlm_question: In this face, is the skin unnaturally smooth and poreless while the eyes and teeth look overly sharp and artificial? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Requires a mediapipe face landing, so it silently reports not-detectable on stylised 2D and extreme profiles. THE CROP RULE is decisive here: on a full frame the judge sees nothing. Overlaps post_fx.denoise_smearing on the skin measurement.

entries.label: AI upscale hallucinated micro-detail
entries.description: Invented high-frequency texture from a learned super-resolution model, crisper than the source could support.
entries.frame_evidence: Surfaces carry dense fine detail that is uniformly sharp everywhere, with no soft transitions and no grain, including in areas that should be out of focus.
entries.detector_note: Pre-screen deterministically for high hf_mf_energy_ratio combined with near-zero grain sigma and an unusually flat sharpness map, then crop 320px on a textured surface and ask the qwen2.5vl judge.
entries.vlm_question: Does the surface texture in this image look artificially over-sharpened and smeared into unnatural squiggly detail, rather than looking like a natural photograph? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Crop mandatory. This judgement is unreliable in both directions; the deterministic pre-screen (very sharp AND no grain AND flat sharpness map) is the more trustworthy part and should be reported alongside.

entries.label: Aliasing / jaggies on edges
entries.description: Hard single-pixel staircase steps on near-horizontal or near-vertical edges, from absent or insufficient anti-aliasing.
entries.frame_evidence: A diagonal edge is built from visible square pixel steps with no intermediate grey values.
entries.detector_note: Sample the edge-normal profile on near-diagonal contours and count how many pixels of intermediate value lie between the two plateaux; aliasing gives zero or one, anti-aliased edges give two or more with a regular ramp.
entries.notes: Any subsequent scaling or compression adds intermediate values and hides the aliasing; a negative result on a re-encoded delivery is uninformative. Also normal and expected in some deliberate pixel-art and limited-palette 2D styles.

entries.label: Anamorphic desqueeze error
entries.description: An image stretched or squashed horizontally by an incorrect desqueeze factor.
entries.frame_evidence: Round objects and faces read as ovals, and bokeh discs are elliptical in the same direction as the distortion.
entries.detector_note: Use the mediapipe FaceMesh interocular distance against the eye-to-chin distance and compare the ratio against the population norm across many detected faces; corroborate with the bokeh_axis_ratio from post_fx.bokeh_disc_shape, which should be oval in the same axis.
entries.notes: Real faces vary widely in proportion, so a single face proves nothing; needs several faces across a shot and agreement with the bokeh measurement. FaceMesh often fails on 2D stylisation, making the entry not-detectable there.

entries.label: Anamorphic horizontal streak
entries.description: A long thin horizontal light bar through a bright source, from anamorphic optics or a simulation of them.
entries.frame_evidence: A narrow luminous line extending symmetrically left and right from a highlight, far longer than it is tall.
entries.detector_note: Run cv2.Sobel structure-tensor orientation on the highlight neighbourhood; a streak gives a coherent near-0-degree orientation over a run whose length/width from cv2.minAreaRect on the thresholded ridge exceeds ~8:1.
entries.notes: Horizontal architectural elements (window sills, strip lights, horizons) pass the aspect test; require the ridge to peak at a highlight and decay monotonically outward.

entries.label: Streak colour cast
entries.description: The characteristic blue or cyan tint of an anamorphic streak, versus warm or neutral variants.
entries.frame_evidence: The horizontal bar reads distinctly blue against a white core.
entries.detector_note: Sample skimage.color.rgb2lab (a,b) along the streak ridge away from the clipped core and report mean hue angle and chroma.
entries.notes: The streak overlays scene colour additively, so a strongly coloured background biases the sampled hue; sample only where the underlying region is dark.

entries.label: Apparent midtone gamma
entries.description: The shape of the tonal distribution in the midtones, the visible consequence of a gamma or midtone push.
entries.frame_evidence: The image reads flat and milky, or dense and contrasty, in its middle values.
entries.detector_note: Compute the luminance CDF and report the code value at the 50th percentile plus the gamma exponent that maps a linear ramp onto the measured CDF; report per channel too.
entries.notes: HONEST LIMIT: without the ungraded source this measures the OUTPUT distribution, which is scene content convolved with the curve. It cannot recover the applied transfer function and must never be reported as one.

entries.label: Banding contours in gradients
entries.description: Visible stepped contours across what should be a smooth gradient, from insufficient bit depth or a heavy grade on 8-bit data.
entries.frame_evidence: A sky or wall shows concentric or parallel bands of flat colour separated by hard edges.
entries.detector_note: Find smooth-gradient regions (low cv2.Laplacian variance but nonzero cv2.Sobel magnitude), then count iso-luminance level transitions along the gradient direction; banding gives long runs at exactly one code value separated by single-code steps.
entries.notes: Dithered banding is invisible to the run-length test; run post_fx.dither_pattern alongside. Compression can create false plateaux in flat regions.

entries.label: Barrel / pincushion distortion
entries.description: Straight lines in the scene bowing outward or inward, from wide or long lens geometry or a deliberate simulation.
entries.frame_evidence: Architectural edges near the frame border curve visibly while lines through the centre stay straight.
entries.detector_note: Detect long edge chains with skimage.feature.canny plus contour following, fit a straight line to each, and report the mean signed sagitta (max deviation from the chord) as a function of the chain's distance from the frame centre.
entries.notes: Requires genuinely straight objects in the scene, which the analyzer cannot verify; organic and natural content makes this entry not-detectable rather than negative.

entries.label: Effective bit depth
entries.description: The real number of distinct code values surviving in the delivered image, which can be lower than the container's nominal depth.
entries.frame_evidence: Histogram teeth: occupied bins spaced at a regular interval with empty bins between them.
entries.detector_note: Autocorrelate the luminance histogram to find a comb pitch; effective_bits = log2(256/pitch). Report the comb strength so a false comb can be rejected.
entries.notes: Any per-channel gain applied after quantisation produces a comb that reflects the grade rather than the source depth; this measures the delivered file only.

entries.label: Bleach bypass look
entries.description: High contrast with heavily reduced saturation and retained highlight structure, emulating skipped bleach.
entries.frame_evidence: A harsh, silvery, near-monochrome image that still holds detail in the brightest areas.
entries.detector_note: Report the conjunction of low mean_chroma, high iqr_luminance, and low highlight_clip_frac, each against shot-relative thresholds.
entries.notes: A composite index of three other measurements with an arbitrary threshold; report the components so the index can be second-guessed.

entries.label: Anisotropic / stretched bloom
entries.description: Glow that spreads further along one axis than the other, as in anamorphic or horizontally-blurred bloom passes.
entries.frame_evidence: The halo around a round highlight is visibly oval, usually wider than tall.
entries.detector_note: Compute the second-moment covariance of the halo residual (frame minus core mask region) with skimage.measure.regionprops on the thresholded halo; report eigenvalue ratio and major-axis angle.
entries.notes: A non-round source produces an oval halo with isotropic bloom; only run on cores whose own eccentricity is below 1.2.

entries.label: Clipped plateau feeding bloom
entries.description: The bloom source is a hard-clipped flat region at code maximum rather than a rolled-off highlight.
entries.frame_evidence: Inside the glow the highlight is a featureless flat white patch with a hard boundary.
entries.detector_note: Count pixels at or above 254/255 in all three channels inside the core mask, and measure the intensity variance of that region; a plateau shows near-zero variance and a step edge in cv2.Sobel.
entries.notes: An 8-bit re-encode can clip a highlight that was rolled off in the master, so this describes the delivered file and not necessarily the comp.

entries.label: Anime glow-dodge / screen glow layer
entries.description: A drawn glow layer composited in screen/add over cel art, characteristic of 2D anime lighting passes.
entries.frame_evidence: Inside the glow region the black ink lines of the drawing are washed toward the glow colour and lose contrast, while outside it they stay full black.
entries.detector_note: Extract the ink-line mask (low-L, high cv2.Laplacian response, thin after skimage.morphology.skeletonize); compare mean line darkness inside versus outside the halo annulus; an additive layer raises the line floor by a roughly constant offset.
entries.notes: Fails where the artwork has no strong ink outlines (painterly backgrounds, effects-only frames).

entries.label: Tinted bloom hue shift
entries.description: The glow carries a different hue from the highlight that produced it, e.g. a warm amber skirt around a white core.
entries.frame_evidence: A neutral white blowout is ringed by a coloured wash.
entries.detector_note: Convert with skimage.color.rgb2lab; compare mean (a,b) of the core mask against mean (a,b) of the halo annulus; report the delta-ab vector and angle.
entries.notes: Coloured content sitting under the halo drags the annulus chroma; use the annulus median and reject frames whose underlying background chroma variance is high.

entries.label: Bloom intensity
entries.description: How much energy the glow adds relative to the core that generated it.
entries.frame_evidence: A faint wash versus a heavy milky flare occupying more area than the source highlight.
entries.detector_note: Integrate halo excess L over the annulus set and divide by the integrated core L above threshold; report the ratio.
entries.notes: Clipped cores under-report their true energy, so this ratio is biased high wherever the source is blown out.

entries.label: Multi-scale pyramid bloom
entries.description: Bloom built from several blur levels, giving a tight bright core skirt plus a very wide faint skirt.
entries.frame_evidence: The halo falloff has two distinct slopes: a fast one within a few px and a slow one carrying far across the frame.
entries.detector_note: Fit one-Gaussian versus two-Gaussian models to the radial profile with scipy.optimize.curve_fit and compare via reduced chi-square / AIC; report both sigmas and the improvement.
entries.notes: A two-component fit will almost always beat a one-component fit numerically; require a fixed AIC margin or this reports pyramid bloom everywhere.

entries.label: Bloom / glow present
entries.description: A luminous skirt of light spreading outward from bright regions, added in comp rather than present in the plate.
entries.frame_evidence: Highlights are surrounded by a soft luminance halo that decays smoothly outward and crosses over neighbouring darker detail.
entries.detector_note: Threshold luminance (skimage.color.rgb2lab L) at the 99th percentile to build a core mask; dilate with cv2.dilate and sample mean L in successive 2px annuli via scipy.ndimage.distance_transform_edt; declare bloom when the annulus decay is smooth and exceeds a null built from equally-strong NON-highlight edges (matched gradient magnitude) in the same frame.
entries.notes: Without the matched-gradient null this fires on every soft-focus bright object. Atmospheric haze in-camera produces the same annulus profile and is not separable from comp bloom on a single frame.

entries.label: Bloom radius
entries.description: The spatial extent of the glow skirt, in pixels and as a fraction of frame height.
entries.frame_evidence: The distance from a highlight edge at which the added glow falls to a small fraction of its edge value.
entries.detector_note: Fit a Gaussian plus constant to the radial halo profile (mean L per distance-transform ring) using scipy.optimize.curve_fit; report sigma in px and sigma/frame_height.
entries.notes: Halos from adjacent highlights overlap and inflate sigma; restrict fits to blobs whose nearest bright neighbour is more than 4 sigma away.

entries.label: Selectively matted glow
entries.description: Bloom applied through a matte so some equally-bright regions glow and others do not.
entries.frame_evidence: Two highlights of the same measured brightness in one frame, one haloed and one clean.
entries.detector_note: Bin bright blobs by peak L and test whether halo_core_energy_ratio is bimodal within a luminance bin using a two-sample split on the ratio distribution; report the gap and the count on each side.
entries.notes: Requires several comparable highlights; specular size and shape also modulate halo energy, so a small gap is not meaningful.

entries.label: Bloom pumping / flicker
entries.description: Glow intensity oscillating frame to frame, typically from an auto-exposure or per-frame threshold on noisy input.
entries.frame_evidence: Over a few frames the same static highlight breathes brighter and dimmer in its halo without the source changing.
entries.detector_note: Track a static bright blob across UNIQUE-CEL indices only, recompute bloom_halo_core_energy_ratio per index, and report the coefficient of variation and its dominant frequency via scipy.signal.welch.
entries.notes: Must run on unique-cel indices: on 2s and 3s the duplicate frames contribute exact zeros to the variance and halve the apparent pumping.

entries.label: Bloom threshold knee
entries.description: The source luminance above which the bloom operator starts contributing energy.
entries.frame_evidence: Bright blobs above some brightness all carry halos while blobs just below it carry none.
entries.detector_note: Segment bright blobs with cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats over a sweep of L thresholds; regress per-blob halo integral against per-blob peak L with scipy.optimize.curve_fit on a hinge function; report the hinge x-intercept in normalised L.
entries.notes: Needs at least ~8 bright blobs spanning a luminance range in one frame; a shot with a single light source cannot constrain the knee and must report null rather than a number.

entries.label: Soap-bubble bokeh (bright rim)
entries.description: Bokeh discs with a rim brighter than their centre, from spherical aberration or a naive post defocus kernel.
entries.frame_evidence: Background highlights look like hollow bright-edged bubbles.
entries.detector_note: Sample the radial intensity profile inside each bokeh blob; report the ratio of rim intensity (0.8-1.0 of radius) to centre intensity (0-0.3).
entries.notes: Clipped bokeh centres flatten the profile and hide the ratio; exclude blobs whose centre is at code maximum.

entries.label: Cat-eye (optical vignetting) bokeh
entries.description: Bokeh discs progressively clipped into lemon shapes toward the frame edges by the lens barrel.
entries.frame_evidence: Central background highlights are round while corner ones are lens-shaped and point at the frame centre.
entries.detector_note: Regress bokeh_axis_ratio and the fitted ellipse major-axis angle against blob radius and radial direction; cat-eye gives axis ratio falling with radius and the major axis aligned tangentially.
entries.notes: Needs bokeh blobs spread across the frame; a cluster of blobs in one region cannot constrain the radial trend. Its absence in an otherwise perfect bokeh field is itself a CG tell.

entries.label: Bokeh disc shape
entries.description: The shape an out-of-focus point light takes, which is the projection of the aperture.
entries.frame_evidence: Small background lights render as discs, polygons or ovals rather than points.
entries.detector_note: Threshold bright blobs in the defocused region, filter by area consistency, and report circularity 4*pi*A/P^2 and the fitted ellipse axis ratio from cv2.fitEllipse.
entries.notes: Requires isolated point sources in the defocused region; a shot with no background highlights simply cannot report bokeh shape and must log not-detectable.

entries.label: Onion-ring bokeh texture
entries.description: Concentric ridges inside each bokeh disc, from aspherical element turning marks.
entries.frame_evidence: Inside a large background highlight there are visible concentric rings rather than an even fill.
entries.detector_note: Crop the largest bokeh blob to 192px, upscale 3x with cv2.INTER_CUBIC, and ask the qwen2.5vl judge; a deterministic pre-screen can measure radial intensity oscillation via scipy.ndimage.map_coordinates ring sampling.
entries.vlm_question: Inside the bright circle in this image, are there concentric rings or ridges, rather than a smooth even fill? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Crop and upscale are mandatory; at full-frame scale a bokeh disc is a few dozen pixels and the VLM has nothing to see. Compression ringing can create false rings.

entries.label: Polygonal bokeh / blade count
entries.description: Straight-edged bokeh revealing a stopped-down iris with a countable number of blades.
entries.frame_evidence: Background highlights render as hexagons, heptagons or octagons.
entries.detector_note: cv2.approxPolyDP on each bokeh contour at 2 percent perimeter epsilon; report the modal vertex count across at least three blobs and the fraction agreeing.
entries.notes: Small or dim bokeh blobs cannot support polygon fitting; enforce a minimum diameter of roughly 20px or the vertex count is noise.

entries.label: Swirly bokeh at edges
entries.description: Bokeh smeared tangentially toward the frame corners, the Petzval swirl look.
