entries.frame_evidence: Background highlights near the edges are stretched into arcs curving around the frame centre.
entries.detector_note: Test whether the fitted bokeh ellipse major axis is tangential (perpendicular to the radial direction) with elongation increasing with radius.
entries.notes: Shares its measurement with cat-eye vignetting but with the opposite axis orientation; report both alignments so a mis-sign cannot be hidden.

entries.label: Animated CA amount
entries.description: CA strength keyframed over the shot, typically ramped up on impacts or transitions.
entries.frame_evidence: Fringe width grows and shrinks across a few frames with no change in lens or framing.
entries.detector_note: Recompute ca_corner_rg_px over UNIQUE-CEL indices and report range, peak index and slope; a real lens holds CA constant at constant zoom.
entries.notes: A zoom changes real CA too; correlate against measured frame scale change from cv2.phaseCorrelate before calling it keyframed.

entries.label: CA present on overlays and titles
entries.description: Fringing that also affects burned-in graphics or titles, revealing the effect was applied after the graphic was composited.
entries.frame_evidence: A hard-edged synthetic graphic carries the same coloured fringe as the photographic content behind it.
entries.detector_note: Locate high-contrast rectilinear regions (long straight cv2.HoughLinesP segments with flat interiors), crop 256px around a graphic edge, and ask the qwen2.5vl judge.
entries.vlm_question: Along the edge of the text or graphic shape in this image, is there a coloured red or blue fringe? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Crop required. Never route this to moondream: it involves text and moondream confabulates on text. RapidOCR is not installed, so the graphic region has to be found geometrically.

entries.label: CA sign / dispersion direction
entries.description: Whether red is displaced outward and blue inward, or the reverse, which distinguishes physical dispersion from an arbitrary comp setting.
entries.frame_evidence: Fringe colour order across a corner edge, e.g. red on the outer side and cyan on the inner side.
entries.detector_note: Report the sign of the fitted radial slopes for R and B; physical lateral CA gives opposite signs for R and B with G between them.
entries.notes: Same-sign R and B slopes mean the effect is not a lens dispersion model and is probably a comp scale-per-channel node.

entries.label: Longitudinal CA / purple fringing
entries.description: Axial colour error giving magenta and green fringes on out-of-focus high-contrast edges regardless of frame position.
entries.frame_evidence: Purple halos on backlit branches or specular edges anywhere in frame, including the centre.
entries.detector_note: Sample skimage.color.rgb2lab (a,b) on each side of strong edges along the edge normal (from skimage.filters.sobel_h/sobel_v); flag when one side is magenta-shifted and the other green-shifted AND post_fx.chromatic_aberration_lateral shows no radial trend.
entries.notes: JPEG/H.264 chroma ringing at 4:2:0 also produces magenta-green edge pairs; check the fringe survives at a lower compression proxy or is wider than 2px.

entries.label: Per-channel resolution mismatch
entries.description: One colour channel measurably softer than the others, from lens focus error, chroma subsampling or a deliberate channel blur.
entries.frame_evidence: Fine detail is crisp in green but mushy in blue on the same edge.
entries.detector_note: Per channel compute high-frequency energy from numpy.fft.rfft2 above a fixed radial cutoff, normalised by that channel's total energy; report ratios between channels.
entries.notes: 4:2:0 subsampling always makes chroma softer, which shows up here as a blue and red deficit; report jointly with post_fx.chroma_subsample_edge_bleed before attributing to optics.

entries.label: Uniform per-channel translation
entries.description: A constant XY offset applied to whole colour channels, the stylistic RGB-split look rather than a lens model.
entries.frame_evidence: The same coloured double-image offset appears identically at the frame centre and the corners.
entries.detector_note: Run skimage.registration.phase_cross_correlation on the whole frame per channel pair; a large global shift with a near-zero radial slope from post_fx.chromatic_aberration_lateral is the signature.
entries.notes: A strongly colour-biased scene can bias whole-frame phase correlation; verify with several independent tiles.

entries.label: Low-frequency chroma noise
entries.description: Coloured blotches in shadows, from high-ISO chroma noise or aggressive luma-only denoise.
entries.frame_evidence: Soft red-green patches several dozen pixels across in dark areas, with no matching luma structure.
entries.detector_note: Lowpass the a and b channels of skimage.color.rgb2lab with cv2.GaussianBlur(sigma~8) and measure their variance inside shadow masks; report the ratio of chroma variance to luma variance at that scale.
entries.notes: Genuinely coloured shadow lighting (practical gels, coloured bounce) is the main false positive; requires the luma to be flat where the chroma is not.

entries.label: Chroma subsampling edge bleed
entries.description: Colour resolved at half the luma resolution, so saturated edges bleed and step in 2x2 blocks.
entries.frame_evidence: A red object against a blue background shows a colour boundary that is blockier and offset from the luminance boundary.
entries.detector_note: Compare the gradient magnitude of the Y channel against Cb and Cr at high-saturation edges, and test whether the chroma channels are constant over 2x2 pixel blocks; cross-check pix_fmt from ffprobe.
entries.notes: ffprobe gives the container's declared format directly, which makes this entry near-certain for the delivered file; what it cannot tell you is whether the subsampling was already baked into the master.

entries.label: Lateral chromatic aberration
entries.description: Colour channels scaled slightly differently about the optical centre, so fringing grows with distance from the centre.
entries.frame_evidence: High-contrast edges near the frame corners carry cyan/red fringes on opposite sides, while centre edges are clean.
entries.detector_note: Tile the frame into an annular grid; per tile run skimage.registration.phase_cross_correlation(R, G, upsample_factor=20) and the same for B vs G; project each shift onto the tile radial unit vector and fit shift_radial = k*r with numpy.polyfit.
entries.notes: Tiles with no edge content give random shifts; weight the fit by tile gradient energy. Coloured motion blur and subject colour edges bias individual tiles, so trust only the fitted slope.

entries.label: Clipped highlights
entries.description: Highlight detail lost to code maximum, either in camera or by the grade.
entries.frame_evidence: Flat white regions with a hard boundary and no texture.
entries.detector_note: Report the fraction of pixels at code 253-255 per channel, the count of contiguous clipped regions above a size floor, and whether channels clip together (neutral clip) or separately (coloured clip).
entries.notes: Specular highlights on water or metal clip in almost every real image; only large contiguous clipped areas are worth reporting.

entries.label: Cross-process / crossed channel curves
entries.description: Per-channel curves pushed in opposite directions, giving colour casts that differ between shadows and highlights within the same channel.
entries.frame_evidence: Shadows go cyan while highlights go yellow, with unnaturally saturated mid colours.
entries.detector_note: Bin pixels by L into 8 bins and report per-channel mean per bin; cross-processing shows channel curves that cross each other rather than staying ordered.
entries.notes: Scene content dominates each L bin, so the crossing is a property of this frame's colours as much as of the curve.

entries.label: CRT phosphor mask / aperture grille
entries.description: An RGB stripe or dot mask simulating a CRT's phosphor structure at pixel scale.
entries.frame_evidence: At close inspection the image is built from repeating red, green and blue vertical stripes or triads.
entries.detector_note: Take per-channel column-mean signals and compare their phases at the dominant horizontal spatial frequency from numpy.fft.rfft; a phosphor mask gives equal-frequency peaks in all three channels at 120-degree relative phase.
entries.notes: Destroyed by any downscale or chroma subsampling; a negative result on a compressed or resized delivery is uninformative.

entries.label: Crushed blacks
entries.description: Shadow detail destroyed by clipping at or near code zero.
entries.frame_evidence: Large areas of dead flat black with no separation, and a spike at the bottom of the histogram.
entries.detector_note: Report the fraction of pixels at code 0-2 in all channels, and the histogram spike ratio at the floor relative to the neighbouring bins.
entries.notes: A night exterior legitimately contains large true blacks; the spike ratio (a discontinuity, not just a lot of dark pixels) is the discriminating measurement.

entries.label: Datamosh I-frame bloom / block displacement
entries.description: Blocks of the frame jumping to wrong positions or holding stale content, from duplicated or corrupted reference frames.
entries.frame_evidence: Rectangular patches on a regular grid sit at the wrong offset or show content from a different moment, with hard block boundaries.
entries.detector_note: Block-match 16x16 tiles against the previous frame with cv2.matchTemplate; flag tiles whose best offset is a large outlier relative to the local median offset field, and report the count and the grid alignment of the offending tiles.
entries.notes: Genuine fast motion with occlusion also produces outlier block matches; the grid alignment of the outliers is what distinguishes a codec artefact from real motion.

entries.label: Datamosh P-frame smear
entries.description: Motion vectors from one shot applied to the pixels of another because I-frames were removed, so the image advects without refreshing.
entries.frame_evidence: Content drags and stretches in macroblock-sized clumps that carry old colours into new positions, with no new detail appearing.
entries.detector_note: Measure the fraction of the frame whose change from the previous frame is pure displacement (high cv2.calcOpticalFlowFarneback magnitude) with near-zero new high-frequency energy from numpy.fft.rfft2, and test that the displacement field is piecewise constant on a 16px grid.
entries.notes: Requires unique-cel indexing so held frames are not read as zero-advection. A slow dissolve also adds no new high frequencies and can trip the second metric alone.

entries.label: Day-for-night grade
entries.description: Daylight footage graded dark and blue to read as night, betrayed by daytime lighting cues surviving the grade.
entries.frame_evidence: A dark blue image that still contains hard sun shadows, a bright sky or blown daylight windows.
entries.detector_note: Crop 384px on the highest-contrast shadow boundary in a frame that measures as dark and blue (low mean L, shadow_hue_deg in the blue range) and ask the qwen2.5vl judge.
entries.vlm_question: Does this dark blue image show hard sharp shadows like bright sunlight, rather than soft dim night lighting? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Crop mandatory. This is a judgement call even for a person; treat any yes as a flag for review, never as a determination.

entries.label: DCT block artefacts
entries.description: Visible 8x8 or 16x16 discontinuities from block-transform compression at low bitrate.
entries.frame_evidence: Flat areas break into square tiles with faint seams aligned to a regular grid.
entries.detector_note: Compute the mean absolute horizontal and vertical pixel difference as a function of coordinate modulo 8 and modulo 16; blocking gives a clear peak at the block boundary phase. Report the peak-to-mean ratio for both grid sizes.
entries.notes: An 8-pixel-periodic scene texture (tiles, grilles) can align with the grid; the phase must be consistent across the entire frame, which scene texture rarely is.

entries.label: Deep focus / no defocus anywhere
entries.description: Everything from foreground to background is equally sharp, common in unmodified CG renders and in flat 2D.
entries.frame_evidence: Distant and near detail resolve equally crisply in the same frame.
entries.detector_note: Report a unimodal, high-mean tile sharpness distribution with low spread, together with a null verdict from post_fx.depth_of_field_present.
entries.notes: A frame with little depth range is trivially deep-focus; not informative unless the shot clearly contains near and far content.

entries.label: Deinterlace blend ghosting
entries.description: Two fields averaged into one frame, giving a soft double image on motion instead of combing.
entries.frame_evidence: Moving edges show a symmetric semi-transparent double rather than teeth, and vertical resolution is halved.
entries.detector_note: Look for doubled edges (two peaks in gradient autocorrelation) on moving tiles combined with a near-zero comb_score and reduced vertical high-frequency energy relative to horizontal.
entries.notes: Indistinguishable from post_fx.frame_blend_ghosting except by the vertical-only resolution deficit; report both entries together.

entries.label: Denoise blotching / watercolour patches
entries.description: Patchy regions of averaged colour from non-local-means or wavelet denoising pushed too far.
entries.frame_evidence: Flat irregular puddles of colour in what should be continuous-tone shadow areas.
entries.detector_note: Segment near-flat regions in shadows and measure the count and size distribution of plateaux whose boundaries do not align with any gradient in the pre-denoise-scale structure (compare against a cv2.pyrDown/pyrUp reconstruction).
entries.notes: Chroma noise blobs from post_fx.chroma_noise_blobs are the inverse artefact and can co-occur; both are shadow-region phenomena and easy to confuse.

entries.label: Denoise smearing / plastic texture
entries.description: Fine low-contrast texture erased while edges are preserved, giving waxy surfaces.
entries.frame_evidence: Skin, fabric and foliage read as smooth plastic while hard object outlines stay crisp.
entries.detector_note: Measure local variance at small scales in mid-contrast regions and compare against the frame's edge-scale gradient energy; denoise gives collapsed small-scale variance with intact large-scale gradients. Report the ratio against the shot's own distribution.
entries.notes: A genuinely smooth subject reads identically. The project's waxy-skin work shows this ratio is only interpretable relative to comparable material elsewhere in the same shot.

entries.label: Temporal denoise ghost trail
entries.description: A faint trailing copy behind a moving subject, from temporal noise reduction averaging across frames.
entries.frame_evidence: A dim residue of the subject's previous position lingering behind it in the direction it came from.
entries.detector_note: After motion-compensating the previous UNIQUE cel onto the current one, look for a low-amplitude positive residual in the region the subject just vacated, aligned opposite the flow vector.
entries.notes: Occlusion holes produce residual in the same place; require the residual to be a scaled copy of the subject rather than background revelation.

entries.label: Per-pixel depth for DOF and haze checks
entries.description: A depth estimate for every pixel, which would turn several suggestive entries in this shard into real measurements.
entries.frame_evidence: Not a visual observable; a missing capability that several other entries depend on.
entries.detector_note: Needs a monocular depth network (Depth Anything, MiDaS or similar). torch 2.10 and onnxruntime are installed but no depth weights are; there is no depth capability in the audited runtime today.
entries.notes: Blocks honest verdicts on post_fx.dof_sharpness_gradient, post_fx.dof_depth_matte_halo, post_fx.haze_vs_diffusion_filter and post_fx.edge_sharpness_mismatch, all of which currently substitute screen position for depth and say so.

entries.label: Shallow depth of field present
entries.description: Part of the frame is in focus and part is not, from optics or a post defocus pass.
entries.frame_evidence: A sharp subject sits against a background whose detail is smoothly dissolved.
entries.detector_note: Build a sharpness map from per-tile cv2.Laplacian variance (or the high-frequency fraction of numpy.fft.rfft2 per tile); test the tile distribution for bimodality against a unimodal null and report the separation.
entries.notes: A frame whose background is genuinely textureless reads as defocused; require the soft region to still contain low-frequency structure. Heavy compression flattens background detail and mimics DOF.

entries.label: Diffusion filter / pro-mist haze
entries.description: An overall softening filter that lifts blacks and blooms highlights uniformly, with no radial dependence.
entries.frame_evidence: The entire frame carries a low-contrast veil, fine detail stays but sits on a raised floor, and every highlight has a small halo.
entries.detector_note: Measure the ratio of low-frequency to high-frequency energy from numpy.fft.rfft2 on L, plus the black-point offset; diffusion shows a raised floor with retained high-frequency edges (unlike blur, which removes them) and a flat glare-versus-radius profile.
entries.notes: Real atmospheric haze, fog and a dirty lens are indistinguishable from a diffusion filter by pixels alone.

entries.label: Digital sensor noise
entries.description: Electronic noise from a camera sensor, shadow-weighted and with a different spatial spectrum than film grain.
entries.frame_evidence: Fine noise concentrated in the darkest parts of the image, often with a slight colour blotchiness.
entries.detector_note: Combine a shadow-peaked grain_sigma_by_l_bin with a near-white residual power spectrum (numpy.fft.rfft2 of the residual is flat to Nyquist) and low grain_autocorr_hwhm_px.
entries.notes: Modern grain emulations deliberately imitate sensor statistics; this distinction is a heuristic, not a determination.

entries.label: Uniform directional blur
entries.description: A single blur angle and length applied to the entire frame regardless of content, a post effect rather than a shutter.
entries.frame_evidence: Every part of the frame, including things that are not moving, is smeared the same way.
entries.detector_note: Report the standard deviation of the tile blur-angle field and length field; a uniform post blur gives near-zero spread across every tile including static background.
entries.notes: Camera shake blur is also globally uniform; disambiguate by whether it persists on frames with no measured global motion.

entries.label: Dither noise pattern
entries.description: Deliberate low-amplitude noise added to break up quantisation banding.
entries.frame_evidence: A very fine, very low-contrast speckle visible only in smooth gradients, of amplitude around one code value.
entries.detector_note: In smooth-gradient regions measure residual sigma; dither sits near 0.5-1.5 code values with a blue-noise-shaped spectrum (numpy.fft.rfft2 power rising toward Nyquist), unlike white grain.
entries.notes: Below the 8-bit quantisation floor after re-encode this vanishes entirely; a negative result on a compressed proxy means nothing.

entries.label: Defocus bleeding over the subject
entries.description: Background blur eating into a sharp foreground edge, from a soft or misaligned depth matte.
entries.frame_evidence: The outline of the in-focus subject is chewed or softened where the blurred background overlaps it.
entries.detector_note: Crop 256px on the sharpest silhouette segment (highest gradient contour bordering a low-sharpness tile) and ask the qwen2.5vl judge.
entries.vlm_question: Is the outline of the sharp object in this image eaten into or smudged by the blurry background, instead of having a clean crisp edge? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Crop mandatory. Genuine shallow DOF softens edges slightly at the exact focal boundary, so a yes here is weak unless the gradient width varies along the same contour.

entries.label: Post-DOF depth matte halo
entries.description: A ring of intermediate blur hugging a sharp foreground silhouette, from a depth-map-driven defocus applied in 2D.
entries.frame_evidence: Around a sharp subject there is a narrow band where the background is less blurred than it is further away.
entries.detector_note: Build the tile sharpness map, dilate the sharp-subject mask, and test whether sharpness in the annulus just outside the silhouette is significantly higher than in the far background at equal depth cue.
entries.notes: Genuine subject-adjacent background elements are often at a similar depth and legitimately sharper; this needs the halo to follow the silhouette at constant width to be meaningful.

entries.label: Focus falloff profile
entries.description: How quickly sharpness decays away from the focal plane, the perceptual read of aperture.
entries.frame_evidence: The transition from sharp to soft is either abrupt (very shallow) or gradual (deep).
entries.detector_note: Order tiles by their distance from the sharpest tile cluster and fit the sharpness decay; report the decay rate and the width of the in-focus band in tiles.
entries.notes: Tile distance in screen space is not depth; the profile is only meaningful in shots where depth varies monotonically with screen position.

entries.label: Duotone / gradient map
entries.description: Luminance mapped onto a two-or-three-colour ramp, so hue is a deterministic function of brightness.
entries.frame_evidence: Every dark pixel in the frame is the same hue and every bright pixel is another, with no independent colour variation.
entries.detector_note: Regress Lab (a,b) on L across all pixels; a gradient map gives near-perfect fit (very high r2) because chroma carries no information independent of luminance.
entries.notes: The r2 test is strong and cheap; its false positive is a scene lit by a single coloured source, which also makes hue a function of brightness.

entries.label: Dust specks and positive dirt
entries.description: Small bright or dark points appearing for a single frame, from dirt on the negative or a dirt overlay.
entries.frame_evidence: Isolated 1-4px white or black dots scattered over the frame that are gone in the next frame.
entries.detector_note: scipy.ndimage.white_tophat and black_tophat with a small structuring element to isolate point outliers, then reject any speck that persists at the same motion-compensated position in the neighbouring unique cels.
entries.notes: Sensor hot pixels persist and are correctly rejected by the persistence test, but compression noise spikes are not; require the speck to exceed the local sigma by a wide margin.

entries.label: Edge sharpness mismatch between elements
entries.description: A composited element whose edges resolve at a different sharpness from the plate it sits in.
entries.frame_evidence: One object in the frame has noticeably crisper or softer outlines than everything at the same apparent depth.
entries.detector_note: Measure edge gradient width (10-90 percent rise distance) per contour and cluster the results; report the gap between clusters and the area occupied by each, restricted to regions with comparable sharpness_map values.
entries.notes: Depth of field legitimately makes edges at different depths differ; this only means something when the elements are at the same apparent depth, which the analyzer cannot establish on its own.

entries.label: Per-element segmentation for comp integration checks
entries.description: Knowing which pixels belong to which composited element, the prerequisite for reliable grain, sharpness and grade matching between elements.
entries.frame_evidence: Not a visual observable; a missing capability.
entries.detector_note: Needs a segmentation model (SAM, or a detector such as YOLO). ultralytics and insightface are NOT installed; mediapipe covers only people (pose/face/hands), which is far short of general element segmentation.
entries.notes: post_fx.grain_mismatch_between_elements and post_fx.edge_sharpness_mismatch currently substitute a coarse tile clustering for real element masks, which is why both carry large false-positive caveats.

entries.label: Emulsion blotch / chemical stain
entries.description: An irregular soft-edged discoloured patch, from damage or a decay overlay.
entries.frame_evidence: An amorphous brown or green stain sitting on top of the image for a short run of frames.
entries.detector_note: Pre-screen for connected regions whose Lab chroma departs strongly from the local neighbourhood with soft boundaries and short temporal persistence, crop 384px, and ask the qwen2.5vl judge.
entries.vlm_question: Is there a brown or discoloured stain or blotch sitting on top of this picture, that is not part of the scene? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Crop mandatory. Genuinely stained or discoloured objects in the scene are indistinguishable to the VLM; this entry is a flag for review only.

entries.label: Film grain present
entries.description: A stochastic texture overlaying the image, either real emulsion grain or a grain plate added in comp.
entries.frame_evidence: Flat areas that should be featureless carry a fine random speckle that changes every frame.
entries.detector_note: Isolate flat ROIs (tiles whose cv2.Laplacian variance is in the lowest decile), estimate residual sigma with skimage.restoration.estimate_sigma(channel_axis=-1), and confirm the residual is temporally decorrelated across UNIQUE-CEL indices.
entries.notes: Compression denoises flat areas hard, so a low sigma can mean a clean encode rather than a clean plate. On a duplicate-frame pair the temporal decorrelation reads 0 spuriously; unique-cel indexing is mandatory.

entries.label: Identify the specific film stock or LUT
entries.description: Naming which print stock emulation or which commercial LUT produced the look, rather than merely describing it.
entries.frame_evidence: A characteristic combination of curve shape, split tone, halation ratio and hue clamping specific to one stock or LUT.
entries.detector_note: Needs a classifier trained on a labelled corpus of stock and LUT renders of identical source material; nothing in the installed stack (cv2/numpy/scipy/skimage/torch with no trained weights) can do this, and the ollama VLMs cannot resolve the required colorimetric precision.
entries.notes: Logged as a blind spot on purpose. The measurable descriptors in the colour_grade group are the honest substitute; they characterise the look but cannot name it.

entries.label: Fixed-pattern row / column noise
entries.description: Horizontal or vertical banding noise from sensor readout, appearing as whole-line offsets.
entries.frame_evidence: Faint horizontal streaks running the full width of the frame in shadow areas.
entries.detector_note: Take the residual row means and column means, then scipy.signal.welch on each 1D signal; row noise shows broadband power in the row-mean signal far above the shot-noise floor predicted from sigma/sqrt(width).
entries.notes: The sqrt(width) null model is essential here; without it any frame with horizontal content reads as row noise.

entries.label: Drawn sparkle / cross-star (2D)
entries.description: A hand-drawn four- or six-point star sparkle used in 2D animation, with hard vector-like edges rather than an optical falloff.
entries.frame_evidence: A crisp symmetric cross of light with sharply defined tapering arms and a flat white core, sitting on flat cel colour.
entries.detector_note: Measure edge hardness along the arm normals (cv2.Sobel gradient width in px) and compare against the optical starburst model; drawn sparkles have 1-2px transitions and near-perfect 90 or 60 degree symmetry, plus zero surrounding grain.
entries.notes: A rendered starburst with a very small blur radius can also have hard edges; combine with the flat-fill background test from post_fx.grain_on_flat_fill_2d.

entries.label: Ghost chain along the optical axis
entries.description: A row of repeated bright shapes spaced along the line joining the light source and the frame centre.
entries.frame_evidence: Several translucent discs or polygons of decreasing brightness marching across the frame from the light toward and past the centre.
entries.detector_note: Threshold and label blobs with cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats, then test collinearity of blob centroids with the source centroid and the frame centre (perpendicular distance under a few px) and report count and spacing regularity.
entries.notes: Practical lights in a row (street lamps, ceiling fixtures) can be collinear with the centre by chance; require at least three blobs and low spacing variance.

entries.label: Ghost aperture polygon
entries.description: Ghosts shaped as polygons whose side count reveals the simulated iris blade count.
entries.frame_evidence: A ghost with visibly straight edges and corners rather than a smooth circle.
entries.detector_note: cv2.findContours on each ghost mask then cv2.approxPolyDP with epsilon at 2 percent of the perimeter; report the modal vertex count across ghosts and the circularity 4*pi*A/P^2.
entries.notes: Low-contrast ghost edges make approxPolyDP unstable; only trust the vertex count when at least two ghosts agree.

entries.label: Textured iris ghost (stock plate)
entries.description: Ghosts carrying visible dust, scratch or hexagonal internal texture from a photographed flare element.
entries.frame_evidence: Inside the ghost shape there is fine dirt-like structure rather than a smooth gradient.
entries.detector_note: Crop the largest ghost to 256px, upscale 2x with cv2.INTER_CUBIC, and ask the qwen2.5vl judge.
entries.vlm_question: Inside the bright ring-shaped shape in this image, is there visible speckled dust or scratch-like texture, rather than a smooth even glow? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Crop only; moondream must not be used here as the fine texture question invites confabulation. Sensor noise inside a dim ghost mimics the texture.

entries.label: Streak from an off-screen source
entries.description: A flare whose originating light lies outside the frame, so only its streak or ghosts are visible.
entries.frame_evidence: A bright bar or ghost chain that enters from a frame border with no visible light source at its origin.
entries.detector_note: Trace the ridge with skimage.filters.frangi or a Sobel ridge follower; if intensity increases monotonically toward a frame border and no local maximum exists inside the frame, flag off-screen origin.
entries.notes: A ridge clipped by a foreground object can look border-bound; check that the ridge actually reaches the frame edge.

entries.label: Chromatic rainbow ghost
entries.description: A ghost with radial hue rotation, from a simulated dispersive coating.
entries.frame_evidence: Concentric colour rings inside a single ghost, cycling through hue from centre to rim.
entries.detector_note: Within a ghost mask, regress skimage.color.rgb2lab hue angle against normalised radius; a monotone hue sweep beyond a set number of degrees flags the rainbow ghost.
entries.notes: Very small ghosts contain too few pixels to fit a hue gradient; enforce a minimum ghost area.

entries.label: Non-tracking pasted flare
entries.description: A flare element that stays put while the plate moves, betraying a stock overlay dropped on top of the shot.
entries.frame_evidence: Across a camera move the scene slides but the streak or ghosts remain locked to the same screen position.
entries.detector_note: Estimate global plate motion with cv2.phaseCorrelate on a masked frame, then compare it to the tracked flare centroid motion over unique-cel indices; a near-zero flare motion with non-zero plate motion is the flag.
entries.notes: A locked-off camera makes both motions zero and the test uninformative; gate on plate_motion_px above a floor.

entries.label: Flare tracks the source optically
entries.description: Ghosts translate opposite to the light source about the frame centre as the camera moves, as real internal reflections do.
entries.frame_evidence: Over several frames the source moves one way and the ghost chain slides the other way through the frame centre.
entries.detector_note: Track the source blob and ghost centroids across UNIQUE-CEL indices; fit ghost_displacement = -k * source_displacement about the frame centre and report k and fit quality.
entries.notes: Must use unique-cel indices; on duplicated frames the displacement is exactly zero and k is undefined, which reads as a failed track rather than a static flare.

entries.label: Flash frame / single-frame luminance spike
entries.description: One or two frames of a near-white or near-black full-frame flash, used as an impact or transition device.
entries.frame_evidence: A single frame whose mean luminance is far outside the range of every neighbouring frame.
entries.detector_note: Flag frames whose mean L departs from the local rolling median by more than a wide multiple of the local MAD, and whose neighbours revert; report the polarity and duration in frames.
entries.notes: A genuine practical flash (lightning, camera strobe, muzzle flash) is measurement-identical. Report duration, since a one-frame full-frame spike is more likely an edit device than a practical.

entries.label: Focus breathing
entries.description: Field of view changing slightly as focus is pulled, a lens characteristic absent from most CG and post defocus.
entries.frame_evidence: During a focus pull the whole frame appears to zoom marginally in or out.
entries.detector_note: Estimate per-frame scale with log-polar cv2.phaseCorrelate against the shot's first unique cel and correlate the scale trajectory against the rack focus trajectory.
entries.notes: Scale estimation is sensitive to subject motion; only trustworthy on locked-off shots. Its absence during a rack is a CG or post-defocus tell but not a proof.

entries.label: Frame-blend retime ghosting
entries.description: Double images from a retime that cross-dissolves neighbouring frames rather than interpolating motion.
entries.frame_evidence: A moving subject shows two distinct semi-transparent copies of itself with a clear gap, not a continuous smear.
entries.detector_note: Autocorrelate the gradient magnitude of the moving ROI: a blend gives two discrete peaks (a doubled edge) where true motion blur gives a single broadened lobe; report peak count and separation.
entries.notes: Drawn multiples in 2D animation produce the same doubled-edge signature by design; check applies_to context before calling it a retime defect.

entries.label: Frame duplication cadence (unique-cel index)
entries.description: The map of which frames are genuinely new images versus held duplicates, the prerequisite for every temporal metric in this domain.
entries.frame_evidence: Consecutive decoded frames are byte-for-byte or near-identical, then a new drawing appears.
entries.detector_note: Per adjacent pair compute mean absolute difference and skimage.metrics.structural_similarity; classify a frame as a duplicate below a MAD threshold calibrated per shot against the codec noise floor; emit the unique-cel index list and the modal hold length (1=on 1s, 2=on 2s, 3=on 3s).
entries.notes: MUST run before any pair or short-window entry in this shard. Anime on 2s and 3s gives exactly-zero optical flow between duplicates and that zero is an artefact, not a measurement. Codec noise makes duplicates non-identical, so the threshold has to be calibrated, not fixed.

entries.label: Gain / white point per channel
entries.description: Where each channel's ceiling sits, the numeric read of the gain control.
entries.frame_evidence: The brightest pixels clip at different levels per channel, tinting the highlights.
entries.detector_note: Report the 99.9th percentile of each channel histogram and the per-channel clipped-pixel fraction.
entries.notes: Same caveat as lift: no highlight in the scene means no ceiling to measure.

entries.label: Gate weave
entries.description: Whole-frame sub-pixel translation jitter from imperfect film registration, added deliberately in film emulations.
entries.frame_evidence: Over a run of frames the entire image drifts a fraction of a pixel up, down and sideways, most visible on locked-off shots.
entries.detector_note: Estimate the global translation between consecutive UNIQUE cels with cv2.phaseCorrelate at sub-pixel precision, highpass the resulting trajectory to remove intended camera motion, and report the residual RMS in px and its spectrum.
entries.notes: On a moving camera the highpass cannot fully separate weave from handheld micro-motion. On 2s and 3s the trajectory is sampled only at cel changes, which aliases the weave spectrum; report the sampling rate alongside the frequency.

entries.label: Frame generated or altered by a diffusion model
entries.description: Whether the image was produced or retouched by a generative model rather than rendered or photographed.
entries.frame_evidence: Diffuse statistical fingerprints in the frequency domain and in local texture statistics, not a single visible feature.
entries.detector_note: Needs a trained provenance classifier. Reported frequency-domain heuristics are not reliable across generators and degrade to chance after re-encoding, so the installed stack cannot support a verdict.
entries.notes: post_fx.ai_upscale_hallucinated_texture and post_fx.ai_upscale_face_artefact catch only the crude super-resolution case on a crop, and even those are flags for review.

entries.label: Glow bleeding across an occluder
entries.description: The glow spills over a foreground object that should be in front of the light source, revealing a 2D post-process rather than a lit render.
entries.frame_evidence: A silhouette edge that crosses the halo is uniformly lifted on both sides instead of blocking the light.
entries.detector_note: Crop a 256px box centred on the intersection of the strongest luminance contour and the halo boundary (found with skimage.feature.canny plus the halo mask) and ask the qwen2.5vl judge; the crop is mandatory since the halo is invisible at full-frame scale.
entries.vlm_question: In this image, does the glow spread across and over the dark object in front of the light, instead of being blocked by it? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: THE CROP RULE applies; a full frame gets a confabulated yes. Genuine atmospheric scatter in front of an object looks identical, so a yes is evidence of a 2D glow pass, not proof.

entries.label: GOP quality pulsing
entries.description: Image quality improving at each keyframe and degrading through the GOP, a rate-control artefact.
entries.frame_evidence: Detail and blocking visibly breathe on a fixed period of roughly 12 to 60 frames.
entries.detector_note: Track block8_boundary_ratio and hf energy per frame over the shot and autocorrelate; report the period and, where available, cross-check keyframe positions from ffprobe -show_frames -select_streams v.
entries.notes: ffprobe keyframe positions make the alignment check strong. On 2s and 3s content the hold pattern adds its own periodicity to any frame-level metric, so report post_fx.frame_duplicate_cadence beside this.

entries.label: Grade drift within a shot
entries.description: Colour or exposure changing over a single shot, from auto-exposure, auto-white-balance or a keyframed grade.
entries.frame_evidence: Over a few seconds the whole frame warms, cools or brightens with no lighting change in the scene.
entries.detector_note: Track frame mean L and mean (a,b) across UNIQUE-CEL indices and report the trend slope and total excursion; separate stepwise (auto-exposure hunting) from smooth (keyframed) by the derivative's roughness.
entries.notes: Genuine lighting changes in the scene are the obvious confound; a drift that affects a static background region as much as the subject is the stronger evidence.

entries.label: Grade mismatch across a cut
entries.description: Adjacent shots that should match visibly differ in black point, white point or colour cast.
entries.frame_evidence: Across a cut the same location or subject jumps in warmth or density.
entries.detector_note: Compare shot-median black floor, white ceiling, mean_chroma and mean (a,b) between consecutive shots detected by a cut detector (frame-difference plus histogram-correlation threshold); report the deltas.
entries.notes: Different content across a cut legitimately differs in every one of these; only meaningful when the two shots share subject or location, which the analyzer cannot verify on its own.

entries.label: Recover the applied grade curve
entries.description: Determining the actual lift-gamma-gain or curve values that were applied, as opposed to the resulting pixel distribution.
entries.frame_evidence: None available: the graded frame alone contains the output, not the operator.
entries.detector_note: Mathematically underdetermined without the ungraded source. Every entry in the colour_grade group that mentions gamma, lift or gain measures the OUTPUT distribution, which is scene content convolved with the unknown curve.
entries.notes: This entry exists so that post_fx.apparent_gamma_curve and post_fx.lift_black_offset are never read as recovered grade values. A detector with no null model produces confident numbers that mean nothing, and this is the specific place that trap lies.

entries.label: Grain versus exposure curve
entries.description: How grain amplitude varies with local brightness: film peaks in the midtones, sensor noise dominates the shadows, and a naive overlay is flat.
entries.frame_evidence: Speckle is obvious in shadows and invisible in midtones, or the reverse, or uniform everywhere.
entries.detector_note: Bin flat ROIs by mean L into 8 bins and report sigma per bin; classify the curve shape by the location of its maximum.
entries.notes: Needs flat ROIs spanning the exposure range; a low-key frame yields only shadow bins and the curve shape cannot be classified.

entries.label: Grain mismatch across composited elements
entries.description: Different image elements in the same frame carrying different grain amplitude, a classic tell of an unmatched composite.
entries.frame_evidence: A CG or 2D element in the frame is conspicuously clean while the photographic background is grainy, or vice versa.
entries.detector_note: Compute per-tile grain sigma across the frame and test for spatial clustering of sigma into distinct populations (variance-ratio between a coarse region split versus within-region variance); report the max inter-region sigma gap and the region masks.
entries.notes: Detail-rich areas suppress the flat-ROI estimator and read as low sigma, so a sigma gap can just be a texture gap; restrict to tiles that pass the flatness test in both regions.

entries.label: Grain over flat cel fill (2D)
entries.description: Grain added over 2D animation, unambiguous because cel colour fills are mathematically flat before it.
entries.frame_evidence: A large single-colour character fill carries visible speckle where the source drawing had none.
entries.detector_note: Find flat-fill regions by colour quantisation (large connected components of near-identical RGB after cv2.pyrMeanShiftFiltering), then measure residual sigma inside them; any nonzero sigma above the codec floor is added texture.
entries.notes: The cleanest grain measurement available in 2D, because the pre-grain image is known to be flat; the only confound is codec ringing near region borders, so erode the mask before measuring.

entries.label: Per-channel grain independence
entries.description: Whether the three colour layers grain independently (film-like) or move together (luma-only grain or post-demosaic sensor noise).
entries.frame_evidence: Grain appears as coloured speckle versus purely monochrome speckle.
entries.detector_note: Compute the 3x3 Pearson correlation matrix of the R, G, B residuals over flat ROIs with numpy.corrcoef; near-1 off-diagonals mean luma-only grain, low off-diagonals mean independent layers.
entries.notes: Chroma subsampling correlates the chroma residuals artificially; measure in a 4:4:4 decode or note the codec's subsampling from ffprobe.

entries.label: Grain plate tiling or looping
entries.description: A finite grain clip repeated spatially or temporally, so the same random pattern recurs.
entries.frame_evidence: The same grain arrangement reappears after a fixed number of frames, or a visible seam repeats across the frame.
entries.detector_note: Cross-correlate the residual of frame t against t+lag for lags 1..N over unique cels and look for a secondary peak; spatially, autocorrelate the residual over the whole frame and look for off-centre peaks at a fixed pitch.
entries.notes: Requires a long enough shot to see the period; short shots must report not-detectable rather than no-loop.

entries.label: Grain sigma
entries.description: The amplitude of the grain in code values, the primary dial of any grain node.
entries.frame_evidence: How coarse and visible the speckle is in a flat midtone patch.
entries.detector_note: Report median skimage.restoration.estimate_sigma over flat ROIs, in 8-bit code values and normalised to 0-1, per channel and for luma.
entries.notes: estimate_sigma assumes additive Gaussian noise; heavily structured grain plates violate that and the number becomes a relative index, not a physical sigma.

entries.label: Grain particle size
entries.description: The spatial scale of individual grain particles, distinguishing fine 35mm from coarse 16mm or an upscaled grain plate.
entries.frame_evidence: Grain reads as tight pepper versus visible clumps several pixels across.
entries.detector_note: Autocorrelate the flat-ROI residual with scipy.signal.fftconvolve (self-correlation) and report the half-width at half-maximum of the central lobe in px.
entries.notes: An upscale after graining inflates the measured size; report jointly with post_fx.native_resolution_estimate or the number means the delivery scale, not the stock.

entries.label: Frozen (non-animating) grain
entries.description: A grain or texture overlay that does not change frame to frame, betraying a still plate rather than a per-frame process.
entries.frame_evidence: The identical speckle pattern sits in the same screen position across several distinct frames.
entries.detector_note: Motion-compensate consecutive UNIQUE-CEL frames using cv2.calcOpticalFlowFarneback plus cv2.remap, then correlate their flat-ROI residuals; correlation near 1 means frozen grain.
entries.notes: This is the entry most damaged by 2s/3s animation: two duplicate frames correlate at 1.0 trivially. Compute only between distinct cels, and skip the entry entirely when the shot is a freeze.

entries.label: Identify the grain stock or plate source
entries.description: Naming which film stock or which commercial grain library a grain texture came from.
entries.frame_evidence: A specific joint distribution of size, sigma, per-channel independence and luminance dependence.
entries.detector_note: Needs a matcher against a labelled grain corpus. The full descriptor vector IS measurable deterministically by the grain_noise group; only the lookup is missing.
entries.notes: Same shape as post_fx.lens_model_identification: measurement available, reference corpus absent.

entries.label: Grain in clipped blacks or whites
entries.description: Whether grain persists inside clipped regions, which tells you whether it was added before or after the clip.
entries.frame_evidence: Pure black areas are either dead flat or still faintly speckled.
entries.detector_note: Mask pixels at code 0-2 and 253-255, and measure residual variance inside those masks versus the flat-ROI sigma.
entries.notes: Codec deadzoning kills noise in near-black regardless of comp order, so a flat black is weak evidence; a speckled clipped black is strong evidence of grain applied last.

entries.label: Green spill / key colour fringe
entries.description: Residual key-screen colour clinging to the edges or transparent areas of a keyed element.
entries.frame_evidence: A green or blue tint along hair edges and semi-transparent regions of a foreground subject, absent from the background.
entries.detector_note: Sample Lab hue in a narrow band inside the silhouette contour and compare against the element's interior hue distribution; spill shows a hue excursion toward green or blue confined to the edge band.
entries.notes: Genuine green rim light and green background bounce produce the same edge hue; a spill verdict is only credible when the background contains no green source.

entries.label: Hair in the gate
entries.description: A dark curved filament intruding from a frame edge and wobbling slightly, from debris in the camera gate.
entries.frame_evidence: A thin dark wiggling line entering from the frame border and persisting across many frames in roughly the same place.
entries.detector_note: Apply skimage.filters.frangi or meijering ridge filtering, keep thin dark curvilinear components that touch a frame border, and require them to persist across unique cels with only small displacement.
entries.notes: Thin dark scene content touching the frame edge (wires, branches, cables) is the dominant false positive; the wobble (small non-rigid motion while the plate moves differently) is the only real discriminator.

entries.label: Halation channel radius ratio
entries.description: The numeric ratio between the red and blue glow radii, the compact signature of an emulation stock.
entries.frame_evidence: Measurably wider red skirt than blue skirt on the same highlight.
entries.detector_note: Report sigma_R/sigma_B and sigma_R/sigma_G from the per-channel radial fits, with bootstrap confidence over the blob population.
entries.notes: Meaningless on any frame whose highlights are already coloured red; require near-neutral cores (delta-ab under a small threshold).

entries.label: Halation red bleed
entries.description: Film-style halation where light scattered back off the base spreads further in the red channel than in green or blue.
entries.frame_evidence: A warm red-orange fringe hugging the outside of blown highlights and bright edges, thickest on the brightest edges.
entries.detector_note: Compute the per-channel radial halo profile around the core mask and fit a Gaussian per channel with scipy.optimize.curve_fit; halation is sigma_R > sigma_G > sigma_B with the red excess concentrated in the first few rings.
entries.notes: Lateral chromatic aberration also produces a red-shifted edge but is radius-dependent and one-sided; run post_fx.chromatic_aberration_lateral first and subtract its predicted offset before claiming halation.

entries.label: Distinguish atmospheric haze from a diffusion filter
entries.description: Deciding whether a low-contrast veil comes from the air in the scene or from glass in front of the lens.
entries.frame_evidence: Both lift blacks and soften highlights across the frame.
entries.detector_note: Real haze scales with subject DISTANCE and a filter does not, but recovering per-pixel distance requires a monocular depth model that is not installed (see post_fx.depth_estimation_for_dof_checks).
entries.notes: Becomes solvable the day a depth model is added; until then post_fx.diffusion_filter_haze reports the veil without attributing it.

entries.label: Local tonemapping halo
entries.description: Grey halos around high-contrast boundaries from a local-contrast or HDR tonemapping operator.
entries.frame_evidence: A dark band on the bright side and a light band on the dark side of a strong edge, wider than any sharpening halo.
entries.detector_note: Sample luminance profiles across strong edges along the normal and measure overshoot amplitude versus distance; tonemap halos are wide (tens of px) and low-amplitude, unlike sharpening halos which are narrow and high-amplitude.
entries.notes: Shares its measurement with post_fx.sharpening_halo; the two are separated only by the width/amplitude ratio, so report both and let the ratio decide.

entries.label: Distinguish optical bloom from comp bloom
entries.description: Deciding whether a glow was created by the lens and filters or added afterwards in comp.
entries.frame_evidence: Both produce the same radial halo profile around highlights.
entries.detector_note: No pixel measurement separates them on a finished frame. The only weak cues are post_fx.glow_ignores_occlusion (a 2D pass may bleed over foreground) and post_fx.bloom_selective_matte (optics cannot be matted), and both have benign explanations.
entries.notes: Report the two weak cues as evidence, never as a verdict.

entries.label: Whether an artefact is intentional or a defect
entries.description: Deciding whether a measured artefact is a deliberate stylistic choice or an unwanted error.
entries.frame_evidence: None: the pixels are identical either way.
entries.detector_note: Not a perceptual question. Every entry in this shard reports WHAT is present and at what strength; whether it is wanted is outside the analyzer's reach.
entries.notes: The most important blind spot in the shard. Crushed blacks, heavy grain, glitch, banding and datamosh are all deliberate looks in some material and failures in others; the analyzer must never label a finding as a defect on its own authority.

entries.label: Interlacing comb artefact
entries.description: Alternating scanlines from two different moments, giving toothed edges on moving objects.
entries.frame_evidence: Horizontal comb teeth along the vertical edges of anything that moves, absent on static objects in the same frame.
entries.detector_note: Split into even and odd row fields, measure the difference between them in high-motion tiles, and compute a comb score as the ratio of vertical-neighbour difference to two-row-apart difference; report field order by testing which field leads in the direction of motion.
entries.notes: Fine horizontal texture (venetian blinds, dense stripes) yields the same row-alternation ratio; gate on the tile also having high measured motion.

entries.label: Whole-layer defocus (2D)
entries.description: A 2D background cel blurred as a whole layer while the character layer stays sharp, the standard anime substitute for optical DOF.
entries.frame_evidence: The painted background is uniformly soft with a single blur amount, and the sharp character edge sits on it with no transitional blur.
entries.detector_note: Confirm bimodal tile sharpness where the soft population has near-constant blur (low variance of estimated sigma across background tiles at different apparent depths) and the sharp/soft boundary coincides exactly with the ink-outline mask.
entries.notes: The tell is constant blur across background elements at very different depths; a real lens would vary. Fails on backgrounds painted with soft brushwork throughout.

entries.label: Lens flare present
entries.description: Any non-image light artefact attributed to internal lens reflection, real or simulated.
entries.frame_evidence: Bright geometric shapes, streaks or ghosts overlaying the scene and not attached to any surface in it.
entries.detector_note: Detect candidate regions deterministically (bright blobs plus elongated ridges), crop a 384px box around the brightest candidate, and ask the qwen2.5vl judge; the deterministic sub-entries below carry the measurements, this one carries the verdict.
entries.vlm_question: Does this image contain a lens flare - a bright streak, ring or row of coloured shapes caused by light hitting the lens? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Ask on a crop, never the full frame. A VLM will say yes to any bright light source; treat a yes with no supporting streak or ghost measurement as unconfirmed.

entries.label: Identify the lens from its optical fingerprint
entries.description: Naming the specific lens from the joint signature of flare, bokeh, distortion, vignette and CA.
entries.frame_evidence: A consistent combination of blade count, swirl, cat-eye rate, distortion sign and flare colour across a shot.
entries.detector_note: Needs a fingerprint database and a matcher trained on measured lens characteristics; the individual measurements exist in this shard but there is no reference corpus to match them against.
entries.notes: The component measurements ARE available deterministically; only the identification step is missing. Report the fingerprint vector and leave the naming to a human.

entries.label: Lift / black offset per channel
entries.description: Where each channel's floor sits, the numeric read of the lift control.
entries.frame_evidence: The darkest pixels in the frame sit above zero, differently per channel.
entries.detector_note: Report the 0.1th percentile of each channel histogram in code values, and the spread between channels.
entries.notes: This is the delivered floor, not the grade node value: a scene with no true blacks in it has a high floor with no lift applied.

entries.label: Lifted / matte blacks
entries.description: A raised black floor giving a faded film or matte look.
entries.frame_evidence: The darkest thing in the frame is a soft grey, and no pixel approaches zero.
entries.detector_note: Report the 0.1th-percentile luminance code well above zero together with near-zero black_clip_frac; distinguish from veiling glare by the absence of any spatial dependence on distance to highlights.
entries.notes: A fog-filled or hazy scene has the same floor; the spatial-uniformity metric is what separates a grade from atmosphere.

entries.label: Light leak
entries.description: A soft coloured wash entering from a frame edge, emulating light striking the film outside the gate.
entries.frame_evidence: A warm orange or red gradient bleeding in from one border and fading toward the frame centre, unattached to anything in the scene.
entries.detector_note: Heavily lowpass the frame (cv2.GaussianBlur sigma ~ height/12), subtract the shot-average low-frequency field, and fit a monotone gradient anchored at a frame border; report the border, chroma and gradient extent.
entries.notes: A practical light just outside frame produces the same gradient; the discriminator is that a leak is unaffected by camera motion, which requires the shot-average subtraction to be motion-compensated.

entries.label: Pulsing / animated light leak
entries.description: A leak whose strength varies over a few frames, the standard animated overlay behaviour.
entries.frame_evidence: The edge wash swells and fades over roughly half a second while the scene is unchanged.
entries.detector_note: Track leak_peak_delta_l across UNIQUE-CEL indices and report the amplitude range, rise time and whether the pulse is smooth (keyframed) or stepped (a looping plate).
entries.notes: Unique-cel indexing is required; on 2s the pulse is sampled at half rate and the rise time doubles.

entries.label: Limited-range (16-235) levels
entries.description: Video-range code values delivered or interpreted as full range, or the reverse, producing washed or clipped blacks.
entries.frame_evidence: The histogram has hard walls at code 16 and 235 with nothing beyond, or content crushed against 0 and 255.
entries.detector_note: Inspect the luminance histogram for empty bins below 16 and above 235 with a mass pile-up exactly at those codes; cross-check the container's colour range flag from ffprobe -show_streams.
entries.notes: A low-contrast scene can occupy 16-235 naturally without any range issue; only the pile-up AT the boundary codes is evidence.

entries.label: Flat log / ungraded image
entries.description: Footage delivered in a log or otherwise flat transfer with no grade applied.
entries.frame_evidence: Low contrast, milky blacks, desaturated colour and a histogram bunched in the middle with empty ends.
entries.detector_note: Report a narrow luminance IQR centred near mid-grey, a raised black floor, low mean_chroma and near-zero clipping on both ends.
entries.notes: Indistinguishable from a deliberately faded look; the tell is the near-total absence of BOTH clipping ends combined with low chroma.

entries.label: LUT hue clamping / collapse
entries.description: Distinct input hues mapped onto the same output hue, flattening colour separation.
entries.frame_evidence: Several visibly different source colours read as the same hue, and the hue histogram shows hard spikes.
entries.detector_note: Build a 360-bin hue histogram from Lab hue angle weighted by chroma and look for isolated spikes carrying disproportionate mass with empty neighbours.
entries.notes: A scene that genuinely contains only a few colours (2D animation with a limited palette especially) gives the same spikes; in 2D this entry is close to uninformative.

entries.label: 3D LUT lattice quantisation
entries.description: Colour clustering onto a coarse grid, the fingerprint of a low-resolution 3D LUT applied without tetrahedral interpolation.
entries.frame_evidence: Smooth colour gradients break into faceted patches, and the frame's distinct colours cluster at regular spacings.
entries.detector_note: Histogram the unique RGB triplets, compute nearest-neighbour distances in Lab, and look for a regular lattice pitch; also check for reduced unique-colour count relative to a similar ungraded frame's expectation.
entries.notes: 8-bit delivery plus codec quantisation already clusters colours; the lattice must be regular AND coarser than the codec's own quantisation to mean anything.

entries.label: Matte line / dark edge fringe
entries.description: A thin dark or light outline around a composited element, from a shrunken or mis-processed alpha channel.
entries.frame_evidence: A consistent 1-2px darker rim following the entire silhouette of one element, including where it crosses light and dark background.
entries.detector_note: Trace the strongest closed contour with cv2.findContours, sample the luminance profile along its normal at many points, and test whether an inward or outward dark rim of constant width persists REGARDLESS of the background luminance on that side.
entries.notes: Ink outlines in 2D animation are exactly this signature by design, so in 2D the entry is uninformative; the background-independence test is what makes it meaningful in live action and 3D.

entries.label: Mechanical vignette (hard corner cut)
entries.description: A hard-edged corner obstruction from a matte box, filter ring or hood, rather than a smooth optical falloff.
entries.frame_evidence: An abrupt dark arc cutting into one or more corners with a defined edge.
entries.detector_note: On the shot-average frame apply skimage.feature.canny in the corner regions; a mechanical vignette gives a continuous arc edge with gradient width under a few px, unlike the smooth optical model residual.
entries.notes: A dark object genuinely occupying a corner (a doorway, foreground silhouette) also gives an arc; require it to be present in every frame of the shot at the same coordinates.

entries.label: Monochrome or single-tone image
entries.description: An image with essentially one hue, whether pure greyscale or sepia/cyanotype toned.
entries.frame_evidence: Everything in the frame shares a single colour cast with only luminance varying.
entries.detector_note: Report hue angle concentration (circular variance of chroma-weighted hue) plus mean chroma; near-zero chroma is greyscale, high concentration with nonzero chroma is toned.
entries.notes: A near-monochrome scene (fog, night, a red-lit room) is indistinguishable from a toning grade on one frame; the shot-level stability of tone_hue_deg is the better cue.

entries.label: Mosquito noise around edges
entries.description: Shimmering high-frequency noise clustered around sharp edges in compressed video, from quantised high-frequency DCT coefficients.
entries.frame_evidence: A halo of fizzing speckle hugging text or hard object outlines, changing every frame while the edge stays still.
entries.detector_note: Measure residual sigma inside a dilated band around strong edges versus in flat regions far from edges, and confirm the residual is temporally uncorrelated across unique cels while the edge itself is static.
entries.notes: Sharpening ringing occupies the same band but is temporally stable; the temporal decorrelation is what separates them, and it needs unique-cel indexing.

entries.label: Motion blur direction
entries.description: The angle of the smear, which should match the direction of motion.
entries.frame_evidence: The orientation of the streaks on a moving subject.
entries.detector_note: Take the minor-eigenvector angle of the tile structure tensor, or the orientation of the spectral nulls in the Radon transform (skimage.transform.radon) of the ROI.
entries.notes: Angle is defined modulo 180 degrees, so direction of travel is not recoverable from the blur alone; sign comes from flow.

entries.label: Blur direction disagrees with motion
entries.description: Post-added blur whose angle does not match the measured direction of travel, a strong tell of a faked or generic blur pass.
entries.frame_evidence: An object moves horizontally but its smear runs diagonally or vertically.
entries.detector_note: Compute the angular difference between blur_angle_deg (mod 180) and the mean cv2.calcOpticalFlowFarneback direction inside the same ROI, between unique cels; report the residual in degrees.
entries.notes: Flow is unreliable on low-texture and near-occlusion regions and will produce large spurious residuals; gate on roi_flow_coherence.

entries.label: Motion blur streak length
entries.description: How far a moving point is smeared within one exposure, in pixels.
entries.frame_evidence: The physical length of the streak trailing a fast-moving highlight.
entries.detector_note: Estimate the blur kernel length from the cepstrum (numpy.fft of log-magnitude spectrum) of a moving ROI: a linear motion kernel puts periodic nulls in the spectrum whose spacing gives the length.
entries.notes: The cepstral method needs textured content inside the ROI; on a flat moving object it returns noise. Report the confidence and suppress low-confidence lengths.

entries.label: Object blur versus camera blur
entries.description: Whether the blur field is global (camera movement) or localised to moving subjects (object motion blur).
entries.frame_evidence: Either the whole frame including the background is smeared, or only the subject is while the background stays crisp.
entries.detector_note: Compare the tile blur-angle/length field against the global motion estimated by cv2.phaseCorrelate; global blur matches the camera vector everywhere, object blur shows a bimodal field with static background tiles.
entries.notes: A pan with a tracked subject inverts the expectation (background smeared, subject sharp); report both regions rather than a single verdict.

entries.label: Motion blur present
entries.description: Directional smearing of moving content from a finite shutter, rendered or added in post.
entries.frame_evidence: Moving objects are streaked along their direction of travel while static objects stay sharp in the same frame.
entries.detector_note: Compute the local structure tensor from cv2.Sobel gradients per tile; a blurred tile shows strong gradient anisotropy with the weak axis along the blur direction. Confirm by checking the anisotropic tiles coincide with high |v| in cv2.calcOpticalFlowFarneback between UNIQUE cels.
entries.notes: Anisotropic texture (hair, grass, brushed metal) mimics directional blur; the flow-agreement check is what separates them and it fails on duplicate frames.

entries.label: Estimated native resolution
entries.description: The real resolution the image was mastered at, inferred from where its spectrum dies.
entries.frame_evidence: Detail stops resolving at a scale corresponding to a smaller frame size.
entries.detector_note: native_height = delivered_height * spectral_cutoff_frac_nyquist, reported with the cutoff confidence and snapped to nearby standard heights (480/576/720/1080/1440/2160) only as a secondary annotation.
entries.notes: Reports an upper bound at best: a soft lens, a diffusion filter or a low bitrate all lower the cutoff, so the estimate is systematically pessimistic. Never present the snapped value as the source resolution.

entries.label: Nearest-neighbour upscale grid
entries.description: Pixels duplicated in integer blocks, giving a hard blocky grid rather than a smooth interpolation.
entries.frame_evidence: Diagonal edges show perfect square staircases whose step size is constant across the frame.
entries.detector_note: Compute the horizontal and vertical difference images and check whether nonzero differences occur only on a regular lattice; report the lattice pitch, which is the integer scale factor.
entries.notes: Any resampling or re-encode after the nearest-neighbour upscale destroys the lattice purity; a partial result should be reported as inconclusive rather than as a fractional scale.

entries.label: Uniform night filter layer (2D)
entries.description: A flat blue multiply or overlay layer placed over a daytime 2D palette to make it read as night.
entries.frame_evidence: Every flat cel fill in the frame is shifted by the same hue and multiplier, so the palette relationships are preserved exactly under a blue wash.
entries.detector_note: Extract flat-fill region mean colours, and test whether they are related to a known or inferred day palette by a single affine transform (fit a 3x4 matrix across regions and report residual); a uniform layer gives a very low residual across all fills.
entries.notes: Without the day version of the same shot this can only show that all fills are consistent with ONE affine transform, which a deliberately painted night palette can also satisfy.

entries.label: No post-process signature detected
entries.description: The explicit negative case: the frame carries no measurable bloom, CA, vignette, grain, blur, banding or codec artefact above the detection floors.
entries.frame_evidence: Clean flat rendering with no halos, no fringing, no corner falloff and no texture in flat fills.
entries.detector_note: Emit the conjunction of null verdicts from the primary deterministic entries in this shard, together with each entry's measured value and its detection floor, so that not-found is distinguishable from not-detectable.
entries.notes: This entry exists so the analyzer never reports silence as a clean result. Every null must carry its detection floor, because a low-bitrate proxy suppresses grain, banding, CA and blocking simultaneously and would otherwise look like a pristine master.

entries.label: Optical-flow retime warping artefact
entries.description: Rubbery local distortion around silhouettes produced by flow-based frame interpolation or speed ramping.
entries.frame_evidence: Edges of a moving subject bend, tear or melt locally for one or two frames while the rest of the frame is stable.
entries.detector_note: Find candidate frames deterministically (high flow-divergence regions from cv2.calcOpticalFlowFarneback with local non-rigidity), crop a 320px box on the worst region, and ask the qwen2.5vl judge.
entries.vlm_question: Is the edge of the moving object in this image bent, torn or melted in a way that looks like a digital glitch, rather than a clean solid edge? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Crop mandatory. Motion blur alone will also be called melted by a small VLM, so pair the yes with a low blur_anisotropy_ratio before reporting.

entries.label: Oversharpening ringing and crunch
entries.description: Multiple oscillating rings beyond the first halo, plus exaggerated micro-texture, from excessive sharpening.
entries.frame_evidence: Repeating light-dark ripples propagating away from a strong edge, and texture that looks etched.
entries.detector_note: Count zero-crossings in the edge-normal profile beyond the first overshoot, and measure the ratio of high-frequency to mid-frequency energy from numpy.fft.rfft2 against the shot median.
entries.notes: Codec mosquito noise produces the same ringing near edges; separate by whether the ripples are symmetric about the edge (sharpening) or one-sided and blocky (codec).

entries.label: Paint-out / rig removal patches
entries.description: Regions cloned, patched or painted to remove wires, rigs, markers or unwanted objects.
entries.frame_evidence: A patch whose texture is duplicated from elsewhere in the frame or whose motion does not match its surroundings.
entries.detector_note: A clone-detection approach (block matching a region against the rest of the frame) exists in principle with cv2 alone, but on real footage with repeating texture it produces overwhelming false positives; a reliable verdict needs a trained forgery-localisation model, which is not installed.
entries.notes: Deliberately NOT claimed as deterministic. A naive cv2 clone detector would report confident findings across every brick wall, hedge and crowd in the material.

entries.label: Paper / canvas texture overlay
entries.description: A static physical-media texture multiplied or overlaid over the whole image, common in 2D and stylised work.
entries.frame_evidence: A consistent fibrous or woven texture visible over every element including flat fills, identical in every frame.
entries.detector_note: Correlate the flat-region residual between motion-compensated unique cels: a static overlay correlates near 1 in SCREEN space while the image moves. Report the residual's spatial autocorrelation, which shows the weave pitch for canvas.
entries.notes: Shares its screen-space-static test with post_fx.grain_static_frozen; the two are separated by the texture's spatial structure (regular weave versus white noise), so report the autocorrelation shape.

entries.label: Pixel sorting
entries.description: Runs of pixels reordered by brightness along rows or columns, a deliberate glitch-art effect.
entries.frame_evidence: Long horizontal or vertical streaks in which colour varies monotonically and smoothly, cutting across scene content.
entries.detector_note: Scan rows for maximal runs whose luminance is monotone over a long span and whose per-pixel gradient is nearly constant; report run count, mean run length and directionality.
entries.notes: Smooth gradients in the image (skies, walls) are monotone over long runs too; require the run to terminate abruptly against unsorted content.

entries.label: Posterisation / reduced level count
entries.description: Global reduction of the number of distinct tonal levels, either as a stylistic choice or from severe quantisation.
entries.frame_evidence: The whole image is built from a small number of flat tones with hard boundaries between them.
entries.detector_note: Count occupied luminance histogram bins and unique quantised colours; report the effective level count and the fraction of frame area inside flat plateaux.
entries.notes: 2D cel animation is posterised by construction, so in 2D this entry describes the medium and not a post effect; report it but do not treat it as a defect.

entries.label: Projector / exposure flicker
entries.description: Whole-frame luminance fluctuating frame to frame, from projection, shutter irregularity or an added flicker effect.
entries.frame_evidence: The image pulses brighter and darker across successive frames with no change in scene content.
entries.detector_note: Track frame mean L across UNIQUE-CEL indices, detrend, and report the residual coefficient of variation and its dominant frequency via scipy.signal.welch.
entries.notes: Mains-frequency banding from artificial lighting, and codec rate control, both produce frame-level luminance variation; the frequency helps but the analyzer cannot disambiguate on pixels alone.

entries.label: Rack focus over the shot
entries.description: Focus travelling between subjects during a shot.
entries.frame_evidence: Over several frames one region sharpens as another softens, with the framing unchanged.
entries.detector_note: Track per-region tile sharpness across UNIQUE-CEL indices and detect an anti-correlated crossover between two regions; report the crossover frame and duration.
entries.notes: Subject motion in depth produces the same anti-correlation; check that neither region's screen position or scale changes.

entries.label: Radial / zoom blur
entries.description: Blur whose direction is everywhere radial from a centre point, the classic zoom-punch effect.
entries.frame_evidence: Streaks fan outward from one point in the frame, growing longer toward the edges.
entries.detector_note: Fit the tile blur-angle field to a radial model with a free centre (least squares over tile angle versus the tile-to-centre direction) and report centre, residual, and the growth of blur_length_px with radius.
entries.notes: A genuine fast dolly produces the same field; separable only by whether the frame scale actually changes between frames (cv2.phaseCorrelate log-polar).

entries.label: Number of encode generations
entries.description: How many times the material has been compressed and re-compressed.
entries.frame_evidence: Compounding block, ringing and banding artefacts, but with no scale that maps to a generation count.
entries.detector_note: The measurements in the upscale_codec group describe the CURRENT delivery only. Recovering generation count requires the original, and the artefacts of one harsh encode and three mild ones are indistinguishable.
entries.notes: Report post_fx.dct_blocking and post_fx.mosquito_noise as descriptions of the delivered file and stop there.

entries.label: Render denoiser blotching
entries.description: Loss of fine shading detail and patchy smearing from an AI render denoiser (OIDN, OptiX) run on a low sample count.
entries.frame_evidence: Soft irregular patches in indirect-lit and volumetric areas where the shading gradient should be smooth, with crisp edges preserved.
entries.detector_note: Same measurement as post_fx.denoise_blotch_watercolour applied to shadow and indirect-lit regions, plus a temporal check that the blotch boundaries move incoherently between unique cels rather than sticking to geometry.
entries.notes: Indistinguishable from footage denoising (post_fx.denoise_blotch_watercolour) on pixels alone; the temporal incoherence of the patches is suggestive of a render denoiser but is not conclusive.

entries.label: Volumetric ray-march step banding
entries.description: Concentric or planar bands inside god rays and fog from too few ray-march steps.
entries.frame_evidence: A light shaft or fog volume is built from discrete shells or slices rather than a continuous gradient.
entries.detector_note: Restrict post_fx.banding_contours to regions identified as low-texture bright gradients (volumetrics), and additionally test whether the band boundaries are parallel or concentric to the light direction rather than iso-luminance-arbitrary.
entries.notes: Shares its measurement with 8-bit banding (post_fx.banding_contours); only the geometric coherence of the bands with the light direction distinguishes a ray-march step count from a quantisation artefact.

entries.label: Path-tracer fireflies
entries.description: Isolated ultra-bright single pixels from under-sampled specular paths in a path-traced render.
entries.frame_evidence: Scattered blazing white pixels that appear on surfaces and in volumes and change position every frame.
