entries.detector_note: scipy.ndimage.white_tophat with a 1-2px structuring element to isolate point outliers exceeding the local 99.9th percentile by a wide margin; require them to sit ON lit geometry (not in flat black) and to be temporally uncorrelated across unique cels.
entries.notes: Measurement-identical to post_fx.dust_specks; the only separators are that fireflies are almost always positive-polarity, sit on bright specular material, and can exceed the surrounding highlight by a large factor. In a delivered 8-bit file they may be clipped and indistinguishable.

entries.label: Distinguish rendered motion blur from post motion blur
entries.description: Deciding whether blur came from the renderer sampling the shutter or from a 2D vector blur in comp.
entries.frame_evidence: Both produce a directional smear aligned with motion.
entries.detector_note: Post vector blur fails at occlusion boundaries and cannot blur a rotating object correctly, but those failures are subtle and are also produced by a renderer with too few shutter samples; there is no reliable separating measurement on a finished frame.
entries.notes: post_fx.motion_blur_flow_mismatch catches only the crude case where the blur angle is simply wrong.

entries.label: Rolling shutter skew and jello
entries.description: Vertical lines leaning during a fast horizontal pan, and wobbling under vibration, from a sequentially-read sensor.
entries.frame_evidence: Poles and building edges tilt consistently in one direction during a whip pan and straighten when the camera stops.
entries.detector_note: Detect long near-vertical lines with cv2.HoughLinesP and track their angle across unique cels; regress the angle against the frame's horizontal global motion from cv2.phaseCorrelate. Jello is the high-frequency residual of that regression.
entries.notes: Needs long straight vertical features; useless on organic content. In 2D and CG this is normally absent, so a positive is itself a strong live-action or deliberate-simulation cue. | TIER CORRECTED by completeness critic: All three deterministic while frame_metrics.rolling_shutter_skew - the primitive they all rest on - is marked unsupported. entries.label: Rotational / spin blur
entries.description: Blur tangential to circles about a centre, from a spinning object or a spin-blur node.
entries.frame_evidence: Streaks curve around a point, with the smear perpendicular to the radius.
entries.detector_note: Same field fit as radial blur but against the tangential direction; report the centre, residual and whether length scales linearly with radius.
entries.notes: Radial and tangential models are 90 degrees apart, so a bad centre estimate can flip one into the other; fit both and compare residuals.

entries.label: S-curve contrast
entries.description: Toe and shoulder compression with a steepened midtone, the standard contrast look.
entries.frame_evidence: Histogram mass piles up near both ends with a thinned middle, and blacks and whites roll off softly.
entries.detector_note: Fit the luminance CDF against a linear reference and report the residual shape: an S-curve gives positive residual at the toe and negative at the shoulder; also report the interquartile luminance range.
entries.notes: Same limitation as gamma: this is the output distribution. A high-contrast scene shot flat reads the same as a low-contrast scene graded hard.

entries.label: Overall saturation
entries.description: How chromatic the image is overall.
entries.frame_evidence: Colours read vivid, natural or nearly monochrome.
entries.detector_note: Report mean and 95th-percentile chroma sqrt(a^2+b^2) from skimage.color.rgb2lab over the whole frame, weighted to exclude clipped and near-black pixels.
entries.notes: Chroma in Lab is luminance-dependent; a dark frame reads as low saturation even at high HSV saturation, so report both if the analyzer needs a perceptual number.

entries.label: Scanline overlay
entries.description: Regular dark horizontal lines overlaid to suggest a CRT or video monitor.
entries.frame_evidence: Evenly spaced darker rows across the entire frame, present over every element including flat areas.
entries.detector_note: Take the row-mean luminance signal and run scipy.signal.welch or numpy.fft.rfft; a scanline overlay gives a sharp spectral peak at a fixed vertical period with harmonics, present even in flat regions.
entries.notes: Interlacing comb and venetian-blind lighting also give a row-periodic signal; scanlines are content-independent, so verify the peak survives when only flat tiles are used.

entries.label: Skin protected from desaturation
entries.description: A grade that desaturates the environment while holding skin chroma, the standard qualified-key look.
entries.frame_evidence: Faces retain full colour while the surrounding scene is muted.
entries.detector_note: Build a face ROI from the mediapipe FaceMesh 468-point contour (cheek and forehead triangles, excluding eyes, brows and lips), measure mean chroma inside it, and compare against the mean chroma of the frame excluding all face ROIs; report the ratio.
entries.notes: Requires a detected face; reports not-detectable on frames without one. FaceMesh is unreliable on stylised 2D and on strong profiles, so the 2D case will often fail to land a ROI at all.

entries.label: Sharpening halo / edge overshoot
entries.description: Bright and dark rims flanking high-contrast edges, from unsharp masking or in-camera edge enhancement.
entries.frame_evidence: A light outline on the bright side and a dark outline on the dark side of a crisp edge, a few pixels wide.
entries.detector_note: Sample luminance profiles along the normal of strong edges (from skimage.filters.sobel plus non-maximum suppression) and measure overshoot and undershoot amplitude relative to the plateau values on each side; report the mean over many edges.
entries.notes: Genuine bright rim lighting on a subject looks the same on one edge; require the effect to be systematic across many independent edges in the frame.

entries.label: Shutter angle feel
entries.description: The ratio of blur length to inter-frame displacement, which reads as the effective shutter angle.
entries.frame_evidence: A 180-degree feel smears roughly half the frame-to-frame travel; a 360-degree feel smears all of it; a short shutter smears none.
entries.detector_note: shutter_angle_deg = 360 * blur_length_px / interframe_displacement_px, where displacement comes from cv2.calcOpticalFlowFarneback between CONSECUTIVE UNIQUE CELS and is divided by the hold length so it is per output frame.
entries.notes: The single most cel-sensitive metric in this shard: on 2s the naive displacement is doubled and the shutter angle is halved. It is also only valid on rigid, textured, laterally moving subjects.

entries.label: Skin tone line alignment
entries.description: Whether skin hue sits on the conventional skin-tone axis or has been pushed off it by the grade.
entries.frame_evidence: Faces read plausibly fleshy versus greenish, magenta or sunburnt.
entries.detector_note: Take the mediapipe FaceMesh cheek ROI, convert to Lab, and report the hue angle and its deviation from the ~+50 degree skin axis; also report the intra-face hue spread.
entries.notes: The skin axis is a convention derived from vectorscope practice, not a physical constant, and it varies with the subject; use the deviation as a relative signal within a shot, never as an absolute correctness verdict.

entries.label: Smear frame / drawn multiples (2D)
entries.description: An animator-drawn stretched or repeated limb standing in for a motion-blurred exposure.
entries.frame_evidence: On a single frame a limb appears as an elongated ribbon or as several ghosted copies with hard outlines.
entries.detector_note: Detect regions with high elongation (skimage.measure.regionprops eccentricity above 0.95) that carry ink outlines (thin dark contours) and appear for only one unique cel; combine with post_fx.frame_blend_ghosting doubled-edge measurement.
entries.notes: Overlaps the animation domain; kept here because the analyzer must not misreport a drawn smear as a comp motion blur or a retime defect.

entries.label: Drawn speed lines (2D)
entries.description: Radiating or parallel drawn lines standing in for motion in 2D animation, a graphic device rather than an optical blur.
entries.frame_evidence: Dense hard-edged straight lines converging on a point or running parallel across the frame, drawn over or instead of the background.
entries.detector_note: cv2.HoughLinesP on skimage.feature.canny edges; test whether the detected lines converge on a common vanishing point (least-squares intersection with low residual) and report line count and density.
entries.notes: Architectural perspective also gives convergent lines; require high line count, near-uniform line length and the near-total absence of background detail between them.

entries.label: Splice jump / frame displacement
entries.description: A one-frame vertical or horizontal displacement of the whole image, emulating a film splice passing the gate.
entries.frame_evidence: For a single frame the entire picture jumps by several pixels and then snaps back.
entries.detector_note: Flag single-frame outliers in the cv2.phaseCorrelate global-translation trajectory that exceed the local median absolute deviation by a wide margin and revert on the next unique cel.
entries.notes: A dropped frame or a cut produces a large phase-correlation outlier too; require the trajectory to revert, which a cut does not do.

entries.label: Highlight tint
entries.description: The hue pushed into the brightest part of the range by the gain control.
entries.frame_evidence: Bright areas that should be white read warm or cool.
entries.detector_note: Take pixels in the top 10 percent of L that are not clipped, and report mean (a,b), hue angle and chroma.
entries.notes: Clipped pixels are neutral by construction and will drag the estimate toward zero chroma; exclude anything at code 255.

entries.label: Shadow tint
entries.description: The hue pushed into the darkest part of the tonal range by the lift control.
entries.frame_evidence: Deep shadows read blue, green or magenta rather than neutral.
entries.detector_note: Take pixels in the lowest 10 percent of L and report mean (a,b) in Lab, plus hue angle and chroma; compare against the frame median chroma as a baseline.
entries.notes: Coloured practical lighting in the shadows is indistinguishable from a lift tint on a single frame; a shot-stable value across very different content is the stronger cue.

entries.label: Screen-space AO halo
entries.description: Dark occlusion shading applied in screen space, producing a dark band that hugs silhouettes regardless of real geometric contact.
entries.frame_evidence: A soft dark outline of near-constant screen-space width around foreground objects, present even where nothing is behind them to occlude.
entries.detector_note: Sample the luminance profile along the outward normal of strong silhouette contours and test for a negative lobe of constant SCREEN-SPACE width that does not scale with the object's apparent distance.
entries.notes: Profile-identical to post_fx.matte_line_fringe; the discriminator is that an AO band is wider, softer and follows only convex silhouettes, whereas a matte line is 1-2px and follows the whole alpha edge.

entries.label: Screen-space reflection cutoff at frame edge
entries.description: Reflections that fade or vanish as their source leaves the frame, the defining failure of screen-space reflection.
entries.frame_evidence: A reflection in a floor or water surface fades out toward the bottom or side of frame, or pops as the camera moves.
entries.detector_note: Identify candidate reflective regions (near-vertical mirror symmetry of structure about a horizontal boundary via correlation of flipped patches), then measure whether reflection contrast decays toward the frame border and whether it changes discontinuously between unique cels during camera motion.
entries.notes: Detecting the reflective region at all is the weak link; the symmetry test only works for flat horizontal reflectors seen near-on and fails for rough or curved surfaces.

entries.label: Starburst diffraction spikes
entries.description: Radial rays emanating from a point light, produced by a stopped-down iris or added as an effect.
entries.frame_evidence: Symmetric thin rays radiating from a small bright source at regular angular intervals.
entries.detector_note: Sample L on concentric rings around the source with scipy.ndimage.map_coordinates, take the angular power spectrum with numpy.fft.rfft, and read the dominant angular harmonic to count spikes.
entries.notes: Requires an unclipped ring radius; if the source blows out a large area the rings sample only the plateau and the spectrum is flat.

entries.label: Stylistic RGB split glitch
entries.description: Hard channel offsets used as a glitch look, distinguished from lens CA by being large, constant across the frame and often animated per frame.
entries.frame_evidence: A visible red and cyan double image of the whole frame, equal at centre and corners.
entries.detector_note: Combine a large global shift from post_fx.ca_uniform_rgb_translation with a near-zero radial term and frame-to-frame instability of the shift vector over unique cels.
entries.notes: Shares its measurement with post_fx.ca_uniform_rgb_translation; the only separating evidence is magnitude and per-frame jitter, so a static split cannot be distinguished from a heavy-handed CA node.

entries.label: Time-base wobble / line jitter
entries.description: Each scanline horizontally displaced by a small random amount, from an unstable tape transport.
entries.frame_evidence: Vertical edges look ragged and wobble, with the raggedness changing every frame.
entries.detector_note: Estimate a per-row horizontal shift by 1D cross-correlation of each row against the previous frame's same row, then report the standard deviation of the row-shift signal and its high-frequency content.
entries.notes: Real vertical motion also produces per-row shifts, but coherently; the signature here is that the shift is uncorrelated between adjacent rows.

entries.label: Teal-orange split grade
entries.description: The complementary grade that pushes shadows toward teal and skin-range highlights toward orange.
entries.frame_evidence: The frame's colours cluster into two opposed families, warm on the subject and cyan in the shadows and background.
entries.detector_note: Build a 2D histogram of skimage.color.rgb2lab (a,b), test for bimodality along the ~+60/-120 degree hue axis, and separately correlate pixel hue angle with L; teal-orange gives a strong negative hue-luminance coupling on that axis.
entries.notes: A genuinely warm subject against a genuinely blue sky produces the same histogram; this measures the delivered look, never the intent.

entries.label: 3:2 pulldown cadence
entries.description: A 24fps source distributed over 30fps video with a repeating pattern of clean and combed frames.
entries.frame_evidence: Across five consecutive frames, three are clean and two are combed, and the pattern repeats.
entries.detector_note: Compute comb_score per frame across the shot and autocorrelate the resulting sequence; a 3:2 cadence gives a period-5 peak. Report the detected period and phase.
entries.notes: Interacts badly with 2s/3s animation, whose own hold pattern also creates periodicity in frame differences; run post_fx.frame_duplicate_cadence first and report both periods rather than one.

entries.label: Temporal AA ghosting and trails
entries.description: Smeared trails behind moving objects and thin geometry from temporal anti-aliasing accumulating stale samples.
entries.frame_evidence: A faint translucent trail following a moving object, and thin features like wires or hair shimmering and dragging.
entries.detector_note: Motion-compensate the previous unique cel and look for a positive low-amplitude residual behind the object, aligned opposite the flow vector; TAA additionally shows the residual concentrated on thin high-frequency features (high skimage.filters.frangi response).
entries.notes: Shares its measurement with post_fx.denoise_temporal_ghost; both are temporal-accumulation artefacts and the analyzer should report them as one finding with two candidate causes.

entries.label: Tilt-shift focus band
entries.description: A narrow in-focus strip with blur on both sides, from a tilted lens plane or a miniature-faking post effect.
entries.frame_evidence: A horizontal band across the frame is sharp while both the top and the bottom are blurred.
entries.detector_note: Collapse the tile sharpness map along x and fit a single-peaked profile in y; tilt-shift shows one interior maximum with monotone decay both ways, unlike ordinary DOF which decays in one direction.
entries.notes: A landscape with sky above and foreground below can produce the same profile from real optics; report band symmetry, which is near-perfect for the post effect and rarely so in camera.

entries.label: Unpremultiplied / bright edge halo
entries.description: A bright rim around a composited element from incorrect premultiply handling in the comp.
entries.frame_evidence: A light halo of constant width outlining an element, brighter than both the element and the background.
entries.detector_note: Same contour-normal profile as post_fx.matte_line_fringe but testing for a positive rim whose value exceeds both adjacent plateaux; report amplitude and background independence.
entries.notes: Sharpening halos have the same profile; the discriminator is that a premultiply halo follows only ONE element's silhouette while sharpening halos appear on every strong edge in the frame.

entries.label: Uniform upscale softness
entries.description: The whole image band-limited below the delivery resolution, from being upscaled from a smaller master.
entries.frame_evidence: Nothing anywhere in the frame resolves to single-pixel detail, even on hard edges that should be crisp.
entries.detector_note: Compute the radially averaged power spectrum from numpy.fft.rfft2 of the luminance and find the frequency at which power drops into the noise floor; an upscale gives a clean cutoff well below Nyquist that is identical across the whole frame.
entries.notes: Soft focus, heavy denoise and low-bitrate encoding all lower the cutoff; the discriminator is that an upscale's cutoff is the same in every tile including sharply focused ones.

entries.label: Global glare wash on source entry
entries.description: Whole-frame contrast collapse when a very bright source enters or is uncovered in the shot.
entries.frame_evidence: Across a handful of frames the black point rises and overall contrast drops as a light source becomes visible.
entries.detector_note: Over unique-cel indices in the shot, correlate per-frame 1st-percentile L against per-frame 99.9th-percentile L; a strong positive correlation with rising black point is the glare signature.
entries.notes: An auto-exposure or an in-camera iris pull produces the same correlation; distinguishable only if frame mean luminance moves the other way.

entries.label: Local veiling glare near a source
entries.description: Shadow values lifted in proportion to their proximity to a bright source, from lens or filter scatter.
entries.frame_evidence: Blacks close to a lamp read milky grey while blacks on the far side of the frame stay dense.
entries.detector_note: Take the 5th-percentile L of tiles across the frame and regress it against tile distance to the brightest blob centroid; report the slope and its significance against a shuffled-distance null.
entries.notes: Scene content correlates with light position (things near a lamp are genuinely lit), so this is suggestive only; the shuffled-distance null keeps it from firing on ordinary lighting falloff.

entries.label: Vertical emulsion scratch
entries.description: A persistent thin vertical line running the full frame height, from film sliding against grit.
entries.frame_evidence: A bright or dark hairline the full height of the frame that stays at nearly the same horizontal position for many frames.
entries.detector_note: Detect columns whose column-mean luminance deviates sharply from their neighbours across the full frame height, then track the column index over unique cels; a scratch holds position while the image moves.
entries.notes: Vertical architecture aligned with the frame gives the same column signature but moves with the plate; the plate-independence test is essential.

entries.label: VHS chroma bleed and lag
entries.description: Colour information smeared horizontally and shifted right of the luminance, from low-bandwidth analogue chroma recording.
entries.frame_evidence: Saturated colours run in horizontal tails past the object edges, offset to one side.
entries.detector_note: Compare horizontal high-frequency energy of the Y channel against Cb/Cr (numpy.fft.rfft2 restricted to the horizontal axis) and cross-correlate a row of Y against the same row of Cr to recover the chroma lag in px.
entries.notes: All 4:2:0 codecs halve chroma resolution, so the hf ratio alone proves nothing; the horizontal-only asymmetry and the nonzero lag are the VHS-specific parts.

entries.label: Head switching noise band
entries.description: A torn, displaced strip of noise across the bottom few scanlines where the tape head switches.
entries.frame_evidence: The bottom 1-3 percent of the frame is a band of skewed noise or horizontally offset image.
entries.detector_note: Compare per-row horizontal phase offset (cv2.phaseCorrelate row-band against the band above) for the bottom rows against the frame body; head switching gives a large abrupt offset confined to the last rows, persistent across frames.
entries.notes: Letterbox bars and burned-in subtitles also occupy the bottom rows; require the band to contain high-entropy noise rather than flat black.

entries.label: Tracking error noise band
entries.description: A horizontal band of hash and displacement that rolls vertically through the frame over time.
entries.frame_evidence: A ragged noisy stripe crosses the image and moves up or down over successive frames.
entries.detector_note: Compute per-row noise energy (row-wise residual sigma) per frame, find the row-band maximum, and track its vertical position across unique cels; report band height and vertical drift rate.
entries.notes: A genuinely noisy horizontal scene element (foliage, water) can be the row-noise maximum every frame; the drift is the discriminating measurement.

entries.label: Animated / breathing vignette
entries.description: Vignette strength changing over the shot, from an animated post effect or an iris pull.
entries.frame_evidence: The corner darkening deepens or lifts over a few seconds while the framing holds.
entries.detector_note: Fit corner/centre ratio per UNIQUE-CEL index on a rolling window and report the range and trend slope.
entries.notes: Per-frame fits are content-contaminated; use a rolling mean of at least 8 unique cels per estimate.

entries.label: Colour-shifted corners
entries.description: Corners that shift hue as well as darken, from lens colour cast, IR pollution or a tinted post vignette.
entries.frame_evidence: Corner regions read cooler or warmer than the frame centre beyond what darkening alone would do.
entries.detector_note: Fit the radial model per channel or compare mean skimage.color.rgb2lab (a,b) in corner versus centre tiles of the shot-average frame, after normalising L.
entries.notes: Sky in the corners and ground in the centre is a common content confound; use the shot average and require consistency across all four corners.

entries.label: Elliptical / anamorphic vignette
entries.description: Iso-luminance contours that are ovals rather than circles, typical of anamorphic optics or a stretched post vignette.
entries.frame_evidence: The bright centre region is wider than it is tall (or the reverse) rather than round.
entries.detector_note: Fit an elliptical radial model with independent x and y scale terms and report the axis ratio and rotation.
entries.notes: On a 2.39:1 frame a circular vignette already looks oval in normalised coordinates; always fit in pixel space, not normalised space.

entries.label: Vignette falloff shape
entries.description: Whether the darkening follows a gentle natural cos^4-like falloff or a sharper post-applied ramp.
entries.frame_evidence: The transition from lit centre to dark corner is either a long smooth gradient or a comparatively abrupt ring.
entries.detector_note: Report the fitted exponent n and compare against the cos^4 reference profile; report RMS deviation from cos^4.
entries.notes: Exponent and strength trade off in the fit; report their covariance or the number will look more precise than it is.

entries.label: Off-centre vignette
entries.description: A vignette whose darkest point is not at the frame centre, from a shifted post effect or a decentred lens.
entries.frame_evidence: One corner or one side is markedly darker than its opposite.
entries.detector_note: Include cx, cy as free parameters in the radial fit and report the offset from frame centre in normalised units.
entries.notes: Directional scene lighting averaged over a short shot mimics a shifted centre; require a long shot or many frames.

entries.label: Vignette present
entries.description: A radial darkening toward the frame corners added optically or in post.
entries.frame_evidence: Corners consistently darker than the centre across the whole shot, independent of what is in them.
entries.detector_note: Average L over all UNIQUE-CEL frames of the shot to suppress content, heavily lowpass with cv2.GaussianBlur(sigma ~ frame_height/16), then fit a radial model I(r)=a*(1-s*r^n) with scipy.optimize.curve_fit; report s and fit quality.
entries.notes: A single frame cannot separate vignette from scene lighting. On a locked-off shot with a dark border in the content, the shot average keeps that bias; report the fit r2 and refuse below a threshold.

entries.label: Vignette strength
entries.description: How much corner luminance is lost relative to the centre.
entries.frame_evidence: Measured stop difference between the frame centre and the extreme corners.
entries.detector_note: Report corner/centre luminance ratio from the fitted model and convert to stops via log2.
entries.notes: Reported on the delivered (graded) image, so a strong S-curve after the vignette exaggerates the stop figure.

entries.label: Zero-shutter / staccato motion
entries.description: Large frame-to-frame motion with no blur at all, the crisp look of a 0-degree shutter, stop motion, or unblurred CG.
entries.frame_evidence: A fast-moving object is perfectly sharp in every frame yet jumps a long way between frames.
entries.detector_note: Flag when interframe_displacement_px is high while blur_anisotropy_ratio in the moving ROI stays at the static-region baseline.
entries.notes: Normal in 2D animation, which is why applies_to is both but the finding is only interesting for 3D and live action.

entries.label: Absolute scale, distance and room dimensions
entries.description: Real-world metric size of objects and spaces.
entries.frame_evidence: Objects whose true size a viewer could only infer from prior knowledge.
entries.detector_note: Monocular metric scale is unrecoverable without a calibrated camera, a known reference object or a metric depth model - none of which exist in this pipeline.
entries.notes: Any pipeline claim about metres or room size would be fabricated. Logged so the blind spot is explicit.

entries.label: Temperature, sound, smell and other non-visual scene state
entries.description: Scene conditions that leave no reliable visual trace.
entries.frame_evidence: Breath vapour or heat shimmer occasionally hint at temperature; usually nothing does.
entries.detector_note: No visual channel carries these reliably. Breath vapour and heat haze are separately detectable as particles and flow jitter, but they are rare and not equivalent to the condition.
entries.notes: Listed to close the domain honestly: the analyzer sees light, not weather on the skin.

entries.label: Anachronistic object for the stated era
entries.description: An object present in frame that does not belong to the declared period of the production.
entries.frame_evidence: A single prop - a wristwatch, a power line, a plastic bottle, a zip - inside an otherwise period-consistent frame.
entries.detector_note: Per declared era, a FIXED template list of forbidden object kinds is asked one at a time as a yes/no question on tiled crops; the object kinds may be named by a text LLM in advance but the questions themselves are templates.
entries.vlm_question: Is there a [OBJECT_KIND] visible anywhere in this image? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Measured earlier at 2/7 when the VLM was allowed to author its own questions; only templated questions scored usefully. High false-positive rate on cluttered backgrounds.

entries.label: Any animal present
entries.description: A non-human living creature anywhere in the frame.
entries.frame_evidence: A quadruped, bird, fish or insect body form distinct from human anatomy.
entries.detector_note: qwen2.5vl on the full frame and on the four quadrant crops (THE CROP RULE - small animals vanish at full-frame scale).
entries.vlm_question: Is there an animal visible in this image? Answer yes or no.

entries.label: Fish, aquatic life or insects
entries.description: Small non-mammalian creatures - fish, sea life, insects or swarms.
entries.frame_evidence: Streamlined bodies drifting in a water volume, or many small erratic bodies moving on independent trajectories.
entries.detector_note: qwen2.5vl on crops; corroborate a swarm deterministically with high particle count and near-zero directional coherence.
entries.vlm_question: Are there fish, insects or other small creatures visible in this image? Answer yes or no.

entries.label: Door, window or archway
entries.description: A framed opening in a wall, which is also the main staging device for entrances.
entries.frame_evidence: A rectangular or arched boundary whose interior differs in brightness and content from the wall plane around it.
entries.detector_note: qwen2.5vl on wall-plane crops; corroborate with the quadrilateral detector plus an interior/exterior luminance step.
entries.vlm_question: Is there a door, window or archway in this image? Answer yes or no.

entries.label: Atmospheric perspective
entries.description: Distance-dependent loss of contrast and saturation.
entries.frame_evidence: Contrast and saturation falling progressively toward the horizon, with distant elements shifting blue.
entries.detector_note: Regress per-row RMS contrast and mean saturation against row index within the non-sky region (numpy.polyfit); report slope and the Lab b* trend with the same regression.
entries.notes: A vertical gradient in the grade, a graduated ND filter, or a painted sky do the same thing; positive slopes are a cue, not proof of depth.

entries.label: Autumn foliage colouration
entries.description: Foliage regions dominated by orange, red and yellow rather than green.
entries.frame_evidence: Canopy-textured regions whose hue mass sits in 10..35 (HSV) instead of 35..85.
entries.detector_note: Build the foliage texture mask (structure-tensor coherence + mid-frequency energy), then compute the hue histogram inside it and the warm/green mass ratio.
entries.notes: A warm grade or golden-hour light turns green foliage warm; run against the un-graded proxy or require the ratio to exceed the frame-global warm shift. | TIER CORRECTED by completeness critic: deterministic material naming from Gabor anisotropy, hue bands and highlight statistics, in the same shard where scene_semantics.material_class_open_set is model and material_glass_transparent is vlm. Gabor anisotropy wi

entries.label: Reused background art
entries.description: The same painted background reused in different shots or scrolled repeatedly.
entries.frame_evidence: Two shots whose background pixels match almost exactly after alignment, or a pan whose content repeats at a fixed period.
entries.detector_note: Perceptual hash (custom DCT phash in numpy) of the subject-masked background per shot, plus autocorrelation of a panned strip to find a repeat period.
entries.notes: Legitimate for animation - reuse is normal practice, so this is an observation, not a defect.

entries.label: Background defocus
entries.description: Background rendered out of focus relative to the subject.
entries.frame_evidence: Background edges spread over many pixels, point highlights swelling into discs, subject edges staying crisp.
entries.detector_note: Ratio of variance-of-Laplacian in the subject ROI to the background ROI (subject ROI from mediapipe selfie segmentation or the central saliency blob); plus count of near-circular blobs above p98 in the background.
entries.notes: 2D animation fakes this with a blur pass, which this detector will happily report - which is correct, since it is measuring the rendered result, not a lens.

entries.label: Background extras versus principals
entries.description: Separation of foreground principals from background population.
entries.frame_evidence: Sharp, large, centrally weighted figures versus small, soft, edge-distributed figures.
entries.detector_note: Cluster detected person bounding-box heights (numpy histogram, 2 modes by Otsu on the height distribution); label the large-sharp cluster principal using the Laplacian-variance sharpness of each box.
entries.notes: Fails when everyone is at the same depth, and when a principal is deliberately staged small in a wide.

entries.label: Background hold under character animation
entries.description: The animation convention where the background is a static plate and only the character region changes.
entries.frame_evidence: The background pixels are bit-identical across many consecutive frames while the character region changes on 2s or 3s.
entries.detector_note: Per-region temporal difference: background mask mean abs difference below 0.5/255 across >= 6 consecutive frames while the character mask difference exceeds it; report the cadence of the character region separately.
entries.notes: A locked-off live-action shot on a still subject looks identical; the discriminator is that the character cadence is quantised to 2s or 3s.

entries.label: Burned-in subtitle band
entries.description: Subtitles rendered into the picture rather than carried as a separate track.
entries.frame_evidence: A horizontally centred block of light glyphs with dark outlines in the lower fifth of the frame, stable in position and changing on dialogue cadence.
entries.detector_note: Restrict to the lower 22% band; require text regions whose glyphs are near-white with a dark 1-3px border (dilate-minus-erode ring test), centred horizontally, and persisting for >= 8 unique cels then changing wholesale.
entries.notes: In-world signage low in frame and lower-third graphics both land in the band; the outline ring test is the main discriminator.

entries.label: Frame clutter / busyness
entries.description: How visually dense the frame is.
entries.frame_evidence: Many competing edges, objects and colours with no dominant simple shape.
entries.detector_note: Combine cv2.Canny edge density, colour histogram entropy in Lab, and the number of superpixels (skimage.segmentation.slic) whose mean colour differs from all neighbours by > 8 Lab units.
entries.notes: Film grain and compression noise inflate edge density; measure on a mildly denoised copy and report the noise floor.

entries.label: Global colour cast
entries.description: A tint applied over the whole frame.
entries.frame_evidence: Neutral surfaces (whites, greys, highlights) rendered off-neutral in a consistent direction.
entries.detector_note: Take pixels above the 95th luminance percentile and compute their mean a*/b* offset from neutral; a consistent non-zero offset across the highlight population is the cast.
entries.notes: Fails when there is no true white in the scene, which is common in single-source and night interiors.

entries.label: Crowd density class
entries.description: Whether the frame reads as sparse, moderate or dense with people.
entries.frame_evidence: Repeated head-sized dark blobs over a large area, overlapping bodies, no visible ground between figures.
entries.detector_note: qwen2.5vl closed-choice on the full frame plus the two densest tiles; supported by the deterministic crowd texture term (mid-frequency energy peak at head scale).
entries.vlm_question: How crowded is this scene? Answer with one of: no people, a few people, a moderate group, a dense crowd.

entries.label: Crowd headcount estimate
entries.description: A numeric estimate of people in a dense crowd.
entries.frame_evidence: A field of overlapping heads whose count exceeds what any per-person detector can resolve.
entries.detector_note: Needs a density-map crowd counter (CSRNet / SASNet class) trained for headcount regression. Not installed; ultralytics and sklearn are also absent, so no per-head detector fallback exists today.
entries.notes: Logged as a known blind spot. torch 2.10 is present, so this is an add-weights problem, not an environment problem.

entries.label: Crowd motion coherence
entries.description: Whether a crowd moves as one body or churns in all directions.
entries.frame_evidence: Flow vectors across the crowd region sharing one direction (a march) versus cancelling out (a milling throng).
entries.detector_note: cv2.calcOpticalFlowFarneback over the crowd region on unique cels; mean resultant length of the flow direction distribution, plus divergence via numpy.gradient (a panic disperses, a march translates). computed only on UNIQUE-CEL indices (duplicate-frame runs collapsed by mean abs frame difference < 0.4/255 before any temporal math)
entries.notes: Camera motion must be removed first or every crowd reads as perfectly coherent.

entries.label: Day vs night (luminance proxy)
entries.description: Cheap classification of a scene as daylit or night-lit from tonal statistics alone.
entries.frame_evidence: Daylight fills the mid and upper histogram broadly; night collapses the mass low with isolated bright practical sources.
entries.detector_note: Lab L: p50, p90, fraction > 200, fraction < 40; plus count of small saturated bright blobs (threshold at p99.5 then cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats with area < 0.2% of frame).
entries.notes: A day-for-night grade, a low-key interior at noon and a dark cinema grade are indistinguishable from real night on tone alone; this is a prior, not a verdict.

entries.label: Book, paper or document
entries.description: Paper media as a prop.
entries.frame_evidence: A bright rectangular low-texture plane, often held, often carrying text-like structure.
entries.detector_note: qwen2.5vl on any bright quadrilateral found by cv2.findContours + cv2.approxPolyDP with 4 vertices and high internal luminance.
entries.vlm_question: Is a book, letter, newspaper or sheet of paper visible in this image? Answer yes or no.

entries.label: Dominant colours (k=5)
entries.description: The five colours that account for most of the frame.
entries.frame_evidence: The largest colour clusters in the image.
entries.detector_note: cv2.kmeans on Lab pixels (subsampled to 20k) with K=5, criteria (EPS+MAX_ITER, 20, 1.0), attempts=3; report cluster centres as hex plus their pixel shares. sklearn is not installed; cv2.kmeans is the implementation.
entries.notes: K-means centres are unstable frame to frame; quantise to a fixed palette lattice before comparing across frames or the 'palette change' will be noise.

entries.label: Screen or emissive device
entries.description: A phone, monitor, television or holographic display in frame.
entries.frame_evidence: A bounded rectangle noticeably brighter and of a different colour temperature than its surround, sometimes with a scan/refresh cadence.
entries.detector_note: Find quadrilaterals whose interior mean L exceeds the surrounding annulus by > 40 and whose interior Lab b* differs from the surround by > 8; optionally test for a temporal luminance ripple across unique cels.
entries.notes: Windows, mirrors, lamps and paper in a shaft of light all satisfy the brightness and colour-difference test; the class is emissive-rectangle, not device. | TIER CORRECTED by completeness critic: deterministic material naming from Gabor anisotropy, hue bands and highlight statistics, in the same shard where scene_semantics.material_class_open_set is model and material_glass_transparent is vlm. Gabor anisotropy wi

entries.label: Era or period class
entries.description: The historical period the scene presents itself as.
entries.frame_evidence: Architecture, vehicles, lighting technology, clothing, street furniture and signage style taken together.
entries.detector_note: qwen2.5vl closed-choice on the full frame plus the two highest-information background crops; run the same template question on each crop and require agreement.
entries.vlm_question: Which period does this scene look like? Answer with one of: pre-industrial, 19th century, early 20th century, mid 20th century, present day, future, or unclear.
entries.notes: Following the era-gate lesson: the class list is a fixed template, never model-authored per shot, or the answers stop being comparable across frames.

entries.label: Flat colour-fill fraction
entries.description: How much of the frame is filled with perfectly uniform colour - the structural signature of cel animation.
entries.frame_evidence: Large connected regions whose pixels are identical or within a couple of code values.
entries.detector_note: Quantise Lab to a 2-unit lattice, run cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats, and sum the area of components larger than 0.5% of the frame whose internal standard deviation is below 1.5 code values.
entries.notes: Heavy denoising, banding and low-bitrate compression manufacture flat regions in photographic material.

entries.label: Fog, mist or haze
entries.description: Suspended moisture reducing contrast with distance.
entries.frame_evidence: Global contrast compression, whitened blacks, and a contrast gradient that worsens toward the horizon.
entries.detector_note: Dark-channel prior: min over BGR in a 15x15 window; high mean dark-channel plus low global RMS contrast; fit contrast versus row to confirm a depth-linked gradient.
entries.notes: A low-contrast grade, a milky lens, a lifted-black look and smoke all match; the row-gradient term is what distinguishes atmospheric depth from a flat grade.

entries.label: Food or drink
entries.description: Edible items, dishes, cups or bottles.
entries.frame_evidence: Vessels on a surface, plated food, a cup at mouth height.
entries.detector_note: qwen2.5vl on the table-plane crop or the hand crop.
entries.vlm_question: Is there food or a drink visible in this image? Answer yes or no.

entries.label: Foreground element in frame
entries.description: Set dressing or scenery staged between camera and subject.
entries.frame_evidence: A region at a frame edge or the bottom of frame that is either much sharper or much softer than the subject and occludes it.
entries.detector_note: Compute a per-tile sharpness map (variance of cv2.Laplacian); flag edge-adjacent tiles whose sharpness differs from the subject ROI by > 2x AND that share a boundary with the subject silhouette.
entries.notes: A dirty lens, vignetting and heavy grain all change edge-tile sharpness; on flat 2D art there is no defocus cue at all and this is near-useless.

entries.label: Frame contains no people
entries.description: An establishing or insert frame with no human subject at all.
entries.frame_evidence: No face, no body silhouette, no hands anywhere in the frame across the whole cel.
entries.detector_note: No mediapipe face/pose/hand detection above 0.5 confidence anywhere in a 2x2 tiled pass at full resolution; confirmed for 2D with one qwen2.5vl yes/no.
entries.notes: Absence of detection is not absence of a person - a back-turned figure, a hand at the frame edge or any stylised character can read as empty. mediapipe is trained on photographic humans; on stylised 2D faces/bodies it fires unreliably or not at all, so a null detection on anime is not evidence of absence.

entries.label: Frame within a frame
entries.description: A subject framed by an in-scene aperture - doorway, window, arch, mirror.
entries.frame_evidence: A closed quadrilateral or arch boundary surrounding the subject with a tonal step at its edge.
entries.detector_note: Quadrilateral candidates from cv2.findContours + approxPolyDP; flag those that fully contain the subject bounding box and have a mean luminance step > 25 across their boundary.
entries.notes: Picture frames, screens, mattes and rectangular set dressing behind the subject all qualify geometrically.

entries.label: Furniture
entries.description: Seating, tables, beds, shelving or cabinetry.
entries.frame_evidence: Rectilinear man-made volumes at human scale resting on the ground plane.
entries.detector_note: qwen2.5vl on the background crop after subject masking.
entries.vlm_question: Is there furniture such as chairs, tables, beds or shelves in this image? Answer yes or no.

entries.label: Nonsense or malformed lettering
entries.description: Text-shaped marks that are not real words - a signature failure of generated imagery and of background set dressing.
entries.frame_evidence: Glyph-like forms with correct stroke weight and baseline but no valid word structure, or letters that mutate between cels.
entries.detector_note: qwen2.5vl on the tight text crop, asked as a closed judgement; corroborate temporally by checking whether the read string is stable across unique cels of the same shot.
entries.vlm_question: Is the text in this image made of real readable words, or is it nonsense letter shapes? Answer: real, nonsense, or unclear.
entries.notes: Foreign-language text the VLM cannot read is routinely labelled nonsense; always pair with script_or_writing_system before believing a nonsense verdict.

entries.label: Global contrast
entries.description: The tonal range the frame actually uses.
entries.frame_evidence: The spread between the darkest and brightest meaningful tones.
entries.detector_note: (L p95 - L p05) / 255, plus RMS contrast (standard deviation of L / mean L), plus the fraction of the 0-255 range with non-trivial histogram mass.
entries.notes: Fog, haze, lifted-black grades and low-quality upscales all compress this the same way.

entries.label: Golden hour warm low sun
entries.description: Warm, low-angle sunlight colouring the whole frame.
entries.frame_evidence: Global warm shift with long raking shadows and a warm-to-cool gradient across the sky band.
entries.detector_note: Lab b* mean > 12 with a* mean > 3 over the non-subject region, plus a monotonic b* gradient across the sky band rows (numpy.polyfit slope).
entries.notes: Sepia grades, firelight, tungsten interiors and orange-teal blockbuster grading all reproduce this exactly; must be confirmed against sky presence.

entries.label: Object held in hand
entries.description: A prop being gripped by a character.
entries.frame_evidence: A non-skin mass bounded by the finger landmarks, moving rigidly with the wrist.
entries.detector_note: mediapipe Hands landmarks 0/5/9/13/17 define a palm ROI; inside a dilated ROI measure non-skin-chroma pixel fraction (YCrCb gate) and its rigid co-motion with the wrist landmark across unique cels.
entries.notes: Gloves, sleeves and dark skin outside the YCrCb gate all read as a held object; hand landmarks themselves are unreliable on stylised 2D.

entries.label: Headroom
entries.description: The gap between the top of the subject's head and the top of the frame.
entries.frame_evidence: Empty space above the head, or the head clipping the frame edge.
entries.detector_note: From mediapipe face mesh / pose, take the topmost head landmark y; headroom = that y normalised, and report negative values when the head is clipped.
entries.notes: Hair volume, hats and helmets sit above the landmark set, so the geometric headroom is systematically overestimated. mediapipe is trained on photographic humans; on stylised 2D faces/bodies it fires unreliably or not at all, so a null detection on anime is not evidence of absence.

entries.label: High-key versus low-key
entries.description: Whether tonality is concentrated in the highlights or the shadows.
entries.frame_evidence: A histogram bunched above mid-grey with few shadows, versus one bunched below with isolated highlights.
entries.detector_note: Fraction of pixels above 0.66 and below 0.33 of full scale, plus histogram skewness (scipy.stats.skew) of L.
entries.notes: A bright sky in an otherwise dark frame pushes the highlight fraction up without the image being high-key.

entries.label: Horizon line present and its height
entries.description: A dominant near-horizontal division between sky/upper space and ground.
entries.frame_evidence: A long straight boundary crossing most of the frame width with a tonal or colour step across it.
entries.detector_note: cv2.Canny then cv2.HoughLinesP with minLineLength > 0.5*W; keep lines within +/-15 degrees of horizontal; pick the one with the largest mean luminance step across it (sampled +/-8 px); report its normalised height.
entries.notes: Rooflines, tabletops, walls, banding and letterbox mattes are all long horizontal edges with a tonal step.

entries.label: Horizon tilt (dutch reference)
entries.description: The roll of the horizon relative to the frame.
entries.frame_evidence: The horizon line running at an angle to the frame bottom.
entries.detector_note: Angle of the selected horizon line in degrees; when no horizon exists, fall back to the dominant orientation peak of the edge-orientation histogram near horizontal.
entries.notes: A tilted horizon can be a dutch angle, a handheld drift, or simply a sloping road; this measures the pixels, not the intent.

entries.label: Depth layer count
entries.description: How many distinct depth planes the shot is built from.
entries.frame_evidence: Groups of pixels that share a motion speed distinct from other groups during any camera or subject move.
entries.detector_note: cv2.calcOpticalFlowFarneback on unique cels; histogram of flow magnitude; count separated modes via scipy.signal.find_peaks with a prominence floor; require each mode to hold a spatially connected support region. computed only on UNIQUE-CEL indices (duplicate-frame runs collapsed by mean abs frame difference < 0.4/255 before any temporal math)
entries.notes: Zero camera and subject motion gives one mode and a false 'single layer'; the flow between duplicate cels is exactly zero and that zero is an artefact, hence the unique-cel rule.

entries.label: Lead room / looking space
entries.description: Space left in front of a subject who faces or moves toward one side.
entries.frame_evidence: The subject placed off-centre with the larger empty area on the side they face.
entries.detector_note: Face yaw from the mediapipe face-mesh (nose versus ear landmark asymmetry); compare the free-space width on the faced side against the opposite side.
entries.notes: Requires a visible face; profiles and back-turns break the yaw estimate. mediapipe is trained on photographic humans; on stylised 2D faces/bodies it fires unreliably or not at all, so a null detection on anime is not evidence of absence.

entries.label: Leading lines toward the subject
entries.description: Strong linear structure that points at the subject.
entries.frame_evidence: Roads, rails, walls or shadows whose direction aims at the subject centroid.
entries.detector_note: For each long Hough line, compute the perpendicular distance from the subject centroid to the line's infinite extension and the angle between the line and the centroid direction; count lines pointing within 15 degrees and passing within 10% of the frame diagonal.
entries.notes: Requires a subject; in an empty landscape it reports nothing even when the composition is built on leading lines.

entries.label: Lightning flash
entries.description: A single-cel global illumination spike from an off-screen or in-frame discharge.
entries.frame_evidence: One or two cels whose mean luminance jumps far above the shot baseline and returns, sometimes with a visible branching bolt.
entries.detector_note: Per-unique-cel mean L series; flag cels where (L - median) > 6 * median absolute deviation and the excursion lasts <= 3 cels; optionally detect a thin high-contrast branching structure via skeletonised threshold.
entries.notes: Cuts, camera flashes, muzzle flashes, explosions and white flash transitions are identical on the luminance term alone.

entries.label: Abstract or limbo background
entries.description: A background that carries no location information at all - flat colour, gradient, speed lines or pattern behind the subject.
entries.frame_evidence: Background region with near-zero edge density and near-constant hue, or filled with regular graphic striping rather than depicted objects.
entries.detector_note: Mask out the largest subject region (mediapipe segmentation or the central high-edge blob); on the remainder compute cv2.Canny density, hue circular variance and the fraction of pixels within 4 Lab units of the region median; flag when edge density < 0.01 and flat fraction > 0.7.
entries.notes: A defocused photographic background is also flat and low-edge; separate on chroma noise (a real defocus keeps sensor/film grain, a cel limbo does not).

entries.label: Cave, tunnel or underground passage
entries.description: Enclosed subterranean or bored passage.
entries.frame_evidence: Irregular rock or lined tunnel walls surrounding a dark centre, light source at one end, no sky.
entries.detector_note: qwen2.5vl on the full frame; support with a bright centroid surrounded by a dark annulus (radial luminance profile rising toward the frame centre).
entries.vlm_question: Is this a cave, tunnel or underground passage? Answer yes, no, or unclear.

entries.label: Shop, restaurant or bar interior
entries.description: Retail or hospitality interior.
entries.frame_evidence: Counter or bar line, stocked shelving, menu boards, table-and-chair repetition, price/product signage.
entries.detector_note: qwen2.5vl closed-choice prompt on the full frame plus the text-region crops from the signage detector.
entries.vlm_question: Which best describes this interior: shop, restaurant, bar or cafe, or none of these?

entries.label: Corridor or stairwell
entries.description: Interior circulation space rather than a destination room.
entries.frame_evidence: Strong one-point perspective down a narrow enclosed volume, repeated doors, or a stepped diagonal of treads and a handrail.
entries.detector_note: qwen2.5vl on full frame; cross-check with the vanishing-point detector (vanishing point inside frame and > 6 supporting Hough lines).
entries.vlm_question: Is this a corridor, hallway or stairwell rather than a room? Answer yes, no, or unclear.

entries.label: Domestic room type
entries.description: Which kind of living space an interior is - kitchen, bedroom, bathroom or living room.
entries.frame_evidence: Room-defining fixtures: a countertop and hob, a bed and bedside table, tiling and a basin, or sofa-and-television seating.
entries.detector_note: qwen2.5vl closed-choice on the background crop after masking the largest person region; repeat on the two largest fixture-bearing crops (THE CROP RULE) and require agreement.
entries.vlm_question: Which room is this? Answer with one of: kitchen, bedroom, bathroom, living room, or none of these.
entries.notes: Hospital wards, inns, hotel rooms and studio flats blur every one of these classes; low crop agreement must be reported as unclear.

entries.label: Named real-world place
entries.description: Identification of the actual real place or landmark depicted.
entries.frame_evidence: A recognisable landmark silhouette, skyline or signage naming a real location.
entries.detector_note: qwen2.5vl asked only after the landmark-shaped crop is isolated; must be recorded as a guess with confidence, never as a fact.
entries.vlm_question: Is there a well-known real-world landmark visible in this image? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: The VLM will confidently name plausible cities for generic streets; treat any positive as unverified. A dedicated landmark-recognition model is not installed.

entries.label: Industrial, warehouse or machine space
entries.description: Interior dominated by industrial structure rather than habitation.
entries.frame_evidence: Exposed girders, pipework, crates or pallets, gantries, large-scale machinery.
entries.detector_note: qwen2.5vl on the full frame.
entries.vlm_question: Is this an industrial, factory or warehouse space? Answer yes, no, or unclear.

entries.label: Institutional interior
entries.description: Office, classroom, hospital, laboratory or other institutional interior.
entries.frame_evidence: Repeated identical furniture units, signage, strip lighting, uniform flooring.
entries.detector_note: qwen2.5vl closed-choice prompt on the full frame.
entries.vlm_question: Which best describes this interior: office, classroom, hospital, laboratory, or none of these?

entries.label: Interior vs exterior
entries.description: Whether the shot is staged inside an enclosed structure or outdoors.
entries.frame_evidence: Ceiling/wall junction lines and bounded light falloff versus open sky, distant horizon and sun-driven shadows.
entries.detector_note: qwen2.5vl on a 3x3 tiled downscale of the full frame plus one centre crop; majority vote over tiles; record per-tile agreement.
entries.vlm_question: Is this shot set indoors or outdoors? Answer with one word: indoors, outdoors, or unclear.
entries.notes: Covered arcades, vehicle interiors with large windows and anime limbo backgrounds are genuinely ambiguous; treat tile_agreement < 0.6 as unclear rather than forcing a class.

entries.label: Same location reused across shots
entries.description: Recognising that two separate shots are staged in the same place.
entries.frame_evidence: Matching background structure, palette and set dressing under different framings.
entries.detector_note: Per-shot background descriptor = concatenated Lab colour-layout (8x8 grid means) plus an edge-orientation histogram, computed after masking subjects; cluster shots by cosine distance with a fixed threshold and report the clusters.
entries.notes: A grade change, a time-of-day change or a lighting change moves the descriptor far more than a camera-angle change does; this over-splits.

entries.label: Open road or highway
entries.description: Exterior road corridor outside a built-up area.
entries.frame_evidence: A tarmac band converging to a vanishing point with lane markings, verges and few or no facades.
entries.detector_note: qwen2.5vl on the full frame; support with a long near-vertical-converging Hough line pair from cv2.HoughLinesP.
entries.vlm_question: Is this an open road or highway outside a town? Answer yes, no, or unclear.

entries.label: Ruins, rubble or wreckage
entries.description: Environment defined by destroyed or decayed structure.
entries.frame_evidence: Broken walls, collapsed roof lines, scattered debris fields, exposed reinforcement, burnt or blasted surfaces.
entries.detector_note: qwen2.5vl on the full frame.
entries.vlm_question: Does this environment show ruins, rubble or wreckage? Answer yes, no, or unclear.

entries.label: Ship deck or open boat
entries.description: Exterior staged on the deck of a vessel.
entries.frame_evidence: Rigging, masts, railings and a horizon that pitches or rolls relative to the frame.
entries.detector_note: qwen2.5vl on the full frame; support with horizon_tilt_angle variance across the shot exceeding 1.5 degrees.
entries.vlm_question: Is this shot set on the deck of a boat or ship? Answer yes, no, or unclear.

entries.label: Sky, aerial or outer space
entries.description: Shot with no ground contact - open sky, in-flight, or beyond the atmosphere.
entries.frame_evidence: Sky or starfield filling most of the frame, cloud layers below or around, no horizon or a planetary limb instead of one.
entries.detector_note: qwen2.5vl closed-choice on the full frame; support with sky_pixel_fraction > 0.6 for atmosphere, or luminance p75 < 30 plus the point-star detector for space.
entries.vlm_question: Which best describes this scene: open sky or in flight, outer space, or neither?

entries.label: Urban street
entries.description: Exterior street or plaza in a built-up area.
entries.frame_evidence: Building facades on one or both sides, kerb line, road markings, street furniture, receding facade perspective.
entries.detector_note: qwen2.5vl on the full frame; support with vanishing-point support-line count and sky_pixel_fraction in 0.05..0.45.
entries.vlm_question: Is this an urban street or public square? Answer yes, no, or unclear.

entries.label: Underwater
entries.description: Camera positioned below a water surface.
entries.frame_evidence: Strong blue-green cast with suppressed red channel, caustic light patterning, drifting particulate, surface visible above.
entries.detector_note: qwen2.5vl on the full frame; support deterministically with mean(R) < 0.6*mean(B) and low-frequency caustic flicker energy in the temporal difference of unique cels.
entries.vlm_question: Is this shot taken underwater? Answer yes, no, or unclear.
entries.notes: A heavy teal colour grade or a night-blue scene reproduces the red deficit exactly; the caustic flicker term is the only one that separates them.

entries.label: Vegetated landscape - forest, field or parkland
entries.description: Exterior dominated by plant cover, from dense woodland to open farmland and parkland.
entries.frame_evidence: Repeated vertical trunk structures and dense canopy texture, or a broad low-relief green or straw-coloured ground plane with a high horizon and hedgerows.
entries.detector_note: qwen2.5vl closed-choice on the full frame; support with the foliage mask area, its vertical distribution, and the near-vertical Hough line count (trunks).
entries.vlm_question: Which best describes this scene: forest or wood, open field or farmland, park or garden, or none of these?
entries.notes: Anime foliage is flat-shaded and carries far less high-frequency texture than photographic foliage, so the texture support term must not gate the VLM answer.

entries.label: Vehicle interior (any transport)
entries.description: Shot staged inside a moving conveyance - road vehicle, train, aircraft, ship or cockpit.
entries.frame_evidence: Window or porthole framing a moving exterior, seat backs and rows, dashboards or instrument panels, roof lining or fuselage ribs.
entries.detector_note: qwen2.5vl closed-choice on the full frame; support with a window-region flow test - interior pixels near-static while a bounded window region carries high coherent flow on unique cels.
entries.vlm_question: Which best describes this interior: road vehicle, train carriage, aircraft cabin, ship interior, or none of these?
entries.notes: A parked vehicle gives no window flow, and a rear-projection or LED-volume plate gives window flow with no real motion.

entries.label: Water landscape - shoreline, sea, lake or river
entries.description: Exterior defined by a large body of water, whether seen from the shore or from on it.
entries.frame_evidence: A wide rippling plane with specular glints meeting a straight horizon, or a wet/dry sand boundary and a breaking surf line.
entries.detector_note: qwen2.5vl closed-choice on the full frame; support with the water-surface material detector covering > 20% of pixels and a horizontal boundary between a textured warm band and a rippling band.
entries.vlm_question: Which best describes this scene: beach or shoreline, open sea, lake, river, or none of these?
entries.notes: Anime water is often a flat painted colour with no ripple energy at all, so the deterministic support must never gate the answer.

entries.label: Wilderness terrain class
entries.description: Which kind of uninhabited landscape an exterior is - mountain, desert, snowfield, tundra or moor.
entries.frame_evidence: Large-scale landform silhouettes against sky with little or no built structure: ridgelines, dunes, snow plains, bare rock.
entries.detector_note: qwen2.5vl closed-choice on the full frame; support with the sky-boundary roughness term (jagged for mountain), the lower-band green fraction (low for desert and snow) and the snow mask fraction.
entries.vlm_question: What kind of landscape is this? Answer with one of: mountains, desert, snow or ice, forest, grassland, or none of these.
entries.notes: Matte paintings and stylised 2D landscapes flatten the deterministic support terms; treat those as VLM-only.

entries.label: Logo or brand mark
entries.description: A stylised identifying mark on a product, garment or building.
entries.frame_evidence: A compact high-contrast symbol with flat colour fills, repeated identically across shots.
entries.detector_note: qwen2.5vl on compact high-contrast flat-fill regions.
entries.vlm_question: Is there a company logo or brand mark visible in this image? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Identifying WHICH brand needs a logo-recognition model that is not installed; only presence is claimable.

entries.label: Open-set material classification
entries.description: Naming the material of an arbitrary surface region.
entries.frame_evidence: Any surface whose material a human would name at a glance.
entries.detector_note: Needs a material classifier of the MINC/OpenSurfaces family, or a segmentation model with material labels. Nothing of the kind is installed; the deterministic entries above are proxies for a handful of classes only.
entries.notes: Honest blind spot: the deterministic material entries measure texture statistics, not material identity, and will disagree with a human on stylised material.

entries.label: Fabric and cloth
entries.description: Woven or draped textile surfaces.
entries.frame_evidence: Soft folds with smooth shading gradients along fold axes and a fine regular weave texture at close range.
entries.detector_note: qwen2.5vl on a garment crop; deterministic support from structure-tensor coherence along elongated fold ridges detected by skimage.filters.frangi.
entries.vlm_question: Is the material shown in this crop cloth or fabric? Answer yes, no, or unclear.

entries.label: Foliage and vegetation
entries.description: Leaves, grass, canopy and undergrowth.
entries.frame_evidence: Green-dominant regions with dense isotropic high-frequency structure and many small self-similar shapes.
entries.detector_note: Hue mask 35..85 with S > 40, intersected with high mid-frequency band energy (difference of Gaussians) and low orientation coherence; report area and mean scale.
entries.notes: Anime foliage is flat-shaded with almost no high-frequency content and will fail the texture term; green-lit scenes and green screens false-positive. | TIER CORRECTED by completeness critic: deterministic material naming from Gabor anisotropy, hue bands and highlight statistics, in the same shard where scene_semantics.material_class_open_set is model and material_glass_transparent is vlm. Gabor anisotropy wi

entries.label: Fur or hair surface
entries.description: Keratin surfaces with fine directional strand structure.
entries.frame_evidence: Dense, fine, strongly oriented filaments with a coherent flow field and anisotropic specular banding.
entries.detector_note: Structure-tensor coherence (skimage.feature.structure_tensor + eigenvalues) high with a smoothly varying dominant orientation field; strand scale from the peak of the radial FFT profile.
entries.notes: 2D hair is drawn as flat masses with a few highlight shapes and has no strand structure at all; this entry effectively only measures 3D and live action. | TIER CORRECTED by completeness critic: deterministic material naming from Gabor anisotropy, hue bands and highlight statistics, in the same shard where scene_semantics.material_class_open_set is model and material_glass_transparent is vlm. Gabor anisotropy wi

entries.label: Glass or transparent material
entries.description: Surfaces you can see through, with refraction or reflection.
entries.frame_evidence: Background content visible but displaced, doubled or distorted inside a bounded region, plus edge highlights.
entries.detector_note: qwen2.5vl on the candidate crop; deterministic support from a bounded region whose interior gradient statistics match the surround but whose edges carry strong thin highlights.
entries.vlm_question: Is the surface in the centre of this image transparent glass? Answer yes, no, or unclear.

entries.label: Brick, tile or stone masonry
entries.description: Surfaces built from repeating units with visible seams.
entries.frame_evidence: A regular rectilinear lattice of mortar lines or grout at a consistent pitch.
entries.detector_note: 2D FFT of the region (numpy.fft.fft2); look for two orthogonal off-DC peaks with consistent spacing; confirm with cv2.HoughLinesP producing two dominant perpendicular angle clusters.
entries.notes: Windows on facades, floor tiles, grids, fences, tatami and any repeated architectural module produce the same FFT peaks; this measures periodic structure, not stone. | TIER CORRECTED by completeness critic: deterministic material naming from Gabor anisotropy, hue bands and highlight statistics, in the same shard where scene_semantics.material_class_open_set is model and material_glass_transparent is vlm. Gabor anisotropy wi

entries.label: Metal / specular surface
entries.description: Surfaces that read as metallic through highlight behaviour.
entries.frame_evidence: Small, very bright, low-chroma highlights with hard falloff on an otherwise mid-tone body, plus mirror-like tonal inversion across curvature.
entries.detector_note: Within a candidate region: ratio of L p99.5 to L median, highlight blob compactness, and chroma at the highlight (metal highlights stay near-neutral or take the body colour); histogram skewness via scipy.stats.skew.
entries.notes: Wet plastic, glass, polished stone and rendered clearcoat give the same numbers; anime paints highlights as flat white shapes, which reads as extreme specularity everywhere. | TIER CORRECTED by completeness critic: deterministic material naming from Gabor anisotropy, hue bands and highlight statistics, in the same shard where scene_semantics.material_class_open_set is model and material_glass_transparent is vlm. Gabor anisotropy wi

entries.label: Skin surface
entries.description: Regions of exposed human skin.
entries.frame_evidence: Contiguous areas within the human chroma envelope with low high-frequency texture and soft shading.
entries.detector_note: YCrCb gate Cr in 133..173 and Cb in 77..127, morphologically opened, then intersected with mediapipe pose/face regions when available.
entries.notes: The classic failure: this gate is biased toward mid-tone skin and collapses under strong colour grades, firelight and night-blue looks. On 2D it selects flat fill colours that may not be skin at all. Never report a demographic from it.

entries.label: Snow and ice surfaces
entries.description: Frozen surfaces as a material rather than as a season cue.
entries.frame_evidence: Very high luminance, very low saturation, low texture, with blue-shifted shadow regions and occasional sharp specular ice glints.
entries.detector_note: Snow mask (L > p85, S < 30, low Laplacian variance) plus the Lab b* of its shadowed sub-regions being negative (blue shadows).
entries.notes: Same failure set as snow_cover_present: overexposure and white surfaces. | TIER CORRECTED by completeness critic: deterministic material naming from Gabor anisotropy, hue bands and highlight statistics, in the same shard where scene_semantics.material_class_open_set is model and material_glass_transparent is vlm. Gabor anisotropy wi

entries.label: Water surface
entries.description: A body of water seen from above the surface.
entries.frame_evidence: A broadly horizontal plane carrying travelling ripples, glints, and a compressed reflection of what is above it.
entries.detector_note: In the candidate band: temporal power spectrum of pixel luminance across unique cels showing a narrow low-frequency ripple band; plus reflection correlation with the vertically flipped region above; plus glint blob count. computed only on UNIQUE-CEL indices (duplicate-frame runs collapsed by mean abs frame difference < 0.4/255 before any temporal math)
entries.notes: Anime water is frequently drawn as a static flat colour with stylised highlight shapes and will score zero on ripple power while obviously being water.

entries.label: Wood
entries.description: Wooden surfaces - planks, beams, furniture, panelling.
entries.frame_evidence: Warm mid-tone regions with strongly anisotropic fine grain running along one axis, plus plank seam lines.
entries.detector_note: Gabor filter bank via cv2.filter2D at 8 orientations; wood scores high anisotropy (max/mean orientation energy > 2.5) with hue in 10..30 and moderate saturation.
entries.notes: Hair, fur, brushed metal, fabric weave and motion blur are all anisotropic; the hue term is doing most of the work and a grade breaks it. | TIER CORRECTED by completeness critic: deterministic material naming from Gabor anisotropy, hue bands and highlight statistics, in the same shard where scene_semantics.material_class_open_set is model and material_glass_transparent is vlm. Gabor anisotropy wi

entries.label: Mirror or strongly reflective surface
entries.description: A prop that shows a reflected image of the scene.
entries.frame_evidence: A bounded region containing a plausible but geometrically displaced copy of scene content, often including a subject not otherwise framed.
entries.detector_note: qwen2.5vl on any bounded region that the reflection-correlation test scores above 0.4.
entries.vlm_question: Is there a mirror or a reflection of the scene in this image? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Directly affects person counting: an unrecognised mirror inflates every subject count in the shot.

entries.label: Multiplane scroll speed ratios
entries.description: The explicit speed ladder of a multiplane or parallax-scrolled 2D background.
entries.frame_evidence: Three or more discrete horizontal scroll speeds, each held exactly constant across cels.
entries.detector_note: From the flow modes, report the sorted list of median speeds and the pairwise ratios; test constancy by the variance of each mode's speed across the shot's unique cels. computed only on UNIQUE-CEL indices (duplicate-frame runs collapsed by mean abs frame difference < 0.4/255 before any temporal math)
entries.notes: Discrete, perfectly constant speeds are the 2D signature; a real dolly produces a continuum instead.

entries.label: Two subjects overlapping
entries.description: One character overlapping another in screen space.
entries.frame_evidence: Two person regions whose bounding boxes intersect, with one silhouette contour continuous across the overlap.
entries.detector_note: IoU of the two person boxes > 0.05 plus the T-junction ordering test on their silhouettes to say who is in front.
entries.notes: Multi-person tracking identity is not maintained across a full occlusion, so 'who is in front' can swap labels between cels.

entries.label: Narrative, cultural or symbolic meaning of the setting
entries.description: What a location means in the story or in its culture.
entries.frame_evidence: A setting that reads as ominous, sacred, domestic or hostile to a human viewer.
entries.detector_note: Not a frame observable. A VLM will answer fluently and the answer will be unfalsifiable, which is worse than no answer.
entries.notes: Kept in the taxonomy so the analyzer explicitly records that it does not do this, rather than quietly drifting into it.

entries.label: Near-monochrome or single-hue scene
entries.description: A frame whose colour is essentially one hue, or none at all.
entries.frame_evidence: All chroma clustered in one narrow hue band, or chroma near zero everywhere.
entries.detector_note: Circular variance of the chroma-weighted hue distribution below 0.15, or chroma_p90 below 8 for true greyscale.
entries.notes: Underwater, firelight, night-blue and flashback sepia all land here for different reasons; this term does not distinguish them.

entries.label: Negative space
entries.description: The share of the frame carrying no subject and little detail.
entries.frame_evidence: Large continuous areas of sky, wall, water or flat colour with no salient content.
entries.detector_note: 1 - (union of the subject mask and the pixels above the 60th percentile of the spectral-residual saliency map, after morphological closing); report the largest single empty component too.
entries.notes: Textured but unimportant background (foliage, crowds) scores as busy rather than negative even when it reads as empty.

entries.label: Fantastical or invented creature
entries.description: A creature with a body plan that is not a real animal.
entries.frame_evidence: Extra limbs, wings on a mammal, impossible scale, hybrid anatomy.
entries.detector_note: qwen2.5vl on the creature crop; per the creature body-plan lesson, ask about specific body parts one at a time rather than for a holistic description.
entries.vlm_question: Does this creature have a tail? Answer yes, no, or cannot tell.
entries.notes: A single front-on anchor view hides tails and extra limbs entirely; the per-part question must be run on more than one view before any body-plan claim is logged.

entries.label: Subject occluded by a scene object
entries.description: A prop or piece of set hiding part of the subject.
entries.frame_evidence: A contiguous block of the subject silhouette replaced by non-subject content, with the subject's visible parts unchanged.
entries.detector_note: Landmark visibility below 0.5 for a spatially contiguous group of pose landmarks while the remaining landmarks stay above 0.8 and the overall bounding box is stable across cels.
entries.notes: Low visibility scores also mean motion blur, cropping and simple detector failure. mediapipe is trained on photographic humans; on stylised 2D faces/bodies it fires unreliably or not at all, so a null detection on anime is not evidence of absence.

entries.label: Depth ordering of overlapping objects
entries.description: Which of two overlapping elements is in front.
entries.frame_evidence: One silhouette interrupts the other's contour; the interrupted contour resumes on the far side.
entries.detector_note: At the intersection of two segmented regions, test contour continuity: the region whose boundary is continuous across the overlap is in front (T-junction analysis on the cv2.findContours output).
entries.notes: Needs clean segmentation; on busy or low-contrast frames T-junctions are ambiguous and the ordering flips between cels.

entries.label: Off-screen space and geography
entries.description: What lies outside the frame and how shots relate spatially.
entries.frame_evidence: Eyelines, exits and entries that imply a space the camera never shows.
entries.detector_note: Requires assembling a spatial model across shots from eyelines and screen direction; no such reasoning exists here, and the per-shot terms (travel direction, exit edge) are only its raw inputs.
entries.notes: The travel_direction and exit/entry edge metrics are the honest ingredients; the inference itself is not implemented.

entries.label: Painted background versus outlined character
