entries.description: The structural split in 2D animation between a painted background and line-drawn characters composited over it.
entries.frame_evidence: Hard, dark, near-constant-width outlines around the character with no equivalent outlines in the background art.
entries.detector_note: Detect near-black thin edges (L < 60, width < 3 px after distance transform) and map their spatial density; a character region shows a closed outline loop while painted background regions show soft painted edges instead.
entries.notes: Digital 2D with line-less painting styles, and 3D renders with a toon outline shader, both defeat this split.

entries.label: Painted versus 3D-rendered background
entries.description: Whether the environment is hand-painted art or a rendered 3D set - the core hybrid-production question.
entries.frame_evidence: Painterly brush structure and hand-placed light versus geometrically perfect surfaces with uniform texture detail and consistent shading falloff.
entries.detector_note: qwen2.5vl on two background crops at native resolution (THE CROP RULE - the distinction is invisible at thumbnail scale).
entries.vlm_question: Is the background in this image a hand-painted illustration or a 3D computer render? Answer: painted, render, or unclear.
entries.notes: Modern 2D productions paint over rendered geometry, so the true answer is often 'both' and the closed question cannot express it.

entries.label: Palette entropy
entries.description: How many distinct colours the frame really uses.
entries.frame_evidence: A frame built from a few flat fills versus one with continuous colour variation.
entries.detector_note: Shannon entropy of a 16x16x16 Lab histogram, normalised by log(4096).
entries.notes: Directly separates flat 2D cel art (low entropy) from photographic material (high entropy) - useful as a medium prior as well as a palette measure.

entries.label: Palette shift within a shot
entries.description: The scene's colour changing during a single shot - a lighting change, a fade, a magic effect or a grade ramp.
entries.frame_evidence: The colour histogram drifting steadily across the shot's cels without a cut.
entries.detector_note: Chi-square distance between the Lab histogram of each unique cel and that of the shot's first cel; report the trend slope and the maximum distance, with the shot's own frame-to-frame noise as the null. computed only on UNIQUE-CEL indices (duplicate-frame runs collapsed by mean abs frame difference < 0.4/255 before any temporal math)
entries.notes: Auto-exposure, a moving subject filling frame, and flicker all shift the histogram without any scene change.

entries.label: Parallax between depth layers
entries.description: Different depth planes moving at different screen speeds during a camera move.
entries.frame_evidence: Foreground scenery sliding across the frame faster than the background during a dolly or pan.
entries.detector_note: Take the two largest flow-magnitude modes from the layer detector; parallax_ratio = median|v| of the near mode / median|v| of the far mode, with a bootstrap confidence interval over unique-cel pairs. computed only on UNIQUE-CEL indices (duplicate-frame runs collapsed by mean abs frame difference < 0.4/255 before any temporal math)
entries.notes: A pure pan on a flat plate gives ratio ~1.0 by construction; the null model is the same shot's own static segment, and without it the ratio has no meaning.

entries.label: Period architecture cue
entries.description: Building style that dates the setting.
entries.frame_evidence: Timber framing, sash windows, brutalist concrete, curtain-wall glass, neon-clad megastructure.
entries.detector_note: qwen2.5vl closed-choice on the largest building-containing crop.
entries.vlm_question: What kind of building style is shown? Answer with one of: timber or stone pre-modern, brick industrial, mid-century modern, contemporary glass, futuristic, or unclear.

entries.label: Person count (photographic)
entries.description: How many people are present in the frame in live-action or photoreal CG.
entries.frame_evidence: Distinct human faces and bodies resolvable as separate individuals.
entries.detector_note: mediapipe.tasks.vision.FaceDetector (BlazeFace, multi-face) union mediapipe PoseLandmarker with num_poses=5; deduplicate by IoU of face box against pose head box; report count and per-detection confidence.
entries.notes: Saturates around 5 poses and loses back-turned, heavily occluded, small or extremely wide-angle people; the count is a floor, never a total.

entries.label: Character count (2D / stylised)
entries.description: How many characters are present in a drawn or stylised frame.
entries.frame_evidence: Separately outlined character bodies with distinct silhouettes.
entries.detector_note: qwen2.5vl on the full frame downscaled to 768px, asked for a bounded count; repeat on left/right half crops and take the max of the halves versus the whole as a consistency check.
entries.vlm_question: How many people or characters are visible in this image? Answer with a number from 0 to 10, or 'many'.
entries.notes: mediapipe is trained on photographic humans; on stylised 2D faces/bodies it fires unreliably or not at all, so a null detection on anime is not evidence of absence. VLM counts drift badly above about six characters and in crowds; treat 'many' as a class, not a number.

entries.label: Practical light source as a prop
entries.description: A lamp, candle, torch, fire or lantern present as an object in the scene.
entries.frame_evidence: A small saturated core with a smooth radial falloff and, for flame, a flicker in luminance across cels.
entries.detector_note: Threshold at p99.5, keep blobs with a monotonically decreasing radial mean-L profile out to 5x the blob radius; measure the per-cel luminance variance of the core for flicker. computed only on UNIQUE-CEL indices (duplicate-frame runs collapsed by mean abs frame difference < 0.4/255 before any temporal math)
entries.notes: Specular highlights, sun glints, lens flares and rendered bloom are all radially falling-off bright cores.

entries.label: Prop continuity across a cut
entries.description: An object present in one shot and absent in the next within the same scene.
entries.frame_evidence: A prop occupying a stable position on a surface in one shot and missing from the equivalent position in the next.
entries.detector_note: qwen2.5vl asked the same templated presence question on matched crops from consecutive shots of the same location cluster.
entries.vlm_question: Is there a [OBJECT_KIND] on the surface in this image? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Needs a fixed object list to ask about (there is no open-set detector); a framing change alone can move a prop out of the crop and fake a disappearance.

entries.label: Prop pick-up or release event
entries.description: The moment a held object leaves or enters the hand.
entries.frame_evidence: palm_nonskin_fraction steps across a small number of cels while the hand stays tracked.
entries.detector_note: Step detection on the palm_nonskin_fraction series (difference exceeding 3x its within-shot MAD) with the hand-landmark confidence staying above 0.5 either side of the step.
entries.notes: Any hand rotation changes the palm ROI content and fakes a step; needs the hand-orientation term as a covariate.

entries.label: Open-set prop inventory
entries.description: The full list of discrete objects actually present in the frame.
entries.frame_evidence: Every separable object with its own silhouette and material.
entries.detector_note: Needs a general object detector. ultralytics/YOLO and insightface are not installed; mediapipe ships an ObjectDetector task but its EfficientDet-Lite .tflite weights are not present locally and would only cover the 80 COCO classes.
entries.notes: The single largest blind spot in this domain. Everything below is a hand-picked VLM substitute for the classes that matter most; the open set itself is not measurable today.

entries.label: Quadruped animal
entries.description: A four-legged animal such as a horse, dog, cat or livestock.
entries.frame_evidence: A horizontal body mass on four supports with a distinct head and tail.
entries.detector_note: qwen2.5vl closed-choice on the animal crop returned by the presence pass.
entries.vlm_question: What kind of animal is this? Answer with one of: horse, dog, cat, cattle or livestock, other four-legged animal, or not an animal.

entries.label: Rain streaks
entries.description: Falling rain rendered as elongated bright or dark streaks.
entries.frame_evidence: Many short parallel high-contrast strokes at a consistent angle, present in one cel and gone in the next.
entries.detector_note: On unique cels, high-pass the frame (frame - cv2.GaussianBlur), threshold at p99, then cv2.HoughLinesP with minLineLength ~ 0.02*H and maxLineGap 2; measure count, mean angle and angular standard deviation. computed only on UNIQUE-CEL indices (duplicate-frame runs collapsed by mean abs frame difference < 0.4/255 before any temporal math)
entries.notes: Anime rain is drawn as long clean strokes and reads far more strongly than photographic rain; scratches, hatching, speed lines and film damage all produce oriented streaks.

entries.label: Per-pixel relative depth
entries.description: A dense monocular depth estimate for the frame.
entries.frame_evidence: The whole frame ordered from near to far.
entries.detector_note: Needs MiDaS / Depth-Anything / ZoeDepth weights run under torch. torch 2.10+cu128 is installed but no depth weights are present, so this cannot run today.
entries.notes: Would replace half the proxies in this group. Explicitly logged as a not-detectable capability, not a silent gap.

entries.label: Rule-of-thirds alignment
entries.description: How close the main subject or a strong line sits to a thirds line or intersection.
entries.frame_evidence: The subject centroid, or the eye line, sitting near x=1/3 or 2/3 of the frame.
entries.detector_note: Distance from the subject centroid (or the face-mesh eye midpoint when available) to the nearest thirds intersection, normalised by frame diagonal; also distance from the horizon to the nearest horizontal third.
entries.notes: Purely geometric: proximity to a thirds line is not evidence of intent, and a centred composition is not a defect.

entries.label: Saturation class
entries.description: How saturated the image is overall.
entries.frame_evidence: Vivid versus muted rendering of the same content.
entries.detector_note: Mean and 90th-percentile chroma in Lab (sqrt(a^2+b^2)); bucket into desaturated / natural / vivid with fixed thresholds.
entries.notes: Highly saturated 2D cel art routinely lands in 'vivid' by construction; compare within a medium, not across media.

entries.label: Scene brightness class
entries.description: The overall exposure class of the frame.
entries.frame_evidence: Where the bulk of the luminance histogram sits.
entries.detector_note: Lab L percentiles p05/p25/p50/p75/p95 over the full frame; bucket p50 into dark / low / normal / bright with fixed edges, and report the raw percentiles alongside the class.
entries.notes: Always report the percentiles with the class; the class edges are a convention and only the percentiles are comparable across titles.

entries.label: General scene classification
entries.description: A single-label scene category drawn from a large standard taxonomy.
entries.frame_evidence: The whole frame, classified as one of hundreds of place categories.
entries.detector_note: Needs a Places365-class CNN under torch. Weights are not present; the location entries above are hand-picked VLM substitutes covering perhaps thirty classes of the several hundred a real classifier would give.
entries.notes: Would make most of the location_class group cheap and consistent; currently every location call costs a VLM invocation.

entries.label: Script / writing system of visible text
entries.description: Which writing system the visible text uses.
entries.frame_evidence: Glyph shape statistics - Latin word spacing, CJK square blocks, Arabic connected baseline, invented alien glyphs.
entries.detector_note: qwen2.5vl closed-choice on a tight text crop.
entries.vlm_question: What writing system is the text in this image? Answer with one of: Latin, Chinese or Japanese, Korean, Cyrillic, Arabic, invented or unreadable, or no text.
entries.notes: Also the cheapest test for invented/fictional scripts, which are an era and world-building cue.

entries.label: Season class
entries.description: The season the environment depicts.
entries.frame_evidence: Foliage colour and density, snow cover, bare branches, blossom, clothing weight of subjects.
entries.detector_note: qwen2.5vl on the full frame plus the largest foliage/ground crop.
entries.vlm_question: What season does this scene show? Answer with one of: winter, spring, summer, autumn, or unclear.
entries.notes: Interiors and night scenes carry almost no seasonal evidence; expect 'unclear' to dominate and do not force a class.

entries.label: Severe weather state
entries.description: Storm, blizzard, sandstorm or other extreme atmospheric condition.
entries.frame_evidence: Combination of dense particulate, low visibility, violently displaced vegetation and dark sky.
entries.detector_note: qwen2.5vl on the full frame plus one background crop, after the deterministic rain/snow/fog terms flag anything.
entries.vlm_question: What weather does this scene show? Answer with one of: clear, rain, snow, fog, storm, sandstorm, or unclear.

entries.label: Sign, poster or billboard
entries.description: A dedicated signage object in the environment.
entries.frame_evidence: A high-contrast bounded panel mounted on a wall, pole or building, usually carrying text or a symbol.
entries.detector_note: qwen2.5vl on quadrilateral candidates that also contain a text region.
entries.vlm_question: Is this object a sign, poster or billboard? Answer yes, no, or unclear.

entries.label: Silhouette staging
entries.description: The subject rendered as a dark shape against a bright field.
entries.frame_evidence: A bounded dark region with almost no internal detail sitting on a much brighter background, its outline still readable as a figure.
entries.detector_note: Subject mask mean L below the 20th percentile AND background mean L above the 70th percentile AND subject-region internal Laplacian variance below the frame's 10th percentile.
entries.notes: Any dark object against a window reads as a silhouette; without a subject mask this fires on furniture.

entries.label: Single-subject frame
entries.description: Exactly one person occupies the frame.
entries.frame_evidence: One body, one face, and no second skin-toned or outlined human region.
entries.detector_note: merged_person_count == 1 held for >= 80% of the shot's unique cels; corroborate with a single dominant saliency blob.
entries.notes: Mirrors, portraits on walls, posters and reflections add phantom second subjects.

entries.label: Sky region fraction (exterior proxy)
entries.description: Fraction of the frame occupied by a sky-like region, used as a cheap exterior prior.
entries.frame_evidence: A large low-texture region in the upper frame that is either blue-hued or near the top of the luminance histogram.
entries.detector_note: Top 45% band; mask = (cv2.Laplacian var in 16x16 tiles < p20) AND (HSV H in 85..135 with S>40 OR V > global p90); largest connected component via cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats.
entries.notes: White ceilings, blown-out windows, blue painted walls and overcast white skies all false-positive; night skies false-negative on the luminance branch.

entries.label: Snow or frost cover on surfaces
entries.description: Settled snow or frost on ground and objects, as distinct from falling snow.
entries.frame_evidence: Large connected very bright, very desaturated, very low-texture regions that follow surface topology.
entries.detector_note: Mask = (L > p85) AND (S < 30) AND (local Laplacian variance < p25); take connected components with area > 3% of frame; measure their vertical distribution.
entries.notes: Overexposure, white walls, paper, sand at noon and blown highlights are all indistinguishable on these three terms alone.

entries.label: Falling snow
entries.description: Airborne snow particles crossing the frame.
entries.frame_evidence: Many small bright roundish blobs with a shared slow downward drift across consecutive unique cels.
entries.detector_note: Blob set from p99 threshold with area 2..40 px and circularity > 0.6; match blobs across unique cels by nearest neighbour; require median displacement direction within 40 degrees of down and speed variance low. computed only on UNIQUE-CEL indices (duplicate-frame runs collapsed by mean abs frame difference < 0.4/255 before any temporal math)
entries.notes: Dust motes, bokeh, ash, embers, cherry petals and rendered sparkle VFX are the same measurement; only colour and drift speed separate them, and unreliably.

entries.label: Science-fiction or fantasy setting
entries.description: Whether the environment is presented as non-historical - futuristic technology or a fantasy world.
entries.frame_evidence: Impossible architecture, holographic displays, magic effects, non-terrestrial sky, invented signage script.
entries.detector_note: qwen2.5vl on the full frame.
entries.vlm_question: Is this environment realistic-contemporary, science-fictional, or fantasy? Answer with one word: realistic, scifi, or fantasy.

entries.label: Speed-line or impact background
entries.description: The graphic background that replaces the environment during an action beat.
entries.frame_evidence: The environment gone, replaced by dense parallel or radial high-contrast lines converging on the subject.
entries.detector_note: Very high diagonal_energy_ratio with an orientation histogram dominated by one narrow peak (parallel) or by lines whose extensions converge on a single interior point with a very high inlier ratio (radial), combined with a collapsed palette entropy.
entries.notes: Rain, hatching, venetian blinds and real converging architecture all produce oriented line fields; the collapsed palette entropy is what marks the graphic background.

entries.label: Star field / night sky texture
entries.description: Many small point highlights on a dark low-texture field.
entries.frame_evidence: Dozens to thousands of sub-5-pixel maxima scattered on a near-black background with no connecting structure.
entries.detector_note: On the sky/dark region: local maxima via scipy.ndimage.maximum_filter comparison, keep maxima with area < 6 px and local contrast > 25; count and measure spatial Poisson dispersion.
entries.notes: Sensor noise, dust, bokeh specks and snow particles produce identical statistics; the dispersion index and the absence of frame-to-frame drift are the only separators.

entries.label: Subject screen position
entries.description: Where in the frame the subject sits, in normalised coordinates.
entries.frame_evidence: The centre of the subject silhouette relative to the frame.
entries.detector_note: Centroid of the mediapipe pose landmark set (or of the segmentation mask), normalised to 0..1 in x and y; for 2D fall back to the largest saliency blob centroid.
entries.notes: The saliency fallback tracks whatever is most contrasty, which in a cel frame is often a background highlight rather than the character.

entries.label: Subject clipped by the frame
entries.description: Part of the subject lies outside the frame - a composition state, not an event.
entries.frame_evidence: The body silhouette meets a frame border with no visible contour closure.
entries.detector_note: Count mediapipe pose landmarks whose normalised coordinates fall outside 0..1 or whose visibility drops while their neighbours stay high AND the body mask touches that border.
entries.notes: mediapipe extrapolates landmarks beyond the frame with plausible coordinates, so out-of-range values are informative but not exact. mediapipe is trained on photographic humans; on stylised 2D faces/bodies it fires unreliably or not at all, so a null detection on anime is not evidence of absence.

entries.label: Approach or recede in depth
entries.description: The subject getting nearer to or further from camera.
entries.frame_evidence: Monotonic growth or shrink of the subject bounding box across cels without a change of framing.
entries.detector_note: Linear fit of subject_height_ratio against unique-cel index; report slope, R-squared and whether the frame's global scale (from the affine estimate) is stationary. computed only on UNIQUE-CEL indices (duplicate-frame runs collapsed by mean abs frame difference < 0.4/255 before any temporal math)
entries.notes: A zoom or dolly produces the same growth; the global-affine scale term is what separates subject motion from camera motion.

entries.label: Subject enters frame
entries.description: A subject crossing into the frame from off-screen.
entries.frame_evidence: A subject region first appearing in contact with a frame border, then growing inward over consecutive cels.
entries.detector_note: Track the person bounding box across unique cels; flag first appearance where the box touches a border (within 2% of frame width) and its area increases monotonically for >= 3 cels. computed only on UNIQUE-CEL indices (duplicate-frame runs collapsed by mean abs frame difference < 0.4/255 before any temporal math)
entries.notes: A cut to a subject already at the edge looks identical; the shot boundary list must gate this or every cut generates false entries. mediapipe is trained on photographic humans; on stylised 2D faces/bodies it fires unreliably or not at all, so a null detection on anime is not evidence of absence.

entries.label: Subject exits frame
entries.description: A subject leaving the frame across a border.
entries.frame_evidence: The subject region shrinking against a frame border until it disappears.
entries.detector_note: Mirror of the entry test: last-seen box touching a border with monotonically decreasing in-frame area over >= 3 unique cels.
entries.notes: Indistinguishable from a subject walking behind a foreground object that happens to sit at the frame edge.

entries.label: Subject passes behind an object
entries.description: A transit event in which the subject is progressively hidden then revealed by a nearer element.
entries.frame_evidence: Occlusion fraction rising then falling while the subject's implied trajectory continues uninterrupted across the hidden interval.
entries.detector_note: Occlusion fraction time series showing a rise-then-fall with the pre- and post-occlusion centroid displacement consistent with the pre-occlusion velocity (linear extrapolation error below one body width). computed only on UNIQUE-CEL indices (duplicate-frame runs collapsed by mean abs frame difference < 0.4/255 before any temporal math)
entries.notes: A cut inside the occlusion window destroys the trajectory test; must be run within one shot only.

entries.label: Subject passes in front of an object
entries.description: The reverse transit - the subject wipes across background content.
entries.frame_evidence: Background pixels are progressively replaced by subject pixels and restored behind, while the subject silhouette stays complete.
entries.detector_note: Per-pixel background model over the shot (numpy median of unique cels); count pixels transitioning background -> subject -> background with the subject silhouette remaining topologically closed. computed only on UNIQUE-CEL indices (duplicate-frame runs collapsed by mean abs frame difference < 0.4/255 before any temporal math)
entries.notes: Needs a static or motion-compensated camera to build the background median; on a handheld or moving shot the model must be warped first.

entries.label: Subject scale / shot size proxy
entries.description: How much of the frame height the subject occupies - the observable behind wide/medium/close-up.
entries.frame_evidence: The pixel height of the subject's bounding box relative to the frame height.
entries.detector_note: Pose bounding box height / frame height; for face-only framings use the face-mesh bounding box and mark the measurement as face-derived.
entries.notes: A crouching or lying subject has a small height ratio at a close camera distance; this measures screen occupancy, not lens or distance.

entries.label: Subject travel across the shot
entries.description: The total screen-space path length the subject covers within a shot.
entries.frame_evidence: The trajectory traced by the subject centroid from the first to the last cel of the shot.
entries.detector_note: Sum of per-unique-cel centroid displacements, normalised by frame width; also report net displacement and path straightness (net / total). computed only on UNIQUE-CEL indices (duplicate-frame runs collapsed by mean abs frame difference < 0.4/255 before any temporal math)
entries.notes: Camera motion is included unless compensated by the global affine estimate; a pan following a walker can read as zero subject travel.

entries.label: Subject screen direction
entries.description: Which way across the frame the subject is moving - the observable behind screen direction continuity.
entries.frame_evidence: The sign and angle of the net centroid displacement over the shot.
entries.detector_note: atan2 of the net centroid displacement; bucketed into left/right/up/down/static with a dead zone of 3% of frame width.
entries.notes: The single most useful term for detecting a crossed screen direction between shots, but it needs a stable shot list first.

entries.label: Sun or moon disc in frame
entries.description: A visible celestial disc, as opposed to merely its light.
entries.frame_evidence: A near-circular saturated bright region with a radial luminance falloff, usually in the sky band.
entries.detector_note: Threshold at p99.8 luminance, morphological close, fit circularity 4*pi*A/P^2 > 0.75 via cv2.findContours; confirm radial falloff by comparing mean L in concentric annuli.
entries.notes: Practical lamps, lens flares, headlights and rendered bloom balls satisfy the same test; sky-band membership is the only discriminator and it fails for interiors.

entries.label: Surface roughness / texture energy
entries.description: A generic, material-agnostic measure of how textured a surface is.
entries.frame_evidence: Fine-scale luminance variation on a surface that is otherwise uniformly lit.
entries.detector_note: skimage.feature.graycomatrix / graycoprops contrast and homogeneity at distances 1,2,4 and four angles, plus variance of cv2.Laplacian, computed per superpixel (skimage.segmentation.slic).
entries.notes: Compression blocking, grain and upscaling artefacts all contribute; report the shot's own quietest superpixel as the noise floor.

entries.label: Warm/cool split grading
entries.description: The complementary split where subjects sit warm against a cool environment.
entries.frame_evidence: Two separated hue clusters roughly opposite on the colour wheel, one on skin, one on the background.
entries.detector_note: Circular hue histogram (weighted by chroma); find the two strongest peaks with scipy.signal.find_peaks; report their angular separation and mass ratio; require separation in 140..220 degrees.
entries.notes: Any scene with warm practicals against a blue night sky is naturally bimodal without being graded that way.

entries.label: Text content readout
entries.description: What the visible text actually says.
entries.frame_evidence: Legible glyphs on a sign, screen, page or garment.
entries.detector_note: qwen2.5vl ONLY, on a tight crop of each text region upscaled to at least 224px height (THE CROP RULE); one region per call.
entries.vlm_question: What text is written in this image? Copy it exactly, or answer 'none' if there is no readable text.
entries.notes: moondream MUST NOT be used for this - it confabulates plausible text on any crop. rapidocr is not installed, so there is no deterministic OCR cross-check available today.

entries.label: Text-like region present
entries.description: Whether anything in the frame has the structure of written text.
entries.frame_evidence: Rows of similarly sized, similar-stroke-width connected components aligned on a common baseline.
entries.detector_note: cv2.MSER_create() regions filtered by aspect ratio 0.1..5 and area; group by baseline via row projection; require >= 3 components per row and stroke-width variance below a threshold (distance-transform based).
entries.notes: Fences, railings, windows, brickwork and repeated texture all produce baseline-aligned component rows; this finds text-shaped structure, not text.

entries.label: Time of day class
entries.description: Semantic time of day read from sky colour, shadow behaviour and practical lighting.
entries.frame_evidence: Sky hue and gradient, shadow length and direction, warm low sun versus overhead white light versus artificial pools of light.
entries.detector_note: qwen2.5vl on the full frame plus a sky-region crop when sky_pixel_fraction > 0.05.
entries.vlm_question: What time of day does this scene show? Answer with one of: day, night, sunrise or sunset, or unclear.

entries.label: Time-of-day or lighting jump between shots
entries.description: Adjacent shots in the same location that disagree about light.
entries.frame_evidence: A step change in overall brightness or colour temperature across a cut where the location descriptor says it is the same place.
entries.detector_note: Within a location cluster, compare adjacent shots' luma_p50 and lab_b_mean; flag steps beyond 2.5x the within-shot variation of either side.
entries.notes: Deliberate lighting changes, cutaways and inserts trip this constantly; it is a candidate list for a human, not a verdict.

entries.label: Two-subject configuration
entries.description: Two people share the frame, the base configuration for dialogue and confrontation staging.
entries.frame_evidence: Two separated body regions, often at similar scale, with a gap of background between them.
entries.detector_note: merged_person_count == 2; also emit the normalised horizontal separation of the two centroids and their height ratio (a proxy for depth stagger).
entries.notes: Over-the-shoulder framings give a huge height ratio and can be misread as one subject plus background clutter.

entries.label: UI, HUD or graphic overlay
entries.description: Non-diegetic graphics composited over the picture.
entries.frame_evidence: Perfectly axis-aligned elements that do not move with the camera and survive across a cut unchanged.
entries.detector_note: Pixel-wise temporal standard deviation across unique cels within a shot AND across the shot boundary; overlay pixels have near-zero variance while the plate underneath changes; combine with an axis-alignment test on the region's edges.
entries.notes: Locked-off shots make the whole frame low-variance; the cross-cut term is what makes this work and it needs the shot list to be correct first.

entries.label: Vanishing point
entries.description: The convergence point of the scene's perspective lines.
entries.frame_evidence: Multiple long straight edges converging toward a common point.
entries.detector_note: cv2.HoughLinesP long lines, excluding near-horizontal and near-vertical; RANSAC over line intersections (custom numpy implementation - sklearn is not installed) to find the point with the most inliers.
entries.notes: Flat 2D backgrounds often have hand-drawn perspective that does not converge exactly; a low inlier ratio must suppress the estimate rather than report a noisy point.

entries.label: Vehicle make, model or specific type
entries.description: Identifying a vehicle precisely enough to date or place it.
entries.frame_evidence: Grille, badge, body line and proportion detail on a vehicle in frame.
entries.detector_note: Needs a fine-grained vehicle classifier. Not installed; the VLM will guess a make confidently and be wrong, so its answer must not be logged as a finding.
entries.notes: This is exactly the shape of question where a VLM produces a confident, plausible, unverifiable answer - do not ask it.

entries.label: Vehicle in frame
entries.description: Any vehicle visible as an object in the scene.
entries.frame_evidence: A large rigid body with wheels, hull or fuselage that moves as one unit.
entries.detector_note: qwen2.5vl on the full frame plus the lower-band crop; for photographic material corroborate with a large rigid flow cluster distinct from background flow.
entries.vlm_question: Is there a vehicle such as a car, cart, boat, train or aircraft in this image? Answer yes or no.

entries.label: Vertical symmetry
entries.description: How mirror-symmetric the frame is about its vertical axis.
entries.frame_evidence: Left and right halves carrying matching structure.
entries.detector_note: skimage.metrics.structural_similarity between the left half and the horizontally flipped right half, computed on a downscaled greyscale copy; also report the best-matching axis offset by sliding +/-10% of width.
entries.notes: Symmetric architecture, corridors and locked-off two-shots all score high; a symmetric frame with an asymmetric subject scores low despite reading as symmetrical.

entries.label: Left-right visual weight balance
entries.description: Whether the frame's visual mass sits evenly about the vertical centre.
entries.frame_evidence: Heavy dark or high-contrast masses concentrated on one side.
entries.detector_note: First moment about the vertical centre line of a weight map w = 0.5*saliency + 0.3*edge_density + 0.2*(1-normalised luminance); normalise by total mass and frame width.
entries.notes: The weight map's coefficients are a convention, not a measurement; only comparisons made with identical coefficients are meaningful.

entries.label: Warm/cool balance
entries.description: Whether the frame sits warm, cool or neutral overall.
entries.frame_evidence: The overall colour bias of the image away from neutral.
entries.detector_note: Mean and median Lab a* and b* over all pixels and over the non-skin pixels separately; class thresholds at |b*| > 6.
entries.notes: Large skin or sky areas dominate the average, which is why the non-skin variant is reported alongside.

entries.label: Weapon in frame
entries.description: Any weapon - bladed, blunt or firearm - visible in the frame.
entries.frame_evidence: A long thin high-specular straight form with a hilt discontinuity, or a compact dark angular object at hand height with a barrel axis and a two-hand grip.
entries.detector_note: qwen2.5vl closed-choice on the hand crop expanded 3x, and on any long thin high-contrast structure found by the edge-skeleton pass (THE CROP RULE - a blade is a few pixels wide at full-frame scale).
entries.vlm_question: Is a weapon visible in this image? Answer with one of: bladed weapon, gun, other weapon, or no weapon.
entries.notes: Tools, umbrellas, phones, cameras and controllers held in a shooting or slashing grip are the standard false positives; a rifle at distance is usually below the VLM's resolvable size.

entries.label: Weather continuity across shots
entries.description: Whether weather stays consistent within a sequence.
entries.frame_evidence: Rain streaks present in one shot and absent in the next exterior shot of the same location.
entries.detector_note: Compare the rain, snow, fog and wet-surface terms across shots inside one location cluster; flag disagreements where both shots are exterior.
entries.notes: Coverage shot on different days is the usual cause and is a genuine finding, but so is a tighter framing that simply excludes the rain.

entries.label: Wet ground / rain-slick surfaces
entries.description: Surfaces made reflective by water, independent of visible falling rain.
entries.frame_evidence: Elongated vertical smears of light on the ground band, raised specular highlight count, mirrored bright shapes below their sources.
entries.detector_note: Lower 40% band: count highlight blobs above p98 with vertical elongation > 2.0; plus normalised cross-correlation between a ground strip and the vertically flipped strip immediately above it.
entries.notes: Polished floors, ice and rendered glossy shaders give the same reading; this measures glossiness, not water.

entries.label: Wind acting on the environment
entries.description: Air movement inferred from what it moves - foliage, cloth, hair, dust, banners.
entries.frame_evidence: Coherent oscillatory displacement in flexible regions while rigid structure stays fixed.
entries.detector_note: cv2.calcOpticalFlowFarneback on unique cels; inside foliage/cloth texture masks measure the dominant direction consistency (mean resultant length) and the temporal autocorrelation period of the mean displacement; require rigid-region flow near zero. computed only on UNIQUE-CEL indices (duplicate-frame runs collapsed by mean abs frame difference < 0.4/255 before any temporal math)
entries.notes: Camera movement moves everything and must be compensated first (global affine from cv2.estimateAffinePartial2D) or every shot reads as windy.

entries.label: Leaves blowing through the air
entries.description: Detached leaves tumbling across frame on the wind.
entries.frame_evidence: Small mid-sized blobs travel across open background with rotating, non-ballistic paths.
entries.detector_note: cv2.createBackgroundSubtractorMOG2 (history=60, varThreshold=24) on camera-compensated unique cels; keep contours with area between 20 and 400 px; track by nearest-neighbour; report path curvature and rotation of the fitted ellipse angle.
entries.notes: This is a generic airborne-particle detector; it cannot say the blobs are leaves rather than paper, ash or birds.

entries.label: Sudden airborne debris burst
entries.description: The moment a gust picks up a mass of loose material.
entries.frame_evidence: The count of moving foreground blobs jumps sharply within one or two unique cels.
entries.detector_note: MOG2 foreground blob count per unique cel; detect a step change with a cumulative-sum change-point test; report the onset index and the pre/post blob-count ratio.
entries.notes: A cut inside the analysed window produces an identical step; run only inside a single shot.

entries.label: Null model for atmospheric metrics
entries.description: The shuffled or static-patch baseline every atmospheric measurement is compared against.
entries.frame_evidence: The same detector run on shuffled unique-cel order, or on a region that should be static, yields a value that defines the noise floor.
entries.detector_note: For each temporal metric, re-run it on a randomly permuted unique-cel order (10 permutations) and on a hand-chosen static control patch; emit the mean and 95th percentile of the null distribution alongside the observed value, plus the z-score.
entries.notes: Without this, cloud drift, shimmer, twinkle, sway and dust motes all report confident non-zero values on pure noise. Every FOUND verdict in this domain should carry its z-score.

entries.label: Atmospheric perspective / depth fade
entries.description: Distant elements becoming lighter, bluer and lower in contrast.
entries.frame_evidence: Successive mountain ridges or building layers get progressively paler toward the horizon.
entries.detector_note: Regress local contrast and saturation against the dark-channel transmission map across the frame; a strong negative correlation of contrast with haze (and a hue shift toward the atmospheric light hue) is the depth-fade signature.
entries.notes: Transmission is a proxy for depth, not depth; a true depth map would need MiDaS or similar, which is not installed.

entries.label: Aurora curtain rippling
entries.description: The slow lateral waving of the aurora curtain.
entries.frame_evidence: The lower edge of the glow undulates sideways between unique cels while the sky stays fixed.
entries.detector_note: Extract the lower boundary of the aurora mask as a 1D height signal per column; cross-correlate consecutive unique cels to get a lateral phase shift; report wave speed and wavelength from the boundary FFT.

entries.label: Aurora present
entries.description: Auroral light curtains in the sky.
entries.frame_evidence: Large soft green or magenta luminous structures hanging in a dark sky.
entries.detector_note: Candidate gate: dark sky mask containing a connected region with hue in the green (90-160 deg) or magenta band, saturation above 0.2, area above 3 percent of the sky; crop and confirm with qwen2.5vl.
entries.vlm_question: In this crop of the night sky, are there glowing green or purple curtains of light like an aurora? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Green stage lighting, tinted fog and lens flare in a graded night scene all trip the colour gate.

entries.label: Aurora vertical striations
entries.description: The fine vertical rays that make up an auroral curtain.
entries.frame_evidence: Thin bright vertical streaks running through the glow, denser near its lower edge.
entries.detector_note: Directional energy: apply cv2.Sobel dx inside the aurora candidate mask and compare horizontal-gradient energy to vertical-gradient energy; a ratio above 2 indicates vertical striping. Confirm with the angular peak of the 2D FFT.
entries.notes: Only meaningful inside a confirmed aurora mask; otherwise it just measures vertical texture.

entries.label: Blowing snow along the ground
entries.description: Loose snow driven low across a snow surface.
entries.frame_evidence: White streaks skate horizontally over a white ground with the terrain visible beneath.
entries.detector_note: Streak detection restricted to the lower region with a very bright background; measure the streak angle distribution and the ratio of streak flow speed to any falling-snow speed measured higher in frame.
entries.notes: Low contrast (white on white) makes the streak mask fragile; report the streak SNR.

entries.label: Bokeh / glow particle overlay
entries.description: A compositing layer of soft glowing discs added as atmosphere.
entries.frame_evidence: Large soft translucent circles drift over the image, unaffected by scene geometry.
entries.detector_note: Large (over 200 px area) low-contrast circular blobs with high circularity, soft Gaussian falloff, that pass OVER foreground objects without occlusion; check the occlusion property by testing whether the blob boundary is cut by foreground edges.
entries.notes: Genuine out-of-focus highlights in live action are physically identical; the occlusion test is the only real discriminator and it fails on transparent foregrounds.

entries.label: Visible breath in cold air
entries.description: A condensation plume from a character breathing out.
entries.frame_evidence: A soft low-contrast light plume appears in front of the mouth and disperses over a few frames.
entries.detector_note: Place a plume ROI in front of the mouth using mediapipe face-mesh landmarks 13/14 and the head yaw; detect a transient low-contrast bright residual inside it that expands and fades over 3-10 unique cels while the mouth is open.
entries.notes: Extremely low contrast against a bright background; also confounded by cigarette smoke, steam and dust in the same ROI.

entries.label: Global camera motion compensated
entries.description: Whether scene motion has been separated from camera motion before any atmospheric metric is read.
entries.frame_evidence: A pan drags the entire frame, mimicking coherent cloud drift and rain slant.
entries.detector_note: cv2.estimateAffinePartial2D (RANSAC) on cv2.calcOpticalFlowPyrLK tracks from goodFeaturesToTrack seeded OUTSIDE the sky and particle masks; warp before differencing; emit the estimated translation, rotation and scale plus the inlier fraction.
entries.notes: When the frame is almost entirely sky or almost entirely rain there are too few static features and the estimate collapses; report inlier_frac and downgrade every dependent metric when it is low.

entries.label: Cape or coat flutter
entries.description: Loose garment material rippling in the wind.
entries.frame_evidence: The garment silhouette below the shoulders changes shape frame to frame while the body stays rigid.
entries.detector_note: Garment ROI from mediapipe pose landmarks 11/12 (shoulders) and 23/24 (hips) expanded downward and outward by 1.8x; measure silhouette boundary deformation RMS between unique cels and the flow magnitude ratio of garment ROI to torso ROI.
entries.notes: Walking motion alone deforms the garment ROI; the torso-normalised ratio is what separates wind from locomotion.

entries.label: Clothing visibly soaked
entries.description: Garments darkened and clinging from rain.
entries.frame_evidence: The fabric is darker and shinier than its dry appearance and follows the body more closely.
entries.detector_note: Crop the torso ROI from mediapipe pose landmarks 11/12/23/24 and ask qwen2.5vl; deterministic support from a within-shot drop in torso-ROI mean luminance without a global exposure change.
entries.vlm_question: In this crop, do the clothes look wet and soaked through? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Without a dry reference of the same costume this is guesswork; a shot-internal drop is the only usable evidence.

entries.label: Sky coverage by cloud
entries.description: How much of the visible sky is cloud rather than open sky.
entries.frame_evidence: Proportion of the sky region occupied by non-gradient bright or grey mass.
entries.detector_note: Cloud mask area / sky mask area, where the cloud mask is the residual after fitting and subtracting a smooth vertical sky gradient (numpy.polyfit degree 2 on row means) and thresholding at 2 sigma.

entries.label: Cloud dissipation / clearing
entries.description: Cloud mass thinning or shrinking over the shot, sky opening up.
entries.frame_evidence: Cloud edges soften and cloud coverage shrinks frame over frame.
entries.detector_note: Same trend fit as formation but negative slope, combined with a falling mean gradient magnitude on the cloud contour (softening edges) measured with cv2.Sobel.
entries.notes: Distinguishing dissipation from a dissolve transition requires the shot-boundary list; run after shot segmentation.

entries.label: Cloud drift direction
entries.description: The compass-like screen direction the clouds travel.
entries.frame_evidence: Consistent angular bias in the sky-region flow vectors over a short window.
entries.detector_note: Circular mean and circular variance (scipy.stats.circmean/circvar) of np.arctan2(v,u) over sky-mask flow vectors with |v| above the noise floor.
entries.notes: Uncompensated camera pan produces a perfectly coherent fake drift; always report residual_after_camera_comp alongside.

entries.label: Multi-speed cloud layers
entries.description: Two or more cloud decks drifting at different speeds or directions.
entries.frame_evidence: The sky-region flow magnitude histogram has two separated modes across the same window.
entries.detector_note: np.histogram of sky-mask |flow| into 32 bins; scipy.signal.find_peaks with prominence>0.1*max; report peak separation and the angle difference between the two clusters.
entries.notes: Foreground haze or a dirty sky mask that leaks buildings creates a spurious second mode.

entries.label: Cloud drift speed
entries.description: The bulk translation rate of cloud mass across the sky.
entries.frame_evidence: Cloud silhouettes occupy measurably different pixel positions between two unique cels while the ground stays fixed.
entries.detector_note: Build sky mask (top-down flood of pixels with V>0.55 and low local gradient energy, seeded from the top image rows); cv2.calcOpticalFlowFarneback(pyr_scale=0.5, levels=4, winsize=31, iterations=3, poly_n=7) between consecutive UNIQUE-CEL frames; subtract global camera motion estimated by cv2.estimateAffinePartial2D on cv2.goodFeaturesToTrack points taken OUTSIDE the sky mask; report median |v| inside the sky mask.
entries.notes: Zero drift on a duplicate cel is an artefact; must run on unique-cel indices only. A sky with no texture yields an undefined flow that Farneback fills with zeros.

entries.label: Backlit cloud rim / silver lining
entries.description: A bright rim on the cloud edge facing a sun behind it.
entries.frame_evidence: A thin, very bright band hugging one side of the cloud silhouette.
entries.detector_note: Extract the cloud contour with cv2.findContours; sample intensity along outward normals; flag when the outer 3-8 px band exceeds the cloud interior mean by more than 1.5x and the bright band is one-sided (angular concentration of bright normals).
entries.notes: Clipped skies saturate the rim and the interior equally, killing the ratio.

entries.label: Cloud formation / build-up
entries.description: Cloud mass increasing in coverage over the length of a shot.
entries.frame_evidence: The cloud silhouette occupies a larger fraction of the sky at the end of the shot than at the start.
entries.detector_note: Per-unique-cel cloud mask from skimage.filters.threshold_local on the sky-region luminance residual; fit a linear trend (numpy.polyfit degree 1) of mask area fraction versus unique-cel index; positive slope with R2>0.6.
entries.notes: A camera tilt that brings more cloud into frame looks identical; require the sky mask area to stay stable.

entries.label: Hard-outlined cel cloud
entries.description: Drawn clouds bounded by a uniform ink line rather than a soft render.
entries.frame_evidence: A continuous dark stroke of constant width traces the cloud silhouette.
entries.detector_note: cv2.Canny on the sky region; measure stroke-width consistency along the cloud contour via a distance transform on the inked mask (std/mean of local stroke width below 0.25 indicates a drawn line).
entries.notes: Heavy compression rings around a soft cloud can mimic a thin outline.

entries.label: Ray-march step banding in cloud
entries.description: Concentric luminance steps from too few volumetric integration samples.
entries.frame_evidence: Faint terraced bands inside the cloud body at regular intensity intervals.
entries.detector_note: Histogram of luminance inside the cloud mask; detect a comb pattern via scipy.signal.find_peaks on the histogram with near-uniform peak spacing, and confirm spatially with contiguous iso-luminance strips.
entries.notes: 8-bit quantisation of a very smooth gradient produces the same comb; require the spacing to exceed 2 luma levels.

entries.label: Looping scrolled cloud background
entries.description: A drawn cloud layer panned on a repeating cycle so the same shapes return.
entries.frame_evidence: The identical cloud shape re-enters frame at a fixed interval.
entries.detector_note: Track the cumulative phaseCorrelate shift of the sky band; autocorrelate the sky band strip signature (row-mean vector) over the shot and look for a peak at a non-zero lag with normalised correlation >0.95.
entries.notes: Genuinely uniform cloud texture also autocorrelates highly; require a sharp peak, not a plateau.

entries.label: Cloud shadow sweeping the ground
entries.description: A large soft darkening travelling across terrain as a cloud passes the sun.
entries.frame_evidence: A low-frequency luminance gradient on the ground translates across the frame without any texture moving.
entries.detector_note: Downsample the ground region to 1/16, cv2.GaussianBlur sigma=8, then cv2.phaseCorrelate the blurred luminance fields of consecutive unique cels; a coherent shift with near-zero texture-level flow indicates an illumination sweep rather than object motion.
entries.notes: Auto-exposure ramping in live action produces a global luminance change with no shift; check that the shift magnitude exceeds the noise floor.

entries.label: Time-lapse billow / boiling
entries.description: Clouds visibly growing and churning non-rigidly, as in a sped-up time-lapse.
entries.frame_evidence: Cloud edges deform and puff outward between frames rather than sliding rigidly.
entries.detector_note: Compute flow divergence div = d(u)/dx + d(v)/dy via np.gradient on the Farneback field; mean positive divergence inside the cloud mask well above the mean over the whole sky indicates expansion rather than rigid translation.
entries.notes: Compression artefacts on a low-bitrate sky produce fake divergence; gate on a minimum sky texture energy.

entries.label: Cloud type (cumulus / stratus / cirrus)
entries.description: The meteorological family of the visible cloud.
entries.frame_evidence: Puffy cauliflower masses versus flat grey sheet versus thin fibrous streaks.
entries.detector_note: Crop the largest cloud component with 15 percent padding and ask qwen2.5vl; corroborate with deterministic shape stats (mask solidity, aspect ratio, edge fractality) but do not let the stats alone decide the class.
entries.vlm_question: In this crop of the sky, are the clouds mostly puffy and rounded, mostly a flat featureless grey sheet, or mostly thin wispy streaks? Answer with one of: puffy, flat sheet, wispy.
entries.notes: Meteorological accuracy is not the goal; the analyzer only needs a stable coarse label. Stylised anime clouds are almost always answered as puffy.

entries.label: Volumetric cloud noise texture
entries.description: The fractal-noise interior detail of a ray-marched volumetric cloud.
entries.frame_evidence: Cloud interior carries isotropic multi-scale detail with no drawn edges.
entries.detector_note: 2D FFT power spectrum inside the cloud mask; fit the radial power falloff exponent (a near 1/f^b spectrum with b between 1.2 and 2.2 and low angular anisotropy is the volumetric signature).
entries.notes: Film grain over a painted cloud also adds broadband energy; compute the same statistic on a flat sky patch as a control.

entries.label: Aircraft contrail
entries.description: A straight thin condensation trail across the sky.
entries.frame_evidence: A narrow high-contrast straight line crossing the sky region, sometimes with a bright head.
entries.detector_note: Detect straight-line candidates in the sky mask with cv2.HoughLinesP (minLineLength = 0.2*frame_width, maxLineGap=8) and send each candidate crop to qwen2.5vl for confirmation.
entries.vlm_question: In this crop of the sky, is there a thin straight white trail left by an aircraft? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Wires, cables, and film scratches are the dominant false positives, which is why the confirm step is a VLM and not the Hough alone.

entries.label: Crepuscular rays through cloud
entries.description: Multiple sun rays fanning out from behind a cloud edge.
entries.frame_evidence: Several bright wedges radiate from one point in the sky.
entries.detector_note: Radon transform (skimage.transform.radon) of the sky region; look for several strong linear features whose extensions intersect within a small radius; report ray count and convergence radius.
entries.notes: Radon is expensive; run only when sun_present_flag or a strong sky brightness gradient exists.

entries.label: Zero-flow artefact on duplicate frames
entries.description: The false measurement of stillness produced by running optical flow between two identical frames.
entries.frame_evidence: The flow field is exactly zero everywhere, which no real footage produces.
entries.detector_note: Flag any flow field whose maximum magnitude is exactly 0.0 or whose non-zero fraction is under 0.1 percent; log it as NOT DETECTABLE for that window rather than as no-motion.
entries.notes: This entry exists specifically to stop the analyzer reporting no wind, no rain and no cloud drift on every held frame of an anime.

entries.label: Dust devil / small whirlwind
entries.description: A visible rotating column of dust.
entries.frame_evidence: A vertical hazy column with particles spiralling around it.
entries.detector_note: Propose from a local curl blob in the flow field near the ground, crop, and confirm with qwen2.5vl.
entries.vlm_question: In this crop, is there a spinning column of dust or debris rising from the ground? Answer yes or no.

entries.label: Dust sheet blowing across the ground
entries.description: A low translucent sheet of dust or sand driven along a surface.
entries.frame_evidence: A soft light-coloured veil moves horizontally near the ground, partly hiding the texture beneath.
entries.detector_note: Low-frequency luminance residual in the lower third that translates coherently (phaseCorrelate) while the underlying texture-level flow stays near zero, plus a local contrast reduction inside the moving band.
entries.notes: Shares its whole signature with cloud shadow sweep except for the contrast reduction; report both metrics together.

entries.label: Falling ash
entries.description: Grey or black flakes drifting down after fire or eruption.
entries.frame_evidence: Desaturated dark or pale flakes fall slowly, often against a hazy warm background.
entries.detector_note: Slow-falling particle track with near-zero saturation and an ambient warm or dark background; report particle count, fall speed and saturation.
entries.notes: Indistinguishable from grey snow by motion alone; the surrounding colour cast is the only hint.

entries.label: Falling petals
entries.description: Blossom petals drifting down as ambient atmosphere.
entries.frame_evidence: Small coloured flat shapes descend slowly with lateral swaying and rotation.
entries.detector_note: Airborne-particle tracking (MOG2 plus nearest-neighbour) with the added conditions of non-neutral hue, slow descent, high lateral oscillation and a rotating fitted-ellipse angle.
entries.notes: Confetti, embers, leaves and drawn sparkle overlays satisfy the same motion statistics; only the hue and rotation combination hints at petals.

entries.label: Fireflies / ambient bioluminescence
entries.description: Small self-luminous points drifting in a dark scene.
entries.frame_evidence: Warm yellow-green points blink on and off while drifting slowly against darkness.
entries.detector_note: Precondition on tracked slow warm bright points with a strong on/off duty cycle in a dark frame, then confirm with qwen2.5vl.
entries.vlm_question: In this crop of a dark scene, are the small glowing points fireflies or floating magical lights? Answer yes or no.

entries.label: Flag or banner rippling
entries.description: A flag, banner or hanging cloth waving in the wind.
entries.frame_evidence: A rectangular fabric region shows travelling S-curves along its free edge.
entries.detector_note: Find high-saturation or high-contrast quadrilateral regions with one fixed edge; extract the free-edge boundary as a 1D signal and detect a travelling sinusoid via lagged cross-correlation between unique cels.
entries.notes: The region proposal is weak; without an object detector the analyzer may measure a curtain, a sail or a poster instead.

entries.label: Floating dust motes
entries.description: Fine dust suspended in a light beam or in still air.
entries.frame_evidence: Tiny soft points drift slowly and randomly with no net direction.
entries.detector_note: Tracked particles with very low speed, near-zero net displacement bias, small area, and often a defocused (low local sharpness) appearance; report the isotropy of their displacement directions.
entries.notes: Sensor noise and encoder dither generate matching statistics; the noise-floor control is mandatory.

entries.label: Fog bank rolling in
entries.description: A mass of fog advancing into or across the scene.
entries.frame_evidence: The low-contrast region grows and its boundary translates between unique cels.
entries.detector_note: Track the fog band boundary and the low-contrast mask area across unique cels; report boundary advance speed and area growth rate.

entries.label: Fog thickening or thinning
entries.description: Atmospheric density changing over the shot.
entries.frame_evidence: Distant detail progressively disappears or re-emerges.
entries.detector_note: Dark channel prior transmission estimate (min over channels of a 15x15 min-filter, normalised by the atmospheric light taken as the 99.9th percentile of the dark channel) averaged per unique cel; fit a trend across the shot.
entries.notes: Exposure and grading changes shift the estimated atmospheric light and therefore the transmission; anchor to a near-field patch.

entries.label: Flat fog overlay card
entries.description: A uniform translucent white layer composited over the scene instead of depth-varying atmosphere.
entries.frame_evidence: The whole frame is veiled by the same amount regardless of distance.
entries.detector_note: Near-zero correlation between local contrast reduction and any depth proxy (row position, transmission variance), combined with a very low spatial variance of the transmission map.
entries.notes: A genuinely uniform fog at close range behaves the same way physically.

entries.label: Ground fog layer
entries.description: A shallow fog bank hugging the ground with clear air above it.
entries.frame_evidence: A horizontal band of reduced contrast sits low in frame, with objects cut off at a soft line.
entries.detector_note: Per-row local contrast profile (mean of the local std map by row); detect a low-contrast band bounded above by a contrast step, then confirm the band edge is soft (wide 10-90 transition).
entries.notes: A defocused foreground gives the same contrast band; require the band to be horizontal and to span most of the frame width.

entries.label: Foliage completely still
entries.description: Vegetation with no motion at all, indicating still air or a static background plate.
entries.frame_evidence: Leaf texture is pixel-identical between unique cels after camera compensation.
entries.detector_note: Mean absolute residual inside the foliage mask between camera-compensated unique cels below the estimated noise sigma.
entries.notes: This is the critical null case: reporting it explicitly is what stops the analyzer from claiming wind everywhere.

entries.label: Foliage sway amplitude
entries.description: How far leaves and branches move under wind.
entries.frame_evidence: Leafy regions shift a few pixels back and forth between unique cels while trunks stay put.
entries.detector_note: Foliage-candidate mask = high local Laplacian variance AND green-ish hue OR high texture density; Farneback flow inside the mask after global camera compensation; report the 90th percentile |v| normalised by frame height.
entries.notes: The mask is a texture/colour heuristic, not a plant detector; autumn or alien foliage falls outside the hue gate, so the texture branch must be able to fire alone.

entries.label: Looping drawn foliage cycle
entries.description: Hand-drawn foliage animated as a short repeating cycle.
entries.frame_evidence: The same two or three leaf drawings alternate for the length of the shot.
entries.detector_note: Perceptual hash (per-region dHash) of the foliage ROI per unique cel; count distinct hashes and detect a repeating hash sequence with period 2-6.

entries.label: Foliage sway frequency
entries.description: The oscillation rate of wind-driven foliage, separating a gentle breeze from a gust.
entries.frame_evidence: Foliage displacement reverses direction at a regular interval across a window of unique cels.
entries.detector_note: Per-unique-cel mean signed flow along the dominant wind axis inside the foliage mask; numpy.fft.rfft of that 1D signal over the shot; report the dominant frequency in cycles per unique cel and its power fraction.
entries.notes: Frequency is only interpretable in Hz if the unique-cel rate is known; on 2s/3s anime the effective sampling rate is 8-12 Hz, which aliases anything faster.

entries.label: Frame too stylised for atmospheric measurement
entries.description: A frame whose rendering (flat colour, extreme abstraction, solid background) makes every atmospheric metric meaningless.
entries.frame_evidence: The frame contains a handful of flat colour regions and no gradient, texture or depth cue.
entries.detector_note: Unique colour count below 32, near-zero gradient energy outside edges, and no sky gradient fit; when this fires, all sky, haze and depth-fade entries must be logged NOT DETECTABLE.
entries.notes: Impact frames, silhouette shots and abstract sequences are common in anime and would otherwise generate a page of confident nonsense.

entries.label: Steady wind bend (no oscillation)
entries.description: Vegetation held over at a constant angle by sustained wind rather than swaying.
entries.frame_evidence: Grass or reeds lean consistently one way across all frames of the shot with little motion.
entries.detector_note: Dominant orientation of elongated structures via the structure tensor (skimage.feature.structure_tensor) inside the vegetation mask; report mean orientation deviation from vertical with low temporal variance.
entries.notes: A statically painted background with leaning grass reads identically and is arguably the correct answer.

entries.label: Grass ripple / wind wave over a field
entries.description: A visible wave of bending travelling across a grass or crop field.
entries.frame_evidence: A band of darker or lighter grass sweeps across the field between frames.
entries.detector_note: On the low-frequency luminance field of the ground texture region, cross-correlate consecutive unique cels at multiple lags along candidate directions; a consistent non-zero lag peak with lag proportional to frame separation is a travelling wave.
entries.notes: Cloud shadow sweep produces the same low-frequency travelling luminance and must be disambiguated by the presence of texture-level flow inside the band.

entries.label: Hail bouncing off a surface
entries.description: The characteristic rebound of an ice pellet after ground contact.
entries.frame_evidence: A particle reverses its vertical velocity at a surface and rises briefly before falling again.
entries.detector_note: Requires reliable per-particle tracking through the impact frame at 8-12 unique cels per second; the rebound is typically 1-2 samples long and nearest-neighbour tracking cannot preserve identity through it. Would need a trained small-object tracker.
entries.notes: Logged as a blind spot; a rise in transient ground blobs will still be reported by rain_ground_splash_pops.

entries.label: Hail falling
entries.description: Hard ice pellets falling faster and larger than snow.
entries.frame_evidence: Large bright particles fall fast on near-vertical paths and strike surfaces hard.
entries.detector_note: Precondition on large blob area with high fall speed (much faster than snow, blobbier than rain), then confirm on a crop with qwen2.5vl.
entries.vlm_question: In this crop, are hard round ice balls falling and bouncing, rather than rain or snow? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: The deterministic precondition alone cannot separate hail from heavy rain drops seen close to camera.

entries.label: Hair and cloth disagree about wind
entries.description: Hair moving while clothing hangs dead, or the reverse, which reads as a simulation error.
entries.frame_evidence: One deformable region has strong motion while another on the same body has none.
entries.detector_note: Compare hair_roi_flow_mean against garment_torso_flow_ratio in the same unique-cel window; flag when one exceeds 3x the wind noise floor while the other sits at the noise floor.
entries.notes: Stiff garments (armour, leather) legitimately do not move; this can only be a flag for review.

entries.label: Hair blows with the scene wind
entries.description: Whether hair direction agrees with the wind direction established elsewhere in frame.
entries.frame_evidence: Hair streams the same screen direction as rain streaks, foliage lean and flags.
entries.detector_note: Compare the hair displacement angle to the shot-level wind axis derived from rain_streak_angle, cloud_drift_angle_deg and vegetation_lean_deg; report the absolute angular disagreement.
entries.notes: A character running in still air produces backward hair with no scene wind; the disagreement is only meaningful when a scene wind axis exists with confidence.

entries.label: Hair blown by wind
entries.description: Hair pushed off its rest position by air movement.
entries.frame_evidence: The hair silhouette above and beside the head extends and shifts to one side across frames.
entries.detector_note: Place a hair ROI from mediapipe face-mesh landmarks (forehead 10, temples 234/454, scaled up 1.6x in height); measure the ROI silhouette mask centroid offset from the head axis and its per-unique-cel displacement with Farneback flow inside that ROI.
entries.notes: Fails when the face is not detected (back of head, heavy stylisation, non-human character); mediapipe face-mesh is unreliable on anime faces, so record face_landmark_confidence with every value.

entries.label: Haze density (dark channel)
entries.description: How much the air scatters light in this frame overall.
entries.frame_evidence: Blacks are lifted and colours are washed toward a single ambient tint.
entries.detector_note: Dark channel prior: J_dark = min over a 15x15 window of the per-pixel channel minimum; atmospheric light A from the top 0.1 percent of J_dark; transmission t = 1 - 0.95 * J_dark / A. Report mean and percentile transmission.
entries.notes: The dark channel prior fails on genuinely bright white scenes (snowfields, white walls), reporting fog where there is none; always report the fraction of the frame that is legitimately white.

entries.label: Heat shimmer / mirage distortion
entries.description: Air turbulence over a hot surface warping the image above it.
entries.frame_evidence: Distant edges wobble and swim in a localised band while the camera and subject are still.
entries.detector_note: Farneback flow between unique cels on a static shot; inside a candidate band, require small-magnitude (under 2 px) high-spatial-frequency flow with near-zero mean, high curl and low temporal autocorrelation; a static-camera precondition from the global homography.
entries.notes: Codec macroblock jitter in a flat region has the same statistics; the flat-region control patch is mandatory. Also invisible in 2D unless deliberately drawn.

entries.label: Horizon line
entries.description: The boundary between sky and ground or sea.
entries.frame_evidence: A long roughly horizontal edge separating a low-texture upper region from a textured lower one.
entries.detector_note: Lowest row of the sky mask per column, then RANSAC line fit (cv2.fitLine with DIST_HUBER) across columns; require inlier fraction above 0.6.

entries.label: Leaf detaching from a tree
entries.description: A leaf separating from foliage and entering free flight.
entries.frame_evidence: A small blob leaves the foliage mask boundary and thereafter follows a free trajectory.
entries.detector_note: Requires per-leaf instance tracking through a cluttered textured region; nothing installed can segment and track a single leaf reliably. Would need an instance segmenter or a trained small-object tracker.
entries.notes: Logged as a known blind spot; the coarser airborne_particle_track entry will register the leaf only after it is clear of the canopy.

entries.label: Lightning bolt in frame
entries.description: The discharge channel itself visible as a bright line.
entries.frame_evidence: A thin very bright irregular line spans part of the sky for one or two frames.
entries.detector_note: On the frames flagged by the flash detector, threshold at the 99.9th percentile, skeletonize with skimage.morphology.skeletonize, and require an elongated connected skeleton with length above 0.15 of frame height and a width under 4 px.
entries.notes: Wires, poles and drawn effect lines can survive the threshold; requiring co-occurrence with a flash frame suppresses most.

entries.label: Multi-stroke flicker train
entries.description: The rapid multi-stroke stutter of a real discharge.
entries.frame_evidence: The scene flashes several times in quick succession within a few frames.
entries.detector_note: Cluster flash events within a 12-frame window; report stroke count, inter-stroke interval and the peak amplitude sequence.
entries.notes: Strobe lights, muzzle flashes and camera flashes at an event produce identical trains.

entries.label: Forked lightning branches
entries.description: How many times the bolt splits.
entries.frame_evidence: The bright channel divides into secondary limbs.
entries.detector_note: Count skeleton branch points (pixels with 3 or more 8-neighbours in the skeletonized bolt mask) and endpoint count; report branch order.
entries.notes: Skeletonization noise on a thick glow creates spurious branch points; morphological cleaning first is essential.

entries.label: Lightning flash (global luminance spike)
entries.description: The whole scene briefly lit by a lightning discharge.
entries.frame_evidence: Mean frame luminance jumps for one to three frames then falls back.
entries.detector_note: Per-frame mean luminance series (on ALL frames, not only unique cels, since the flash may occupy a single held frame); flag samples exceeding the local median by more than 4 MAD with a rise time of 1 frame and a decay under 6 frames.
entries.notes: Camera flashes, explosions, cuts to a brighter shot and a white transition all produce the same spike; shot-boundary exclusion is required.

entries.label: Bolt reaching the ground
entries.description: The discharge visibly terminating at terrain rather than staying cloud-to-cloud.
entries.frame_evidence: The bright channel extends below the horizon line and ends at a surface.
entries.detector_note: Check whether the lowest skeleton endpoint falls below horizon_row_norm and within a few pixels of a detected surface; report the contact point in normalised coordinates.

entries.label: Inverted / negative flash frame
entries.description: The stylised inverted or hard two-tone frame used for impact in 2D animation.
entries.frame_evidence: One or two frames render the scene in inverted or posterised tones.
entries.detector_note: Correlate frame N with the inverted frame N-1 (255 - I); a high negative-correlation match combined with a very low unique-colour count indicates a stylised inversion frame.
entries.notes: This is a directorial device rather than weather, but it fires the flash detectors and must be labelled so it is not logged as lightning.

entries.label: Lightning rim-lighting a character
entries.description: A character momentarily edge-lit by the discharge.
entries.frame_evidence: A bright outline appears along one side of the figure exactly on the flash frame.
entries.detector_note: Build a silhouette band from mediapipe pose landmarks (convex hull of visible landmarks, dilated by 6 px minus eroded by 6 px); compare mean band luminance on the flash frame against the two neighbouring frames; require the gain to be one-sided.
entries.notes: Requires a pose detection on the flash frame, which is the frame most likely to be blown out and fail landmark extraction.

entries.label: Shooting star / meteor
entries.description: A brief bright streak crossing the night sky.
entries.frame_evidence: A short line of light appears for a handful of frames, lengthening then fading.
entries.detector_note: Temporal median subtraction over the shot, then cv2.HoughLinesP on the positive residual; require the line to exist in fewer than 8 consecutive unique cels and to translate along its own axis.
entries.notes: Airplane lights, wire rigs and scratch artefacts also produce transient lines.

entries.label: Mirage / inverted reflection on hot ground
entries.description: A false water-like reflective sheet or an inverted image on a hot road or desert.
entries.frame_evidence: The ground far away appears wet and mirrors the sky and objects above it.
entries.detector_note: Confirm on a crop; deterministic support from a vertical-mirror correlation between a distant ground band and the region above it.
entries.vlm_question: In this crop, does the distant ground look like a shimmering sheet of water reflecting the sky? Answer yes or no.

entries.label: Mist rising off water or ground
entries.description: Wisps of vapour lifting off a surface.
entries.frame_evidence: Thin translucent tendrils curl upward from a water or ground boundary.
entries.detector_note: Precondition on low-contrast residual with a net upward flow component just above a detected water/ground boundary, then confirm the crop with qwen2.5vl.
entries.vlm_question: In this crop, is mist or steam rising upward off the surface? Answer yes or no.

entries.label: Moon visible
entries.description: A moon disc in the sky.
entries.frame_evidence: A pale compact disc on a dark sky, far dimmer than a sun and often with surface mottling.
entries.detector_note: Same circular bright-component test as the sun but gated on a dark sky (sky mean V below 0.35) and a moderate peak luma; report interior texture variance to separate moon from a lamp.
entries.notes: Streetlamps, paper lanterns and practical bulbs in a night sky region are the main false positives.

entries.label: Moon phase
entries.description: How much of the moon disc is lit, from crescent to full.
entries.frame_evidence: The bright part of the moon covers only part of a circular outline.
entries.detector_note: Fit the minimum enclosing circle to the bright moon component (cv2.minEnclosingCircle); lit fraction = component area / circle area; terminator curvature from the concavity of the dark boundary.
entries.notes: For a crescent the enclosing circle is under-determined from the lit arc alone; the value is a proxy, not an ephemeris.

entries.label: Moonlight direction matches moon
entries.description: Whether subjects are lit from the side the moon actually sits on.
entries.frame_evidence: The rim highlight on characters faces the same screen side as the visible moon.
entries.detector_note: Crop a subject plus the moon region as two crops and ask qwen2.5vl about the light side, then compare with moon_x_norm; the deterministic half is the lit-side estimate from a landmark-derived face-ROI luminance asymmetry.
entries.vlm_question: In this crop, is the person lit more strongly from the left side or the right side of the picture? Answer left or right.
entries.notes: A practical light source in scene legitimately overrides the moon; this can only ever be a flag, not a verdict.

entries.label: Papers or leaves scattering in a gust
entries.description: A burst of flat sheets thrown into the air and tumbling.
entries.frame_evidence: Many mid-sized bright flat objects appear at once and follow chaotic, flipping paths.
entries.detector_note: Requires classifying tumbling flat objects and separating them from birds, confetti and debris; no installed detector does this. The generic airborne-particle tracker will register the burst as unlabelled blobs.
entries.notes: Blind spot logged deliberately; airborne_particle_burst_onset carries the measurable half.

entries.label: Particulate layer that does not move
entries.description: An atmosphere layer that is frozen, a common compositing error.
entries.frame_evidence: The same particle pattern sits at identical pixels across many unique cels.
entries.detector_note: Cross-correlate the particle residual mask between unique cels; a correlation above 0.9 at zero lag after camera compensation means the layer is static.
entries.notes: This is the single most useful particulate QC metric and it is cheap; it also catches a still frame being analysed as motion.

entries.label: Petals rather than other particulate
entries.description: Confirming that the ambient falling particles are flower petals.
entries.frame_evidence: The individual shapes read as petals when magnified.
entries.detector_note: Crop a 96x96 window around the largest tracked particle (upscaled 4x with cv2.INTER_CUBIC, since the crop rule requires the defect to fill the crop) and ask qwen2.5vl.
