entries.vlm_question: In this close-up crop, are the falling objects flower petals? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: At 8-12 unique cels per second a single petal is often motion-blurred beyond recognition; expect low confidence.

entries.label: Precipitation agrees with the wind direction
entries.description: Whether rain or snow slant, foliage lean, flags and hair all indicate the same wind.
entries.frame_evidence: Rain slants left while the flag streams right.
entries.detector_note: Collect all available shot-level direction estimates (rain_angle_from_vertical_deg, snow_drift_angle_deg, vegetation_lean_deg, flag wave direction, hair displacement angle, cloud_drift_angle_deg) and report their circular variance plus the maximum pairwise disagreement.
entries.notes: Clouds legitimately move on a different wind from surface air, so cloud drift must be weighted separately from the surface estimates.

entries.label: No precipitation present (confirmed null)
entries.description: An explicit confirmation that no rain, snow or hail is present, as opposed to a detector that did not run.
entries.frame_evidence: The temporal residual carries no renewed streak or blob population above the noise floor.
entries.detector_note: Report NOT FOUND only when the unique-cel gate passed, camera compensation had a good inlier fraction, and the residual energy is within the null-model 95th percentile; otherwise report NOT DETECTABLE.
entries.notes: The three-state distinction (FOUND / NOT FOUND / NOT DETECTABLE) is only meaningful if entries like this one exist to carry the confirmed null.

entries.label: Puddles forming during rain
entries.description: Standing water appearing and spreading on the ground over the shot.
entries.frame_evidence: Reflective patches on the ground grow in area across the shot.
entries.detector_note: Reflective-patch mask (high sky-reflection correlation plus low texture) area fitted against the unique-cel index within a shot; require a static camera.
entries.notes: Wet-look grading and moving specular highlights both change the mask area without new water.

entries.label: Backlit rain
entries.description: Rain catching a light source from behind so the streaks glow.
entries.frame_evidence: Streaks are much brighter than the background and concentrated near a light source.
entries.detector_note: Mean streak-residual intensity relative to local background, and the spatial correlation of streak brightness with distance from any detected bright source.

entries.label: Drawn rain (uniform ink lines)
entries.description: Rain animated as identical straight strokes rather than varied streaks.
entries.frame_evidence: Every rain line has the same width, length and colour, often pure white or pure black.
entries.detector_note: Among confirmed rain streaks, report the coefficient of variation of length, width (from a distance transform) and colour; a CV below 0.15 on all three is the drawn signature.

entries.label: Rain splashes on the ground
entries.description: Small crowns or bursts where drops hit a surface.
entries.frame_evidence: Tiny bright transient shapes pop on horizontal surfaces and vanish within a frame or two.
entries.detector_note: In the lower ground region, detect residual blobs with area 4-60 px whose lifetime is 1-3 unique cels and whose vertical velocity is near zero (they do not travel); report their rate per unique cel.
entries.notes: Compression mosquito noise on a wet street produces the same transient blobs; require the rain-streak detector to have fired in the same window.

entries.label: Rain intensity (light / heavy)
entries.description: How much rain is falling, from a few streaks to a dense curtain.
entries.frame_evidence: The number of streaks per unit area rises and the background loses contrast.
entries.detector_note: Confirmed streak count per megapixel plus the drop in global RMS contrast against a rain-free reference frame of the same shot if one exists; bucket into light / moderate / heavy by fixed thresholds and always emit the raw number too.
entries.notes: The buckets are conventions, not physics; downstream consumers should use the raw density.

entries.label: Water droplets on the camera lens
entries.description: Drops sitting on the front element, distorting the image locally.
entries.frame_evidence: Circular blurred patches stay fixed in frame while the scene moves behind them.
entries.detector_note: Propose candidates as regions whose local sharpness is far below the frame median and which do NOT move under camera compensation, then confirm the crop with qwen2.5vl.
entries.vlm_question: In this crop, are there water droplets sitting on the camera lens in front of the scene? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Bokeh balls, dirt on the lens and a smeared filter give the same static-blur signature, which is exactly why the tier is vlm.

entries.label: Repeated rain particle sprite
entries.description: A CG rain system reusing one sprite so identical drops recur.
entries.frame_evidence: The same drop shape appears many times at different positions, pixel for pixel.
entries.detector_note: Take the highest-contrast streak patch as a template and run cv2.matchTemplate TM_CCOEFF_NORMED over the residual; count matches above 0.95 and report the duplicate fraction.
entries.notes: Drawn 2D rain is even more self-identical than CG rain, so this only distinguishes styles when applies_to is known.

entries.label: Expanding ripple rings on standing water
entries.description: Concentric rings spreading from each drop impact on a puddle.
entries.frame_evidence: Small circles appear and grow on a reflective patch.
entries.detector_note: cv2.HoughCircles on the band-passed puddle region across unique cels; match circles between frames and confirm a monotonically increasing radius; count confirmed expanding rings.
entries.notes: HoughCircles is notoriously parameter-sensitive; on a low-contrast puddle the recall is poor, so a zero count is weak evidence of absence.

entries.label: Sheeting rain / rain curtain
entries.description: Rain so dense it forms visible moving sheets rather than discrete streaks.
entries.frame_evidence: Large soft translucent bands sweep through the frame, greying out the background.
entries.detector_note: When streak individuation fails (very high residual energy but low Hough line count), look for low-frequency translating luminance bands via phaseCorrelate on the blurred residual; that combination is the sheeting signature.
entries.notes: The same low-line-count high-energy state is produced by heavy noise or a dissolve; require the band translation to be coherent.

entries.label: Rain starting or stopping
entries.description: The onset or cessation of rain inside a single shot.
entries.frame_evidence: Streak density rises from zero or falls to zero over a handful of unique cels.
entries.detector_note: Change-point detection (cumulative sum) on the rain_streaks_per_mpx time series within a shot; report onset index, direction and ramp length.

entries.label: Rain fall angle
entries.description: How far the rain is slanted from vertical, a direct proxy for wind.
entries.frame_evidence: All rain dashes lean the same number of degrees off vertical.
entries.detector_note: Circular mean of Hough line angles among confirmed rain streaks; report as degrees from vertical with sign.
entries.notes: Camera motion during the exposure tilts the apparent streaks in live action; log camera_translation_px alongside.

entries.label: Rain streak length
entries.description: The drawn or motion-blurred length of each rain streak.
entries.frame_evidence: Individual dashes span a measurable fraction of frame height.
entries.detector_note: Median Hough segment length among confirmed rain streaks, normalised by frame height.
entries.notes: In live action streak length is an exposure-time artefact, not a rain property; in 2D it is a style choice.

entries.label: Rain streaks visible
entries.description: Falling rain rendered as elongated streaks.
entries.frame_evidence: Many thin bright near-parallel dashes overlay the scene and change position every frame.
entries.detector_note: Temporal median of 7 camera-compensated unique cels; positive residual thresholded at 2.5 sigma; cv2.HoughLinesP(rho=1, theta=pi/360, threshold=12, minLineLength=6, maxLineGap=2) on the residual; require 15 or more lines with angular std below 12 degrees.
entries.notes: Sensor noise, sparkle overlays and drawn speed lines all generate streak candidates; the angular concentration plus per-frame renewal (streaks must NOT persist at the same pixels) is the discriminator.

entries.label: Rain falling on a dry-looking ground
entries.description: A continuity error where precipitation is present but surfaces show no wetness.
entries.frame_evidence: Heavy streaks in the air over a matte, light, unreflective ground with no splashes.
entries.detector_note: Fire only when rain_streaks_per_mpx is high while specular_blob_count and splash_rate_per_ucel are both at zero; then confirm on a ground crop with qwen2.5vl.
entries.vlm_question: In this crop of the ground, does the surface look wet and shiny, or dry? Answer wet or dry.
entries.notes: Stylised animation routinely omits wet ground by convention; this is a flag, not a defect verdict.

entries.label: Rainbow
entries.description: A coloured arc from refracted light in falling water.
entries.frame_evidence: A curved band of ordered spectral colours crosses the sky.
entries.detector_note: Propose candidates deterministically (an arc-shaped region with a monotone hue ramp along its radial direction), then confirm the crop with qwen2.5vl.
entries.vlm_question: In this crop of the sky, is there a rainbow with bands of colour in an arc? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Chromatic aberration, prism flares and graded skies all produce radial hue ramps.

entries.label: Rainbow colour band order
entries.description: Whether the spectral bands run in the physically correct order and how many are drawn.
entries.frame_evidence: The colours proceed red through violet across the width of the arc.
entries.detector_note: Sample hue along the radial normal of the fitted arc; count distinct hue plateaus and check the hue sequence direction against the expected outer-red ordering.
entries.notes: Only run inside a VLM-confirmed rainbow; stylised rainbows frequently use non-physical band counts by design.

entries.label: Rising embers / sparks
entries.description: Glowing particles carried upward on thermal currents.
entries.frame_evidence: Small warm bright points travel upward with flicker and curved paths.
entries.detector_note: Tracked particles with a net UPWARD displacement, warm hue (0-45 deg), high luminance relative to their local background, and per-particle intensity flicker above the noise CV.
entries.notes: Belongs partly to the fire domain; included here as ambient particulate because it drives the same detector.

entries.label: Sandstorm / haboob wall
entries.description: A towering advancing wall of dust obscuring the scene behind it.
entries.frame_evidence: A large opaque brown mass with a defined leading edge advancing across the frame.
entries.detector_note: Gate on a strong warm colour cast plus a rising dark-channel haze estimate, then confirm the crop with qwen2.5vl.
entries.vlm_question: In this crop, is there a huge wall of dust or sand rolling toward the camera? Answer yes or no.

entries.label: Anticrepuscular or shadow rays
entries.description: Rays converging at the antisolar point, opposite the sun.
entries.frame_evidence: Faint dark and light wedges converge low in the sky away from the sun.
entries.detector_note: Requires distinguishing very low-contrast converging wedges from grading vignettes and cloud structure; no available detector reaches usable precision and there is no null model that would make a positive meaningful.
entries.notes: Recorded so the blind spot is explicit rather than silently absent.

entries.label: Sheet lightning (flash without visible bolt)
entries.description: A cloud lit from within with no channel visible.
entries.frame_evidence: The clouds glow bright for a frame or two but no line is present.
entries.detector_note: Flash detector fires while the bolt skeleton test fails, and the brightened region is confined to the cloud mask with soft edges.

entries.label: No sky visible (interior or enclosed)
entries.description: The frame contains no open sky at all.
entries.frame_evidence: No bright low-texture region reaches the top edge of the frame.
entries.detector_note: sky_mask_area_frac below 0.01 with no top-edge contact; emitted explicitly so that all sky metrics can be logged NOT DETECTABLE rather than zero.
entries.notes: This entry exists to distinguish absent-from-frame from present-but-unmeasured, which the analyzer must log differently.

entries.label: Posterised sky banding
entries.description: Visible stepped bands in a sky that should be a smooth gradient.
entries.frame_evidence: Horizontal contour lines across an otherwise flat gradient.
entries.detector_note: Second derivative of the row-mean luma profile; count zero-crossing clusters with amplitude above the frame noise sigma estimated from a flat patch (skimage.restoration.estimate_sigma).
entries.notes: This is a compression/limited-palette artefact in live action but a deliberate style in cel anime; do not report it as a defect without knowing applies_to.

entries.label: Flat untextured sky
entries.description: A sky painted as a single flat colour with no gradient or cloud.
entries.frame_evidence: The sky region has near-zero luminance variance across its whole area.
entries.detector_note: Std of luma and std of hue inside the sky mask below tight thresholds and cloud_coverage_frac near zero.

entries.label: Hue rotation across the sky
entries.description: The sky shifting hue from horizon to zenith, e.g. orange to deep blue.
entries.frame_evidence: Hue angle changes progressively down the sky column.
entries.detector_note: Convert the sky mask to HSV, take circular mean hue per row, and fit hue-versus-row with a circular linear regression; report total hue swing in degrees.

entries.label: Blown-out sky
entries.description: The sky exceeding the recordable range and clipping to pure white.
entries.frame_evidence: Large connected regions of the sky sit at or near the maximum code value with no detail.
entries.detector_note: Fraction of sky-mask pixels with all channels above 250 and local variance below 1; report the largest clipped connected component size.
entries.notes: Deliberate blown-highlight aesthetics and true exposure errors are indistinguishable at pixel level.

entries.label: Sky mask confidence
entries.description: How much to trust the sky segmentation that every sky metric depends on.
entries.frame_evidence: The mask may include white walls, snowfields, blown ceilings and out-of-focus bright backgrounds.
entries.detector_note: Combine top-edge contact fraction, mask compactness, interior texture energy and hue plausibility into a single 0-1 score; downgrade every sky-derived metric proportionally.
entries.notes: This entry is the honest carrier for a segmentation that is a heuristic and not a model.

entries.label: Overcast grey sky
entries.description: A uniformly clouded sky with no visible sun and low saturation.
entries.frame_evidence: The sky is a broad low-saturation grey with a weak gradient and no discrete cloud edges.
entries.detector_note: Sky-mask mean saturation below 0.12, cloud_coverage_frac above 0.85, and cloud contour count low.

entries.label: Sky reflected in water
entries.description: The sky and its clouds mirrored on a water surface below the horizon.
entries.frame_evidence: A vertically flipped copy of the sky palette appears below the horizon line, softened and darker.
entries.detector_note: Correlate the sky band with the vertically mirrored band immediately below the horizon using cv2.matchTemplate TM_CCOEFF_NORMED after cv2.GaussianBlur on both; require correlation above 0.5.
entries.notes: Wet asphalt and polished floors reflect the sky the same way; the entry does not claim the surface is water.

entries.label: Sky region present in frame
entries.description: Whether any open sky is visible at all in this frame.
entries.frame_evidence: An upper band of the frame that is bright, low-texture and continuous to the top edge.
entries.detector_note: Seeded flood fill from the top image row on a joint criterion of V>0.45, local Laplacian variance below the frame median, and hue within a broad blue/grey/warm sky band; require area above 1 percent of frame.
entries.notes: White walls, snow fields and blown-out ceilings all pass this test; every downstream sky metric must carry sky_mask_confidence.

entries.label: Vertical sky gradient
entries.description: The smooth darkening or lightening of the sky from horizon to zenith.
entries.frame_evidence: Sky luminance changes monotonically down the column of the frame.
entries.detector_note: Row means of luminance inside the sky mask; numpy.polyfit degree 1 slope in luma-per-frame-height, with R2 of the linear fit as the smoothness measure.

entries.label: Warm low-sun sky palette
entries.description: The orange/magenta palette characteristic of sunrise or sunset.
entries.frame_evidence: Sky hue concentrated in the 5-45 degree band with high saturation near the horizon.
entries.detector_note: Fraction of sky-mask pixels whose hue lies in the warm band and whose saturation exceeds 0.35, weighted toward the lower third of the sky mask.
entries.notes: This measures palette, not the actual time of day; a stylised fantasy sky can be permanently orange.

entries.label: Sleet / mixed rain and snow
entries.description: Precipitation containing both streaked liquid and slower blob-like frozen particles.
entries.frame_evidence: Fast streaks and slow round particles fall in the same frame.
entries.detector_note: Deterministic precondition: both the streak detector and the blob detector fire above threshold in the same window with clearly different velocities; then confirm on a crop with qwen2.5vl.
entries.vlm_question: In this crop, is the falling precipitation rain, snow, or a mix of both? Answer rain, snow, or mix.
entries.notes: Small VLMs bias heavily toward whichever is more visible; treat mix as low confidence.

entries.label: Snow accumulating on surfaces
entries.description: Snow visibly building up on the ground or on props over the shot.
entries.frame_evidence: Bright coverage on horizontal surfaces increases from start to end of the shot.
entries.detector_note: Fraction of ground-region pixels above a high-luma low-saturation threshold, fitted linearly against the unique-cel index within one shot; require sky_mask stability and camera stability.
entries.notes: Exposure drift raises the bright-pixel fraction identically; anchor with a reference patch that should not change.

entries.label: Blizzard / whiteout
entries.description: Snow so dense that the scene loses contrast and depth.
entries.frame_evidence: The background is greyed nearly to flat white and individual flakes cannot be separated.
entries.detector_note: Joint condition: very high residual energy, failed blob individuation, mean luminance high and global RMS contrast far below the shot median, plus a dark-channel transmission estimate near 1.
entries.notes: Fog, over-exposure and a white-out dissolve are indistinguishable from this alone; require snowfall_present earlier in the shot.

entries.label: Drawn snow (identical discs)
entries.description: Snow animated as repeated identical white circles.
entries.frame_evidence: Every flake is the same perfect disc of the same radius and pure white.
entries.detector_note: Coefficient of variation of snow blob area and circularity below 0.1, with the modal colour at or near pure white and near-zero colour variance.

entries.label: Snowflake fall speed
entries.description: How fast the flakes descend, distinguishing lazy drift from driven snow.
entries.frame_evidence: Flakes cross a given fraction of frame height in a countable number of unique cels.
entries.detector_note: Nearest-neighbour tracking of snow blobs across unique cels; median vertical displacement per unique cel normalised by frame height, plus the tracked-fraction as a reliability measure.
entries.notes: At 8-12 unique cels per second, fast snow moves too far between samples for nearest-neighbour matching and the velocity underestimates; report track_success_frac.

entries.label: Snowflake size spread
entries.description: Whether the flakes are uniform sprites or a varied population, and whether depth layering is implied.
entries.frame_evidence: Some flakes are large and soft, others tiny and sharp, in the same frame.
entries.detector_note: Histogram of snow blob areas; report median, IQR and the number of separated modes from scipy.signal.find_peaks.

entries.label: Snow blown sideways
entries.description: Wind pushing the falling snow off vertical.
entries.frame_evidence: Flake trajectories lean consistently to one side.
entries.detector_note: Circular mean of tracked snow displacement angles; report degrees from vertical and the dispersion.

entries.label: Snow falling
entries.description: Snowflakes descending through the frame.
entries.frame_evidence: Many small bright blobs drift downward at low speed, changing position every unique cel.
entries.detector_note: Temporal median subtraction on camera-compensated unique cels; blob detection on the positive residual (area 2-60 px, circularity above 0.5); require the blob population to be renewed each frame and to have a net downward displacement.
entries.notes: Dust motes, bokeh, ash and sparkle overlays are the same detection; the separators are downward bias, speed and colour neutrality, none of which is decisive alone.

entries.label: Drawn cross/star sparkle
entries.description: The four- or six-pointed drawn sparkle used stylistically for stars and highlights.
entries.frame_evidence: A bright point with symmetric radiating spikes at fixed angles.
entries.detector_note: Around each bright point, sample intensity on a polar grid; count angular lobes via scipy.signal.find_peaks on the angular profile; 4 or 6 evenly spaced lobes is the drawn sparkle signature.
entries.notes: Real lens diffraction spikes from a small aperture look identical and are common in live action.

entries.label: Star density variation / Milky Way band
entries.description: A denser band or patch of stars, typically the galactic band.
entries.frame_evidence: A diagonal swathe where star density and diffuse glow are visibly higher.
entries.detector_note: Star blob density map on a coarse grid plus the low-frequency luminance residual of the dark sky; fit a band orientation via PCA of the high-density cells.

entries.label: Star field
entries.description: Points of starlight in a night sky.
entries.frame_evidence: Many small bright points scattered across a dark sky region with no structure between them.
entries.detector_note: Difference of Gaussians (skimage.feature.blob_dog, min_sigma=0.8, max_sigma=2.5) inside a dark sky mask; require more than 20 blobs with radius under 3 px and a near-uniform spatial Poisson distribution.
entries.notes: Sensor noise and dust in a dark sky create identical blobs; require the blobs to persist across at least 2 unique cels at the same location after camera compensation.

entries.label: Star twinkle
entries.description: Stars pulsing in brightness frame to frame.
entries.frame_evidence: Individual star points change intensity between unique cels without moving.
entries.detector_note: Track matched star blobs across unique cels after camera compensation; per-star intensity coefficient of variation; report the fraction of stars whose CV exceeds the sensor noise CV.
entries.notes: Compression flicker in dark regions produces exactly this signature; the noise-floor control patch is mandatory.

entries.label: Rotating storm cell
entries.description: Cloud mass turning around a centre, as in a mesocyclone or a stylised vortex.
entries.frame_evidence: Flow vectors in the sky curl around a common point across several unique cels.
entries.detector_note: Curl = d(v)/dx - d(u)/dy from np.gradient on the Farneback field inside the sky mask; require a spatially coherent single-signed curl blob with area above 2 percent of the sky mask.
entries.notes: A camera roll produces a whole-frame curl; reject when the curl also covers the ground mask.

entries.label: Sky darkening as a storm builds
entries.description: Progressive loss of sky luminance across the shot as cloud thickens.
entries.frame_evidence: The sky is measurably darker and less saturated at the end of the shot than at the start.
entries.detector_note: Linear trend of sky-mask mean luminance and saturation against unique-cel index within one shot, with a stable non-sky reference patch as the exposure control.
entries.notes: Without the reference patch this measures exposure change, not weather.

entries.label: Sun diffused behind cloud
entries.description: The sun visible only as a soft bright patch through cloud.
entries.frame_evidence: A broad bright region with no hard disc edge sits inside the cloud mass.
entries.detector_note: Crop the brightest sky region and ask qwen2.5vl; deterministic support from a low sun_circularity together with a high bloom_r50_px.
entries.vlm_question: In this crop of the sky, is the sun shining through cloud as a soft glowing patch rather than a sharp bright disc? Answer yes or no.

entries.label: Sun disc visible
entries.description: A discrete sun disc or its saturated core appearing in frame.
entries.frame_evidence: A small compact region at maximum luminance surrounded by a radial falloff.
entries.detector_note: Threshold the sky region at the 99.7th luma percentile; keep components with circularity 4*pi*A/P^2 above 0.7 and radially decreasing surrounding intensity measured on concentric rings.
entries.notes: Practical lights, reflections off glass and specular water glints all pass; a sky-mask requirement suppresses most of them.

entries.label: Sun rising or setting during the shot
entries.description: The sun disc measurably changing height across the shot.
entries.frame_evidence: The bright core moves vertically relative to the horizon over the shot.
entries.detector_note: Track sun centroid y relative to horizon_row_norm across unique cels; fit a linear trend and report sign and rate.
entries.notes: A camera tilt moves the sun in frame without changing its elevation; subtract the horizon row to compensate.

entries.label: Solar or lunar halo
entries.description: A 22-degree ring of light around the sun or moon from ice crystals.
entries.frame_evidence: A faint circle at a fixed radius encircles the light source.
entries.detector_note: Radial intensity profile centred on the detected source; look for a local maximum at a radius well beyond the bloom falloff, and confirm the ring is closed by checking angular coverage of that maximum.
entries.notes: A lens ghost ring and a defocused iris produce a similar annulus.

entries.label: Sun screen position
entries.description: Where the sun sits in the frame, normalised.
entries.frame_evidence: The bright core sits at a specific fraction of frame width and height.
entries.detector_note: Centroid of the sun component in normalised 0-1 coordinates; also emit the offscreen-direction estimate from the radial gradient of the glow when the core is out of frame.

entries.label: Single-frame thunder flash
entries.description: A one-frame near-white frame used as a lightning hit.
entries.frame_evidence: One frame is drastically brighter or fully white and the frames on either side are normal.
entries.detector_note: Detect isolated single-frame luminance outliers where frame N-1 and N+1 are within 5 percent of each other and frame N differs by more than 40 percent; report the frame index.
entries.notes: Also produced by a dropped/duplicated frame, a splice, or a white flash-frame transition.

entries.label: Time-of-day mismatch across a scene
entries.description: Shots in the same scene implying different times of day.
entries.frame_evidence: One shot is golden-hour warm and the adjacent shot is midday neutral.
entries.detector_note: Deterministic precondition from a large sky hue and shadow-length change between adjacent shots; confirm the reading with qwen2.5vl on a representative frame from each shot.
entries.vlm_question: In this image, is it sunrise or sunset, midday, or night? Answer sunrise or sunset, midday, or night.
entries.notes: Grading differences between shots produce the same hue delta; treat as a review flag.

entries.label: Time-of-day shift during the shot
entries.description: The sky measurably changing colour or brightness over the course of one continuous shot.
entries.frame_evidence: Sky hue and luminance at the end of the shot differ from the start with a monotonic path between.
entries.detector_note: Per-unique-cel sky-mask mean hue (circular) and mean luma; fit monotonic trend and report total drift; only valid within a single shot segment.
entries.notes: Auto white balance and auto exposure in live action mimic this exactly; cross-check against a non-sky grey reference patch drifting in the same direction.

entries.label: Unique-cel index gate
entries.description: The list of frames that carry a genuinely new drawing or render, on which every temporal metric must be computed.
entries.frame_evidence: Consecutive frames are bit-near-identical when animation is on 2s or 3s.
entries.detector_note: Per-frame mean absolute difference against the previous frame, plus a dHash comparison; a frame is a duplicate when MAD is below the estimated noise sigma AND the hash distance is 0. Emit the unique-cel index list and the effective unique-cel rate.
entries.notes: MANDATORY PRECONDITION for every temporal entry in this domain. On a 24 fps anime file the effective rate is typically 8-12 per second; any metric expressed in Hz must state that rate.

entries.label: Volumetric light shaft in fog
entries.description: A visible cone or beam of light made solid by suspended particles.
entries.frame_evidence: A straight-edged bright wedge extends from a light source through the air.
entries.detector_note: Detect elongated bright regions with straight converging edges whose apex coincides with a detected bright source; measure edge straightness via Hough and the intensity falloff along the beam axis.
entries.notes: A hard-edged bright architectural surface can mimic a shaft; requiring apex coincidence with a source suppresses most.

entries.label: Chop and whitecaps
entries.description: Broken wave crests producing white foam, indicating strong wind.
entries.frame_evidence: Small bright irregular patches scattered on the water surface, appearing and vanishing.
entries.detector_note: Bright blobs inside the water region whose lifetime is under 5 unique cels and whose luminance exceeds the water mean by more than 2.5 sigma; report count density and mean lifetime.
entries.notes: Sun glitter produces bright transient blobs too; the glitter entry uses the same primitives and the two must be reported together, not chosen between.

entries.label: Ripple travel direction on water
entries.description: The direction the wind-driven surface waves travel.
entries.frame_evidence: Ripple crests advance consistently across unique cels.
entries.detector_note: Lagged cross-correlation of the band-pass filtered water region between unique cels over a set of candidate directions; take the argmax direction and speed.
entries.notes: Aliasing: if the ripple wavelength is shorter than twice the per-unique-cel displacement, the measured direction can invert.

entries.label: Water sheeting off a surface
entries.description: Rainwater flowing down a wall, window, rock or roof.
entries.frame_evidence: Thin bright vertical streams travel downward on a solid surface, unlike falling rain which crosses open air.
entries.detector_note: Detect near-vertical elongated bright residuals whose support lies ON a detected surface (not against sky) and whose downward speed is far lower than the measured rain streak speed.

entries.label: Wind ripple texture on water
entries.description: Fine capillary ripples roughening a water surface under wind.
entries.frame_evidence: The water surface carries a dense high-frequency directional texture rather than a mirror finish.
entries.detector_note: Inside a candidate water region (below horizon, high sky-reflection correlation or high specular sparkle), take the 2D FFT and report high-frequency energy fraction and angular anisotropy.
entries.notes: The water region proposal is itself a heuristic; report water_region_confidence.

entries.label: Weather continuity between shots
entries.description: Whether the weather state stays consistent across a cut within a scene.
entries.frame_evidence: Rain is heavy in one shot and absent in the next of the same sequence.
entries.detector_note: Compare the shot-level weather vector (rain density, snow count, transmission mean, sky luma/hue, cloud coverage) across adjacent shots; report the L2 distance and the largest single-component jump.
entries.notes: A legitimate time cut or location change makes a large jump correct; the analyzer can only report the jump, not judge it.

entries.label: Lighting matches the stated weather
entries.description: Whether subject lighting is consistent with the sky, e.g. hard sun shadows under an overcast sky.
entries.frame_evidence: A character carries a crisp directional shadow while the sky behind is flat grey cloud.
entries.detector_note: Deterministic precondition: sky_overcast_flat_grey fires while a hard cast-shadow edge (10-90 transition under 4 px) exists on a subject; then ask qwen2.5vl on a two-part crop.
entries.vlm_question: In this crop, does the person have a hard sharp shadow like direct sunlight? Answer yes or no.
entries.notes: Bounce cards, practicals and stylised anime shading routinely produce hard shadows under overcast skies; this is a flag for review only.

entries.label: Surfaces gone wet and reflective
entries.description: Ground and props darkened and made specular by water.
entries.frame_evidence: Roads and pavements darken while gaining sharp bright reflections of lights.
entries.detector_note: In the ground region, report the joint change of mean luminance (down) and the count of high-contrast elongated bright reflections (up) relative to a dry reference elsewhere in the sequence; also report specular sharpness via the Laplacian variance of the bright reflections.
entries.notes: Without a dry reference from the same location this measures absolute reflectivity, not wetness; log reference_available.

entries.label: Drawn wind speed lines
entries.description: The graphic straight or curved lines used in 2D animation to render wind itself.
entries.frame_evidence: Long thin parallel strokes overlay the scene at a consistent angle.
entries.detector_note: cv2.HoughLinesP on the Canny edge map; require 6 or more lines with angular std below 8 degrees, length above 0.15 of frame width, and low colour variance along each line; check that they cross object boundaries (overlay behaviour).
entries.notes: Rain streaks satisfy the same Hough test; the discriminators are line length, spacing regularity and the fact that speed lines are usually opaque and cross characters.

ask_on_rule: LOCAL properties (open/closed/present/defective) are asked on a tight CROP; GLOBAL properties (framing, camera angle, shot size, light direction, spatial relations) are asked on the FULL FRAME. Measured: on a crop the VLM answered camera angle, light direction and shot size differently from the full frame, stably and wrongly — a crop is a new framing, so it replaces the answer rather than revealing it.
